Heading: 4.3 kg tumour mass removed, docs say surgery ‘unusual’ - Indian Express
Content:
The much-awaited first Night Food Street of the city will be ready to operate by the end of the month. Located near the PGI, the project would give an enchanting night life to the residents of the city.

The street, being constructed at the cost of Rs 14.28 lakh, will have eight kiosks initially. The terms and conditions of how these kiosks will be allotted will be settled in the Finance and Contract Committee meeting to be held this month.

The idea of the Night Food Street was initiated by former Mayor Harjinder Kaur. The foundation stone was laid by present Mayor Pardeep Chhabra in January this year. Though the Night Food Street had to start functioning by April, the project was delayed.

The idea was to have something on lines of a Food Street in Lahore. Once constructed, each kiosk will be 7'-6" X 7'-6".

The idea had been initiated keeping in mind the large number of students who stay in the adjoining sectors as well as Panjab University. The attendants of patients at PGI also look for late night snacks but not many options are available for them. With a number of colleges also present in the area, the Night Food Street is expected to attract a lot of people.

"The details of how the allotment is to be done are being worked out. The officials have been directed to look into the details," Mayor Pardeep Chhabra said.

While this will be the first Night Food Street, there are proposals to have a few more at different places in the city.

Heading: The legacy of a land - Indian Express
Content:
The Cheema Medical Complex, Mohali, on Wednesday claimed to have performed an "unusual and risky" surgery after removing a tumour from the ovary of an elderly person. According to doctors, the tumour weighing nearly 4.3 kg was extracted from the area surrounding the pelvis after a complicated surgical procedure involving "exploratory laparotaomy".

The surgery team comprised experts from the Cheema Medical Complex and was led by Dr Parampreet Ghuman, Consultant Obstetrician and Gynecologist. Dr Ghuman told that Angrez Kaur had come to the hospital with a history of abdominal pains and discomfort.

"Difficulty in breathing and decrease in appetite were the other symptoms which led us to examine the patient and conclude the presence of a huge abdominal mass arising from the pelvis. This was later established to be a large ovarian tumour."

The doctor added, "Exploratory laparotomy was performed upon the patient and the huge mass removed."

"The patient, Angrez Kaur, has recovered remarkably well after the surgery," said Dr Ajaiwant Cheema, managing director of the hospital. Dr Parampreet said that despite a number of similar surgeries performed by her earlier, this surgery was unique as it was the largest tumour removed by her.

Heading: Dancing queen - Indian Express
Content:
A bunch of Punjabis are making sure that Punjab's on everyone's mind

Post 9/11, the world stood torn and tortured, divided and desperate. Territories were marked, everyone was on guard, everyone was attacked and identity faced a massive crisis. The human race had never felt so violated, so angry, so isolated. Amidst this sea of anarchy, suppression and suspicion, a small wave gained mass and movement, and rose, from a land where the five rivers flow, from a place called Punjab. In their quest to take this amazingly rich state's history and culture across nations, we came across couple of Punjabis who are busy re-introducing Punjab to the people of the world. Be it through art, films, animation or books, these creative minds are making sure that every Singh feels like a King.

"The world is a fast changing place, and we need keep up with the pace," Jagmeet Samundri starts on a infotaining note, one which strives to keep the world library posted on other cultures and traditions. A filmmaker by profession, Samundri's using the medium to tell people who Punjabis are, where they come from, what do they look like and "most importantly, who their Gurus are." His 43 minute documentary of Guru Gobind Singh, The Rise of the Khalsa, was recently screened at the New York Film Festival. "Punjabi children living abroad should be made aware about the religion and I feel films are the best way to teach them," he focuses on a story that's educative as well as entertaining.

Okay, so have our share of Akshays raising a toast to 'Singh is King', Hard Kaur rapping with a fevered passion, the likes of Johnny Lever and Jaspal Bhatti pinning the audience to 'the big bang theory' that's so synonymous with Sardars. The glitz and glamour aside, there's a parallel group of people who are keeping the faith alive, who are acting as global voices and putting Punjab high on the world map and making it big in art circles, international film festivals and best bookselling lists. Take, for instance, Amarjit Virdi. He started out as an artist who sculpted and painted only on Punjab's history and culture, and his buyers were NRIs. Today, he has picked up animation and is out with his first independent animated feature, Maharaja (on Ranjit Singh). "Before that, I worked on Sahibzade," he tells us, now being offered the idea of converting it into a feature film. "I've always felt like doing something for my state, giving back its glory, promoting it in the manner its Gurus and forefathers would've liked to," Virdi feels the expectations are too high and we need to fulfill these.

While there's Raj Babbar, Mangal Dhillon and Daljit Ami working on varied topics of interests and issues gripping the state, www.sikhcouncilusa.org, www.swfftoronto.com- exclusively for promoting the Sikh culture, The Kaurs and Punjabi Parvasis connecting Punjabis all over, filmmaker Amarjit Singh's already screened his film on Maharaja Dalip Singh at the House of Commons in England. In Mumbai shooting yet another full fledged venture of, for and by Sardars, Singh observes no matter where we are, we can never cut off completely from our roots. "The scenario has changed, Sardars are no longer perceived as funny laughable characters. They have a depth to them. Moreover, this is also a way to bridge the communication gap, physical and mental between generations, and those living abroad," he adds. Meanwhile, writer Khushwant Singh's travelogue on the Sikhs of UK and the US is the talk of the town. Now that he's looking forward to adding more such travelogues of Sikhs across the globe, Khushwant feels that this will ultimately serve the purpose of reference material, of a document "for generations to come. Sikhs Unlimited and more such books are mediums to showcase path-breaking works of Punjabis across the world. It does not talk of big names, but the people who have impacted communities with their work," says Khushwant, highlighting Punjabis as a global community, especially in the cold world of post 9/11. What to say, Singhs are truly the Kings!

Heading: In transit - Indian Express
Content:
Patiala's Isha Dang wins Boogie Woogie' Kids' Dance Championship

Here's another Punjabi doing the region proud. Fourteen-year-old Isha Dang of Patiala did the city and Punjab proud by winning the Boogie Woogie Under-15 Kids' Dance Championship in Mumbai. Competing with 43 dancers from all over the country, Isha proved to be the best performer in the grand finale of the contest held on September 8. Isha comes home with Rs five lakh and a trophy and is incidentally the first child dancer from Punjab to have won such a contest at the national level. The grand finale of the Boogie Woogie Kids' Championship will be aired on Sony Television on October 10. Isha, who has been in Mumbai for the last two months for the contest, had won the second prize in the Boogie Woogie Kids' Championship in July 2004.

"I am happy to have won the coveted contest. My hard work and training have paid off. I thank Punjabis and Patialvis for supporting me all along," said an elated Isha, a Class IX student of Our Lady of Fatima Convent School. For now, she wants to concentrate on her studies as she aspires to compete for Civil Services. Her dance teacher Daisy Ahluwalia and her parents were with her during the grand finale. Dancing since the age of three, she has to her credit as many as 190 performances in the country and 92 prizes at both national and international level and Patiala is all set to give the little lady a rousing welcome.

Heading: Asha forever - Indian Express
Content:
Balwant Thakur doesn't have many prerequisites for staging a play. His acts are mobile & flexible

He's driven by challenges and creativity. So, even an assigned project is turned into a work of art. That's how Sainyan Bhaye Kotwal, the final play of the National Theatre Festival took shape. The play has been staged all over the country by various directors, and theatre director Balwant Thakur took it up for it was different from the productions his group Natrang had been staging. "I prefer to call it a satire rather than a comedy, one that's a symbolic picture of the contemporary political happenings and a caricature of the bad governance has been depicted in the play. The theme is contemporary and relevant to any part of the world,'' Thakur's production has his signature style and he's made a few changes in the script and updated it as well. Balwant is happy that the audiences have received it really well. What's best, the production is mobile, sans many frills, so it can be taken anywhere, "and also staged in a huge theatre, street or a small space. It's versatile and in my opinion, theatre has to be flexible, so it can reach out to more people, that's the entire idea. That's why when we travel with our plays, my requirements are negligible. We make sure we are self-sufficient in every way.'' Natrang, as a theatre group primarily practices Dogri theatre rooted in the soil of Jammu and Thakur's plays are replete with culture, tradition, music, folklore of the region. Thakur never tires of exploring the culturally rich area which is in a constant state of strife, "the situation is absurd here, there are many stakeholders, aspects and we are complicating matters,'' Thakur is busy writing a book, the Origin and Development of Dogri Theatre. The unknown aspects of Dogri theatre, the contributors, the rich culture and heritage, I hope to document all that and more.''

Heading: Work on Khedar thermal power plant on schedule - Indian Express
Content:
In her 75th year, the singer is going as strong as ever

Singing legend Asha Bhonsle celebrated her 75th birthday in great style at the Taj Land's End, Bandra, by releasing a new album, Precious Platinum. The new album is a collection of songs composed and arranged by composer Nitin Ramesh Shankar. "People can't sing item songs when they just want to sing to themselves or to others. There should be some songs which, for instance, a lady sitting at home can just sing," she said.

The video of one of the tracks from the album, Tum Jo Mile, was also screened for the audience. Regarding the shooting of the video, which is set amidst waterfalls on the Western Ghats, Bhonsle joked, "I was standing on a precipice and I was afraid that it would be my last song. We shot for three days in rainy and windy weather and at the end of it, I fell ill." The diminutive diva, who's been singing since she was 16, is the world's most recorded artist. She's also the only Indian artist to be nominated twice for the Grammy awards.

Age has dealt lightly with Bhonsle as was evident when she entered the venue, and held court with the grace and élan that comes from years of being the reigning queen of Indian airwaves. She was in a reminiscent mood as she talked about her long association with the music industry. "I have been singing for 65 years. Now you sing happy birthday to me."

Heading: Alliance or not: BJP is in a fix - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda inaugurated the first 600-MW boiler drum-lifting event at the 1200-MW Rajiv Gandhi Thermal Power Plant being set up at Khedar in Hisar district. "The construction work of the plant is going as per schedule and it will be completed by November 2009. This is an important event in construction of the power plant.This will be country's first single 600-MW unit to be installed. With this milestone, the plant construction is poised to be completed ahead of schedule," said Hooda.

After completing the required civil work, the boiler drum for Unit-I was lifted to the height of about 100 metres on the top of the boiler.

This is the first project to be awarded mega-project status in the Northern region under the mega project policy of the Central government. The two units will be commissioned within 35 and 38 months, respectively, from the project award date. The mega power status will eventually result in the reduction of cost of generation of power and would provide with better quality.

The reduction in the cost of generation will automatically affect the cost at which the consumer buys power. After the commencement of the project, an additional 288 lakh units would be available to cater to the needs of the state. The energy generated would be supplied to additional 4.4 lakh consumers, who constitute 11 per cent of the existing consumers.

Hooda also laid the foundation stone of a residential colony for the employees of the power plant. Both Hooda and Randeep Singh Surjewala, Power Minister, planted saplings at the Rajiv Gandhi Power Plant camps.

Hooda said priority was given to development of power sector during his rule. Haryana got the much-delayed Deenbandhu Chhotu Ram Thermal Power Project in Yamunanagar commissioned at a cost of Rs 1,834 crore.

Indira Gandhi Super Thermal Power Project is being set up in Jhajjar district at a cost of Rs 7,892.42 crore. For the next three consecutive years, one power generation plant would be commissioned every year, adding to the power generation capacity of the state, he added.

Heading: After Asian Paints, Rohtak IMT eyes other industries - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana BJP is in a dilemma over a poll pact in the forthcoming Parliamentary elections. If it does decide in favour of an electoral alliance, it has two choices -- the Indian National Lok Dal (INLD), headed by former chief minister Om Prakash Chautala, or the newly-formed Haryana Janhit Congress (BL) under the leadership of Bhajan Lal and his MP son Kuldeep Bishnoi.

Having failed to find a satisfactory answer, the state unit of the BJP is likely to discuss and finalise the issue at the three-day national executive committee meeting of the party at Bangalooru, from September 12 to 14. BJP MP from Sonepat, Kishan Chand Sangwan, Haryana BJP president Atam Prakash Manchanada, senior leaders Ram Bilas Sharma, and Om Prakash Dhankar and former Haryana BJP president Ganeshi Lal would attend the meeting.

The attitude of the party leaders has not helped the matter as well. One section of the BJP has vehemently opposed a pact with any other party. However, going by the recent drubbing the BJP received in the three by-elections at Adampur, Gohana and Indri, where the three BJP candidates together could not gather even 10,000 votes, the national leadership has realised the futility of the pompous claims of the state BJP to come to power on its own.

Another section of the state BJP is opposed to the pact with INLD. The state leadership has not forgotten the humiliation suffered at the hands of the INLD during their alliance in 2000. Even though they came to power, but a rift between the leaders of the two parties soon developed.

However, the two may be forced to go for yet another alliance. The strong rural base of INLD and the urban face of the BJP could be advantageous for both.

On the other hand, given the previous experience with INLD, it would be advisable to go for an alliance with the Haryana Janhit Congress (HJC).

Senior BJP leader Ram Bilas Sharma said, "We want to focus on all the anti-Congress votes in the next elections. We will see whether it would be prudent to go alone or have a pact. We will discuss the matter in the national executive committee meeting of the BJP.'' He added, "We did not win many seats both in the Parliamentary and the Assembly elections last time. But this time we are very confident of putting up a better performance.''

Heading: Woman killed by husband - Indian Express
Content:
After attracting the Asian Paints investment for the Industrial Model Township (IMT), Rohtak, the Haryana government is making all efforts to bring more industries to Rohtak, which also happens to be Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda's native place.

Rewarding the L&T for completion of the Panipat flyover project before time, the Haryana Industrial and Infrastructure Development Corporation (HSIIDC) has hired the company to develop the infrastructure for IMT Rohtak.

Unlike IMT Manesar, where all three units of the infrastructure development- roads, electricity and public health were given to three different companies, the L&T has been given the contract to develop the complete infrastructure at Rohtak.

Asian Paints in its first phase had invested Rs 875 crore, ensuring direct and indirect employment for 1,500 persons at this plant. The HSIIDC, developing this IMT, had conducted interviews to allot 10 acres to the vendors on prioritybasis. Three vendors of Asian Paints were allotted land.

"We have received excellent response and hope to execute all major projects slated in the first phase on time. Soon the IMT would open up new vistas of development for the people of the area," said Rajeev Arora, Managing Director, HSIIDC.

Meanwhile, the Lotte Group of Korea has also lined up for allotment of 25 acres at the IMT to develop a confectionery unit. The HSIIDC is processing the request.

The IMT Rohtak would come up in an area of 3,000 acres and the corporation has already acquired more than 1,000 acres.

Most of the land has been allotted to Asian Paints, which has started work on the first phase of its project that would result in production of 1.5 lakh KL, finally scaling up to 4 lakh KL .

The company would contribute Rs 40 crore annually to the state exchequer and Rs 700 crore to the Central exchequer.

Authorities are of the view Asian Paints will do to Rohtak what Maruti has done to Gurgaon in terms of development, investment and employment generation.

"The company will have many vendors in the IMT and they would also contribute to the exchequer. We have received morerequests for allotment of land which would be considered at the time of next interviews for allotment," said a senior official.

Heading: Baddi: a dream gone sour - Indian Express
Content:
A 28-year-old woman, Suman, was murdered by her inebriated husband, Ramawtar, today. A habitual drinker, Ramawtar allegedly killed Suman by smashing her head with a stone.

Ramawtar is absconding. Suman's body was found in a pool of blood. She is survived by three sons. Neighbours said Ramawtar used to regularly beat Suman up in an inebriated state.

The police have taken the body in custody for a postmortem. The statements of the neighbours and relatives of Ramawtar have been recorded and a case registered.

In another incident in Hansi, five persons were injured over a claim to the ashes of one Bala, who died under mysterious circumstances in Kurukshetra. Sources said the husband of the deceased, Jagdish, and his elder brother Vikram had gone to Hansi to collect Bala's ashes. There, a clash took place between Jagdish and Bala's brothers, Sanjay, Bajinder and Satish.

Jagdish and Vikram received serious injuries and were referred to PGI, Rohtak. Bala's family has alleged that she was killed by Jagdish and his brother Vikram.

Heading: Baddi belt villagers against master plan - Indian Express
Content:
Asia's largest pharma hub could wither away if tax holiday ends

A contour map of the Baddi belt shows just a series of undifferentiated blocks in a wide strip of land near the foothills of the Himalayas. As one drives up to the most-discussed industrial belt, just 40 kilometres from Chandigarh, the blocks metamorphose into factories. The most striking aspect, however, is the absence of any reasonably pucca road in the entire belt.

The Baddi-Barotiwala-Nalagarh industrial belt is a classic example of a dream gone sour. It was brought into being by a massive tax incentive package in 2003, but successive governments in Himachal have only concentrated on ensuring that the tax holiday is extended beyond 2010 without bothering to develop the zone. The area has everything going for it — adequate power, a rarity in India, peaceful industrial climate and proximity to Delhi, Chandigarh and Amritsar.

But, thanks to two decades of inaction — the first units set up shop here in 1991— the zone, which has become Asia's largest pharmaceutical hub, could wither away as soon as the tax holiday goes.

Lack of infrastructure and haphazard industrial development in this town, located in Solan district of Himachal Pradesh, has given nightmares to investors and locals alike. Companies such as Omaxe, Amaravati, Shakun Infrastructure and Suncity projects are striving hard to find buyers for their housing complexes.

The lackadaisical approach of the three state governments of Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh towards improvement of inter-state connectivity has been a major impediment in trade expansion by industrial units.

This belt has also earned the dubious distinction of forcing industry captains to demand roads, housing for workers and even hospitals, much before the employees did so. Rajender Guleria, president of Baddi Barotiwala Nalagarh Industries' Association (BBNIA), says, "We have been approaching the chief ministers of Punjab and Haryana for a long time, but have only got a lukewarm response. As a result, industrial growth is suffering."

The state government's response has been the classic control mindset. To prevent further overcrowding in Baddi, it is planning to freeze new industrial establishments. Baldev Thakur, deputy CEO, Baddi-Barotiwala-Nalagarh Industrial Development Authority, says, "Only those industries will be allowed to set up units in Baddi which have already acquired land. But the Baddi-Barotiwala-Nalagarh Industries' Association is opposing the move. To decongest Baddi, the state government has acquired 600 bighas and 1,800 bighas for new industrial areas in Manpura and Bagheri villages, respectively, for attracting fresh investments.

Where on one hand industrialists rue poor condition of roads, locals complain about absence of good schools, hospitals and recreational facilities. Vijay K. Arora, senior vice-president (communication, administration and corporate affairs) Vardhman Group, says, "We set up base in Baddi in 1991 but have seen no significant development taking place as far as infrastructure and basic facilities are concerned. Even though the internal roads have improved, inter-state connectivity is still inadequate."

Due to the increasing migrant labour force in the industrial belt, the area is slowly transforming into an unorganised slum. Thakur says, "Since there is no provision for accommodation of migrant labour in majority of the industrial units, they live in slums." To tackle this problem, the Himachal government has approved a housing scheme for labourers, with CII as the facilitator.

With about 750 units having already commenced production from Baddi industrial belt and 2,234 units registered with the Industries Department of the state on provisional basis, the investment in the region is likely to touch Rs 20,000 crore.

With the industrial package for Himachal due to expire on March 31, 2010, speculation is already rife about industries shifting base. However, the state government is making efforts to seek extension of the package till 2013, as was originally planned.

Heading: Naina Devi stampede: Govt to take action against erring officials - Indian Express
Content:
Implementation of the master plan in Baddi-Barotiwala-Nalagarh industrial belt may lead to abolishing of the Baddi Nagar Panchayat and Nalagarh Municipal Committee. Besides, it would also scrap the powers of all gram panchayats, provided as per the 74th amendment of Panchayati Raj Act, to carry out developmental activities in their respective areas.

Sources in the Town and Country Planning Department revealed that the draft proposal of the master plan, which will empower the Baddi-Barotiwala-Nalagarh Industrial Development Authority (BBNIDA), clearly mentions that "the two civic bodies of Baddi and Nalagarh will cease to exist and their functions and powers will be assumed by the BBNIDA".

Notably, the proposal of the government to implement the master plan in the region is being opposed by public representatives and villagers, including elected representatives of Panchayati Raj Institutions, on the plea that it would hamper developmental activities in rural areas and cause harassment to villagers.

"We are not against the development of the area, but certain proposals of the plan will snatch away the rights of panchayats and villagers," said the chairman of Zila Parishad, Ram Kumar.

Notably, over two dozens pradhans of gram panchayats, members of Block Development Committee and Zila Parishad have submitted their objections with the officials concerned. The last date for submitting these objections is September 12. The pradhans have also submitted a memorandum to the Chief Minister, urging him to withdraw certain proposals of the master plan.

"We have passed a resolution against the proposal of the government," said president of Baddi Nagar Panchayat Bhupinder Kaur Chaudhary.

On the other hand, Doon MLA Vinod Chandel said the issue had already been taken up with the Chief Minister and the demand of the people would be looked into.

Heading: 18 IAS, 17 HAS officers transferred - Indian Express
Content:
The state government has initiated the process for taking action against the officials who were on duty when the stampede at the Naina Devi temple complex occurred in Bilaspur on August 3. The state Cabinet, after adopting the inquiry report submitted by Divisional Commissioner, Mandi, two weeks back, has given a nod for implementing findings of the report, which includes fresh precautionary measures for crowd management.

The report mentions laxity on part of officials deputed at the time of the incident in sectors 4 and 5, where the incident occurred, against whom the Cabinet has approved disciplinary action. Though the exact number of officials who would face the music in the entire episode is not clear, Principal Secretary (Home) S.C. Negi said, "The departments concerned would now initiate the process for disciplinary action. No action has been recommended against the Superintendent of Police, Bilaspur, and the police officials involved are only of the level of DSPs or sub-inspectors or executive magistrates."

The Cabinet, in its meeting held on Tuesday evening, also decided to implement fresh measures for crowd control recommended by the inquiry officer. Now on, the registration of visitors to the temple would be done at the entrance counters and batches of not more than 200 would be allowed to go ahead of the entrance.

Special arrangements have been recommended on occasions like Navratra fairs, holidays, Tuesdays, Saturday and Sundays to manage the rush of visitors. The pilgrims would be routed through a circular way to the main temple and back to the base area where basic facilities of water and toilets would be made available. Streetlights, medical facilities through the community health centre (CHC), dependable public address system, guide cell, more CCTV cameras and training of the temple staff in disaster management are other recommendations in the inquiry report.

The Cabinet has also decided to direct the Deputy Commissioner and Superintendent of Police of the district to camp at the site during fairs and rush days to oversee the arrangements and submit a monthly note to the state government.

Heading: NRI comes as messiah for poor villagers - Indian Express
Content: Additional Director General of Police B.S. Thind on Wednesday appeared before the investigating officer for recording his voice sample at Parwanoo. Police sources said Thind arrived at 2.30 pm and left at 3 pm. Facing charges of cheating and extortion levelled by a Parwanoo businessman, Ashok Mittal, on June 15 this year, Thind had earlier expressed his inability to join the investigations and appear for a voice test before the investigating officer at Parwanoo on medical grounds. Thind was twice summoned by the Parwanoo police to join the investigation. Thind, currently posted in the state Human Rights Commission, had mentioned Himachal Sadan, New Delhi, as his address for communication. He had initially sought exemption till September 9. Thind was first summoned by the Parwanoo police on August 11, but he said he would be able to do so only after August 27. After this, he was summoned on August 30.

Heading: Army celebrates raising of Engineer Sqn - Indian Express
Content:
Nijjar has financed more than 700 pucca houses in over 24 villages

For more than two dozen poor villages of Punjab and some 1984 riot victims in Maharashtra, Surinder Singh Nijjar is a messiah. He has done for them what the government has failed to do, and that too without expecting anything in return, except the satisfaction of helping the needy. The result - they look upon him as God and believe in him as much.

Nijjar, a Non-Resident Indian (NRI) hailing from Birmingham in England, has helped thousands of families including those of Dalits, backward classes and the Scheduled Castes in the remotest villages, to get pucca houses. Nijjar has financed more than 700 houses for the poor, and is continuing with his remarkable contribution.

"It all started in 2005, when there were floods in some parts of Punjab. Nijjar read about them on the Internet. He contacted his relatives in the state, and came to India to survey the situation," says Lal Singh, the sarpanch of Mardanpur village.

Lal Singh highlights that Nijjar gave money to the displaced villagers and promised them cemented houses, which he got constructed at his own cost. Since then, Nijjar has financed scores of such houses for poor villagers.

"Mera kutcha makan taan sara dub gaya si, par Nijjar ji ne mainu pakka ghar de ditta, te mere bete nu mistri da kamm vi dila ditta (my kutcha house had been washed away by the flood, but Nijjar gave me a new cemented one, and also got my son employed as a mason," says Mahinder Kaur, a Dalit woman in her 70s, residing at Kamikalan village.

Each house that Nijjar has got constructed bears a small board, 'Fortel Aid UK 2007'. "Fortel is the name of his firm in England. Perhaps this is the only praise that he is claiming for his philanthropist deeds," smiles Kulwinder Singh, a landlord of Ghanaur, who has been helping Nijjar voluntarily for about three years.

Nijjar has taken up humanitarian work in a large number of villages, including Tepla, Ramnagar, Rajgarh, Bapror, Mardanpur, Sindarsi, Gadhepur, Kaapuri, Harigarh, Harimajra, Gandian Kherhi, Ukri Khalaspur, Jand Mangoli, Chamori, Sarjaarpur, Lo Simbli, Unsor, Katharkherhi, Najama, Salempur, Khanpur etc. "A year ago, Nijjar read about the plight of some villagers on Punjab border. He got pucca houses constructed for them at his own cost," says Lal Singh.

Nijjar has also got constructed about 100 houses for the 1984 riot victims in a village near Hazoor Sahib in Maharashtra.

"The houses have been made in Talegaon village, and handed over to the victims," says Kulwinder Singh.

The villagers cannot thank Nijjar enough. "After the floods in 2005, many politicians and district officials visited our village. But ultimately, none helped us. Nijjar not only got pucca houses constructed for us, but also paid for our ration," points out Joginder Singh, a daily-wager whose house was built by Fortel Aid.

Nijjar has also got houses constructed in villages in Amritsar and Jalandhar. He is now considering financing such houses in Mansa too.

The publicity-shy philanthropist
Nijjar, who hails from Kapurthala, is media-shy, and was not available for comment. His generosity is touching indeed. In addition to his other efforts, Nijjar has started a scheme for poor village girls. He donates Rs 5,000 to the family of the girl for her marriage, irrespective of their caste. "In this way, he has helped many needy families," says Kulwinder Singh.

Heading: Probe ordered into police action in immoral trafficking case - Indian Express
Content:
The Army today celebrated the raising of an Engineer Squadron at New Amritsar Military Station, Khasa. The squadron was raised yesterday.

Lt Gen Noble Thamburaj, General Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Southern Command and Colonel Commandant of 'The Bombay Sappers' visited New Amritsar Military Station to celebrate the occasion. He was accompanied by Lt Gen VS Tonk, General Officer Commanding, Vajra Corps.

A ceremonial mounted parade was presented by the newly-raised Engineer Squadron in the honour of the Colonel Commandant. An Army spokesman said that Lt Gen Noble Thamburaj has played an instrumental role in raising the squadron.

The General Officer Commanding-in-Chief hoisted the Engineers Flag during the parade, and commended the troops for the high standard of professionalism displayed by them.

Anita Thamburaj, president of AWWA Southern Command, Maj Gen PS Paul, General Officer Commanding, Panther Division, Commandant BEG and Centre Kirkee and a large number of veterans of Bombay Sappers were among those present on the occasion.

Heading: Al fresco classrooms on embankment - Indian Express
Content:
Inspector general (Border Range) Rajpal Meena has ordered a probe into the action taken by the police in the case pertaining to immoral trafficking, in which the district police had nabbed 18 youngsters, including nine girls.

The youths were nabbed during a raid at Sangam Cinema on August 19. They had been let off soon after. However, these youngsters were booked later, and challans were served on them. The youngsters were in the age-group of 18 to 25 years. Sources said the police action has shocked the IG, who has directed Batala SP to conduct a probe, on the order of Punjab DGP.

"The matter is being probed, and the findings will be submitted to the court," said the IG.

Sources said that the relative of a girl involved in the case had complained to the DGP about the arrests, following which the probe was ordered. Sources said that the officers handling the case did not inform the IG that challans had been served on 23 persons in the case.

The action of the police has raised questions about the procedures followed by them. It has also caused quite a flutter among the youth involved in the case, whose families are contemplating taking legal recourse.

The youngsters hail from affluent families. Charges of immoral trafficking were slapped on them because according to the police, they were caught in a compromising position. Many of these youngsters are college students studying in Amritsar.

Heading: AICC stands by Amarinder - Indian Express
Content:
Flood waters have receded, but the woes of schoolchildren of Doaba haven't.

With the school buildings washed away in Jalandhar and Kapurthala districts, students of over 50 schools are being forced to take classes on the dhussi embankment.

The students are ferried in tractor-trolleys to their schools, as the link roads have been damaged.

Besides, all the records in the schools have got washed away and the dilapidated classrooms, where stink is all-pervasive, now house insects, reptiles and a few stray dogs.

About 115 students of Sheikh Mange Government School, which was submerged under six feet-deep water, have been taking classes on the embankment.

There is no drinking water available for them. The groundwater has been contaminated by the toxins released from nearby factories, said Harneet Singh, a teacher in Sheikh Mange school.

"The children are also suffering from various ailments that have afflicted the area after flood," added Singh.

Condition of various other schools in Batawali, Bharowana, Bhawanipur and Chananwindi was no different. Giddarpindi sarpanch Balbir Singh said they have been cleaning the school for the past couple of weeks, but haven't got rid of the slush. Even the computers have been damaged.

Kapurthala DEO Rup Lal said the condition of 14 schools in the district was bad. "We are preparing records of damage to submit to the department. The condition will soon improve," he said.

Heading: Punjabi language Bill passed - Indian Express
Content:
All India Congress Committee (AICC) General Secretary Manish Tiwari said the Congress stands by former Punjab chief minister Amarinder Singh. He said a false report was presented to defame him and it was a plain case of political vendetta. "The SAD-BJP government will get a befitting reply in the coming Lok Sabha elections," said Tiwari. He also questioned the credibility of the report, which has indicted Amarinder in a land scam.

The AICC General Secretary, who started his campaign for the coming Lok Sabha elections, also listed the achievement of the UPA government. He added that NSG waiver was a big achievement for the country.

Heading: Illicit relations: Two commit suicide - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab Assembly today passed four Bills, including the Punjab Official Language (Amendment Bill, 2008), which makes Punjabi compulsory in all the schools of the state till Class X. Works in all government offices and subordinate courts will also be carried out in Punjabi.

As per the Bill, strict disciplinary action would be taken against the defaulters.

Another Bill on Punjabi language, Punjab Learning of Punjabi and Other Languages, was also passed. This law would ensure that all students from Classes I 10 X study Punjabi from April 2009 session, besides Hindi and English.

Two Bills on VAT amendments were also passed.

Pension through panchayats

Pensions are now being disbursed through gram panchayats, and the payments up to June last have been made. However, there is no proposal to disburse them through post offices. This was stated by Chaudhary Swarna Ram, Technical Education and Social Security Minister, in reply to a question by Makhan Singh.

Illness fund

The Punjab Government has received Rs 45.25 lakh from the Centre till March 2008 under the State Illness Fund for poor patients. This fund was operational during this fiscal, as there was no stipulation by the Centre on spending the money in the financial year in which it was received. Hence, the question of taking action against anybody on fund lapse does not arise. This was stated by Punjab Health Minister Laxmi Kanta Chawla in reply to a question by Ajit Inder Mofar.

Fraud case

Barnala SP (Headquarter) has been inquiring the complaint of fraud by residents of Ram Nagar Chhannan village in Barnala, in which they have alleged that a fake project report was submitted by Punjab Medicinal Plants Board to get subsidy. The bank documents and revenue records were also being examined. This was stated by Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal in reply to a question by Harchant Kaur.

Heading: Amritsar scam tip of iceberg: Sukhbir - Indian Express
Content:
Illicit relations between two married persons ended in suicide. Balour Singh (29), a resident of Kheeva Kalan village and father of two, allegedly had relations with Shinder Kaur (30), wife of Najar Singh and a mother of three.

Balour and Shinder took this extreme step after their families came to know about their relationship.

According to Shinder's family, she had gone out to work in the fields on Tuesday, but did not return till late evening. Late in the night, both Najar and Shinder Kaur returned after consuming some poisonous substance. Seeing their condition, their parents rushed them to a hospital, but they died on the way. The police have treated the case under Section 174 of the CrPC and handed over the bodies to their families after post-mortem.

Heading: Hopes of Kirpal’s family grow dimmer - Indian Express
Content: SAD president Sukhbir Badal on Wednesday lashed out at former CM Capt Amarinder Singh, accusing him of "creating a history of scams". Sukhbir, who was in the district for inaugurating and laying foundation stones of various project, said the Amritsar scam was just "tip of the iceberg" and there were "more scams" by Amarinder that would be exposed. The projects set in motion by Sukhbir included five reverse osmosis (RO) systems in Nathana constituency, irrigation distributary strengthening project, construction of two school building under a Nabard scheme and strengthening of water channels.  	—ENS

Heading: Lyrics of life - Indian Express
Content:
Hopes of release of Kirpal Singh, an Indian prisoner on death row in Pakistan, have become dimmer as the government in the neighbouring country has reportedly shifted him to the punishment cell.

Kirpal is alleged to have developed health problems in the new cell and has asked his kin to contact the Indian embassy in Pakistan.

Ashok Kumar, nephew of Kirpal, said his uncle's friends in Pakistan, who have been recently released from jail, contacted his family in Mustafabad Saidan in Gurdaspur and told them about his condition.

Besides contacting the embassy, the family also plans to approach the Pakistan government.

Ashwini Kumar, another nephew of Kirpal, said the news had come as a shock for the family, whose hopes had risen after Pak rights activist Ansar Burney had spotted him in the jail and promised to help him.

Ashwini said his uncle was the only Indian in the punishment cell, also known as the 'kasur cell', where prisoners who had committed serious crimes were lodged. "I wonder why my uncle has been shifted there," he said.

Gurmeet Singh Sandhu, who is working for the release of Kirpal, said, "He has asked us to contact the embassy, but so far we have had no luck."

He said Kirpal had said that he was not allowed to move around freely in the new cell. "He has also complained of unhygienic food being served there. He also said that items of daily use, such as utensils and bedding, were not being provided," Sandhu said.

Saying that the family would approach the authorities in Pakistan, Sandhu said they hoped a favourable response as this government had initiated the move for annulment of death sentences of Indians in Pak jails.

Kirpal Singh, who "inadvertently" crossed over to Pakistan in 1991, was convicted by an anti-terrorism court in Lahore. A Pak court had given him a clean chit in cases of bomb blast and destruction of property in 2005, but had upheld the case of spying.

Heading: Shrub Culture - Indian Express
Content:
After soaring the skies, Wing Commander BS Flower attempts to touch the heart

Every song should have a body and soul of its own. Whenever you hear one, it must make you feel that you have experienced an episode," states Wing Commander B S Flower (Retd). A script-writer and poet, words whether written or sung have always had a place in Flower's life since his student days. As he puts it, "Nobody becomes a poet, either you are one or you are not!" His first collection of Punjabi poetry 'Naamgeer' was published in '75 and a decade later, 'Phullan di Waad'. And in his latest book 'Dard hi Ban-de Geet Suhane', Flower surfs human emotions and relations. "I was serious about writing. Though being in the Air Force I had less time, I never stopped writing." The year '95 saw Flower pen a film script and Hindi songs. "I did get good offers but could not manage travelling frequently to Mumbai,so that took a backseat."

In 2002, Flower wrote a play Aatish for Punjabi Arts Association in Canada. Based on the lives of Punjabis settled in Canada, the play was a hit. "But what became more popular were the songs of the play. Everybody commented on them, be it appreciation or criticism. It was then that the transition from poetry to lyrics happened," recalls Flower. On returning to India, he got in touch with music director Kanwar Iqbal Singh. "He suggested that I write a book. So here I am, with my first collection of songs," giving shape to the universal and profound emotion of pain. He explains quoting Shelley, "Our sweetest songs are those that tell of saddest thought," adding that this one emotion has charmed him since he began writing.

"Printed poetry as opposed to songs sung should be complete poetry in itself, there is no background music to create the effect. So it has to come straight from the heart," and share a great connection with the reader's heart. Kanwar Iqbal guided the song-writer to create his signature style. "So instead of writing only light-hearted songs I chose to reflect the denser mood portraying it with sensitivity," he signs off.

Heading: SC/ST panel pulls up govt, seeks wholesale changes - Indian Express
Content:
Most of the shrubs bear flowers almost all through the year but when it is their actual time of flowering, they put forth ultimate effect. Ixora in the accompanying picture is an excellent specimen shrub that bears flowers in various hues viz. white, yellow, orange, pink red, golden yellow and crimson. The plant is very hardy. It responds to addition of super phosphate in case where you find almost all the leaves turning yellow.

I obtained one Baramasi Lemon plant which the nurseryman said would be seedless. I find it is not totally so and at times contains two or three seeds. Is there any variety that is totally seedless?
Parminder Kaur, Mohali
When we call seedless then two or three soft seeds (aborted) included come under the 'seedless' category. However, there are totally seedless types too but that you will have to find out and a plant made from such a plant will be true to type.

Please tell me the name of a few flowering plants with red/orange flowers. These could be climbers, shrubs or even trees.
Maninder, Panchkula
The plants with flowers of such hues are Gulmohur, Chorisia, (trees), Golden Shower, and Tecoma campesis (climbers) and Ixora, Hibiscus and Gulmohari (Shrubs)

The new growth in my mango plant is sagging (drying) at many terminals. What could be the reason?
Tarlochan Singh, Chandigarh
The culprit is the stem borer. The young caterpillars bore into the new shoots, drying these by making tunnels. Spray thiodan @ 1.5 milliliter to a liter of water now and repeat after a fortnight.

Please tell me about some good early fruiting peaches. I want to plant them during this season.
Raminder Singh, Panchkula
By 'this season', do you mean this monsoon? No, this is not the time. Peach is a deciduous plant and sheds leaves during winter and that is the time fro planting them. You can plant Prabhat, Partap, Earli Grande etceteras. These are early ripening cultivars.

Heading: Cong will win, says minister - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the Congress and the BJP fought over the issue of unauthorised colonies in the Delhi Assembly today, the Committee on Welfare of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Castes pulled up the government "after serious deliberations" on various issues.

The committee, set up under the chairmanship of legislator Surender Kumar, has recommended raising the outlay for the benefit of SC colonies, the allocation for which is Rs 22 crore for the financial year 2008-09. A report by the nine-member committee was presented in the Assembly today.

The committee has recommended urgent action against problems like electrification of localities, scholarships to students from these communities, and loan schemes for students pursuing higher studies.

Surender Kumar, chairman of the committee, told Newsline: "We visited villages and inquired among the people from these communities on the matter and found they are facing serious problems."

The electrification of villages and provision of 50 per cent subsidies has not been implemented till date. Expressing "grave concern" that such a vital scheme was "never brought to the notice of the committee members", the panel has recommended that the SC/ST department take up the matter and there be no "interference by the development department in this case". Questions have also been raised over the percentage of marks fixed for students from the SC/ST communities. The committee has highlighted the fact that scholarships are issued to students from OBC and minority communities with no limit on percentage of marks, whereas for the SC/ST communities, there is a condition of 55-60 per cent marks. It has recommended that this be "immediately scrapped" and students be given scholarships on the same pattern.

Raising the issue of construction of hostels for students from these communities, the committee said it found that hostel facilities are available to just 100 such students in Delhi. It has recommended the construction of hostels in all seven Lok Sabha constituencies of Delhi and that "priority be accorded to SC/ST students of Delhi while allotting hostel facilities".

Highlighting the fact that only two students have been benefited under the scheme, it has also recommended that the condition of a "guarantor" for allotment of loans to students pursuing higher studies be "removed with immediate effect", as it "complicates the process", which needs to be "simplified" and "made transparent".

Heading: MCD hails end of demolition watch panel - Indian Express
Content:
Weeks before the Assembly elections, Urban Development Minister Rajkumar Chauhan declared that the Congress government would win the upcoming elections due to its decision of regularising the 1,639 unauthorised colonies in the Capital.

Chauhan was replying to the allegations made by the Opposition calling the government's move to distribute provisional authorisation certificates to the colonies a poll stunt. "It was due to the co-ordination between the Centre and Congress government in the Capital that 40 lakh residents of 1,639 colonies will now have a better standard of living," said Chauhan. The minister also praised his party on the nuclear deal clinched by the UPA government, saying the low-cost housing scheme for the poor will prove to be Congress's ticket to victory in the elections. The heated debate on unauthorised colonies lasted nearly three hours. Chauhan added that the government has allotted Rs 1,043 crore for development in the year 2008-2009, out of which Rs 439.25 crore has been released till September. He said the government will be spending Rs 2,800 crore in the next five years for the regularization process. "It took the government ten years to take such a tiny step, and a permanent regularisation certificate still remains a far cry," said leader of Opposition Jadgish Mukhi. BJP MLA Vijay Jolly said that despite government's claims of pumping money for the development of the unauthorised colonies, most areas still face powercuts and water shortage that last for 24 to 30 hours at a stretch. He also alleged that a majority of these colonies do not have proper roads, streetlighting, sewer facilities and other basic amenities.

Heading: Monsoon session: BJP says Cong govt ‘a complete failure’ - Indian Express
Content:
Senior municipal officials welcomed the High Court's decision today to dissolve the monitoring committee it appointed to oversee demolition of unauthorised construction and encroachments in the Capital.

The Bench, in turn, directed MCD to set up a nodal committee comprising its senior officers; the committee will have a six-month duration. But the civic body wants to make the most of the stipulated period by developing a transparent and effective system to check unauthorised construction, Mayor Arti Mehra said. "The system of booking unauthorised construction will be computerised and made online," she said. Mehra said the civic body would also break up the functions of detection of such illegal construction and encroachment, and their demolition.

"The Building Department will be strengthened, and control rooms will be equipped with required machinery," she said. Building plans will now get online sanctions and the panel will also issue completion certificates, it was announced. "The MCD would suggest a plan that aims to strengthen self-corrective measures," Leader of the House Subhash Arya said. "We were capable of developing a foolproof and refurbished mechanism to check unauthorised construction. There was no need for these institutions (monitoring committees)."

In the Standing Committee meeting the MCD today proposed to move the Supreme Court to dispense with its committee that oversees de-sealing. "Such committees are of no help to MCD," municipal councillor Sarita Chaudhary said. "Instead, they cause confusion."

Heading: Gurgaon: NRI held with 5 kg heroin - Indian Express
Content:
The monsoon session of the Delhi Assembly began on Wednesday with BJP leaders creating a ruckus and declaring the Sheila Dikshit government a "complete failure" over the last ten years.

While farmers of the Bharatiya Kisan Union (BKU) clashed with police near the Vidhan Sabha in the morning, Assembly members from the BJP accused the government of corruption and misleading the general public over price rise, power distribution and even the Indo-US nuclear deal being carried out by the present government.

According to Delhi BJP chief Dr Harshvardhan, despite repeated claims of the government of changing the situation, the city has been witnessing prolonged powercuts that last for an entire day.

"There have been prolonged powercuts in unauthorised colonies like Sangam Vihar, despite the government claiming to have initiated the process of regularisation for these colonies. This is just election politics," BJP MLA Vijay Jolly added.

Power Minister AK Walia, countering the allegations, said that load-shedding is occasionally imperative to prevent tripping of the Northern Grid. However, the percentage of load-shedding is barely 0.38 per cent of the power demand in the Capital, he added.

The BJP Opposition, led by Jagdish Mukhey, took on the government on the issue of price rise in the Capital and said that all of Congress' policies were "against the benefit of the common man".

Heading: NZ governor general visits JNU - Indian Express
Content:
An NRI from Canada has been arrested from Gurgaon by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) on charges of possessing over 5 kg of contraband heroin.

Sixty-four-year-old Harish Joshi was arrested on Tuesday under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act (possessing and smuggling of narcotic drugs), DRI officials said.

Sources said he was initially picked up by the agency on Monday evening from outside the posh DLF Phase V in Gurgaon along with an accomplice and a large suitcase.

"On opening the suitcase, we found 5.2 kg of heroin," an official said. According to DRI officials, Joshi, chairman of the Grimus group of companies, which run several education institutes across the world, has admitted his involvement in the narcotic trade for quite some time to the agency.

"He gave us a statement under Section 180 of the Customs Act which is admissible in the court. He was put under arrest on Tuesday and was immediately produced before the Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate who has remanded him in 14 days' judicial custody," a senior DRI official said.

Joshi was under surveillance for several days after agency was tipped off about the fact that he was to deliver the drugs to his accomplice in Canada.

Heading: Accused of graft, cop’s third bail plea rejected - Indian Express
Content:
Anand Satyanand, the Governor General of New Zealand, who was applauded for supporting a clean waiver by the Nuclear Suppliers' Group (NSG) for New Delhi, on Wednesday, also received immense appreciation from teachers and students at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU).

On a maiden, one-week visit to India, the leader of Indian origin made sure he did not miss visiting one of the most reputed universities of India. Invited by the School of International Studies, Satyanand met with students and teachers. His wife accompanied him.

In his address, Satyanand spoke about the evolution of New Zealand, its multi-ethnic community, and strengths in the field of agriculture and capacity in the field of information technology.

Speaking on contemporary issues, Satyanand condemned terrorism: "It has become a serious concern in the world. I pay my tributes to the innocent victims of terrorism in Bangalore and Ahmedabad in India."

The leader also spoke about the need for developing collaboration between universities of the two countries. "In future, we should have academic exchanges between the two countries," he said to the audience in the Seminar room of the Administrative Block. Satyanand was then introduced to the high dignitaries of the university and was given a brief overview of the campus.

Professor Ramadhikari Kumar, Rector II of JNU, who had received Satyanand, later told Newsline: "It was a goodwill visit by Satyanand that also proved that India is getting greater attention from people around the world."

Satyanand was born in an Indo-Fijian and Anglo-Indian family and was raised in Auckland. In 2006, he became the first Asian to become the Governor General of New Zealand. He is married and has three children.

JNU students present demands to UGC
Students of JNU belonging to the National Students Union of India took out a protest march from UGC to ITO on Wednesday. They demanded that Rs 2,500 be given as merit-cum-marks scholarship to BA and MA students; an equivalent of the Rajiv Gandhi Fellowship to PhD students; the release of Rs 8,000 and 5,000 as fellowships to PhD and MPhil students; the extension of the Maulana Azad Fellowship to college students; and the urgent sanction of a special grant to JNU for new hostels. Bharat Kumar, NSUI leader, said UGC Chairman agreed to first two demands.

Heading: Rahul turns up the heat - Indian Express
Content:
Reluctance to produce a mobile phone which is touted as a vital link for unearthing the role of Delhi Police officers in extorting nearly Rs 20 lakh from an aide of kidney racket kingpin Dr Amit Kumar, has cost an accused constable his bail yet again. Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (ACMM) A K Kuhar denied Constable Naresh Kumar bail —his third application— during a recent hearing after an earlier order was cited whereby Kumar's plea was rejected on the ground that he had refrained from co-operating with the investigators. After dismissal of the first bail application, Kumar had approached a sessions court in July in pursuit of reprieve. However, none was in store as the court was apprised of the fact that the constable had not helped in the recovery of his mobile phone.

As per the Economic Offence Wing (EOW) sleuths, during interrogation, the constable refused to divulge any details about his phone, and told them he might have destroyed it, the cops informed the sessions judge. The court had, thus, thrown out his application, keeping this in mind. The constable had moved his third bail plea before the ACMM, who read out from the earlier decision of the sessions court in the matter and noted that "there was no change in the circumstances" which could warrant him the relief.

Heading: Aditya’s moment of brilliance gives hosts Delhi upset win - Indian Express
Content:
Ganapathy takes the first-round lead at his happy hunting ground

The Golden Greens golf course sits right at the edge of the Aravallis, but the man who seems to own this picturesque piece of property comes from south of the Vindhyas.

Rahul Ganpathy had already won a title here this year — the Solaris Chemtech Open — and so knew this beautiful but punishing course inside out. Aware that there was no room for error here, the Mysore lad played a flawless five-under 67 on Wednesday to take the sole lead after Round One of the Rs 30 lakh AIS Open.

Driving the ball well, Ganapathy consistently managed to find fairways and unerring putting saw him holing five birdies. At the end of the day, he was a deserving leader, being the only one in the 126-strong field to have returned a blemish-free card.

"I couldn't have asked for a better start," said Ganapthy, who played in the morning session. "I was hitting the ball very well and my putting was great too."

Those who saw him sinking a monster of a putt on the par-four 12th hole won't disagree. After he had landed his approach shot some 25 feet off the pin, he sensationally holed it for his birdie No. four. "That was incredible. One of the longest putts I have made in the last three-four weeks."

So what was his strategy today? "On this course it is simple: keep the ball in regulation and birdies will come along," said the 29-year-old.

Putting the round right
But Digvijay Singh, a stroke off the pace at four-under and sharing the tied second spot with Feroz Ali Mollah and Ashok Kumar, would beg to differ. Singh, who has had a fairly rewarding season at the domestic PGTI and some decent outings at the European and Asian tours, was hitting the ball all over the place, yet he hit half a dozen birdies.

"Well, I would say my putter rescued me. I was hitting here, there everywhere. Thankfully, my putter was hot today. I hope it remains the same tomorrow," Singh said.

It was the other way round with Gaurav Ghei, who was in the same group with Singh. The veteran golfer drove the ball well, but struggled with his short game. He mixed five birdies with three bogeys for his round of 70 to assume the tied-sixth position.

"Digvijay's hitting and my putting, and it would have been seven-over for the day," said Ghei. He might have been cracking a joke, but was damn serious in his intent and went straight to the practice green after signing his card. "My strategy for tomorrow is clear. I would like to go out and try stay in contention for the weekend."

Among others, Bangalore's Gaurav Diwan was placed fifth after playing a round of three-under 69.

Meanwhile, the players voiced their concern over the condition of the greens. Surprisingly, even Ganapathy was one of them. "The course isn't playing well. The greens are tough and that makes putting difficult."

Ghei concurred but placed the blame on the weather. "The greens are not that good but that is probably due to the unusually heavy rains this season."
