Heading: Delhi test ground for big matchExpress News Service - Indian Express
Content:
They called him graceful, superb, sublime, till the eulogies seemed almost exaggerated. David Beckham's emergence as the most popular English footballer has had much to do with his abilities as a free-kick specialist.

Delhi's Aditya Lal was just a kid when the former Manchester United skipper was gaining ground in world football, but at the Ambedkar Stadium on Wednesday, Lal did something that would have done any footballer proud — a scorcher of a strike from about 10 yards ahead of the centreline, that sneaked through the right corner of the post. The free kick, found its way past the Assam goalkeeper with a sharp dip at culmination.

Clamour wasn't the immediate aftermath, but a resounding silence. However, Lal's way of describing it was simply, "the best goal I have ever scored," something the centre back doesn't get too many chances to.

More importantly, it was the goal that helped the Delhi team pull off an upset 2-1 victory over heavyweights Assam in their first match of the quarter-final league of the Subroto Cup.

Lal has another Manchester United connection. The Vasant Valley student had attended the Manchester United Soccer School in August 2007. His one-month stint there was more about tactical details, but the real experience was meeting the Red Devils. "Meeting the Manchester United team was a huge experience. Even though I didn't get to talk to them much, watching them from close was a dream come true. I managed to ask (Nemanja) Vidic a few questions on fitness," Lal says.

The Serb's advice on spending time in the gym looked to have worked for the 15-year-old as well as the team, as they seemed to be physically overpowering the Assam players.

Disregarding stereotypes
The lessons on tactics back in Old Trafford were devoted to the short one-touch passes and the formation of the forward line. "Indian players play a lot of long, aerial passes, but in England we concentrated on practicing one-touch passes. We were told that the forward line should always advance creating a triangle between the players and that's exactly what we did today," he says.

It's certainly early days for the centre back, but he already seems to have begun disregarding traditional stereotypes. So much so that he readily rejects coach Pradyut Gogoi's view that none of the players here will continue with the game after a certain point as they play football just for fun and can't compromise with academics.

"I'll certainly continue playing football and my parents have been very supportive. In fact they were the ones who arranged the Manchester United trip," he insists.

Heading: AITA to organise junior camp with eye on 2010 - Indian Express
Content:
The 40-over-a side practice match at Ferozeshah Kotla had some positive signs for the Delhi team gearing up for the Mohammad Nissar Trophy but Wednesday's game was more about testing the surface rather than scanning the players in the middle. And the newly-laid wicket seems to have come out as a disappointment to the players.

The four-day game against Pakistan's Sui Northern Gas Pipeline Limited will be played on the same pitch where the bowlers struggled to extract any bounce or lateral movement on Wednesday, even as the batsmen looked uncomfortable with the ball not coming up to them uniformly.

The wicket is expected to settle down, but it's unlikely to change its nature — which means that Delhi, despite boasting a strong fast-bowling arsenal in Ishant Sharma, Ashish Nehra, Pradeep Sangwan and Amit Bhandari, will probably be looking at another result decided by the batsmen.

"It's too early to say how the wicket will play for the (September 15) match. This is the first game on this surface and we wanted to test its bounce. It doesn't have the carry or the grass cover that will help fast bowlers, but it should improve with rolling. On the flip side, when our bowlers bowl in tandem, the wicket will look much different. It's about the quality of the bowlers as well," said Vijay Dahiya, coach of the Delhi team.

Nehra bowled a sharp quick spell with the new ball and Bhandari troubled the batsmen on a couple of occasions, but there was little else to mention about the bowling department. Virender Sehwag watched the match from the sidelines, recuperating from an ankle injury, while Pradeep Sangwan was unwell. Aakash Chopra continued his blazing form of last season with an unbeaten 70 with 12 boundaries from 116 balls, while Mithun Manhas, Rahul Diwan, Punit Bisht and Mayank Tehlan had decent stints in the middle.

Heading: The Impressionist - Indian Express
Content:
AS 19-year-old Prajnesh Gunneswaran and his even younger opponent Ronak Manuja exchanged fierce groundstrokes in a bid for a quarter-final spot, perhaps they were unaware they were being observed with a keen eye on the 2010 Commonwealth Games. The chairman of the tennis programme for the Delhi Games, Jaidip Mukerjea was taking in the action at the $15,000 ITF Futures tournament in the Capital, and he appeared particularly interested in this second round match.

"We will organise a special camp of sorts next week where we will work on certain players for 2010. Twenty boys and twenty girls have been selected, mostly under-20 players. Of course, we will have to adjust their personal schedules accordingly, but it should fall into place. We will get a coach from abroad as well."

On court, Gunneswaran simply continued his excellent display from Tuesday's victory over fifth seed Ashutosh Singh, and broke Manuja in the first game of the match for a great start. A few cracking returns left his 17-year-old opponent reeling, and there was little the youngster could do but shake his head. The left-handed Chennai player, who spends most of his time on the clay courts of Spain, continued giving Manuja trouble on his serve, but he managed to hold on. A single break of serve, though, was all Gunneswaran needed to wrap up the first set 6-4.

A similar strong beginning in the second set brought the match to a swift end, breaks in the first and fifth games giving him a 6-4, 6-2 victory and a last-eight berth. Up next for Prajnesh is a tough proposition, second seed Yucihi Sugita of Japan, who defeated qualifier Nikunj Siwach 6-3, 6-3 to make the quarter-finals. VM Ranjeet, who had upset third seed Korean Hyun Woo Nam on Tuesday, retired from his match against PC Vignesh with the score at 7-6 (3), 4-6, 3-2.

Fourth seed Sunil Kumar Sipaeya squuezed past compatriot Tushar Liberhan in three sets, 3-6, 6-4, 6-4. Vishnu Vardhan could not overturn the challenge of top seed Peter Gojowczyk, losing his match 6-4, 6-4. Rupesh Roy defeated Abhijeet Tiwari 6-3, 6-4 to make his way into the last eight. Aqeel Khan and Hsin-han Lee also won their matches on Wednesday.

Heading: A Novel Affair - Indian Express
Content:
Sabyasachi Mukherjee on his designs for the junior Bachchans and his New York Fashion Week collection

For someone who has made a successful career in clothes in earthy tones, Sabyasachi Mukherjee has done an about turn, and says he is in love with unabashedly bright colours all over again. And the man responsible for it is none other than the post-Impressionist French artist Paul Gauguin. "There's a joie de vivre in his works that is infectious. I have always admired him, particularly his self-portraits and works like The Yellow Christ. I finally decided to decode it into ensembles. I have used his paintings as a subtext and worked on the colour palette accordingly," says the Kolkata-based designer, who will showcase the collection on September 12 at The Salon at Bryant Park at the Mercedes Benz New York Fashion Week.

There are, of course, other influences, equally Bohemian, on the 34 garments that he will show at his third appearance in New York. From the 20th century German Expressionist artist Emil Nolde to French balladeer Edith Piaf, Mukherjee has taken the very best from his idols and translated them on to his clothes. There are handprinted silks in Art Deco motifs, discharge printed chiffons, bomber jackets with multi-coloured textured embroidery among other things. "In my three seasons in New York, this is my best collection yet. Even though as designers our concept of clothes is to change with the season, I believe each garment should have something more to take it forward beyond the stipulated time frame. I want my clients to feel free and happy to be themselves," he says.

It's probably one of the reasons why Mukherjee's loyal followers, particularly those in Bollywood, can never get enough of him. Post the fashion week, his little black book is choc-a-bloc with assignments, chief among which is director Mani Ratnam's ambitious bilingual project, Ravan, a re-interpretation of the Ramayana. The film, slated to go on the floors by the end of the month has Ahbishek Bachchan and Aishwarya Rai playing Ram and Sita, while Govinda plays Hanuman and south Indian actor Vikram gets into

Ravan's skin. Even rookie actor Ranbir Kapoor has been roped in for a role in the epic. Mukherjee is slated to style the look of the magnum opus, post his fashion week commitments. "I enjoy doing films because it gives me ample scope to break the monotony of working linearly on collections. Working with Mani Ratnam is a challenge in itself. When you have people like Abhishek and Ash, who have an inherent sense of style, it becomes all the more interesting," he says. Watch out for the next milestone.

Heading: Double Delight - Indian Express
Content:
Vikram Bhatt is upbeat about his next horror film and his new real-life role — of a first-time author

Horror movies are his forte, claims director Vikram Bhatt, whose period supernatural film 1920 hits the screens tomorrow. "1920 isn't just a horror film. It's a classic that has a fantasy mix of the horse cart, the castle and a great story," he says. His last hit was six years ago — Raaz, a supernatural thriller — and he has his fingers crossed about the new venture.

The next few months will also see Bhatt don another hat, of an author. His debut book Summer Of Frost is a love story, with elements drawn from his own life. "It's a story of second chance at one's first love. It's not entirely fiction, it has a lot of personal feelings involved from my own life," he says.

Having written a number of regular columns in the past, Bhatt has always had a passion for the pen. But, while the rest of the film industry began blogging with gusto, he took to the pen. "I would love to have the book launch on my birthday in January, though I'm not sure if that would be possible," he smiles.

For now, it's 1920 on his mind. The film has been shot at Allerton castle in England, one of the 10 most haunted castles in the world. "Funnily, I didn't know that it was haunted until we started shooting. But I fell in love with the place, it was exactly how I had imagined it to be," he says.

While 1920 stars newbies Rajneesh Duggal and Ada Sharman, Bhatt adds that Aditya Narayan, son of singer Udit Narayan, will debut in his next film Shapit— which goes on floors next year. "I don't have a fixation with newcomers," he clarifies quickly. "The industry has only seven or eight selling actors who obviously can't be cast in every movie. I'm always looking for new talent and there is potential in these new actors."

Interestingly, Bhatt does not believe in auditioning any of the newcomers.

1920 has turned out to be an extremely expensive film, says the director. "I haven't done my accounts as yet but there's certainly a lot of money involved and the costs are steadily climbing," he says. "But then, good cinema doesn't come cheap."

Heading: Call centre woman murdered in S Delhi flat - Indian Express
Content:
These identical twins give classical music a global twist in their new album

These identical twins may dress alike and have the same obsession with classical music, but when it comes to their favourite instruments, they love to differ — Fateh Ali opts for the sitar while Murad Ali plays the sarangi. The brothers, however, have come together to create a unique jugalbandi of sitar and sarangi in their album, Convergence, released by Shubha Mudgal at the India Habitat Centre on Tuesday.

Sons of Ustad Ghulam Sabir Khan of the Moradabad gharana of sarangi players, Murad and Fateh have grown up amid music. "Creating a fusion album without any confusion was the sole aim of this album," says Fateh.

Convergence, he adds, also has influences like lounge, rock, jazz and latin music. But the highlight is the magic of the sitar and sarangi playing together, the pluck and bow blending in sweet harmony.

"World music is the order of the day, which is wonderful as long as you retain the classical base," says Murad, who plays the fretless sarangi, which is not common among youngsters today.

The brothers presented one of the tracks of the album — Infinity, in which the strains combine to create a sense of tranquility. Fateh also gave a technically intricate solo performance with raag jhanjoti by way of an elaborate alaap, jod and jhala.

The other tracks are Déjà vu, Colour of Love, Temptations and Saturday Night in Delhi. "The best thing about the album is that every instrument has a temperament of its own,"said Mudgal.

Heading: Apex court to Ansal brothers: Surrender by 4 pm, today - Indian Express
Content:
A 25-year-old call centre employee was found strangled at her paying guest accommodation in Gautam Nagar, South Delhi, late Wednesday afternoon. The victim, Shalini Saxena, was strangulated with the wire of her cellphone (Nokia) charger.

The police said her clothes were in disarray, which leads them to suspect the involvement of a "love angle". Deputy Commissioner of Police (South) H G S Dhaliwal, however, said there were no injuries indicating any struggle or sexual assault.

The police said Saxena was alone at the PG when the incident occurred — her roommate found the body on her return home at 4.45 pm. The room, police officials said, was not locked: the roommate walked straight in, before running out screaming in fright. A bystander then called the police.

The area houses many students and working women, who stay primarily as paying guests.

"The entry into the room was friendly and we suspect someone who knew the victim murdered her," DCP Dhaliwal said. "A case of murder has been registered as of now; the matter is being probed further."

He said the police have not detained or arrested anyone till now.

A senior officer said, "We have recovered some letters from her room and are scanning them. We are also looking at all recent phone calls and text messages sent out and received on her phone."

According to the police, Saxena worked at a call centre in Gurgaon and had been staying as a paying guest at E-69/1, Gautam Nagar, for the past six months. The PG accommodation is on the first floor, and three girls each stay in the two rooms.

Newsline tried to contact the owner — identified only as one "Mrs Sharma" — but found her mobile phone switched off.

One of Saxena's roommates, who did not want to be named, returned home at 8.45 pm and was "shocked numb" to find the crowd of onlookers, police and media personnel around the house. When told that Saxena had been murdered, she said, amid sobs, "I met and spoke to her yesterday. I stay in the room next to hers but we shared the same PG in this area before we moved in here.

"I didn't know her very well, though."

Saxena's roommate Lily said she kept to herself most of the time. "She was very shy but I don't know much about her personal life," Lily said.

Police officials said Saxena came from Saharanpur, Uttar Pradesh. Her father Vijay Saxena is a bank employee there and has been informed. The body has been transferred to AIIMS mortuary and a postmortem would be conducted after her family members arrive.

Heading: Artists cry foul at city art academy’s brush with chaos - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday cancelled the bail granted to Sushil and Gopal Ansal earlier this year and ordered them to surrender before the additional chief metropolitan magistrate at the Patiala House district court by 4 pm on Thursday.

The apex court's Bench of Justices B N Agarwal and G S Singhvi said the brothers did not deserve bail, specially because of their conduct during the long trial. During this time they had been accused of tampering with evidence and judicial records — a charge being examined by a lower court.

The court said: "Tampering with judicial records is a crime worse than murder or dacoity. We are of the view that it was not a fit case for the High Court to have granted bail."

The court also observed that the conduct of an accused is crucial while considering bail, even if his offence was bailable.

The Ansal brothers had been convicted under Section 304 A — causing death due to a rash and negligent act — and sentenced to two years in jail.

A group of eminent lawyers, led by senior counsel Fali S Nariman, presented the brothers' case for over five hours on Wednesday but could not dissuade the court from ordering their arrest.

The apex court, in fact, had ordered the immediate arrest of the real estate tycoons and two managers of the theatre — also out on bail — but Nariman managed a day's respite. The other two, Ajit Chowdhary and Nirmal Singh Chopra, had been charged under Section 304 IPC (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) and sentenced for seven years.

The court also rejected the bail plea of former Delhi Vidyut Board (DVB) employee B N Satija and the theatre's gatekeeper Manmohan Unniyal, charged similarly.

The apex court on Wednesday refrained from giving a detailed order because that would have "prejudiced" the other related cases the accused were fighting. But it asked the chief justice of the High Court to ensure that these cases were heard daily. "The concerned judge will make all efforts to deliver the judgment as expeditiously as possible," the apex court ordered.

The Bench was hearing an appeal filed by the Association of Victims of the Uphaar Tragedy (AVUT). The organisation had challenged the bail granted to the Ansal brothers and the other two.

On November 20 last year, a trial court had convicted the real estate tycoons and 10 others for the horrific fire in 1997 at the Uphaar theatre that killed 59 people. Owners of the theatre, the Ansal brothers, were sentenced to two years in November, 2007 but managed bail in January this year.

The two managers were also given bail.

On tampering of evidence, the police had said some of these documents included a police memo with details of recoveries made immediately after the fire at the cinema hall, and also records with the fire services, detailing the repair of a transformer installed inside Uphaar.

"When the trial court verdict came eight months ago, I felt they (Ansals) were walking free. Today I feel vindicated that justice has finally been done. It was for this moment that I have waited for 11 years. It was for this that I have not missed a single day in court."
- Neelam Krishnamurti, whose two children died in Uphaar fire

Heading: Sultan ghari’s tomb: A father’s tribute - Indian Express
Content:
Established in 1954 to promote art, Lalit Kala Akademi is often associated by artists with memories of grand exhibitions and hours spent in the library, sifting through chronicles on art. But voices of distrust are echoing now, with several artists questioning the way of its functioning in the absence of a general council and executive board, both dissolved at the end of their five-year term in December 2007. 

"There is no transparency in its working. High-ranking officials take decisions on their own, as there is no general council or executive," says artist K R Subbanna, elected as member of the general council by artists this January.

While the state akademis and governments have nominated representatives in the general council, the Department of Culture is required to select 10 candidates as members of the body from a list of 30 already submitted by selected members of the general council. This will be followed by selection of eminent artists, who will be part of the council.

Subbanna says the list of 30 recommended names was sent to the Culture ministry in June but the department has not yet responded. "The formation of the general council and executive board should ideally not take more than four months but the procedure seems to be taking almost a year."

Ashok Vajpeyi, appointed the Akademi's chairman in April, calls it procedural delay. "The artists need to be patient," he says. "The list is with the ministry and a meeting will be called and rest of the members selected as soon as we get a response. The executive board will be formed after that."

He says the Akademi's constitution "allows me to take decisions, which will be put for approval before the general council and the executive once it is complete".

But artists claim the problems date back to the time before Vajpeyi took over as chairman. Artist M K Puri, a member of the executive board in its last session, says, "The constitution requires every decision to be taken in a democratic manner but over the years the Akademi has become a bureaucratic institution. For instance, as executive board members we had only passed a proposal for renovation of galleries in Rabindra Bhawan but the management is revamping the administrative block as well."

A select group of artists had sent a letter to Tourism and Culture minister Ambika Soni in October 2007, highlighting "irregularities in working of the Akademi". But, "we haven't received any response yet," says artist Mukul Panwar, one of the signatories.

In 1990, artists like Manjit Bawa and G R Santosh had reportedly written a letter to then Prime Minister V P Singh regarding misuse of funds and irregularities concerning appointment of officials at several posts.

In 2005, another set of artists had written to Union Urban Development minister Jaipal Reddy, asking him to set up an independent committee to investigate functioning of the Akademi.

Heading: Rail trail - Indian Express
Content:
Students of DAV Public School, Vasant Kunj, take part in the heritage walk at Sultan Ghari's Tomb conducted by The Indian Express in association with INTACH and ASI

An Express Schools' initiative
Quest is a project conducted by The Indian Express in schools in and around Delhi. It covers more than 50 schools in Delhi and NCR.

Quest aims at stirring awareness and opinions. Today, when all that children see are shopping malls and cineplexes, we at The Indian Express want to show a completely different picture of this city to them. Delhi has changed beyond nostalgia and recognition since Independence. How many of these kids know of the 'Seven Cities' of Delhi or the stories of the pigeon fliers of Old Delhi?

The idea behind such an activity is to create awareness about the various structures and monuments that the students do not know about. This is a specially designed programme, which will help the students appreciate the rich culture and background of this city. In association with INTACH and ASI, this is a small effort on our behalf to depict a phase of our national life and the decay of a whole culture, a particular mode of thought and living. The visit is followed by the students sending in articles, pictures, poems, paintings, and collages to express their experiences about the heritage walk.

A trip to Sultan Ghari's tomb
Sultan Ghari's Tomb is located on the Andheria More Road near Mahipalpur, just opposite C-9, Vasant Kunj. It was built by Iltutmish for his son Nasiruddin Mahmud. His tomb is an enclosure in an octagonal underground pit. It was very dark inside. Iltutmish built the tomb and it was restructured by Feroz Shah. It has a very nicely designed wall on the western side, as people prayed and worshipped facing the west. Besides the tomb, there is a small room- like structure that is curved on the outside. In this room-like structure, lies buried Nasiruddin Mahmud. There is also a very deep well and near it is a small temple, a sign of India's unique culture. There is a huge pillar that was built in the later centuries. The whole tomb complex is very beautifully designed and is very spacious. Stairs lead up to a terrace, the view from where is very beautiful. It is obvious that the king wanted to build a beautiful monument in the memory of his son.
— SIMRAN DALAL, VIII B

AN EXCURSION
We were taken on a heritage walk to Sultan Ghari's Tomb. It was a fun-filled walk about our history. Sultan Ghari is basically a tomb built by Iltutmish for his son Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah. The tomb is very different and unique in its structure and is supposed to be one of the first tombs of the Sultanate period. It is made of Delhi Quartzite, with fine marble decoration. In the middle of this tomb is an octagonal platform, under which lies the grave of Nasiruddin Mahmud. The pillars that support this tomb are made of red sandstone. There are inscriptions and writings on the walls from the Quran. The tomb was actually built around 1231.

Apart from this, we saw the tomb of Iltutmish's two other sons as well. Only one remains; the other must have been destroyed. This structure depicts both Hindu and Muslim architecture. A few repairs were made by Feroz Shah Tughlaq. We also saw the ruins of houses of that period. The trip was tiring but exciting. The walk around the monument was a great and amazing experience. It is one of the best trips that I have ever had.
— A R RAKSHITHA, VIII A

Heritage Site in Our Backyard
Our school is located in B Block, Vasant Kunj, but we were not aware that there was a heritage site so close to our school. In fact, our bus driver had to ask for directions before we could reach Sultan Ghari, where The Indian Express had organised a heritage walk. Sultan Ghari's Tomb is located just opposite Sector-C, Pocket-9 of Vasant Kunj. Built by Iltutmish, the slave of Qutubuddin Aibak, for his eldest son in 1231, Sultan Ghari's Tomb represents the first tomb built for a Muslim royal in North India in the Medieval period. You will have to travel to Malakpur Kohli village on the Mehrauli-Palam road to visit Sultan Ghari's Tomb. The tomb's structure is very impressive; its architecture exudes structural elegance. The Tomb was in ruins till the Delhi Development Authority took up a project to restore it in 2003.
— TANYA GUPTA, VIII B

Tete-e-tete With Our Heritage
The Indian Express organised a heritage walk for us to Sultan Ghari's Tomb this Monday. We were told many things about this monument. The walk was very enjoyable and it increased our knowledge as well. We were told that Sultan Ghari's Tomb was built by Iltumish for his son Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah. It was built in 1231. Feroz Shah Tughlaq also had some repairs carried out on the structure. It is made of Delhi quartzite and is decorated with marble. Here we saw the grave of Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah. People believe that wishes made at the grave on Thursdays are fulfilled. We also saw the tombs of Muissudin Behram Shah and Ruknuddin Feroz Shah, built around 1236 and 1241. We also saw some houses of that period. I wish I could go there once again, as it was a great experience!
— POOJA MADAN, VIII A

A MONUMENT OF FAITH
Sultan Ghari's Tomb is a heritage site, built during the Sultanate period in the 13th Century in Malikpur, by Iltutmish. It is believed that if someone has any problem, they can come here and pray for help, and their wishes will be fulfilled. Newly-married couples also visit the tomb for blessings. The monument is a little crowded on Thursdays, when people flock here to visit the local Sufi saint.

It's entrance is from the western wall, which is open. Usually, the entrance is never made in this direction, as Muslims offer their prayers towards Mecca in the west. But its structure is very typical. It is very beautifully decorated with marble and inscriptions from the Quran. Some inscriptions are in the Kufic script and others in the more comman Naksh. Allah is written in Arabic in a very beautiful manner at its centre. At the front there are pillars. The original ones are made of red Delhi Quartzite, as it was easily available in Delhi. More pillars were erected by Feroz Shah Tughlaq, who repaired the whole mosque. They are made from stones brought from UP. Its style of architecture is known as Indian Islamic architechture, as two types of designs were used for the pillars. Many changes were made by Feroz Shah Tughlaq. There is an eight-sided platform in the middle. The tomb is also decorated with Hindu script taken from temples. There is a well outside the mosque; it was the first Tughlaq well in Delhi and is typical of the 13th Century. Behind the mosque there were many houses but only some ruins have survived. The mosque is very beautiful. I really enjoyed the heritage walk.
— PRAGYA MARU, VIII A

OUR HERITAGE
O! O!
Really! How Wonderful are
Taj Mahal, Red Fort, Qutub Minar
And a lot of such places
Where hearts of
Our ancestors lie
People say


Our monuments are made up
Of stones, bricks and mortar
But I say
These are not stones
These are not non-living.
All these are the
Hearts of our ancestors
We go there and
Establish a bond with our
Rich heritage and glorious past
— MANSI GARG, VIII-C

We invite schools to be a part of this Express Group initiative. For queries mail to heritagewalks@expressindia.com

Heading: ‘No signs’ of CBI chargesheet in near future - Indian Express
Content:
The Old Yamuna bridge: A relic of the Raj
The old Yamuna Bridge or Bridge No. 249 in technical railway parlance, was constructed in 1866 by the East India Railway at a cost of £16,16,335. It was built with a total length of 2,640 feet and consisted of 12 spans of 202.5 feet each. With the completion of this bridge, two principal cities of North India, Kolkata and Delhi, were connected by the Railways; this being the last link of the trunk line on this route. In 1913, this was converted into a double line by adding down line girders of 12 spans of 202 feet each and 2 end spans of 42 feet to the bridge. For the movement of road traffic, two road bridges were provided below the lines. The entry of trains into Delhi Junction Railway Station, in such close proximity to the Red Fort, never ceases to impress the rail traveller, reminding all that after the Uprising of 1857, Delhi was a fortified city. The old Yamuna Bridge has an identical twin, a bridge further downstream at Naini on the Allahabad — Mughalsarai section of the now North Central Railways. The old Yamuna Bridge, with its huge iron girders, will be history when the new bridge, under construction a little way upstream on the Yamuna, becomes operational. But it would certainly not mean curtains for this iron monster and it will continue to remain one of the most famous landmarks of the city. Its role will be limited to carrying road traffic from East Delhi to Central Delhi and back.


— MANISH TIWARI, Director
INFORMATION & PUBLICITY, MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

Wrestler Bishamber Singh
Sushil Kumar's bronze medal at the Beijing Olympics reminded us not only of our country's wrestling heritage but also of the contribution the Indian Railways have made towards this sport. While Sushil Kumar is the most recent railwayman to don Indian colours, perhaps the most outstanding and well known of all Railway wrestlers has been Bishamber Singh, who was the leading wrestler of his time in the 1960s. An eminent wrestler, coach and technical expert, and Arjuna Award winner, Bishamber Singh died in 2004 at the age of 61. An akhara wrestler, he was able to adapt to modern freestyle wrestling and won laurels in the 57 kg category. He first came into prominence when he won the Hind Kesari title in 1962, followed by a 6th position in the Tokyo Olympiad in 1964, which also resulted in his being nominated for the Arjuna Award the same year. In 1966, he won a gold medal at the Jamaica Commonwealth Games. In 1967, he won a silver medal at the FILA World Wrestling Championship in the 57 kg freestyle wrestling category, the only Indian till date to do so. Coincidentally, the 1967 championships were conducted in New Delhi. Bishamber Singh retired from the Indian Railways as a Sports Officer a year before his death. A week prior to his untimely demise, Bishamber was presented (in absentia) the Bhishma Pitama Award by the Indian Style Wrestling Association of India.


— J L Singh, retired railway official

Did you know?
* Jodhpur Railway was the only state railway entrusted with the construction, maintenance and operation of British Indian lines
* In 1942, the Bharuch-Jambusar Railway created history as it was a rare instance of a British-owned railway system being passed on to a native state
* Ranjitsinh Gaekwad, the present maharaja of Vadodara, received a priceless gift on his fifth birthday some 60 years ago from his father, Pratapsinh Gaekwad. The gift was a fully functional toy train that ran on ten inch gauge rails. The young prince and his siblings used the train to travel from Laxmi Vilas Palace to the palace school, which incidentally, is now the Fatehsinh Museum. The steam locomotive can be seen even today on the museum grounds
* Maharaja Jaswant Singh was the first Indian king to have built a railway in his kingdom
— Vikas Singh, railway enthusiast

Heading: Youths throw acid at girl - Indian Express
Content:
CASE HEADING NOWHERE? Probe agency has little hope of recovering Arushi-Hemraj's mobiles, murder weapon

A day after the CBI admitted that it would miss the 90-day deadline for filing chargesheet against the three accused of murdering Arushi Talwar and the family's help Hemraj, it appears that there are "no signs of a chargesheet in the next few months" as well.

Senior CBI officials said on Wednesday that it is next to impossible to trace "substantive evidence" — the teenager and Hemraj's mobile phones and the khukri believed to be the murder weapon. Officials said it is highly unlikely anyone other than the accused would have knowledge of their whereabouts.

Though the investigating agency had on Tuesday announced a Rs 1 lakh reward for anyone giving information leading to their seizure, sources said investigators are not pinning much hope of any success there, too. But the CBI still would "arrange for public notifications" about the reward at public places such as bus terminals, railway stations, airports, and others, sources said.

The CBI's last hope of bolstering its case, sources said, is any information coming out of Nepal. The agency had yesterday announced sending an official communiqué to authorities in Kathmandu for help in recovering evidence. The CBI believes Krishna or Rajkumar, two of the three accused in the twin-murder, crossed the border and hid the murder weapon and the phones there since both come from Nepal.

"But that would be a miracle," the source said. "It would also save the agency from more criticism, for CBI has already made many attempts to trace the weapon and mobiles, without success. Krishna, Rajkumar and Vijay Mandal also did not disclose anything about this in their narco and brain-mapping tests."

The CBI claims it has forensic evidence against all three accused, besides their confessional statements, blood sample reports and fingerprints. It also has a clear picture on the supposed sequence of events on the night of May 15-16. But since these are reportedly not helping establish much, the agency needs corroboration of these facts with "substantive evidence" to close its investigations.

Experts say truth can be corroborated with help of forensic evidence, confessions and evidence on accomplices. But a case cannot be proved by forensics alone. "Nothing can replace substantive evidence. It is crucial to establish guilt," senior criminal lawyer R K Naseem said.

Court to be informed under Sec 173 CrPc
CBI sources said in case the agency does not file chargesheet for long, it would keep the court informed on the status of investigation. It would then decide on the time needed for CBI to further its probe.

Heading: Consumer awareness drive to conclude with lucky draw - Indian Express
Content:
The clothes of the girl have been sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory for clinical examination

A 20-year-old girl received severe burns when three miscreants threw acid at her in Junagadh on Tuesday.

In her complaint, victim Asha Bhoy stated that Pago Hira along with two others, stopped her on the College Road, threw acid and fled. She was rushed to Junagadh Civil hospital for treatment.

Junagadh police has registered complaints against the three accused under IPC sections 323, 324, 504, and 114. Investigating officer and sub-inspector K D Rathod, however, said: "The substance thrown at the girl was not acid, but an inflammatory fluid. We have sent the girl's stained clothes to the Forensic Science Laboratory for clinical examination," he said.

"Prima facie it seems personal rivalry was the reason behind the incident. Two days ago, the girl had had a quarrel with the family members of the prime accused," he said.

Heading: Self-financed engineering colleges threaten strike over recommendations on fee structure - Indian Express
Content:
The year-long ambitious project of the state government to increase public awareness on the importance to demand for bills on purchase, will conclude on Thursday as those who heeded the message will now be rewarded through a lucky draw.

In the year-long collection which began on July 1, 2007 and continued till February 28, 2008, the Commercial Tax Department of the city collected over 1,92,020 bills in its Vadodara chapter. Minister of Finance, Labour and Employment, Vaju Vala will be in the city to distribute awards of the lucky draw.

From the grant given by the state government to promote the cause, prizes worth Rs 37,10,000 will be distributed.

They include Maruti cars, colour televisions and other guaranteed gifts.

Bills of any commodity amounting to over Rs 100 was to be submitted with the tax department. These could include bills of petrol, diesel and other products.

Heading: Govt criticised for not implementing Forest Rights Act - Indian Express
Content:
Irked over the recommendations of Justice RJ Shah committee, the Self-Financing Engineering Colleges Association has threatened to initiate protests opposing the same unless the state government reconsiders the recommendations.

CL Patel, president of the association and Chairman of Charutar Vidya Mandal, Vallabh Vidyanagar, said that the fee range recommended by the committee is very low as compared to the amount the Self-financed Engineering Colleges (SFEC) spend on each student. With such a fee structure, it will be very difficult for the SFECs to function, he said.

"So far the recommendations have been made for three institutions. The fee range recommended by the committee for the first year batches is between Rs,43,000 to Rs. 47,000, while the fee for other students have remained unchanged," Patel said, adding that the SFECs spend anything between Rs. 60,000 to Rs.75,000 per year on each student.

"We have already submitted a memorandum to the committee explaining our cost implications. Our counterparts in Maharashtra, Karnataka and other states, enjoy phenomenal independence in terms of admissions and fee structure," he said.

He said that the SFECs are abiding by the existing guidelines and are not even asking for any other form of liberty. All they are asking for is the independence to fix the fee at a reasonable sum, whereby they do not have to incur losses.

"The association will meet on September 14 and request the Chief Minister to reconsider the recommendations. In case our demands are not met, we may have to take some action as it will be very difficult for us to carry on like this," he said.

Heading: SEBI office likely to open near Nehru Bridge - Indian Express
Content: Congress, the main Opposition in Gujarat has criticised the government for not implementing in letter and spirit the provisions of Forest Rights Act in the State, under which tribals are allowed to till forest land. Raising the issue at the marathon three-hour meeting of the State Tribal Advisory Council chaired by Chief Minister Narendra Modi here on Tuesday, senior Congress MLA Anil Joshiyara complained that the government was dilly-dallying in implementing the provisions of the Act, thus depriving tribals of their rights to till forest land they possessed till 2005 — the cut off date fixed under the Central Act.

Heading: Surat bombs: accused sent to 24-hr police custody - Indian Express
Content:
Rajasthan also brought under Ahmedabad jurisdiction

Investors will heave a sigh of relief when the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) opens its regional office here some time in January. SEBI officials who have already visited the city to finalise the location of the office, are likely to choose a place somewhere near Nehru Bridge.

Ramaben Mavani, who heads the Rajkot Shahar/Jilla Grahak Suraksha Mandal, Rajkot, said it was an old demand that SEBI had now fulfilled. She said the move was justified in view of the fact that a majority of capital market investors lived in Gujarat, where heavy subscriptions and market transactions materialised routinely. "The SEBI presence in this state will ensure that companies behave properly with investors and do not do a vanishing act. It is the Saurashtra-Kutch region, which witnessed heavy investments and an equally large number of complaints," she said.

She said the decision should have been taken long ago, but it was still not too late. "The ordinary investor will also be able to establish direct contact with SEBI to resolve their grievances. The one big advantage will be that the SEBI message of investor protection will reach deeper in the interiors of the state where a new investment climate is developing in the wake of fresh awareness. The SEBI presence will serve as a watchdog for companies in the region and will provide a protective umbrella to the investors," she said.

Capital market investors in Rajasthan, have, however, expressed reservations about being brought under the jurisdiction of the Ahmedabad regional office from the present Delhi office. According to them, they were better off with the Delhi regional office.

Deepak Saxena of Consumer Unity and Trust Society, a Jaipur-based investor protection body, said his organisation will hold discussions with SEBI officials when they visit Jaipur on Friday.

"We welcome the SEBI decision to open a regional office in Ahmedabad, but bringing Rajasthan under it would be cumbersome for the people of the state because Ahmedabad is a bit far as compared to Delhi," he said.

Saxena said that south Rajasthan investors might find visiting Ahmedabad more convenient rather than Delhi. But placing entire Rajasthan under the jurisdiction of the new regional office will not be feasible, he added.

The capital market regulator had made the announcement to open a SEBI regional office for Gujarat last month and the sentiment here has been bullish.

Himmatsinh Jhala, president of the All Gujarat Investor Protection Trust, Ahmedabad, said that Sabarkantha MP Madhusudan Mistry had played a great role in this regard. With this, problems with errant brokers like selling stock without consulting the client would be minimised. "Besides, we have learnt that at the Ahmedabad office, SEBI will appoint Gujarati and Hindi speaking officials to remove the language barrier and ensure better interaction with the people approaching them," he said.

Heading: DCB says it didn’t hand over Sajid Mansuri to Rajasthan Police - Indian Express
Content:
A metropolitan court on Wednesday sent Tanveer Pathan and Zahir Patel, the two accused of playing a "major role" in planting the 30 bombs across Surat city, to 24 hours police custody.

The accused were produced before the court by the Surat Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) after their 15-day remand in connection with another Surat bomb case ended on Wednesday.

The DCB applied for the initial 24-hour custody of the accused in connection with the blasts under Kapodara police station in Surat. Two explosive-laden cars were found in the area after the Ahmedabad bomb blasts.

Earlier, the two accused were remanded to police custody for a different case registered in connection with the explosive-laden cars.

A DCB official said: "We have now arrested them in connection with another case related to the explosive-laden cars found in Surat. We want to find out the entire plot that led to the planting of bombs in Surat."

While seeking the custody of the two, the DCB had earlier told the court that it has evidence against the accused which clearly suggests their involvement in collecting the explosives found in the car and planning the logistics of the operation. The DCB also said the accused were in constant touch with Sajid Mansuri, an accused in the Ahmedabad blasts case.

The DCB is likely to seek further police custody for the accused on Thursday when the initial 24-hour remand ends.

Heading: Hookah bar raids welcome, but what about ban on gutka? - Indian Express
Content:
In an affidavit filed before a metropolitan court in Ahmedabad, the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) has said that it had not handed over the custody of Sajid Mansuri, one of the accused in the Ahmedabad serial blasts case to Rajasthan police for interrogation at any point of time.

The DCB, however, admitted that Masuri was taken to Rajasthan for investigation of the blast case and collection of evidence and is now back in Ahmedabad.

The affidavit comes after Hashim Qureshi, Mansuri's lawyer, filed an application stating that his client's custody was handed over to the Rajasthan police without informing the court.

Mansuri is accused of playing a role in the Jaipur bomb blasts as well. In his application, Qureshi had also alleged that the investigating officer in the case, Mayur Chavada, had delegated the job of taking Mansuri to Rajasthan to some other officer in violation of the law. The issue came to light when Mansuri's wife had gone to meet him at the DCB office only to be told that her husband has been taken to Rajasthan.

Countering these arguments, special public prosecutor J M Panchal said the application was filed with the aim of creating "hurdles and hindrances" in the crucial stage of the ongoing blasts investigation.

Panchal said that the investigating officers have wide powers for collection of evidence and are in no way required to inform the court about taking an accused anywhere for the purpose, once the custody has been granted to the police. He also said that for the purpose of investigation and collection of evidence a police officer has the right to take the help of his subordinates. A hearing on the issue is scheduled for September 12.

Heading: This year’s theme: Think globally, act locally - Indian Express
Content:
The civic body may be showered with accolades for its current crackdown on hookah bars. But, it also reminds one of a similar, abortive drive, launched 12 years ago with similar vigour and later given a quiet burial.

It was about banning the sale of gutka and other tobacco products in the vicinity of hospitals and educational institutions. No one in the mighty Ahmedabad Muncipal Corportation (AMC) as much as speaks of it now.

A humble reminder to the AMC health department officials elicited a sheepish response on the matter. According to them, the menace has spread far and wide and it was beyond the handful staff of the department to curb it.

When the drive was first launched in 1996 during the tenure of Keshav Varma at the helm of the civic administration, it was implemented quite strictly. But it was back to square one the moment he left.

Time and again, media drew attention of the civic authorities to this violation of the AMC order, but the health department kept skirting the issue talking about staff shortage. Forget about gutka and other tobacco products being sold within 100 metres of schools and hospitals, instances were brought to the AMC notice wherein they were being sold at the school and hospital gates! And yet, no action was taken.

AMC's medical officer, health, Dr Suhas P Kulkarni admits that the civic administration cannot punish errant gutka-sellers or take action against hookah bars beyond a point.

About hookah bars, Kulkarni said: "We are forwarding their details to estate department so that other irregularities such as lack of Building Use permission etc are also unearthed and action can be taken against such bars as a deterrent". He said the AMC was in the process of locating a Central Government agency so that samples could be sent for further analysis under the provisions of the Tobacco Products Control Act, 1993 and other related regulations.

"First, we will verify contents of the samples and then take action under the Food and Drugs Adulteration Act against the violators," he said. According to Dr Kulkarni, as of now, consumption of tobacco was not an offence, which could warrant arrest of a person, but if that was found to be along with other objectionable conduct then it would surely attract police action. He admitted that while the AMC was able to swoop down on hookah bars, its machinery was not able to control the sale of gutka near educational institutions despite clear orders that no gutka or tobacco products could be sold within 100 metre distance of educational institutions.

Heading: Red Ribbon Express to make people aware about HIV/AIDS - Indian Express
Content:
Tension prevailed at the Nyay Mandir area of the city on Wednesday when shopkeepers and hawkers pelted stones at the Vadodara Municipal Corporation's (VMC) anti-encroachment team, which had visited the area to remove illegal encroachments.

The VMC officials visited the area as part of their weekly drive to check the encroachments by roadside vendors and hawkers, who do business on the pavements of the commercial area.

Mahesh Rabari, Ward Officer, Nyay Mandir, was also with the team when a verbal altercation ensued between the encroachers and the VMC officials. The incident eventually turned violent when people began pelting stones at the officials. Nyay Mandir is one of the busiest markets of the city, where hand carts and roadside stalls are a common sight.

"Traffic at Nyay Mandir area is very heavy. Traffic congestion is caused generally by the road side stalls and hand carts. We often drive them away from that area. We cannot employ our own squad every time, as it is also the responsibility of the police to check deal with the issue," said a VMC official.

He added: "These roadside vendors and hawkers have their own goons who act as a security cover for them."

Heading: Ganesh devotees to get insurance cover - Indian Express
Content:
To make the people aware about HIV/AIDS, the Red Ribbon Express, which has been trailing across the country for the last 10 months, will enter Valsad in Gujarat on Thursday.

The Centre, National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO), Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan and the Railways have launched together this drive.

The train will halt at 15 major cities of the state and at several rural stations to reach out to the people.

With its three days halt at Vadodara on September 17, the team will reach out to over 72 villages in the Vadodara jurisdiction.

"Six cultural teams will spread in different directions from the central location and each team will cover four villages per day. They will spread awareness about HIV/AIDS through plays and dramas," said R R Joshiara, Deputy Director of Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan, which is also handling the journey across the state.

He added that to see what the people have understood, around 10 people from among the audience will be evaluated for feedback.

"We have been arranging the proceedings with the sarpanch of the panchayats. Together with the street plays, various health and educational camps will be set up. The departments concerned will undertake blood donation camps, counselling on AIDS and health issues there," he added.

This specially designed train was flagged off in December 2007 from Delhi and has already visited Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttarakhand, Assam, West Bengal, Orissa, Andhra

Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, followed by Goa and Maharashtra.

The train will leave the state on October 16, and is slated to visit Rajasthan followed by Punjab, Haryana, and Chandigarh to complete the journey on November 11 this year.

Heading: Animal activist held for keeping endangered owl - Indian Express
Content:
This year, Lord Ganesh has insured the life of every devotee visiting the Raopura Yuvak Mandal Ganesh Mahotsav in Vadodara. The mandal at Kharchikar no Khancho has taken a third party insurance cover of Rs 10 lakh from the United India Insurance Company in Vadodara for the pandal visitors.

"We have taken this insurance for the devotees in the wake of the Ahmedabad blasts. Our mandal is among the most popular in Vadodara and we receive a huge crowd every year. We want to insure the life of every devotee who comes here," said Virendra Sharma, co-coordinator, Raopura Yuvak Mandal.

According to the insurance, if any untoward incident or a calamity arises, the affected people will be helped with the insurance money.

This year, the mandal's Ganesh idol is 21-feet high and is in the form of Lord Hanuman. The mandal has borne an expense of Rs 5-6 lakh for the décor, which depicts the message of Karma through two episodes of the Sundarkand. The pandal is spread across 2,400 sq ft and has an additional 27,000 sq ft for the visitors.

But the Vadodara police has denied a threat perception in the aftermath of the blasts. The police have provided security to all the pandals across the city. The police have also arranged for additional manpower, officers and paramilitary personnel to ensure a safe Ganesh Chaturthi celebration.

Vadodara Joint Commissioner of Police Pravin Sinha, said: "It might be true that some organisers opted for the insurance for various reasons. But as far as policing is concerned, we are providing adequate security to the Ganesh Puja pandals. If some of the organisers have sought insurance for the pandals, it is their concern. All we can say is that law and order situation in the city is up to the mark."

N A Solanki, Inspector, Raopura police station, added: "We are on a 24-hour duty in the city. We are ensuring the security in the city during the festival."

There are around 1,800 Ganesh pandals in Vadodara and all are following the security instructions given by the police. Besides, private security guards with hand-held and door frame metal detectors have also been deployed at all the pandals to keep a check on visitors.

"We have about 170 volunteers for the security of the visitors. We have arranged for metal detectors; and the volunteers are checking the baggage of the visitors at the entrance. We don't take any help from police as generally the mandals have their volunteers to ensure the safety in the pandals," said Raju Pawar of the Kalupura Sai Parivar Sarvajanik Ganesh Mandal in Vadodara.

Heading: Hawkers pelt stones at VMC officials - Indian Express
Content:
In a shocking incident, forest officials arrested wildlife rescuer Rakesh Wadhwana for illegally keeping in possession a rare and endangered species of owl.

Social forestry department in Vadodara has ordered an inquiry over Rakesh Wadhwana of Crocodile Group at Ajwa Road in the city for keeping the Spotted Owl (Athene Blewitti) for over a month.

Incidentally, Crocodile Group is headed by former Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) councillor Ashok Pawar.

Wadhwana, according to forest officials, acquired the endangered bird in August this year.

But, he did not return it to the forest officials within 48 hours as per the forest department rules.

The Spotted Owl is a schedule-I specie and has been listed under the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN)-World Conservation Union.

Speaking to Newsline, Nayan Desai, Deputy Conservator of Forest (DCF), Vadodara social forestry said: "It is a rare and endangered specie. Under the Wildlife Protection Act 1972 Section 39 (2) and (3), if a person finds it, it has to be returned to the social forestry official within the next 48 hours."

"It is learnt that Wadhwana had got the owl in an injured state," Desai said.

"On Tuesday, the accused was produced at the local Judicial Court K G Patel and later released on bail," informed S J Sheikh Assistant Conservator of Forest (ACF), Vadodara Social Forestry department.

Forest Spotted Owlet reportedly lives under the hollows of timber and has become an endangered specie due to depletion of the forests in the past 20 years. In the year 2007, Maharashtra based NGO, Enviro Search, visited Vadodara and Surat forest circle to trace this specie, but found none.

Heading: Open book exam format put on hold - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP rebels on Wednesday announced the formation of the Maha Gujarat Party and released the outfit's symbol and constitution. The conch has been chosen as the party symbol and golden yellow as the party colour. The party constitution released on Wednesday highlights integral humanism as its core.

Former Home Minister Gordhan Zadafia has been chosen the party president and Bhavnagar MLA Sunil Oza the general secretary. The first convention will be held in Ahmedabad on September 25 when other posts and the party structure will be announced.

Zadafia, who is also the chairman of the Sardar Patel Utkarsh Samiti (SPUS), said the golden yellow colour symbolises sacrifice.

The party leaders, most of whom have roots in the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), said they had the opportunity to contest the 2007 Assembly elections on a Congress ticket or as Independents. They also had ample opportunity to go back to the BJP fold, but decided against it, they added. "We have sacrificed post, power and prestige for the new party," said Oza.

The Maha Gujarat Party has been touted as the first regional party in Gujarat where politics revolves around the Congress and the BJP.

Oza said: "Today the ruling BJP is pleasing their national bosses and putting the interests of the state at stake. The opposition Congress too has failed to play its role. A regional party that puts the state's interest on top priority is the need of the hour. The Maha Gujarat Party will play the role of a regional party. Mamata Banerjee has proved what role a regional party can play."

A lot has changed since October 2007, when many top BJP leaders, unhappy with the autocratic style of Chief Minister Narendra Modi, launched a rebel group by the name of SPUS. The SPUS had a marriage of convenience with the Congress, and together with BJP heavyweights like former Chief Minister Keshubhai Patel, Suresh Mehta, senior MPs Kanshiram Rana and Vallabh Kathiria and other MLAs, ran an anti-Modi campaign in run up to the polls.

Modi won the elections with a thumping majority and within a couple of months, veterans like Patel Rana and senior leaders like Kathiria and Bechar Bhadani (MLA from Amreli) went back to the BJP.

At the first convention on September, former MLA Balu Tanti is likely to be a party of the new party, besides the likes of Zadafia, Oza and former Rajkot Rural MLA Siddharth Parmar.

Oza added that the new party will be based on Hindu Ideology.

Heading: GUJCOC: UPA divided over Presidential assent - Indian Express
Content:
Following opposition from parents' bodies and the Congress, the Gujarat government on Wednesday decided to put on hold the Gujarat State Secondary and Higher Secondary Board's (GSHSEB) decision to conduct 'open book' examinations for Classes VIII, IX and X from the current academic year.

Government spokesman Jay Narayan Vyas said the decision has been put on hold after a comprehensive review. He said school exams will be conducted as per the existing system.

He said the government will consider the idea of an 'open book' exam system only after seeking the view of educationists, and parents' and students' bodies across Gujarat in the next three months.

On being asked whether Board Chairman R K Pathak had made a hasty announcement on the new examination system, he said: "I am not here to contradict what Pathak had done or said earlier. The Board is an autonomous body, which can take decisions independently. But, the government is within its right to review it".

Later, in a press statement, State Education Minister Ramanlal Vora said the GSHSEB had on Tuesday sent a proposal to his department about conducting 'open book' exams in schools. The government will take a decision on whether to accept the Board's recommendations in toto or in part only after seeking the views of academicians, he said.

According to sources though, the education minister had reportedly reprimanded the Board chairman for not taking him into the confidence before taking the decision. Vora was also learnt to have taken up the issue with Chief Minister Narendra Modi at Wednesday's Cabinet meeting.

'Bad weather churns out better pilots'
AHMEDABAD:"Bad weather churns out better pilots," this was what Pathak said on being asked if students would be able to adapt to the 'open book' examination system. He said the board was an autonomous body, but the government could always review its decisions.

Rohit Pathak: 'A Man of Letters'
AHMEDABAD:Rohit Pathak has put the Modi government in a tight spot ever since he announced the 'open book' system. As the Vadodara Municipal Commissioner, he had ordered the demolition of a dargah in the Walled City area for reportedly easing the flow of traffic, which led to riots. Incidentally, the website, www.essenceoflifethepoem.org, which has uploaded his poetry, lists him as being awarded twice as the best district development officer by the state government. It also says that Pathak has been conferred with "A Man of Letters" award by the International Association of Educators for World Peace (IAEW) of the UN.

CM wants debate on 'open book' format
NEW DELHI: It was during a video conference with students and parents on Teachers' Day that Modi mooted the idea of an "open book" examination format in the state.

Sources say that "the idea should be debated by educationists before the state government formulates a definitive policy on the issue."

Heading: Govt decides to bring official resolution for GUJCOC in Assembly - Indian Express
Content:
There is a sharp division within the UPA government over the grant of Presidential assent to the Gujarat Control of Organised Crime (GUJCOC) Bill, 2003. The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has now placed the matter before the Union Cabinet.

This is, however, not the first time that the matter is being placed before the Union Cabinet. In 2006, the Cabinet returned the Bill to the MHA and asked it to hold consultations with the Ministry of Law and Justice in order to identify clauses in the proposed law that could be susceptible to misuse.

While the MHA has categorically said that it is not in favour of granting an assent to the proposed law, it would not be for the Union Council of Ministers to decide the fate of the proposed law, which is stuck with the MHA since 2004.

Sources say a powerful section within the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) is in favour of the law being cleared. They feel that denying the law to the BJP-ruled Gujarat – even as similar laws, the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act, (MCOCA) – in force in two Congress-ruled states, could put the Centre in a fix with the Lok Sabha elections round the corner.

According to sources in the PMO, the MHA has already sent a detailed note for circulation among the Cabinet Ministers. It states why the proposed law should not be recommended for grant of Presidential assent. The MHA wants the Cabinet to ask the President to withhold assent of the proposed Bill indefinitely.

Senior BJP leader L K Advani and Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi had earlier spoken to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and other Central Government functionaries to clear the Bill.

Modi has repeatedly told the Centre that his state requires the law to counter anti-nationals elements, who have become very active. He has also told the Centre that apart from the fact that the law was passed by the state legislature on the directions of the Union Government, the GUJCOC Bill is a carbon copy of the MCOCA, which is in force since 1999.

A PIL, seeking directions to the Union Government to obtain assent of the President on GUJCOC Bill, is also pending with the Gujarat High Court.

Last month, the High Court had told the Centre that it could not sit on the GUJCOC Bill indefinitely without referring it for Presidential assent. "It has been decided to place the matter before the Cabinet. Whatever they decide will be the official line," said a senior PMO functionary.

Heading: Cannot give consent to GUJCOC, Centre tells High Court - Indian Express
Content:
A there-day monsoon session of the state Assembly beginning September 25 is likely to witness a lengthy duel between the ruling BJP and the Opposition Congress. The state government has decided to bring in the Assembly an official resolution urging the UPA government at the Centre to clear the Gujarat Control of Organised Crime (GUJCOC) Bill.

Today, the Assembly Secretariat received a written communication from the government in this regard. The communiqué said that the resolution be included in the House agenda on the first day of the Monsoon Session. Assembly Secretary D M Patel confirmed this to Newsline in the evening. The official resolution will stress upon the need for a stringent legislation like GUJCOC to deal with terrorist activities in the state, especially in view of the recent serial blasts in Ahmedabad, and the recovery of "live bombs" from Surat. It will also ask the UPA government to send the amended GUJCOC Bill, which had been passed in the Assembly in 2004 for Presidential assent. Reacting to the ruling BJP's move, GPCC spokesman and senior Congress MLA Arjun Modhwadia said: "My party will oppose the resolution during a debate in the House, as there are certain draconian clauses in the Bill, including the one which says that a confession made by a person before a police officer not below the rank of SP and recorded by such a police officer shall be admissible in the trial of an accused…..". He said the amended Bill was passed by majority in the Assembly when the House was not in order. The Bill was thus passed un-Constitutional and cannot be accepted, he said. He added: "The Congress will request the Centre not to clear the Bill for Presidential assent."

Heading: Youth from Navsari reneges on marriage promise, held in UAE - Indian Express
Content:
In an affidavit filed before the Gujarat High Court on Wednesday, the Centre said that it cannot put the Gujarat Control of Organised Crime (GUJCOC) Bill for Presidential assent as it "is not in consonance with the policy of the Central government."

The affidavit said that GUJCOC is similar to POTA and cannot be considered by the Centre. The Centre filed the affidavit in reply to a writ petition by Justice on Trial, a NGO, which had sought a direction from the High Court to send the bill for Presidential assent. The matter was being heard before the division bench of Chief Justice K S Radhakrishnan and Justice M S Shah. In its petition, the NGO, headed by retired High Court Judge S N Soni, said that strong laws like GUJCOC were needed to fight terror. It said that the Bill, which has been passed by the Gujarat Assembly, was being withheld by the Centre without any cohesive reason, while similar laws prevailed in Maharastra and Karnataka. The affidavit by the Centre said: "Since the Bill that repealed POTA was passed by Parliament and assented to by His Excellency the President, the executive at the national level cannot lead to the passage of a bill passed by the state legislature, if a law of the same nature has been repealed by the Union Legislature." The affidavit also said that a number of provisions required for control of crime under POTA have been incorporated under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act. It said the provisions are under the consideration of the Centre and that the proposals of the state government have already been sent to the Cabinet for consideration. The case is posted for next hearing after a month.

Heading: Life’s rocking - Indian Express
Content:
Trendy gym accessories not only add to your looks but also boost you up for more workouts

A quick run, a trek to the hill, daily sessions at the gym, a few games of tennis, a stint on the volleyball court or whatever kind of exercise you may indulge into, workouts are not only important for health reasons but they are equally important to keep you lively and going. Whether you love working out or you deem it to be an every-day task, there are little essentials that can make your exercise regimen a bit more interesting and comfortable.

"If you are jaded with your workout, seek a change in your appearance. Enhance your exercise routine with a sports gear that has it all to make you look smart and fit. With this look on side, you can definitely make your workouts more exciting," says fitness expert Kaizaad Kapadia of K11 Fitness Academy.

"When you are well dressed and look good, it will automatically encourage you to workout. While you are stylishly kitted with your gym gear, there are some essentials like gym towels or sweatbands that are necessary when it comes to dabbing the sweat. A towel is an important thing in your gym kit. Always use cotton towels as they are soft on the skin," advises Kapadia.

As the fitness bug has struck people of all ages, a wide range of sports accessories in classic and retro designs are available these days. Flaunting a spacious and stylish sports bag where one can carry everything he needs could be a style statement at the gym. These fitness hold-alls and sack bags help you have your head down knowing everything is just in place. Pair of workout gloves will revise your fitness regime and will make you look and feel like a sportsman when you are working your way at the gym and will also keep you warm if out jogging out in the cold. Gym caps, sweatbands, bags, sippers and sunglasses are essential elements for a sporty look, be it outdoor or indoor exercise routine.

"Gloves made from soft graded genuine leather made with grip technology build strength amid wrist and forearm that is needed while using dumbbells and barbells. Caps are very useful during workouts. If you are jogging or running they keep your hair back and also keep the sweat from you eyes. Caps also help in covering up a bad hair day," says Gaurav More, store manager, Reebok Lifestyle. Wear colourful sweatbands or carry a cool sipper to add a dash of style to your gym wear but basic thing like socks also need a right pick. "One must use socks that are made from soft materials as they support the skin. They protect the feet from abrasion, blisters and sores that are caused due to brunt of the pressure," says More.

While to add to the element of entertainment, customise your kit with a smart ipod sport kit or a tech-style MP3 player clubbed with stereo headphones that will have your favorite records to keep you upbeat during your workouts.

Heading: What’s so funny? - Indian Express
Content:
A walk from the Raghuvanshi Mills compound to Phoenix Mills with newbie actor Shahana Goswami seems longer than usual. Every second glance from a passers-by speaks volumes of her popularity and her newly-acquired celebrity status. Post Rock On, this versatile actress is a runaway success. "With the success of Rock On, my life has taken a U-turn. Today, wherever I go my character Deby goes with me," she smiles, pleased with the adulation.

Dressed in blue denims, a white top and beads around her neck, she is your typical collegian with oodles of ardour and zest. And for this 22-year-old, her success story has only begun.

After doing minuscule roles in Yun Hota To Kya Hota and Honeymoon Travels Pvt Ltd she is now looking forward to her next big release, Ru Ba Ru with Randeep Hooda, on Friday. "This one is a romantic story, about a live-in couple's relationship and the ups and downs they go through. I nag quite a bit in this movie too," she says, afraid of the fact that after two 'nagging wife' roles she might be stereotyped as one.

A Delhiite by birth, Mumbai has been her home for the last four years. "I have lived here through my graduation years and I have been a part of Jaimini Pathak's theatre group, 'Working Title', which initially helped me get into films," she says, looking around for some shade to escape the city's humid weather. But she has never been trained in acting. "It is in my genes," she proudly states, giving instances of her parents' involvement in theatre and dance.

For Goswami, Ru Ba Ru happened while she was still in college completing her graduation. She gave her first shot for Ru Ba Ru in Bangkok, much before she was signed on for Rock On. But ironically enough the latter has turned out to be her first big release. "It is all good. What I fear is with the success of Rock On, expectations are sky high. Everyone around me expects me to give a brilliant performance in this one as well," she says, as we pass by a magazine stall with posters of Rock On.

Success has kept her grounded. This, we can see in the little things that make her happy. As we walk around Phoenix Mills, she stumbles upon a host of white and mauve periwinkle flowers along the periphery of the compound which she admires, something that is typical of her character in her forthcoming movie as well.

However, she refuses to look at any of the restaurants around. "I am on a strict diet; I can only have juice right now. This profession makes you do all sorts of things. But I make sure I binge once a week at least," she says, while climbing the stairs that lead to The Bowling Company.

Heading: Play Punjab - Indian Express
Content:
Thirty years later, Shyam Benegal returns to comedy with Welcome to Sajjanpur

The promos of Welcome to Sajjanpur promise yet another rom-com set in rural India. What arouses ones interest, laced with disbelief, is the name at the end—Shyam Benegal. A pioneer of New Cinema, the filmmaker was never famous for his comic timing. Charandas Chor (1975) and Mandi (1983) were replete with funny moments, but an out-and-out comedy hadn't come out of his stable till date.

Reinventing the self for Benegal is as frequent as taking up a new film. This is true of him if you consider his newest film. "With every film, I have tried to reinvent myself. Otherwise, one becomes a creature of habit," he says. Though comedies have proven to be money-spinners of late, the director with an intellectual tag feels that dabbling in comedy is more of a coincidence than a design in his case.

"There is humour in my films. But I don't have an answer to why I took a long time to do a comedy. I took up subjects that interested me at those moments," Benegal says. The desire to make his audience happy too prodded him to direct Welcome. "Comedies can evoke a chuckle, laughter, riotous laughter and even hysterical guffaw. I just want my audience to return home happy," he says.

The script of Welcome to Sajjanpur was with Benegal for three years. But the camera started rolling only after UTV backed the project. "Making a comedy is not easy even at best of times. It demands certain sensitivity. Actors need to approach it with wit. The director plays along with the camera," says the 73-year-old. With actors Shreyas Talpade and Amrita Rao, Benegal says he is very happy with the cast.

Managing a perfect cast has been one of Benegal's strengths ever since he debuted with Ankur in 1974. In later years, he worked extensively with stalwarts like Naseeruddin Shah, Om Puri, Shabana Azmi and Smita Patil. "It is not easy to get the casting right, always. It happened accidentally in my films," he says. But then, Indian has several good actors. "The problem arises when one wants work with stars."

Benegal is very happy over the opportunities the present milieu offers to make films. "It's a great time for filmmakers and it's even better for young directors," says the maker of Manthan, elaborating on how the multiplexes have changes the movie-going experience. "India is a young country. It's the youth who would make a difference even in the film business," says Benegal.

Wooing the youth could be the motive behind planning yet another comedy when the popular verdict on Welcome to Sajjanpur is still unknown. Benegal's reply sounds familiar: "My next film too is going to be a comedy. It's a subject that appealed to us. We are working on the script and the film will be on the floors by the end of this year."

Heading: City’s red light area moves to makeshift tents - Indian Express
Content:
Composer Gaurav Dayal has struck gold with his album Play Groove Punjab

It's not everyday that Wyclef Jean drops a line saying that he liked your music. And when Gaurav Dayal woke up to one of those days, he was over the moon. The Delhi-based music arranger, sound designer and composer for some of the most popular Punjabi pop albums in the late 90s, Gaurav Dayal decided to put all his music education into an album that he hoped would change the way people looked at Punjabi music. The result is Play Groove Punjab (BIG Music, Rs 125), the highest selling and most downloaded non-Bollywood album out of India this year.

Tired of hip-hop remixes and hearing staple beats in every Bollywood soundtrack and pop album, Dayal chose to compile a multi-artist album in late 2007. "All the tracks that I was composing or designing before catered to the artist only. I'm not Punjabi and I wanted to compose my own tribute album to a genre that gave me my first break," says Dayal who hit the big league in Indi-pop circles with Jassi's hit single Dil Le gayi Kudi in 1999. Working in between other commercial sessions, tentatively arranging loops, hook lines, and choosing artists wasn't easy but Dayal wanted the album to sound international.

"With the best equipment and arrangement, Punjabi music can appeal to people who like other genres as well. I wanted to arrange the sound in a truly international way but with brand new compositions, merge the traditional instruments in a completely different format," says Dayal who even went to New York City's renowned recording studio Masterdisk that boasts of artists such as Jay-Z and Beyonce. Industry observer Jasmine Malik who works with record label HMV isn't surprised that the album has done so well.

"Compared to solo artist albums, a multi-artist compilation does better because it gives it's buyers a choice. I've known Dayal's work and he's not been afraid to try different things, to challenge the way we listen to popular music," she says. The album is a collection of ten richly layered songs replete with guitar solos, strings, hand claps and liberally sprinkled with infectious beats.

Dayal invited some of Punjab's most prolific singers and amongst them, Husna Di Sarkare and Sohna Yaar Mera by Rana and Ishq Tere Ne by Shubha Mudgal stand out. Rocker chick Aditi Singh Sharma of Crimson and Level 9 has even sung the English hook line in Husna Di Sarkare which has become the most downloaded Punjabi track since the release of the album.
