A Google search belies the popularity of the album as listeners from across North America, Canada, Germany and Australia have posted favourable comments along with praise for the album.

Heading: Buddha’s reply to critics: Bengal is not Singur - Indian Express
Content:
In order to escape police action, prostitutes from Bhavnagar Road have now started operating from makeshift tents on the outskirts of the city, say cops

With the police conducting several raids in Bhavnagar Road, Rajkot's red light area, sex workers have been forced to move their business elsewhere. These women have resorted to a new way of practicing the illegal trade - makeshift tents.

According to the police, sex workers set up these makeshift tents near busy places so as to get customers in large numbers.

On Tuesday, the 'night patrolling' team of Kuwadwa police station arrested four sex workers from a makeshift tent set up outside Indian Oil Corporation's (IOC) gas refilling station on Rajkot-Ahmedabad highway.

After receiving the information, the patrolling team raided the area and found the four sex workers with customers.

While the customers managed to escape, the police arrested the sex workers under Sections 110 and 117 of the Bombay Police Act. The sex workers are Sunaina Raju, Anjli Shantiranjandas, Sangita Ranjit and Mamta Govind, all residents of Ahmedabad's Paldi area.

Pravin Makwana, head constable, Kuwadwa police station, said: "The pimps appointed by these sex workers visit the huge truck parking space outside the IOC depot and strike a deal with interested customers. They send these customers to the sex workers, who operate from a makeshift tent just outside the depot. We have been patrolling the area regularly. We conducted the raid after a tip off from an informer. I think after several police raids in red-light areas, sex workers have resorted to makeshift tents to continue the illegal trade."

Last week, the crime branch of the police conducted a surprise raid in Bhavnagar road and arrested around 12 sex workers. Since then the police has been patrolling the area on a regular basis. In order to escape the cops, prostitutes from Bhavnagar road have now started operating from makeshift tents on the outskirts of Rajkot city, particularly in front of IOC's gas refilling station, as it is frequented by truck drivers.

When contacted, S K Dave, Deputy Commissioner of Police, Rajkot, said: "Over the last week, we have arrested a few prostitutes from Bhavnagar road under Prevention of Immoral Trafficking Act as they have been operating from their own or rented houses. In Ahmedabad-Rajkot highway case, we detained the prostitutes under the Bombay Police Act."

According to sources, a group of sex workers operated from a makeshift tent during the recent Tarnetar fair held in Surendranagar. The pimps visited the fair regularly, asking people, ranging from visitors to stall owners, about their requirement for prostitutes.

Dave said: "Practicing prostitution on highways is common, as sex workers get good business from truck drivers. However, such kind of an activity is not possible in the fairs held in our region, as heavy police force is deployed during the fairs."

Heading: Bloodbath if others get our land, warn farmers who gave their plots - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday ordered the initiation of contempt proceedings against few members of a controversial music school in Mumbai for making remarks against several judges of the Bombay High Court besides the Chief Justice of India.

Perusing the replies by Leila David and Annette Kotian, members of Vasai-based Boss Music School, a Bench headed by Justice Arijit Pasayat observed, "we have considered the reply filed by the petitioners (David and Kotian) which are equally contemptuous and we feel that action needs to be taken against them for contempt of this court and charges will be framed against them."

While asking Solicitor General G H E Vahanvati to assist the court in the matter, the Bench also took serious note of the documents annexed in their reply. "You have threatened the CJI that if the situation is not resolved, the CJI will find himself in hot water," the Bench said. "You have drawn cartoons of the CJI and compared him with Osama bin Laden and Saddam Hussain. Comparing the CJI with Laden and Saddam does not take away your fallacious allegations."

Kotian, 23, and David, in her 80s, who were issued contempt notices last month, alleged that the CJI refused to stop the "genocide" committed by the judges against their school and denied them the basic fundamental right of life and liberty. This further annoyed the Bench.

Heading: Beijing hopes shattered, injured athlete dreams of a comeback - Indian Express
Content:
SINGUR: 4-member committee visits site

Even as the four-member committee set up to look into rehabilitation of Singur farmers visited the Tata Motors plant on Wednesday morning, a large number of villagers who had voluntarily given their land for the Nano project said they would not allow their land to be given back to other farmers.

"If the Government returns the land, we should be the first one to reclaim it," said Sheikh Sohrab Ali. "Otherwise there would be bloodbath," he warned as a large number of villagers, who had voluntarily gave their land, keenly watched the team go round the plant site and the vendor park.

Nearly 200 families from Joymollah had voluntarily given their land for the project, while seven did not. "Almost 125 acres of land of the vendor park belonged to us. How can the Government give it to others?" they asked.

"We have given our land for the Tata factory. Almost everyone in our village did so. Now if the state Government gives our land to farmers from other areas, there will be a bloodbath," said Sheikh Sohrab Ali, whose family had given up 25 bighas of land which is now part of the vendor park.

Later, Commerce and Industries Secretary Sabyasachi Sen said the farmers who had voluntarily given their land in Singur have in a petition to the

Government urged not to give their land to other farmers. The petition adds a new dimension to the rehabilitation process.However, the panel representing the Save Farmland Committee and the state Government visited the Tata Motors Nano plant in search of a solution to the crisis. But after an inspection that lasted almost three hours, the differences between the two sides persisted. Rabindranath Bhattacharjee, the Trinamool Congress MLA from Singur, and Becharam Manna, member of the committee representing the agitators, said that they have identified over 300 acres of vacant land inside the project site which has not been used yet. They felt this land can be returned to the unwilling farmers. The members representing the state, WBIDC MD Subrata Gupto and Hooghly District Magistrate Neelam Meena, ruled out the idea outright. "We have visited various areas inside the Tata Motors plant and could identify 300 acres of vacant land. This land can be returned to the farmers and unrecorded sharecroppers," said Bhattacharjee after the inspection.

Manna went a step further. He said: "There is so much land inside. We have found vast stretches of vacant land. The vendor plant is vacant and can provide us the land. There are other areas too. We have identified vast stretches of land in Joymollah, Sahapara and Gopalnagar areas."

The state Government officials, however, chose to remain silent on the issue. "What 300 acres? They are free to say what they wish. All I can say is that we have visited the southern side and the western side of the Nano project area and will soon file a report to the Government," said Gupto.

The panel members representing the farmers alleged they were misled. "When I identified a vast stretch of vacant land at one point, they said it is for car parking. What do you mean by car parking I shouted back, this is a vacant land," said Bhattacharjee.

Heading: 3-year jail, fine, for Czech scientists - Indian Express
Content:
Till sometime ago, Pinky Pramanik was touted as a medal prospect for the recently-concluded Beijing Olympics. The Bengal middle-distance runner was one of the brightest athletes at the national and international meets after a memorable 2006. When she won the 4x400m gold in the Doha Asian Games that year, many predicted her to be India's trump card for the 2008 Olympics.

But Pinky's fortunes slumped in 2007, just when she should have been setting herself up for the Beijing Games. She was down with a severe foot injury that had troubled her throughout 2007. The tough girl, however, fought hard and bounced back clocking an impressive 11.07 seconds in the 100m dash at a major meet in Kolkata in August last year. Less than two weeks later, she clocked 54.01sec in her favourite 400m category at a state championship.

Since then, however, her career took a nosedive. This year, the athlete tried to stage a comeback at the National meet, inter-state meet and several other key tournaments that were to mark as selection trials for the Beijing Olympics. But despite securing a berth in the 200m finals at the inter-state meet in Madurai in May, Pinky had to pull out of the championship due to a hamstring injury.

She is one of the most prominent female athletes the country has produced in recent years — gold at the Asian Grand Prix, South Asian Games, and a spree of national championships. And precisely therefore, decline in her form comes across as a tough blow for the Indian athletic community.

Coach Sushanta Sinha, under whose grooming the Bengal athlete had excelled earlier, is clueless about his disciple's mighty fall. "Though she has tremendous mental strength, she is whimsical and not disciplined. She hasn't contacted me in the last three months. She might have been depressed with the injury that terminated her dreams for the Beijing Olympics," he said. The coach also added, "I doubt she would be able to bounce back."

Debasish Banerjee, secretary of the Amateur Athletics Association of West Bengal (AAAWB), is equally concerned. He said: "I haven't seen her for long. I only heard that she has stopped practising after pulling out of the inter-state meet last May. I do not think that such a wonderful athlete would go astray. The association will try to convince her to stage a return."

Not many are aware however, that after her Beijing dreams were shattered, she went into hibernation to regain her strength. Living away from the limelight, she told The Indian Express: "I don't want to express my anguish. I have been suffering from a hamstring injury since the inter-state meet in Madurai. My doctor says I may recover within the next two months."

The athlete has certainly not forsaken her dreams to return to the track. "I am trying to make a comeback for the 2010 Commonwealth Games." She also cited an example. "Sushmita Sinha Roy (Bengal athlete who took part in the Beijing Olympics), is 24-year-old. I will be 25 in 2010 and if I recover from the injury, I can put up a spirited performance," Pinky said.

Heading: Singur has little effect on toons - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly three months after their arrest in Darjeeling on June 22 for collecting rare specimens of insects from a protected forest area, Chief Judicial Magistrate of Darjeeling awarded punishment to Czech entomologists Petr Svacha and Emil Kucera. While Svacha was slapped with a fine of Rs 20,000 and his passport impounded for one month, Kucera was sentenced to three years simple imprisonment and fined Rs 60,000. He was, however, granted bail. Lawyer of the scientists, Taranga Pandit said both were sentenced under the Wildlife Protection Act and the National Biodiversity Act.

Speaking to The Indian Express from Darjeeling, Czech Ambassador Dr Hynek Kmonicek said his government would not like to comment on the judgment awarded by an impartial judicial system. He said: "I'm satisfied with the order. We have always maintained that the scientists should be punished for what they did, not for what they did not. The allegations that they were collecting specimens in a national park for commercial purpose and that they trade such insects is not true."

The Ambassador further added, "It's surprising that different sentences were handed down to them for the same offence, committed at the same place and at the same time."

The court, however, explained for the difference in their punishment. Pandit said, "Svacha was let off with a fine because the court took into consideration his reputation as a renowned entomologist and his educational background. He was said to be a victim of circumstances." The counsel added, "An appeal would be filed against Kucera's sentence before the District and Sessions Court of Darjeeling within a month."

The ambassador also mentioned the uproar over the issue in his country. "It may be a small issue in India but in Czech Republic it is a huge affair. Since the day the entomologists were arrested, the matter has been widely reported by Czech media with an average of 60 print and electronic media reports coming out everyday." Hinting at the impact of bandh in the Hills on the trial, Kmonicek said, "The scientists had to spend a month in jail without trial as the courts were closed. It was a trying time for them and their families."

Ever since their arrest on June 22, the scientist community in India and abroad has been appealing to grant leniency for the Czechs. Reacting to the sentence, Priyadarsanan Dharma Rajan, Fellow Scientist, Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment told The Indian Express from Bangalore that the conviction was a great disappointment. "The order has hurt the world scientific community. Justice is denied to the scientists, whose purpose was only to conduct research. Instead, if the scientists were let off with the specimens they collected, their knowledge would have been a great asset for the data deficient northeast Himalaya biodiversity area," said Dharma Rajan.

Heading: UK doctor says Basu is stable - Indian Express
Content:
Even while the state government remains caught up in the land acquisition row over the Tata Nano project in Singur, the Information Technology department has vowed to provide land to IT major Infosys by the year-end.

"The Singur problem has caused a certain amount of damage to the IT image of the state. But we are trying hard to salvage it. Companies are still sceptical about the situation, but those who have already invested in West Bengal know the ground reality," said Debesh Das, state IT minister.

"We are holding talks with Infosys and are committed to providing land by this year," he added, emphasising on the emergence of Kolkata as an animation hub in recent times.

At a seminar organised on Wednesday by the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), in collaboration with the Information Technology department of the government and WEBEL (West Bengal Electronics Industry Development Corporation Ltd), industry experts also opined that the city has marched ahead in areas of animation and gaming, with prominent players making a foray into the state.

The state has 21 active animation companies and 6 training institutes, including the WEBEL animation-training centre. On Wednesday, West Bengal opened its doors to one of the largest production houses in the country, DQ Entertainment International.

"The state is now focusing on the animation industry. We already have DQ Entertainment Ltd, one of the largest animation production houses, start its operations in the state from today. We also aim to create Bengali literary works in animated forms," said Das.

"The animation and gaming industry has a potential to emerge as a major revenue spinner for the Indian IT-BPO sector at the export and domestic level along with being a big employment generator," said Tapas Chakravarti, managing director and CEO, DQ Entertainment.

"We invested Rs 11 crore and have over 280 employees. Some of our work from Hyderabad is being shifted here," he said.

The government is now hopeful that more such animation production houses would come to West Bengal. Das also announced that the IT department would create an animation park in Rajarhat over 25 to 30 acres. The park, which is slated to be completed by next year, will host a number of animation production companies.

The government also showed its intention of boosting the small and medium-scale industries, and floated the concept of allowing anyone interested to start an IT industry.

"Anyone who wants to start an IT industry can do it within 24 hours. All the extensive formalities can be handled later. We will provide the infrastructure at our plug-in sites," said Das.

Heading: Police had special funds to control situation - Indian Express
Content:
Eminent neuro-surgeon, Dr R P Sengupta was flown in from United Kingdom on Wednesday to examine CPM patriarch Jyoti Basu.

There was a detailed discussion with the board of doctors who decided to continue with the treatment till Thursday. A review of the situation will be once again done on Thursday, said hospital officials.

In a written statement, S Upadhaya, senior vice-president of the hospital, said there has been no change in the condition of Basu since Tuesday and that his condition was stable. "Basu was examined by a board of doctors on Wednesday and advised a normal diet," the press release read. Several CPM leaders visited the veteran leader including Brinda Karat, Nirupam Sen, Debobroto Biswas and Subhas Chakraborty.

Heading: Stung CPI legislator resigns from Assembly - Indian Express
Content:
It was two years ago in September 2006 that police were first deployed in Singur to maintain law and order, even as a fence was being constructed at the Tata small car factory site.

While land-related agitations in other parts of the country, including Nandigram, have had fatalities, there has been no casualty despite protests over the last two years.

Injuries have been kept to a bare minimum.

"We got information beforehand about a secret meeting held in the villages. We also came to know what the protestors were planning. We would be ready for them even before they embarked on their secret mission," said a senior officer of Hooghly district.

Citing an example, a senior officer said Trinamool activists Becharam Manna and some others were arrested when a peaceful procession began to turn violent in August 2007.

"We had information that the leaders had decided that they would attempt to break the wall of the factory. We had deployed more policemen than usual and were ready to handle a violent protest," said the officer.

The credit goes to the police for building up credible sources. A senior officer associated with Singur from the beginning said that the government had distributed a generous amount of money to create a network of informers.

"We had penetrated deep within the agitating villagers. We were allocated more money for the purpose," said the officer.

"Apart from the districts affected by Left-wing extremists, the allocation is between Rs 5,000 and Rs 10,000 per month. We got more than Rs 40,000 a month for building sources in Singur," said an officer.

But that is not all.

Sources said that the police also set up a good "rapport" with some of the leaders of the Singur Krishi Jomi Raksha Committee by arranging jobs for the relatives of the leaders at factories in other parts of Hooghly.

The police also said the entire Singur operation was done on a war footing. The distance of the Tata factory site was a prime hinderance for the policemen.

"There was no food or means of transportation for the policemen. Separate units were set up so the entire garrison could have food, water and a roof. There was a DSP who was entrusted with the duty of force deployment. Other inspectors, such as OC Bhadreswar and OC Pandua, were entrusted with duties such as providing food and water," said an officer.

Heading: Rs 500-cr drainage project set to collapse for lack of planning - Indian Express
Content:
CPI legislator from Nandigram Mohamed Ilyas has resigned from the membership of the state Assembly, months after he was caught on camera allegedly taking a bribe from an NGO for development work. Speaker of the Assembly Hashim Abdul Halim said on Wednesday: "Ilyas had sent me a resignation letter last Friday. I have accepted it. By-elections will soon be held for the Nandigram Assembly seat."

A few months ago, a local TV channel had showed in a sting operation that Ilyas took money from an NGO to issue certificates. After the uproar in the Assembly, the Speaker had set up a committee headed by the Congress legislator Gyan Singh Sohanpal to probe the allegations. The committee is yet to submit its report.

The CPI, which is a partner in the nine-party Left Front and at present has eight legislators, has endorsed the resignation of Ilyas who had won the Nandigram seat in the 2006 Assembly poll. Asked whether Ilyas would be again nominated for the by-elections, CPI leader Manju Kumar Mazumdar said, "We are yet to take a decision on it."

Heading: Enteric diseases spread, 230 affected - Indian Express
Content:
With several glitches, the much-hyped Rs 500-crore drainage and sewerage upgradation project, a part of the Kolkata Environment Improvement Project (KEIP), seems to be in doldrums.

The project funded by the Asian Development Bank is at present being carried out in some wards in Behala and Jadavpur. In these areas, the drainage system has collapsed and the drinking water supply system is facing threats.

"In many areas, water pressure has dropped. On Hemanta Mukherjee Road, it was found that the water pipeline has gone five feet below the road. The KEIP is supposed to take care of all these," Anjan Das, councillor, ward 129. In Jadavpur, the water pipeline developed leakages while the drainage project was being carried out. "The unplanned work of KEIP is making the situation worse. We have repeatedly asked the Mayor and the Municipal Commissioner to take prompt action to stop this work, but to no avail," said the councillor.

Besides, most of the roads including Brajamani Debya Road, Satyajit Roy Sarani, Gopal Misra Road, Biren Roy Road (west) have been broken and are yet to be repaired.

"The soil that has been dug out by the project workers has not been cleared yet. All the surface drains have completely choked," Shyamadas Roy, councillor, ward 126.

"Since there has not been a heavy downpour, the situation has been under control. This in spite that some areas were still reeling under knee-deep water. But once heavy rain starts, the situation will become worse," Roy added .

"This is an irrelevant issue that is being discussed. While carrying out a developmental work these kinds of things can happen. We cannot comment over the issue," said Bibhas Maity, Director General (Water Supply) of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation.

"We cannot comment over the problems since we are not authorised to speak," said Soumya Ganguly, director general, project KEIP. According to a civic official, the KEIP did not ask for the map of the drinking water pipeline. The KEIP did a local survey and started its work, he added.

Heading: Domestic workers come together to protest exploitation - Indian Express
Content:
The number of people affected by enteric disease has reached around 230 in ward 101 in south Kolkata. And the numbers may increase further — the affected area in ward 101 is large and includes Rabindra Palli and Purba Phulbagan.

An official of the health camp set up in the area said: "We have registered some 230 people who are suffering from enteric disease. Although only a few of them are undergoing treatment at the local hospitals, we are ensuring that the others follow the preventive measures".

The outbreak occurred due to water contamination, caused by a breach in a drinking water pipeline. The KMC health officials, however, provided different figures. "Around 25 patients have registered in the KMC health camp today. Apart from this, we are not aware of other cases of enteric disease," said Debdwaipayan Chattopadhaya, Chief Medical Health Officer, KMC.

To bring the situation under control, the KMC has sent four health teams to survey the area. Chandana Ghosh Dastidar, local councillor, said: "We have started the chlorination process. Water sample has been collected from 12 more spots. We are waiting for the report. Since the leakage remained undetected for three days, the contamination has spread to a large area."

Heading: HC seeks opinion on teachers’ qualification - Indian Express
Content:
Kapila Das of Narendrapur has been working as a domestic help since she was barely 10 years old. But humiliation and exploitation that she was subjected to by her employers in earlier years, continue till date even as she turned 45 recently. Das is one of over 50,000 women, who work as domestic helps in West Bengal.

Under the banner of Sara Bangla Paricharika Samity (SBPS), thousands of women from across the state who work as domestic helps gathered on Wednesday to raise their voice against the exploitation they face. Many of them are physically and mentally tortured at their workplaces, even raped at times.

Secretary of the SBPS Lilly Pal said, "Our members are routinely ill-treated. We approach the police but get no justice." The organisation has nearly 17,000 members.

To get social security from the government, the Samity has been demanding a registration of their organisation under the state labour ministry since 2005. There has been no response from the government yet.

On Wednesday, the members submitted a deputation to the state labour minister in this regard. Their other demands include according the domestic helps the status of a labourer, distributing them identity cards, sanctioning fixed holidays, minimum wages, health concessions and BPL cards.

Sandhya Naskar, a Samity member from Dakshin Barasat, asked, "Do not we have a right to live with dignity?" To secure a rightful place in the society, Naskar asked the government to issue identity cards for domestic helps. "We perform important household work but are neither paid the appropriate amount nor treated like human beings. This is because the government does not recognise us as a separate workforce," she added.

Nayona Dolai (15) from Bagnan said: "Most of us come from distant villages and struggle to make our ends meet in cities. But we never get the status of a worker and the required wages. My employers abuse me. They even refuse to provide me food sometimes." Newspapers routinely flash news of domestic helps robbing their employers but their exploitation by the employers is never reported.

"We want concession for monthly rail tickets and free education for our children," said Debi Naskar, who works in four houses, gets Rs 1000 per month and is the sole bread winner of her family after her husband expired sometime ago.

Heading: Govt plans to improve situation at Writers’ - Indian Express
Content:
Referring a case to the Chief Justice, Justice Tapen Sen of the Calcutta High Court sought the opinion on the essential qualification for the recruitment of teachers by the School Service Commission (SSC).

Sovan Mondal, a resident of Howrah, had filed a petition seeking an inquiry into the appointment process of teachers, the SSC has been undertaking in the secondary schools in the state from 1998.

He alleged that the SSC had invited applications in different years when B Ed was not essential for a candidate. But the rules framed by the National Council for Teachers Education (NCTE) mandated that B Ed degree should be considered essential for the appointment of teachers. The NCTE rule had come into affect from 2000.

Mondal alleged in the petition that the SSC had appointed teachers without adhering to the guidelines framed by the NCTE. As a result, those with B Ed are being deprived.

Mondal had passed B Ed and cleared the written examination of SSC in 2006 and 2007. But he had failed to pass the interview in both the years.

He pointed out in the petition that about 3,500 B Ed candidates were shortlisted for appointment in schools out of 24,225 candidates in 2007. A total of 6,000 B Ed candidates were called for interview last year.

After the hearing, Justice Sen sought the opinion of the Chief Justice over whether B Ed qualification should be essential for getting appointment as teachers in schools.

Heading: ‘MATCH FIXED!’ — Bagan official CRIES FOUL as Md Sporting INCH CLOSER TO TITLE - Indian Express
Content:
Worried over the deteriorating work culture at the Writers' Buildings, which has witnessed processions and dharnas by employees even during working hours in the recent past, the state government plans to take certain initiatives to improve the situation. It has set up a one-man committee to probe the incident, where a deputy secretary of the Finance department was manhandled on Tuesday. Minister for Finance Asim Dasgupta announced this on Wednesday.

The incident occurred after a showcause notice was issued to six employees of the department, owing allegiance to the Trinamool-backed Mahakaran Sangram Committee. The notice was served to the employees for participating in a dharna on August 19. This triggered a scuffle between the members of the committee and the CPM-backed coordination body. The police had to intervene to bring the situation under control.

The committee has been asked to file its report before September 15. "I have spoken to Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee, Chief Secretary Amit Kiran Deb and Home Secretary Asok Mohan Chakrabarti on this issue. We will not allow the work culture at the Writers' Buildings to be spoiled," Dasgupta said.

Heading: TT camp near Singur - Indian Express
Content:
Hot on the tracks of title win, Md Sporting score landslide 4-1 win over CPT; League leaders Mohun Bagan secy Anjan Mitra says match was 'fixed'

The task was cut out. Mohammedan Sporting needed to score seven goals in their last two matches of the CFL Premier Division if they aspire to finish with the title, pipping Mohun Bagan.

Well, the black-and-white brigade seems to be going on the right track so far, halfway through. They scored a convincing 4-1 victory over Calcutta Port Trust (CPT) today at the Yuba Bharati Krirangan, and are very much within sniffing distance of the title.

Mohammedan Sporting's fate now hangs largely on the upcoming East Bengal-Mohun Bagan derby clash this week. If league leaders Bagan happen to lose in that match, then Md Sporting would need a 4-goal win in their concluding clash against Chirag United SC to bag the title. As for Bagan, Barreto & Co need just a draw against East Bengal to ensure their Premier Division title.

Expectedly, Mohun Bagan club secretary Anjan Mitra has already raised the pitch, claiming that today's high-scoring match was fixed, and that efforts are being made to make sure Mohammedan Sporting leapfrogs Bagan to clinch the title.

In today's key match, CPT goalkeeper Subhash Sinha Roy's poor showing literally helped Mohammedan Sporting on way to a massive victory. Roy conceded 3 of the 4 goals in such inexcusable manner that CPT coach Biswajit Bhattacharya was forced to replace him with Shibram Dey after the first half.

Mohammedan Sporting's goal-machine this season, Theodore Sunday, took his tally to 9 goals, the highest so far in the Premier Division. It was Sunday who opened the day's scoring, and as early as into the very first minute — thanks to a careless Roy under the bar. Mike Okoro doubled the scoring in the 31st minute off a Farukh Hyder cross. And again, Roy wasn't in any position to effect a save.

Then came Jyothi Kumar's goal, in the 44th minute. Expectedly, it was a gift from Roy who first foiled Mike Okoro but then sent the ball straight to Jyothi.

An even more spirited Mohammedan Sporting got a few more chances into the second half, but the more responsible Shibram stood like a wall. Okoro broke the hiatus, scoring a foal in the 84th minute to make it 4-1, just 10 minutes after CPT's Ayen Daniel scored his side's only goal.

As the result muted premature celebrations in the Mohun Bagan camp, the club's secretary Mitra cried foul. "This match was fixed. Had this match not been fixed, then CPT would have fielded their experienced goalie (Shibram) right from the beginning. It was clear from the attitude of the other goalie (Subhash), who conceded 3 goals, that what he did was quite intentional," a visibly upset Mitra told reporters shortly after Md Sporting defeated CPT today.

Heading: Minors stay on sale, cops flounder - Indian Express
Content:
While TMC supremo Mamata Banerjee was raising the pitch on the Nano project in Singur, just 10km away, an organisation for mentally-challenged children —'Kishalay' in Naseebpur — has launched a one-of-its-kind table tennis coaching camp for 20 kids, all mentally disabled. This camp is a follow-up of a bigger camp for mentally-challenged kids conducted last summer by the Bengal Table Tennis Association (BTTA) in Kolkata from May 15 to June 14.

BTTA general secretary Subrata Dey, meanwhile, rubblished suggestions from certains sections of the TT community that the initiative was no more than just a gimmick. He said: "No, we don't believe in that. We deeply feel for them (the kids participating) and that is why we came up with this programme, despite limited resources."

The BTTA has installed a world-class TT board at the camp, manufactured by Meerut-based makers Stag. Mantu Murmu, who coached the kids at the summer camp in Kolkata, is in charge of training the children.

Heading: In 2 months, your ration card will have a barcode - Indian Express
Content:
Every passing year, number of rescued girls falls; activists say not enough crackdowns

Whether the rape allegation that a 17-year-old Hyderabadi made against the police is proved or not, the harsh reality is that poor minor girls from various parts of the country do get sold into the red-light area in Budhwar Peth - and that the police have been rescuing fewer and fewer minor girls.

Social activists say the police are not cracking down on strong "local support". The police insist they are cracking down but concede that brothel owners do enjoy local support.

The red-light area is under the jurisdiction of Faraskhana police station, whose figures confirm that the count of rescued girls has reduced over the years. In 2006, as many as 172 sex workers, including 109 minors, were rescued. In 2007, this went down to 127 (72 minors); in 2008, the count so far is only 67 sex workers, including 33 minors.

Of the 366 sex workers rescued since January 2006, most hail from Hyderabad, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, the northeastern states and also Nepal and Bangladesh. On Monday, a police team led by sub inspector Vimal Bidwe rescued seven girls, one of whom is from Bibvewadi in Pune. Most of these girls were forced into the racket just four months ago.

"The trafficking of minors would not have been not possible without local support," said Seema Waghmode, director of Kayakalp, a non-governmental organisation working in the red-light area for the last 14 years.

"Sometimes activists of social organisations like ours or other informers tip off the police whenever they see a young girl in the brothel. The police then conduct a raid, rescue the girls and also arrest the brothel keepers. But we soon find new girls being forced into the trade. This clearly indicates that some influential persons are supporting the illegal trade," she said.

Deputy commissioner of police (crime) Anil Kumbhare conceded that there was local support for the brothel owners. "The police have been taking action against such supporters frequently. The social security cell of the crime branch has arrested several women traffickers," he said.

Senior police inspector V T Pawar of Faraskhana police station said 126 agents including eight Bangladeshis have been arrested in the last two-and-a-half years. "It is not that only agents lure the poor girls on job assurances and sell them to brothels. Sometimes girls are sold into the brothels by their near ones. We had a case last year where a girl child was sold into the racket by her parents. This girl was rescued by the police and the case is pending in the Supreme Court," Pawar said.

Heading: How to rein in a student traffic offender: name him on college notice board - Indian Express
Content:
Biometric cards will store family head's thumb impression and information about him, help curb rampant use of bogus cards

Biometric bar-coded ration cards will become a reality in Pune from November, with a card being distributed to every household.

The device is like a smart card that stores information about the head of each family as well as his thumb impression. All fair price shops will be issued a card reader, in consultation with the respective tehsildars.

The person going to the fair price shop has to produce his card, which will be read by the card reader and his details shown. This will ensure that the correct quantity is issued to the person.

A contract was recently signed between Spanco Telesystems and Solutions (STS) and the Food and Civil Supplies Ministry for rolling out the biometric bar coded ration cards. Spanco will be undertaking the project for the entire State, with Pune and Mumbai being the priorities. In April, The Indian Express was the first to highlight the novel project.

According to officials, over 10 lakh laminated cards will be distributed in the city. "The biometric system is being introduced to keep a check on bogus ration cards, which are rampant across the State."

Spanco Telesystems Vice-President Ravi Bhatnagar said that data collection in the city has started and the company would be ready to issue the cards by November. "The district collectorate is helping us with the data and we should be right on schedule," he assured.

Pune will be the first city, followed by Mumbai, to have these biometric bar coded ration cards. Additional Collector Vasant Vaidya said that the laminated cards will ensure transparency and accountability in the Public Distribution System (PDS).

The company has a target of issuing 1.8 crore laminated ration cards in the State. Its Associate Vice-President Tushar Mohanty said that a site survey of Pune city is currently on and a functional requisite study, too, is being carried out.

A Global Positional System will help chart the route of civil supplies from the Food Corporation of India to the respective district godowns and the bar code will bring about accountability. The project, which will be under public-private partnership basis, will involve 475 officers of the Food and Civil Supplies Department while more than 1 lakh ration shops in the State will issue the cards to citizens.

Mohanty said that the huge effort is aimed at ensuring that the material reaches the target citizens without any pilferage — with state-of-art technology helping in effective monitoring of goods movement. MIS reports will be generated and there will be forecasting for various months as an added feature.

"The scheme is designed to ensure that the right beneficiary gets the desired amount of foodgrains and other benefits."

Bhatnagar informed that the system will be implemented across the state in three years. "We are looking at covering approximately 10,6740 fair price shops, 354 supply offices, 33 district supply offices, five regional offices and 44 ration offices in the State."

Heading: Morale down, cops at Faraskhana police station cry slander - Indian Express
Content:
The city traffic police have found a novel way to dissuade students and company executives from violating traffic rules: make their offences public before their teachers, classmates and colleagues.

They have prepared a list of lawbreakers that they will send to colleges and companies whose students and staff have committed the offenders, with a request that the names be displayed on the college or company notice board. This, they believe, will embarrass the offenders enough to make them more careful.

The police wrote to college principals and company managements that they have taken this decision as various previous measures have failed. They have sent list of 500 offending students to principals of 67 colleges over the city, and another of 250 offenders to 40 companies in which they are employed.

In the letter to principals, the police said it was up to them to discipline the students. Pune being an educational hub, many students stay in hostels independently and don't have parents to discipline them. "So it is the onus of the college to mould and discipline them," the police said.

They have requested the colleges not to allow the students to park their vehicles in college parking lots unless they produce a driving licence. In addition to displaying the names on their notice boards, the police have requested colleges and companies to penalise them at their level.

The police have fined 35 students of Wadia College, 22 of Fergusson College, 16 of Poona College, 49 of Bharati Vidyapeeth, 19 of MIT Group colleges, 39 of DY Patil Group of Institutes, 30 of Symbiosis Group of Institutes, 26 of SP College, 15 each of Sinhagad college and Modern college and 12 of Garware College.

Heading: This Dassera, gold buyers likely to get green ‘toppings’ - Indian Express
Content:
The mood is somber at the Faraskhana police station, under whose jurisdiction falls the city's red light area of Budhwar Peth. The rank and file is rattled by the allegations of a 17-year-old girl from Hyderabad, who has accused 14 policemen of raping her at a lodge in Nana Peth in 2005 and said that girls are first brought before the police and then sent to brothels.

One police officer admitted that morale was low while most denied the allegations. "The morale of the police has taken a severe beating due to the allegations. The police feel that their image has been tarnished," said the officer, speaking on condition of anonymity.

He added, "Some vested groups are out to defame the police. The reports in the media are highly critical of the police. The president on the National Law Trust, Khalid Nishu, who has taken a stand on behalf of the girl, has several cases registered against him. He is accused in cases of rape, dowry demand and cheating. The Hyderabad police issued a lookout notice against him May 2008."

Joint Commissioner of Police Rajendra Sonawane said, "All the allegations will be verified. We will employ narco analysis and lie detector tests, if need be. The crime branch team headed by deputy commissioner of police Anil Kumbhare is investigating the case. Since this case is being investigated, I cannot say any more at this juncture. A lot of people talk nonsense, but the truth will be known after the findings of the inquiry are out."

Senior police inspector V T Pawar, posted at Faraskhana, said the police play a positive role. "As and when we get information, we crack down and rescue girls forced into prostitution. We have rescued as many as 366girls in two years."

Heading: Special trains - Indian Express
Content:
The latest to join the green brigade in the city, the jewellers may gift every customer, who purchase gold from them on Dassera (buying gold on Dassera is considered auspicious), a Shami tree sapling.

The Department of Social Forestry has proposed to distribute about one lakh saplings of Shami tree to the Pune Jewellers Association, which is considering gifting the saplings to those who buy gold from them on Dassera which will fall on October 9. The idea is to urge people to plant more trees and save the dwindling Shami trees from vanishing.

The state Social Forestry department has sent a letter in this regard to the president of Pune Jewellers' Association, Fatechand Ranka requesting him to consider the proposal of distributing Shami saplings to consumers.

"The premise is certainly good and we are keen to implement it this year. But before we move in that direction, we need to hold a joint meeting with the Social Forestry and Association panel," said Ranka.

Director of Department of Social Forestry, Prakash Thosre said, "We have created a bank of about four lakh Shami seedlings. Out of this, we have plans to sell about one lakh saplings to the jewellers, who can gift them to their consumers. We will rope in the volunteers of National Green Corps (Rashtriya Harit Sena), which has school students among them, for help." "Apart from jewellers, we are also considering banks and establishments where there will be a flow of customers on Dassera," Thosre said.

Meanwhile, the Association has sent around 600 circulars about the initiative to its members. "Once we finalise on the implementation of the plan, we might gift the saplings to the consumers on the spot or give them a token and ask them to collect the saplings from the stalls set up by the Social Forestry department," said Ranka.

Heading: Jimmy Connors to start new tennis academy - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Railways has decided to run a Commonwealth special train between Pune and Hazrat Nizamuddin to meet the demands of passengers during the commonwealth youth games.

The train will depart from Pune station on every Tuesday and Saturday.

It will ply from Pune on October 4,7,11,14 and18. Train no 0178 will run from Hazrat Nizamuddin on every Wednesday and Sunday on September 5,8,12,15 and 19.

The reservation for Pune Hazrat Nizamuddin express will be opened from September 12.

* The Central Railways is now running a special local train from Pune to Lonavala to cater to the rush during the Ganesh festival. The train leaves Pune station at 1.25 am and reaches Lonavala at 2.55 am. The train will run till September 15, according to railway PRO Y K Singh.

Heading: Ayush Nahar does city proud - Indian Express
Content:
Neil Macleod, director of Savills, a global real estate provider, in collaboration with Jayant Pawar and the Solaris group of companies will soon develop a resort in the Pune- Mumbai-Goa triangle.

The resort, which will be constructed in an area of 250 acres, will incorporate a residential tennis academy called Jimmy Connors Tennis Academy, an 18-hole PGA Golf course, a five star hotel and SPA surrounded by 100 exclusive villas. "We will be focusing on quality and style with superb sporting facilities. Today, we see the start of it with the inception of the first Jimmy Connors Tennis Academy in India," said Macleod.

"Being a tennis player and staying just behind the Deccan Gymkhana tennis courts since childhood, I have grown up playing and following the game of tennis and legends like Jimmy Connors. We are exploring various opportunities of working with Jimmy Connors," said Jayant Pawar.

When Connors was asked why he chose India, he said,

"I believe that there is talent among the youth and they have a never-say-die attitude. These are two essential qualities that make a champion. Also people from Savills and Solaris have been very cooperative, thus making this whole process much easier." He also said that he would be looking for players who are willing to make tennis their top priority. "Our aim is to groom those players who are truly interested in the game and gradually improve upon them," he said.

Heading: Cop injured as jeep hits motorcycle - Indian Express
Content:
Ayush Nahar, a student of standard 6 currently studying in St. Vincent's school, won gold medal in the 6th sub-junior state Wushu competition held from September 5 to 7 at the Swayamvar Mangal Karyalaya Barshi, Solapur. He won the gold in the 20 kg category and was also awarded a trophy for 'Best Fighter' in this event.

His coach, Tushar Apte, will now help him prepare for the national level tournament, which is scheduled to take place sometime during the month of November.

Heading: Captivating clicks - Indian Express
Content:
A traffic police sub inspector officer sustained injuries after a jeep driver hit the motorcycle he was riding at Shivaji Road in Kasba Peth on Tuesday.

The driver, who was identified as Santosh Sopan Shinde was later arrested by the police. Shinde is a resident of Shindewadi in Haveli taluka.

Sub inspector Raut, riding a motorcycle, was on his way to Gadgil chowk when Shinde, who was driving his jeep at great speed hit the motorcycle at the back. Raut sustained injuries on his leg. Raut has registered a complaint against the accused at the Faraskhana police station.

Heading: Who was Dali? - Indian Express
Content:
Glimpses of Pune Festival – a photography exhibition by Santosh Potdar revived the memory of the remarkable performances Pune Festival has witnessed so far

Those moments froze in time serving the document of performances that created history. Nineteen years that witnessed the amount of talent being showcased at Pune Festival did not just remain a faint memory, lost in the clutches of the transition of time. Thanks to the efforts of Santosh Potdar, who since last 19 years clicked tirelessly to capture every single moment of the festival. The moments which when put together provided the art lovers with a visual treat.

And now those frozen moments graced the wall of the photography exhibition that Potdar had put up this Pune Festival. Glimpses of Pune Festival had 220 photographes of the event under three galleries — Summary, Mahilautsava and Celebrity.

The exhibition spanned across years, reviving the memory of various cultural performances that graced the festival. " Hema Malini in these 19 years has performed more than 15 times and has performed 14 different ballets. I have clicked her pictures every year thus in a way documenting each and every move of it," shares Potdar. For Potdar, photographing artistes is an art form he is completely dedicated to. "A photographer is one who is thoroughly familiar with his or her subject. When you are photographing a performer you must have the knowledge of what he or she is performing," elaborates Potdar. According to Potdar one gets a perfect frame when a particular segment ends. "When a stanza ends the performer pauses for a second and that is when you get a perfect frame," elaborates Potdar.

An expert in capturing just the right moment, Potdar feels use of flash during a performance can mar the quality of the composition to a great extent. Potdar who himself has clicked maximum number of photos without a flash, advices, "It's very important for a photographer to know when to use a flash and when not to. To preserve the originality of an artiste's expression it is important that the flash is turned off otherwise it will divert the attention of the artiste causing him or her to miss out on one bhaav or the other."

From celebrities to budding talents who performed at Ugawate Tare, Potdar in his photochemical masterpieces preserves a storehouse of talent that can be showcased to revive the memory of the festival. 220 photographes hung at the exhibition to provide the testimony of the talent that Pune Festival has not only showcased but also churned out since last 19 years.

Heading: Exploring new realms - Indian Express
Content:
Getting Dali and Dada mixed up is a criminal mistake. However, there was a phase when many Surrealists crossed over to become Dadaists. Salvadore Dali was a painter who remained committed to the aesthetics of beauty and his fevered imagination continued to conjure up images that were often considered the ravings of a mad man. He did, however, admit to being influenced by the Dadaist movement, but many aesthetes are of the opening that Dali's work was too painterly to be anti-establishment. Dali was born in Catalonia, Spain, in 1904. Dali's father, Salvadore Dali Cusi, held an exhibition of his charcoal drawings in 1916 and subsequent trips to Paris were instrumental in forming his decision to become an artist. The hallmark of Dali was not just his eccentricities but his vision combined with impeccable skill. His command over the brush could conjure up images that were hyper-real and yet he would employ distortions and fantasy landscapes to transform reality.

Demystify art, e-mail georgina.maddox@expressindia.com

Heading: Deceased dreams - Indian Express
Content:
After rocking the nation with Punjabi songs, Daler Mehndi admires the Supreme, the Sufi way

Daler Mehndi is a inventive singer who got youngsters all over the world dance to his Punjabi pop. In a zestful performance at the Pune Festival, Mehndi's husky tones resonated to the beats of all time Bhangra hits, as he had a huge crowd grooving to his numbers at the musical nite on Tuesday at the Pune Festival. Mehndi and his troupe, performed to a vigour packed show that had the best of Mehndi's hits over the decade.

"Well you can say that my music is universal and it has been adored and accepted extensively by the people, that is the reason why I am here today, performing at this renowned festival," said Mehndi, who began his performance with his personal favorite Namo Namo and pulled the crowd through his songs and remixes of various film songs and albums. "We had sung Namo Namo in concerts across Pakistan and it was a big hit. Live concerts are about how competently you present before the thousands of people, it is a joint effort and my troupe is very meticulous."

After having heaved the nation to caper to the beats of Punjabi pop and bhangra for more than a decade, Daler Mehndi is now onto experimenting the flipside with his first Sufi album Bismillah. "The compositions of Bismillah do not talk about a particular personality or any one religion but reveres the supreme power. The Sufi music in this album is extremely poignant and it had a tremendous influence on the musicians during its making. Many have worked free of charge. I have been working on this album since the last two years and am sure it will take the country by storm," adds Mehndi who has not only sung for the album but has also written and composed music for Bismillah.

Having lent his voice for chart toppers of films like Rang de Basanti and Sing is Kinng, Mehndi wants to continue with his own albums besisdes playback singing. "The Punjabi numbers in the films are used to pull the crowd. However, it is the taste of the world. The music, rhythm and style has been widely used in Indian and international compositions," adds Mehndi.

The singer attributes his versatility to his strong classical base. Reviewing his career Mehndi says, "The most fulfilling thing is the uniform hype on my work ever since 1995. I have given one hit each year that has musically united the nation and this unification through my music has been extremely gratifying."

Heading: American politics knocks at LU’s door - Indian Express
Content:
Ruzbech Bharucha, in his book My God is a Juvenile Deliquent, brings forth the plight of the teenagers in the observation homes nationwide

An agonizing sentiment seals the hopes, as one reads through My God is a Juvenile deliquent. The book authored by the city-based Ruzbeh Bharucha, focuses on the emotional, physical and psychological life of the juvenile delinquents. It renders out the facts in the observation homes across the country.

"The journey for the last one and a half year with the children who are mostly migrants has been depressing. So much that I fell ill several times and thought of discontinuing the study. It is the hostility and the complete despair that I have examined in the observation homes. There are more than 30 000 children who are juvenile delinquents in India. The children might have committed a petty crime in the past but many a times the judicial custody of 14 days is extended given the workload on judiciary. The principal magistrates are overloaded with work and the children are ignored. Even if they are set free the cops slap false records against them for professional elevations and the vulnerable children are sent back to the observation homes. It is very unfortunate that no one has ever attempted to bring this issue to light," adds Bharucha who feels that the system is harbouring an environment where reform is not talking place and this can nurture criminal tendencies in a big way.

"The appalling experiences have hardened the teenagers so much that they now are provoked to indulge into anti-social activities in vengeance," adds the author.

Bharucha has written books as well as directed documentaries that have portrayed issues dealing with the life of women and their children in the prisons, AIDS and HIV in Tihar jail, as well as paranormal and spiritual forces in the cosmos. "Paranormal life is what I like to write and indulge in but noting these socially grave issues is my responsibility," says Barucha whose book Fakir has been on the top bestseller list last year.

"I am presently working on a script and also planning to make a film on my first fiction Rest In Pieces," says Bharucha who is also the executive editor of the newly launched The 4th D Wellbeing Journal.

Heading: Is JE vaccine effective? Study to begin in Oct - Indian Express
Content:
With the US presidential election generating a huge excitement across the globe, even remote corners of Uttar Pradesh have not remained untouched.

On Wednesday, the US embassy in association with the UGC Academic Staff College of Lucknow University held a lecture on "US Politics" in Lucknow to make people aware about the issues that dominate presidential elections in the United States.

Delivering the lecture, Michael P Macy, counselor for cultural affairs at the US embassy, highlighted the significance of local issues and the involvement of people in it. Macy said US citizens have always been more involved in elections of local representatives than with the presidential race as local issues matter the most.

"US citizens are more concerned about elections of local leaders like state representatives and Governor because only these elected people take up the local issues. During the 2004 presidential election, over 64 per cent of US voters had registered themselves for voting but only 50 per cent of them exercised their franchise. Above 90 per cent of them turned out to vote during the election of state representatives," Macy said.

He reasoned this by saying: "American presidents hold limited powers. They could neither initiate a budget for any purpose nor declare a war. They could only check and balance the power of state. The president never considers the problems of poor and middle class population."

On the other hand, Macy said that local representatives like Governor and Senators could take financial and development related decisions at a local level.

"For example, local issues like same-sex marriage, ban on greyhound racing, repealing of state's income tax, religious issues and change in course curriculum are believed to be more important for public where government could not interfere."

But these issues comprise the list of referendums declared by the contestants of local representatives to get the mandate, Macy added.

Macy also said that for the November 4 elections, there are only two contestants for president, 218 contestants for state-level leaders and 102 for Senators election.

Macy, who had completed his research on "Non-State judicial process for Muslim community" at Aligarh Muslim University, chose the occasion to donate 22 books on politics to the Lucknow University.

Heading: Potato farmers in dire straits as prices drop after bumper harvest - Indian Express
Content:
Even two years after the introduction of China's Japanese Encephalitis (JE) vaccine in the country, no sero-surveillance study has been conducted to check its efficacy.

This, after the Centre had recommended that the National Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation conduct a study in this connection in February.

The sero-surveillance study is now expected to start by mid-October in Uttar Pradesh and Assam.

In Uttar Pradesh, the research will be conducted by NIV-Pune in collaboration with Gorakhpur's B R D Medical College. PATH will provide technical support to the study.

In Assam, Regional Medical Research Centre of Indian Council of Medical Rerearch will conduct the study in collaboration with the Army Medical College.

"It is true that the sero-surveillance as well as the case control study to ascertain the efficacy of the vaccine has been pending for a long time. But now the ground is being set to initiate the study as soon as possible," said Dr Pritu Dhalaria, programme manager of the JE Project team in India for PATH — an international non-profit organisation that provides technical support to the Centre in its JE programme.

Dhalaria added, "Dr M M Gore of National Institute of Virology (NIV), Pune will be the principal investigator for the project in Uttar Pradesh."

The study will be based on 200 JE cases from Uttar Pradesh and Assam. The project will also study around 800 children, picked up randomly.

According to sources, a case study from Nepal was taken into consideration before the vaccine was introduced in 2006.

According to the study, the vaccine provided 95 per cent protection — out of 100 children immunised, only 95 were completely protected from the disease.

Till last year, children belonging to 18 districts of Uttar Pradesh and four in Assam, have been administered the vaccine.

Heading: Violence erupts in Azamgarh, six injured, 22 held - Indian Express
Content:
The euphoria among the potato growers in the state after a record harvest this year turned out to be short-lived.

The farmers in the state's potato belt, which stretches from Kanpur to Agra, now rue the record production that has plummeted the price of the vegetable to a record low of Rs 350 to Rs 400 per quintal in all major markets.

Against the average production of 100 to 105 lakh metric tonnes (MT), this year during the Holi, potato production touched 140 lakh MT. The state consumes close to 60 lakh MT and the rest is either exported to other states or foreign markets. During March and April, the farmers had to face a tough time to store their harvest in the cold storages that displayed "house full" signboards. Now, with prices plummeting, the farmers are in no mood to take out their crops from storages.

"The glut in the market has ruined farmers and also the cold storage owners," said Raghavendra Singh who owns a chain of cold storages in Sirsaganj in Mainpuri district. "Against the usual 40 per cent release of stored potatoes by August every year, this year farmers have hardly taken out 10 per cent," he added.

The potato farmers and cold store owners categorically blame the UP State Agriculture Produce Marketing Board for its failure to promote the export of potato.

In 2005, the Samajwadi Party government had taken up the export of the potato from state and to ensure participation of farmers in potato export scheme, an "UP Potato Export Facilitation Society" was also set up with 21 farmers as members from the potato belt of Farrukhabad, Kannauj, Agra, Etawah, Mainpuri, Ferozabad, Meerut and Hapur. The society included representatives from cold storage industry. The UP Agriculture Produce marketing Board had also provided "Brand Promotion Grant' to the potato farmers participating in export scheme. As a result, 250 MT of potato was exported in 2006.

But for the last two years, the office of the UP Potato Export Facilitation Society, set up at Vashi in Mumbai at the cost of Rs 25 lakh, is lying unused. The state accounts for close to 50 per cent of the potato produced in India, followed by West Bengal. UP is the 12th largest potato producer at the globally.

"The lack of enterprise among the potato growers and traders was the key reason for the poor exports and we have done everything possible from our end to promote exports like providing grants for brand promotion and transport subsidy.

Yet this year, the export was mere 400 MT to Nepal and 100 MT to Mumbai," said Rajesh Kumar Singh, director of the Agriculture produce marketing board.

Minister for Horticulture Narayan Singh, who hails from Agra, said: "There is some problem due to the bumper crop this year but there is no unrest among the farmers." He dismissed the hardships faced by the farmers as "malicious propaganda by the opposition parties".

Heading: Parivar men held for threatening VHP leader - Indian Express
Content:
Violence erupted in Bilariyaganj area of Azamgarh district after members of two communities clashed late on Tuesday night.

The incident occurred after some people pelted stones on the gate of a shrine, where the prayers were being offered.

In response, annoyed community members gathered and tried to damage shops belonging to the other community.

Over six persons sustained minor injuries in the incident, the police said.

Superintendent of Police (Rural) S K Rana said: "The mob, angered by the throwing of stones, started raising slogans and damaged shops, which had been closed by then. The other community retaliated."

The police rushed to the spot and dispersed the mob. A big contingent of police has been deployed in and around the area to avoid any untoward incident, he added.

Senior Superintendent of Police Ramit Sharma said, "Both sides have lodged FIRs and 22 people, 11 from each community, have been arrested."

Rana said police have warned both the communities to maintain peace and the miscreants would be dealt with strictly.

Heading: Govt waives entertainment tax for the Children’s Film Festival - Indian Express
Content:
The Ayodhya police have arrested two men, one belonging to Bajrang Dal and another to the Hindu Yuva Vahini for threatening to kill Ram Vilas Vedanti, a senior Vishwa Hindu Parishad leader.

The accused had allegedly posed as members of SIMI and Al-Qaeda.

On August 30, Vedanti had lodged a complaint with the police saying that he was receiving death threats from some SIMI and Al-Qaeda extremists on his mobile phone.

The police traced the phone calls and arrested the accused — Ramesh Tiwari and Pawan Pandey — late on Tuesday evening.

While Tiwari is president of Katra unit of Bajrang Dal in Gonda district, Pandey is a convener of Hindu Yuva Vahini in Katra. Senior Superintendent of Police Faizabad R K S Rathore said, "We are interrogating the accused."

In-charge of Ayodhya Kotwali police station A K Singh said: "The police are trying to find out connections of the youths. A few more persons are also suspected to be involved. We are trying to arrest them."

Incidentally, on August 30, when Vedanti had called a media conference at his residence in Ayodhya to tell the media about the death threats he received, the two youths were present at the venue.

Asked if the accused belonged to Hindu outfits, since they were also seen at his residence, Vedanti said: "They must be Muslims bearing Hindu names. They were not present at my media conference."

Mahant Yugal Kishore Sharan Shastry, a former member of VHP's central committee and a former aide of Vedanti, said: "Vedanti wants to contest Lok Sabha election from Gonda. To prepare his votebank, he and his supporters have been spreading communal tension in the constituency."

Their aim, he said, is to divide votes on the basis of religion. "These death threats are also a part of their strategy," he added.

Vedanti has had a controversial political background. During his public meetings, he has been repeatedly urging the Hindu masses to repeat Gujarat experiments in Uttar Pradesh.

As an MP from Machhlishahar in 13th Lok Sabha, he was charged with various corruption cases for wrongfully spending the funds allocated to him under the Member of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme.

Vedanti had contested for the Amethi Lok Sabha seat against Rahul Gandhi in the last elections on a BJP ticket but lost his deposit after managing just 2,000 votes.

Heading: Gomti Nagar to get public library - Indian Express
Content:
The state government has decided to waive the entertainment tax from the Children's Film Festival that began on September 5 in Lucknow.

As per the orders issued by Govindan Nair, Principal Secretary (Tax and Registration Department) on Wednesday, no entry ticket will be charged from children and their parents for the festival either by cinema owners or the management of any school.

The 17 films screened during the month-long film festival have been produced by the Information and Broadcasting Ministry.

Some the prominent names include The March of Times, Mother Teresa Mubarak Begum, Messenger, The Balloon, The Last Horizon and The Nature and Man.

The films are being screened between 9.30 am to 12.30 pm in Capital cinema in Hazratganj.

During the film festival, no poster or picture will be displayed by the cinema owner which will have a detrimental effect on the children, the government order stated.

If the cinema hall does not abide by the norms, then it will have to pay entertainment tax in future and will be charged tax for the present screenings as well, the order further stated.

Heading: ‘Fossils help in understanding plant evolution’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) has invited Expression of Interest (EOI) from various organisations for setting up a public library in Gomti Nagar. It will be the first ever library constructed by the LDA in any of its housing schemes.

In the EOI, the organisation will have to provide details like library profile, operations, technology and management system. A double-storey building that was constructed two years ago in 746-square metre area in Vipul Khand-3 will house the library. The building was earlier meant for a badminton court and cost the LDA Rs 46 lakh.

"Along with books and journals on various subjects, the library will be equipped with audio visual facilities, a cyber café and a reading hall," said LDA Vice-Chairman Mukesh Kumar Meshram.

He said that a very nominal rent will be charged from the organisation that will run the library.

An official associated with the housing scheme said: "Along with a wide collection of books, the library will have a reception, a record room, a waiting lounge on the ground floor and a meeting hall on the first floor." He added, "Besides, a parking space of 100 square metre and open space of 140 square metre will also be provided for the convenience of visitors."

Justifying the decision to set up a library that was earlier meant for setting up a badminton court, Meshram said: "The LDA was not making any profit from it. Once the library is opened, the LDA will fund it. The agency will continue to maintain the building in future."

Dinesh Mishra, Vice-President of Gomti Nagar Jan Kalyan Samiti expressed pleasure over the LDA decision to open a public library in Gomti Nagar.

"At present, retired people and students have to depend on public libraries in Hazratganj and Kaiserbagh. But this library will be a great help for residents of Gomti Nagar and nearby localities," said Mishra.

Heading: HC seeks records on appointment of Chandra - Indian Express
Content:
Scientists must not only update their knowledge of fossils but also of living plants in order to get the overall picture, said Professor Sir Peter R Crane of University of Chicago.

Crane proposed this in his speech on "Fossils and Angiosperm Evolution: Lessons from Fagales and Prospects for the Future" on the occasion of Foundation Day at Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeobotany (BSIP).

Providing an instance, he said the discovery and description of well preserved fossil materials belonging to the Cretacious and Cenozoic eras has allowed scientists to understand the evolution of Fagales, a species of trees that include oaks, beeches and walnut trees.

He said there was a great potential for fossil fuel exploration in the country. "There is still much to learn about bio-diversity and extinction of plants," said Crane.

Calling this an exciting time to be in the field, he said fossils have boosted the study of angiosperm palaeobotany, which deals with fossils of angiosperms — flowering plants that have hidden seeds.

Talking about the institute's founder, Director Dr N C Mehrotra said Birbal Sahni had viewed fossils from an overall perspective, including extinct and living plants.

Ajaib Singh Brar, Vice-Chancellor of the Lucknow University, said fossil research offers great potential for exploration of petroleum products.

Heading: BSNL, HCL tie up to offer PC-Broadband package - Indian Express
Content:
The Allahabad High Court asked the government on Wednesday to produce the records related to consultation process of the appointment of Justice Satish Chandra, whose appointment was challenged by an advocate, M C Gupta.

Hearing the writ petition, a Division Bench of Justice Shushil Harkauli and Justice Vikram Nath ordered that the documents should be brought in a sealed envelope and only the court will be entitled to examine these. The records will be produced before the court by Friday and the next hearing is on September 16, said Ravi Kiran Jain, counsel of the petitioner.

Gupta, a practicing lawyer at the Allahabad High Court, had filed the petition and requested the court to issue a writ of quo warranto, directing Chandra to justify the constitutionality of his appointment as an HC judge.

Heading: Man alleges harassment at the hands of policeman - Indian Express
Content:
No longer will prospective Internet users have to wait for a long time for a connection. According to a tie-up between Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) and manufacturer HCL, the customers will be offered a broadband connection and a personal computer (PC) at discounted rates.

"This is an attempt to improve the PC density in the state, which is very poor compared to other states. We are offering a rebate of 10 per cent in broadband connection while the payment for the PCs can be made in installments," said Rajesh Kumar, general manager, marketing, BSNL.

Hyderabad and Trichur have been chosen for a pilot project that will ease payment processes. A single bill will be created for repaying the PC installments, broadband and the telephone bill. BSNL will implement a centralised billing system for this purpose and launch it on a nationwide scale after a successful implementation at the two cities.

The BSNL will waive the installation charges and registration fees as well as reduce tariff rates on existing and new plans. The most economical package — Plan 250 — will be available at Rs 199 for the first year.

The PC manufacturer is offering a range of desktops and laptops ranging from Rs 14,000 to Rs 33,499. A tie-up with other PC assemblers like Acer India, LG Electronics India, e-SYS Technologies and Sai Infosystems is also in the pipeline.

Heading: Defamation suit: Tytler may depose in city court today - Indian Express
Content:
Chander Parkash, a resident of Dugri, has alleged that he is being threatened and harassed by Division Number 5 Station House Officer (SHO) Shivinder Singh Dhillon.

Talking to mediapersons, Chander Parkash alleged that, "The SHO has connived with one of my relatives who lives on the Chandigarh Road. On March 2, the SHO took me to the police station and slapped false corruption charges against me. The SHO also took away my gold bracelet, two gold rings, mobile phone and Rs 6,500. He further demanded Rs 1 lakh to release me." Chander Parkash claims that he is just out of jail after the High Court granted him bail in the case. Parkash also claims that police harassment has affected his business adversely as he had to close down his hotel outside bus stand in the city.

Meanwhile, SHO Shivinder Singh denied the allegations claiming, "The man enjoys close proximity with a senior police officer and used to take money from people on the pretext of getting their work done. This is what he did with his relative Devinder Kapur from whom he took around Rs 1 lakh for some work. As per the deal, Chander Parkash should have returned the money which he did not. He rather threatened Kapur with dire consequences if he asked for money. We lodged an FIR and proceeded as per the law and will do the same in the due course of the case."

Chander Parkash, meanwhile, alleged that, "Kapur nurtures ill feelings against me after I turned down the matrimonial alliance between his daughter and my son."

Heading: Tax evasion detected - Indian Express
Content:
Congress leader Jagdish Tytler, one of the main accused in the 1984 Sikh riots case, is likely to depose before the city court tomorrow. Tytler faces a criminal defamation case filed against him by a well-known lawyer practicing in the Supreme Court, H S Phoolka. The case will be heard in the court of JMIC K.K. Bansal.

Harpreet Makkar, counsel for the complainant, informed, "As per the law, Tytler should appear tomorrow failing which the court can issue arrest warrants against him." Giving the details of the case, Makkar said, 'This case was filed some two years back when during a discussion on a national television channel, Tytler had made defamatory utterances against Phoolka. Tytler had used words like blackmailers and men who had eaten away widow pension…. terms like this."

On the issue of this case being filed in Ludhiana, Makkar said, "Phoolka belongs to Ludhiana and he has been a student of Punjab Agricultural University. Moreover as per the law, any court can admit this case where the defamatory article has reached in form of publication or broadcast as programme. Notable here is that Tytler had a few days ago field a petition in the Punjab and Haryana High Court requesting for taking this case out of Punjab as he feared threat to his life in the state. Tytler had requested that this case be shifted to anywhere in Haryana. Makker informed, "The petition has been dismissed by the HC and hence the case still stays in Ludhiana."

Tytler along with Congress leaders H.K.L. Bhagat and Sajjan Kumar are the main accused for the engineering the 1984 Sikh riots that broke out after the then Prime Minister, Indira Gandhi was shot dead by her own bodyguards. Phoolka, who is the standing counsel for the 1984 riot victims, has meanwhile along with journalist Manoj Mitta written the first account of the 1984 riots in a book titled "When a tree shook Delhi."

Heading: Ishmeet’s kin reiterate demand for a CBI probe - Indian Express
Content:
The Income Tax department today raided three textile units, Shreyans Meters and Maini Hosiery, both located in Industrial Area -A, and Puneet Exports, situated at Janakpuri.

The survey raid was continuing till the time of filing of this report. The department officials said they had collected documents indicating tax evasion. However the exact amount of the evasion would be determined only after scanning various documents, they said.

Heading: Rs 1.88-cr worth loans to help BPL families - Indian Express
Content:
Family members of Star Voice of India 2007 winner Ishmeet Singh reiterated their demand for a CBI probe into the singer's death with the assistance of Interpol thrown in.

The demand was raised by the family members who have just returned from Male, Maldives, after their investigations at the beach resort where Ishmeet died while swimming.

Leading the pack, Ishmeet's uncle, Dr Charan Kamal Singh recounted his observation during the Maldives trip, at a press conference held today.

Dr Singh said that, "During our visit to Maldives from September 3 to 6, the family members met the Indian High Commission in Maldives, the police investigation team, officials and workers of the resort and the main organiser of the show for which Ishmeet had gone to the island nation."
