Picking holes in the eyewitness accounts of Vyom and Arunima, Dr Singh charged that not a single person - out of more than 250 odd employees of Chhaya Island Dhonveli Beach Rresort — had seen Ishmeet going or being at the swimming pool alive with them.

Dr Singh said, "Moreover, the statements given by both to the Indian High Commission and the police investigators are contradictory. While Vyom told the High Commission officials that he went along with Arunima and Ishmeet inside the pool whereas in his statement given to police investigators, he said, "I went to the resort's swimming pool with Ishmeet".

Similarly, said Dr Singh, the statements of Sanjit Shah of the Indian troupe and the local organiser, Hassan Ishan, in Maldives were also found to be contradictory.

Dr Singh also raised the issue of the head injury suffered by Ishmeet, which he claims remains unexplained. Dr Singh said, "Our main concern is how the injury was inflicted as neither the so-called eyewitness statement nor the preliminary investigations have been able to throw light on it," he said.

The family also displayed an SMS which it claims is very strange and which Ishmeet had received it on July 22. The SMS says, "VOI bn ne ka itna ghamand mat kro ue jyada din tak tumhara nhi rhega (don't be proud of being VOI so much won't last long)." "Exactly a week after that Ishmeet was no more," said Ishmeet's uncle, raising another angle to the conspiracy theory.

Heading: Make-over contest held at KCW - Indian Express
Content:
Manpreet Ayali, chairman, Zila Parishad, has informed that under the centrally-sponsored schemes, loans amounting to Rs 1.88 crore would be arranged for 244 beneficiaries — individuals and groups — from various banks during this financial year to enable them to start their own ventures.

Ayali today presided over the meeting of the governing body, set up for implementing schemes, to review the progress of these schemes.

Ayali said that the loans would be arranged for people living below poverty line and a subsidy of Rs 10,000 per family would be provided on the loans to the scheduled caste families and handicapped persons. He said that to the non-scheduled-caste families, Rs 7,500 per family would be provided as a subsidy.

In the meeting, Ayali asked the officers to ensure proper selection of the beneficiaries under these schemes and make arrangements for required training for starting their ventures. He said that the elected representatives should also be consulted while finalising the lists.

He told the officers to educate the people about these schemes in the villages, so that they could avail of the benefits.

Priyank Bharti, ADC (D), while addressing the meeting said that all the departments/officers had already been geared up to implement these schemes efficiently and added that no laxity on the part of any officer would be tolerated.

Among others present at the meeting included Ramesh Kumar Kapoor, APO, Ajit Singh, Lead Bank Officer, Punjab and Sind Bank, Harmesh Kumar, DDM NABARD, Neena Gupta, District Programme Officer, Gurdial Singh, Chairman Block Samiti Machhiwara, Balwant Singh, Chairman Block Samiti Ludhiana-1, Inderjit Singh Grerwal, Chairman Block Samiti Raikot, Gurmukh Singh Chairman Block Samiti Pakhowal and Sat Pal Singh Chairman Block Samiti Ludhiana- 2.

Heading: 14 held for thefts during rural police drive - Indian Express
Content:
About 40 students participated in the "Make-over contest" organised in the Department of Cosmetology of Khalsa College for Women, Civil Lines, on Wednesday.

The participants were asked undergo a make-over by altering their make-up, hair style, attire and jewellery in just 15 minutes. Pushpinder, Karishma Kapoor, Richa, Anjali and Rajveer Kaur were declared the winners at the contest.

"The contest was tight, and giving judgement was a tough call," said the judge, Rippy Chatwal from Shehnaz Hussain Herbalz.

Vyoma Agarwal of the Department of Cosmetology said the contest was aimed at exploring the potential and creativity of the students in make-over and styling.

The guest of honour, Dr Varinder Thind, principal of the college, appreciated the efforts of the staff and students. The staff members, Shama Mohindra, Renu Saini, Navjot Kaur and Amarpreet Kaur were also present on the occasion.

Congress leaders held
Five Congmen from Ludhiana including the district Congress president Jagmohan Sharma were among the 20 Congress leaders arrested today outside the Mini Secretariat in Chandigarh on Wednesday.

The leaders alleged that they were standing peacefully when police team came and said that they had violated Section 144. Among those held were Kamal Puri from Patiala. Later they were taken to Sector 3 police station.

Heading: Pharmacology quiz organised at CMC - Indian Express
Content:
The Ludhiana rural police have arrested 14 people during the last week and recovered stolen items worth 2 lakh from them. The drive has been carried out by the police parties from Sidhwan Bet, Raikot and Dehlon

The police, according to the SSP, Ludhiana Rural, Gurpreet Singh Bhullar, have recovered a car, inverters, jewellery besides Rs 70,000 in cash and 34 bags of wheat from their possession of the thieves. The total value of the stolen things is pegged at Rs 2,02,913.

Bhullar informed that the police party of Raikot arrested the accused Suresh Kumar, Deepak and Manpreet Singh and recovered Rs 70,000 in cash, and a diamond ring valued at Rs 25,000 from their possession. During the interrogation, the accused disclosed that they had cut the grills and stolen cash of Rs 84000 and one diamond ring from the Punjab Handloom shop situated at Raikot.

Similarly, the police party of Sidhwan Bet received a tip-off that Amritpal Singh, a resident of Shimlapuri, Kumar, a resident of Uttar Pradesh, Bablu, a resident of Lohara Colony, Shimlapuri, Pinku, a resident of Sahnewal, and Pappu, a resident of village Lohara were planning to commit a dacoity.

The police party of Dehlon arrested three accused, Baldev Singh and Shanker Bahadur, and recovered 34 bags of wheat which had been stolen from godowns of Markfed, Quila Raipur. The Jagraon police arrested the accused and recovered a Verna car.

Heading: Amit overpowers Aman to surge ahead - Indian Express
Content:
Department of Pharmacology, Christian Medical College and Hospital, organised fourth Annual Pharmacology Quiz, PHARMIZ-2008 in the hospital auditorium today.

Dr Abraham G Thomas, Director CMCH and Dr Sunil Kumar Singh, Principal CMC inaugurated the quiz. Dr Dinesh Baydal, acting head, Department of Pharmacology, explained the format of the quiz before conducting the quiz. He added that four teams from MBBS admission batches 2003, 2004, 2005 and 2006 were selected through a preliminary test.

Two students from each batch scoring highest marks were selected to form a team of that particular batch. The quiz was an audiovisual treat. There were six rounds, all rounds were on multi-media. History round was very interesting. Students appreciated the academic enrichment through this innovative quiz. Audience too got a chance to participate and won prizes. It was attended by faculty members and a large number of medical students of CMC.

The winners of the quiz were medical students Ankush PM and Jensi George, from the batch of 2005. Dr Sunil Kumar Singh, while distributing prizes, emphasised that fun filled activities like quiz in academics was very important to increase the interest level of students in the subject.

Dr Kim Mammen, Deputy Director, CMC, Dr VP Singh, Deputy Medical Superintendent, Dr Tejinder Singh and Dr Sheila Das, Vice Principals were also present at the occasion.

Heading: Salam Zindagi brings succour to  thalassaemic kids - Indian Express
Content:
Showing tremendous potting skills and cue ball control, Amit Verma edged past Aman Khullar 3-0 (62-34, 47-17, 57-14) to surge ahead in the top four in round robin league during the 23rd Chandigarh Billiards and Snooker Championship being held in Sector 22 in Chandigarh on Wednesday.

In senior snooker category, top seed Rajat Kheneja defeated Arif Akhtar 3-0. Rajat came up with break of 42, 28 in the first frame. Continuing with his fine form, Rajat made breaks of 26, 29. Arif showed some resistance in the third frame but Rajat cleared the table with break of 35. Rajat has also moved ahead in top four in the league.

In an exciting match, Sameer Chandi outplayed Sanjay Duggal 3-1. With small breaks of 22, 21 Chandi sealed the first set. Sanjay claimed the second set in a brilliant effort 60-48. But in third and fourth frame, Chandi potted well and won 75-32 and 53-38.

Sandeep Duggal snuffed out the challenge of Shiwan Choudhary 3-0 in straight sets. Sandeep Duggal made break of 32, 28 to win first frame 98-22. The second frame was claimed by Sandeep 58-38. Third frame also Sandeep clinched by Sandeep.

In junior snooker semi-final match, Madhur defeated Rishab 2-0 (46-31,36-24) to reach the final.

Results:

Sr. Snooker: Sumeer Chandi bt Sanjay Duggal 3-1(52-32, 48-60, 75-32, 53-38), Rajat Khaneja bt Arif Akhtar 3-0 (81-03, 47-11, 60-51), Sandeep Duggal bt Shiven Choudhary 3-0 (98-22, 58-38, 76-34), Amit Verma bt Aman Khullar 3-0 (62-34,47-17, 57-14).

Jr. Snooker: Madhur bt. Rishab 2-0 (46-31, 36-24).

Heading: Swimming event organised - Indian Express
Content:
Salaam Zindagi Foundation organised its eighth blood donation camp in a row, where 51 bottles of blood were donated for thalassaemic children.

Satate Minister Madan Lal Bagga, who was present on the occasion, appreciated the efforts of Salaam Zindagi in helping the poor thalassamic children and other downtrodden sections of the society. Bagga assured every possible help to the NGO.

Dr Baldev Singh Aulakh, a prominent transplant surgeon and kidney specialist of DMCH explained the importance of blood donation and other medical aspects related to blood donation in length.

S.M. Sharma, principal of Arya College for Boys, also hailed the efforts of the foundation on the occasion. Manjit Saini, president of Salaam Zindagi Foundation, thanked the team of Bharat Social Welfare Society led by Pawan Kumar, Balram Mehta and Ashok Marwaha.

Heading: Kabaddi tourney from today - Indian Express
Content: Sat Paul Mittal School, Phase-2, Dugri organised a swimming gala here today. Over175 swimmers participated in the events in the age-groups of U-6, U-8, U-10, U-12 and U-14 in both boys and girls categories. Lt.Col Dr.D B Sharma, Director of the school welcomed parents and also highlighted the achievements of the school in sports for the session 2008-2009.

Heading: Patiala’s Isha wins ‘Boogie Woogie’ kids dance championship - Indian Express
Content:
Power Grid Corporation of India Limited, Northern Region Transmission System-II (NRTS-II) will organise a two-day Regional Kabaddi Tournament at Sector 42 Sports Complex from September 11 to 12. Five teams from corporate centre, SRTS-I, ERTS-I, NRTS-I and hosts NRTS-II, comprising players from Hyderabad, Tamil Nadu, Patna, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Punjab, and Jammu and Kashmir will participate in the tournament that will be played on a league-cum-knockout basis. Roshan Sunkaria (IAS), commissioner, Chandigarh Municipal Corporation will inaugurate the championship.

Inter-school tournament from September 26
The Education Department, Chandigarh Administration, will conduct the third phase of inter-school tournament in various disciplines from September 26 to October 4 at different venues in Chandigarh. U-14, U-17, U-19 for (boy and girls): Chess (GMHS-38), U-14 (girls) cricket (GMSS-32) U-16, 19 (boys) (GMSS-19).

Heading: Saving Bhawai: Carrying the tradition on his head for 35 years now! - Indian Express
Content:
Fourteen-year-old Isha Dang of Patiala did the city and Punjab proud by winning the 'Boogie Woogie' Under-15 Kids Dance Championship in Mumbai yesterday.

Competing with 43 dancers from all over the country, Isha proved the best performer in the grand finale of the contest held in Mumbai on the intervening night of September 8 and 9. She has won a trophy and Rs 5 lakh in cash. Incidentally, Isha is the first kid dancer from Punjab to have won such a contest at the national level. The grand finale of the Boogie Woogie Kids Championship would be aired on Sony Television on October 10.

She had competed with a total of eight finalists from all over the country in the finals. She earlier cleared different stages of the contest from amongst a large number of dancers. Incidentally, Isha had earlier won the second prize in Boogie Woogie Kids championship in July 2004. An elated Isha told The Indian Express on phone, "I am happy to have won the contest. My hard work and training has paid off. I thank Punjabis and Patialvis for supporting me all along."

She said she would now concentrate on her studies as she aspires to compete for the civil services examination. Her dance teacher Daisy Ahluwalia was also present with her during the grand finale, besides her parents.

Isha is a Class IX student of the local Our Lady of Fatima Convent School. A prolific dancer, she had camped in Mumbai for the past over two months to win the contest.

She had started dancing as a hobby at the tender age of three. She has so far given at least 190 performances in India, UAE and Singapore, and has won as many as 92 prizes at both national and international level.

Daughter of accountant Harinder and teacher Meenakshi, Isha has turned out the pride of Punjab after winning the contest. She would be arriving in her home town Patiala tomorrow morning, where she would be accorded a warm welcome.

Heading: A ground for budding sportspersons - Indian Express
Content:
It is not an easy task to carry seven pitchers on the head and still be able to maintain balance. Certainly not, when one dances around and stands on upturned glasses or on the edge of swords.

"This is called Bhawai, the traditional folk dance form of Rajasthan. It is a unique dance form that originated from the need to transport water across a distance in the desert as womenfolk carry pitchers from oases to homes," says Dr Roop Singh Shekhawat.

Carrying the load of 'pitchers' for 35 years now, Dr Shekhawat is a reputed artiste from Rajasthan, who is known for his efforts to save the dying art form of Bhawai.

A PhD in Rajasthani folk dances, Dr Shekhawat is one of the very few well-known artists of Bhawai in the country at present. He today left the audience spellbound with his performance, with a touch of Kathak, at the Ramgarhia Girls' College.

However in his early days, he was not only questioned on his performances of Bhawai, being a male and a Rajput, but he was also subjected to social boycott by his own community.

"Now it's different, I am now invited by the President to perform. The same people, who despised me, now honour me. They have now understood that I was only taking care of our traditions. Today, I have an institute of my own which trains students in Kathak, Bhawai and other traditional folk dances," he adds.

"Sadly, Bhawai is being called a fast-dying dance form today as the dance requires a lot of dedication and concentration. And that is why I have been carrying this load on my head for 35 years now," he said, when asked about his love of Bhawai, "I can now proudly say that today I have trained ten students, seven boys and three girls in this dance form."

Narrating his tale, he said, "I was 15 when I first took to this dance form after my Guruji once noticed me balancing pots on my head. 'You are born to carry them,' he told me, and I understood it. Though it is replete with gestures and expresions of a woman, the dance is practised by both men and women."

Bhawai's nail-biting, gyrating moves with impeccable expressions generated so much curiosity and interest among the students that for half an hour's performance, there was not even a single head that turned away from where he performed on the stage.

As all eyes were fixed on the column of seven pitchers balanced one by one on a glass placed on the head, this 52-year-old artiste created euphoria in the hall when he stood on the edge of swords, glasses and plate.

Dr Shekhawat also left a message for the audience saying in the end that it was now their duty to take care of the traditions, be it Gidda or Sammi or Bhawai.

Heading: Toy train at Rakh Bagh to chug in a little late - Indian Express
Content:
Schools in urban areas are known for their excellence in academics, sports and other co-curricular activities. But Nanakana Sahib Public School, Gill Road, which caters to the rural students, has succeeded in breaking this monopoly by maintaining its excellence in sports. Since 2002, the school has produced over a dozen state-level as well as national-level volleyball and handball players. This will be for the first time that a school in the district will host the CBSE National Handball Championship from November 27 to November 30.

School Principal Harmeet Kaur said, "Being in the rural area, we get students with very good stamina and physical health. The sports staff works hard and polishes their talent."

The school spends about Rs 50,000 per annum on sports. We give refreshment worth Rs 15 to 20 per player everyday."

Suman Kant, a physical education teacher and coach of the school said, "We have won many championships. Two years ago, our girls in the Under-19 category had won a volleyball championship at the state level. And cluster (Haryana, Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Chandigarh) level championship was also won by our girls two years ago. Last year, four players of Under-10 handball team were selected for state and one Navjot Kaur from our school was selected for a national championship. This year too, two girls from Under-14 and one from Under-19 have been selected in the state handball team."

Apart from handball and volleyball, the school has also produced sportspersons in other areas. Suman Kant said, "This year we remained second place in cricket at the zonal level and one of our players has been selected for the state cricket team." Many players from the school have represented at national championship in handball and volleyball. In weightlifting, Harjot Singh won a gold medal at the sports meet organised by the Punjab School Education Board.

Harmeet Kaur said, "This year Harjot participated in state-level meet and qualified for the national championship."

Heading: Despite Big B ‘sorry’, protests on - Indian Express
Content:
MC denies no-objection certificate till the time tracks are fully fixed; contractors say repair work complete

If you are looking forward to take a joyride in the toy train at Rakh Bagh then your wait might get a little longer. Though the contractor maintaining the park had announced the relaunch of the service, the MC authorities have categorically decided not to give a no-objection certificate (NoC) to the contractor till the time the tracks are repaired. After the tracks developed some problem, the rail service in the park was stopped three years ago.

Earlier, the garden was being maintained by the Municipal Corporation and hence for want of funds, the service remained suspended but later the private contractor decided to restart the service.

Surinder Kumar, Landscaping officer, while talking to Newsline, said, "The repair of tracks need around Rs 12 lakh. The contractor has not yet completed the repair of tracks as per the specifications of the Railways. Moreover, a team from the Railways is yet to inspect the tracks."

He added, "The contractor will earn out of ticket charges, hence, he should repair the tracks."

Yogesh Rai, the contractor, however, said, "We have repaired the tracks and only after that we started trails. We have also written to the Railways for a formal visit so that they can check the tracks from the safety point of view. Once the Railways gives it a green signal, MC will be able to give us a formal NoC."

Meanwhile, city residents are eagerly waiting for the toy train to resume. Walkers can be seen along with their kids asking for tickets and even the date for the launch of the facility.

Heading: Study policy change to help Mumbai grow vertical, CM tells MMRDA - Indian Express
Content:
Multiplex attacked, effigies burnt; premiere of The Last Lear called off

Even as the premiere of Amitabh Bachchan-starrer The Last Lear was called off on Wednesday after suspected Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) activists attacked a suburban multiplex cinema, members of the party continued to spew venom against the Bachchan family and the city's police force, despite the latter having issued over a thousand prohibitory orders against party men.

The Juhu branch of PVR multiplexes was vandalized by four unidentified men at noon on Wednesday. The vandals threw stones and shattered a glass window housing a poster of the to-be-released The Last Lear and an LCD screen.

"We have not yet identified whether the miscreants belong to any party but we are investigating it," said Senior Police Inspector D Katkade of Juhu Police station. No one was hurt in the incident.

"Joint police commissioner K L Prasad should remember that Mumbai is an integral part of Maharashtra. He is paid by taxpayers of the state," said MNS spokesperson Shirish Parkar. "Where was he when swords were brandished on the city's roads?"

In retaliation to Jaya Bachchan's remarks during the music launch of Drona, Abhishek Bachchan's upcoming film, 15 MNS workers staged a protest opposite Dahisar station on Wednesday afternoon. The protesters burnt effigies of Jaya Bachchan and Samajwadi Party's Maharashtra head Abu Asim Azmi. Four people were arrested by the officers of MHB Colony police station. "We are tracking down the remaining accused as well as the shakha pramukh Deepak Aarey," said Senior Police Inspector K Gaekwad of MHB Colony police station.

Meanwhile, Amitabh Bachchan said at a press conference that if, despite his apology, a law and order situation persists, it would be the administration's job to tackle the matter. "We will wait for the investigation report and I am prepared to go to jail if I have committed a crime. If after our apology the matter still persists it becomes a problem of law and order, it is for the administration to take care," he said.

Earlier, Bachchan said he believes Jaya's comments were not "anything negative" but said the family leaves it to the government to decide. Tongue in cheek, the actor added he has no problems with his "friend" Raj Thackeray though the latter has threatened not to permit any film starring any Bachchan family member to be released in Mumbai.

Heading: State govt’s move to curb civic bodies’ powers mockery of democracy: Mayor - Indian Express
Content:
Months after visiting World Bank officials suggested that laws should be changed to allow Mumbai grow vertically like New York, Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh on Wednesday asked the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) to conduct a study on the policies to be adopted for such a development.

He was speaking at a meeting of the MMRDA, which also discussed key projects like Sewri-Nhava Shewa Mumbai Trans Harbour Link (MTHL), Mumbai Metro, monorail and construction of two feeder flyovers for the under-construction Bandra-Worli sea link being.

In December last year, senior World Bank officials, who were in Mumbai for meetings with government officials, had advocated an FSI policy like New York. Bank officials had said that Mumbai can be transformed into a world-class city, but there are too many laws that need to be amended — some by the local government, others by the Central government — to facilitate development on par with metropolitan cities in the world. They had said since land is scarce, Mumbai should grow vertically like New York to make builders compete with one another for wooing buyers.

At Wednesday's meeting, Deshmukh stated that the proposed Coastal Management Zone (CMZ) notification was impractical and asked representatives of local self-government bodies to meet the Union environment minister in this regard.

Deshmukh assured that the recommendations of the Krantiveer Lahuji Matang Samaj commission which went into the measures to be taken for social, educational and economic betterment of the Matang community would be placed before the state cabinet. The report of the committee, which contains 83 recommendations, including five per cent educational reservations and financial aid for promoting business opportunities, was presented to Deshmukh on Wednesday.

The meeting was attended by Minister of State for Urban Development Rajesh Tope, Legislative Council Deputy Chairperson Vasant Davkhare and senior bureaucrats.

Heading: Yes, our own TIFR too has contributed to Big Bang experiment - Indian Express
Content:
The Shiv Sena-led Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has strongly opposed the Congress-led State government's decision to issue suo motu orders to municipal bodies in matters of public interest. Asking the State government to desist from interfering in civic affairs and curtailing local bodies' powers, Mayor Shubha Raul has written a letter to Governor S C Jamir urging him to disapprove of the decision.

Last week, the State cabinet passed a decision which will allow it to issue directives to municipal corporations and councils on policy matters, their duties and responsibilities, issues concerning the public interest, and national and state government programmes and schemes. These directives would be binding on the local bodies to implement.

Raul said in her letter that if the cabinet decision is implemented, the State government would be able to interfere in municipal functioning. "I strongly oppose such curtailing of powers and independence of the BMC. It will affect smooth functioning of the civic body," she pointed out.

She also cited instances from the Constitution, which on the one hand favours powers for local self government and on the other wants the State to curtail them. "This is a mockery of democracy. The Governor should not give his assent to this decision and should send it back to the Cabinet for reconsideration," the letter states.

The government will have to amend the Mumbai Municipal Corporation Act, 1888, as it is mandatory to implement the reforms prescribed for local bodies if they are to avail of aid under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) and Urban Infrastructure Development for Small and Medium Towns (UIDSMT) schemes. At present, the recommendations or directives of the State government are tabled with the civic body for seeking approval, first of the concerned committee and then of the general body, before it can be implemented.

Standing Committee Chairman and Sena leader Ravindra Waikar, too, is writing to Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh complaining about the move. "If the State Government's decisions are made mandatory, the BMCs powers will be curtailed. All corporators from across party lines are opposed to this decision and we want the state government to withdraw it," he said.

Heading: Swish new road planned to link Nariman Point to Cuffe Parade - Indian Express
Content:
It designed, tested and built the Outer Hadron Calorimeter and some other parts of the Compact Muon Solenoid

As the world's largest particle accelerator, the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), became operational today, there was a perceptible buzz at the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) as a live telecast of the events while they unfolded at Geneva's European Organisation for Nuclear Research (CERN) was aired. Scientists at CERN will try to circulate a beam through the particle accelerator and the LHC will be used to recreate the conditions that followed the Big Bang, after which they will prepare for a larger experiment scheduled in October.

Though the much-awaited LHC has various components that have been built in various parts of the world and assembled at CERN, parts of the Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) like the Outer Hadron Calorimeter were designed, tested and built at TIFR, before being shipped for assembly at CERN.

"Though it is a global initiative and so many nations were involved, India has made many contributions to the machine itself," said TIFR Senior Professor N K Mondal, who is leading one of the two teams. "Also involved in the experiment were a number of other Indian institutions like the Universities of Punjab, Jammu and Rajasthan, as well as the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE)," he said.

"It is a significant contribution that we have made as a country, and it has involved over 150 labs all over the world, and scientists from everywhere have come together as a unit," said TIFR High Energy Physics Head of the Department Tariq Aziz. "India was there right in the beginning, and there are contributions from everywhere — the USA, Europe, Japan, and China among many others," added Mondal.

The ALICE experiment, also part of the LHC, has contributions from some Indian organisations, especially Kolkata's Variable Energy Cyclotron Centre, which was also responsible for fitting the LHC with a Photon Multiplicity Detector. Over 7,000 scientists from eight countries around the world are responsible for the LHC experiment, and work on the detector has been going on for over 10 years.

Heading: To buy drugs, son of real estate agent turns to chain-snatching - Indian Express
Content:
The MMRDA would be approaching the Pune-based CWPRS to prepare a design for the proposed road

Mumbaiites who enjoy their evening strolls at the Queen's Necklace would soon be able to walk up to Cuffe Parade with the Arabian Sea on one side, if a grand plan drawn up by the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) materialises. The plan, passed at a meeting on Wednesday, is to reclaim land at the land's end at Nariman Point to construct a 1.2-km road leading from the National Centre for the Performing Arts (NCPA) to Cuffe Parade.

According to Ratnakar Gaikwad, Metropolitan Commissioner, MMRDA, the Authority on Wednesday cleared that proposal to construct a road from National Centre for Performing Arts at Nariman Point to MLA Hostel (Manora) on Jagannath Bhosale Marg and would be extended up to junction of Nathalal Parekh Marg—that leads to Cuffe Parade. The proposed road would be open to vehicular traffic along with a Marine Drive-like promenade for pedestrians.

"Currently, people go up to a little further of NCPA till the dead end is, but with this proposal cleared a road would be constructed over reclaimed land with the sea on one side. The road is proposed to be around 12.5 meters wide of which 2.5 meters is proposed foot path," Gaikwad said. The estimated cost of the road is Rs 50 crore.

Traffic in the business hub of Nariman Point is also expected to be more streamlined with the addition of an extra road between Marine Drive and Cuffe Parade.

The MMRDA would be approaching the Pune-based Central Water and Power Research Station (CWPRS) that would prepare a design for the proposed road, Gaikwad added. The MMRDA will now be approaching the authority for environmental clearance. "An environmental clearance will be sought. After a go ahead the construction would start," he said.

Heading: Police get I-T records of matka king’s wife, son - Indian Express
Content:
Addiction to drugs led the 22-year-old son of a real estate agent resort to chain-snatching. The accused, Pritesh Doshi, was arrested from near Pritam Hotel on SV Road while he was allegedly conducting a recce of the area for potential targets.

Doshi was held on the night of September 5 after being spotted by the policemen who were on the lookout for chain snatchers.

Police Inspector Surendra Jaiswal from the Kandivali police station says, "Since past few days, there had been a rise in the incidents of chain snatching in the areas of Kandivali, Charkop, Malad and Borivali. After consulting with our seniors, a special team was formed to crackdown on such offenders and we started patrolling strategic areas in plain-clothes."

Jaiswal said they had received information from sources that many chain snatching offences in their jurisdiction had been committed by a person riding a red-coloured Pulsar bike. "Based on the information, we started keeping a special watch for the bike of the same description. On the night September 5, our team that was near Pritam Hotel on SV Road spotted a biker riding a bike matching the given description keenly observing women wearing jewellery. Suspecting something fishy, he (Pritesh) was immediately apprehended and on being interrogated, he confessed to snatching chains to buy drugs. We have recovered 5 chains worth Rs 1, 85,000 from him so far," said Jaiswal.

During investigations, it was discovered that Pritesh comes from a well-to-do family and his father works as an estate agent. "From what we have gathered, he is the only son and his father used to pamper him. Pritesh used to get a sum of Rs 350 everyday as pocket-money and his father had also bought a bike for him. However, as Pritesh had started taking drugs and could not manage enough money, he decided to indulge in chain snatching," Jaiswal said.

"We have further got to know that he was arrested last year by the D N Nagar police in a mobile phone theft case," he added.

Heading: Revision of road width by MMRDA cuts down number of PAPs by half - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai Police Crime Branch, probing the murder of 'matka king' Suresh Bhagat, have obtained income tax records of his ex-wife Jaya Chedda and their son Hitesh Bhagat. The records reveal that their stated annual income was in excess of Rs 2.5 crore each for the past two years of tax assessment. The police are collecting these details as part of a larger probe into the duo's assets, which may be seized under the stringent MCOCA if found to have been procured by way of organized crime.

Joint Commissioner of Police, Crime, Rakesh Maria said, "Records show that for the period of assessment 2008 to 2009, Hitesh Bhagat has stated an annual income of Rs 2,55,65,000 with a tax payment of Rs 60 lakh. For the same period, Jaya Chedda's income is shown to be Rs 3,62,47,000, with tax of Rs 42,75,000. For the period 2007 to 2008, Hitesh's stated income was Rs 3,55,48,000, and he paid Rs 42.5 lakh in tax, while Jaya's income was Rs 3, 62,47,000 and she paid tax totaling Rs 42, 75,000."

Though the duo have stated their source of income to be the purchase and sale of shares, the police suspect these figures to be an eyewash to convert black money into white. "We are collecting evidence so that the special MCOCA court may attach their assets. Jaya and Hitesh own jewellery shops, and have invested in a big way in real estate. Benami properties owned by them are also being identified by us," added Maria.

On June 13, Suresh Bhagat and six others were murdered in an orchestrated accident on the Alibaug-Pen Road, when a truck collided head-on with the Scorpio in which they were traveling. The Crime Branch arrested eight people, including Jaya and her son Hitesh, and applied MCOCA in the case.

The Crime Branch has already frozen several bank accounts held by Jaya and Hitesh. This was supposedly involved in the buying and selling of shares and is believed to be a front for money laundering. The police have also seized a Lamborghini sports car imported by Hitesh at a cost of Rs.3 crore.

"So far, we have identified bank accounts, shares and Hitesh's car totalling around Rs 20 crore. The bank accounts and car have been seized, and the matter of shares is under process. Besides this, we are also identifying properties and immovable assets of the accused," said Senior Police Inspector, Ramesh Mahale, of Crime Branch Unit 1.

Heading: HC directs cops to trace 70-year-old missing for 4 yrs - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) on Wednesday reduced the road width from 120 feet to 90 feet on the JP Road in Andheri through which the first Metro rail is proposed to pass. With this decision, the MMRDA would be less burdened with rehabilitation of the project affected persons.

"The earlier proposed road width of 120 feet for the Versova-Andheri-Ghatkopar corridor from Navrang Cinema to Western Express Highway via Mathurdas Vasanji has been reduced to 90 feet by the authority, following the demands of the locals," said Ratnakar Gaikwad, Metropolitan Commissioner, MMRDA. Gaikwad added that keeping in mind the escalating costs and the number of project-affected persons, the MMRDA decided to reduce the road width to 90 feet.

The stretch from Navrang Cinema to western side of Andheri station from WEH to eastern side of the station has been a debatable issue for the implementing agency and has been facing a lot of opposition from the affected establishments. According to figures provided by the MMRDA, there were 1044 project affected persons (PAPs) to be rehabilitated, but with the revision in the width of the road the number of PAPs has been cut down by half. "With the revision, 515 structures will be affected, of which 155 commercial PAPs would be rehabilitated at the Andheri Municipal Market," Gaikwad said.

According to Gaikwad, with over 1000 establishments affected, the rehabilitation of the PAPs would have been difficult at the Andheri Market that is proposed to be rebuilt into a mall. "It was not structurally feasible to rehabilitate PAPs with a 120 feet wide road," Gaikwad added.

Gaikwad assured that now with the decision on the width of the road, the construction of the Metro rail on the stretch can start. "Work can start on JP Road provided the establishments go back by 5 to 10 metres. Around 15 shops would have to be fully relocated," explained Gaikwad. He added that while once the piers are erected traffic would have to be closed completely on the one-way road.

Heading: HC directs woman to file fresh plea for child’s custody in family court - Indian Express
Content:
A day after a minor girl who was missing for over a year was produced in the High Court, the police was directed to trace a 70-year-old woman who has been missing since 2004 within two weeks, failing which the court would ask the Director General of Police to look into the matter personally.

The court was hearing a habeaus corpus petition, filed by Shakuntala Khatri, stepdaughter of the missing woman, Shantabai Tonde. A division bench of Justice Bilal Nazki and Justice A A Kumbhakaoni, observed: "When we made the police commissioner a party and directed him to personally look into the case where a 16-year-old was missing, they found her in two weeks. This time too, we shall make the director general of police look into the case if the woman is not found within two weeks."

According to Shakhuntala, before her marriage in 1977 she used to stay with Shantabai at Jawahar Nagar in Goregaon. After Shakhuntala got married, she often used to visit her mother, but in November 2004 when she visited her, she found the house locked. Shakhuntala thought that she might have gone to her native place in Mulshi Taluka, Pune.

However, when she again visited Shantabai on December 22, 2004, she found one Ram Patel alias Kalia staying in the house. When she inquired about her mother, Kalia told that he had been staying in that house for years and don't know anyone by the name of Shantabai. After that Shakhuntala went to the Goregaon police station and filed a missing person's complaint.

After repeated attempts when police could not trace the woman, Shakhuntala moved the court seeking that the police produce her mother before the court. Shakhuntala feels that her mother is forcibly being restrained at some place by Patel and her life is in serious danger.

The court adjourned the matter for two weeks.

Heading: Govt okays car decks to avoid traffic snarls on Sea Link - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court on Wednesday told Deepti Nandlal, who is fighting a legal battle for the custody of her four-year-old child with her husband Rishi Nandlal, a South African national, to file a fresh application for the child's custody in the family court.

A Division Bench of Justice B H Marlapalle and Justice D B Bhosale directed Deepti (34) to do so after Rishi (46) refused to accept the terms of a mutual consent divorce given to him by the high court last week. The court also ruled that meanwhile the child's custody will remain with the mother, and if Rishi wants to meet the child will have to deposit his passport in court whenever he comes to India and.  

The court, while hearing the case in the chamber, had given the proposal of mutual consent divorce to Rishi. According to the proposal, he is directed to deposit Rs 5 lakh as fixed deposits in the name of his son and the interest accrued would be reinvested. He also has to pay a monthly maintenance of Rs 5, 000 to the child and Rs 10,000 to Deepti. If he comes down from South Africa, he will be allowed to stay overnight with his child after he deposits his passport with the court.

Earlier, the judges had spoken to the couple as well as the child in their chamber. The court had later observed that "both of them (the couple) seem to have convinced themselves that the marriage is beyond repair" and had as interim relief to Deepti given the custody of the child to her. Later, Deepti's lawyer Mukesh Vashi had said, "This is the proposed order and if Rishi is agreeable to the order, this will be final. If not, the matter will be argued further."  

In April 2003, Deepti married Rishi, a civil engineer who was settled in South Africa (SA) and had the country's citizenship. After their marriage, Deepti too settled in SA. However, in 2006, she came to India along with Rishi and her son Amit (name changed).

Immediately after her return, on December 21, 2006, Deepti filed a petition before the family court seeking Amit's custody. However, the family court rejected her petition stating that though the couple got married in India, Amit was born in SA and hence was a citizen of that country, and it (family court) had no jurisdiction to allow child custody.

Deepti then approached the HC against the family court's order. However, till that the time, Deepti had not filed for divorce. It was only in October 2007 that she sought a divorce in the family court.

Heading: Civic body to develop catchment areas of Tansa and Modak Sagar - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to avert traffic snarls at the end of the Bandra-Worli Sea Link, the government has cleared the proposal to construct two back-to-back car decks to prevent bottlenecks at Worli sea face, once the sea link is opened to traffic in January.

"The authority approved the proposal to construct two car decks costing Rs 15 crore each on Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan Road at Pratiksha Point and Thadani Junction connecting the Bandra-Worli Sea Link. Cars and two-wheelers would be allowed to use the decks, while other heavy vehicles would go under it," said Ratnakar Gaikwad, Metropolitan Commissioner, MMRDA. He added that the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) has issued tenders for the car decks along this stretch, to divert the cars that will zoom off the Bandra Worli Sea Link and onto the narrow, four-lane Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan Road.

The issue of the colossal jams at the Sea Link was discussed earlier in August at a brainstorming session of Unified Mumbai Metropolitan Transport Authority (UMMTA). The MSRDC was keen on implementing the decks as part of the traffic dispersal system in place before January 2009, when the link will become operational as over 1.40 lakh vehicles are expected to use the cable-stayed sealink every day.

The MSRDC has also proposed to construct skywalk on the Worli Dairy crossing to the entry point of the Bandra Worli Sea Link. When asked by when the MSRDC plans to start work on the skywalk, Gaikwad responded, "It's not the priority currently as pedestrians can cross through other means, but the work on the car decks would commence shortly."

Heading: Court convicts man for cheating woman - Indian Express
Content:
To prevent soil erosion and silting of drinking water, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation will be developing catchments areas of Tansa and Modak Sagar from where the city gets its share of water. The civic administration has said that improvement of the catchment areas will strengthen the dam structures and increase the ground level water circulation by way of afforestation and forest conservation. The Rs 5.21 crore proposal involves carrying out mass plantations, building infrastructure for the dam, creating bunds and barrages along 9519.24 hectare catchment at Tansa and 3912.54 hectare catchment at Modaksagar. The civic Standing committee approved the proposal on Wednesday.

It was the forest conservation department that first mooted the proposal, to be implemented in the next five years. However, the BMC decided to fund the project and is hoping for Central assistance under the National Lake Conservation Project.

The proposal will also involve conservation of the existing flora and fauna, with steps to be taken to prevent any form of destruction to plant life in these areas. Collectively, Mumbai is supplied 1,600 million litres of water every day by the two reservoirs. These regions also provide shelter to migratory birds.

Heading: 4 Hemant Pujari aides held for extortion - Indian Express
Content:
A Sessions Court on Wednesday sentenced a man for two years' rigorous imprisonment for cheating a woman by making false promise of marrying her.

The court held the accused, Joshimuddin Mojumullah, guilty of cheating and establishing physical relation with the woman with a fake promise.

The complainant, while staying with her brother, had developed friendship with Mojumullah, a neighbour. When their friendship grew in to love, they decided to get married. But Mojumullah back tracked and did not keep his promise. According to police, in September 2006, when the complainant had gone for her medical check-up, she discovered of her being seven month pregnant.

The woman's brother then spoke to Mojumullah and asked him to keep his word of marrying her but the latter refused. Later, the family filed a complaint of rape and cheating against Mojumullah at RCF police station. Mojumullah was subsequently arrested and sent to custody.

Public prosecutor Kiran Makasare examined six witnesses in all including the complainant's family members. Though a case of rape was registered against the accused, the charge was later altered as the prosecution could not prove the case of non-consensuality. The accused was convicted on charges of cheating under section 417 of the IPC and fined Rs 20,000.

Heading: BMC beefs up security at hqs, Dinanath Mangeshkar auditorium - Indian Express
Content:
The Anti-Extortion Cell (AEC) of the Mumbai Police Crime Branch on Wednesday arrested four aides of fugitive gangster Hemant Pujari, for allegedly demanding Rs 1 lakh from a vegetable vendor in Khar (east).

The arrested accused have been identified as Suresh Babu Pujari (36), Leeladhar Anchan (24), Tejraj Anchan (24) and Vijay Bhange alias Vijay Vada Pav (34). Hemant Pujari and Kishore Pujari have been named as wanted accused in the case.

"The arrested accused had identified themselves as Hemant Pujari's men, and since August 25 had started demanding Rs 1 lakh as extortion amount from a vegetable vendor Mahendra Mahatma Singh in Khar (east). A case of extortion was registered at Nirmal Nagar police station, and AEC officers today arrested the culprits. They have been remanded to police custody till September 16," said Joint Commissioner of Police, Crime, Rakesh Maria.

"This shows how weak the gang has become in the city. They are unable to get recruits and they are now in such a desperate situation that they have to target small vegetable vendors for extortion," said Maria.

Heading: Ulhasnagar whistle-blower refutes extortion charges - Indian Express
Content:
After taking numerous security measures, including installation of CCTV cameras, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation is now set to install X-ray baggage scanning machines at its headquarters, at the entry and exit points of the office.

The same will also be installed at the Dinanath Mangeshkar auditorium at Vile Parle (E) as a precaution against any terror or anti-social activity. The civic headquarters earlier had X-ray baggage scanners, however they had to be replaced due to wear and tear and non-functionality of the machines. Civic authorities felt the need to beef up the security at the auditorium, as the place hosts people in large numbers who come to see plays and other functions held in the premises.

A total of four machines costing Rs 65 lakh will be installed, 3 at the BMC headquarters (gate numbers 2, 6 and 7) and one at the auditorium.

Heading: Ganesh visarjan: Police keep noise levels under control - Indian Express
Content:
Recognises his voice in two recordings produced against him in the High Court

Hari Tanwani, the man who filed a public interest litigation regarding the illegal buildings in Ulhasnagar, accepted before the Bombay High Court that the voice in two of the three audio and video recordings produced against him in extortion cases is his own. However, Tanwani denied allegations of extortion made on the basis of those recordings. Acting on his PIL, the HC had ordered demolition of 855 unauthorised structures in Ulhasnagar.

"There are several cases of extortion lodged against me and their sole purpose is to defile my image," said Tanwani. In 2005, municipal secretary of Ulhasnagar Municipal Corporation lodged a complaint with the Central police station alleging that Tanwani published a defamatory piece against him and demanded Rs 2,000 per month for not doing so. In 2008, two other cases of extortion were lodged against him. In the first, a builder identified as Hardasmal Tharwani accused Tanwani of demanding Rs 10 lakh by threatening to expose him claiming he was constructing illegal structures. In the second case he was nabbed while allegedly accepting Rs 20,000 from Rajesh Watyani, another builder.

Of the three recordings produced in the High Court, one was in MP3 format and of a conversation between Tanwani and businessman Jairaj Kalyani in which Tanwani is alleged to have demanded Rs 1 lakh, while the other recording is that of a TV interview. "They are trying to mislead. In the TV interview, I asked the public to report to the police if the authorities seek bribe for not taking action against unauthorized construction," clarified Tanwani. The third recoding is also a secretly recorded conversation based on which Tanwani has been accused of making objectionable comments against the judiciary. Tanwani, however, has denied that the third tape contains his voice.

Speaking to Newsline, Tanwani said that the voice in the two tapes was his and it was secretly recorded during a meeting with the businessman while he was seeking advertisement for his Sindhi weekly Mehraan in 2000. "This is a conspiracy to thwart my public interest litigation. I had gone to Octroi contractor's office to discuss an advertisement. I had accepted a cheque payment for the same. Everything is above the table. There is nothing to hide," said Tanwani.

The Bombay High Court on September 4, 2008, said that it would hear the audio recording and translated transcripts produced in the case. Tanwani has already submitted an oral statement to the court admitting that voice in the two tapes is his.

Regarding the third tape, Tanwani said, "This is not my voice. It sounds like a very long monologue and not a conversation between two people. Why would a person make incriminating statements to oneself?"

He said that there was a conspiracy to taint him by filing false cases against him. Vicky Kukreja, one of the persons who has approached the High Court seeking action against Tanwani, said: "This is an exercise to bring facts to the notice of the court to expose the petitioner's misdeeds. Tanwani has turned the public interest litigation into a private interest."

Heading: Five of highway robbery gang held - Indian Express
Content:
This Ganesh visarjan, it seems the city's major hospitals would be spared of the noise disturbances so common during the festival. A preliminary report released by the Awaaz Foundation, keeping track of noise violations during Ganesh visarjan, has pointed out that on Monday - a major visarjan day - noise was effectively controlled at sensitive areas like Jaslok Hospital (Peddar Road), King Edwards Memorial Hospital (Parel), Tata Memorial (Parel), Nanavati (Juhu) and Harkisandas Hospital (Girgaum). The report stated that unlike the previous years, police personnel were seen near hospital zones, diverting procession routes and barring use of firecrackers, loudspeakers, drums and other noisy instruments in the vicinity.

According to Vijay Singh Jadhav, DCP-HQ1 (Operations), the police at different zones have been given specific instructions to take strict action against noise offenders in silent and residential zones. Jadhav said, "We have asked all zonal police to book offenders under the noise offence law. Besides, the noise curbs in silent zones, we are also adhering to the 6 am to 10 pm noise deadline strictly. This Ganeshotsav, we allowed a 12 midnight deadline only on two days - the fifth day and the last day of immersion."

According to the report, while hospitals like Nair, Hinduja, Nanavati, Sion, K L Rajeha Hospital, and B J Hospital (Santacruz) recorded no noise disturbances in their immediate surroundings, Tata Memorial recorded noise levels at 73.2 decibel (dB) at 7.30 pm, KEM recorded 73.2 dB and Bhatia Hospital in Mumbai Central recorded the highest at 90.1 dB (measured at 8 pm).

Sumaira Abdulali of Awaaz, said, "It was heartening to note that the police personnel and constables posted on the streets were aware of the noise curbs and were being hands-on in taking action. Near Hinduja Hospital, we even observed that when an atom bomb was burst directly in front of the hospital, the police immediately intervened."

She pointed out, "The emphasis now is on firecrackers. Many people, probably due to the curbs on loudspeakers, have turned to bursting atom bombs."

The report also stated that noisy instruments and firecrackers used beyond the restricted areas created pockets of comparatively less noisy areas . In some cases, the surrounding noise filtering through, elevated the level beyond the permissible limits. Meanwhile, Abdulali pointed out that while noise norms were being maintained near most of the major hospitals, they were was being violated around smaller hospitals and educational institutions.

Heading: Tourism industry for regulatory policy framework - Indian Express
Content:
A gang of highway robbers landed in the police net on Tuesday afternoon. Police officials from zone six, who were recently organised into a special anti-dacoity team, caught the five-member gang led by 21-year-old Pravin Mahadev Helkar alias Don red-handed and recovered several firearms, including illegal pistols, a revolver and ammunitions from their possession. The RCF police station have registered a case against the five accused for attempted robbery and possession of illegal weapons.

After they were arrested, Helkar and his associates- Suresh Singh alias Singh, Jeetendra Maurya Rashid Shaikh and Nitin Chacho- confessed to plotting an armed dacoity in a jeweller's shop on CG Gidwani Road. The police apprehended them when they had assembled near the Vasant theatre. "The gang has over 15 cases of robbery registered against them and Don himself is wanted in several cases," said police sub-inspector Sanjay Bhapkar. "On August 1, the gang was involved in a firing and in another instance a railway ticket examiner accepted lift from them and was held hostage in the car till he parted with Rs 10,000. He was forced to phone his brother directing him to get the money in exchange for being let off unharmed," said Bhapkar. The accused have been remanded to police custody till September 18. ENS

Heading: Oil prices under $98, at 6 month low - Indian Express
Content:
Tourism industry in the country has asked the government to formulate a regulatory policy framework to promote responsible tourism, stressing that more coordinated efforts are needed to develop the sector.

Noting that success of the industry depends on the management of "support" sectors that impact the development and showcasing of tourism products, players in the sector also asked policy makers and stakeholders to get their act together to introspect and articulate what more needs to be done.

"The most important of all is the strategic initiatives that government needs to provide in an appropriate regulatory policy framework. As the interested stakeholders, we need to introspect and articulate what needs to be done to make India Incredible," said Rathi Vinay Jha, Secretary General, World Travel and Tourism Council, India Initiative.

"We need effective coordination across sectors that address infrastructure, culture, environment, heritage and nature and also across support sectors in aviation, hospitality, human resources and travel services to promote tourism," she said.

At the recently concluded two-day round table conference of "World Travel and Tourism Council", India Initiative in Khajuraho, policy makers, industry leaders, media and opinion makers came together to interact on issues impacting Tourism in India and to map its future.

"What we have achieved and what we wish to achieve is required to be look into to meet future changes and challenges in the sector. Over the past few years, the industry has had to contend with a series of unprecedented challenges," said Jyotsna Suri, Chairman of The Bharat Hotels.

"New tourism is a force capable of improving economic and social well-being right across the globe," Suri said.

Emphasising that the government should encourage more public-private partnership initiatives, Arjun Sharma, Managing Director of India Tours and Travels, said, "public sector has a special responsibility to ensure the sustainability of key tourism assets that preserves the attractiveness of tourism destinations and the competitiveness of tourism companies."

Industry experts also asked government to stop charging unwanted taxes and increasing surcharges from the tourists.

WTTC Global President Jean-Claude Baumgarten said "government should stop charging unwanted taxes and increasing surcharges. Growth of the tourism sector, if it's not inclusive, it will not pay off."

"Tourism is a service sector on which economy and growth of the country depends and it is the responsibility of the government to provide it its proper place. It was always put on back burner. We urge the ministry to take some concrete steps," said Radha Bhatia, chairman of World Travel and Tourism Council, India Initiative.

Heading: India okays changes in IMF pact - Indian Express
Content:
Oil prices tumbled to six-month low below USD 98 a barrel on Thursday as the dollar rallied and demand for energy decreased around the world amid an economic slowdown, traders said.

Prices had risen earlier in the day as Hurricane Ike headed toward key energy facilities on the southern US coast and after OPEC on Thursday reduced output to curb falling prices, analysts said.

Brent North Sea crude for delivery in October dropped to USD 97.85 dollars a barrel on today -- the lowest level since March 5. It later recovered to USD 98.22 dollars, a loss of 75 cents from Wednesday's close.

New York's main contract, light sweet crude for October, slid 93 cents to USD 101.65 dollars a barrel.

"Crude oil futures slipped further ... as the market focused on demand concerns and the strengthening dollar," said Sucden analyst Michael Davies.

A strong dollar makes goods, such as oil, priced in the US unit more expensive for foreign buyers, dampening demand.

The euro on Thursday slid below USD 1.39 for the first time in a year on heightened concerns about a weak European economy, dealers said.

Concerns about oil demand in a slowing global economy were meanwhile highlighted by the latest monthly report from the International Energy Agency (IEA), which cut its estimate for global oil demand this year by 100,000 barrels per day and in 2009 by 140,000 bpd.

The IEA monthly report, published on Wednesday, highlighted shrinking oil demand in North America, saying consumers mainly in the United States are cutting back energy use in response to high prices.

The same day, the US Department of Energy said that stockpiles of distillates, which include heating fuel, had dropped by 1.2 million barrels in the week ended September 5.

The consensus forecast was for a bigger decline of 2.2 million barrels.

Heading: Inflation down at 12.10% - Indian Express
Content:
The government on Thursday approved a proposed amendment in the IMF's articles of agreement that will increase India's quota in the multilateral funding agency.

With the proposed amendment, India's quota in IMF, in terms of Special Drawing Rights or reserve asset, will go up from 1.91 per cent to 2.44 per cent.

Reserve assets, which are supposed to supplement a country's official reserves comprising gold and foreign exchange, are a potential claim on the freely usable currencies of member countries to determine the exchange value of one's own currency unit.

In absolute terms, India's quota will increase from 4,158.2 million SDR to 5821.5 million SDR.

Heading: Inflation may have peaked: PM adviser - Indian Express
Content:
Inflation fell to 12.10 per cent, extending the decline to the third week in succession, even as the finance ministry pointed out that 30 essential commodities have become expensive during the week ended August 30.

Inflation dipped by 0.24 per cent for the week ended August 30 from 12.34 per cent a week ago though none of the indices in the broad category declined.

However, prices of some food items, including imported edible oil and fruits, saw a fall.

According to a statement by the finance ministry, inflation of 30 essential commodities increased to 7.52 per cent during the week from 6.90 per cent a week ago.

In the food articles group, imported edible oil prices which had been rising quite a bit, declined by four per cent.

Besides, prices of fruits, maize and spices went down, the official data showed.

The finance ministry's statement also said that "in the primary articles group, the annual point to point inflation declined to 10.07 per cent compared to 10.79 per cent reported last week and 11.83 per cent for the week ended August 9, 2008."

Out of total of 98 items in the primary articles group, 19 commodities have shown a decline in prices in the current week as compared to August 16, 2008, the statement said.

The prices of various articles, including rice, maize, moong, masur, gram, onions and potatoes, declined during the week, the statement added.

In the manufactured group's category, there was no increase in prices of 296 items out of total of 318 commodities, the finance ministry added.

However, some of the manufactured items like sugar, khandsari, cement, groundnut oil, salt, tyre cord fabric and acids became dearer during the week, the statement added.

Heading: GMR to invest Rs 10,000 cr in nuke power plant - Indian Express
Content:
India's inflation rate may have peaked and there could be a pause in the monetary tightening by the RBI, the chief of Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's Economic Advisory Council said on Thursday.

"My gut feeling is that it has peaked. It would not increase is my gut feeling," Suresh Tendulkar said in a telephone interview.

India's annual inflation rate has fallen for two consecutive weeks after peaking in early August, but is still above 12 percent. The latest data will be released on Thursday at around 6 p.m. local time.

Asked whether the Reserve Bank of India would pause in its rate tightening, Tendulkar said: "If inflation has peaked, my hunch is they would pause."

Heading: Cabinet approves 10 food parks - Indian Express
Content:
GMR Energy plans to invest over Rs 10,000 crore in setting up a 2,000-3,000 MW nuclear power plant in the country in the next 5-7 years, a company executive said on Thursday.

"We have held talks with equipment as well as fuel suppliers and will firm up a plan in the next one years time," GMR Energy Executive Vice-President Avinash R Shah told reporters in New Delhi.

GMR Energy is a unit of GMR Infrastructure Ltd. Shah said the company has hired very experienced people from state-owned Nuclear Power Corporation, including former Chairman and Managing Director M R Srinivasan, for its nuclear foray.

"Right now it is at planning and preparation stage. In the next six months to one year, we should have a broad plan in place," he said.

GMR is in talks with equipment and fuel suppliers in France, United States and Korea for the power plant, he said.

"We may get a strategic partner (with nuclear technology) but I cannot say anything more now."

He said GMR Energy, which currently has 800 MW of thermal power generating capacity, may list in the next 1-2 years.

"We have projects to take up the capacity to 4,500 MW in about five years from now," he said. Of the under construction projects, 1,500 MW would be hydroelectric power - two in India and three in Nepal.

Two coal-based power plants adding 2,200 MW capacity are under construction in Orissa and Chattisgarh.

GMR, he said, had got coal mines in South Africa and Indonesia for 3,500 MW additional thermal power plants the company was planning to set up on coastal location in Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Gujarat in next 5 to 7 years.

In addition, 1,500 MW of hydroelectric power plants are also being conceived, taking the total generating capacity to 10,000 MW. This does not include the nuclear power plants.

"We are investing between Rs 16,000 crore to Rs 20,000 crore for adding 4,500 MW capacity," Shah said.

Heading: Major economies still at risk of recession - Indian Express
Content:
India's Cabinet on Thursday approved a scheme to establish 10 mega food parks and said it would grant half of the project cost in most parts of India.

The scheme would help the food processing industry grow and reach its potential and would also lead to greater share in the world food trade, a government statement said.

India aims to set up 30 food parks by 2011.

Heading: ‘Rs 1200 cr loss per day due to power cut’ - Indian Express
Content:
The world's major industrialised economies are still at risk of falling into recession this year, and more so than just a month ago, even as elevated inflation leaves policymakers unable to slash interest rates.

Reuters polls of around 200 economists in the US, Europe, Japan and Britain published on Thursday show a still-floundering US economy grappling with the credit crunch and a deterioration in the outlook for Europe -- particularly Britain.

The survey was taken after news of a sudden leap in the US jobless rate to 6.1 per cent and most responses came after the government seized at the weekend the giant, but ailing, mortgage lenders Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.

While the poll figures reveal a brightened outlook for the US this year after a much better than expected performance in the second quarter, the equally sharp downgrade to the full-year 2009 GDP forecast offsets that improvement.

"A vicious circle is still unfolding of credit weakening the economy, and the economy weakening credit, typical of recessionary periods," said Steven Wieting, economist at Citigroup in New York.

That comes despite a powerful rally in the dollar over the past month that now has a majority of top foreign exchange strategists convinced it has ended seven years of retreat and is now at the start of a multi-year upturn.

"A slowdown in world economic growth and renewed strength in the US dollar has helped calm oil and other commodity prices, giving consumers and businesses alike a little more breathing room," noted Ellen Beeson Zentner, economist at Bank of Tokyo/Mitsubishi UFJ in New York.

But she added this rise in the currency will be hurtful to export growth, which has been one of the key supports to the US economy throughout this year. On the flipside, weakness in the euro could help springboard Europe's eventual recovery.

INFLATION STICKING

One surprising conclusion from the polls is the near-$50 plunge in the oil price to around $100 a barrel has had little effect on the outlook for full-year 2009 inflation, even though it is seen gradually declining as the year progresses.

There were no downgrades to the view for inflation save for a sliver off of the median for the euro zone this year to 3.5 per cent and to core inflation in Japan next year to 1.0 per cent.

Indeed, viewed over the last year since the credit crunch began, the inflation consensus in the poll makes for unsettling reading, particularly for the Bank of England.

One year ago, the consensus for inflation in 2008 was to average 1.9 per cent, just below the 2.0 per cent target. Now it is 3.8 per cent, nearly double the target, and up from the poll last month.

In the meantime the pound has plunged on recession worries.

"Sterling's latest bout of weakness will reinforce upward inflation pressures," said Stephen Lewis, chief economist at Monument Securities.

That said, inflation is likely to fall sharply toward the end of next year from around 4.7 per cent in the next three months to 1.8 per cent in the fourth quarter of 2009.

Economists now see two quarter-point cuts in the first quarter of 2009 to 4.50 per cent and a 55 per cent chance of recession -- up from 45 per cent last month and just 20 per cent at the start of the year.

For the euro area, the median expectation for 2009 inflation was 2.0 per cent in the poll nearly one year ago.

Now, it's 2.4 per cent -- versus European Central Bank staff forecasts for 2.6 per cent and unchanged from the last poll. That does a lot to explain why economists still don't see ECB rates coming down until the second quarter of next year.

The median euro zone GDP forecasts for this year was downgraded to 1.3 per cent and to just 0.9 per cent in 2009.

And a Bank of Japan rate hike from the already meagre 0.50 per cent is not likely until the end of next year and is increasingly unlikely to happen at all given the gloomy outlook for the world's second largest economy.

Heading: Sensex down by 338 points - Indian Express
Content:
Industrial units in the state are likely to incur a production loss of Rs 1,200 crore per day as a result of power cut imposed by the power supplying company, said Gujarat Cahmber of Commerce and Industry (GCCI).

Chairman, GCCI, Rajesh Shah said the 30 per cent power cut imposed by the Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Ltd (GUVNL), will incur a loss of Rs 1200 crore per day.

The state-run GUVNL has decided to impose the power cut on processing industrial units for next couple of days to meet the demand from the farm sector.

Shah said that to get maximum output from the production units, it needs to run at over 80 per cent of its original capacity, but with power cut imposed by GUVNL, the target cannot be achieved.

Power cut will have an adverse effect on small industrial units as the big industries have their own captive power generation capacity, while small and medium size unit are completely dependent on the GUNVL for power supply, he added.

The GUVNL had already imposed a compulsory two-day holiday on some industries across the state from September 6, but it has not helped the company getting required power to divert toward agriculture for meeting its increasing demand.

Heading: Demand for office space on the rise in Chennai - Indian Express
Content:
Tracking weak global trends, the benchmark Sensex on Thursday fell sharply by over 338 points on relentless selling by funds, particularly in oil & gas and power counters.

The 30-share Sensex on the Bombay Stock Exchange, dropped 338.32 points at 14,324.29 on reports of the global markets falling to more than two-year low on concerns of credit market losses increasing and global economic growth declining.

The Indian rupee weakening to two-year low against the US currency also raised concerns of more capital outflows as some foreign funds indulged in reducing their portfolios.

The wide-based National Stock Exchange index Nifty also lost 109.95 points at 4,290.30, after dipping to 4272.75 and a high of 4399.30 points.

All the sectoral indices on BSE closed in the red. Oil and gas, power indices bore the maximum brunt of selling to close lower at 3.39 per cent and 2.97 per cent respectively.

Heaviest in the Sensex club Reliance Industries slipped below the Rs 2,000 level on heavy selling by foreign funds and retail investors. Bluechips BHEL, Larsen and Toubro and ICICI Bank also came under pressure bring down their sectoral indices.

Marketmen said trading sentiment turned weak on reports of Lehman Brothers Holdings posting a 3.9 billion dollar third quarter loss. They said Lehman's losses further hiked fears of deepening credit crisis in the world's biggest economy.

Reliance Industries, which has been weak for the past two trading sessions, weakened further by Rs 85.95 at Rs 1997.60. ONGC stocks lost Rs 41.15 at Rs 1,035.45, Indian Oil Rs 11.70 at Rs 411.20 and Abban by Rs 30.10 at Rs 2320.20.

Power index was second worst performer and lost 78.82 points at 2,576.42 after Tata Power declined by Rs 37 at Rs 1,012.10. BHEL, another sector heavy, fell by Rs 46.40 at Rs 1664.75 on all round selling.

A sharp fall in the value of rupee fail to enthuse traders in IT stocks which generally gain strength on local currency's weakness. Infosys fell by Rs 10.15 at Rs 1,749, Tata Consultancy lost Rs 15.05 at Rs 836.10 and Financial Technologies Rs 23.65 at Rs 1499.50.

Heading: 'Realty outlook positive mid-to-long term' - Indian Express
Content:
Demand for office space continues to rise in Chennai even as a million sqft area had been created in city in the second quarter of the current fiscal, a recent survey says.

The survey conducted by property demand assessing firm Colliers International revealed that the investors were particular that they got space in the prime central business district of Anna Salai and Parrys corner, besides the IT corridor.

Besides, companies also want residential accommodation in the fast growing suburbs in South Chennai, as most of the IT companies were located there, Colliers International Regional Director C Saravanan told reporters after releasing the report.

The demand for office space in the city was primarily driven by IT, telecom and financial sector companies, he said.

Though the supply position of space to IT companies had improved during the quarter, the demand from non-IT sector could not be met, the survey revealed.

Heading: Car sales in Aug down 4.36 pc, bike sales up - Indian Express
Content:
Describing the current bearish trend of the real estate sector a 'transitory slowdown', consultancy firm Ernst & Young on Wednesday said that the outlook of the sector is still 'positive' in the medium-to-long term.

"Ernst & Young believes that the market is witnessing a transitory slowdown. However, considering the opportunities present as well as the strong economic fundamental drivers, the outlook for the mid-to-long term is positive," it said in a report released at a Ficci-organised summit in Mumbai.

The momentum of the market in the mid-to-long term would be sustained by the emergence of new markets, innovative products, ongoing corporatisation of the sector, integration with global markets, greater transparency and new funding mechanisms, it said.

Hiranandani Group of Companies Managing Director Niranjan Hiranandani at the event said that the real estate sector was set to grow by 100 times in the next ten years as compared to the previous ten years, though profit margin would be less.

"The age of super-profit is over for the real estate sector and developers would have to contented with the low profit margins. If you do not believe in this and keep on waiting, somebody else will take business away from you," Hiranandani said.

E&Y said that the growth space of the real estate sector was affected by several interdependent factors including the volatility of the stock markets, rising exchange rates, increasing costs and credit crunch.

"This in turn resulted in a relative decline in margins in 2007-08, predominantly attributable to overheated land prices and high development costs," it said.

However, the margins were still higher than the comparable global average, the report said.

Investment vehicles such as real estate mutual funds and real estate investment trusts, when introduced amid the positively changing regulatory scenario, are expected to further catalyse the evolution of the sector, it said.

Heading: Synthetic textile exports to be hard hit: Trade Body - Indian Express
Content:
Domestic passenger car sales declined by 4.36 per cent in August to 94,584 units from 98,893 units in the same month last year.

According to the figures released by the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), motorcycle sales in the country during the month was up by 15.9 per cent at 4,85,294 units as against 4,18,702 units in the corresponding month a year ago.

Total two-wheeler sales in August also soared by 14.25 per cent at 6,20,927 units, compared with 5,43,504 units in the same month last year.

Commercial vehicle sales, however, decreased last month by 6.34 per cent to 34,294 units from 36,615 units in the year-ago period, SIAM said.

Heading: 90,000 MW of power in 11th 5-year plan - Indian Express
Content:
The Synthetic & Rayon Textiles Export Promotion Council has said that the reduction in duty drawback rates across the board for all synthetic textile products, would affect the country's export.

"The reduction, in some cases as high as from 17 per cent to 2.6 per cent, will have serious repercussions and will derail export activity and affect achievement of target fixed for exports," an SRTEPC press release said in Mumbai on Wednesday.

At stake are exports of synthetic textiles, valued over Rs 12,000 crore from the country, the release said.

Duty drawback plays an important role in maintaining the competitiveness of export products as it neutralises the incidence of the customs and excise duties on the products, the release said.

The exporters are already under pressure due to increased competition overseas, fluctuating currency and rising raw material costs and the move would further affect them adversely, it said.

India's main competitor, China, has increased the subsidy from 9 per cent to 13 per cent for all man-made fibre textile items from August 1 this year, the release said, adding that, "the worst-affected are the exporters of synthetic filament and spun yarn, where the drawback rates have been severely cut."

Synthetic yarns and fibres accounted for almost 42 per cent of the total synthetic textile exports, totaling Rs 5,300 crores, last year, the release said.

Heading: IEA asks India to remove fuel subsidies - Indian Express
Content:
The government on Thursday revised its target of power capacity addition to 90,000 MW in the 11th five-year plan (2007-12), up by 11,423 MW from the earlier estimate of 78,577 MW, in order to meet the growing demand of electricity in the country.

"We will add 90,000 MW by the year 2012 to meet electricity demand of the nation," Union Minister of Power Sushilkumar Shinde told reporters on the sidelines of a FICCI event in New Delhi.
