The frequency of shutdowns experienced in the Valley was worse during the 1990s. However, compared to the last couple of years, this year's duration of shutdown was relatively high.

The academic calendar in the Valley has been severely hit and it can be gauged by the fact that most of the educational institutes have remained closed for five months, including the winter vacation, leaving a working period of only four months in the current academic session.

In fact, this year, the number of holidays observed so far in educational institutions is 74, excluding 90 days of winter vacations. These 74 days include 11 days of state holidays, seven days of summer break, 26 Sundays and 30 days of strikes and curfews.

The Common Entrance Test (CET) for medical and engineering courses, which was scheduled to be held in July, has been postponed thrice and so have the other examinations in Kashmir University. The CET is now scheduled for September 13 and 14.

Prior to appearing for the exams it is mandatory for college students to attend 180 working days in their respective institutes, but they have attended around 70 days in colleges due to the present crisis.

A similar situation had emerged in the early 1990s when the turmoil began in the Valley, and college and university students were promoted to the next session or class without even appearing for examinations. However, mass promotion is not an option for the authorities this time. The Government has asked schools, colleges and university authorities to organise additional classes to compensate for the academic losses. They are hopeful of completing the syllabus within the given time so that students can appear for examinations on time. The officials are holding a meeting of education officers to discuss the situation and have also appealed to the teaching community to put in extra efforts to complete the pending syllabus.

Heading: Another leopard cat killed outside Corbett - Indian Express
Content:
The website of the Vibrant Gujarat Global Investor Summit 2009 cites a bizarre reason for Gujarat's boom in the clinical research industry: "the racial purity of Indians".

"Following the outsourcing of clinical research work from the West, India is becoming a choice destination for the clinical research organisation (CRO) sector. Ahmedabad's Sarkhej-Gandhinagar Highway will house about a dozen such CROs.... Pharma companies choose India as their destination for the reason that Indians (belong to a) pure race, mainly because of fewer inter-caste marriages...." states the website.

The CR industry in Gujarat, which registered a turnover of Rs 500 crore last year, is set to expand further in the coming years.

According to the state Government-run website, more than infrastructure, labour pool, education system, cost effectiveness and the excellent process quality that India and Gujarat offer, it is the pure genetic make-up of Indians that is drawing foreign phrama firms to the state.

The statement has stunned industry experts even as a site promoter maintained that the content was uploaded only after a series of meetings with the departments concerned.

The Gujarat State Biotechnology Mission and the Information Department could not say much about the website content. Akshaykumar Saxena, director, GSBTM, a nodal agency established to promote biotechnology in the state, said, "It is not on our department's site. I do not know about vibrant Gujarat."

Dr Bhagirath Patel, director, Shivrath Centre of Excellence in Clinical Research, said: "The clinical research industry, especially based on outsourcing, is flourishing like never before. But the state Government's reason for this has come as a shocker."

Bhagyesh Jha, the promotion in-charge of VGGIS and director of the State Information Bureau, expressed ignorance about any such content on the website. "I will have to check it," he said.

Heading: Now, Bachchan says sorry - Indian Express
Content:
In the second incident of its kind in one week, a leopard cat on Tuesday was mowed down outside Corbett Tiger Reserve on the National Highway connecting Ranikhet to Ramnagar.

A week ago, another leopard cat, which is a house cat-sized animal with leopard-like markings, was killed after being hit by a vehicle on the same highway. Leopard cats are protected under Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, and are highly prized for their fur by poachers.

Park director Vinod Singhal said, "Animal deaths around Corbett Tiger Reserve by speeding vehicles has become a very serious matter." While the buffer zone of the tiger reserve lines one side of the National Highway, animals cross the road to move towards the Kosi river through patches of privately-owned land or civil forest. "Since this is a highway, we cannot step in and put speedbreakers. But we have written to the national and state highway authorities and the local traffic police. We are also putting up heavy signboards around the area to caution traffic to slow down. Animals tend to move towards the Kosi river," said Singhal.

Last December, a tiger was hit on the same road by a Volvo bus but survived.

Despite the high number of animal deaths around Corbett, the state Government is working on a review petition in the Central Empowered Committee of the Supreme Court to build a road connecting Garhwal and Kumaon through Corbett.

Heading: Bachchan-Thackeray ties still intact, says Uddhav - Indian Express
Content:
Even as Amitabh Bachchan apologised and sought "forgiveness" for certain remarks made by his wife, Jaya, the premiere of his film, The Last Lear, scheduled to be held on Thursday, was called off after suspected Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) activists attacked a suburban multiplex cinema here.

Addressing a press conference today, Bachchan said they were ready to go to jail if found guilty. "I have heard that Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister R R Patil has ordered an inquiry into Jaya's remarks and asked the police to examine the tapes of the function. I will wait for the report and we are prepared to face the consequences. If found guilty, we are prepared to go to jail," he said.

Earlier in the day, Bachchan tendered an apology on his blog. "Everything that we possess today is what came to us from this great state and city. We never have and never can look at Maharashtra with disrespect. If inadvertently this is what has been construed, then we apologise and are sorry and seek forgiveness for any sentiments that have been hurt," he wrote.

At the press conference, he said: "Despite the apology, if this matter still persists, it is a law and order issue and the state administration has to take care."

Asked if he would invite MNS leader Raj Thackeray to watch The Last Lear and settle the matter, the actor said: "He is my friend and has given me a lot of respect. I would also give him the same respect."

When asked whether he was planning to meet Shiv Sena chief Bal Thackeray, he said: "Balasaheb is like a father figure and has treated me like a family member. I can meet him whenever I want to."

Asked whether he would seek an apology from Raj, Bachchan replied, "we are a peace-loving family. We expect nothing. Everybody has the freedom to say that they want to."

Meanwhile, four unidentified men vandalised the Juhu branch of the PVR multiplex at noon on Wednesday. "We have not yet identified whether the miscreants belong to any party but we are investigating it," said Police Inspector D Katkade of Juhu police station. No one was hurt in the incident.

Heading: Cong: Patil should act against MNS - Indian Express
Content:
Even as Amitabh Bachchan launched a strong defence of wife Jaya and showcased his family's love for Marathi and Maharashtra, Shiv Sena executive president Uddhav Thackeray on Wednesday said the two families had not fallen out despite the party's scathing criticism of Jaya for her "anti-Marathi" comments.

The Sena mouthpiece, Saamna, had on Tuesday lashed out at Jaya for her desire to speak in Hindi at a Bollywood event last week, which had also caused Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray to call for a boycott of Bachchan family films and product endorsements until she apologised. Do not provoke us, the Saamna editorial had warned, indicating that Raj may have driven a wedge into the friendship between the Bachchans and the Thackerays.

"We said what is there to be said," Uddhav told The Indian Express. Asked if that did not hurt the close ties the two families had, he replied: "No, nothing happens to that. That relationship is still there." Asked whether he or his father would meet the Bachchans if the latter wanted to, Uddhav said he would respond in detail after the 10-day Ganesh festival ends this Sunday.

The critical Saamna editorial had come as a surprise despite the one-upmanship games between the Sena and Raj's breakaway group. However, political observers pointed out that the editorial had also sought to balance its criticism of Jaya with some praise for Amitabh.

Uddhav's comments came hours after Amitabh stood up for his family and himself through his blog but also sought to apologise if Jaya's remarks had caused hurt. "The casual, off-the-cuff remarks made by her were without malice or deliberate intent, but if it has caused hurt to the sentiments of Maharashtra, Maharashtrians and indeed the city and citizens of Mumbai, then she must regret and offer apology," he wrote on a plane from London to Mumbai on Tuesday.

Heading: Jaya remarks wrong, says Munde - Indian Express
Content:
While Congress president Sonia Gandhi was concerned about the developments in Maharashtra in the wake of the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) leader Raj Thackeray's attempt to whip up anti-North Indian sentiments in the state by playing up Jaya Bachchan's controversial comments recently, the Congress on Wednesday sought to lay the blame on the NCP for the state government's failure to rein in the MNS.

Margaret Alva, the AICC general secretary in charge of the state, on Wednesday briefed the Congress president about the developments. Alva later spoke to CM Vilasrao Deshmukh to apprise him of the concern expressed by the top party leadership about the developments in the state. Some action should be taken to ensure the lives and properties of non-Maharashtrians, she told the CM. "The Congress president is concerned about it," said Alva.

"The Home Minister (R R Patil) is from the NCP. He should act. I cannot give direction to him," said the AICC general secretary. "There are unfortunate developments in Mumbai with language and state being made an issue by certain political parties to divide Mumbai with their eyes on the coming election. Mumbai has always been home to people from all over the country and anyone who tries to destroy this ethos is trying to destroy Mumbai," said Alva.

"You can write both Hindi and Marathi on the same typewriter. It's the same Devanagri script. The issue of language is unnecessarily being exaggerated for political reasons," said Mumbai Congress chief Kripashankar Singh.

Heading: Lower Haj subsidy on Cabinet agenda today - Indian Express
Content:
After the MNS and the Shiv Sena, BJP leader and former deputy Chief Minister Gopinath Munde on Wednesday slammed Jaya Bachchan and said that her remarks were "wrong (ayogya)".

"She has no right to insult Maharashtra after staying in Maharashtra," said Munde, adding that Jaya was "going against her grain" by making such comments. "Jaya Bachchan's statement is wrong. She is proud of Hindi, it is the national language. (But) there should be no disputes over language," he said.

He alleged that the Congress-NCP government in Maharashtra was promoting the MNS in a bid to cut into the votes of the saffron alliance.

While the last two Lok Sabha elections saw bipolar contests with the Congress-NCP pitted against the BJP-Shiv Sena, Munde said the the coming general elections could see multi-cornered fights with the BSP, MNS and a possible third front entering the fray. "There may be a five-corned fight. There is no possibility of a straight fight now," he said.

Heading: Interest subsidy on education loan likely to be cleared - Indian Express
Content:
The Union Cabinet is likely to discuss a proposal of the Civil Aviation Ministry to increase the contribution of Haj pilgrims from Rs 12,000 to Rs 16,000.

While the proposal has the concurrence of the Group of Ministers, it might be difficult for the Civil Aviation Ministry to ensure consensus among all allies. With polls in six states in the next three months and general elections early next year, political observers said the UPA may not wish to invite the resentment of a sizeable minority population.

The Civil Aviation Ministry is concerned that the Haj subsidy bill has bloated by more than Rs 400 crore since 1994 when it was merely Rs 10 crore. The Government's contribution to every pilgrim has also shot up from Rs 17,000 in 1994 to Rs 47,000 in 2007.

If the Cabinet approves the proposal, it will likely reduce the subsidy burden by Rs 50 crore to Rs 550 crore. However, if allies block the move and prevail upon the Government to take on the additional bill, the subsidy level will touch Rs 600 crore.

The Cabinet may also discuss the proposal of Chemicals and Fertilisers Minister Ram Vilas Paswan to the PM seeking to increase the quota for Haj pilgrims to 1,25,000 from 1,10,000. Last year, however, the total number of Haj pilgrims, including private tour operators stood at 1,57,000. As of now, the Government plans to retain the quota at the current level. The Allahabad High Court had stayed the grant of subsidy to any religious pilgrimage. The Centre had filed a special leave petition before the Supreme Court that subsequently vacated the stay.

Heading: Home Ministry to send Gujarat terror Bill to Cabinet - Indian Express
Content:
The Government will help shoulder the burden of interest that students bear on education loans, with the proposal for the same set to get the Cabinet go-ahead on Thursday. The Human Resource Development (HRD) Ministry's plan — which has the backing of the PMO and the Planning Commission — proposes to bear the entire interest cost of education loans during the moratorium period.

The Centrally-sponsored scheme to subsidise professional education will be targeted at students from the 'non-creamy' layer. It is one among several listed on the UPA Government's Common Minimum Programme that promises that the Government "will ensure that nobody is denied professional education because he or she is poor".

"A proposal to introduce a scheme for providing interest subsidy during the moratorium period on education loans taken by students with parents that earn less than a certain income is under the consideration of the Government. It is for those who are pursuing professional education in India," Minister of State for Human Resource Development D Purandeswari had earlier said in the Lok Sabha.

Purandeswari added that the scheme falls under the revised Model Educational Loan Scheme formulated by the Indian Banks' Association.

HRD Minister Arjun Singh had also recently announced that the scheme was on the right track.

The moratorium period refers to the duration of academic courses, when the student usually does not pay monthly instalments for loans.

The total interest component for this moratorium period is added to the principal once the repayment begins after the student has landed a job.

The interest burden which the Government proposes to bear for the moratorium period is expected to cost around Rs 4,000 crore over the entire 11th Plan period. The scheme is likely to benefit nearly five lakh students from families earning Rs 2.5 lakh or less per annum.

At present, the interest rate on education loans runs into double digits — upwards of 12 per cent for amounts up to Rs. 4 lakh; the greater the loan, the higher the interest.

This loan facility will be available for those students who will take admission to professional courses offered by recognised institutions, both government and private.

Heading: Election Commission meets J-K officials on polls - Indian Express
Content:
There is sharp division within the UPA Government over the grant of Presidential assent to the Gujarat Control of Organised Crime (GUJCOC) Bill, 2003, forcing the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) to place the matter before the Union Cabinet.

This would, however, not be the first time that the matter would be placed before the Union Cabinet. In 2006, the Cabinet returned the Bill to the MHA, asking it to hold consultations with the Ministry of Law and Justice in order to identify clauses in the proposed law that could be susceptible to misuse. While the MHA has categorically said it was not in favour of grant of assent to the proposed law, it would not be for the Union council of ministers to decide the fate of the proposed law, which is stuck with the MHA since 2004.

Sources say a powerful section within the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) is in favour of the law being cleared. They feel that denying the law to the BJP-ruled Gujarat even as a similar law, the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA), is in force in the two Congress-ruled states, could put the Central Government in a fix with the Lok Sabha elections round the corner. Sources in the PMO say the MHA has already sent a detailed note for circulation among the Cabinet ministers. It states why the proposed law should not be recommended for grant of Presidential assent.

The MHA wants the Cabinet to ask the President to withhold assent of the proposed Bill indefinitely.

Senior BJP leader L K Advani and Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi had earlier spoken to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and other Central Government functionaries to clear the Bill. Modi has repeatedly told the Centre that his state required the law to counter anti-national elements active in the area. He has also told the Centre that apart from the fact that the law was passed by the state legislature on the directions of the Centre, the GUJCOC Bill is a carbon copy of the MCOCA, which is in force since 1999.

Heading: Saraswati killing: Orissa SIT releases sketches of two suspects - Indian Express
Content:
After deliberations with political parties, the Election Commission on Wednesday met top Jammu and Kashmir officials to ascertain their views on the timing of elections in the state.

EC sources say that while state Chief Secretary S S Kapur and Director General of Police Kuldeep Khoda were confident of the bandobast for the elections, the former, in his presentation, also strongly pitched for creating conditions conducive for a "credible voter turnout in the elections".

"More than the timing of the elections, it's important that various political parties should be taken on board, especially when the Hurriyat is bent on playing the spoiler in the elections," EC sources quoted the J&K officials as saying. "State officials feel that political mobilisation is as important as an early election in the state," the sources added.

This particular view has also been articulated by the Congress and the National Conference when they met the EC top brass on Tuesday. Others like the BJP have stressed more on an early election in the state.

The state delegation said that Jammu had returned to normal while the Valley remains a problem area "although things are not as bad as they were a few weeks back", added the sources.

Apart from the three election commissioners and the two state officials, state chief electoral officer B R Sharma was also present at the meeting.

Later, the EC had a meeting with Home Ministry officials led by Home Secretary Madhukar Gupta. MHA sources said that "more such meetings could be held if needed".

The EC is said to be in favour of an early election. The tenure of the Assembly was to end on November 20, but after the imposition of Governor's rule, the commission must complete the election process by January 10. The EC, according to sources, wants to complete the process before the onset of winter in the state.

Heading: Rajnath meets Samiti leaders, raises pitch on Amarnath - Indian Express
Content:
The Special Investigation Team of the Orissa Police on Wednesday released the sketches of two suspects in the case related to the killing of VHP leader Swami Laxmanananda Saraswati.

Saraswati (84) and four of his associates — Kishore Baba (45), Amritananda Baba (62), Mata Bhaktimayee (40) and Puranjan Ganthi (28) — were killed on August 23 by 30-odd masked assassins at his ashram in Jalespeta in Kandhamal district. "The crime branch has issued the sketches on the basis of information from the eyewitnesses," said DGP Gopal Chandra Nanda. One killer is in the age group of 20-25 years, while the other is between 30-35 years. "Both the men conversed in the local dialect as spoken by the people in Koraput district," said the police.

The sketches come a day after Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik brushed aside demands for a CBI probe into the killing. Patnaik had expressed confidence that the SIT would be able to nab the culprits.

"We will paste the sketches at all police stations as well as public places. They will also be aired on TV for the benefit of the public. Anyone giving information on these two suspects will be suitably rewarded," said Crime Branch SP S K Biswal.

The SIT headed by Criminal Investigation Department-Crime Branch SP Yatindra Koyal started its investigations into the case on August 28, five days after the killing.

Meanwhile the Maoist flip-flop over the killing continued with the People's Guerrilla Liberation Army of the CPI(Maoists) on Wednesday denying its direct or indirect involvement. "We have no role in Swamiji's killing, some people are trying to defame our image. We would take stern action against those who are blaming us for the killing of Swamiji," said the organisation in posters that were put up in Raikia area.

Heading: With no birth date, CPM MP Abdullakutty turns to Nadi astrology - Indian Express
Content:
BJP president Rajnath Singh on Wednesday raised the pitch on Amarnath when he exhorted the Shri Amarnath Sangharsh Samiti to include the "nationalisation" of the 15-km Ranga Mode-Baltal camp dirt track stretch, leading to the Amarnath shrine, in their charter of demands. Drawing a parallel with the disputed Ayodhya structure, since acquired by the Government, he wondered "if it was Article 370 that prevented the state from doing something similar for the Amarnath shrine".

"I was wondering if you would have liked to include this in your charter of demands," he asked the leading members of the Samiti at a function organised to felicitate them.

"I appeal to all parties to reconsider their position on Article 370. We would have supported it, had the Article helped Jammu and Kashmir address various problems afflicting it," he said.

Rajnath added that the fund allocation in the state should be in proportion to the population in different parts of the state.

"Apart from Jammu, Ladakh, too, has been discriminated against in the state," the BJP president said.

Exhorting the Election Commission to take "appropriate action" against political parties supporting the hoisting of Pakistani flags or waving of black flags on Independence Day, he came down heavily on those advocating the opening up of the Muzaffarabad route.

"It amounts to redrawing of national boundaries. Muzaffarabad is in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, and a 1994 Parliament resolution is committed to winning back the territory for the country. How can we ever renege on that commitment," he asked.

Rajnath's assertions were in keeping with his stance as a hardliner, much like in the Delhi BJP national executive, where he first raised the demand to scarp Article 370.

Heading: Paramilitary forces to get Special DG - Indian Express
Content:
Communists may be ideologically against superstition and astrology, but A P Abdullakutty, the CPI(M) MP from Kannur, the party citadel in North Kerala, has sought refuge in Nadi astrology, the art of reading one's destiny from thumbs.

In the first issue of Yathra, a travel magazine published by the Mathrubhumi newspaper group, Abdullakutty has penned an article on his spiritual journey to Vaitheeswaran Koil, in Tamil Nadu's Thanjavur district, famous for the centuries-old Nadi astrology. In the article, the MP said he had squatted in front of a Nadi astrologer, in his search for his birthday, which his family had failed to give all these years. After having got the birthday, the star and other related details of his horoscope, the comrade said he had emerged out of the village a contented man.

Abdullakkutty, a supporter of V S Achuthanandan, went to Thanjavur last month soon after the CPI(M)-DYFI combine's hunt against superstitions, launched after the arrest of fake godman Santhosh Madavan. The DYFI had dubbed its drive against fake god men as "second renaissance", and several innocent swamis were attacked during the drive.

In the article 'Your thumb says it all', Abdullakutty writes that his date of birth has been an issue haunting him all these years. He had not celebrated birthdays as he did not know the exact date. He said the journey to Vaitheeswaran Koil was a search for destiny, after he had exhausted all other means.

"It is believed that the past, present and future of all humans were foreseen and recorded by ancient sages like Vasishta and Agastya in palm leaves and kept in Vaitheeswaran Koil. There is a scripture pertaining to each individual, comprising all details from birth to death."

Abdullakuty said he asked the astrologer to read chapters on birth and family and the latter gave 'almost' correct answers. He said he was taken aback when the astrologer asked whether he was an MP or an MLA. "After some time, the astrologer came with my horoscope and read out all details about my birth, including the star, date and time of birth etc. And he continued to say things about my past and future. I did not hear it...I was satisfied that I got a birthday. That was enough," he completes the write-up.

"I am an ordinary human being. Hence, it is quite natural to express all feelings. I believe in God. Hence I performed the Umra," Abdullakutty told The Indian Express. He seems to be little worried about the controversy his visit to the astrologer is likely to generate in the party. "I have visited Ajmer and many other pilgrim centres in the country and the visit to Vaitheeswaran Koil should also be seen in that perspective. It should not be seen as matter of religious belief," he said.

Tryst with controversy

• The two-time MP from Kannur faced public censure after he spoke out against hartals. He wanted all parties, including the CPI(M), to stop organising hartals, a bane of Kerala.

• He performed the pre-Haj Umra in Mecca, generating much heat in the party circles.

• He faced allegations about running a partnership business firm without the consent of the party and was relegated to a lower committee from the district committee.

• The 41-year-old comrade served as the state president of SFI. But he never went up in the CPI(M) organisational ladder. Now, he is just an area committee member in Kannur.

Heading: ‘Parivar men threatened Vedanti’ - Indian Express
Content:
In RESPONSE to a long-standing demand to quicken the decision-making process and improve the efficiency of the Central Paramilitary Forces, the Government is likely to approve the strengthening of the top management in a Cabinet meeting on Thursday.

Central to the process is the creation of the post of Special DG who will be based near areas of operation and be empowered with financial and functional decision-making powers, sources said. The proposal is to create three posts of Special DGs in CRPF, two in BSF and one in the CBI. The Special DGs of CRPF will be based in Srinagar for heading operations in Jammu and Kashmir, in Patna to command operations in the Naxal-affected states and in Guwahati for operations in the North-Eastern states. Similarly, BSF will have Special DGs in Chandigarh and Kolkata managing the force's operations along the Pakistan and Bangladesh borders respectively, sources said. The CBI Special DG is proposed to be based at its headquarters in Delhi.

The Special DG will hold the rank of Director General but will be in a slightly lower pay scale. Sources said the idea was to ease the burden on the Director General and reduce the time-lag in decision making, often one of the most crucial factors in deciding the effectiveness of an operation.

If cleared by the Cabinet on Thursday, the decision will come at a very opportune time for 19 senior IPS officers who were empanelled in the DG rank on Wednesday. All of them except one belong to the 1974 batch of the IPS.

Since there are not enough DG level posts at present to accommodate all of them, the creation of posts of Special DGs will offer a few vacancies fit for their seniority.

Heading: Gujarat puts ‘open book’ exams on hold - Indian Express
Content:
The Ayodhya police have arrested a Bajrang Dal and a Hindu Yuva Vahini activist for posing as SIMI and al-Qaeda extremists and threatening Ram Vilas Vedanti, a senior Vishwa Hindu Parishad leader.

On August 30, Vedanti had lodged a complaint with the Ayodhya police saying he was being threatened by some SIMI and Al-Qaeda extremists over the phone. After providing tight security to Vedanti, the police put his phone under surveillance. The callers were tracked down and arrested on Tuesday evening. The arrested men have been identified as Ramesh Tiwari, Katra unit chief of the Bajrang Dal in Gonda district, and Hindu Yuva Vahini's Katra unit convener Pawan Pandey.

Faizabad SSP R K S Rathore said the police were interrogating the two. Ayodhya Kotwali police station in-charge A K Singh said some others suspected to be involved in the conspiracy were absconding.

Incidentally, the two youths were present when Vedanti called a press conference to inform mediapersons about the "death threats". "The youths arrested must be some Muslims bearing Hindu names. They were not present at my press conference," Vedanti claimed on Wednesday.

Heading: Deshmukh for study on how Mumbai can grow vertically - Indian Express
Content:
Following opposition from parents' bodies and the Congress, the Gujarat government on Wednesday decided to put on hold the Gujarat State Secondary and Higher Secondary Board's (GSHSEB) recommendation to conduct "open book" examinations for Classes VIII, IX and X from the current academic year.

Government spokesman Jay Narayan Vyas said the exams would be conducted as per the existing system. He added that the government would seek the view of educationists, parents and students over the next three months.

During a video conference with students and parents on Teachers' Day, Chief Minister Narendra Modi had also mooted the idea of an "open book" examination format in the state.

"Modi spoke on the difference between smaran shakti (learning by rote) and samajh shakti (learning by encouraging students to think), while answering questions from a group of students," said sources close to the Chief Minister.

"The present system puts a premium on learning by rote, both by teachers and students. The teachers' notes too get repeated year after year," Modi is reported to have said.

Sources said Modi is all for the "open book" format. "He only feels that the idea should be debated by educationists in the state before the state government formulates a definitive policy on the issue," said a source.

In a press statement today, State Education Minister Ramanlal Vora said the government would take a decision on whether to accept the Board's recommendations in toto or in part only after consulting experts.

Board chairman R K Pathak had earlier said he would announce the decision to conduct "open book" exams on Monday. "I don't want to make any comments on the Board's decision that has already triggered an unsavoury controversy," he said today. He maintained that the Board was an autonomous body, but the government could always review its decisions. Asked if students would be able to adapt to an "open book" examination system, Pathak said: "Bad weather churns out better pilots."

Heading: Modi one of our best leaders, an able administrator: Advani - Indian Express
Content:
Months after visiting World Bank officials suggested that laws should be changed to allow Mumbai to grow vertically like New York, Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh on Wednesday asked the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) to conduct a study on the policies to be adopted for such a development.

He was speaking at a meeting of the MMRDA, which also discussed key projects like Sewri-Nhava Shewa Mumbai Trans Harbour Link (MTHL), Mumbai Metro, monorail and construction of two feeder flyovers for the under-construction Bandra-Worli sea link being.

In December last year, senior World Bank officials, who were in Mumbai for meetings with government officials, had advocated an FSI policy like New York. Bank officials had said that Mumbai can be transformed into a world-class city, but there are too many laws that need to be amended — some by the local government, others by the Central government — to facilitate development on par with metropolitan cities in the world.

They had said since land is scarce, Mumbai should grow vertically like New York to make builders compete with one another for wooing buyers.

At Wednesday's meeting, Deshmukh stated that the proposed Coastal Management Zone (CMZ) notification was impractical and asked representatives of local self-government bodies to meet the Union environment minister in this regard.

Deshmukh assured that the recommendations of the Krantiveer Lahuji Matang Samaj commission which went into the measures to be taken for social, educational and economic betterment of the Matang community would be placed before the state cabinet. The report of the committee, which contains 83 recommendations, including five per cent educational reservations and financial aid for promoting business opportunities, was presented to Deshmukh on Wednesday.

Heading: CPM dist committee seeks Achuthanandan’s ouster - Indian Express
Content:
In an interview to The Indian Express, BJP prime-ministerial candidate L K Advani refused to commit on the question of having Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi on the centrestage in New Delhi. He insisted it was not a question, but a "suggestion for action".

•Recently we saw serial blasts in Ahmedabad and bomb recoveries in Surat. Do you think there has been an intelligence failure?

Intelligence failure does happen in various cases in different governments. But what is alarming is the failure on the terrorism front as such. Can someone explain why Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan or Gujarat cannot have anti-terror laws when it is in place in Maharashtra? This shows the complete lack of will to deal firmly with terrorism.

The consequence of such laxity on the part of the UPA Government has put the internal security of the country at stake.

Other countries, where human rights are supreme, have special stringent anti-terror laws. Even the US anti-terror law is more stringent than our POTA. The first and the foremost need of the hour is that the authorities should convey the message of zero tolerance to the perpetrators of terror. The UPA Government has failed abysmally in this regard.

•You recently had a joint press conference with Narendra Modi in Delhi. What is the political implication of this?

We have already made a statement. The reason for calling him was that a terror attack had taken place in Gujarat and the Gujarat Government had attained remarkable success in preliminary investigations.

So we thought of calling him as well.

•How do you rate Narendra Modi as a national leader?

No doubt, he is one of the best leaders. He is also a very good administrator. He is doing great work here.

•L K Advani has always been viewed as the hardliner in the BJP. Is this image an asset or a liability now as the would-be PM?

These cliches are irrelevant. A hardliner is a person who decides and stands firm on the decisions. What is wrong in that? One should not be a fanatic.

•In Gujarat, the SC/ST morchas are carrying out community-specific membership drives. Is there a paradigm shift in the party once viewed as a party of the higher castes?

There is no paradigm shift. From the beginning, the BJP tried to include everyone and maintained a holistic approach. That is why you will see that in most of the governments we have been party to, the tribal minister has been a BJP member.

Heading: Indian Idol row: SC grants anticipatory bail to RJ Nitin - Indian Express
Content:
For the first time in the state, a CPI(M) district committee controlled by Pinarayi Vijayan has sought the removal of V S Achuthanandan from the Chief Minister's post.

At the meeting held yesterday, the Kottayam district committee openly aired its displeasure over facing the next Lok Sabha elections with Achuthanandan as the Chief Minister. Achuthanandan has less than half-a-dozen loyalists in the 34-member committee. The district committee meeting was attended by Vaikkom Vishwan, party central committee member and convener of Left Democratic Front.

The meeting was held to discuss the "anti-party activities" in the Kottayam area committee, which is controlled by the V S faction. Ten members of the area committee have been served showcause notice. The Pinarayi faction wanted to flush out all V S loyalists from the area committee and issuing showcause notices was part of that strategy, said sources.

During the valedictory function of the party state conference in Kottayam, several inebriated party workers had shown "over enthusiasm" when V S stood up to address the gathering. The subsequent chaos at the venue had forced the party to suspend the function in an unceremonious manner. The party had held the Kottayam area committee responsible for the incident.

Meanwhile, after touring the dissident-infested party stronghold of Onchiyam in Kozhikode on Wednesday, Pinarayi told mediapersons that there was perfect unity in the party, which would suffer little from the exit of a couple of local leaders.

He was referring to the formation of a new Communist party at Onchiyam, by V S loyalists.

Heading: Girl kills self, kin blames Doomsday rumours - Indian Express
Content:
In a breather for popular radio jockey Nitin with the Red FM 93.5, the Supreme Court on Wednesday granted him an anticipatory bail in a case where he was accused of making derogatory remarks towards the Nepali community during one of his shows aired in September last year.

Nitin landed in trouble as the remarks made while talking about Prashant Tamang, the winner of TV show Indian Idol, were construed as ridicule to the entire Nepali community. In his show Morning No. 1, Nitin had allegedly remarked, "If chowkidars are the Indian Idols (meaning Prashant Tamang) then where from we are to obtain chowkidars." Following this, one Dinesh Gurung and few others lodged a complaint that formed the basis of an FIR against Nitin.

Disagreeing with the Calcutta High Court's decision on refusing the RJ the anticipatory bail, a Bench of Justices R V Raveendran and L S Panta said, "On prima facie scrutiny of the material on record, we are of the view that in the backdrop of the facts and circumstances narrated hereinabove, it is a fit case where the appellant is entitled for the grant of anticipatory bail."

"We do not see any satisfactory and convincing reason for custodial interrogation of the appellant (Nitin) for the alleged offence registered against him," the Bench observed. "The appellant (Nitin) can be interrogated by the investigating officer without taking him in custody."

The court, however, directed that in case of his arrest, he shall be released immediately on furnishing a personal bond of Rs 10,000 along with one surety. The court also ordered the RJ to be available for interrogation whenever required.

Heading: French Development Agency to start operations in India - Indian Express
Content:
While scientists the world over were busy trying to unlock the secrets of how the universe was born, a 16-year-old girl ended her life in a tiny corner of Madhya Pradesh, reportedly terrified by the Doomsday rumours that were caused by the experiment's relentless coverage in the electronic media.

Much before television channels returned to "we told you these were only rumours" mode, Chhaya had succumbed to the sulphos tablets she consumed at Ashareta village in Rajgadh district.

The teenager's parents are labourers and have a small television in their one-room home that only gets Doordarshan. She watched the scary programmes on a TV with DTH facility owned by her uncle. She then appeared to have become consumed by them.

Former sarpanch of Ashareta Babulal Parmar told this paper late on Wednesday that a few other children in the village, too, showed signs of fear but Chhaya was unstable.

"Bhukamp aane wala hai, dharti phatne wali hai achha hai mai pahle hi mar jaun (An earthquake is coming, the earth is going to split open. It's better to die before that happens)," she told Virendra Singh Yadav, a head constable at Shajapur's district hospital, where she was taken for treatment. Yadav told The Indian Express that the victim's relatives told him that she had been restless ever since she started watching the news reports.

The incident also exposed how substandard health facilities are in some parts of MP. The girl was first brought to the district hospital in the neighbouring district, 25 km from her village, and later referred to Indore's M Y Hospital. She was conscious and even put her thumb impression on her statement to the police.

Her relatives, including her father Biharilal and uncle Ramprasad, said there was no other reason for her to take such an extreme step. They said she was afraid that the hill near their home would cave in on Wednesday and bury the entire family. She took the tablets around 3 pm on Tuesday.

Dr M Lalwani, who conducted the post-mortem, told The Indian Express that the body did not have any injury marks and there was nothing to suggest that there was any foul play.

Heading: Singur an exception, has sent wrong message: Buddha - Indian Express
Content:
The French Development Agency (AFD), which welcomed the NSG waiver for India, will soon start its India operations with focus on promoting clean technologies and energy-efficient projects. The two countries hope to ink an agreement to begin AFD operations here during the visit of Prime Minister Manmohan Singh to France later this month.

AFD, which contributed 3.5 billion Euros for financing several development projects in Mediterranean countries, South-East Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa, looks forward to work in the areas of diversification of energy sources, urban development and, forestry and culture.

"We plan to propose our support to the Government of India on Overseas Development Assistance (ODA) terms in areas the government will prioritise," Jean-Michel Severino, the Chief Executive Officer of AFD told reporters. He held discussions with top officials in the Department of Economic Affairs, Planning Commission and the Bureau of Energy Efficiency to tie up the loose ends in the agreement to foster closer economic ties. "We have identified alternative sources of energy such as solar, wind power, biomass and geothermal as areas for possible cooperation," said Severino.

Heading: Czech scientist gets three-year jail term, other let off with fine - Indian Express
Content:
Following the insecurity expressed by the business community in West Bengal after the Singur fiasco, Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee on Wednesday stepped in for some much-needed damage control. "Singur is an exception, West Bengal is not Singur. Singur is definitely a problem and I am trying my level best to solve it once and for all," Bhattacharjee said on Wednesday.

The fact that the Tatas are yet to resume work on the Nano small car project, inspite of a string of meetings held under Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi, which included a face-to-face with Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee, appeared to be a sore point with the CM.

Buddha chose to be upfront about the turn of events while attempting to reassure investors, more so in the light of Infosys' marked reluctance to set up shop here. "It is true that after the incidents in Singur, Infosys has shown some apprehensions about investing here. I have asked IT Minister Debesh Das to speak to the Infosys management, and assure them that the Government would guarantee that no such problem would surface when Infosys starts work in Bengal."

"We are not ignoring agriculture. But after our past success in agriculture, we have to move towards industrialisation. Singur had sent wrong messages within and outside the country," he added.

The CM added: "The young generation in West Bengal want industrialisation and nobody can stop it." He said foreign companies are keen to invest in the state, especially in IT and IT-enabled services. He pointed out that the Japanese had shown keen interest in investing in petro chemicals in Haldia.

Heading: E-waste management: Bangalore shows the way - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly three months after their arrest in Darjeeling for collecting rare specimens of insects from a protected forest area, Czech entomologist Petr Svacha was today fined Rs 20,000 while his colleague Emil Kucera was sentenced to three years simple imprisonment and imposed a fine of Rs 60,000. Kucera was, however, granted bail. The Chief Judicial Magistrate of Darjeeling convicted the scientists under the Wildlife Protection Act and the National Biodiversity Act. Svacha's passport has been impounded for a month.

Speaking to The Indian Express from Darjeeling, Czech Ambassador Dr Hynek Kmonicek said: "It's surprising that different sentences were handed down to them for the same offence, committed at the same place and at the same time."

Taranga Pandit, the counsel for the scientists, added: "Svacha was let off with a fine because the court took into consideration his reputation as a renowned entomologist and his educational background. He was said to be a victim of circumstances."

Ever since their arrest on June 22, the scientific community in India and abroad has been appealing for granting leniency for the Czechs. Priyadarsanan Dharma Rajan, fellow scientist, Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment, said the conviction was a great disappointment. "The order has hurt the world scientific community. Justice is denied to the scientists, whose purpose was only to conduct research. Instead, if the scientists were let off with the specimens they collected, their knowledge would have been a great asset for the data deficient northeast Himalaya biodiversity area," he said.

Heading: Travelling gets cool in Punjab, state puts luxury on wheels - Indian Express
Content:
Home to 1,700 IT companies, Bangalore is fast becoming a dumping ground for electronic wastes generated by these firms. The city generates 8,000 tonnes of e-waste annually. But it's manageable, says P Parthasarthy, a chemical engineer from IIT Chennai who started E-Parisaraa — a project supported by the Indo-German e-waste initiative.

The pilot project to manage e-waste without causing ecological damage has been set up with the backing of the state Pollution Control Board, which would like to see the project replicated in other cities of the country as well.

The business model is simple. Most software firms in the city such as IBM, HP, Lucent and Mphasis have agreements with E-Parisaraa to collect their e-waste. E-Parisaraa pays these firms for the e-waste and brings it to their processing facility at Dobbespet, in the outskirts of the city. What makes E-Parisaraa different is that, unlike the backyard handling of e-waste, there is no melting involved in the sorting.

The waste enters the disassembly-line process where it is dismantled and sorted in plastics, rubber and metal sheets. The leftover printed circuit boards (PCBs) and glass items such as tube lights and picture tubes go to the next stage where they are then cut into strips and powdered.

E-Parisaraa has the capacity to recycle up to three tonnes of waste per day, but it is dealing with only one tonne at present. "This is because the backyard scrap dealers have better penetration in the city and have access to most of the scrap. They see us as competition and do not sell us scrap even if we offer better prices," explains Parthasarthy.

E-Parisaraa is an initiative aimed at recycling electronic gadgets and equipments almost entirely and bringing them back into use by industries. While glass and plastic are sold to recyclers approved by the state Pollution Control Board, hazardous components like chromium, arsenic, mercury, nickel, cadmium and lead are separated manually.

E-Facts

What makes e-waste?

• Discarded electronic devices like TVs, PCs, floppies, CDs, batteries, switches, telephones, ACs, cellphones, electronic toys, refrigerators, washing machines, dryers, kitchen utensils and even aircraft parts. Computers account for 25 per cent of e-waste.

Why is it hazardous?

• Domestic e-waste including computer, TV, mobiles and refrigerators contain over 1,000 toxic materials, which contaminate soil and ground water. Exposure can cause headache, irritability, nausea, vomiting and eye pain. Recyclers may suffer liver, kidney and neurological disorders. Chemicals such as beryllium, found in computer motherboards, and cadmium, found in semiconductors, can lead to cancer.

• About 80 per cent of e-waste generated in the US is exported to India, China and Pakistan.

• Unorganised recycling and backyard scrap-trading form close to 100 per cent of total e-waste processing activity.

• About 25,000 workers are employed at scrap-yards in Delhi alone where 10,000 to 20,000 tonnes of e-waste is handled every year.

• There are e-waste scrapyards in Meerut, Ferozabad, Chennai, Bangalore and Mumbai.

Heading: Gujarat BJP rebels form new party - Indian Express
Content:
If Delhi Metro's success has sparked off demands by state governments across the country for similar trains, Punjab has come up with its own alternative transport solution, ensuring that people get to enjoy travelling in air-conditioned buses at existing fares.

A commuter in the state can today travel in an AC State Roadways bus, paying as low as 53 paise per kilometre. This means that a distance of around 90 km between Jalandhar and Amritsar costs around Rs 50, which is comparable to standard bus fares anywhere in the country. Not only are the people of the state loving it, the State Roadways has also seen a surge in profits.

Punjab has 5,000 buses — half owned by the Government and the rest by 10 private transporters — and around 1,500 of these are now air-conditioned. The number is steadily increasing.

Explaining the turnaround, Principal Secretary, Transport, D S Jaspal says: "We did a study and it showed that any bus less than five years' old gave a profit of Rs 5 per km. But any bus older than 7 years ran losses of Rs 80 per km. Our fleet comprised buses which were as old as 15 years, so we weren't going anywhere. It was a vicious cycle of running poor quality buses and making losses."

A need was felt for private investment, and here's where the Government took a crucial decision. Last year, it slashed the tax on plying AC buses in the state.

"An AC bus was levied with a tax of around Rs 9 lakh per year. We brought it down to Rs 50,000. To attract outside investment we had to give this concession. We were chastised for subsidising for the rich but today, the common man can have a comfortable journey without any upward revision in fares," says Jaspal.

Says Sukhbir Badal, president of the ruling Akali Dal: "Bus transport is not to be synonymous with dilapidated buses. We owe it to the common man to provide him quality at a reasonable price."

The stiff competition ensures that the customer is the undisputed king. On a bus from Chandigarh to Jalandhar, the difference is evident: gone is the cranking engine noise, replaced by a soft purr; seats carry panel knobs for adjusting air-conditioning; while an LCD TV plays the latest Hindi film, which you can tune off with a turn of another knob. The first-aid box and fire extinguisher are prominently placed.

As Raghubir Singh, a farmer from Nawanshahr, says, "Honestly speaking I don't have an AC at home. But at Rs 100 I can have this comfort for my two-and-a-half-hour journey."

Equally satisfied is Gurpinder Singh, a bank executive: "I commute to Amritsar. I have to dress formally and in a normal bus I would bake like a snail on hot asphalt. This has changed."

Customer satisfaction, in turn, is translating into profits. Punjab Roadways, which till last year ran up losses amounting to Rs 30 crore, this year registered a profit of Rs 1.5 crore. Buoyed by the response it has decided to add 200 new AC buses.

The private players are making profits too, running at an average occupancy of 75 per cent. On some routes — like Bathinda to Chandigarh — the demand is so high that owners have used up the aisle space to add seats.

"There, the problem is different," says Jaspal. "Since we can't monitor it, the private players are charging rates even lower than what is mandated by law. This adversely affects the State Roadways' margins. We are trying hard to keep track."

The Principal Secretary expects the success to next rub off on the quality of staff. It is easy to believe him, listening to the dapper, denim-clad 25-year-old Munish Rawat, the bus conductor on a Jalandhar route.

He quit his job at a bank to do this, he says. Lugging a modern swipe machine, Rawat explains: "The competition is stiff, so these roadways companies are luring people. I make around 12,000 every month, including over-time incentives, which is much more convenient than facing dust and grime to coax people to open bank accounts."

Heading: Afghanistan gets Khooshi - its first TV show on family planning - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP rebels in Gujarat on Wednesday announced the formation of the Maha Gujarat Party and released the outfit's symbol and constitution. Former Home Minister Gordhan Zadafia has been chosen party president and Bhavnagar MLA Sunil Oza general secretary. The first convention of the party will be held in Ahmedabad on September 25 when other posts and the party structure will be announced.

The conch has been chosen as the symbol and golden yellow the party colour. The party constitution released on Wednesday highlights integral humanism as its core. Zadafia, who is also the chairman of the Sardar Patel Utkarsh Samiti, said the golden yellow colour symbolises sacrifice.

The party leaders, most of whom have roots in the RSS, said they had the chance to contest the 2007 Assembly elections on a Congress ticket or as Independents. They also decided against going to the BJP, they added. "We have sacrificed post, power and prestige for the new party," said Oza.

The Maha Gujarat Party has been touted as the first regional party in Gujarat where politics revolves around the Congress and the BJP. Oza said: "A regional party that puts the state's interest on top is the need of the hour."

Heading: Indian Railways to rebuild Lanka rail line hit by tsunami - Indian Express
Content:
After the death of her old school friend in childbirth, brought on by the pressure of bearing a baby boy, a young woman doctor decides to move to the village and educate people on family planning and birth control practices. In the process she has to overcome hostile village elders and orthodox priests who consider birth control against the will of God.

While Indian TV may have little space for such a story, it is moving audiences in a country far unlikelier: Afghanistan, where the topic of birth control is so controversial that it is referred to as 'birth spacing'.

While Khooshi, in Dari language, joins the list of Indian soap operas currently airing in Afghanistan, and earning a huge following, it deals with a subject considered taboo in this country, bound by tradition and fighting off the Taliban, while at the same time having one of the worst infant and maternal mortality rates in the world.

Tracing the life of a young female doctor from a hospital in Kabul who takes voluntary transfer to a village medical centre, and produced by an Indian television team, Khooshi started airing on the popular Ariana channel last week on prime time. The response after the first episode has been good, with the people relating to its approach to the sensitive issue.

The plot unravels the 'advantages' of birth control and shares knowledge about oral contraceptives and condoms. The lead role is played by Indian actress Soumya Tandon recently seen in Jab We Met as Kareena Kapoor's sister.

Most of the other roles are played by Afghan actors and the serial has been shot mostly in villages around Kabul. The first seven episodes were shot in 35 days by an Indian crew from the Kabul-based AINA Media & Culture Centre.

"We conceptualised the story as a family drama, and though the subject is very hard to tell to the public, we took comedy as a medium. We thought about using the struggle of a woman doctor to drive home the point with female viewers," says Prasant Satapathy, the director of the serial.

Satapathy is relieved that there have been no protests so far. "Making a film or TV serial in Afghanistan is not easy as religious sensitivities are involved. But thankfully people liked our first episode and are even telling us that it is better than any local director showing their religion and culture," he says.

Heading: Cong lowers heat over Beijing:  China was part of NSG consensus - Indian Express
Content:
A 600-km railway line in Sri Lanka, which hit international headlines during 2004's tsunami after more than a 1,000 passengers were killed after being hit by powerful waves, will now be rehabilitated by Indian Railways.

Having bagged the $74 million export order from Sri Lanka's Transport Ministry, as part of the Southern Railway Line Upgrade Project, Rail India Technical and Economic Services (RITES), a public sector undertaking under the Railway Ministry, will upgrade the Colombo-Matara railway line. Senior officials from Sri Lanka's Transport Ministry and RITES recently signed an agreement to this effect. The project is financed by the Indian Government's Line of Credit and is likely to be completed within three years.

Sources said that the integrated project not only envisages the restoration of the railway line but also the induction of new passenger train services on this route.

"RITES will be supplying Diesel Multiple Unit (DMU) train sets and diesel locomotives. It will also set up comprehensive maintenance facilities, including machinery and equipment for of the upkeep of DMU train sets," an Indian Railways source told The Indian Express. As part of the project, RITES is also to train Sri Lankan railway personnel in Indian Railways' establishments.

The project will see RITES rehabilitate a 1,100-km track on this section, which has extensive passenger train movement and is a crucial rail link in Sri Lanka.

"The plan is to supply around 20 DMU rakes and three locomotives for the project. While the diesel locomotives will be manufactured at Diesel Locomotive Works, Varanasi, the DMUs will be manufactured at Integral Coach Factory in Chennai," sources said.

Significantly, this is not the first time RITES has secured a major project abroad. In 2007, the Tanzanian Government awarded RITES a 25-year concession to operate the 2,700-km Tanzanian Railway Corporation (TRC) metre-gauge network along with improving the infrastructure and buying new rolling stock for both passenger and freight services.

In May this year, another Railway PSU, IRCON, had bagged the $1 billion electrified double-tracking project between Seremban and Gemas in Malaysia. This mega project involves the construction of 34 river bridges, 107 small bridges and one 8-km-long tunnel. The first phase of this project is to be completed by July , 2010.

Heading: SRK lights up in Amritsar college, smoke from Centre’s ears - Indian Express
Content:
Amid the heated buzz against China over its stand at the NSG, the ruling Congress today sought to lower the temperature and endorsed Chinese Foreign Minister Yang Jiechi's stand that Beijing had not opposed the waiver and, instead, played a constructive role in Vienna.

"We have nothing within our knowledge to contradict him (Yang). During negotiations (at NSG meeting), something may have occurred. But ant bhala to sab bhala (all's well that ends well)," said AICC spokesperson Shakeel Ahmed. China was very much part of the "consensus" behind the waiver, he said.

The Indian Express had first reported that Congress president Sonia Gandhi had not responded to Yang's request for an appointment and no meeting was possible the next day. Both the Congress and the MEA said today there was no meeting "scheduled."

The party issued a statement underlining its "long-standing relationship" with the Chinese Communist Party that had "grown from strength to strength." Citing Sonia's Olympics visit, it said both parties had "signed an MoU for exchange of leadership development and programmes as part of party-to-party contact."

This comes days after National Security Advisor M K Narayanan said that New Delhi would convey its "disappointment" to China over the latter's stance at Vienna.

Sources, however, have confirmed that Yang did seek an appointment and could not be accommodated. Party leaders said this was because Sonia was scheduled to address two public rallies in Rajasthan that day. "There was no snub, the request came way too late," said a senior Congress leader.

Meanwhile, the Prime Minister hosted a lunch for External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee and his "nuclear deal team." While the PM congratulated the team for its "great job," Mukherjee returned the compliment quoting Dryden: "Beware the fury of a patient man".

Heading: Helipads to roads: 800 cr for Naxal war - Indian Express
Content:
As the ban on smoking in public places comes into effect from October 2, Bollywood star Shah Rukh Khan looks set for another run-in with Union Health Minister Anbumani Ramadoss who had earlier asked him to desist from smoking on screen. This time, King Khan is in a bit of a spot — the Health Ministry, taking note of a Punjab government complaint that he was smoking on the Khalsa College campus in Amritsar during the shoot of Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi, has directed state health authorities to issue Khan a notice.

The Ministry has also asked Mumbai-based NGOs to send leaflets on the ill-effects of smoking to Khan's home everyday. The idea is to make him quit smoking.

"If he doesn't understand the hard way, he should be taught a lesson via Gandhigiri, the way Sanjay Dutt did to Boman Irani in Lage Raho Munna Bhai. This is also the way to approach his wife and son who, after seeing these leaflets, may ask him to quit smoking," a senior Ministry official told The Indian Express.

Punjab health authorities have decided to send Khan a notice for violating the law which prohibits a person from smoking in a public place and at an educational institute. Officials said the fine of Rs 200 was hardly a deterrent, so it was "a good idea" to send him literature on the dangers of smoking and "may work".

In February this year, Khan, reacting to Ramadoss's advice to him not to smoke on screen, said he was impressed with the minister's concern about public health. "I am very impressed with the fact that he wants me not to smoke. I too want to quit smoking in real life." But defending smoking scenes on screen, he said the depiction of such habits was just a part of the character.

"I want to tell you on behalf of every actor, director and producer that anything negative in movies like fighting, firing, smoking, drinking and rapes are not for their glorification, but they are a part of characters. Films can't be all about good things," he said.

Heading: Terror email: To ‘clear’ his name, Haywood on way back to Mumbai - Indian Express
Content:
A fortnight after raising a 10,000-strong special anti-Naxal force, Combat Battalion for Resolute Action (COBRA), the Centre is ready with a Rs 800-crore package to provide security and mobility to local police to take the fight into the bastion of Left-wing extremists.

This year alone, at least 470 people, including 160 security personnel have been killed in Naxalite violence. Last year, of the 650 dead, 218 were security personnel.

A five-point agenda from the Home Ministry comes up for approval before the Cabinet tomorrow:

• Provide mobility to police into forests and inaccessible areas where Naxalites usually hide

• Ensure secured camping and helipads for immediate pursuits

• Security at remote police posts for personnel and magazine safety

• Tarmac approach roads at each post to prevent mines laying by the extremists

• Strengthening armoury at each jail to thwart attacks by Naxals to free imprisoned extremists

The money will be available over the 11th Five Year Plan with "core focus" on eight districts: Aurangabad and Gaya in Bihar, Bijapur and Dantewada in Chhattisgarh, Chatra and Palamu in Jharkhand, Malkangiri and Rayagada in Orissa. Besides, there would be "special attention" over the years on Khammam in Andhra Pradesh, Balaghat in Madhya Pradesh, Gadchiroli and Gondya in Maharashtra, Sonabhadra in Uttar Pradesh. Including West Bengal, 76 districts in the country are hit by Naxalites who are also getting active in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Kerala.

It was only after Prime Minister Manmohan Singh described Naxalism as the No 1 internal security threat that the ministry started to look at it in a different light. The CRPF's proposal for COBRA was caught in bureaucratic hassles and cleared on August 28 by the Cabinet Committee on Security after pressure from the Ministry. COBRA will focus on "effectiveness and operational success" and its members will get exclusive training in terrain and topography of the area of operation.

Heading: Amarinder will move court after House expels him on ‘corruption’ - Indian Express
Content:
US national Kenneth Haywood, who left India last month while being investigated in connection with the Ahmedabad bomb blasts e-mail sent from his account, is set to return to Mumbai tonight in a bid to clear his name.

Sources said Haywood, the Navi Mumbai-based employee of business skills coaching firm Campbell White, is flying back from his home in the US through London on British Airways flight BA 139 due to land after midnight on Wednesday.

Sources said Haywood sent "feelers" to Mumbai Police that he regretted the way he left India despite a look-out notice. While he is not expected to be arrested since the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) has since given him a clean chit, Haywood is expected to visit ATS tomorrow.

Haywood and nine others who had access to the network — from where the email was sent allegedly by a group called the Indian Mujahideen — were subjected to polygraph and brain-mapping tests on August 13. Although there were no restrictions on his movement and his passport wasn't seized, Haywood had been asked to stay put in the country and a lookout notice was circulated. But he left with his wife and daughters on August 17. A Home Ministry probe blamed his exit on a human error by the Immigration Department at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport.

Heading: Singur stalemate won’t give second thoughts to Mittal - Indian Express
Content:
In an unprecedented move, former Punjab Chief Minister Amarinder Singh was expelled from the state Assembly today after a House committee indicted him in an alleged graft case. His Patiala seat was declared vacant for a by-election.

Calling it "political vendetta", Amarinder Singh said: "They (his rivals) could not corner me on any issue, so they devised this method. I will go to the High Court and get a stay. We were not heard at all in the House."

The expulsion of Singh, who was Chief Minister from 2002 to 2007, came amid chaotic scenes with the Opposition Congress MLAs protesting a resolution moved by Harish Rai Dhanda, chairman of the House committee that indicted him for alleged irregularities in a land transfer deal in Amritsar.

In a parallel move, the House asked the Vigilance Bureau to register a case and submit an inquiry report within two months to the Speaker.

Slogan shouting Congress MLAs, barring Singh and Leader of Opposition Rajinder Kaur Bhattal, rushed to the well of the House and clashed with the watch-and-ward staff as they tried to reach the Speaker's podium. They later staged a walk out.

The House also adopted by voice vote a breach of privilege motion against Amarinder Singh and Congress MLA Makhan Singh on the charge of casting aspersions on Speaker Nirmal Singh Kahlon, Dhanda and the House committee.

Heading: OPEC decides to curb overall output through quotas - Indian Express
Content:
Unfazed by the see-sawing fortunes of Ratan Tata's Nano car project at Singur, global steel tycoon Lakshmi Niwas Mittal today described Singur as a one-off incident and made it clear that he was having no nightmares on account of it. He ruled out any possibility of backing out from building two steel plants in the country worth at least $20 billion.

"Singur does not give us nightmares. One instance of Singur cannot be an example for the entire country. If we can get the 123 deal passed without the help of communist parties, why cannot we resolve the issue of Singur? There is nothing that is going to deter us. I am confident that the Nano issue will be resolved. After all, Tatas are doing a wonderful thing and they are doing it for the people of India... I am sure and confident that the West Bengal government and Tatas would resolve the issue very soon and amicably," Mittal said when asked to comment on his projects in Orissa and Jharkhand in the light of the developments at Singur.

Arguing that the standoff at Singur would not make Indian any less attractive investment destination, the chief of ArcelorMittal argued, "One can face this kind of problem in any other country. One particular project can face this kind of opposition from people. But the country as a whole is interested in growing."

But Mittal is clearly not enthused by the progress of his two projects in the country which are facing both delays and cost overruns. "Globally, we are seeing the prices of every input item and other required things going up in the range of 30-50 per cent, implying that there could be escalation," Mittal said, but did not specify the quantum of cost overrun of the projects. When asked to spell out the level of cost overrun he said, "We cannot say at this moment till we reach a level where construction starts. We will release our revised figures after the necessary approvals."

Mittal's projects are yet to have adequate mining linkages in the form of captive mines.Mittal made it clear that any meaningful progress of his projects was feasible once the company had substantial mining allocation. The present allocation of 65 million tonne of iron ore in Karampada mines was not enough, he said. But Mittal hoped that despite constraints in land acquisition and inadequate linkages, ArcelorMittal would begin construction in the first half of 2009 and likely commission the first phase of production by by the end of 2012. ArcelorMittal controls roughly 10 per cent of the global steel output. Mittal urged the Orissa and Jharkhand governments to expedite approvals.

Reacting to Mittal's concerns, the Orissa government today said it would expedite approval process for speedy implem- entation of mega projects including the steel plant by ArcelorMittal.

On Nano plant

Singur does not give us nightmares. One instance of Singur cannot be an example for the entire country. If we can get the 123 deal passed without the help of communist parties, why cannot we resolve the issue of Singur?

On cost overruns

When we started, we estimated they will cost about $20 billion ... but there is a delay, costs are going up. The more the delay, the higher the cost overruns.

On buyouts in India

It is very unlikely that we get an M&A opportunity in India as Indian entrepreneurs are doing very well and whatever expansion we are planning in India would be through greenfield projects.

Heading: Infrastructure growth drops to 4.3% - Indian Express
Content:
OPEC said on Wednesday it would trim overall output by more than 500,000 barrels of oil a day by adhering closer to production quotas — a compromise meant to avoid a backlash from the biggest petroleum consuming nations and stop the rapid decline in oil prices.

Oil prices, at least early on, held steady after extended declines. Also coming out of the meeting was an agreement between Russia and OPEC to improve bilateral cooperation in energy issues.

Heading: NHPC IPO likely by late October or early November - Indian Express
Content:
Following the trend over the previous 3-4 months, the index of infrastructure output once again grew a meagre 4.3 per cent in July, compared to a relatively robust growth of 7.2 per cent in July of last year. The index, which comprises the six core infrastructure sectors — crude oil, petroleum refinery products, coal, electricity, cement and steel — and carries a weight of 26.7 per cent in the index of industrial production (IIP) has been on a downhill ride throughout the current fiscal so far. At 4.3 per cent, this growth was, however, marginally higher than the 3.5-4 per cent growth witnessed over the previous months. During the period April-July, the index registered a cumulative growth of 3.7 per cent as against 6.6 per cent over the same period last year.

All the component sectors, except coal and petroleum refinery products, registered growth rates significantly lower than those witnessed over the same period last year. Coal witnessed a jump of 5.5 per cent in production in July as compared to a growth of only 1.1 per cent in July last year. Over the April-July period, too, growth this year was far higher at 7.7 per cent as compared to 0.8 per cent last year. Despite this, electricity production has lagged considerably growing at just 2.6 per cent over the April-July period as against a healthy growth of 8.21 per cent last year. Analysts believe this is a result of the huge demand-supply gap in coal. "Despite the jump in coal output over the past few months, there is significant pressure on its demand for power generation. Coal imports, too, are fraught with problems," said R Venkatesan, head of industry division at NCAER.

Oil refinery products, on the other hand, witnessed a sharp jump in production from 4.7 per cent in July last year to 11.8 per cent this July.

All the other sectors, that is, crude oil, oil refinery products, cement and steel, continued the downtrend witnessed over the past few months. While crude oil production declined by 3 per cent in July and 0.9 per cent over the April-July period, steel and cement registered growth rates of 3.8 per cent and 6.5 per cent respectively over the April-July period. Last year, over the same period, steel and cement had grown by 6.8 per cent and 7.7 per cent respectively.

Heading: Banks get relief on MF exposure guidelines - Indian Express
Content:
National Hydroelectric Power Corporation's (NHPC) initial public offer (IPO) of 167.74 crore shares (face value Rs 10) is likely to hit the market by the end of October or early November. The issue comprises a fresh issue of 111.83 crore equity shares by NHPC and disinvestment of 55.91 crore equity shares by the government. While 163.54 crore equity shares will be offered to the public, 4.19 crore equity shares will be reserved for NHPC's employees. The issue will constitute 13.64 per cent of the post-issue capital of NHPC.

According to NHPC chairman S K Garg, "Starting from the 11th Five-Year Plan, the government has stopped providing budgetary support to the company. It has given the company the mandate to disinvest up to 24 per cent of the paid-up capital of the company, of which this initial public offer constitutes the first tranche."

NHPC has so far constructed 13 hydroelectric power stations and has an installed capacity of 5,175 MW. Presently, it is engaged in the construction of 11 projects, which are expected to increase its capacity by 4,622 MW. Further eight projects, with an anticipated capacity of 5,751 MW, are awaiting sanction from the CCEA. Survey and investigation work are being carried out to prepare project proposal reports for nine additional projects, totalling 7,255 MW.

Two-thirds of the proceeds from the IPO will go to the government and one third to the company. Rating agency ICRA will rate this IPO.

Chairman Garg expressed confidence that the IPO would sail through. "This IPO will be a challenge as the market is volatile. But the shares of a public sector company are being disinvested after a long gap. Given our financial strength, the state of the power sector where demand far exceeds supply, and reasonable pricing of the issue, the response should be good."

NHPC has strong financials. In FY 2008, it generated total income of Rs 3,675.61 crore, while its net profit was Rs 1,232.31 crore. Between 2004 and 2008, the company's net profit has grown at a compounded annual growth rate of 17.99 per cent. Chairman Garg is confident of maintaining this growth rate in profit even in future. "We expect to maintain a high growth rate in profits even in future, because, according to the tariff policy, we get an assured return on equity of 14 per cent." Two initiatives currently underway should boost NHPC's efficiency further. For monitoring of its projects, the company is introducing an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system. It is also undertaking an organisational restructuring exercise for which Ernst and Young has been appointed consultant.

Heading: DoCoMo may take $933-mn stake in Tata Teleservices - Indian Express
Content:
The Reserve Bank of India has extended the time given to banks to treat advances to equity-oriented mutual funds as capital market exposure by three more months — till December 13. By then, banks would also have to comply with the norms that consider payment commitments made by them to stock exchanges to facilitate transactions by mutual funds within the limit of their capital market exposure.

"On a review, it has been decided to extend the transition period to comply with the requirements by another three months, that is, up to December 13," the RBI said in a notification.

The guideline, which would be effective from December 13, says finance extended by banks to equity-oriented mutual funds would form part of banks' capital market exposure.

Heading: Parekh hits out at realty lobby for ‘absurd’ margins - Indian Express
Content:
NTT DoCoMo Inc, Japan's biggest mobile phone operator, is in talks to buy a stake in India's Tata Teleservices in a deal that may exceed 100 billion yen ($933 million), company sources said.

The news boosted shares in a unit of Tata Teleservices, Tata Teleservices (Maharashtra) Ltd, by as much as 4 percent in the Indian market. DoCoMo is increasingly expanding its overseas presence as growth in the Japanese market slows, and the Tata deal would follow its $350 million investment in Bangladesh's No. 3 cellphone carrier TM International (Bangladesh) Ltd.
