Heading: Shinde: I'll be happy to see Pawar PM - Indian Express
Content:
Armed with an axe, Rukmani Majhi, 45, of Gatibeda village in Sunabeda wildlife sanctuary area, takes a break from household chores every evening to take position on a "morcha" (a fortified platform), along with other men and women of her village, all armed with traditional weapons like bows and arrows, to watch out for Maoists.

For the first time since 2008, when Maoists set up base in the area, two villages on the Orissa-Chhattisgarh border, Sunabeda and Gatibeda in Nuapada district — a part of the "liberated" zone — have taken up arms against them. The two villages together have a population of around 4,000, mostly belonging to the Chakotia Bhunjia tribe.

While no district administration official or local police would venture into the area earlier, the Central Reserve Police Force's (CRPF) CoBRA and Orissa Police's Special Operations Group (SOG) personnel have been camping in the Sunabeda forest rest house since December.

Officials said the change was due to the successful elections in Chhattisgarh. The Maoists had threatened to disrupt the Chhattisgarh polls. But other than some minor incidents, the elections were conducted successfully. According to officials, after the Chhattisgarh polls, people in the two villages started to stand up to Maoists, refusing them food, shelter or any other help.

"This is the first time that we are seeing such resistance against Maoists anywhere in the country. Not everyone wants to help them, but they were doing so till now out of fear. After the Chhattisgarh elections, we got information that locals were rising against the Maoists. It was a conscious strategy to set up camps there, they have to be protected too," said Dilip Trivedi, DG, CRPF.

"When news of the successful polls reached other states, it was taken as a failure on the part of the Maoists. These two villages started resisting the Maoists and also put up a fight against them with bows and arrows," said a senior officer.

"We had been going to these areas for combing operations, but this is the first time that we have set up a base there. This would not have been possible without local support," said another official.

Since the two villages are located on the border with Chhattisgarh, they have often provided a safe refuge for Maoists in the past. In fact, the top Maoist leadership reportedly conducted their fourth central committee meeting in February last year in a village called Kodinga in Sunabeda area. While there are 50 other Naxal-affected villages in the area, they are yet to put up any resistance.

Trivedi said the Maoists are now being seen as "outsiders", as most of them hail from either Andhra Pradesh or Chhattisgarh. "The villagers don't see any gain in siding with the Maoists. We are hopeful that there will be resistance in other areas too," he said.

"One grouse among the villagers was that Maoists were taking their children away. This has given them enough reason to put up a resistance," said an officer.

For Maoists, Nuapada is strategically important as it is the gateway to western Orissa districts of Bargarh, Sambalpur, Bolangir and Kalahandi. If they can dominate Nuapada, it will be easy for them to build a seamless red corridor in western Orissa that connects Bastar in Chhattisgarh to Saranda in Jharkhand.

"When we first entered the area last month, we found several villages around the sanctuary that were not even on the Survey of India map. The villagers had no option but to support the Maoists," said R Jaykumar, a CRPF commandant in charge of the area.

The CRPF has sent a detailed report to the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) on the new developments. "We have started by deploying a small team there. After reviewing the situation, we will deploy more men," said an officer.

Heading: Thousands spoil durbar debut - Indian Express
Content:
Just days ahead of the AICC session on January 17, where the Congress is expected to make its stand clear on party vice-president Rahul Gandhi's candidature as its prime ministerial candidate, Union Home Minister Sushil Kumar Shinde on Saturday was quoted as saying that he would be "happy" to see NCP president Sharad Pawar as the Prime Minister.

"I would be happy if Sharad Pawar becomes the Prime Minister. He is my political guru, I must admit I entered politics because of Sharad Pawar. He brought me to politics in Maharashtra," Shinde was quoted as saying at an interaction with the media in his constituency, Solapur, in western Maharashtra.

"Everyone has ambition. He has been trying (to become the Prime Minister) since 1992... I believe Pawar has been a victim of Delhi politics... There is no reason for harbouring two views about my support to Pawar as Prime Minister. I have said this many times, even on the national platform," he was quoted as saying.

When contacted by The Sunday Express, Shinde did not deny the remarks, but claimed that he was quoted out of context. "My support to Pawar as Prime Minister was in response to questions asked by mediapersons. It was not as if I was pitching Pawar's candidature. It should be seen in the right perspective and not projected wrongly," he said. "My support will always be for Rahul Gandhi as Prime Minister," he said, asserting his loyalty to party president Sonia Gandhi and Rahul.

In Delhi, AICC general secretary in charge of Maharashtra Mohan Prakash refused to comment, saying he was unaware of the context in which Shinde made the observations. Party spokesperson Meem Afzal claimed Shinde had already denied the remarks, and hence he had nothing to add.

But a senior Congress minister in Maharashtra said, "It does not augur well for the party which is pitching Rahul Gandhi for the post". Some Maharashtra PCC leaders indicated a "ploy" to streamline the party's strained relationship with the NCP. "Shinde is a seasoned Congress leader. He would never make a mistake. There is a definite ploy," said a party leader.

"Shinde's support to Pawar has a hidden political agenda — to mend fences with the NCP in his own constituency," said a senior AICC leader.

The NCP, meanwhile, said Pawar was not in the race for the top job. "We all know Sharad Pawar is the most capable leader to become the Prime Minister. But he is not in the race. The NCP understands its political limitations. The party contests limited seats in the Lok Sabha which makes it difficult to stake claim for the top post. The arithmetic is not in our favour," said party chief spokesperson Nawab Malik.

"Shinde's statement is his personal view. What he meant was that if Pawar becomes the Prime Minister, he would have liked it as he is a leader from Maharashtra. But he also indicated that he would like to go by the party's decision," said MPCC spokesperson Ratnakar Mahajan.

"Shinde's open support to Pawar as PM is to ensure NCP helps him in Solapur. The 2014 Lok Sabha elections will be crucial for Shinde as he faces unrest from farmers in the region," said another MPCC leader. The NCP is known to have some strongholds in his Solapur Lok Sabha seat.

"Moreover, the AICC is already exploring the possibility of picking Shinde as one of the probable candidates for the top post in order to consolidate the Dalit vote bank in its favour. Even if it doesn't declare Shinde as the candidate, it wants to use his No. 2 position at the Centre to retain its Dalit vote bank," he added.

\"Shinde has supported Pawar's candidature as Prime Minister. It was shown on television channels, so how can we deny what appears in public. Moreover, he has spoken extensively on Pawar and not just made a passing remark. However, we don't doubt Shinde's loyalty to Rahul's leadership," said another state Congress leader.

Shinde and Pawar are known to share a close friendship. During the 2009 Maharashtra Assembly elections, Pawar and his daughter Supriya Sule launched the campaign of Shinde's daughter, Pranati, in Solapur Assembly constituency. Pawar also campaigned for Shinde during the Lok Sabha elections.

"Pawar and Shinde have always been friendly despite the Congress and NCP often being at loggerheads," said a senior NCP leader.

Meanwhile, the BJP said Shinde's remarks showed the Congress has accepted that Manmohan Singh's successor will not be from the party. "In a way, Shinde has already conceded that no Congress leader will be the next Prime Minister. He may daydream about who should be the Prime Minister, but the people have already reposed their faith in Narendra Modi's leadership," said BJP spokesperson Prakash Javadekar.

with inputs from Delhi

\

Heading: Six dud firms to transfer money to Virbhadra, family - Indian Express
Content:
The first of Arvind Kejriwal's planned daily janta durbars collapsed an hour after it started Saturday, after a heaving crowd of over 20,000 people threatened to physically swamp the chief minister and his cabinet colleagues, and the meeting teetered on the edge of disintegrating into complete chaos.

Kejriwal and Urban Development Minister Manish Sisodia were forced to retreat into the secretariat building about an hour after the durbar started at 9 am, leaving the other ministers attempting to hear the people's complaints.

The chief minister said he was in danger of being crushed by the crowd, and announced that the durbar was being suspended until the government was able to plan better and put proper arrangements in place.

Standing on the roof of the reception wing of the secretariat, Kejriwal told the crowd behind police barricades: "I accept that there were problems with the arrangements. I am deeply sorry that we could not listen to all your problems. People climbed on to the chair and table at which I was seated, and I could have been crushed if I had not left... We will come back to you with full arrangements and have another janta durbar in four to five days."

"When the crowd became unmanageable, there were two options before me, either to resort to a lathicharge or to talk to the people. I chose the second option. Next time we will have the janta durbar at a stadium," he said.

The chief minister had announced that the entire cabinet would sit outside the Delhi secretariat every Saturday to listen to the people's grievances, and would attempt to solve the urgent problems on the spot. Every weekday, a minister would receive grievances from the public.

A large proportion of the people who thronged the road outside the Delhi government headquarters were contract workers seeking permanent jobs.

Kejriwal said: "I realise that the maximum grievances are among contractual workers from BSES, Asha workers, teachers. I assure you that we have taken note of your complaints.

"On Monday I will ask all departments for data on the number of contractual staff, and why they cannot be made permanent. They will submit a report in a week, and I will try to take a decision in a month. You have waited for so many years, give me this much time."

He also requested them not to come back at the next janta durbar, so that other complaints could be heard.

The chief minister and six cabinet ministers sat in the open outside the secretariat along with senior officials, as people began handing in their complaints. Health Minister Satyendra Jain, whose mother passed away on Saturday morning, was not present.

Each person was given a slip to confirm the receipt of his complaint. Officials at the help desk said those who had supplied their mobile phone numbers would receive a confirmation SMS. \"All written complaints will be put up on our web site and the status of action taken on the complaint will be constantly updated," an official said.

Barely 15 minutes into the durbar, however, the crowd — Kejriwal said there were 5,000 people against an expected 500, while police sources said at least 20,000 people had turned up — turned unruly. Delhi Police and Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) personnel struggled to manage the crowd, which broke the barricades at some places. The entire stretch of road from ITO to Rajghat was closed, and barricades were erected on the divider so that people could occupy one carriageway.

Some 300-400 police personnel were present outside the secretariat. "There was seating arrangement for 1,000 people outside the secretariat, but a much larger crowd turned up, leading to the chaos," a police officer said.

Several people returned disappointed. "I had come here in the hope of getting relief from my problems. But I was pushed around, and I am leaving after having waited for five hours. I wanted to meet the CM to seek a job for my physically handicapped son. There is no one to look after his needs after I retire," said M S Kaushik.

The BJP accused the AAP of promoting anarchy. "This is definitely promoting anarchy. It is a sign of bad governance," senior BJP leader Harshvardhan said.

Heading: After telling Delhi to sting, AAP wants Lokpal to snoop - Indian Express
Content:
The web of financial transactions between Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Virbhadra Singh, members of his family and controversial businessman Vakamulla Chandrashekhar involve money transfers from him to the CM and his family via at least five companies that ceased to exist. And, in one case, money moved back and forth between the two sides.

This is revealed in an investigation by The Indian Express based on Registrar of Companies records and bank statements, including the one made public by Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Arun Jaitley.

As per that statement, on January 10, 2012, Chandrashekhar received Rs 49.99 lakh in his personal account from Maple Destinations, a company owned by the CM's son and daughter, Vikramaditya Singh and Aprajita Kumari, respectively. The very next day, this amount was transferred to Tarini International, a company of Chandrashekhar's Tarini group. As per RoC records, in the financial year 2011-12, Maple received Rs 49.99 lakh from Tarini Sugar and Distillaries Ltd, another company of the Tarini group.

No one from the CM's family responded to questions from The Indian Express on this transaction and others and involving companies that didn't exist. Chandrashekhar denied any wrongdoing and said he was "open for any investigation at any levels".

Between November 4 and November 21, 2011, Chandrashekhar, as per his bank statement, received inflows into his personal account amounting to Rs 1.6 crore from six companies. During the same period — November 4 to November 29 — a total of Rs 1.75 crore was transferred to the accounts of Chief Minister Virbhadra Singh, wife Pratibha Singh and son Vikramaditya Singh.

Consider the nature of these transactions:

* One of these six companies is Punjab Foods Private Ltd. On November 21, 2011, Punjab Foods deposited Rs 45.5 lakh into Chandrashekhar's account and four days later, Rs 40 lakh from here was transferred to Vikramaditya Singh's account.

Incidentally, six months earlier, on April 18, 2011, Punjab Foods had filed an application before RoC, Chandigarh, to wind up its operations.

That application stated, "Pritpal Singh (director of the company), informed the members the company is not having any business activity for the last 10 years. Further company is having neither any assets nor any liabilities, therefore Easy Exit Scheme 2011 is opted for the closure of the company".

The company was officially wound up on April 20, 2011. Yet, Chandrashekhar's account showed a deposit of Rs 21.50 lakh from Punjab Foods as late as July 24, 2012.

Speaking to The Indian Express on January 2, Chandrashekhar had said he received money from Punjab Foods against agricultural produce he sold.

* On November 4, 2011, Chandrashekhar had a balance of Rs 4.05 lakh in his account. Over the next five days, Rs 92.90 lakh came into it from Kesari Nandan and Co (Rs 17.99 lakh), Shiva Stores (Rs 15.01 lakh), Jai Durga Impex (Rs 12.25 lakh), Laxmi Enterprises (Rs 7.65 lakh), Siddharth International (Rs 26 lakh) and one Suraj Singh (Rs 14 lakh). On November 11, Chandrashekhar transferred Rs 65 lakh, in two transactions, to Virbhadhra Singh's account.

According to the RoC records, Jai Durga Impex, Shiva Stores, Kesari Nandan and Co and Siddharth International all had ceased to exist before any of these transactions.

From Chandrashekhar's account, a transaction of unknown value failed on November 15, due to "insufficient funds".

* Between November 17 and November 21, Chandrashekhar's account received Rs 45.5 lakh from Punjab Foods and Rs 53 lakh from from one "V Chandra Shekhar". Four days later, Rs 71.80 lakh in two instalments of Rs 40 lakh and Rs 31.8 lakh was transferred to CM's son Vikramaditya Singh from Chandrashekhar's account.

Subsequent to this transfer — and some minor transfers not related to the CM's family — Chandrashekhar's account balance became Rs 55.05 lakh on November 25, 2011. On November 29, 2011 two instalments of Rs 25 lakh each were transferred to Pratibha Singh and Virbhadhra Singh.

His balance after these transactions was Rs 4.73 lakh, marginally higher than what it was when the transactions began.

When asked about the transactions with the CM and his family, Chandrashekhar said: "These companies are vendor companies with whom we have had trade relationships. We have done all transactions legitimately through banks. Whether they are doing business still or not, I am not competent to answer as it is purely their business."

Despite telephone calls and text messages Vikramaditya Singh was not available for comment. Jaitley has accused Virbhadra of granting an extension to Venture Energy and Technology, promoted by Chandrashekhar, for executing a hydel project.

Asked about the money received from Maple, Chandrashekhar said: "I and VVikramaditya Singh together wanted to do a construction project in 2010-11. Accordingly, my part contribution of Rs 2 crore was made to Vikram. Since the project did not take off, he returned the money through Maple. Where is the illegality?" He added: "Shri Virbhadraji is a very noble person and worthy of friendship...I am open for any investigation at any levels."

Heading: Delhi businessman overtakes Vadra’s car, booked for rash driving - Indian Express
Content:
After urging citizens to sting corrupt government officials, the AAP government is pushing hard to pass its version of the Jan Lokpal Bill in Delhi. While the process to draft the bill is already underway, Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal has announced that the Bill will be passed in a special Assembly session by February.

"A committee has been formed to draft the law. The committee under the chief secretary will include secretaries of the departments of home, urban development, law, finance and advocate Rahul Mehra," Kejriwal said on Thursday.

"We will all meet at Ramlila Maidan either in the last week of January or first week of February," he said.

The Bill, he said, would be discussed with the "people of Delhi" at Ramlila Maidan for consent.

A Lokayukta will head the new body to combat graft with powers to conduct its own investigations, surveillance and even tap phones.

"As in the AAP's model Jan Lokpal Bill, the head of the body, in this case the Lokayukta, will have powers to tap phones, conduct independent investigations and surveillance against those who face corruption charges," Urban Development Minister Manish Sisodia said.

According to Kejriwal, the Lokayukta would function as an independent body. "Today if I am accused of corruption, there is no independent body which can investigate me but this will happen once the law is drafted," he said.

Heading: Does AP mean Ahmed Patel, asks prosecutor in Italy court; middleman says don’t know - Indian Express
Content:
A Delhi businessman was penalised by traffic police for "rash driving" after his car overtook the cavalcade of Robert Vadra, son-in-law of Congress president Sonia Gandhi.

A police officer, who did not wish to be named, said the car of Saurabh Rastogi, a businessman who lives in Paschim Vihar, was chased and intercepted by police after Vadra's securityman called the police control room and complained that a car had driven past "dangerously".

The officer said Rastogi was headed towards Lajpat Nagar from the Modi Mill flyover in Okhla at the time of the incident.

"Rastogi was in a Maruti Ritz and Vadra's cavalcade was ahead of him. We were told he had been honking continuously. In a bid to overtake the cavalcade, he accelerated and sped past Vadra's car. It was then that a securityman travelling with Vadra made a PCR call. The traffic police were also informed," the officer said.

Rastogi's car was chased by traffic policemen and intercepted near Amar Colony in south-east Delhi. "He was issued a challan for dangerous driving under Section 184 of the Motor Vehicles Act and let off," the officer said.

Heading: Surat-Amravati Express train flagged off - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: Internal politics take a toll on MSU’s teaching staff - Indian Express
Content:
While the train will run from Surat twice a week, on Thursdays and Sundays, it will return to the city from Amravati on Fridays and Mondays

Minister of State for Railways Narayan Rathwa on Thursday flagged off the much-awaited bi-weekly superfast train from Surat to Amravati from the Surat Railway station.

While the train will run from Surat twice a week, on Thursdays and Sundays, it will return to the city from Amravati on Fridays and Mondays.

The inauguration of the new train has been welcomed by the public, particularly the city's Maharashtrian community. A large number of people from Maharashtra work and stay in the city and have been demanding the introduction of a Surat-Amravati express for quite sometime. According to sources, seeing the crowd from both the destinations, chances are that the train will be made tri-weekly after some time.

On the occasion, Rahwa said: "Surat is the economic capital of Gujarat. The mega industries and business centres in the city attract many people from neighbouring states to come and work here. We had planned to inaugurate two more trains, one from Surat to Mahuwa in Bhavnagar district and the other from Surat to Muzaffarpur in Bihar. We have cancelled the inauguration of Surat-Muzaffarpur Express due to the flood crisis in Bihar."

Work has been started to convert the narrow gauge lines into broad gauge lines in Gujarat. The work on the narrow gauge line between Vadodara and Chhota Udepur is about to finish.

"We have discussed plans with experts in Japan to start three bullet trains in India. The first bullet train will be from Mumbai to Ahmedabad, while the other two will run from Mumbai to Chennai and Amritsar to Delhi," Rathwa said.

Others present at the inauguration ceremony were Congress MP Tushar Choudhary, Minister of State for Home Manekrao Gavit, ex-mayor of Surat city from BJP Dr. Kanubhai Mawani, ex-member of Divisional Railway Users Consultative Committee Wahab Belim and higher officials of Western Railway.

Heading: Spoilsport: VMC not game for upkeep of Akota stadium - Indian Express
Content:
The Mecca of higher education in Gujarat, the Maharaja Sayajirao University (MSU), which is the only English medium autonomous university in the state, is facing an acute shortage of suitable teaching staff due to internal politics and also because of the teachers having better offers from other institutes.

The issue has intensified this year with the replacement of professors and readers by temporary lecturers. More so, with deans from three faculties also retiring this year.

While, the HoD of the Chemistry department Prof Surekha Devi resigned in August this year, another teacher, Prof Satish Joshi from MSU's Electrical department, is in the process of putting in his papers.

Joshi said, "I will soon resign from the post of professor in the Electrical department, as I have an offer from South Gujarat National Institute of Technology, Surat."

MSU Syndicate member, I I Pandya, while citing an example of an Applied Physics Reader George Raju, said, "George was offered the post of a professor in IIT Powai last year, but since he wanted to stay back in MSU he wrote to the former Vice-Chancellor. However, all his demands went unheard and he had to finally resign."

Former HoD of the German department, M K Natrajan, left the varsity last year to join the Banaras Hindu University as a professor.

Professor H G Shukla, from Mechanical Engineering department also resigned last year.

Besides, Prof S G Gupte from the Electrical department, Jay Kumar Reddy from the graphics department of the Faculty of Fine Arts (FFA), Parul Mukherjee from Applied Arts department, and Daulat Swarupia from Management department, have also resigned in the last two years.

Sources at the MSU administration informed Newsline that there are more readers and lecturers, who plan to leave MSU to join IIT Gandhinagar.

Dean of the FFA, Prof Deepak Kannal, while commenting on the resignation of two teachers from the faculty said: "Both the teachers were offered better positions by JNU. I recently met MSU V-C Prof Ramesh Goyal to speed up the appointment procedure. He has taken up the issue in a positive way."

A university lecturer commenting on the sluggish approach of the varsity said, although advertisements for the interviews in Performing Arts and Mechanical department were issued in 2004, the interviews will be held only now.

Prof Goyal said, "Plans are being worked out to appoint deans of three faculties — Commerce, Arts and Science — as the present dean of the Science department, Prof A V Ramachandran will retire this year."

Heading: Fake notes racket: SOG sleuths in West Bengal - Indian Express
Content:
Only soccer stadium of central Gujarat full of weeds, being used as exhibition ground

While the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) is busy planning the allocation of the recently acquired grant of Rs 5 crore for the development of an indoor stadium at Sama, it is clearly ignoring the poor condition of the 23-year-old Akota Football Stadium.

The sports ground, which is the only football stadium in central Gujarat, has not seen any development or improvement over the last few years. The ground, which was once witness to the cheers of the crowd and the whistles of the match referee, is now covered with overgrown weeds and lacks a decent goal post and a cricket pitch. The stadium is now used for exhibitions, stage shows and Navratri events.

"We had sought a contract for the maintenance of the ground from the VMC long back. But they agreed to give a green signal to the proposal only on the condition that the ground would be used during Navratri. It is totally unfair that our year-long hard work to develop the ground will go waste during Navratri," said Hardev Jadeja, honorary general secretary of Baroda District Football Association.

Apart from cultural activities, the ground is occasionally used for motor racing events by racers from Mumbai. This makes the ground even more battered and unfit for other sports. At least 273 students come to the ground regularly to play football and cricket.

"We have stopped asking for any help because we are tired of it. I have been playing in this ground for the past 15 years and have not seen any official taking interest or even visiting the place It is our talent and passion for the game which keeps us going," said a player on condition of anonymity.

VMC Mayor Balkrishna Shukla, who made the announcement about the new indoor stadium a few days back, parroted the oft-repeated phrase that set all queries to rest. "Things are in the pipeline," was all that he had to say about the deplorable condition of the stadium.

Rajendra Shah, from the Tourist Department of VMC, responsible for the maintenance of the stadium, said: "No one takes interest in the ground. We do not get any demand for improvements. Hence, it remains unattended."

Heading: 14-day police remand for Tanveer, Zaheer - Indian Express
Content:
A five-member team of the Special Operation Group (SOG), Vadodara, went to West Bengal on Wednesday night to probe the fake currency racket, wherein two persons of Bangladeshi origin were arrested with fake currency notes from Vadodara railway station on September 7.

According to SOG Police Inspector Karim Polra, the team has been sent to Malda in West Bengal to arrest Mohd Ikram Ali Shiekh who supplied counterfeit currency to the duo.

"The five-member team comprises Police Sub-Inspector A D Parmar and four other policemen," Polra said.

SOG officials had also visited Bharuch, as it was found during questioning that the accused had circulated counterfeit currency in Bharuch.

"The police, however, failed to recover anything as most of the notes were already in circulation," said Police Inspector D L Zala.

The two arrested, Mohammed Nazrul Shiekh (22) and Abdul Majid Shiekh (32) belong to Baghmara village in Malda district of West Bengal. Mohd Ikram Ali Shiekh also hails from the same place.

They had purchased cutlery worth Rs 15,000 from shops in the Walled City areas of Vadodara, Bharuch and Surat and exchanged notes of Rs 500 denomination. "They had bundles of 35 notes of different number series. The series include 8DP 970901 to 900000, 9 AW series and 9 AN series. They had fake currency of a face value of Rs 60,000 with them," Polra added. The police also seized genuine currency worth Rs 13,880 and Rs 15,000 worth cutlery from them.

Heading: GU registrar fined for closing ears to RTI queries - Indian Express
Content:
The duo have refused legal help and have remained unrepresented

The designated metropolitan court, hearing the Surat bomb cases on Thursday, extended the police remand of accused Tanveer Pathan and Zaheer Patel to another 14 days.

Both Pathan and Patel have been accused of being part of the conspiracy of planting bombs in Surat. This is their second 14-day remand.

The accused have remained unrepresented in the court after they refused to take legal help. When offered services of a lawyer through legal aid clinic by Metropolitan Magistrate G M Patel, they refused it again.

In its remand application, the Surat Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) stated that the investigating agency required more time to collect all the evidence pertaining to the case. The two have been booked in a case lodged at the Kapodara police station in Surat where a car loaded with explosives was found.

Reading out the remand application, special public prosecutor J M Panchal said: "Police want to further investigate about the explosive-laden Maruti WagonR car found in front of Purna Hospital. The exact details about how the car was stolen from Navi Mumbai, how it was brought here, and who put the fake number plates, need to be investigated."

More than 17 kg of ammonium nitrate, 9 kg of splinters, 16 kg of screws, 11 detonators, one programmable IC chip among other things were recovered from the car. According to DCB officials, the explosives were meant to cause widespread damage to human life and property.

The DCB is also looking for clues that will help them get to the bottom of SIMI's terror plan. The investigating agency said in the remand application that they had to find the link the accused had with other terrorist plots, and more importantly what their future course of action was.

Heading: Dengue stings again: five cases reported in city - Indian Express
Content:
In two separate cases, the Gujarat State Information Commission has slapped separate penalties of Rs 25,000 and Rs 10,000 on the Public Information Officer (PIO) of Gujarat University for not providing them with information sought under the Right to Information (RTI) Act.

The University Registrar, who is the lone PIO of the university, has been slapped a fine of Rs 25,000 for not providing information to one Pankaj Srimali on 21 specific aspects of the GU admission process. He has incurred another penalty of Rs 10,000 for not responding to the application filed by the dean of the Faculty of Arts, Pradeep Prajapati, who had wanted to know what was done with the letters sent to the GU V-C and registrar by the Governor's office and state Education Department earlier.

"Not only these, there are more cases pending against the University Registrar and we hope to see some more such penalties soon," said Prajapati, adding that the University PIO has failed to address at least five RTI applications, which are now pending before the Commission.

"Such strict measures were necessary for Gujarat University," said R N Das, Gujarat State Information Commissioner. "They have been given enough rope to set their house in order, but unlike the M S University in Vadodara, the GU took our observations casually and failed to implement the RTI," he added.

MSU, which has followed the Commission's order, has appointed the head of all the departments as PIOs, thus de-centralising the system. GU, on the hand, has retained a centralised system and kept the registrar as the only PIO, Das said.

Heading: Now, expect no delays, corruption in approval of your building plan - Indian Express
Content:
While last year, the total number of cases detected was 388, this year it is 107

Monsoon or no monsoon, dengue continues to be a cause of concern during this time of the year.

This year, five cases of dengue in September alone have marked the advent of post-monsoon dengue season. While three of the cases happen to be from Kokhra, Behrampur and Rakhial, two others that have come to light are from Nicole Road and another area in the north zone.

The Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC)'s initiative to conduct door-to-door survey to detect malaria cases in July this year is also being seen as a step to check the number of dengue cases each year.

Last year, the number of total detected cases was 388. Out of this, 124 were sample cases from surveillance centres. This year, the total number of cases is 107 of which 59 are from surveillance centres. This downslide in the number of cases has certainly given a boost to the officials. Moreover, there has been a change in the pattern of symptoms of dengue.

Suhas Kulkarni, Medical Officer Health (AMC) said: "The traditional symptom of shivering is absent nowadays because the disease is being detected early and is treated before it gets complicated."

Rakesh Vaidya, Chief District Health Officer (CDHO) Ahmedabad (Rural) said: "There have been instances of dengue in rural villages, but the instances have been sporadic in nature. Whenever there

is news of a case in any village, we rush there and take all the required steps. This has brought down the number of dengue cases in the rural areas."

Heading: Thunderbolt proves fatal for two - Indian Express
Content:
Civic administration emulates Pune, to adopt AutoDCR software

Having made inroads into Pune, Surat, Coimbatore and several other cities in the country, the Automatic Scrutiny of Development Control Rules (AutoDCR) software is all set to be introduced in Ahmedabad. It will enable the civic administration to cut on delays, corruption and inaccuracies. The software was first launched on a pilot basis in 2005 in some areas of Ahmedabad Urban Development Authority (AUDA) and is now being introduced throughout the city.

The system enables scrutiny of building plans in a very short time and eliminates the three months to one year delay, as is the case now. Plans are required to be submitted to the civic body in a CD, with only the original print of the approved plan and the non-digitised site-related documents in the hard copy format.

The software checks different aspects of the building plan with the rules. If any portion of the plan is rejected, the AutoDCR specifies the rule to which it did not conform to.

For crosschecking the site of construction at a later date, the field engineers will be provided with a Personal Digital Assistant (PDA), which will contain all the points that require verification.

A note can also be made in the PDA to check whether the construction conforms to the rules. The system itself will alert the officials on the date and time of site visits. An automatic alert will be sounded and the message will reach the engineer as well as the promoter, so that both are present at the spot at the fixed time.

Municipal commissioner I P Gautam said for the past one-and-a-half months, officials and applicants were being trained on how to use the software, which has been provided by a Surat-based firm.

Incidentally, Surat has also adopted the same software, but it is Pune that had introduced it full-fledged some time ago, becoming the first city in the country to have such a system.

Gautam hoped that the system would stabilise soon. He said it will help reduce corruption in the town-planning department to a major extent. He added this was because of in-built transparency of the scrutiny process, wherein a match with the GDCR was the sole criterion for passing a plan.

Dilip Patel, a noted city-based architect, who is also on the approved list of AMC, welcomed the decision to introduce the new system.

HOW IT WORKS
An AutoDCR scans the AutoCAD drawings and checks whether the proposed construction plan matches with the General Development Control Regulations. It is a four step process that produces the desired reports: It creates a new project and associates the developed AutoCAD drawings and project attributes; the drawings are required to be in a specified pattern. The system reads the drawing and extracts the geometrical information of layouts and building plans. Finally, based on the project, the software attributes the graphical object information which is mapped to the relevant development control rules. Thereafter, the final detail rules of the verification report are produced, indicating the passed or failed status of each rule.

Heading: Border area development plan gets Rs 21-cr boost - Indian Express
Content:
Ten-year old boy and 35-year-old man killed on the spot after being struck by lightning

In two separate incidents, a 10-year old boy and a 35-year-old man died after being struck by lightning on Wednesday in Surat and Tapi districts.

In the first incident, Vansingh, the youngest son of Jumaram Thakre, a labourer who had migrated to Surat from Nandurbar district in Maharashtra with his family a week ago, died after being struck by lightning.

Vansingh was playing in an open space on Satellite Road in Varachha when it started raining heavily.

He was struck by lightning when he took shelter under a tree. He was killed on the spot.

The Kapodara police rushed to the spot immediately. Seeing the poor condition of the family, people staying in the nearby societies collected Rs 25,000 in cash and gave it to Jumaram for the final rites of his son.

In the second incident, Manubhai Gamit, a resident of Vyara taluka in Tapi district, was on his way back home when lightning struck, killing him on the spot.

Some of the passers-by spotted the body and informed the Vyara police.

According to the police, Gamit worked as a supervisor at the Vyara Sugar factory.

Heading: Mine of protest: Workers oppose sanctuary status for Girnar forest - Indian Express
Content:
Started in 1984, BADP now covers 96 districts in 17 states

New developmental projects worth Rs 21 crore both in civilian and security sectors have been undertaken under the Centre's Border Area Development Programme (BADP) this financial year.

The BADP, which had its origin in the border district in 1984, was the brainchild of the then Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi. Like Chief Minister Narendra Modi, he too was a frequent visitor to the border district.

The countrywide project now covers 96 districts in 17 states.

The programme initially concentrated on creating facilities in the technical field, which was lacking in those days. Though the programme now covers two more bordering districts in the state, it is Kutch which continues to be the highest recipient of the grant every year.

So far, more than Rs 200 crore has been spent on creating infrastructure facilities in all sectors of development.

District Planning Officer J P Thackar told Newsline on Thursday: "The district now gets sizeable funds from the general budget of the state with each development work worth crores of rupees. A sum of Rs 123 crore has been spent so far under BADP since the responsibility for the implementation of the programme came under the district collector in 1994."

He said this year's development projects were meticulously decided under the personal guidance of District Collector R R Varsani who headed the district level committee of BADP. He said these projects, sent to the state level screening committee headed the state chief secretary, were finally approved last March, and the funds were accordingly allotted to begin work.

Thackar said, this time, road projects in the remote border areas have been undertaken. The 24 road projects include the construction of new roads and repairs on old ones.

He added that the six new high school buildings will be constructed in the remotest areas to replace the older buildings, which were hit in the 2001 quake. Thirty-five hamlets will also be electrified.

He added that Madhapur village will have a new playground at a cost of Rs 3.5 crore and the district will see 7 new libraries coming up in the accessible villages. He added that other projects included for irrigation and drinking water include Rs 26 lakh drinking water supply scheme for Nalia.

Thackar further said that the programme envisaged 10 per cent allocation for security related infrastructure facilities for the Amy, para-military and the police.

This year's project for the Army include four bore-well based desalination plants at bets (raised land in the Rann where the Border Outposts (BOPs) are located), repairs and replacement of water pipelines at various BOPs for diesel generator (DG) sets, 10 solar lights, two deep freezers to store anti-snake venom serums and two DSPT for telephone connectivity.

For the Border Security Force (BSF), five RO plants will be set up at its Rann-based BOPs besides one at Savlapir in the creek area.

Other works include the installation of 20 solar lights, two tractor trolleys, 7O PVC tanks, three sanitation blocks, five DG sets, and the repair and replacement of drinking water pipelines.

The projects sanctioned for the police include the construction of check post barriers and new building for staff in far off places in eastern and western Kutch, repeater stations at Mata no Madh, Black Hills, Tapkeshwari and Badargadh, and solar light systems at all Police BOPs.

Heading: No guiding force: PhD remains a pipe dream at GU - Indian Express
Content:
Over 25,000 workers form a joint front to oppose closure of mines after govt's July 2008 decision

Following the closure of the stone mines near Junagadh, which fall within a five km radius of Girnar, some 25,000 odd mine workers and labourers have started an agitation under the banner of the Mine Worker Interest Protection Committee (MWIPC).

They have opposed the grant of sanctuary status to Girnar and called for the resumption of mining activities there. They have started an indefinite relay fast in front of the office of the collector and said that unless their demands are met, or an amicable solution is found to resolve the issue, they will intensify their stir.

In July 2008, the state government had declared the 200 sq km Girnar forest a sanctuary.

Earlier, it was under the reserved forest category. Girnar is the second home of the last surviving group of Asiatic lions after Gir. The forest provides shelter to some two-dozen lions, 50 leopards and hundreds of herbivores.

Haribhai Dabhi, MWIPC leader, said: "The closure of the mines has affected some 25,000 labourers and their family. We are struggling for a daily meal. If mining does not resume soon, a mass exodus cannot be ruled out." He added that the closure of the mines has also affected the education of their children.

Lakhabhai Parmar, a mine workers' leader and the Junagadh Municipal Corporator from ward 17, said if the government fails to resolve the issue, they will resort to a "chakkajam".

He added that the Junagadh Industrial Development Corporation (GIDC) also falls within the five km radius of the sanctuary limit. "All the factories and industrial activities function normally there. When the sanctuary rules do not affect the GIDC, then why are the mines being shut," Parmar said.

Naranbhai Dabhi, a labour leader said: "The mines are located in a safe area outside the sanctuary limit. There is a railway line and the state highway runs parallel to the sanctuary border. The mines are located beyond this highway. No wild animal has been seen roaming around in the mining area."

He said the resumption of mining activities will not damage wildlife or environment. "No heavy machinery is used in these mines. So the question of air, water or sound pollution does not arise," he added.

Heading: Poppy trail: Contraband from Afghanistan seized in Barmer - Indian Express
Content:
Lack of guides, faculties force nearly half of the students willing to pursue a doctorate to drop their plans or move out

Around 50 per cent of students willing to do a doctorate at Gujarat University are unable to register themselves for want of guides and faculties at the different schools of the university.

Due to this reason, students have to either drop their plans of doing PhD here or have to shift to some other university in the state or outside.

The problem is similar in almost all the departments at GU. Incidentally, a report submitted by a committee to check out the scenario of facilities available and its drawbacks at GU for pursuing Ph D, has not resulted in any major step at the university.

In 2007-08, 134 students registered for their PhD under 35 different departments of GU. For the current academic year, 2008-09, the number of students registering for their PhDs is likely to remain the same. The last date of submitting the application is September 15.

H S Oza, Director of School of Commerce at GU told Newsline: "There is a shortage of recognised guides under GU, but you will not find such problems at other universities in the state. Here only three students can do Ph D under a guide, whereas in other universities in the state, a guide can have as many as 6-7 students under him."

He added: "The problem is not only confined to departments that come under the School of Commerce. It is the same with other departments that come under other schools too." Incidentally, in the last two years, none of the students who had applied for PhD at the School of Law have been able to secure guides. At present, the School has only two guides.

According to most of the directors of schools and the head of the departments at GU, there are no proper norms concerning the students who pursue their PhDs at GU.

U C Pande, Director of School of Science at GU said: "As of now, the facilities are limited; even the infrastructure is limited. The main reason behind this is the unavailability of experienced professors who have at least 10 years experience as post-graduate teachers along with a Ph D."

N K Patel, Pro Vice Chancellor (PCV) of GU said: "We have formed a committee to look into this issue and they have proposed giving relaxation to professors to act as guides. We hope to solve the problem of scarcity of guides, slowly, through this."

Patel further said: "The proposed report has already been submitted to GU Vice-Chancellor Parimal Trivedi and we are hopeful that he will look into the matter soon."

Heading: Some skeletons in this mosque’s cupboard? - Indian Express
Content:
Opium smuggled into India despite enhanced vigil on border

At a time when the Indian government is strictly cutting down on cultivation of poppy, more than 20 kg of high quality opium of Afghan origin was recently seized at Nanekapar village, five km from Munabao in Barmer sector. The two accused managed to escape and are yet to be arrested.

Om Prakash, the Deputy Director General of Narcotics Control Bureau (Enforcement), said: "This is the first case of opium of Afghan origin being seized in the country. Considering the large scale of illicit poppy cultivation in Afghanistan, it is indeed an indicator of a very dangerous trend for which all the concerned enforcement agencies, including the NCB, have been alerted."

Over the past few years, availability of opium in India has not been easy because of extra vigil by the enforcement agencies, Prakash said. The probability of it being smuggled into India has therefore increased, he added.

The contraband had been recently seized by the officials of Gujarat Frontier of Border Security Force (BSF) in a joint operation with the Rajasthan Zonal office of the NCB.

The high quality opium is being pushed into India possibly for the drug cartels here, and destinations such as Europe and America.

The seizure has left many BSF officials startled because of the modus operandi used by the accused. In view of increased deployment along the Indo-Pak international border, and fencing work almost nearing completion, cross-border smuggling till now involved what the BSF calls the "conceal and clear method."

"Under this method, smugglers from across the border concealed the consignment at a specific place near the Zero line and fled. Later, smugglers on our side entered through the fence gates in the guise of farmers and picked up the consignment," a BSF officer said.

The seizure of opium of Afghan origin was made following a tip-off. "An ambush was set up with the help of the BSF. The two managed to give us the slip but left the contraband behind. The accused have been identified as local villagers and will be arrested soon," an Intelligence officer at the Rajasthan zonal office of NCB said.

Opium is a narcotic formed from the latex of immature poppy seeds. It contains 10 per cent morphine, which is then chemically processed to produce heroin. There have been many seizures of heroin of Afghan origin, but not of opium.

In India, fields in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh have the license to grow poppy plant. It is then shipped to one of the two huge processing plants at Ghazipur in Uttar Pradesh and Neemuch in Madhya Pradesh, under the strict vigil of the NCB.

Heading: Madhya Pradesh presses for lions’ share, but Gujarat in no mood to oblige - Indian Express
Content:
Suspicious movements inside Limkheda mosque causes concerns for authorities

The Noor Islam Mosque in Limkheda, which was torched during the post-Godhra riots in 2002, is once again in the eye of a storm. This time, it concerns some suspicious movements inside the mosque. Though police investigations have revealed nothing so far, the mosque is still closed to the public on the demand of the local residents.

On September 6, the Limkheda police had picked up the two imams — Maulana Saeed and Maulana Bukhari — for questioning, from Virpur in Kheda district. The two had revealed that they had gone to the Noor Islam Mosque to conduct prayers during Ramzan.

"We picked up the two for questioning after some locals became suspicious about their movement. The locals had also alleged that the two had used stolen motorcycles. This was, however, not found to be true after they furnished us with the necessary details. As of now, we have let them go," said Dahod Superintendent of Police Vipul Agrawal.

Backing the two imams, Farukh Qureshi, the mosque trustee said: "This mosque had been torched in February 2002. We have rebuilt the mosque and two imams had come here for some rituals at the beginning of the holy month of Ramzan."

Though as of now, the trustee and the two imams have returned to Virpur, Qureshi had said before leaving that prayers are yet to be resumed at the mosque as it had been desecrated by miscreants on several occasions. "Before the mosque had been reduced to ashes, people came here to pray from places like Dahod, Godhra, Randhikpur and Vadodara. Many vendors put up their stalls outside its gates. The mosque belongs to everyone; therefore we had decided to make arrangements for people to offer prayers here. However, time and again we have been viewed with suspicion," he added.

Snehal Dharia, a local Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) worker, said there was no mosque in this area.

"It is true that strangers have been seem roaming about the village. They were picked up by the police for questioning. A local person moving around on a scooter with a Vadodara registration number, which belonged to a possible suspect, was also picked up by the police for questioning. But as far as I can recollect, there are no mosques in Limkheda. There is only one madrassa," he added.

District Development Officer Nalin Thakker said he was not aware about any such issue.

Heading: Care for Capital’s destitute, mentally ill: HC asks for solutions - Indian Express
Content:
MP seeks SC intervention for translocation of Gir lions to its Kuno-Palpur sanctuary

Even as the Gujarat government has initiated measures to develop the forest area in and around the world famous Gir Wildflife Sanctuary, Madhya Pradesh has pressed its demand to translocate some of the Gir lions to the 344 km Kuno-Palpur sanctuary in the state.

In response to a PIL, the Supreme Court had recently referred the case involving Madhya Pradesh's demand to the National Board for Wildlife. It had also directed it to submit a detailed report on the issue.

"As directed by the SC, the National Board for Wildlife has just submitted its report to the apex court, recommending the translocation of some lions to our Kuno sanctuary. We are awaiting the court's orders," said P B Gangopadhyay, Madhya Pradesh Principal Chief Conservator of Forest (PCCF) .

He told Newsline over the phone from Bhopal that his department has already taken up a Centre-aided Rs 24 crore Asiatic lion Introduction Project to accommodate some Gir lions, provided Gujarat agrees to transfer them to the Kuno sanctuary. "We have already relocated about 24 villages on its periphery. Besides, the department has also created enough prey-base for the Asiatic lions in case they are shifted here," he said.

Incidentally, the Madhya Pradesh Forest Department has also plans to obtain some pairs of lions from zoos in Hyderabad, Delhi and Bhopal, for breeding in the Kuno sanctuary. Gandgopadhyay added: "We have mooted this proposal, but it will take at least three generations (15-20 years) for zoo-bred lions to be naturalised. We believe it will be easier for us to habitat Gir lions in the sanctuary rather than wait for such a long naturalising period."

But Gujarat has resolved to resist any move to transfer some of the Gir lions to the Kuno-Palpur sanctuary.

Gujarat Forest Minister Mangubhai Patel, said: "If our neighbours pin hope on the apex court to issue orders in their favour, Gujarat will also give a legal fight and ensure that the Asiatic lions as demanded by Madhya Pradesh are not transferred to Kuno-Palpur sanctuary."

He said the conditions in Kuno-Palpur are not congenial for the Gir lions. Besides, the presence of tigers in Kuno is bound to cause frequent clashes between the two apex predators over territories, he added.

Meanwhile, Chief Minister Narendra Modi has said that the Congress-led UPA government at the Centre has been ignoring the lion conservation and habitat development programmes in Gujarat.

Last week, while chairing the Gujarat State Wildlife Advisory Board meeting at Gandhinagar, Modi demanded that the Centre take up conservation of the Asiatic lions on the lines of 'Project Tiger'. He directed senior officials of the state Forest department to draft a comprehensive "Project Lion" plan and submit the same to the Centre.

The CM has also demanded that the Centre allocate funds for the protection and conservation of Asiatic lions, and also for an overall development of the Gir sanctuary and its surrounding forest areas. At the meeting, he asked the Board members to call on Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and make a strong representation for the allocation of funds. Incidentally, Modi had also raised this issue at a recent meeting of the Planning Commission in Delhi.

Pradeep Khanna, Principal Chief Conservator of Forest (Wildlife), Gujarat, said: "Last year, the state government had submitted a detailed project report to the Union Environment and Forest Ministry and sought Rs 61 crore for lion conservation and other developmental activities in and around the Gir Wildlife Sanctuary."

He added: "We have been pursuing this with the Centre on a regular basis, but it has yet to respond to the Rs 61 crore project report."

He added that if the Centre could announce 'Project Tiger' and provide funds of over Rs 200 crore for the protection and conservation of the big cat in as many as 27 tiger reserves across the country, then a "Project Lion" for Gujarat should also be implemented.

The total area of Gir sanctuary is 1,412 sq kms, and it accommodates 359 Asiatic lions.

Heading: In The Assembly - Indian Express
Content:
Bano is a 28-year-old woman rescued early this year from the Chirag Delhi crossing. She has burns on her legs, suffers from depression, is not able to walk and has no clue whether she has a family.

She is the face of the thousands of homeless women in the Capital and features on the cover of a 340-page report produced on Wednesday before a Bench of Delhi High Court, comprising Chief Justice A P Shah and Justice S Muralidhar.

The report, prepared in less than a week, is a joint effort by Sreerupa Mitra Chaudhury, National Adviser, National Legal Services Authority, research scholars and the Centre for the Study of Law and Governance of Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Described as a "substantial beginning" towards investigating the state government's facilities for destitute women and homeless people, the Bench has ordered the Delhi government and the Centre, including the Human Resources Development Ministry, to study the report and come up with "detailed solutions" on the problem by September 17, the next date of hearing.

"The law does not allow a mental patient to be admitted in a hospital without an order from the Magistrate Court. This is a safeguard that is in place to prevent misuse. This, however, also makes it very difficult to arrange for the stay and care of a homeless person, who is also mentally ill, in any hospital," says Chaudhury, who is also the founder and chairperson of Sudinalay Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre.

The report includes a study undertaken by the Institute of Human Behaviour and Allied Sciences (IHBAS, commonly known as the Shahdara Mental Hospital) on the status of mental health care in Delhi. The study shows a 34 per cent deficit in the availability of mental health professionals. That is, for every 50,000 people in the Capital, there is only one psychiatrist available.

Similarly, there is only one trained psychiatric nurse for a populace of 25,000. The institute figures show a deficit of 58 per cent in the strength of nurses.

The IHBAS study also reveals that there are only 0.5 beds available for every 10,000 people of the population.

Statistics on the break-up of service loads between the government and the private sector in primary /general health care service across Delhi shows that the government undertakes 8.52 per cent of the load while private institutions account for 60.2 per cent of the patient intake.

"The state's infrastructure for mental health care can hardly contain the volume of patients, especially migrants who are mentally ill and homeless. There is a need to devise a mechanism for a longer duration of stay for these patients, as chances are minimum that they will ever be able to identify their family or roots," says Chaudhury.

Some of the proposals put forth in the report include sensitisation for "thana" level police officers about mental health laws, compulsory mental health service at all night shelters, rescue homes and rehab centres with anti-depression clinics, and authorisation of civil society bodies to initiate treatment for the homeless in need of help.

* Only one trained psychiatric nurse for a populace of 25,000. The institute figures show a deficit of 58 per cent in the strength of nurses

Heading: Road widening: Clogged traffic on NH-24 may take long to clear - Indian Express
Content:
* Following protests by farmers demanding compensation for land acquired by the government in six villages and the BJP Opposition creating a furor in the Assembly, Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit said she will hold a meeting on September 19 to discuss the issue. While BJP MLAs staged a walk out in protest of the police action taken against the farmers on Wednesday and Thursday, Dikshit said the government "will do whatever legally possible to compensate the farmers."

* On the second day of the Assembly session the Opposition left the government sweating on the issue of water shortage. The Chief Minister agreed that there is a problem of water shortage in the Capital and the distribution of water is faulty. Sheila Dikshit told the Assembly that it would take at least five to six months to reach a solution.

* Delhi government on Thursday said permission has been granted for allotment of flats in eight cooperative housing societies while the process is on for ten others in the national capital. Development Minister Rajkumar Chauhan said this in reply to allegations raised by the BJP leaders that the allotment process has been delayed. The High Court had recently told the registrar of cooperative societies to start the allotment process for 57 societies.

* The Delhi government will review its decision on the regularization policy for nearly 20 colonies close to Sainik Farms. Sainik Farms and other two colonies, Anant Ram Diary and Mehandru Enclave have not be included in the issuance of provisional regularisation certificate. Development Minister Rajkumar Chauhan said area District Commissioner has been told to carry out a study to provide further details.

* The special committee on Environment in its second report tabled in the Legislative Assembly on Thursday suggested that all encroachments on the Yamuna riverbed should be removed. The committee however stated that the riverbed should be developed as a tourist and religious place. 

 * The Public Accounts Committee of the Delhi Legislative Assembly has recommended the framing of guidelines and laws to control the grant of exemptions on tickets issued for events like cricket matches organised by agencies like the Delhi District Cricket Association (DDCA).

Heading: Power crisis in Capital: Govt passes the buck - Indian Express
Content:
It's A tough ride on National Highway 24, thanks to the road widening project undertaken on the stretch between Pandav Nagar and Ghazipur drain.

Delayed several times, the project is likely to take longer now. An underpass, meant to be constructed on the congested Pandav Nagar crossing, is likely to take a few more months to be completed.

The Public Works Department, however, assures that the stretch will be widened and thrown open for the public by next month. The project to double the highway's carriage capacity from the current four lanes to eight lanes was announced more than two years ago and was scheduled to begin by August 10, 2006. The plan was to widen the stretch from Noida More to Khichripur, and build an underpass at the congested Pandav Nagar crossing. The deadline set by the PWD earlier this year was July.

According to PWD engineer-in-chief N M D Jain, the eight lane stretch of about 2 km will be thrown open once the services are shifted from the site. "The BSES is in the process of shifting a pillion. Once they are done with it, we should take about a month," he said. The underpass near Pandav Nagar will have to wait though, he said. "We cannot dig up every stretch and expect motorists to manage. The underpass will be taken up later," he said.

Beside its arterial importance for east-west-bound traffic in the trans-Yamuna area, NH-24 will also have to cope with increased traffic flow during 2010 Commonwealth Games. The highway leads to several major Games venues in East Delhi. The idea of doubling the number of lanes was to cater to this projected traffic growth.

Though the works were expected to be completed by November 2007, the project had run into trouble as the slums around the area had to be relocated by the Delhi Development Authority. This delayed work by about eight months, officials claimed.

Even as the settlements were finally removed by April 2007, the steel and bitumen cost had gone up, which led to the process of getting a revised sanction from the Union Ministry of Surface Transport. The agency has so far spent about Rs 11.68 crore on the project while the sanctioned cost is about Rs 17 crore.

Heading: War Zone - Indian Express
Content:
With the maximum power demand peaking at 3,516 MW, the Capital continued to reel under acute power shortage seen in the last one month.

In a statement issued by Delhi Transco earlier this week, the government acknowledged the widening gap between power demand and supply, but chose to pass the buck onto other states. "Though distribution companies in Delhi had made bilateral arrangements with various states such as Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka among others, due to shortage in these states, power has not been received. States which are not honouring their agreements are Uttarakhand — 100 MW, Karnataka —180 MW and Madhya Pradesh —100 MW," Transco said in the statement.

With Delhi's power generation capacity oscillating between 1,200 and 1,400 MW, as against a demand of 3,800 MW, the city as usual is dependent on power purchase agreements with other states to meet its requirements. Many in the power department feel this dependence on outside sources has caused the current shortage, "While we will always source power through other states, Delhi will certainly be more self-sufficient when the plants at Bawana and Bamnauli begin operations," a senior power department official said. On Thursday too, power shortage led to loadshedding that effected areas like Greater Kailash in South Delhi, Dwarka and parts of East Delhi.

The current power crisis coming just two months before the Assembly polls, sources reveal that Power Minister A K Walia has been issuing instructions to discoms to ensure minimal load-shedding. Walia had earlier met the Union Power Secretary Anil Razdan about the Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) not honouring its agreement. "A Power Purchase Agreement was signed with DVC in the year 2007-08 for supply of 400 MW but due to delay in commissioning of the units, no power is being received," Transco added.

Transco officials have also admitted that the dismal levels of power generation in the Capital have fallen further due to unavailability of gas. "Due to this, power generation in Delhi has been reduced by about 60 to 70 MW," a Transco official said.

The power shortage is also being blamed on the low levels of hydro-electricity generation. "There is an acute water shortage in our rivers, which is directly effecting hydroelectricity generation all over the country, particularly at the Tehri Dam and Nathpa Jhakri plants, which generate power for Delhi," a power department official said.

The issue of overdrawing from the Northern Grid has also been discussed, with rising concerns from many quarters that this could prove dangerous for the grid,

Over the last two weeks Delhi has been habitually over drawing anywhere between 100 and 800 MW. "Loadshedding has thus become unavoidable to avoid a Grid collapse, which would jeopardise the power system of Northern, Western and the Northeast states," Transco had said in its statement.

Heading: Chai Time - Indian Express
Content:
Conflict becomes the focal point of this year's Open Frame Film Festival

Even as an uneasy disquiet looms over the Kashmir valley and people in Israel and Palestine grapple with the fallouts of their ongoing war, when the curtains go up at Public Service Broadcasting Trust's annual Open Frame Film Festival 2008 today, 55 filmmakers will come together with their own visions and interpretations of the aftermath of strife and unrest.

"Our current sociopolitical scenario is marked by conflict. Even in the domain of the personal, there's crisis at home. We thought it would be interesting to see multiple views on the issue," said Rajiv Mehrotra, managing trustee of PSBT.

The festival at the India Habitat Centre will feature over 55 national and international documentary films that chronicle conflict and its various faces. Umesh Aggarwal, who will showcase his hour-long documentary called Divided Colours of a Nation, for instance, has dealt with the issue of reservation. "It took me 15 months to finish it because incidents like the Gujjar riots kept happening throughout and I needed to update my work," he says. He recalls his meetings with a cabinet secretary from Andhra Pradesh, who insists on having reservation, and another schedule caste entrepreneur, a BITS Pilani, IIM Ahmedabad alumnus, who wants it to be a facility only for the needy. "How do you resolve an issue like this particularly when people are so ill-informed about the constitutional provisions," he wonders.

Likewise, for Polish filmmaker and Indophile Malgorzata Skiba, a visit to Leh-Ladakh in 2003, unearthed a Pandora's Box. "The Buddhist nuns there were subjected to a life of servitude. They were ill treated and denied basic rights. It was an archaic and disturbing practice," recalls Skiba. Her film, Autumn in the Himalayas, to be screened on September 14, tells the story of these women and their effort to build nunneries and better their lot. Screened at the 48th Krakow Film Festival in Poland and the Visual Arts Festival in Rhodes, Greece, the film is now set for its India premiere. There will be other Indian and South Asian premieres as well, including Meira Asher's Women See Lot of Things (Netherlands), the story of three ex-war combatants who fought in the decade-long civil wars in Sierra Leone and Liberia, and Jenny Mackenzie's Kick Like a Girl (USA).

Kashmir, of course, has a special place too, with films, installations and forum discussions. An installation themed around terror will be displayed by Kashmiri artist Malik Sajad while a 45-minute film called Crossing the Lines: Kashmir, Pakistan and India, a story of people at war over borders and boundaries, by Pakistani filmmakers Pervez Hoodboy and Zian Mian will be screened on September 15.

"Increasingly, what we want is to move beyond a passive viewing of filmmaking into more engaging discussions," says Mehrotra, adding that the intensive filmmaking workshops that have been included in this year's festival is a move towards that direction.

The festival ends on September 20

Heading: Sushil & Gopal Ansal surrender, sent to jail - Indian Express
Content:
I am happy. They will be behind bars till appeal is decided: Neelam Krishnamurthy

A Delhi court on Thursday sent Sushil and Gopal Ansal to jail after they surrendered before Additional Sessions Judge I K Kochhar a little after 3 pm.

This will be the first time Gopal Ansal is in jail, though elder brother Sushil had spent 40 days in the middle of 1997 after his arrest from Mumbai.

The brothers surrendered because the Supreme Court cancelled their bail on Wednesday, angry that they were still out after conviction, while a trial court was hearing charges against them on the alleged destruction of evidence in the Uphaar fire tragedy, that had claimed 59 lives in June 1997. The apex court's justices B N Agrawal and G S Singhvi had said: "Tampering with judicial records is a crime worse than murder or dacoity."

The brothers had been convicted under Section 304 A — causing death by rash and negligent acts — and sentenced to two years' imprisonment in November 20, 2007. They secured bail in January this year, and had also remained out on bail during the 11-year-long trial.

Theatre managers Ajit Chowdhary and Nirmal Chopra, sentenced by the trial court for seven years, also surrendered before Judge Kochhar on Thursday. The highest court had cancelled their bail on Wednesday.

The brothers entered Judge Kochhar's courtroom at 3.15 pm. The judge called their names, and those of the managers, and after the procedural formalities were over, the four were taken into custody by the Central Bureau of Investigation. The brothers also moved several applications seeking access to medicines, spectacles and wrist watches inside jail. This was opposed by CBI counsel Y K Saxena, but the judge said, "I am ordering the jail superintendent to look up these provisions in the jail manual."

Judge Kochhar, however, acceded to the brothers' request to order media photographers out of the courtroom. The judge also asked journalists to move to the back of the room, observing sharply: "This is not a drama." To avoid facing the camera, the brothers were taken to lock-up through a different route.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday was hearing a petition filed by the Association of Victims of the Uphaar Tragedy (AVUT), which had challenged the bail granted to the Ansal brothers and the other two. The court had harshly pointed out that tampering with records to influence the outcome of a case was "very serious and grave". It said the conduct of the real estate barons did not deserve bail once they had been sentenced.

The judges had wanted them to be arrested immediately on Wednesday, but the brothers' counsels asked for a day for them to surrender. The apex court had also asked the High Court to ensure that the other hearings pending against the brothers — on the host of applications filed by relatives of victims — be taken up on a day-to-day basis. Relatives have sought punishment higher than two years for the Ansals.

The court's response had come as part of a series of proactive observations, whereby the CBI was earlier rapped for its sluggishness and a bailable warrant was also issued against the brothers last month, asking why their bail should not be cancelled.

On Thursday, once the brothers had been led away, the most contented face was that of Neelam Krishnamurthy, who had lost both her son and daughter in the fire. She has been the face of the struggle against the Ansals. Krishnamurthy said, "I was not satisfied when they roamed freely after the conviction. Now I am happy. They will remain behind bars till the appeal is decided."

The judge also asked journalists to move to the back of the room, observing sharply: "This is not a drama." To avoid facing the camera, the brothers were taken to lock-up through a different route.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday was hearing a petition filed by the Association of Victims of the Uphaar Tragedy (AVUT), which had challenged the bail granted to the Ansal brothers and the other two. The court had harshly pointed out that tampering with records to influence the outcome of a case was "very serious and grave". It said the conduct of the real estate barons did not deserve bail once they had been sentenced.

The judges had wanted them to be arrested immediately on Wednesday, but the brothers' counsels asked for a day for them to surrender.
