The apex court had also asked the High Court to ensure that the other hearings pending against the brothers — on the host of applications filed by relatives of victims — be taken up on a day-to-day basis. Relatives have sought punishment higher than two years for the Ansals.

The court's response had come as part of a series of proactive observations, whereby the CBI was earlier rapped for its sluggishness and a bailable warrant was also issued against the brothers last month, asking why their bail should not be cancelled.

On Thursday, once the brothers had been led away, the most contented face was that of Neelam Krishnamurthy, who had lost both her son and daughter in the fire. She has been the face of the struggle against the Ansals. Krishnamurthy said, "I was not satisfied when they roamed freely after the conviction. Now I am happy. They will remain behind bars till the appeal is decided."

Heading: Hit-and-run on BRT corridor, man critical - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court's stand on the conduct of the Ansal brothers during the Uphaar trial means serious trouble for the two, their counsel Ramesh Gupta said on Thursday.

Both brothers were "shocked", sources said when the apex court cancelled their bail on Wednesday. While noting they were fighting charges of tampering with evidence, the court had observed that the conduct of the accused was crucial to decide whether they deserved bail, even though their offence might have been bailable.

Ramesh Gupta told Newsline: "The Supreme Court's decision is too stern. At the moment, I don't see any possibility of bail. When the highest court takes a stand, one cannot expect a lower court to differ."

CBI counsel Y K Saxena, who has represented the state in this legal fight, agreed with the defence counsel.

He said: "The apex court's decision is final. Ansals should now forget about bail till the appeal is decided by the High Court, which has also been directed to expedite the matter." Well-known criminal lawyer R K Naseem said only the Supreme Court can now decide on their bail. He said: "The law is clear. The apex court has cancelled their bail. Only the highest court can now hear any further applications for bail."

However, Ramesh Gupta said if there was "material change" in the circumstances, they could pursue relief on that ground.

Heading: Aspiring film-makers had quit jobs to follow their dreams - Indian Express
Content:
Driver, passenger abandon car after ramming bike

Delhi roads saw yet another hit-and-run case in the early hours of Thursday. A car rammed a motorbike at the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) corridor near Moolchand flyover, injuring two young men, one of whom is in a serious condition.

The driver of the car, allegedly one Utsav Bhasin— a student of MBA in IILM — and his sister Sakshi — a student of Delhi Public School in RK Puram — escaped from the spot within minutes of the accident and are on the run, said a police officer.

The BMW car (registration number HR 26 AK 0020) is registered in the name of M/S Golden Rolls Pvt Ltd, Bahalgarh, Sultanpur, Sonepat. The owner of the car is M K Bhasin, who runs a V-Belt factory in Sonepat.

The incident occurred outside the Vadhera Art Gallery. It is suspected that the car was travelling at a speed of over 100 kilometres per hour. "The impact was such that the motorcycle was dragged for nearly 10 feet after Anuj Chauhan and Mrigank Srivastava, both in their twenties, fell off," an officer said.

The PCR van officers were informed about the accident around 2.30 am. The victims were taken to the AIIMS Trauma Centre. "Mrigank managed to escape with fractures. But the condition of Anuj is critical," the officer said. Chauhan's brother Dr Rahul Chauhan said, "He has been kept on life support. We are praying for a miracle." The youths stayed in a rented room in South Extension. While Chauhan is pursuing an animation course from MAAC Academy, Srivastava makes documentaries for news channels. They were on their way home after watching a movie at PVR Saket when the incident occurred. Madhu Tyagi, the lawyer for the victims who was also present in the hospital, said, "the police have seized the car." On basis of Mrigank's statement, an FIR has been registered. "We have sent four teams to Sonepat to trace the accused," the investigating officer said.

Accused got away in second car
The air bags which popped up as soon as the BMW car hit the motorcycle, had blinded the driver, due to which he couldn't escape immediately, said a police officer. "He couldn't see anything and went on to hit a pole. The car got stuck and he had to get out and abandon it to escape," he added. The car was found 300 meters ahead of the spot of collision. Police sources added that there was another car carrying Utsav's friends following the BMW, which the two used to make their getaway.

Heading: Insurance cover for CNG cab drivers - Indian Express
Content:
Returning from a late night movie at PVR Saket at 2:30 am, Mrigank Srivastava and Anuj Chauhan were heading for the apartment they had hired in South Extension when the BMW hit them.

Anuj's friend Eti Bajpai, an editor with a television channel, and another friend Rohit Sorout, had watched the movie with them. They had reached home when the accident took place. They had taken an auto while Mrigank and Anuj were riding back.

Talking about the wait, Eti said: "We called on their phones till 4 am. Finally a policeman picked up. When we reached the hospital, Mrigank was not there."

While the policemen rushed Anuj to the hospital, Mrigank was lying on the spot for at least an hour and fifteen minutes. "He was brought in when we reached the hospital," Rohit said. Mrigank was a senior editor with Space Television in Noida and had recently quit his job. Anuj, too, had quit as reporter with the S1 News channel a few months ago. Both are budding filmmakers and had given up the jobs to try their luck in the field. Mrigank makes documentaries for various television channels while Anuj has been studying animation at the Maya Institute of Advanced Cinematics.

Recalling the incident, Mrigank, who was driving, said: "Anuj fell off and I was dragged along till I lost conscience." He sustained ankle fracture and injuries on the head. Admitted at the AIIMS Trauma Centre, the doctors were performing surgeries on him till late night. Anuj is admitted in the ICU. "It is a difficult case, his chances of survival are almost nil," a doctor said. Anuj's father Dr Rajendra Prasad Chauhan runs a clinic in Vijaynagar in Ghaziabad. "We want our son to be safe, the culprits should be nabbed," he told Newsline.

477 and rising
This year, 477 hit-and-run cases have taken place so far, in which 256 people lost their lives. The number of injured is 215. The number of fatal accidents is 1,297 this year. The average number of accidents on Delhi roads is around 9,000 per year.

Last year, 1,428 persons had died in accidents till September.

Most of the accidents, police say, take place during the night when rash driving is rampant owing to the presence of fewer traffic cops.

Heading: At Yamuna, a plan to tap rainwater, restore its ecosystem - Indian Express
Content:
Drivers of CNG-powered taxis and autorickshaws in the Capital will soon be given a personal accident insurance cover of Rs 1.5 lakh. About 2 lakh drivers will be benefiting from the scheme — 'Mahasuraksha Yojna'.

The scheme is in the pattern of the one inaugurated in Mumbai in 2006 by Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh. It was initiated by the Mahanagar Gas Limited to encourage the use of CNG in the city.

In Delhi, Congress President Sonia Gandhi will be launching the scheme this month, said sources.

The initiative comes from the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, the Delhi government and Indraprastha Gas Limited (IGL), the sole provider of Compressed Natural Gas in Delhi.

The DTC bus drivers, however, have not been included in the scheme taken up by IGL as part of its Corporate Social Responsibilty.

As opposed to Mumbai, which has only 55,000 taxis running on CNG, about 54,500 autorickshaws, 8,700 taxis and 30,500 light goods vehicles plying in the Capital use CNG. Besides, there are 13,000 minibuses and private buses that use CNG.

After its introduction in the Capital, the scheme will be extended to the National Capital Region areas like Faridabad, Gurgaon, Sonepat, Panipat and Gautam Budh Nagar.

Petroleum and Natural Gas minister Murli Deora had announced the scheme in the Capital in July while urging the Delhi government to open more CNG filling stations.

It was to be formally launched in August, but was delayed due as the Congress president was unavailable, sources said.

THE SCHEME
* Insurance cover of Rs 1.5 lakh to the family in case of death and graded compensation for partial or total responsibility
* Reimbursement of upto Rs 10,000 for medical expenditure in case of fracture or injury
* Rs 25,000 as children's education allowance for one school or college-going student

WHO IS ELIGIBLE:
A driver with a valid driving license and permission to drive a CNG public transport vehicle

PAPERWORK
* The beneficiaries have to submit a copy of the FIR copy and in case of death, a death certificate.
* Necessary documents regarding permits and permissions.

CNG FACTS
* The NCR has around 2,50,000 CNG vehicles
*n Nearly 400 cars convert to CNG every month
* There are 163 CNG stations in the Capital Delhi government is finalising land for 50 more.
* Incorporated in 1998 as a joint venture of GAIL (India) Ltd and BPCL along with the Delhi government, the IGL is the only CNG distributer in the city

Heading: Burning midnight oil in capital's hospitals - Indian Express
Content:
A group of scientists from Delhi University, who created the Yamuna Biodiversity Park at Wazirabad, have now suggested and are working on an additional waterbody and wetland which will trap the Yamuna's monsoon water to prevent flooding in nearby areas.

The Yamuna Biodiversity Park — thought up by the university's Centre for Environmental Management of Degraded Ecosystems (CEMDE) — has been developed over 156 acres. Owned by the Delhi Development Authority, this is a manmade waterbody with dry areas where scientists have also tried to simulate the Yamuna's original ecosystem. However, the area is not linked to the river and, therefore, cannot share its burden of excess water.

Following the flood this year, the scientists are debating the merits of another waterbody of about 200 acres which will be near the river's banks and on the Yamuna flood plain. Depressions will be made in the area to catch flooding water. This waterbody will also be in Wazirabad and will be covered in the biodiversity park's extension plans.

Professor Emeritus of CEMDE, C R Babu, said: "Most of the 300 acres earmarked in the expansion will form this comprehensive waterbody. It will not only arrest flood water but will also improve the sub-soil aquifer or underground reservoir that caters to North Delhi. Given Delhi's growing water needs, this move was much required."

Babu explained there were two kinds of aquifers in Delhi — the sub-soil at North Delhi where the water lurks closer to the surface, and the deeper version in South Delhi, nearly 600 feet underground.

The flood water will also be used for another purpose, experts said. In-charge of the park Faiyaz Khudsar said: "These waterbodies will be a nursery for the Yamuna. We shall create vegetation here — aquatic plants and organisms like molluscs. When the Yamuna floods this area, we can hope the water, while receding, will suck back native plants, crustations and organisms into the river. This will enrich its ecosystem." He added an ambience will also be created to lure back storks and pelicans, which bred in the Capital once but have now vanished.

This year's flood has also made scientists reconsider the setting up of a riverine tree system near the waterbodies. Khudsar said, "We have dropped that idea since trees cannot remain submerged for a long period of time if the river is to swell so much again. We shall create a grassland instead."

Newsline had earlier reported that Delhi has no mechanism in place to utilise flood water. With barely any water-trapping system, a slight rise of 3.44 metres is enough to submerge villages near the river. Each year, during the monsoon, almost 280 million cubic metres of water flows by Delhi unutilised.

Heading: IAF officer’s wife found murdered in Lado Sarai - Indian Express
Content:
Can our hospitals do without interns at night? Is it a learning experience? Newsline takes a look

When Safdarjang Hospital suddenly declared that interns would not be allowed to work night shifts, eyebrows were raised.

As Newsline reported on August 19, a hospital circular said this was done was humanitarian grounds — to save the interns from working long hours. The hospital, instead, was hiring more resident doctors.

The decision drew widespread criticism — for owing to a skeletal staff at nights, the shift offers the most learning opportunities to interns. While the Safdarjung authorities defended their decision, Newsline went to two other hospitals — GTB and LNJP — to observe the training patterns and see how the city's doctors learn their skills.

Guru Tegh Bahadur Hospital
(Affiliated college: University College of Medical Sciences)
The interns report for duty at 9 am. Every alternative day brings a demanding 26-hour shift — from 9 am to noon the next day. And every intern gets three such shifts in a week.

In the Department of Surgery, the morning rounds on Sunday took almost an hour. Afterwards, the interns spent nearly six hours dressing the wounds of patients. Others collected blood and urine samples, filled investigative forms and fetched reports.

During the afternoon, a 60-year-old patient died due to hypotension. Only an intern was on duty at the time.

While such cases are not unusual, night is still the crunch time. "Once evening sets in, we wait around and keep hoping the shift goes by uneventfully," said Istha, one of the interns.

The morning after, they have to update the postgrads about the patients' condition and are relieved by noon the next day, she added.

But while the rounds were going on in the surgery ward, the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology spread over three floors with close to 150 patients — was completely unmanned. The nearest doctors were stationed in the Central Labour Room (CLR). "An intern and a senior resident doctor are in the CLR. If there is an emergency we call for them," said a nurse outside the gynaecology ward.

The GTB Hospital has 100 interns — who shoulder the responsibility of PG students and senior resident doctors.

While students maintain that senior consultants, residents and post-graduate students leave the wards by 4 pm, Medical Superintendent Dr PC Dikshit denied the allegation.

"The interns are never left without guidance. We prepare rosters and teach interns under proper supervision. I am in constant contact with the faculty members and no one has brought up this matter," said Dr Dikshit, insisting that the hospital was following all guidelines provided by Medical Council of India for medical education.

Lok Nayak Jai Prakash Hospital
(Affiliated college: Maulana Azad Medical College)
The stark difference between interns in GTB and LNJP is apparent when you venture into the Nescafe canteen in the premises.

At 3 am, students are sitting around, sipping coffee, struggling to stay awake.

Reason: There is hardly any work.

Unlike GTB hospital, the "night shift" does not mean being marooned with a ward full of patients and no superviser — rather, it involves doubling up as Nursing Orderlies, fetching test reports and X-rays.

"We usually run errands and get very little exposure to real patient care," said Mayank Poddar, one of the interns.

"Blood sampling and BP recording is part of the learning process, but we hardly get to learn more. If anyone wants to set up private practice after completing MBBS, he would have no knowledge of patient care. All that we know is theoretical," said Abhishek Bansal, who is in the ninth month of his internship.

After reporting to duty at 8 am, finishing the morning rounds in the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Bansal conducted blood pressure charting for 16 patients, fetched blood sample reports of six patients and waited out the rest of the shift.

The silver lining is the OPD duty twice a week, where they do get some exposure, he added. "But in the wards, little is explained to us. Sometimes duty stretches for 36 hours but at the end of it, we learn very little," added Poddar.

To make matters worse, there is no timetable. "The attendance marking is ad-hoc and we usually follow instructions from first year post-graduate students who man the wards," Poddar said.

Frustrated by the teaching pattern, the interns — 180 of them — have approached the health department for intervention.

Dr Arun Agarwal, Dean, MAMC said: "Students have to do all kinds of work during internship. In your house you do all types of work and this is the same. Running errands for senior doctors is not the norm but a few students have complained about it," he added.

Another sore point is the stipend. Students at MAMC get Rs 5,700 per month and had recently approached Delhi government's Health Department asking for a raise. "The Central government has to decide these things and they cannot happen overnight," said Dr Agarwal.

THE SCHEDULE
Rural posting: 3 months
Medicine dept: 2 months
Surgery, including Orthopaedics dept: 2 months
Obstetrics and Gynaecology dept: 2 months
Welfare Planning: 15 days
Paediatrics dept: 15 days
Ophthalmology dept: 15 days
Otorhinolaryngology dept: 15 days
Casualty: 1 month

Heading: Daylight robbery: Rs 4 lakh looted from Canara Bank branch in Noida - Indian Express
Content:
Victim stabbed, laptop missing; 3-yr-old son was asleep in room

A 32-year-old woman was found stabbed to death at her flat in Lado Sarai village in South Delhi on Thursday morning.

Police said her laptop is missing, but nothing else has been touched. Her three-year-old mentally challenged son was found sleeping in the same room. A kitchen knife, suspected to be the murder weapon, has been seized.

According to police officers, the victim, Rekha Kuntia was the wife of Pranay Kuntia, a sergeant in the Indian Air Force and is posted at Tughlakabad.

On Thursday, Pranay had left home at 7.30 am.

"Their domestic help, Aman (18), claims he left home 20 minutes after Pranay and went to buy vegetables and general grocery items. He said when he returned around 10 am, he found the main door open," said a police officer.

Acording to Aman, Rekha had locked the door when he left. "When he entered the house, Aman found Rekha lying in a pool of blood in the bedroom. He rushed out and called a friend, who alerted the police at 10.30 am," the officer said.

"There are two stab wounds on the victim's body — one on the neck and another on the shoulder," said DCP, South, H G S Dhaliwal. It is possible that the murderer was an acquaintance as there is no sign of forced entry, he added.

A case of murder has been registered in the Malviya Nagar police station, Dhaliwal added. Aman has been working for the Kuntias for the past eight years, police said. They had purchased the flat (house number 175, Lado Sarai) six years ago, when Pranay was transferred to Tughlakabad.

Rekha had an export business. The missing laptop may have had important files relating to her business, police suspect.

Rekha's neighbour Prashant Kumar said: "They kept to themselves and did not interact much. The lady had some business and parcels often came to her house. Their servant also stayed home most of the time with the child."

Three people, meanwhile, one of them a property dealer, were detained late on Thursday night for interrogation.

Heading: Bhasin out of the country, says guard at his house - Indian Express
Content:
In broad daylight, two motorcycle-borne assailants looted Rs 4.9 lakh from a Canara Bank branch located in Sector 63, Noida, on Thursday. The incident happened around 3.05 pm when the bank employees were counting money that was to be loaded into the bank's ATM.

According to bank manager S K Aggarwal, two masked men entered the bank and one of them threatened the cashier, who was counting money, with a pistol. "The other one went inside the bank and kept the bank employees at gunpoint," said Aggarwal.

The assailants asked the cashier to fill the money in the polythene bag they brought along. "The men took away Rs 4.9 lakh from the bank," said Aggarwal. The robbers, after taking the money, locked up the bank employees. "It took them just three to five minutes to rob the bank," said a police officer.

The police, however, were called 10 minutes after the incident. Fingerprints, meanwhile, have been taken and district borders sealed.

"All bikers are being thoroughly checked. The looters will be nabbed soon," said SP (City), Ashok Tripathi. Ghaziabad and police of nearby districts have also been alerted.

Heading: Call centre employee murder: Cops detain friends - Indian Express
Content:
MK Bhasin, the owner of the BMW (HR 26-AK-0020) that rammed a motorcycle at the BRT corridor, lives in West Punjabi Bagh with his children Utsav and Sakshi and father SR Bhasin.

Newsline visited the house to find Bhasin senior alone at home, bedridden. He said he was not aware of the incident and last saw Utsav at home "on Wednesday evening".

MK Bhasin, the owner of a V-belt factory in Sonepat, had flown to China a few days ago.

Rakesh Kumar, the security guard at his home, said: "Utsav and Sakshi were at home yesterday afternoon, but I don't know when they left. My duty ends at 8 pm."

Bhasin, he said, had been out of the country for the past two days.

The BMW involved in the incident is kept in the gallery of the house. Bhasin owns two other cars.

His wife had expired a few years ago.

Police sources, meanwhile, said teams have been sent to Sonepat to nab the accused, but no arrests were made till late evening.

Police sources have added that till now they have come in contact with the account manager of Bhasin's company, Satish Arora, a resident of Sonepat.

He is being interrogated regarding the whereabouts of Utsav and Sakshi.

Deputy Commissioner of Police (South District), HGS Dhaliwal said: "No one has been arrested yet, however, we hope that the accused will be caught later tonight."

Regarding drinking and driving, Dhaliwal said, "We are not sure whether the driver was drunk. It is a hit-and-a-run case and we are investigating it further."

Police sources added that they also suspect that Utsav does not have a valid license. His father had hired three drivers but on Thursday, he was reportedly driving the car, the police said.

Heading: Once upon a time - Indian Express
Content:
A day after a 25-year-old call centre employee was found murdered at her PG accommodation in Gautam Nagar in South Delhi, her parents waited endlessly outside the AIIMS mortuary for the doctors to conduct a postmortem.

"She was to get engaged next month. We were considering fixing her marriage with an engineer from Noida," her mother Prem Lata Saxena said.

Police have not found any clues in the case and have detained Shalini's close friends. Though no formal arrests have been made yet, police said three people have been detained on the basis of details of Shalini's last phone calls.

A visit to her paying guest accommodation revealed that the rules were relaxed and there was no fixed timings for the girls to return. "It is more like a flat than a PG. Anybody can go in at any time they want. The deceased had a night shift and she mostly stayed indoors otherwise," said a resident.

When Newsline contacted the paying guest accommodation owner at her mobile, one Mrs Sharma, she disconnected the phone.

Meanwhile, Shalini's uncle, identified as Colonel Saxena, alleged she had been raped before being murdered. The police officers, however, denied there was any kind of sexual assault. "There were some marks on the victim's thighs, leading us to believe she had been raped. It was later found that the marks were not recent. As of now, there is no basis of sexual assault. Rape can only be confirmed after the postmortem report," a senior police officer said.

Shalini Saxena was found strangled with her own mobile phone charger's wire on her bed on Thursday afternoon. She was found in a semi-clad state and the entry to the room was friendly, police had said.

Heading: FACE TO FACE with Anjorie Alagh - Indian Express
Content:
Will a new superhero rise in Bollywood with the release of Drona on October 2?ALAKA SAHANI

When dreaming means creating an action-fantasy on celluloid, "letting go" of it can be very difficult. This is what Goldie Behl has been experiencing of late. Drona, written and directed by him, is slated for October 2 release. But Behl still can't check himself from giving those finishing touches. "These are just little things here and there. The film is ready, otherwise. I have to let go of it at some point," he says.

Behl's face, however, defies any anxiety over the release, rather he seems pretty relieved. Maybe Raj Thackeray's decision on Thursday to withdraw his agitation against the Bachchan family has something to do with it. "I just watched Thackeray's announcement on television. It's over," he says. With the film starring Abhishek and mother Jaya Bachchan, he had reasons to worry over the MNS protests.

The concerns were not purely professional. The director's relationship with Bollywood's newest superhero, Abhishek Bachchan, goes back to their childhood days. "Abhishek is like my younger brother. I would like to cast him in all my movies," says Behl. He is repeating the actor as the lead in Drona, along with Priyanka Chopra, after his directorial debut Bas Itna Sa Khwab Hai (2001).

The film, Behl promises, has a once-upon-a-time feel to it. To ensure that Tom Delmar (of Troy fame) was roped in to choreograph the action sequences, London-based sword master Richard Ryan to train the lead actors and 250 artists were engaged for visual effects.

The storyline follows the simple philosophy that everybody is born with a purpose. In the case of Abhishek's character, it is to carry forward the legacy of drona (the protectors of society). This realisation helps turn this boy-next-door character into a superhero and pits him against the larger-than-life evil magician (Kay Kay Menon). "The film will be a blend of the worlds of Amar Chitra Katha and Sin City," Behl says.

Achieving this meant pumping in crores. Though the budget is reported to have touched Rs 60 crore, Behl refuses to confirm. "Sunil Lulla (Producer of Eros) can answer this. We have gone by the demand of the script." Filming Drona has taken him to Prague, Kanamachi, Bikaner and Namibia in the last two years. "We started shooting in December 2006 in Prague. I wanted to capture its winter," he says. The film, which is having a simultaneous overseas release, was also shot in Mumbai, where five grand sets were created.

By deciding to make films, Goldie took over his family business. But it happened under grim circumstances when his father, producer Ramesh Behl, died. The responsibility of completing Indrajeet fell on him. He later assisted Mahesh Bhatt for Angaarey, on whose sets he met his wife Sonali Bendre. The association with Bhatt has been rewarding in other ways also; from him Behl picked up quite a few tricks of filmmaking. Mukul Anand and JP Dutta too have helped in shaping his understanding of cinema.

But has this young director ever thought of facing the camera? "I would be lying if

I say no. But then, acting is a very specialised art. I'm more comfortable behind the camera," says Behl. And it's the sequel of Drona that might send him back to his favourite job soon.

Heading: Role call - Indian Express
Content:
What's on your I Pod?
I have songs of Bob Marley, John Mayer, Ronan Keating, U2, Oasis, REM and Sting. I also have lots of Bollywood songs and ghazals.

What's your DVD pick?
The Godfather.

Your most favourite romantic scene in a movie?
My favourite romantic scene is from Notting Hill, starring Hugh Grant and Julia Roberts. On their first date, they walk in a park at night. The background music starts playing and they sit on the bench together. And the bench says, "For June, who loved this garden, from Joseph who always sat beside her". They kiss and Julia Roberts says, "Some people do spend their whole lives together."

Which hero would you love to go on a date with and why?
Edward Norton. He is one of my favourite actors. The purpose of my date would be to learn how to portray a character. He is hot and a phenomenal actor.

Which dialogue have you mouthed in front of the mirror the most?
"Mujhe bhagvan ke liye chod do", just as a joke. Apart from my own movie dialogues, I have not really mouthed any in front of the mirror.

Who inspired you to become an actor?
My mother is my inspiration. She was the first to put me in front of the camera as a child to do ad films. As a child, I have seen my mom act and I think she is absolutely natural.

The worst film you ever watched? Why?
Can't answer this question. A great amount of effort goes into the making of each film and I am not the one to judge these movies.

Which film do you wish you could be a part of?
I wish I could have been a part of Yuva. I would have loved to do Rani's role. It will be a dream come true to work with Mani Ratnam.

What makes you an actor?
I believe acting is in my blood. Playing various roles and trying to understand different characters is an art. I believe in the character and stick to the script and director's guidelines.

Quiz: From which film is this line: "Your come come memsaab"
Raja Hindustani (correct).

Heading: VERY FILMI - Indian Express
Content:
Randeep Hooda has learnt that picky is tricky. In his new avatar, he is keen to experiment with different genres of cinema

In Bollywood, your reputation often precedes you. A classic example would be of Randeep Hooda, often tagged as Mr Sushmita Sen, even long after his break-up with the former Miss Universe. Hooda hopes that after Ru Ba Ru, he will be known more for his work. "With Ru Ba Ru I have experimented. You will see a more romantic side to me, unlike my previous roles which were more action-packed," he says, hoping that his new onscreen image provides him with the much-awaited success. His role in Ru Ba Ru is more or less similar to his off screen persona, he feels. "I play a young, ambitious boy who has a live-in relationship with his girlfriend. After all the ups and downs they go through, he decides to give it a second chance."

Hooda is also giving his career a second chance; but he makes sure he does not take the celebrity quotient seriously. "Everyone wants to be famous, so do I. But I cannot lose sleep over it. Today, I am not a huge box-office hit nor am I on the cover of film magazines. If I were to take stardom seriously, I would have been depressed," he says, with an impish smile.

With D, Hooda showed a lot of promise and followed it up with a stellar performance in Risk and a striking act in an English film Karma Confessions & Holy. However, box office success has eluded him so far. "These years of constant hard work and struggle have helped me evolve as an actor. There were times when I would hold on to certain things or roles. But now I have learnt to let go," says Hooda with élan.

With time, it seems, he has also learnt the luminous art of diplomacy. "At the end of the day an actor is only a cog in the wheel. But experience helps. I've done six films in as many years. But I've learnt a lot more. I'm losing my unawareness and becoming more humble," he says. But what we fail to understand is, for an actor who looks dapper and charms you with his talk, he insists he has never been mobbed. "I keep sporting different hairdos and hairstyles. Also, I look very different from my onscreen image. Probably, people find it difficult to recognise me and even if they do they don't consider me a big enough star to mob," he comments.

Hooda, who has always been selective about his roles, now wants to make a mark in all genres of cinema. "When I sign a film, I first consider the script and then the director," he says, also mentioning that in the next six months he has plenty to look out for. With Rang Rasiya, Mere Khwabon Main Jo Aaye, Love Khichdi and a couple more slated for release this year, Hooda is definitely a man on a mission.

Heading: FOOT LOOST - Indian Express
Content:
Expanding horizons
UTV Motion Pictures is not a production house that will rest on its laurels. After producing mega movies like Jodhaa Akbar and Race and small budget movies like Aamir, the company is venturing into the world of regional cinema. It is all set to create magic in the Tamil and Telugu film industries by producing five films in both the languages. It has even roped in Tamil superstars Suriya and Vikram and Telugu hitmaker Mahesh Babu. That sure is the way to go if UTV wants to score points with Tollywood fans.

Lover boy
RANBIR Kapoor does not shy away from showing his love and concern for girlfriend Deepika Padukone, even in public. At a recent event, the doting boyfriend who held a mug of coffee was spotted repeatedly asking Deepika if she too would like some. When she declined, he asked if she was okay and whether there was anything else she needed. When posing for photographs, he noticed that she was talking to a TV channel and told her that she had spoken enough and should join him for a photograph. To which the dimpled beauty replied with a smile, "I'm okay, Ranbir".

Family first
AKSHAY Kumar never loses an opportunity to point out that he is a devoted family man and that others should follow suit. At the celebration party of Singh is Kinng, the Khiladi Kumar proudly said that immediately after the party he was leaving for a holiday with his "queen", meaning wifey Twinkle Khanna. At another event, he cheerfully said that everyone should stick to one partner. Now that's something coming from a superstar once known for his charming way with women.

Hansikaa's heart of gold
HANSIKAA Motwani, who recently celebrated her 17th birthday, has shown that she has a major streak of generosity. She has undertaken the responsibility of education and general welfare of 15 orphaned children. That is a very noble initiative indeed. Apart from this, the young actress also has much to celebrate on the professional front. Her first south Indian film Desamuduru won her three prestigious awards, including the Filmfare for South Indian films. Another feather to her cap has been the successful run of her film Kantri in which she stars opposite Junior NTR. That's certainly a lot of achievements for an actress not even out of her teens.

Heading: City Scapes - Indian Express
Content:
Loud & Clear
Big 92.7 FM goes to campuses with 'Sony Ericsson BIG Loud and Famous Fresher Hunt' contest. Conceptualized as a means to capture the excitement in colleges with the entry of new batch of students, the 'Fresher' contest aims to provide a platform to the freshers to showcase their talent. While the first one in IBS, Mohali, was held on September 8, the contest will now go to DAV College, ITFT, Indo Global campus, Chitkara and a few government colleges of the city. The contest will be simultaneously organised in ten cities — Chandigarh, Kanpur, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Trivandrum, Surat, Udaipur, Agra, Vizag and Amritsar. Students from 15 colleges from each city will participate in the contest. BIG Jock will visit colleges and screen participants through various interesting rounds like talent, IQ, Sony Ericsson Loud, louder and loudest, Streax Funky Hairdo contest, BIG talent and Chal cut ley. RJs will also visit the college campuses and conduct the screening on the same along with live links. While the college finalists will get a funky hairdo from Streax, each winner couple per city gets a Sony Ericsson R300 phone.

Between life and death
Virasat theatre group will present its new play "52min60sec" on 13 and 14 September in Punjab Kala Bhawan 7pm onwards.

Written and directed by Asif Ali, who has been awarded Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puruskar by Sangeet Natak Akademi in the field of playwriting, the play is a story of the last one hour of the lives of six young naxalites in hiding to complete an operation. Their mission is successful and they want to celebrate it. However, the next moment they are surrounded by the army. Confusion sets in the hide out. Army commander gives them a time of 59 minutes 60 seconds to surrender and from here the play progresses in its real time.

Enacted by professional actors the play's thrust is on life not on death.

Heading: On a prowl - Indian Express
Content:
Ritu Raj Sharma personifies Chandigarh through his sketches

I want to be Le Corbusier's second hand", a statement you wouldn't often hear in the casual ease that Ritu Raj Sharma sports. An abstract artist, Sharma has been an ardent follower of the architect. Paying a tribute to the life that Corbusier infused into the City Beautiful, Sharma has sketched the city integrating its inhabitants and landmarks. Organised by Sankhyana Environment Foundation, Himachal Pradesh, the exhibition 'Hand Creativity with Architectural Elements' showcases 20 sketches, "however I made 65 in this series," tells Sharma.

Exploring the architectural design of Chandigarh, Sharma has infused colourful portraits, sceneries, sectoral plan, the round-abouts and human figures into the compositions. Common to all sketches is the 'Open Hand'. The 'human scale' used suggestively stands for the shape of the city, "Chandigarh is resting on human scale, as the population rises, it will change the framework of the city," explains Sharma. While the most visible part of every sketch are the rectangular representations of the sectors, curves and figures also stand out in some sketches. Using bright colours like yellow, red, blue and pink against black the artist portrays the energy of the city. "The compositions and the colours tell the ideas that go on in my mind. Once I have the sheet in front of me, the lines start to take their own shape. Since I'm hoping to be the second part of Corbusier's legacy, I try to improve myself on the basis of his themes. I have seen his sketches, I hope to be as good," he signs off.

Exhibition is on at the Indus Bank Art Gallery, sector 8-C, Chandigarh till September 20 between 10am to 6pm.

Heading: My priority is common man: New Patiala DC - Indian Express
Content:
Director Harry Baweja's on a lookout for fresh talent

You can make out the lines of disappointment on his face. The under-eye bags, the slight puffiness, the irritability. Seems like Love Story 2050 has pulled Harry Baweja down. While he disagrees with it, defends it with his life, we sit there, 'facing' it. The only good thing that's come out of it is that Harman's going places. "It couldn't get better for Harman. He's signed up with directors like Sanjay Leela Bhansali, Ashutosh Gowatrikar, Anees Bazmi and his second film, Victory which is on cricket will release on January 30, 2009," the proud dad beats about the success of his son, who, but the way, bears uncanny resemblance to Hrithik. "People have asked him that a 1000 times, and he always points to us - 'why don't you ask my parents how they managed it'!" That's right, blame it on the genes. Meanwhile, what actually brings Harry to town is a talent hunt. In collaboration with ITFT - CMES, (Centre for Media and Entertainment Studies) along with the Department of Tourism, UT, the hunt is to build a talent bank for TV serial and film producers. "We are always on the lookout for fresh talent and this platform will further help in networking and promoting cinematic tourism," says Harry, adding that the winners will get free scholarship for a three year degree course in media at CMES. "The idea is to tap and direct talent. It's for people who don't want to be part of reality shows. In this case, we'll be reaching out to those in the interiors and pick them region-wise," Harry feels that there's immense opportunity and money in fields like writing, directing, special effects, radio, animation et al. "These are creatively satisfying jobs and all that's needed is to create awareness."

On the personal front, Baweja shrugs off queries regarding future projects, although there is a news about directing his son in James and Bond, inspired from the famous British spy. "I cannot commit anything...right now, all I'm doing is relaxing. It's holiday time for me and my family," he evades again. Come to think of it, who wouldn't? "We are all dependent on that one Friday...I feel the audience just couldn't connect or relate or understand my film," he talks of the three years and crores put in it, and the defends with fast changing technology all over the world. "In two years, you'll see flying cars in Europe, people in the US can get into a virtual game as a character...there are skyscrapers coming up in Mumbai...I'm sure there'll be a different world in 2050." With a city that's struggling with its population, nonsensical political issues and is waterlogged every time it rains, all we can do is pray for a change! As for Baweja, he's in a risky business, and he agrees that only those who have the courage to make path-breaking films, those who take a gamble survive. "It may or may not work, but the risk has to be taken."

Heading: Court directs liquor vend allottees to produce bank statements - Indian Express
Content:
Newly-appointed Patiala Deputy Commissioner Vikas Garg said his top priority was the common man and the development of the city. Garg, who earlier served as DC Muktsar, said: "I have identified certain grey areas in the city and will ensure that the plans translate into action."

On Thursday, he met Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal to discuss his plans for the city. The meeting acquires significance as it comes a day after former CM Captain Amarinder Singh was expelled from the Vidhan Sabha. But Garg maintained: "Nothing pertaining to the elections was discussed."

Outlining his immediate areas of concern, Garg said: "Right utilisation of state and central grants will go a long way in solving the problems of the common man."

Heading: Competent Synergies to expand its call centre base - Indian Express
Content:
In the ongoing petition relating to the controversial allotment of liquor vends in Punjab, the Punjab and Haryana High Court has directed the beneficiaries to produce on record their bank statements for the period between March 3 and March 14.

The directions were issued in the wake of a petition filed by one Kanwaljit Singh and others, challenging the allotment of liquor vends in Ludhiana for the year 2008-09.

The petitioner has alleged that the Ponty Chadha Group managed to get the allotment done in favour of "the allottees in his group". He also alleged that the group filed a bunch of applications for one liquor vend.

The petitioner on Thursday filed an affidavit saying that for this purpose, manager cheques were prepared from the account of M/s K Sons and Associates, A-129, New Friends Colony, New Delhi of HDFC Bank, and after noting down the particulars, and obtaining photocopies thereof, the same were deposited back for cancellation, much before the date of draw on March 12.

Heading: Homecoming of the star - Indian Express
Content:
Competent Synergies, a city-based provider of call centre services, is planning to invest Rs 40 crore for setting up infrastructure for new call centres in the suburbs of Chandigarh.

The company, which has its presence in Haryana, Chandigarh, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Jammu and Kashmir, is coming up with a facility to manage a 2,000-seat call centre in the upcoming IT Park in Mohali.

The call centre will generate employment for more than 3,000 people in the field of Business Process Outsourcing (BPO), call centre (inbound, outbound and non-voice) and backend operations. The project is expected to be complete by March 2009.

Sharing the company's expansion plans with Newsline, Sanjay Tandon, chairman, Competent Group, said: "The new facility will be spread over one acre of land and will attract an investment of Rs 40 crore. The funds have been raised partially through the State Bank of Patiala and we are also looking forward to private equity. About 40 per cent equity will be diluted for funding our new projects. The first phase of the call centre, comprising 300 seats, will start by March 2009 and the unit will be fully commissioned by the end of the year."

The Competent Synergies has also tied up with Reliance to set up a 500-seat call centre in its existing facility in Mohali.

At present, the company is serving clients like Bharti Airtel, HFCL Infotel, Tata Teleservices, Spice Communications, Reliance Infocomm, Reliance BPO, Vodafone Essar Mobile Services, ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, ABN Amro Bank, Indusind Bank, Axis Bank, HDFC Limited, Corporation Bank among others from its two locations at Chandigarh and Mohali.

"We have around 25 branches in five states and are expanding our base. With the recent expansion, we have set up a call centre at Mohali with 1,400 seats, generating employment for about 2,500 young aspirants in this region. Our group achieved a turnover of Rs 47 crore in 2007 and the projected annual growth is 40 per cent for this fiscal. Starting the business from an area spread of 100 square feett, we have now reached an area spread of more than 1 lakh square feet," added Tandon.

An NGO by the name of Competent Foundation has also been set up to look after the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives. Competent Group businesses include stock brokerage business, verification/collection, bulk bill delivery, manpower outsourcing, call centre,insurance brokerage, commodity brokerage, central deposit services and training school.

Heading: At colleges too, Open House lacks usual fervour - Indian Express
Content: Isha Dang, winner of a dance reality show on Sony TV, returned to Patiala, her hometown, on Thursday. There were many to receive her at the railway station. "I am glad that I have brought fame to Patiala and Punjab. I plan to concentrate on my studies now but dancing is a priority as well," she said. Isha was accompanied by parents Harinder and Meenakshi. Isha is a student of Class IX at Our Lady of Fatima Public School. Her performance on the show, Boogie Woogie, will be aired on October 10.

Heading: From ‘blue-eyed’ boy to ‘eyesore’ - Indian Express
Content:
Traditionally known to cater to packed houses, the Open House, held as part of the students' elections, failed to generate much enthusiasm today. The parties were clearly indulged in mud-slinging with students' issues taking a backseat.

At DAV College, where the Open House apart from being a show of strength is touted as an exit poll in itself, marked low attendance.

For students, it was the lack of "novelty" in the speeches made by leaders that prompted them to stay away. Tarun Khanna, a student at DAV said, "For the last two years, we have been listening to the same old story of students' rights and issues involving them. These people do not have anything else to offer. What is more amusing is that they repeat the agenda every year as they are unable to fulfill the demands of the students."

Words were fired as missiles as members of the SOPU accused the opposition party for taking students for a ride throughout the year and PUSU members counter alleging that SOPU never worked for the students, but for themselves.

"Since the last one year when PUSU and SOI were in power, they did not do anything for the welfare of students. Despite the right and the means to work for students, they chose not to do anything," said Juganpreet Singh, presidential candidate from SOPU.

Simranjeet Singh of PUSU defended her party while enlisting their achievements. "We put in efforts to improve the infrastructure of the college, the results of which are for everyone to see. Whether we win the elections this year or not, students' welfare will remain our first priority," said Simranjeet Singh.

Colleges like S D and Khalsa wore a silent look as the Open House did not take place in these institutions. According to Jarnail Singh, Presidential candidate from Khalsa College, "For the last few years, we have not been holding the Open House as the college authorities had placed a ban on the event. But we should be having the Open House as candidates get an opportunity to address the students about their agenda."

Students in the college, meanwhile, were in favour of holding Open Houses. "Once students listen to the contestants on the same platform, it becomes easier for us to decide for whom to cast our vote," said Manjot Kaur of Khalsa College.

Heading: Lights, camera, action — hunt on for future stars - Indian Express
Content:
Tilll this April, when Mohali played host to Indian Premier League (IPL) matches, Ranbir Singh Khatra, the then Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), was seen as a "blue eyed" officer of the powers-that-be.

Following his infamous verbal tiff with Ness Wadia, co-owner of IPL's Kings XI Punjab franchise, and his locking horns with Punjab Cricket Association (PCA) president I S Bindra, demanding Rs 1.88 crore as security charges for the matches to be conducted at the PCA Stadium, Khatra became an 'eyesore' of sorts for the state government. His refusal to implement Punjab Director General of Police (DGP) N P S Aulakh's order to suspend the then Mullanpur Garibdass SHO Kashmira Singh is also said to be the reason for which he earned the wrath of his seniors.

Asked to proceed on leave, Khatra's exit was unprecedented and sudden, at a time when the model code of conduct for panchayat elections was in force. Any routine transfer and posting is prohibited during this period.

Though top government officers said Khatra had applied for leave, there seems to be another story behind his exit.

It was on the morning of June 2 that Khatra reportedly received a call from the office of Punjab Chief Secretary Ramesh Inder Singh. He was told to meet Singh at his office in the Civil Secretariat. The reason given to him was: "important and urgent".

The Chief Secretary told him that the state government wanted him to immediately proceed on a long leave. Though Ramesh Inder Singh did not give any specific reason, it was indicated that the "powers-that-be" were not happy over his tiff with Ness Wadia.

Left with no other option, Khatra applied for casual leave between June 2 and 8, followed by an ex India leave between June 9 and July 8.

The media failed to contact Khatra, with his old phone numbers not valid any more. Neither the district police nor the state police control room had his new number.

Till August 27, Khatra awaited a fresh posting. He has now joined as Commandant Batallion at Bahadurgarh.

Sources close to him say Khatra's removal at a time when he was vigorously perusing his case for elevation to the Indian Police Services (IPS) came as a bolt from the blue. He was the lone officer from the Mohali district who enjoyed the longest spell as the SSP — from March 13, 2007 to June 2, 2008. He was the fifth SSP of Mohali, with four former SSPs having been shifted in less than a year of posting.

Heading: ‘Him Darshan’ to woo tourists from Kerala, Gujarat - Indian Express
Content:
With an aim to provide an opportunity to the youth of North India to join the fast developing media and entertainment industry, a talent hunt is being organised in various cities between September 6 and 20.

In Chandigarh, the auditions will take place on September 12 at the ITFT campus in Sector 17. The semifinals and finals of the programme will take place in Chandigarh on September 26 and 27 with the winners to dance and dine with actor Harman Baweja.

While talking about the talent hunt, director Harry Baweja said a scholarship will be awarded to the winners. "It is for a three year degree course at Centre for Media and Entertainment Studies (CMES). Animation, special effects, TV, radio, dance, acting, film, writing, producing, directing—there is immense opportunity in the industry and it is well paid," said Baweja.

He added: "With the increasing multiplexes, the cinema audience has moved from the rickshaw pullers to the middle class who want to watch films that offer something extra in terms of script, story and direction."

A conference is also being organised by the ITFT - CMES with the Department of Tourism to promote North India as a destination for cinematic tourism.

Heading: Health dept to tie up with Mysore institute to detect deafness in newborns - Indian Express
Content:
With the aim to attract tourists from far-off areas like Kerala, West Bengal, Gujarat and Lucknow, the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) has planned a 'Him Darshan' for them, adding destinations like Shimla, Dharamshala, Pathankot and Manali.

With an aim to tap the potential of hill tourism, the corporation plans to woo the frequent travellers and those bored of the normal tourist destinations offered to them.

The Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation plans to start the packages from the winters. "Winters are considered the perfect time to visit the hills, especially by the tourists from states other than North India, who visit hills for the snow," said IRCTC Chief Regional Manager Aneet Dulat.

The company further plans to rope in private national online tour operators like makemytrip.com, travelindia.com and tui.com for the project.

Attempts are also being made for tie-ups with hotel chains as well as Himachal Tours Corporation for securing larger operations.

The narrow gauge hill experience will be covered by rail from Kalka to Shimla, from Shimla to Dharamshala by road and from Dharamshala to Pathankot by rail.

The corporation also plans to widen its base among low-budget tourists. Further, to ensure that the services meted out are up to the standard, it has chalked a plan to ensure that the visitors receive all the services promised by the private players.

"Every hotelier has to attach a feedback form along with the bill receipt if he desires to get the payment for the services rendered to the tourists. These forms will be filled by the tourists and have details regarding their stay and catering services. If the tourist does not want to fill the form, the hotelier will have to get it from him in writing," said Dulat.

Touchscreens at bus stand, railway station for train schedule
Extending online services to city residents, the Northern Railways installed three touchscreen terminals — two at the reservation centre of Inter State Bus Terminus, Sector 17, and one at the railway station — on Thursday. Till now, only one such terminal was placed at the railway station.

Passengers can now avail online services like Passenger Name Record (PNR) status, seat availability and the timetable at the touch of their fingers. The information will be available in Hindi as well as English.

Expressing delight at the installation of the kiosks, a passenger at ISBT-17 said: "Before this we had to line at the enquiry counter for hours and were dependent on clerks for the information. Sometimes, they were not available or are not in the mood to provide a proper answer to our queries. Now, we will be free of all such hassles."

Divisional Railway Manager, H K Jaggi, said: "The touchscreens will add to the number of channels available to passengers for getting information relating to the Railways, which include the website, railway call centre and inquiry counters at stations."

He added that the number of such terminals will be gradually increased, as they gain in popularity.

Heading: Discrepancies in voters’ list ahead of Kharar civic polls - Indian Express
Content:
The UT Health department has decided to hire an audiologist to detect cases of deafness among the newborns in the city. It has also planned to tie up with an institute in Mysore for carrying out the tests.

"This is being done under the National Programme for Prevention of Control of Deafness (NPPCD) that was launched a year and a half ago. There is a shortage of quality audiologists in the country. The few who graduate from the colleges spread across the country prefer to go abroad, as they are offered better remuneration. This is the reason why we are going to tie up with the All India Institute of Speech, Hearing and Audiology in Mysore," said S D Singh, nodal officer of the programme in the UT.

"We aim to appoint at least one audiologist to look after the sophisticated testing facilities at GMSH-16," he added.

Nearly four to five cases of children with deafness below the age of 14 years are treated at the GMSH-16 every day. "If deafness is diagnosed after the child attains five years of age, his speech does not develop. This creates an added burden," Singh said.

The programme has been launched in 25 districts across the country. Plans are in place for procuring machines for conducting the otoacoustic emission testing (OAE), which will cost Rs 3.7 lakh.

Dr Singh said: "There are nearly 6,000 deaf patients in the city, of which 50 per cent of the cases can be treated." The NPPCD, along with training of the medical and paramedical staff and capacity building in the hospitals, also encompasses the rehabilitation of the victims of hearing loss which involves distributing free hearing aids to the children below 14 years.

Two-day medical awareness camp on muscular dystrophy starts today
Nearly 100 patients are expected to attend a two-day medical awareness camp at the Indira Holiday Home, Sector 24, from Friday. The camp is being organised by the Indian Association of Muscular Dystrophy. Muscular dystrophy falls under the category of neuromuscular disorders, where muscles stop synthesising dystrophin, a protein, which is vital for the performance of such functions. The association has earlier held camps in Maharashtra, Andra Pradesh, Delhi and Himachal Pradesh before coming to Chandigarh. — ENS

Heading: Garbage woes: Dadumajra locals irked by MC inaction threaten to protest - Indian Express
Content:
Newsline found 200 voters enrolled in a single house, names of permanent residents deleted from rolls, unidentified men listed as residents, voters shown as residents of houses, which do not exist

Can over 200 persons live in one house? Can anyone live without a house? Can a permanent resident be denied the right to vote? Can a stranger be living in the house without the family's knowledge?

The answer to all these questions is yes if the electoral rolls prepared for the 15 wards of Kharar Municipal Council are to be believed. The polls are slated for September 14.

Ward 4
As many as 183 voters have been listed from house number 2553. Also, non-existent house numbers — 2553/561, 2553/563/4 and 2553/790 — have been created in the list.

Further, 63 and 48 electorates each were enrolled in house numbers 2581 and 2540 respectively.

In this case too, imagined house numbers 2581/838, 2581F, 2581A, 2581B, 2581C, 2581G, 2581/256/4, 2581/264/4, 2540/667, 2540/674, 2540/674/4 and 2540/677 were enumerated in the voters' list.

Ward 5
House number 369 — conveniently divided as 369F, 369E, 369B, 369K, 369C, 369D and 369H — lists 54 voters.

House number 364 has 51 voters under different numbers — 364-I, 364A, 364H, 364E, 364B, 364C and 364D.

Prem Sagar, owner of house number 336C, said: "I was astonished to find five people, whose names I did not even recognise, listed as residents of this house in the voters' list."

The supplementary list is also as surprising. The 393 electorates added to Ward 5 in the list do not have any house number printed along their names, a mandatory detail.

Ward 8
Here 123 electorates have been enrolled at house number 1507 with different numberings.

Another 104, 78, 65 and 29 voters each are listed in house numbers 1699, 1828, 1700 and 1820, respectively.

Ward 1, 6, 11, 13, 15
In Ward 6, 111 voters are shown as residents of house number 1981 while 63 and 57 electorates each are enrolled in house numbers 1855 and 1993 respectively.

Ward 11 has 238 electorates enrolled in house number 1491, 150 in 1502, 111 in 1507, 99 in 1503, 82 in 1506, 58 in 1537, 51 in 1500 and 40 in 1492 with different numberings.

In Ward 15, 47 voters have been added in the supplementary list without stating their house numbers.

The names of 497 and 128 voters were deleted from Ward 1 and Ward 13 respectively notwithstanding the fact that most possessed voter cards.

Kharar Sub-Divisional Magistrate Rajeev Kumar Gupta expressed ignorance about the discrepancies and assured that he will get the lists verified.

"If inconsistencies are found, necessary action will be taken against the erring officials with the consent of the State Election Commission," he added.

But Kharar Municipal Council Executive Officer Sunil Kumar Gulati claimed: "All electoral rolls are correct and up to the mark. They have been prepared after my staff and I have verified the details personally."

Heading: Dera issue: SC sets aside former CJ’s order - Indian Express
Content:
The residents of Dadumajra, irked by the inaction of the Municipal Corporation (MC) to tackle the garbage-dumping woes, have threatened to block garbage trucks coming to the site.

Area councillor Kamlesh says, "The residents have been complaining about the problems for a long time. They are ready to agitate."

The unbearable stench from the garbage lying in the open site has not only made life miserable for residents but has also provided a breeding ground for mosquitoes and flies.

The main reason for the increasing heap is the non-functioning of the Solid Waste Management Plant, owing to which the garbage is not being processed.

The UT Administrator had recently visited the site and instructed civic officials to use scientific means to dispose off garbage. Interestingly, it was before his visit that the area was sprayed after a long time.

Buta Singh, chairman of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes on a recent visit to the city had slammed the Administration for the conditions prevailing in the area.

Alarmed by the poor conditions, the councillors have asked for a health check-up of the residents.

Even with the issue having been discussed several times in the House Meet of the civic body, no solution has yet been found.

The civic officials maintain the civic body is waiting for a reply from the company managing the plant, to whom a notice had been served earlier.

Heading: ‘Jilted lover’ throws acid on girl at Hallomajra - Indian Express
Content:
Apex court remits case back to High Court

In a significant decision, the Supreme Court of India has set aside the orders passed by former Chief Justice of Punjab and Haryana High Court V K Jain in relation with a petition on Dera Sacha Sauda.

The senior standing counsel, Advocate Anupam Gupta, and the former Chief Justice had, earlier, entered into a war of words on the issue. Gupta had challenged the issuance of notices to the UT Administration by Jain.

Owing to the verbal argument, Jain had sought explanation from the Home Secretary and directed him to file an affidavit explaining as to on whose recommendations or directions, Gupta had taken up the argument with Jain. An affidavit, explaining that the contentions raised by Gupta were not dictated by anyone, was filed by the UT Home Secretary in the High Court.

Not satisfied with the affidavit, Jain had directed the UT Administrator to file his affidavit in this regard. Aggrieved by the order, the UT Administration moved the Supreme Court challenging the order.

The Supreme Court had, meanwhile, granted a stay over the hearing of the petition in the High Court. On Thursday, a Division Bench of the Supreme Court set aside the orders passed by Jain and remitted the case back to the High Court for hearing.

Heading: GMCH-32 suicide: chargesheet filed against professor - Indian Express
Content:
A 16-year-old girl sustained serious burns when a youth allegedly threw acid on her. The incident took place at 2.10 pm in Hallomajra on Thursday.

While the accused, Vishal (23) is untraceable, Jyoti is undergoing treatment at the Government Medical College and Hospital in Sector 32.

Police said Vishal and Jyoti lived in the same locality and had an affair for some time. Though the two had recently parted ways, Vishal was trying to come back to her life, while Jyoti had refused to entertain him, they said. Vishal allegedly attacked her to avenge the rebuttal.

Jyoti's mother Jagmati conformed that Vishal had been known to them for quite some time.

Vishal worked as a labourer in a factory. A case under Section 325 of the IPC has been registered against him in the Sector 31 police station.

Doctors at the GMCH-32 said Jyoti sustained burns on her back, right side of the face and her arm. The police said she was not fit to make any statement.

"All efforts are on to nab the youth who has been missing since the incident. We hope to arrest him soon," said Bhupinder Singh, SHO, Sector 31 police station.

The acid attack also left Sushil, an 11-year-old boy who was playing nearby, injured. He sustained minor burns on his back and elbow. He was administered first aid.

Heading: Talks fail, MCM girls up in arms - Indian Express
Content:
The UT Police filed a chargesheet against GMCH professor Dr N K Goel in the abetment to suicide case registered after a student was found dead on the campus in January this year.

The professor had allegedly harassed Jaspreet Singh (21) because he was from the Scheduled Caste category, forcing him to end his life. He has been booked under Section 306 of the IPC and provisions of the SC/ST Act. The professor is out on interim bail.

Jaspreet's body was found hanging in the institute library on January 27. A suicide note recovered four hours after his death had blamed the professor and two colleagues for harassing him. A day after the incident, a case was registered and an inquiry initiated.

A PGI committee was formed to revaluate the exam papers, in which Jaspreet had failed. The committee found that while Goel had given him 14 marks, he deserved 16.5 marks. Jaspreet needed 15 marks to pass the 30-mark exam.

The Central Forensic Science Laboratory confirmed the handwriting in the suicide note as that of Jaspreet. The GMCH had also formed a committee to probe the suicide case.

Heading: Cop posted at CM house dies in accidental firing - Indian Express
Content:
With talks between the college authorities and the agitating students reaching a stalemate on Day Two, the situation at the MCM DAV College worsened on Thursday. Continuing with their protest, the 500-odd girls raised slogans outside the principal's office and also pelted her office with stones.

Geeta Tariyar, a PUSU candidate whose nomination for the president's post was cancelled on Wednesday, said: "We will not let the principal have her way. She did not consider my candidature just because she wanted Himani to become the president. Girls will not tolerate this kind of favouritism any more."

Himani, an independent, has been the president of the college council for the last three years.

Though the authorities tried their best to bring the situation under control, the protesting girls created a ruckus on the college premises. Even as student leaders from Panjab University were denied entry to the college, the girls scaled the walls to "talk" to them. "They are our well-wishers and we want the principal to talk in their presence. We will not listen to what she has to say until and unless they are made a party to it," said Geeta.

The protest took an ugly turn when supporters from both the camps got into a verbal duel. The protesting girls demanded an apology from Himani and asked her to step down. With Himani refusing to apologise, the protesting students raised slogans and threatened to take to the streets if their demands were not met.

Clarifying her stand, Himani said she had not done anything wrong and she would not apologise. "I will not give in. I had earlier thought of giving up the post as the college's discipline was suffering, but now I will fight for myself as well as for the rights of the students who are being taken for a ride," she said.

Talking to Newsline, principal Puneet Bedi said: "We are willing to talk to these girls and solve the matter. But they do not want to listen to us. The college cannot act at their whims and fancies just because they have a few political parties for support." She added that since it was in black and white that Geeta was ineligible to contest the elections, she could not consider her case.

Heading: Results expected by afternoon - Indian Express
Content:
CRPF Constable Sunder Singh (37), who was posted at the residence of Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal in Sector 2, died after his gun went off accidentally. The incident took place around 3.45 pm on Thursday, when Sunder was going to his duty-post from the barracks, police said.

According to Sunder's colleagues, they heard a gunshot and found him lying in a pool of blood. He was rushed to the PGI, where doctors declared him dead on arrival. The bullet had hit Sunder in his chest.

Based on the eyewitnesses' statements, the police are considering it to be a case of accidental firing.

"We were informed by the police control room that a constable had committed suicide at the CM's residence. When we inspected the spot, it appeared that an accidental gunshot claimed Sunder's life. We are investigating the matter," said an officer.

"According to preliminary investigations, Sunder's gun slipped off his hands and while he tried to balance it, he accidentally pulled the trigger. We have recorded the statements of a number of CRPF and Punjab Police constables who were a witness to the incident. We have informed Sunder's family in Garhwal, Uttarakhand. They are expected to reach here by tomorrow afternoon," said Inspector Harsahai, Station House Officer, Sector 3 police station.

The police have initiated inquest proceedings under Section 174 of the CrPC and kept Sunder's body at the Government Multi-Specialty Hospital, Sector 16, where a postmortem will be conducted on Friday.

Heading: PU Open House a flop show - Indian Express
Content:
With its students' council going to polls on Friday, Panjab University claims to be leaving no stone unturned to ensure peaceful polling. Police officers are busy holding meetings on the campus and deciding on the checks and raids to be conducted by them.

Outsiders may face problems tomorrow as none of them will be allowed inside without a thorough checking. They will require stickers, specially issued for the purpose, for their vehicles. In all, around 150 to 200 policemen have been deployed on the campus.

The polling will begin at 10 am and no student will be allowed to enter the classrooms after that. The students are required to carry their identity cards, without which they won't be allowed to cast votes. Results are expected to be out by afternoon.

As a precautionary measure, the gate number 1, from PGI side, will remain closed throughout the day and no bus will be allowed to ply on the campus.

The university authorities raided the hostels on Thursday to see if any outsider was staying there and weapons stored. Taking extra care, barricades have been put up at different places on the campus.

Talking to Newsline, Dean Students Welfare Prof Naval Kishore said: "We have taken all necessary measures to ensure peaceful polls. We have also asked for cooperation from different student leaders for the purpose."

Every booth will have two to five constables posted there to take care of the ballot boxes and ensure peaceful polling. ASP (Central) Madhur Verma said: "From today evening and till the elections are over, we will be keeping the university under tight security and no one will be allowed to enter into any kind of altercation. We anticipate post-poll violence but are all prepared to tackle them. We are trying our best to ensure peaceful polls."

Heading: Headmasters’ selection procedure null, says  High Court - Indian Express
Content:
PU STUDENTS' POLLS: 10 am: polling begins; 200 cops deployed; Gate No. 1 to remain closed

Thin attendance, speeches lacking fire and no question-answer round — it was not a usual Open House at Panjab University from any angle.

Speakers from different parties could be heard taking credit for same achievements and listing same issues. All that the session saw was mud-racking and hooting.

While the seasoned leaders were not allowed to speak, the new faces contesting the polls had little experience of public speaking. Result: the Open House didn't have its usual fervour.

It was the first time that only presidential candidate and another member from the panel were allowed to speak. The new faces couldn't match the oratory skills of senior leaders.

With actually no issues, the candidates found it hard to speak for the allotted 10 minutes and kept repeating the same point.

The House started with different parties coming to the venue in groups, raising victory slogans. The only achievement that the parties listed was reducing the fee hike. And the issue raised by them — here too they were unanimous — was the central university status for PU.

Speaking about his party's achievements, SOPU-ABVP presidential candidate Sahil Nanda said: "Our party has been working for the last 11 years for students' welfare. A win or a loss does not matter, we will continue fighting for their rights."

Next on the stage were the INSO-SOI candidates. Paramvir Singh (Sunny), who is contesting for the post of general secretary, directly attacked both SOPU-ABVP and PUSU-NSUI-HSA leaders.

He said: "We are not like those leaders who face allegations of illicit relations, and those who stab a fellow student. How can such parties fight for the rights of others?" The comments were directly pointed at PUSU member Tejpal Singh Cheema and SOPU leader Brinder Dhillon, respectively.

Members of all parties could be seen hooting in a bid to present a show of strength and belittling the supporters of rival parties.

The House also saw a few girls among the speakers. Parul of the SOPU-ABVP combine and Geetika Gupta of the INSO-SOI alliance are contesting for the post of vice-president. They talked about the issues pertaining to girls.

With not much chaos, the House concluded in peace, though a huge police deployment had been made, anticipating law and order problem.

The students criticised PU for doing away with the question-answer round after the Open House. In the absence of this regular feature, the event had been reduced to nothing more than a platform for the candidates to praise their respective parties. Sukhdev Kundu, the INSO-SOI candidate for president's post, said: "Open House is nothing without a question-answer round. Student leaders just went away without anyone questioning them on the false achievements listed by them. The elections have been reduced to mere eyewash."

At a glance
* Tension prevailed after a SOPU-ABVP member hit a PUSU-HSA-NSUI supporter with a stick. The matter was resolved after the police intervened
* INSO-SOI leaders simply walked away after their speakers were through with the speeches
* Prashant, a speaker from the SOPU-ABVP alliance, had a sore throat. His voice cracked the moment he raised his pitch. It was all laughter that could be heard while he spoke.
* In a bid to distract the audience, INSO member Vikas Rathi came running and stood next to where PUSU supporters were standing and started shouting victory slogans

Heading: 10 more CNG outlets to be opened soon - Indian Express
Content:
The Calcutta High Court held the selection procedure for appointing headmasters in secondary schools by the West Bengal School Service Commission (WBSSC) unconstitutional.

On Thursday, the court also set aside a rule of the WBSSC Act. As per the rule, teaching experience of five years is essential for a candidate to apply for schools run by the West Bengal Secondary Board.

A Division Bench comprising Justices Pratap Roy and Manik Mohan Sarkar observed that the rule framed by the WBSSC in the selection procedure violated Article 14 of The Constitution.

Prdip Kotal of Bankura and Subal Guchait of West Midnapore had filed a petition in 2002 alleging that they were not allowed by the WBSSC to appear for the written examination for the post of headmasters, citing the WBSSC Act.

Kotal and Guchait have MSc and B Ed degrees. In 1995, both had joined a school in Arunachal Pradesh. In 2002, after the publication of the advertisement by the WBSSC, they had applied for the post of headmasters and their applications were rejected.

Kotal and Guchait then filed a writ petition in the Calcutta High Court in 2003, alleging that their fundamental right was violated by the WBSSC.

The commission should not have the right to frame such rules, which were against the spirit of the Indian Constitution, they alleged.

A single Bench had rejected their petition in 2005.They filed an appeal before a Division Bench challenging the verdict of the single Bench.

On Thursday, the Bench also directed the WBSSC to allow the petitioners to appear in the examination for the post of headmasters.

Heading: Foreigners queue up at Kumartuli, lend a dab of colour to idols - Indian Express
Content:
As the deadline of the High Court order for autos to convert to CNG is drawing close, the state environment department is all set to take measures to ensure that no bottlenecks occur in the supply of the fuel.

In a meeting with five oil companies — Indian Oil Corporation, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited, Reliance and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd — on Thursday, the environment department asked them to come up with more LPG outlets. It was decided that the companies will increase the number of outlets in the city.

"Following the High Court order, many auto-rickshaws raised the issue that insufficient supply of CNG is one of the major constraints in converting to cleaner fuel," said M L Meena, Principal Secretary, Environment.

At present, there are 12 CNG outlets in the city. It was decided in the meeting that another 10 will be added by March, 2009, said Meena.

The government had earlier informed the Calcutta High Court that it had issued an order where all registered auto-rickshaws, operating within the Kolkata Municipal Area, were required to convert to CNG mode by March 31, 2009 and no dual fuel option would be permitted. While all registered auto-rickshaws, plying within the municipal area under the Kolkata Metropolitan Development Authority are needed to convert by December 31, 2009.

After going through the government order, the Division Bench incorporated it in its order and directed that it be considered as its own order and asked all departments concerned to strictly implement it. It is, however, felt that only increasing CNG outlets cannot be a solution to environmental pollution.

"There needs to be a coordination between the environment and transport department. Unless the transport department strictly implements the order, there is no point in increasing the number of outlets," said Subhas Dutta, an environmentalist.

Heading: Prime accused in Nobel theft case murdered - Indian Express
Content:
Visit Kumartuli this time of the year and you will see the curious faces and inquisitive whispers of foreign tourists as they make a beeline for the area.
