With Durga idols becoming increasingly popular across the globe, a visit to the Victoria Memorial and a view of the Howrah Bridge are not the only attractions for foreigners.

"I have come here to see Kumartuli. I heard a lot about the activities here during the Bengali festival," said 30-year-old Rex Kimberly from USA.

The tourists from different countries — America, Australia, China, Canada, Japan and England — are eager to look around and observe how idols are created out of clay and fibre glass. While some foreigners come on their own, most come in groups accompanied by a tour guide.

"Foreigners are pouring in. They watch our work and wonder how we make the idols. A few days ago, an American couple visited us to learn how to make idols. They ended up ordering a sculpture for themselves," said Indrajit Das of Birendra Studio, who has been involved in the business for the last 50 years.

Kumartuli has carved a niche for itself in the world of idol-making and sculptures. The idols are exported every year to several countries, including America, Australia and Southeast Asia.

"Almost 20 foreigners visit us daily and watch our artisans as they work. Today, a group of nearly 10 Japanese tourists came and clicked photographs," said Shyamal Pal, a Kumartuli artisan. " Most of the tourists do not come to buy idols but to just see us work," said Shapan Pal, another artisan.

A Canadian national, Khoseque, said: "The sight of artisans working tirelessly to make idols fascinates me. The way they use colour and make an idol with hay and clay is unique." Kumartuli artists claim foreigners are more fascinated by the sculptures of Goddess Kali than of Durga. Accessories like ornaments and decorative items for the idols excite tourists, some of whom take mementos like dolls and fibre images with them.

"Yesterday a foreigner bought a topor," said Pancharam Datta, who works at a shop in Kumartuli. "Foreigners are in awe of our work. They take photographs of the clay images and love to see them being painted with a variety of colours," said Mintu Pal, Secretary, Kumartuli Shilpa Samity.

Heading: N-deal compromises sovereignty of the country, says Brinda Karat - Indian Express
Content:
The prime accused in the Nobel theft case, Jibon Bagdi, was murdered on Thursday. The police said though Bagdi was never chargesheeted in the case, he had provided some clues to the police during the investigation.

Bagdi, a resident of Bolpur, was killed by miscreants in the morning as soon as he stepped out of his house in Parata village. He was repeatedly stabbed on the head, neck and stomach. His wife has registered a complaint at the local police station, naming a local fisherman as the prime suspect.

The police said Bagdi was an expert in identifying and stealing artefacts. He was the prime suspect in the theft of Rabindranath Tagore's Nobel medallion on March 25, 2004. He was arrested in this connection and interrogated. He was released on bail in 2006, as the CBI had failed to make any headway in the case and could not file any chargesheet against him.

Besides the medallion, other memorabilia which went missing in the March 2004 theft included Tagore's gold watch, ornaments and ivory artefacts, which were never recovered. Tagore's Nobel medallion and 43 other items were stolen from Rabindra Bhavan in Santiniketan.

Initially, the West Bengal police and the Criminal Investigation Department started a probe into the matter. Later the probe was handed over to the CBI. Bagdi was also an accused in the murder of his brother.

Heading: ‘Can’t blame teachers for failure of students’ - Indian Express
Content:
Brinda Karat, CPM parliamentarian spoke on the negative aspects of the Indo-US nuclear deal in a symposium organised by Bhashanagar, a Bengali magazine edited by poet Subodh Sarkar.

Sarkar is one of the few eminent personalities who had spoken in favour of the CPM during the Nandigram impasse in the past.

"The nuclear deal compromises India's strategic autonomy," Karat said on Friday.

"Nuclear energy is not the best option even for the developed countries. Australia has one of the richest deposits of uranium but does not have a single nuclear plant. Neither does Scandinavia, Italy and the United Kingdom. In a country like India which is poor in resources, nuclear energy cannot be the best choice," she added.

Karat also slammed the UPA government at the Centre for breaking the consensus that had existed among political parties until now on foreign policy.

"On foreign policies we were one, regardless of the party. Prime Minister Manmohan Singh has deviated from it," said Karat.

India is crucial for tilting the balance towards unilateralism. If India agrees to the growing hegemony of the US, it will be disastrous for the rest of the world, she added.

Karat also elaborated on how the Hyde Act is a gateway for defence agreements, which in turn, will revive the nuclear and defence industries of the US.

Heading: Bloc threatens to withdraw support over retail chains - Indian Express
Content:
State School Education Minister Partha De said the teachers should not be blamed if students do not perform well.

His comment comes a few weeks after the chief secretary wrote to the school education department stating that if students of a school get poor marks, their teachers should be held responsible.

De said: "If a teacher does not perform his or her duty properly, he or she can be held responsible but a teacher can not be blamed if the child secures low marks in examination."

The minister was addressing a gathering of members of All Bengal Teachers Organisation (ABTA) on Thursday. The programme was organised by the West Bengal Board of Secondary Education to commemorate the birth centenary of educationist Satpriya Roy.

De added that Roy, a former education minister and a former secretary of ABTA, had also advocated for not to blame the teachers for students' poor performance.

Taking note of growing trend of private tuitions, the minister said a high student-teacher ratio pushes students to take private tuition. But there are a few guardians who send their children for private tuitions even if they don't need it, he added. 

"Private tuition is a cause of concern and we have asked the State Council of Educational Research and Training to prepare a report on this," said De.

Regarding the medium of instruction in schools, he said, "The government does not follow a clear policy on medium of instructions. Roy had advocated to strengthen the regional languages but also emphaised on learning Hindi and English."

Heading: Talks on, Singur farmers unsure of getting land back - Indian Express
Content:
After vandalising outlets of organised retail chains, including Reliance Fresh, the Forward Bloc has now started criticising the state government's policy of allowing retail and wholesale majors in the city.

To protest against the policy of the ruling party, the Bloc organised a rally from Esplanade to College Street on Thursday. The party held a demonstartion against organised retail and wholesale chains, which paralysed traffic during the busy hours.

"Despite being a constituent of the Left Front government, we will keep organising movements against this policy. This is unfortunate that this policy has been made by a government known earlier as a pro-people government. But at present most of the policies are against the interests of the poor farmers, small shop owners and hawkers," said Ashok Ghosh, Forward Bloc state secretary.

"We have already created pressure on the ruling party to change its policy, which can hamper the livelihood of the poor. If our protests do not bear results, then we have to think of withdrawing support from the government but that will be the last option," added Ghosh.

Heading: No more management quota in engg colleges - Indian Express
Content:
Confusion prevails among the farmers of Singur, even as the meetings between the representatives of the state government and the Krishi Jomi Raksha Committee entered the fourth day.

Several farmers want their land back from the Tata car factory but are not sure that the talks will bear any positive result.

The talks had begun on Sunday after the state government signed an agreement to return the land to those farmers of Singur, who did not accept the compensation for their land acquired for the Nano project.

The four-member committee that was set up to look into the matter and give suggestions has been deliberating the matter over the last four days. When the talks began, the farmers were jubilant that they will get back their land. On Thursday, their hopes and expectations dwindled as the committee hinted that a consensus among its members is not likely to be reached within the stipulated seven days.

Nilmoni Khara, a resident of Khaserbheri village, said the state government should not only return their land but also develop it so that it becomes cultivable. "We want our land back. We have placed great hopes over the meetings that are being held in Kolkata," he added.

His one bigha land and nearly 18 bighas of his relatives' land were acquired for the small car factory of Tata Motors. He also referred to the recent agreement between the state government and the Trinamool Congress regarding the return of land to the farmers. "The Governor was a witness to the agreement and the state government cannot go back on its words now," said Khara.

Amiyo Kole and Radha Rani Kole, residents of Gopalnaga village, also echoed similar sentiments and expressed hope that they would get their lands back.

In a related development, a few Naxalite groups are trying to exploit the situation and mobilise the marginal and unregistered farmers, who have gained nothing from the deal.

One such party had held a rally in Singur on Wednesday. They demanded that the state government should also cater to the needs of the marginal farmers.

Overall, no untoward incident was reported from Singur on Thursday. A police officer said the situation was normal and peaceful.

No rift within CPM over Singur, insists Yechury
CPM leader Sitaram Yechury denied the reports of differences within the Left Front over handling of the Singur tangle. The politburo member said, "The party has only one line and everyone follows that." He was speaking to the media at the party office in Kolkata.

Asked whether the West Bengal government would return the land from within the Nano car project area, he said: " The matter was being discussed at the state level. For the future of Bengal and prosperity of its people, a solution should be found at the earliest."

The four-member committee is holding its meeting and we hope that some solution will be found before the deadline, said Yechuri, who is also a Rajya Sabha MP from West Bengal.

The committee comprises Hooghly District Magistrate Neelam Meena, WBIDC Managing Director Subrata Gupta and two representatives of Trinamool Congress. It held its meeting on Thursday.

After Sunday's agreement at the Raj Bhavan to end the Singur impasse, the issue has appeared to be back to square one as state government and the Tatas have rejected any change in the land pattern of the project site. The Trinamool Congress, however, has insisted that 300 acre of land from the factory site be returned to the farmers.

( With inputs from PTI)

Heading: Kolkata ready to welcome Last Lear Amitabh - Indian Express
Content:
To curb corruption, the West Bengal University of Technology (WBUT) has said that there will be no further admissions to engineering colleges in the state through the management quota this year. The university has asked the colleges to come up with a final list of students admitted through the quota by September 11.

Vice-Chancellor of WBUT Sabyasachi Sengupta said: "All the colleges are expected to submit the number of students they have admitted through the management quota by Thursday. The colleges who do not submit the list will not be awarded any quota this year."

In a meeting with the principals of the state engineering colleges earlier this week, the university had urged the colleges to submit the information by September 11. The step has been taken to check corruption in the admission procedure through the management quota, said officials.

The 60 engineering colleges, which comprises six government colleges and private colleges, have an intake of nearly 18,000 students per year. Each college can admit nearly 10 per cent of its seats through the management quota.

According to sources, most of the quota seats are filled from the residual vacancies of the students who drop out at the last hour. The V-C admits that these vacancies are the root cause of corruption in the admission procedure.

"This year, we have decided to freeze the residual vacancy," said Sengupta. The university will also examine that the students who were admitted this year through the management quota met the required guidelines and did not pay any capitation fee.

Heading: Singur panel will miss deadline - Indian Express
Content:
The premiere of The Last Lear, starring Amitabh Bachchan, might have run into a rough weather in Mumbai, but Kolkata is all set to give a grand opening on Friday.

With Bachchan expected to be in Kolkata on Friday for the premiere, the city is gearing up to give him a warm welcome.

Members of the Amitabh Bachchan Fan Club have already made plans to receive their hero in the airport and take him to his hotel in a 10-car convoy.

"We met him while he was in Kolkata for the shoot. He told us his role in The Last Lear is very different from that of Black, and that it will appeal to everybody. We plan to decorate the halls where the film will be screened," said Sanjoy Patodia, secretary of the club.

Die-hard fans like Damayanti Ray, an IT executive based in Salt Lake's Sector V, have already made plans to watch the film with her husband. "We do not want to read the reviews and then watch it since people might not like off-beat films. We are sure the film will be a treat since it brings a great director and an actor together for the first time," said Ray.

The film starring Bachchan along with Priety Zinta, Arjun Rampal and Shefali Shah, has been in the news for the last two days following Maharshtra Navnirman Sena's violence in Mumbai over Jaya Bachchan's remarks.

In spite of the glitches, producer Arindam Choudhury, however, is confident that the film will do brisk business in Kolkata as well as other metros, including Mumbai.

"We do not expect much problems since Amitabh has already apologised. We are excited about the film," said Choudhury.

The film based on Utpal Dutt's play Aajker Shahjahan will be the second time that Bachchan will feature in an English film. 

Admitting that English films tend to have a niche audience base in the country, Chaudhury nevertheless hopes that the film will appeal to all Bachchan fans.

"Our main target is the multiplex crowd since we feel it will eventually constitute one of the biggest audience base in the coming years. So we are trying to build it up through our films," said Choudhury.

As the language and unusual subject matter is expected to attract a niche urban crowd, and city hall owners admit that it will be difficult to pull a huge crowd.

"It's true that the audience have evolved, yet a film like this will have limited audience. English films still attract a very urban crowd. But as this fillm features Amitabh Bachchan, we still do not know how it will perform commercially, as many such films tend to do well merely through word of mouth publicity," said Abhishek Raina, assistant vice-president, Marketing and Sales of Fame India Limited.

Heading: Buddha calls for better work culture, his employees call for strikes - Indian Express
Content:
The four-member committee set up to settle the Singur crisis, will not be able to meet its deadline, which ends on September 14.

After Thursday's meeting, committee head Rabindranath Bhattcharya, Trinamool MLA from Singur, said: " The committee is expected to submit an interim report to the government after seven days. We will ask for more time," he said.

Justice Chittatosh Mookherjee, legal advisor to the West Bengal Governor in the recent talks, told The Indian Express that the crisis would become more complex if things are dragged. "The issue needs to be settled at the earliest," he said.

But even on Thursday's meeting — though Bhattacharya claimed both parties exchanged views cordially — sources in West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation said the dispute over the quantum of land to be returned from within the project area raged. Trinamool representatives demanded 300 acres, the government representatives said it was possible only to give 40 acres.

The impasse has been on since Monday. On Wednesday, the parties had visited the project site to identify land. But the visit proved unproductive. Justice Mookherjee said both parties will have to climb down if they wanted a solution. To make matters worse, in Singur, the farmers who have already received compensation conveyed to the government that their land cannot be allotted to other farmers. The number of such farmers is increasing, said sources in the commerce department.

"Both Mamata and the state government should take the views of these farmers into consideration, as well," said Justice Mookherjee.

Heading: Five blackbucks found dead in Kanpur Zoo - Indian Express
Content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's dreams for industrialisation is gasping at the altars of Nandigram and Singur.

His call for a better work culture, at least in government offices, also took a beating on Thursday in his very secretariat, the Writers' Buildings. The Mahakaran Sangram Committee — an umbrella organisation comprising eight state government employees' unions of the opposition parties — resorted to dharnas, processions, deputations and a pen-down strike, demanding for the right to hold rallies in the building at all hours. As a result, there was no work at the backyard of Bhattacharjee's own office.

The chaos peaked on Thursday with processions taken out by the unions as members marched through various departments and corridors of the state secretariat. A pen-down strike was simultaneously on from 10 am in the morning to 2 pm in the afternoon.

The agitating employees tried to barge into the protected area, with many of them jostling with a handful of policemen. The police, led by Deputy Commissioner (Central), Damayanti Sen, had to resort to a lathicharge to control the secretariat employees from gatecrashing and entering the protected area. "At least 10 employees and several policemen, including Damayanti Sen, were injured," said Home Secretary Asok Mohan Chakrabarti.

Finance Minister Asim Dasgupta, who was leaving for Delhi in the afternoon and was a witness to the chaotic scenes, said: "I will have a word with the Chief Minister about this."

On Wednesday, Chief Secretary Amit Kiran Deb had issued a circular, copies of which were released to the press on Thursday, stating that it was mandatory for the employees' unions to take a prior permission for taking out rallies in the state secretariat. Such rallies can be allowed only during the lunch hour and with prior approval of the authorities, the circular added. "We are not going to abide by this circular. Neither will the Coordination Committee members," said Sanket Chakrabarty, joint secretary of the Mahakaran Sangram Committee.

Interestingly, a large number of those dissenting, belong to the Coordination Committee of the state government employees — backed by the CPM. On Thursday, these members however did not participate in the rally but sympathised with the pen-down since morning.

On September 9, Swapan Maitra, an assistant secretary in the Finance department, was allegedly manhandled by a section of the employees during a scuffle. He was targeted because he had issued showcause notices to six employees of the Finance department for their participation in a dharna during office hours on August 19.

That was the day it all started. The Mahakaran Sangram Committee took out a procession on August 19, and followed it up with demonstrations every day since then, demanding the cancellation of the Fifth Pay Commission. They also wanted the pay scales of state government government employees revised.

On Wednesday, Dasgupta had also announced he would set up a one-member committee to probe the scuffle. "We will not allow work culture at Writers' Buildings to be disturbed. Departmental action will be taken against those who violated discipline," he had said.

Heading: Soon, students to appear for GDs, interviews for MBA - Indian Express
Content:
Five blackbucks were found dead in Kanpur Zoo late on Tuesday night. Prima facie, the deaths appeared to have been caused by to respiratory failure and problems in blood circulation.

While samples of food, along with water and portions of intestines of the bucks have been sent to the Institute of Vetenary Research of India in Bareilly, a three-member team has been formed to probe the incident.

The keeper of the enclosures of the black bucks at the zoo — Ravindra Yadav and the food distributor Ramnaresh — have been suspended. According to forest officials, the black bucks showed no signs of external injury when they were found dead. The postmortem report found blood clots in the heart, lungs, pancreas and kidneys of the bucks.

Heading: Courts not safe enough, trials begin inside jails - Indian Express
Content:
Admission to the management colleges of the state is going to be tough from the next academic session.

Following the pattern of the Common Admission Test (CAT), the Uttar Pradesh Technical University (UPTU) has decided to introduce group discussions and interviews after the written test to select candidates.

Besides, UPTU will hold separate entrance examination for management courses. Earlier, entrance examinations for BTech and MBA courses were held jointly under Uttar Pradesh State Entrance Examinations (UPSEE).

Under the new process, the university will conduct a written test for over 11,000 management seats in December for 2009-10 session. Engineering entrance exams for the same session will be held in April-May 2009.

UPTU Vice-Chancellor (V-C) Professor Prem Vrat said: "A written test evaluates only the conceptual knowledge of a student, group discussions and interviews will assess communication skills, social awareness and personality of a candidate."

The candidates who clear the written test will be called for a group discussion and interview at 10 centres across the state. "Marks of all the three exams will be added to prepare the merit list. The process will take two to three months and by then the merit list of engineering entrance examination will also be declared. Following which, counseling for both MBA and BTech courses will be held simultaneously," he added.

The V-C maintained that the new admission pattern will help the university to produce quality managers and enable them to get better jobs.

He also added that focus on group discussions will motivate the candidates to groom their personality.

"Prestigious management institutions like IIMs also follow the same pattern and they produce good results," said the professor. 

The proposal regarding the new examination procedure has been approved by the university's academic council and soon it will be tabled before the executive council for final approval.

He added, "The university has upgraded the MBA syllabus from the present session by adding a new subject — Principles and Practices of Management Course."

Earlier, there was no such subject to teach concepts of management and latest developments to students, said Vrat.

Heading: CM makes surprise visit to Secretariat, finds only 1 official - Indian Express
Content:
Trials of alleged terrorists began inside the Lucknow District Jail premises on Thursday. During the first such trial, two cases of terror accused Jalaluddin alias Babu Bhai and Mohammed Yaqub were heard. 

District Government Counsel Ram Saran Dwivedi said: "After several incidents of manhandling alleged terrorists and their lawyers in the court premises, I and the Lucknow senior superintendent of police sent a letter to the Lucknow District Judge. We sought the permission to conduct the trials of terror accused inside the jails." The district judge then sought the opinion of the High Court. After receiving the HC approval on August 26, the judge sent a letter to the District Jail authorities, apprising them of the High Court consent to hold trials inside the jail.

All the 26 cases of terror accused running in different courts of Lucknow were transferred to Special Judge Satish Chandra Singh. It was decided that the judge will hold court once a week inside the jail.

During the hearing on Thursday, the court directed the defence lawyers to appear before the court during the next hearing on September 18. 

A courtroom has been constituted inside the jail. "Several arrangements are needed to furnish this court. We have requested the state government for financial help," said Dwivedi. 

He claimed that Rs 1 lakh has been sanctioned for the renovation of the courtroom but the money has not been released. "I will approach advocate general and principal secretary (home) to release the amount."

On August 12, two lawyers A M Faridi and Mohammed Shoeb were manhandled in the court premises in Lucknow by a group of advocates for taking up the cases of terror accused. After the incident, the lawyers moved the Lucknow bench of the Allahabad Court seeking security cover.

* June 21, 2007: Alleged HuJI militant Yaqub was arrested by the Special Task Force from Hussainganj area and 4.5 kg of RDX was seized from him.
* June 23, 2007: HuJI area commander Jalaluddin alias Babu was arrested from Wazirganj area with explosives. He is currently lodged in a Delhi jail. His lawyer, A M Fareedi said: "He was taken to Delhi by the police a few weeks ago." Jalaluddin was also allegedly involved in the kidnapping of owner of Khadim shoe company, Partho Burman in Kolkata.

Heading: SC calls for records in Hewra college fund scam - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Mayawati decided to pay a surprise visit to the Secretariat on Thursday.

She sneaked into the various rooms on the fifth floor of the annexe building. And Mayawati was surprised at what she saw, or rather did not see — her officers.

Of the eight top officials in her Secretariat, including the cabinet secretary, three principal secretaries and four secretaries, only one principal secretary, V K Sharma, was present at 9.45 am when Mayawati visisted the Secretariat.

In her three-hour inspection, the axe fell on the chief management officer of the Secretariat annexes for poor sanitation in the building. Other erring officers were shown the yellow card.

Much to the surprise of the chief minister, none of her personal staff including her private secretary and personal assistants were present in the office.

The surprise visit sent the officers in a tizzy.

One of Mayawati's secretaries, Navneet Sehgal, considered as her political troubleshooter faced the wrath, when he was trying to reach his office by stairs as the lifts were closed down on her order, according to an eyewitnesses.

The fifth floor office of the secretariat houses Cabinet Secretary Shashank Shekhar Singh, Principal Secretaries J N Chamber, Ravindra Singh and V K Sharma.

After the inspection, she held a meeting with her secretaries and other top officials of the government. Mayawati divided the work among her secretaries and allotted two divisions to each officer who will supervise the development work and flood relief programme.

Heading: After Rahul, chief secy rushes to flood-hit areas - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Thursday gave the Uttar Pradesh government four weeks to submit all records pertaining to alleged misappropriation of funds given to the Chaudhray Charan Singh Degree College at Hewra in UP's Etawah district from former chief minister Mulayum Singh's contingency fund in 2003.

Appearing before the Bench comprising Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan and Justice P Sathasivam, D K Garg, counsel for petitioner Manendra Singh Rai, alleged: "They (state) are in possession of all records with regard to diversion of funds, which is a scam worth over Rs 60 crore."

The petitioner had approached the court challenging the transfer of public funds for a private use.

While three of the respondents, including Joint Secretary, Higher Education have furnished their responses earlier, Mulayam and his brother Shivpal Singh Yadav are yet to file their response.

While the appeal before the apex court challenged the grant-in-aid of about Rs 34.50 crore to the university, the three officers stoutly defended their decision to provide financial assistance.

It was said that the decision was taken in the "wisdom" to provide the educational institution with some extra facilities so as to make it a model institution for the welfare of students in the remote and backward areas.

Heading: Mayawati paves road to Delhi via Bihar - Indian Express
Content:
Following All India Congress Committee general secretary Rahul Gandhi's visit to the flood-affected districts of eastern Uttar Pradesh on Thursday, Chief Minister Mayawati dispatched state Chief Secretary Atul Gupta to the affected areas to supervise the flood relief programme.

Gupta's hands were full for the day as his meetings with secretaries of different state departments were already fixed. On the orders of the chief minister, he had to cancel all meetings and air dashed to Maharajganj. He visited Nichlaul in Maharajganj and conducted an aerial survey of the barrage on Gandak River, located on the Nepal side of the Indo-Nepal border.

Gandhi, after paying a visit to the flood-affected regions in Bihar, visited flood-hit districts in Gorakhpur division. The Amethi MP, who is on a two-day tour of eastern UP, arrived at Deoria by train on Thursday. At the railway station, he was met by Samajwadi Party parliamentarian Akhilesh Yadav, son of Mulayam Singh Yadav. Gandhi also visited Kushinagar, after he was informed that river Narayani was changing its course and turning towards the district. He then reached Gorakhpur, where he flagged off four trucks containing essential commodities for the flood-affected.

On Friday, Gandhi is likely to visit Japanese Encephalities patients at the Baba Raghavdas Medical College.

Heading: Azamgarh clash: senior IPS officers suspended - Indian Express
Content:
After providing a generous flood relief to Bihar, Chief Minister Mayawati announced on Wednesday the names of 36 Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) candidates who will contest from Bihar in the next Lok Sabha polls.

Working on the old political theory that the road to Delhi goes through Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, Mayawati, after acquiring a comfortable status for her party in the state, is concentrating on Bihar, which has 40 Lok Sabha seats.

So far, the BSP, which has been contesting Lok Sabha elections in Bihar since 1991, has not been able to win any seat there. This time, however, the party is entering the Lok Sabha fray keeping an eye on the Centre. "We will make a mark in Bihar. This will help us to reach the Centre," said a senior BSP leader.

The party in-charge of Bihar, Gandhi Azad, said: "At any place, first time the party contests the election to ensure that its ideologies reach the people. The second time, it aims at defeating the main rivals. While victory comes in the third stint, the fourth election is fought to assume power." In the last Lok Sabha elections, BSP could not win any seat in Bihar, though at 10 constituencies, its candidates came second. Next year, it will be BSP's fourth Lok Sabha election in Bihar.

At present, the party has 17 Lok Sabha seats, all from Uttar Pradesh. It now aims at bagging 80 seats across the country in the 2009 elections.

The party is already busy campaigning through its three-point Janhit Chetna Andolan, under which, demonstrations and public meetings are taking place in each district of Bihar. "The party strategy is clear — tell the public how during the July trust vote, Congress and BJP had developed an understanding to restrict Mayawati from becoming the Prime Minister," said Gandhi.

Besides, since the BSP had strongly opposed the nuclear deal, the party is also telling the public, that the Congress has misguided the nation on the deal. Inflation is another issue, which BSP is raising in Bihar.

The Bihar BSP in-charge said: "The public is grateful to Behenji. People feel if she has done so much being the chief minister of a neighbouring state, how much she would do when she becomes the Prime Minister?"

Heading: Traders ‘harassed’ by minister’s men - Indian Express
Content:
Following the communal tension in Azamgarh last Sunday, the state government suspended on Thursday the then Director Inspector General of Police Abhimanyu Tripathi and Senior Superintendent of Police V K Garg of Azamgarh.

The senior officers have been held responsible for their laxity and poor handling of the situation following the recent attack on BJP parliamentarian from Gorakhpur Yogi Adityanath's convoy.

This came after, Inspector General (IG) Varanasi Zone, Praveen Singh had conducted a probe that found the officers accountable for not issuing instruction for deployment of force during the visit of the MP, ignoring the sensitivity of the situation in the area.

Principal Secretary (Home) Kunwar Fateh Bahadur Singh and DGP Vikram Singh had visited Azamgarh on Tuesday to take the stock of the situation. The role of other officials concerned in the district too was under scanner, said the top officials.

"Directives had already been issued to keep a close watch on activities in the hyper-sensitive areas in view of the blasts occurred in other states," said the DGP.

"The DIG and the SSP failed to execute their duties properly and showed a lackadaisical approach in handling the situation," added the DGP.

On the other hand, a report regarding the role of Azamgarh District Magistrate Mayur Maheshwari in the violence was lying with the government and a decision will be taken in this regard soon, said Kunwar Fateh Bahadur Singh.

Following the attack on Yogi Adityanath's convoy in Kotwali area on Sunday, the state government had transferred Tripathi and Garg.

The attack had sparked violence as the groups of two different communities had entered in a clash causing the death of one person and injuring several others.

Heading: Sadhvi murder accused still on the run - Indian Express
Content:
Over a dozen traders, who have shops at 30-A M G Marg, have alleged that they are being harassed and intimidated at the behest of Nand Gopal Gupta alias Nandi, a Cabinet minister in the state government. They claimed that following the instructions of Gupta, the Civil Lines police, power department officials and sales tax officials have been asking them to vacate their shops.

The 30-A M G Marg, spreading across several thousand meters, is situated at the heart of the city in Civil Lines and is a prime commercial land. The land is owned by Veera D Gandhi but it is alleged that she has an agreement with some builders patronised by Gupta.

Nearly 25 traders are running their business on the rented premises, of which 13 have been asked to close down their shops.

Tehzeen Khan, who runs a furniture shop in the area, said: "A fortnight ago, some associate of the minister came to my home and asked me to immediately vacate the shop, failing which I was threatened of dire consequences."

Other shopkeepers including Riyaz Ahmad and Ram Babu Chaurasiya said the police, including the former inspector of the Civil Lines police station, V K Srivastava had visited their shops and asked them to meet Gupta. "We have been running shops here since 1970 and have been paying the rent properly to the land owner," said Riyaz.  

On Thursday, the shopkeepers led by Congress leader Sanjay Tiwari and Samajwadi Party leader Mohd Khalid met the Divisional Commissioner D N Dubey and submitted him a memorandum against the harassment caused to the traders by the minister's aides. The leaders also warned to stage a massive demonstration at the collectorate if the police used force to vacate the premises.       

Denying these charges, Gupta (33) said, "I have no connection with the land. Samajwadi Party is trying to defame me and BSP." He alleged that these leaders were after him because he has become a Cabinet minister at such an young age.

Gandhi's advocate S K Srivastava said the landowner had some dispute with the shopkeepers regarding rent because some of them including Tehzeen Khan and Sidhir Gupta have not paid the rent for several months.

Heading: Forgery, corruption case against former SRA chiefs for allowing illegal construction - Indian Express
Content:
A 60-year-old man accused of murdering 'sadhvi' Chitkalanand Giri in the Anandvan Ashram at Kandivili (45) in August this year has led the police on a wild goose chase from Chembur to other states. The reason being that the man, identified as Padmanabh, who had been staying at the ashram for the past four years had given different accounts of his origin to people he came in contact with.

A police official, who is part of the team conducting the man-hunt for the accused, says on conditions of anonymity, "I have been visiting the ashram almost every day to get more information about him, but every second person I speak to at the ashram tells me a different story about his origins." According to the police one inmate of the ashram had been told by Padmanabh that he had been an engineer working with a company in North India before becoming a monk, whereas another inmate had been told that Padmanabh has his origins in South India. "Despite having deployed officials to different locations in the country, we have still not managed to trace him," said the official.

The body of 'sadhvi' Giri was discovered on August 10 at around 4:30 am by Swami Kashikandji Patel Maharaj (84), the main priest of the Anandvan Ashram in Kandivali. The body was lying in a pool of blood on the floor of his room. Giri, who had been a member of the ashram for the past ten years, had been staying with the Maharaj for the last one month before the incident to look after the health of her guru.

According to ashram inmates, she used to handle administrative and financial duties at the ashram and had got into a dispute with Padmanabh over an issue of Rs 200 which the latter had been demanding as part of his salary. According to the same official, Padmanabh had been mysterious about his origins from the beginning. The police also suspect that he may have a criminal background.

Heading: No entry for pets in lifts, Vashi housing society tells residents - Indian Express
Content:
A case of forgery and corruption has been registered against former CEOs of Slum Rehabilitation Authority (SRA) Debhashish Chakrabarty and Ujjwal Uke for allegedly allowing an impostor posing as an architect and builders to carry out illegal construction work in the slums of Koldongri in Andheri, suburban Mumbai.

The case has been also registered against directors of Global Buildcon Constructions, Anand Rao and Samer Jani, for carrying out construction work in the slums without getting clearance from the Department of Environment and Forest.

Jani is also one of the prime accused in the infamous Telgi fake stamp paper scam and was recently chargesheeted.Magistrate RK Shaikh has directed the police to conduct the investigations and submit the 'investigation report' before the court within two months.

According to the complainant Gangaram Sawant, Global Buildcon along with Tirupathi Balaji Co-operative Housing Society had ventured into SRA housing project in 2001. Nearly 450 families were to be rehabilitated under this project.

But according to the complainant, no clearance was obtained from the Ministry of Environment and Forest. In his complaint, Sawant had produced the tampered copies in which the builders, along with the architect, had also changed the names of the members of the society.

Interestingly, none of the members mentioned in the list ever resided in the slums. Sawant has alleged that the architect Jatin Shah was indeed not a professional architect and was running a firm without possessing any degree.

"Shah has nearly 15 such projects sanctioned by the SRA across the city. All these projects are underway and in a few projects complaints of discrepancies are registered, but SRA has not initiated any action," said Sawant's advocate Anjali Iyer.

Observing that the forgery had taken place in connivance with the builders and the alleged architect, the court has also directed a criminal case to be lodged against the members of the society.

Sawant has alleged that despite having complete knowledge of the scam, SRA persuaded the BMC to issue the TDR. However, denying the allegations, Debhashish Chakrabarty (now chief electoral officer of Maharashtra ) said, "Whenever a complaint is filed, it's the senior official who is made the accused, hence an FIR is registered. Now it is for the present SRA CEO to look into the matter. I will not be in a position to comment."

Meanwhile, Ujjwal Uke and Anand Rao refused to comment.

The society which was formed in 2001 was granted Letter of Intent (LoI) in 2005. Whereas, Transfer of Development Rights were granted in 2008. The building is in a shambles and no possession has been granted to people.

Heading: Police Commissioner seeks six months more to demolish all illegal police chowkies - Indian Express
Content:
Says odour may be harmful to health; SPCA takes up issue

Life for 11-year-old Peter-Pan alias Shimu, a Labrador Retriever, has become tougher than ever. Shimu stays with his owners, Ajay and Nandini Marathe, on the fifth floor of New Sarvodaya Co-operative Housing Society, at Sector 4 in Vashi. Shimu has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis, an ailment in which the patient suffers from severe joint pain. However, Shimu will now have to use the staircase instead of the lift, as a resolution passed by the general body of the society bars pets from using the building elevator.

On August 3, 2008, the general body resolved to prevent use of lifts by residents accompanied by their pets. According to a notice issued to Marathe and the general body resolution, the society fears that the odour of the pets which is left behind in the lifts, can be hazardous to the life and health of the building residents. In the month of May 2008, the society sought numerous documents certifying the fitness levels of the dog. Marathe, who has a licence for the dog, produced a certificate issued by the Bombay Veterinary College that dog is licenced, vaccinated, healthy and does not suffer from any infectious or contagious disease. The Bombay Veterinary College certificate also adds that since the dog is aged and suffering from osteoarthritis, it should be allowed to use the lift, as climbing the stairs would be a painful task.

Marathe tried to find a way out by using air fresheners after the use of lift by the pet dog. However, the society officer tersely told Marathe that use of air fresheners was not recommended.

After a complaint of Marathe, the Society for Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (SPCA) has taken up the issue. S B Kadam, assistant secretary, SPCA said, "SPCA inspectors have paid a visit to the society and asked the office bearers to be practical and permit use of lift for the pet dog concerned. We will be hearing from them soon."

Marathe said, "I paid the watchman from the neighouring building to carry the dog up and down the building thrice a day so that he could answer nature's call. This arrangement worked fine for a few days, however he stopped coming after being warned by society office bearers."

Meanwhile, Marathe has temporarily shifted Shimu to his in-laws place at Pen in Raigad district. Chairman of the housing society Arvind Palwankar said, "It is a very old sick dog with a bad odour. We only prevented Marathe from using the lift. Moreover, Marathe is a nuisance as he relentlessly complains against the society to the authorities about all things trivial."

What the law says
dvocate Rahul Thakur who is associated with In Defense of Animals (IDA) said that the society resolution violates section 11 (3) of Prevention of Cruelty to Animal Act 1960. It is also against article 51 A (g) of the Indian Constitution according to which it is the duty of every citizen to have compassion for animals, living creatures and improve the natural environment. Thakur said, "The society resolution is illegal as it is unconstitutional."

Heading: Residents  claim  ‘drunk’ cop misbehaved with them - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai police commissioner on Thursday filed an affidavit with the High Court seeking another six months to entirely demolish the 117 illegal police chowkies in the city.

Despite the earlier orders of the Court, the demolitions could not be carried out because of the recent terrorist attacks on neigbouring states, the Ganesh festival and Ramzaan during which the city was on high alert. A division bench of Justice Bilal Nazki and Justice Ashutosh Kumbhkoni, while granting the plea, also appointed Additional Solicitor General, Rajendra Raghuvanshi, as amicus curie to the court. The HC had on January 9, ordered the police to demolish a total of 137 police chowkies which were built on land meant for public utility. The affidavit filed by Mumbai police commissioner, Hassan Gaffor, in the court on Thursday, said, "In all, till now only 20 police chowkies have been demolished which were on road and footpath. The rest will be done within six months and thus time should be granted." The HC had asked the authorities to pull down the illegal chowkies following a public interest litigation filed by Khar resident, Indur Chhugani (59), a mechanical engineer and a businessman, last September, seeking that illegal beat chowkies be demolished and police exercise restrain while accepting any kind of gift from the private parties. The HC had, in response to a petition filed by Chugani, given the police commissioner a last chance to file a detailed status report on the demolitions.

Heading: Octroi collection sees 18 per cent jump - Indian Express
Content:
For the predominantly Muslim residents of the Vazir Glass Compound in Andheri who celebrate Ganesh Chaturthi every year, memories of this year's festival will be coloured by an ugly incident.

Claiming that an off duty policeman lathi-charged and abused the participants of the procession on the night of September 9 because they were apparently bursting loud crackers, the residents have now taken their complaint to the local deputy commissioner of police.

Momina Pangarkar (50), one of the residents of the locality and an eyewitness to the incident says, "We had taken the Ganesh procession out of the compound at around 9 pm and were crossing the road near Natraj cinemas when a drunk person, in civilian clothes, identifying himself as inspector Suhas Raikar from the Andheri police station, accosted and started abusing us. He even hit a few youths in the procession with a lathi that he was carrying." Another youth from the procession, Sadiq Ali Sheikh (19) says, "When asked why he was misbehaving with us, he started accusing us of drinking alcohol and obstructing traffic. We are also observing Ramzan, so where is the questioning of us drinking?" According to Sheikh, after hitting some of the members of the procession, he called a police jeep and took them to the police station.

In response, the rest of the procession also turned up at the police station and after many entreaties with the police personnel, the four youths along with some of the band members who were detained were released around midnight.

Despite repeated attempts, Police Inspector Raikar was unavailable for comment.However, DCP KMM Prasanna (Zone 10) confirmed that residents approached him with their complaint in writing on Thursday morning.

Prasanna said that he has asked the ACP of the area to conduct an enquiry into the allegations. "I have spoken to the residents of the locality who had come to meet me today and have directed my subordinates to take down their statements. From what I know so far, Raikar stays in the area where the incident took place and he was apparently disturbed by the loud crackers they were bursting. I have also got to know that he was off duty at the time. But as far as the allegations regarding his misbehaviour with the people in the procession is concerned, it won't be right to comment on it before the inquiry is concluded."

Heading: HC directs State to start Panvel court in four weeks - Indian Express
Content:
After systematically carrying out raids at various godowns and introducing reform measures, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation has seen an 18 per cent jump in its octroi collection this financial year. However, the rise is two per cent less as compared to last year. While the octroi collection between April to September this year has been Rs 2049.94 crore, the collection last year during the same period was 1686.79 crore. There has been a jump of Rs 363.15 crore.

"There is evasion of octroi charges on goods which are directly stored in godowns. We raided such godowns and collected octroi," said joint municipal commissioner, V Radha. She added that goods, especially dry fruits on which octroi are generally evaded, were difficult to catch until now. "Dry fruits attract large octroi fees and are usually hidden with other consignments. We raided such dry fruit godowns in the city, which has also added to the rise."

The frequent raids, civic officials added made other octroi evaders pay their dues. Introduction of the Silver cards last month to encourage cashless transactions is also showing results. "Under this system, by swiping the card the transaction gets loaded. The card acts as a substitute for money. This pilot project has been a success and we plan to replicate the same in other areas too," said Radha.

BMC claims that this project has also helped in reducing vehicle queues and traffic snarls, as the vehicles do not have to wait in line to exchange money.

Heading: Court convicts two gangsters for illegal possession of weapons - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court on Thursday directed the state government to provide necessary facilities for setting up a residential place for Additional District Judge at Panvel within four weeks and to start the Panvel district court at the earliest.

A division bench of chief justice Swatanteer Kumar and Justice A P Deshpande passed the orders while hearing a public interest litigation filed by lawyer Rahul Thakhur, President of Panvel Taluka Bar Association, who stated that even after 13 years a court had not been set up in Panvel.

The petition also stated that the High court had issued a directive in 1992 saying that a separate sessions court must be set up in Panvel, as it was observed that 60 per cent of cases filed at the Alibaug sessions court was from Khalapur, Pen, Karjat, Panvel, and Uran talukas. Hence, setting up a sessions court in Panvel was necessitated and it would ensure that the time of the litigants would be saved as they have to travel all the way to Alibaug from distant places now, the petition stated.

District session judges and registrar general who went to Panvel had submitted a report recently saying that there was no residential place for the judge who would be appointed. Later, the High Court sent a proposal to the state government to set up a residential place for the judge. The government, in return, gave the task to the City and Industrial Development Corporation (CIDCO). Though the CIDCO zeroed in on a plot, it later sold the plot as the state government did not file a timely response.

Later, a new proposal was to be sent to the CIDCO but the judge's house was dangling between the Law Department, Public Works Departmet and Revenue Department with each one of them passing off the buck for financing to buy the plot and as a result the residential place has become a distant dream.

Heading: After posting teams to spot flood victims, BMC says no worry - Indian Express
Content:
A Metropolitian Court on Thursday convicted two alleged gangsters for illegal possession of weapons. The accused, along with two other members of a gang, are also accused of attempting to murder senior advocate Majid Memon in July 2005 in a separate case.

The accused, Vicky Sharma and Mukhtar Shaikh, were sentenced to two years in prison by 37th Metropolitian magistrate N Shirimangale under the Arms act, while the rest, Allwyn D'Souza and Glen Peters, were acquitted in the case. The hearing in Majid Memon case is still to be completed.

The Crime Branch had arrested the four alleged member of the Ravi Poojari gang on November 21, 2005 while they were on their way to extort money from a builder. The Unit XI of the Crime Branch said that after receiving a tip-off, it apprehended the four men at a traffic junction in Kandivli while they were in their car.

Following a search, a loaded 7.62 mm pistol and a 0.38 bore revolver was recovered from Sharma and Shaikh respectively. Both are also accused of firing at Memon. While four bullets were seized from the pistol, a lone bullet was found in the revolver. The police also the same night announced that they had cracked the Memon case, after the arrest of the four accused. According to the police Sharma and Shaikh were the two accused who had opened fire at Memon's car in July 2005 outside his house in Bandra. The four have been booked under the stringent Maharashtra Control of Organised Crimes Act (MCOCA) for the offence in the case, and a separate case under section 3 and 25 of the Arms act was slapped on them.

Interestingly, the case had an astonishing twist during the trial when a senior official of the Mumbai Police deposed in court that he had recovered a 9mm bullet from a 7.62 mm pistol and a 0.38 bore revolver. The officer, Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) Ashutosh Dumre, who is the sanctioning authourity, had said that he went through all the evidence and sanctioned their prosecution under the Arms Act for the recovery of weapons and bullets from them.

However, when defence lawyer Santosh Deshpande cross examined Dumre, he admitted that it was highly impossible to find a 9mm cartridge from a 0.38 bore revolver or 7.62 mm pistol. "The same admission was made by ballistics expert Pramod Misal from the police forensics lab at Kalina. While the investigating officer, Hemant Patil, testified in the court that he did not remember what caliber weapons were seized on the day of the arrests, he did know that the bore size of the pistol and bullet must match," said Deshpande.

Heading: Remains of immersion to be recycled - Indian Express
Content:
After posting teams at railway terminuses to keep a check on people coming from the flood-hit Bihar, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) said there was no need for Mumbaikars to worry about epidemics.

"There has been no increase in patients in the civic hospitals," said Executive Health Officer Dr Jairaj Thanekar. The civic body had set up teams and posted them at CST, Bandra and Lokmanya Tilak terminuses. While as many as 155 patients from Bihar were spotted at LT terminus, seven and four people were identified at CST and Bandra respectively.

With lakhs of people affected in the ravaging Kosi floods and left homeless, the BMC had flung into action fearing many flood-affected people would be moving to Mumbai for a safe shelter.

The civic administration's move to detect patients and provide medication was criticised by the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena that believed the BMC was going out of its way to take care of the flood-affected people coming from Bihar.

Municipal Commissioner Jairaj Phatak, however, defended the civic body's decision.

Heading: HC asks railways to file affidavit regarding steps taken to help accident victims - Indian Express
Content:
PoP, accumulated in artificial lakes, will be turned into bricks or tiles

The eco-friendly gesture of immersing Ganpati idols in artificial lakes does not end there. The plaster of paris, accumulated in these lakes, will be used for manufacturing bricks or tiles and will not be re-immersed in the sea. Mayor Shubha Raul, who has strongly advocated the cause of eco-friendly festival, said that all the POP idols from the artificials lakes will be compulsorily recycled.

"All the devotees have responded positively and extended their support to go ahead with the recycling process," Raul said.

Last year, IIT Bombay, in its report on eco friendly Ganeshotsav, had recommended that remains of POP idols can be made into bricks. However, civic officials had rejected the idea calling it "insensitive and hurting religious sentiments."

"There is nothing insensitive in recycling the remains of idols. Instead of letting the disfigured idols accumulate on the beaches, it is better that some good use is made of POP," the mayor said.

Pestom Sagar Citizens Association, Chembur, over the last six years, has been carrying out the immersion in artificial lake and recycling the idols. "We will soon hold a workshop on idol recycle and converting them into bricks. Those devotees who had immersed the idols in artificial lakes will be given the option of keeping the brick as a momento of the lord or else it will be used in construction projects," Raul said.

Remains of the idols made in natural soil 'Shadu' will be used in gardening and landscaping in the civic gardens, civic officials said.

Raul had invited controversy and wrath of her own party members and president Uddhav Thackeray for her remarks that mandals should reduce the idol heights and that they be made in natural soil. She had also said that idol immersion in the sea should be banned to prevent marine pollution. Since then, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation, in co-ordination with citizens groups, had set up artificial lakes at 20 places. Out of the 1.34 lakh idols, a total of 6,706 idols were immersed in these lakes including household and sarvajanik mandals.

"The plan is to ensure that all the household idols should be immersed in artificial lakes and not sea. Devotees have responded positively and hopefully the results will be better next year," Raul said.

Heading: Mumbai Police in a spot over Ganesh Utsav celebrations - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court on Thursday asked the railways to file an affidavit stating the steps taken by it to help accident victims in terms of insurance, availability of ambulance services and method of dealing with trespassers meeting with accidents.

A division bench comprising Chief Justice Swatanter Kumar and Justice A P Deshpande directed the railways to file the affidavit by October 16 in the court and adjourned the petition hearing till then. The court passed the direction while hearing a public interest litigation filed by one Sameer Zhaveri who stated that there was an increase in the number of fatalities on the city's suburban rail network that carries over six million commuters every day. Sameer also had met with an accident in which he lost his legs.

The petitioner's lawyer argued that the railways were treating passengers who fell out of running trains as trespassers and refusing to pay compensation. Such passengers should be given insurance benefits, he said.

He also said that ambulance facility was not available at all railway stations, thus leading to a rise in fatalities. The railway's counsel, however, contended that all bonafide passengers, who hold a valid ticket, were insured and after its tribunal considered their applications, they were compensated as per the statutes.

Also, parking areas for ambulances have been allotted outside all railway stations and more railways policemen have been deployed to prevent people from crossing tracks, he said.

The bench then asked the railways to file an affidavit explaining steps taken to deal with trespassers, issues like insurance for passengers and ambulance facility.

Heading: Raul to move court if govt does not back off from move to curtail BMC powers - Indian Express
Content:
In a circular issued in later half of 2007, the Mumbai police had attempted to find out the number of its police stations displaying religious images, in a bid to stop this practice. It was meant to portray an image of a secular, irreligious force that favored no religion. However it seems that personal religious allegiances are a little above rules, for this Ganesh Utsav some police stations have put up pandals. In order to ensure that this does not come in the way of their duty, the cops immerse their idols a day before or after the traditional immersion days. Some such police stations are the D B Marg Police station, VP Road Police Station, Matunga and Sion Police stations.

Most of these pandals are decades old. While DB Marg has been celebrating Ganesh Utsav for at least 30 years with the families of officers putting up various small social events, the pandal at VP road is in its 21st year now. Most of these stations have police lines attached to them and the pandals are usually set with help of the families of the officers.

The Maharashtra government had ordered the police stations to take down all religious photographs last year. A similar move was also attempted by now Maharashtra DGP A N Roy when he was in charge of Pune Police. This was done to remove any doubt regarding the police advocating one religion. The police were also asked not to overtly display any religion in state owned premises.

However, this seems to have been largely ignored in this year's festivities. When asked about the pandals in these police stations, Additional Commissioner of Police (South Region) K Venkatesan said, "Why do you want to bring up this issue now? We can discuss it after September 15 ." For now it looks like the Mumbai police has found itself caught between the faith of its officers and the attempt to portray a secular image.

Heading: CCTVs to eye every movement at Girgaum Chowpatty - Indian Express
Content:
A day after writing a letter to the governor, Mayor Shubha Raul has said the elected representatives of the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) will move court against the state government, if the governor gives his approval for amending the Mumbai Municipal Corporation Act, 1888.

Speaking to reporters on Thursday, Raul said, "It's a conspiracy by the (Congress led) central and state governments to control the functioning of the civic bodies. No municipal corporation or council in the state should accept the decision."

Following the last week's decision to amend the Act, Raul had written a letter asking the state government to stay away from interfering in civic affairs and curtailing its powers. "If governor still gives his approval to amend the Act, we will move court. Even Thane mayor opposed the move and together we will go to court," she said.

Raul said if all the state governments' directives were made mandatory, all the powers of the civic bodies will be curbed and there would be no functions 'for us to do'. "We were not even informed about the directives. We came to know about the decisions only through the newspapers," she said.

Last week, the State Cabinet passed a decision which will allow it to issue directives to the municipal corporations and councils on policy matters, its duties and responsibilities, matters concerning public interest and national and state government programmes and schemes. Currently, it had no such powers and could only cancel the decisions of these local bodies.

The state government will have to amend the Mumbai Municipal Corporation Act, 1888 and it is mandatory to implement reforms prescribed for the local bodies to avail of aid under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) and the Urban Infrastructure Development for Small and Medium Towns (UIDSMT) schemes.

Presently, the recommendations or directives of the state government are tabled in the civic body for seeking approval of the respective committee and the general body before it can be implemented.

Heading: HC asks Chhat Puja organisers to deposit Rs 1 lakh - Indian Express
Content:
BMC's closed-circuit vigil will be on from Sept 13 to 15; no such measures at other 3 immersion points

With terror threats on the rise and mammoth turnouts expected during the final days of the Ganpati immersion, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has beefed up security arrangements at Girgaum Chowpatty. In order to ensure that no untoward incident takes place in the presence of VIPs, ministers and foreign consulates at the immersion point, the civic administration has decided to install CCTV cameras and record every single event at the sea-beach premises from September 13 to 15.

However, no such additional measures will be taken at the city's other three immersion points. Five CCTV cameras will be installed at the Girgaum pandal set up by the civic body — from where the Chief Minister, the Mayor and other leaders will bid adieu to the elephant lord.

"There are more VIPs at Girgaum chowpatty and it has been a traditional immersion point. That's why maximum security measures are being taken there," said Additional Municipal Commissioner Madhav Sangle, who is in charge of the Ganeshotsav arrangements.

He however, added that the CCTV and other security measures will not be taken on such a large scale at the other immersion points. "But there will be security guards to man these areas. The police are also underatking security measures at these points," Sangle said.

Before the last day of immersion — Sunday— the Girgaum chowpatty beach will be monitored by the civic administration. "Since the stage will be ready by Saturday, we want to ensure that no one tampers with it. Immersion goes on till the next day and the recording will, therefore, be conducted till Monday," he said. Seven plasma screens will be installed to monitor the proceedings, Sangle informed.

A total of 37,000 civic employees will be involved in the immersion proceedings at 82 points, including the major ones of Girgaum chowpatty, Shivaji park, Mahim and Juhu. The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation is expecting a considerable rise in the number of idol immersions this year.

Heading: Auditorium bombs: No mention of Hindu outfit in chargesheet - Indian Express
Content:
To ensure compliance with the guidelines laid down by it in 2006, the Bombay High Court on Thursday ruled that all those who wish to organise Chhat Puja will have to compulsorily deposit Rs 1 lakh with the suburban collector. A division bench of Justice J N Patel and Justice K K Tated gave the direction while hearing a petition filed by Krishna Kumar Ganga Prasad Agnihotri who had approached the court seeking relaxation of the earlier HC order.

On October 19, 2006, the HC had ruled that there should be no involvement of political parties in the Chhat Puja and no parties should erect a platform on beachfronts. The court had also restrained the organisations performing puja from putting up publicity material like banners or posters. In addition, the HC had imposed restrictions on the use of mikes, loudspeakers and amplifiers during the puja.

The 2006 order was passed on a public interest litigation filed by NGO Save Juhu Beach Committee seeking beautification of the beach following which the court had restrained the use of beach for entertainment and commercial purposes. On Thursday, the bench refused to modify the order stating that they had no powers as the order was passed by another bench.

Shiraz Rustomjee, counsel for the NGO, said that even last year another organiser had sought relaxation of the order which was rejected. The organiser had then approached the Supreme Court where the matter is pending.

Public prosecutor Niranjan Pandit said that the police would grant permission to organise the Chhat Puja after following due process of law. In the PIL, the NGO had stated that the puja is actually supposed to be a family function, however, it is being used by politicians to gain political mileage.

Heading: ‘I did not run away’ - Indian Express
Content:
The state Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) investigating the planting of improvised explosive devices at auditoriums in Thane, Vashi and Panvel earlier this year filed a chargesheet against the six arrested accused at the Mazgaon Metropolitan Magistrates Court on Thursday. According to the ATS, while the chargesheet makes no mention of any role played in the terrorist conspiracy on the part of the Sanatan Sanstha — a Hindu revivalist organisation to which the arrested accused were affiliated — further investigations would continue in the matter.

The chargesheet runs into 1,020 pages, with a total of 195 witnesses including police officials named by the ATS. The six arrested accused — Ramesh Hanumant Gadkari (50), Vikram Bhave (26), Mangesh Dinkar Nikam (34), Santosh Angre (26), Hemant Chalke (27) and police patil  Hari Bhau Divekar (44) — have been charged with attempt to murder, criminal conspiracy, causing disappearance of evidence and causing damage to property, under the Indian Penal Code, as well as sections of the Arms Act, the Explosive Substances Act, and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act. There are no wanted accused mentioned in the chargesheet.

"In our chargesheet we have not mentioned any involvement of the Sanatan Sanstha or its branch, the Hindu Janjagruti Samiti, though the arrested accused were its members. However, our investigations will continue in the matter, and if we find any evidence to suggest a role played by the organisation, we will take necessary action and file a supplementary chargesheet," said Senior Police Inspector BB Rathod of the ATS.

According to the chargesheet, Gadkari and Bhave were the prime conspirators, and they assembled the bombs with the help of Nikam. The conspiracy was hatched at Panvel and in Warsai village in Pen.

"The motive of the accused mentioned by us in the chargesheet is that they wanted to deter the public from watching the play Aamhi Pachpute and the film Jodhaa Akbar and producers from screening them. They felt that the play and the movie were an affront to Hindu sentiments and that they parodied Hindu deities," said Rathod.

On June 16, the ATS arrested Gadkari and Nikam, both members of the Sanatan Sanstha and the Hindu Janjagruti Samiti, in connection with the crude bomb planted at Vishnudas Bhave auditorium in Vashi on May 31, and the bomb that exploded at Gadkari Rangayatan auditorium in Thane on June 4. They were also suspected to be involved in the small explosion that took place at a Panvel theatre screening the film Jodhaa Akbar on February 20.

Heading: Raj accepts Amitabh apology, turns guns on ‘Jaya of police’ K L Prasad - Indian Express
Content:
Haywood says he loves India, questioned by ATS

The Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) today questioned US national Kenneth Haywood, who left India last month while being investigated in connection with the Ahmedabad bomb blasts e-mail sent from his internet account, even as the American claimed that he had not run away and that he loved India and its people.

Haywood, who surprised authorities by returning to the city after midnight on Wednesday by a British Airways flight from London, spent three hours at the ATS office this afternoon and was accompanied by his lawyer and a representative of the church he is associated with. ATS officials said that they recorded his statements in connection with his reported allegation that an ATS officer had asked him for a bribe before he fled India. In his statement to the ATS, Haywood claimed that the entire story was fabricated by the media which reported it.

"We are taking a legal view on the matter and...will question Haywood if need be," ATS additional commissioner of police Parambir Singh Singh said, adding that computers seized from Haywood had been returned to him as tests on the hard drive did not produce any evidence. Singh also said that a separate agency could probe Haywood leaving the country despite a Look Out Notice for him. During the terror e-mail investigation, Haywood had given a written assurance that he would not leave the city until the probe was complete, Singh said and added that the ATS would inquire later why he "left in such a hurry".

Haywood refused to speak to reporters after his visit to the ATS office. Instead, he took pictures of the waiting media on his mobile phone and asked reporters if they did not have "any news" to cover today. However, in an interview to a TV channel, he said that he had gone to the US last month as he had never been a suspect and did not see any reason to be staying here.

"After we returned to the states, I started hearing from the press that we had run away. If that was the case, I would not have come back," he said. "We are staying on. That's the plan. We are staying on. We love India. We love the people of India. We came here to try and make a difference."

Haywood had been subjected to polygraph and brain-mapping tests on August 13. Three computers belonging to Haywood had also been sent for analysis. An interim cyber forensics report indicated that while Haywood's computers were not used to send the e-mail, his WiFi network might have been used as suspected.

The ATS was planning to show him some pictures of blast suspects just a day before he fled the city. Asked if there was a possibility of him being questioned again in connection with the terror e-mail, Singh said, "The investigation in the terror e-mail is very much on. There is no such thing as a clean chit in investigation vocabulary. If there is any evidence at any stage then he will be questioned."

Heading: Braked by politics, Nano fit for road - Indian Express
Content:
MNS chief withdraws agitation, but asks state govt to take serious note of senior police officer's comment that 'Mumbai does not belong to anyone's father'

A day after actor Amitabh Bachchan said that he was apologising if his wife Jaya's (allegedly anti-Marathi) remarks had hurt even a single person's sentiments, Maharashtra Navanirman Sena (MNS) president Raj Thackeray today withdrew his agitation and the ban on movies starring Bachchan family members. However, he launched a new attack — this time on Joint Commissioner of Police K L Prasad for a statement he had made to the media on Wednesday.

Dubbing Prasad the "Jaya Bachchan of the police," Thackeray criticised him for his remark that "Mumbai does not belong to anyone's father" and asked the State government to take serious note of his statement. He also challenged him to take a public survey on the issue within the police force.

Thackeray alleged that Prasad had previously made public statements about "breaking the limbs" of MNS cadre during an earlier "anti-outsider" agitation launched by the party. "If he has an ego of his badge, uniform, and position, he should leave it aside and come down to the streets. Then he will know whose father Mumbai belongs to. An IPS officer should not get involved (in these issues). The State government must take a serious note. A responsible officer entrusted with maintaining law and order is himself breaking the law," Thackeray pointed out.

Despite repeated attempts, Prasad remained unavailable for comment.

"Everyone would have come to know what happens when the Marathi people come together," said Raj, adding that though Jaya had apologised in an interview to a newspaper, the party had been firm on the stance that nothing short of a public apology would suffice.

"Though it was essential for Jaya Bachchan to apologise for her remarks, we have accepted Amitabh Bachchan's gesture to issue the apology after holding a press conference as head of the family. This is a victory of the Maharashtrians," Raj added and called on his cadre and associates to maintain peace.

Alleging that Jaya Bachchan had spoken in Parliament on the issue of making Mumbai a separate state, Thackeray advised her to "stick to written dialogues and not say anything that comes to her mind".

He also reiterated the statement he had made in a speech at a party function at Vikhroli earlier this year — in which he had said that personalities like Amitabh Bachchan, Lata Mangeshkar and Sachin Tendulkar are not bound by territorial boundaries.

"The people of the country see, watch and hear them. Amitabh Bachchan should not be hemmed in boundaries of territory. Keeping personal relations with anyone is his personal question," he had added, noting that Bachchan had acted as brand ambassador for the Uttar Pradesh government.

Thackeray also clarified that the Mumbai police, which had earlier served a gag order on him, had given him permission to address the press conference after he spoke to Commissioner of Police Hasan Gafoor on Wednesday.

Referring to Amitabh Bachchan's blog apology, he opined that it did not have the public outreach of a newspaper or news channel. However, the matter had been cleared after Bachchan's press conference apology, concluded Thackeray.

Heading: This boy writes, that one writhes - Indian Express
Content:
The Nano may still be struggling to clear the political hurdles it is facing in West Bengal, but it came out with flying colours after a lab test in Pune's Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI). Tata Motors' small car met all the requirements to roll out on the Indian roads.

The compliance certificate for the Nano car was issued by the apex central cell of ARAI after various tests. Under Central Motor Vehicles Rules, certification from ARAI is a must before a vehicle can be sold in the country.

Sources in ARAI said the small car had met all the specified criteria for emission, fuel efficiency, safety, noise, vibration, harshness and others. The Nano fulfils Euro IV emission norms, which is above the current Indian regulatory requirement. During the fuel efficiency test, it reportedly lived up to the 20 km-per-litre mark figure cited by Tata Motors.

The car has one of the smallest engines in the form of two cylinders of 624 cc, and a 33-BHP, rear-mounted, multi-point fuel injection petrol engine.

According to Tata officials, the car can touch a top speed of 105 km/hr and has undergone extensive tests for front, rear and side collisions that fulflil its safety aspect. The seating system has been made by Tata Johnson Controls Automotive Ltd. The seats are of low cost but with high comfort.

One of the key highlights of the Nano is that it is coming out with a higher plastic content than in most other cars. The Interiors and Plastics Division based in Pune is supplying Nano various parts including bumpers, instrument panels and trims.

ROADWORTHY
* Emission: Euro-IV compliant
* Fuel efficiency: 20km/litre
* Tank capacity: 30 litres
* Top speed: 105 km/hour
* Other tests: Safety, noise, vibration, harshness standards met

Heading: He’s 10, glued to the TV and convinced the world will end - Indian Express
Content:
He's eight and already an author

Eight-year-old Gurudas Natu, a Maharashtrian mulga (boy) who stays in London, has authored a book titled Helpful Bear and Sports Day, which was released in Pune today.

Gurudas studies in class IV at Belmont Middle School, London. Having developed the habit of writing at the age of six, he has been penning essays, short stories and scripts for drama for some time now.
