Only recently at Kaziranga, animals escaping the flood were hit by vehicles on the highway. "Trains and cars should move at 20 km per hour. When the vehicle moves slowly, it gives the animal some time to react," said UP Principal Conservator of Forests (general) D N S Suman.

National highways run through four tiger reserves : Buxa (West Bengal), Indravati (Chhattisgarh), Pench (MP) and Pench (Maharashtra). State highways run through Bandipur (Karnataka), Corbett (Uttarakhand), Dampa (Mizoram), Melghat (Maharashtra), Nagarjunasagar (Andhra Pradesh), besides Palamau, Panna, Sariska, Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Tadoba-Andhari and Valmiki. That's a total of 15 out of 28 old tiger reserves. This year, 12 new tiger reserves have been given the nod, making it a total of 40 tiger reserves. Of the new reserves, Kaziranga (Assam), Achanakmar (Chhattisgarh), Mudumalai (Tamil Nadu), Sanjay National Park (with a road going through tiger corridor in adjoining Chhattisgarh) have highways going through them.

"We need strict rules set down by the Centre. Clearly, the vehicles which are killing the tigers are very large ones, moving at high speed," said Belinda Wright, executive director, Wildlife Protection Society of India. Others opine that merely setting speed limits will not achieve anything. " Many of the vehicles passing through these roads carry contraband. The exit is say 22 km away from the entry, as is often the case, and provides a conducive environ for a poacher to go inside the forest or the contraband to be loaded and unloaded. Even drivers have a problem, as they don't know how to react when they see an animal. Last year in Kaziranga, we put up 70 barriers to slow down the traffic, which is a more effective solution than setting a speed limit that is difficult to enforce. There should also be a helpline number, which a driver can call if he comes across an animal," said Kartick Satyanarayan from Wildlife SOS.

Heading: Anti-defection petitions: HC rap for J’khand Speaker - Indian Express
Content:
The Centre on Thursday told the Supreme Court that the law and order situation in Kandhamal district of Orissa is now under control, and has improved considerably.

Echoing the Centre's response, the state government also assuaged the fears of the Archbishop of Cuttack, Raphael Cheenath, who had approached the apex court early this month seeking a CBI inquiry into the violence that followed VHP leader Laxmanananda Saraswati's murder.

"The response of the state government to such acts of violence has been fast, decisive and unambiguous. As a result of the efforts, the situation in Kandhamal district has been brought under control and no fresh acts of violence have been reported in the past few days," submitted senior advocate K K Venugopal, appearing for the Orissa government.

The Bench of Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan and Justice P Sathasivam also sought to know what facilities were being provided at the relief camps.

The principal secretary, Orissa Home department, Tarun Kanti Mishra, said in his response that 14 relief camps have been opened in eight affected blocks of Kandhamal district. Besides security arrangements, these camps are providing food, water, medicines and clothes, he said. According to the affidavit, 23,800 people have been given shelter in these 14 relief camps as on September 8.

In the detailed reply, the state also categorically opposed any CBI probe in the matter, pointing out that it had already appointed a Commission of Inquiry for the purpose, headed by retired Justice S C Mohapatra.

Heading: Hewra college scam: SC calls for records - Indian Express
Content:
The Jharkhand High Court has sought to know from Assembly Speaker Alamgir Alam when he would decide on pending anti-defection petitions against four ministers in the Shibu Soren Cabinet.

A bench of Chief Justice Gyan Sudha Mishra and Justice D K Sinha on Wednesday directed the Speaker to file an affidavit on September 18 on the petitions lying with him.

The High Court's direction came a month after it served notices to ministers Stephen Marandi, Kamlesh Singh, Bhanu Pratap Sahi and Enos Ekka besides former minister Chandraprakash Choudhary against whom the anti-defection petitions were pending.

The court disposed of the petition against Choudhary saying prima facie the petition against him did not have merit.

One Kuleshwar Singh along with a few others had filed the petitions against them, seeking a High Court directive to the Speaker for speedy decision on the pending petitions.

They also informed the bench that the petitions against the ministers had been pending with the Speaker since 2005 when Inder Singh Namdhari occupied the post.

Alam has reportedly said he is in the process of taking a decision.

Heading: Vigilance books Amarinder, arrest unlikely - Indian Express
Content: The Supreme Court on Thursday gave the Uttar Pradesh Government four weeks to submit all records pertaining to alleged misappropriation of funds given to the Chaudhray Charan Singh Degree College at Hewra in UP's Etawah district from former chief minister Mulayum Singh's contingency fund in 2003.  Appearing before the Bench comprising Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan and Justice P Sathasivam, D K Garg, counsel for petitioner Manendra Singh Rai, alleged: "They (state) are in possession of all records with regard to diversion of funds, which is a scam worth over Rs 60 crore." The petitioner had approached the court challenging the transfer of public funds for a private use. While three of the respondents, including Joint Secretary, Higher Education have furnished their responses earlier, Mulayam and his brother Shivpal Singh Yadav are yet to file their response.

Heading: Court directs police to book SSP for opening fire on protesters in Samba - Indian Express
Content:
Former chief minister Capt Amarinder Singh was today booked by the Punjab Vigilance Bureau under the Prevention of Corruption Act and charges of cheating, forgery, tampering of official records and criminal conspiracy. Former local bodies minister Chaudhary Jagjit Singh, chairman of Amritsar Improvement Trust Jugal Kishore and former secretary of Vidhan Sabha, Nachhatar Singh Mavi were also booked with him.

Vigilance sources revealed that the former CM would not be arrested for now, as has a blanket bail from the High Court. However, the other accused would be arrested soon.

This is the third case registered by the state Vigilance Bureau against Amarinder after the Akali-BJP combine came to power in 2007. The earlier two cases included the Ludhiana Improvement Trust Scam and the disproportionate assets case.

Sources said the case (FIR No 3) was registered at the SS1, Vigilance Bureau Police Station in Mohali, on the reference of the Punjab Vidhan Sabha under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B of the IPC and PC Act. Other accused in the case include Tara Singh, former under secretary in the Vidhan Sabha; Subhash Chander and Vicky Sharma of Veer Colonisers and some unknown persons and government officials.

Heading: Doctors don’t have all the answers: WHO - Indian Express
Content:
A local court on Thursday directed the police to register a case against SSP Prabhat Singh in connection with the death of two persons in police firing in Samba during the Amarnath land agitation.

Acting on the complaint of Chanchal Singh and Khem Raj Pandha, parents of deceased Sanjeev Singh and Sunny Pandha, the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate directed the crime branch to register a complaint under provisions of CrPC and submit a report within 15 days. The SSP has already been transferred from Samba.

The parents have alleged that the SSP opened fire without any provocation. They claimed that the control of the highway was with the Army and the SSP had no right to open fire. They also alleged that he neither issued any warning to the protesters nor did he receive orders from the District Magistrate before opening fire. Instead of aiming below the knee, the SSP aimed at their heads, killing both on the spot, the petition alleged.

Heading: Lalu train halted after scuffle between Rly staff - Indian Express
Content:
A recent report by the WHO attributes social factors for variations in life expectancy.

Sir Michael Marmot, chairman of the Commission on Social Determinants of Health is in New Delhi to meet government representatives. Vidya Krishnan talks to him about social components of health inequities.

•What are the major points in the report?

We rely too much on medical interventions. The toxic combination of bad policies, economics, and politics is a major reason why people do not enjoy the good health that is biologically possible. A more effective way of increasing life expectancy is implementing schemes that improve these factors and ensuring that benefits reach the target audience.

People need the opportunity to take control of their lives — but conditions need to be right.

•How do you hope to implement your findings?

After a three-year analysis, the report has collected evidence, which should help countries close the gap in a generation's time. We are meeting government representatives because we need commitment from the top.

•What challenges does India face?

India is special because each state has different issues. It's important for the Government to set up a monitoring system with the WHO, allocate funds and have an internal discussion about the report's relevance. Self-help groups and NGOs must pressure the governments to achieve targets of health equity.

•When can India claim to have achieved her goals?

When life expectancy in India is the same as Japan.

Heading: Singur committee to miss deadline - Indian Express
Content:
A minor skirmish between an Assistant Commercial Manager and a Ticket Collector at Kanpur Central Railway Station on Thursday morning snowballed into a controversy with the intervention of the Railway Minister Lalu Prasad Yadav who happened to be passing through the station in his special train.

According to TC Amresh Kumar, ACM UNS Prabhakar slapped him when he bowed to touch his feet. Enraged over the alleged misbehaviour, other TCs came in support of Amresh Kumar and stopped the passing trains. Infuriated over the sudden halt, the Railway Minister Lalu Prasad Yadav immediately suspended the ACM for allegedly hitting the TC.

The ACM, on the other hand, claimed that he was simply being friendly and did not hit the TC intentionally. According to sources, after listening to the protesting TCs, the Railway Minister held the ACM guilty of misconduct and placed him under suspension. However, sources said a compromise was reached between the two parties later and the suspension would in all probability not take place.

Heading: BJP executive meet begins today, to tread cautious line on n-deal - Indian Express
Content:
The four-member committee set up to settle the Singur crisis will not be able to meet its seven-day deadline which ends on September 14.

Emerging from the meeting on Thursday, committee head Rabindranath Bhattcharya, the Trinamul Congress MLA from Singur, said: "We will ask for more time from the state Government. We will need a few more sessions. The committee is expected to submit an interim report after seven days," he said.

Meanwhile, Justice Chittatosh Mookherjee, the legal advisor to the West Bengal Governor during the recent talks, said the crisis would become more complex if things are dragged on and a firm decision is not taken immediately. "The issue needs to be settled at the earliest," he said. Though Bhattcharya claimed both sides exchanged their views cordially during the meeting on Thursday, sources in the West Bengal Industrial development Corporation (WBIDC) said they were actually split over the quantum of land to be given from within and outside the project area.

At the meeting, Trinamool Congress representatives demanded that they wanted 300 acres from within the project area. The Government representatives have, however, stuck to their stance saying it was possible to give only 40 acres from within the project area, sources said. "Till today we have tried to convince the Government as to how 300 acres can be carved out of the project area. I don't know whether they are convinced," Bhattcharya said.

The committee would again meet on Friday.

Heading: Unions strike work at Writers’ Building - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP's three-day national executive meeting focusing on crafting a win in election-bound states begins with party president Rajnath Singh's speech on Friday. The party plans to pass two resolutions during the meet — one political and the other on economic issues.

The Indo-US nuclear deal will figure prominently in the political resolution, debates and speeches of both BJP prime ministerial candidate L K Advani and party president Rajnath Singh.

While the BJP had been harping on "we'll renegotiate the nuclear deal when we come to power" before the NSG waiver, the party is expected to tread a cautious line in its resolutions.

While the party will attack the Manmohan Singh Government "for not spending enough time" to clinch a deal "that could have yielded better returns for the country", it will also say "the deal may appear good only if we are reconciled to a junior partner status vis-a-vis the USA".

Both Advani and Rajnath are likely to harp on "how the country stands to lose tremendously by forfeiting the right to conduct nuclear tests in the future".

While Advani will talk about strengthening of the NDA, Rajnath will speak about "why no one in the party is bigger than the organisation". Advani will refer to the UPA Government's "sullied legitimacy in the wake of the cash for votes scam", and various governance-related issues, including "highly uninspiring term of the Congress-led regime of the last five years".

Rajnath is expected to stick to his familiar position on Amarnath, the Ram Sethu and the hanging of Afzal Guru. He is also expected to argue that the very idea of the Muzaffarabad route for cross-border trade "militates against the 1994 Parliament resolution that says India is committed to reclaiming PoK".

Terror strikes, price rise are some of the issues expected to figure both in Advani and Rajnath's speeches. Both the leaders are likely to draw a comparison of the terror strikes during the NDA regime and the UPA regime and how most of the accused in the latter case "have gone unpunished". They are also likely to charge the UPA with "communalising the war on terror" by various actions of the UPA Government and their allies.

After the presidential speech on day one, election-bound states of Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Mizoram will present their respective status reports. The nuclear deal will be debated on day two.

Heading: EC wants J-K polls on time, Cong not keen - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's call for a better work culture in government offices took a beating at Writers' Building, the state secretariat, with Mahakaran Sangram Committee — an umbrella organisation comprising eight state government employees' unions — resorting to dharnas and pen-down strike on Thursday. As a result, there was no work at the backyard of Bhattacharjee's own office.

The chaos at the state secretariat peaked with processions taken out by the unions through various departments and corridors. A pen-down strike was simultaneously on from 10 am to 2 pm.

The agitating employees tried to barge into the protected area, with many of them jostling with a handful of policemen. The police led by Deputy Commissioner of Police (Central), Damayanti Sen, had to resort to a lathicharge to control the secretariat employees from gatecrashing and entering the protected area. "At least 10 employees and several policemen, including Damayanti Sen, were injured," said Home Secretary Asok Mohan Chakrabarti.

Finance Minister Asim Dasgupta who was leaving for Delhi in the afternoon and was a witness to the chaotic scene said: "I will have a word with the Chief Minister about this."

On Wednesday only, Chief Secretary Amit Kiran Deb had issued a circular, copies of which were released to the press on Thursday, stating that it was mandatory for the employees' unions to take a prior permission for taking out rallies in the state secretariat. Such rallies can be allowed only during lunch break and with prior approval of the authorities, the circular added.

"We are not going to abide by this circular. Neither will the co-ordination committee members," said Sanket Chakrabarty, joint secretary of the Mahakaran Sangram Committee.

Interestingly, a large number of those who are dissenting, actually belong to the Co-ordination Committee of the State Government Employees that is backed by the CPI(M).

On September 9, Swapan Maitra, an assistant secretary in the Finance Department, was allegedly manhandled by a section of employees during a scuffle. He was targeted because he had issued show-cause notices to six employees of the Finance Department for their participation in a dharna during office hours on August 19.

On Wednesday, Dasgupta had announced the setting-up of one-member committee to probe the matter. "We will not allow work culture at Writers' Building to be disturbed. Departmental action will be taken against those who flouted discipline," he said.

Heading: Court rejects Amarinder plea for stay on expulsion - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the Election Commission indicated on Thursday that the Jammu and Kashmir Assembly polls would be held on time, the Congress party did not seem very keen on the prospect. The Congress had in a meeting called by the Election Commission on Monday left the decision to the EC and had not expressed any definite views on the matter.

Chief Election Commissioner N Gopalaswamy told The Indian Express that the deadline for the formation of a new assembly was January 9, when six months of Central rule in the state would be over. "Our deadline is January 9. We will hold the elections at an appropriate time," Chief Election Commissioner N Gopalaswamy said.

However, the Congress was learnt to be more inclined towards deferring the elections for a few months. Though the party has not made its stand public, the majority held the view that the situation in the state was still too polarised to hold free and fair elections with substantial representation of the people.

The Jammu and Kashmir Assembly, whose term was to expire in November this year, was dissolved in July following the resignation of Chief Minister Ghulam Nabi Azad and the state brought under President's rule as violent demonstrations over the transfer of a plot of land to the Amarnath Shrine Board engulfed the state.

Though the controversy has subsided for the time being, some political parties are in favour of deferring the polls in order for the situation to return to normal. Gopalaswamy said the Election Commission was holding consultations with every stakeholder and listening to their views but the final decision would be its own. "It is our mandate to conduct elections and we will do it when we feel it is right to do so," he said.

On Monday, the Election Commission had held a meeting of all political parties in a bid to arrive at a consensus on the issue. The Commission followed that up with a meeting with officials from the Home Ministry and the Jammu and Kashmir state administration, including Chief Secretary S S Kapoor and DGP Kuldeep Khoda, on Wednesday.

Meanwhile, a Home Ministry source on Thursday said it was willing to go along with the Election Commission on whatever dates it decided for holding the polls in Jammu and Kashmir. "We will give our inputs but the decision has to be taken by the Election Commission. We will go along with that," the source said.

Heading: No decision yet on Basu’s surgery - Indian Express
Content:
Former chief minister Capt Amarinder Singh today moved the Punjab and Haryana High Court, demanding quashing of the decision to unseat him from the Vidhan Sabha. However, the court turned down his plea for a stay.

The voluminous petition, running into over 500 pages, will come up for hearing tomorrow before a division bench comprising Justice A K Goel and Justice Ajay Tewari.

Amarinder has demanded that the resolution passed by the special house committee indicting him and two others in the Amritsar land case be quashed. Alleging that the law of natural justice has been violated by the Punjab government, he has alleged that he has again been made a victim of political vendetta. Amarinder has also alleged that he was not given a hearing.

Expressing urgency, the counsels for Amarinder kept shuttling from one court to another, as two division benches recused themselves from the petition. Finally, at 3.30 pm, the petition was referred to another division bench by Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur.

Arguing the petition and demanding a stay on the decision of the House, senior advocate Uday Lalit submitted that the House has no powers to order the registration of an FIR and custodial interrogation of Amarinder. "To find someone guilty is not the function of the House. It is the function of the adjudicating machinery of the government. It is the function of the courts. Likewise, to order the custodial interrogation of an individual is the function of the police. Even the Supreme Court has not appreciated the orders wherein the High Court had ordered the custodial interrogation of an accused. Passing such orders is beyond the jurisdiction of the House," he said.

The Court questioned the reason behind the urgency of the case. Making it clear that no notices or stay will be issued at this stage without hearing the parties, the Court deferred the case to Friday.

Heading: Cabinet liberalises FM policy - Indian Express
Content: Doctors on Thursday decided to put on hold any immediate surgical intervention on 94-year-old Marxist patriarch Jyoti Basu for removing a blood clot in the brain. The condition of Basu, who would continue to be on medication for removal of the blood clot, was stable and he had normal diet and sleep, doctors at the private hospital where the former chief minister was admitted last Sunday, said. He might be under observation for some more days, they said. CPI(M) Politburo members Sitaram Yechury, Brinda Karat and Biman Bose visited Basu in the hospital. Yechury said Basu was "100 per cent mentally alert and was talking, in good health and had lighter moments".

Heading: Truncated House session from October 17 - Indian Express
Content:
The Union Cabinet on Thursday approved major changes in the policy for private FM radio phase II, aimed at providing financial flexibility to promote the growth of the FM industry. In a significant policy relaxation, it allowed FM broadcasting companies to create subsidiaries and go in for mergers, demergers and amalgamation of companies by way of transfer of shares.

The Cabinet lifted the earlier restriction on the transfer of shares for the aforesaid purposes within the period of five years of operationalisation of the channel, subject to the condition of the shareholder fulfilling the eligibility criteria.

However, no shareholder will be allowed to change the ownership pattern of the company through transfer of promoters' shares to new shareholders without the written permission of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting within the five year window period.

The relaxations for the creation of subsidiaries and mergers within the same group would be subject to the condition that the promoters must continue to remain the majority shareholders with at least 51 per cent of the total shares. The new entities, thus created, would have to maintain the FDI component as per the norms and the grant of permission agreement.

In addition, not only will the new company (demerged or amalgamated) have to sign a fresh agreement with the Government on identical terms for the remaining license period but the transfer of shares would also be allowed only once during the first five years of operationalisation.

Heading: Sick during trust vote, two BJP MPs now dead - Indian Express
Content:
Coming amidst peak festive season, a truncated session awaits both houses of Parliament when they resume what has been officially termed the "second part of the 14th session" from October 17. According to the tentative calendar, the session would end on November 21.

To start with, the Government has clubbed the monsoon and winter sessions after having dubbed the preceding two-day special session, convened on the directive of the President with the specific agenda of seeking a vote of confidence on July 21 and 22, the "first part" of the 14th session.

On the face of it, Parliament would be in session for 36 days, but in effect, the two Houses would have just 24 sittings. Two holidays, coupled with Saturdays and Sundays, would claim the rest of the 12 days. Of these, the Government would have barely 18 days for pushing through its own business considering that six Fridays would go for catering to private member's bills.

It is not just the short duration which would mark the session. Festivals like Diwali, (scheduled for October 28), Dhanteras and Bhaiya Dooj would be major diversions for members. The festive season provides MPs the best time for PR work in their constituencies. With Lok Sabha elections on everybody's mind, members' priority is anybody's guess.

Heading: 300 per cent pay hike for President, V-P, governors - Indian Express
Content:
BJP MPs Kishan Lal Diler and D C Srikantappa, who had reported sick during the UPA Government's trust vote on July 22, have died since then.

Diler, the BJP MP from Hathras in UP, was admitted to hospital in the Capital after he complained of breathlessness on the day of the trust vote, but was still made to attend Parliament for voting. The MP died of a heart attach in Aligarh on September 3.

"He had complained of cough, cold and breathlessness around the time of the trust vote, that's why we got him admitted. But, after rumours and speculations about his intentions to abstain on the excuse of medical grounds started floating and even senior BJP leaders started calling up, he decided to attend Parliament and vote," said Diler's son-in-law Satpal Chauhan, a doctor at the Ram Manohar Lohia hospital where the MP was admitted on July 22.

Diler returned to RML after the voting and underwent treatment for nearly a week. "He was a committed leader of the party and the rumours that he might switch over were distressing," Chauhan told the The Indian Express.

Earlier this month, Diler complained of exhaustion after returning to Aligarh from a meeting in Lucknow. "He was taken to a private nursing home, which did not provide due medical attention before referring him to the district hospital. He died thereafter," alleged Chauhan.

Another of the sick MPs, D C Srikantappa, who had won the traditional Congress bastion of Chikamangalur for three times for the BJP, passed away on August 4 after a long fight with cancer.

Despite his illness, the BJP had tried hard to get him to vote. Following the BJP leadership's instructions to its chief ministers to get ailing MPs to attend the Parliament, B S Yeddyurappa telephoned Srikantappa and informed him about the party's plans to airlift ailing MPs to Delhi for the trust vote. However, on doctors' advise Srikantappa stayed put.

"The MPs were moved only after getting the advise of the doctors and the consent of the MPs," said BJP spokesperson Ravishankar Prasad when asked if it was advisable to bring sick MPs for voting.

Several other ailing MPs, including former prime minister A B Vajpayee and Bikaner MP Dharmendra, were brought to the Parliament to vote against the UPA Government.

Heading: Sonia praises Andhra model of women’s empowerment - Indian Express
Content:
Close on the heels of the pay hike for government employees, the Government has decided to hike the total emoluments for the President, Vice-President, and governors. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), which met under the chairmanship of Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, finalised a hike of 300 per cent on Thursday.

Accordingly, while the President's emoluments have been raised from Rs 50,000 to Rs 1.50 lakh per month, the Vice-President's salary has tripled from Rs 40,000 to Rs 1.25 per month, and governors will now earn Rs 1.10 lakh per month instead of the current Rs 36,000.

In addition to the salary hike, the Government also rationalised and increased the post-retirement benefits of the President and Vice-Presidents. The retirement benefits for both have been fixed at 50 per cent of the emoluments they are currently receiving. However, no decision was taken regarding post-retirement benefits for governors.

This move comes after an earlier decision by the Cabinet in January this year, when the emoluments for the President was revised up from Rs 50,000 to Rs 1.0 lakh per month; the Vice President's from Rs 40,000 to Rs 85,000; and governors' from Rs 36,000 to Rs 75,000.

However, though these decisions were supposed to be implemented after passing an amendment to the Act pertaining to the President's and VP's salary and perks, the same could not be undertaken and these functionaries continued to draw their previous salaries.

After the government decided to implement recommendations by the Sixth Pay Commission, under which a secretary to the Government of India would draw Rs 80,000 per month, the pay hike for the functionaries of these constitutional posts were considered necessary. The pay hike for the President, VP and governors will be applicable from January 1, 2006, the date from which the increase in salary for government servants will apply.

Heading: Day after Big B’s apology, Raj relents - Indian Express
Content:
UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi on Thursday said women's empowerment in Andhra Pradesh had become a role model in the country and had aroused curiosity abroad. On a whirlwind tour of Rayalseema region, Sonia interacted with women groups at Renigunta near Tirupati, inaugurated the IIIT in Cuddapah district and wound up her tour by addressing a public meeting at Anantpur district where she reiterated the need for nuclear power to meet the energy requirements of the country.

While interacting with members of self-help groups and women beneficiaries of the NREGS at Tirupati, Sonia said she was often asked by many people about women's empowerment programme in Andhra Pradesh and their desire to replicate it.

Announcing plans for Tirupati, she said the small local airport would be expanded with modern facilities. Also, Rs 2,000 crore had been sanctioned for the expansion and modernisation of the Tirupati railway station. Sonia also announced plans to renovate and conserve 17 important temples in and around Tirupati and turn them into tourist attractions.

"I wish to congratulate Chief Minister Y S Rajasekhar Reddy for ensuring women empowered," she said, accompanied by Chief Minister Y S Rajasekhara Reddy and APCC president D Srinivas.

Heading: Antony assures level playing field for US firms - Indian Express
Content:
A day after actor Amitabh Bachchan offered his apologies if his wife Jaya's remarks had hurt even a single person's sentiments, Maharashtra Navanirman Sena (MNS) president Raj Thackeray on Thursday withdrew his agitation and the ban on movies starring Bachchan family members.

"Everyone would have come to know what happens when the Marathi people come together," said Raj, adding that though Jaya had apologised in an interview to a newspaper, the party had been firm on the stance that nothing short of a public apology would suffice.

"Though it was essential for Jaya Bachchan to apologise for her remarks, we have accepted Amitabh Bachchan's gesture to issue the apology after holding a press conference as head of the family. This is a victory of the Maharashtrians," Raj added and called on his cadre and associates to maintain peace.

Alleging that Jaya had spoken in Parliament on the issue of making Mumbai an independent state, Thackeray advised her to "stick to written dialogues and not say anything that comes to her mind".

He also reiterated the statement he had made in a speech at a party function at Vikhroli earlier this year — in which he had said that personalities like Amitabh Bachchan, Lata Mangeshkar and Sachin Tendulkar are not bound by territorial boundaries.

"The people of the country see, watch and hear them. Amitabh Bachchan should not be hemmed in boundaries of territory. Keeping personal relations with anyone is his personal question," he had added.

Thackeray also clarified that the Mumbai Police, which had earlier served a gag order on him, had given him permission to address the press conference after he spoke to Commissioner of Police Hasan Gafoor on Wednesday.

Referring to Bachchan's blog apology, he said it did not have the public outreach of a newspaper or news channel. However, the matter had been cleared after Bachchan's press conference, he added.

Heading: Bush sends 123 to US Congress - Indian Express
Content:
India and the US have agreed on giving more strategic depth to their defence cooperation and New Delhi has assured Washington that American armament companies will have a level playing field in the country.

Winding up his four-day visit to the United States, Defence Minister A K Antony said the two countries held discussions on issues like Afghanistan, military-to-military cooperation and problems connected with military technology transfer from the US.

Though he said the nuclear deal was not a central part of his agenda in talks with the Pentagon, Antony said he had been told by Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice that she was confident of getting the Indo-US deal approved this year.

The Defence Minister, who was talking to reporters on the sidelines of a function held in his honour by the Indian community here, said he had thanked the US Administration for its help in getting the waiver from the Nuclear Suppliers Group in Vienna.

Antony did not elaborate on problems being faced on technology transfer. However, the two countries are yet to ratify the crucial end-users agreement under which the US has the right of physical verification of weapon systems transferred.

The failure to conclude such an agreement had recently led to delay in delivery of three customised VVIP Boeing executive jets to India.

Antony's remarks assume significance as US armaments majors like Lockheed Martin, Boeing, Raytheon and others are vying for multi-billion dollar contracts in India for sale of helicopters, fighters, radars, missiles and other advanced weapons.

Heading: Paralysed Kargil hero gets aid - Indian Express
Content:
President George W Bush on Thursday sent the 123 Agreement to the US Congress and invited Prime Minister Manmohan Singh to the White House on September 25 when the two may sign the pact if it is approved by then.

The Prime Minister, who will go to the United Nations for attending the General Assembly, will travel to Washington for the meeting.

"The President also looks forward to welcoming Prime Minister Singh to the White House on September 25 to strengthen the strategic partnership and to build upon our progress in other areas of cooperation, such as agriculture, education, trade and defence," White House Press Secretary Dana Perino said.

Bush "is pleased to approve the US-India Agreement for Peaceful Nuclear Cooperation (also known as the 123 Agreement)." The President "looks forward to working with Congress to ensure passage on the agreement this year," she said. The 123 Agreement permits transfer of information, nuclear material and reactors and components for research and power production.

The action of the President, who wants to conclude the process of nuclear deal with India before the Congress session concludes on September 26, comes on top of Administration's efforts to short circuit procedures so that the approval is secured waiving the 30-day mandatory wait in the session.

As required under the Hyde Act, Bush has also sent his Presidential determinations for the Congress to approve the deal that will end over three decades of nuclear isolation of India. He has also sent a memorandum to Secretary of State and Secretary of Energy concerning peaceful use of nuclear energy with India, saying that he has made the Presidential determinations that the agreement will promote and will not constitute an "unreasonable risk" to defence and security. He authorised them to arrange for its execution.

"Civil nuclear cooperation between the United States and India pursuant to the agreement will offer major strategic and economic benefits to both countries," Bush said in his memorandum to the Congress.

With Democrats in control of the House and the Senate, Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice also met with crucial lawmakers including Senate majority leader Harry Reid, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Howard Berman and House Speaker Nancy Pelosi as part of efforts to quicken the process.

Meanwhile, India today reiterated that it will begin nuclear commerce with France and Russia only after the 123 agreement with the US is implemented. The Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson said in New Delhi: "While actual cooperation will commence after bilateral agreements like the 123 Agreement come into force, the Nuclear Power Corporation of India has already commenced a preliminary dialogue with US companies in this regard.

Heading: Girls interrupted, who’s to blame? - Indian Express
Content:
Nine years after the Kargil war, an Army jawan who had sustained serious injuries during 'Operation Vijay' and had become paralysed, has received a financial assistance of Rs 10 lakh from Chhattisgarh Chief Minister's relief fund.

A resident of village Godhori under Dharsivan block of Raipur district, Chandrasen Anant was posted with the Infantry's Mahar regiment.

During the Kargil conflict, he had sustained serious injuries in shelling on the Indo-Pak border in November 1999 and later underwent treatment at Pune Army hospital for two years. He became paralysed as he had sustained spinal chord injuries. Subsequently, he retired on medical grounds from the Army. He was the sole bread winner of his ten-member family who is surviving on his pension.

Raipur District Collector Sonmoni Borah said Anant did not get ex-gratia from the chief minister's Kargil relief fund as he could not register himself earlier with the state Sainik Welfare Board. After undergoing treatment at Army hospital in Pune, Anant was brought by his relatives to his native village where he is still bedridden.

Heading: Dias signs fresh contract - Indian Express
Content:
While the boys are enjoying a rare break from international cricket, the Indian women's cricket team's disastrous performance in England has come under the scanner with the World Cup barely six months away.

World Cup finalists last time, India crashed to a humiliating 4-0 defeat in the five-match series — England were denied a whitewash only because the fifth match was rained out. The team's batswomen, barring captain Mithali Raj, struggled to get into double figures and the skipper was left fuming at her team's collapse. As the side made a quiet return home on Thursday, it was clear that they had suffered because of poor selection decisions over the past few months.

While India struggled to post more than 100 on the scoreboard, their most successful batswoman Anjum Chopra was left cooling her heels back home. The 30-year old Chopra has been in good form in recent domestic events, and was only rested from the Asia Cup to give youngsters a chance. She was called for the Mysore camp before the England tour but was not picked.

The selection committee of Anju Jain, Sandhya Aggarwal, Purnima Rau, Mithu Mukherjee and Vrinda Bhagat has been confused about its youth or experience policy.

Age doesn't matter

Even as Anjum was ignored, the selectors recalled Hemlata Kala — the oldest in the camp at 33 — while 31-year-old Neetu David was brought out of retirement for the England tour ahead of 23-year old left-arm spinner Preeti Dimri. Anagha Deshpande, a young wicketkeeper-opener, was picked for the Asia Cup but the selectors dropped her for 29-year old Sulakashna Naik. And at 32, off-spinner Seema Pujare made her international debut.

India's vice-captain Jhulan Goswami, too, put the blame on batswomen. "The bowlers need some runs on the board to defend. If they don't put up some runs how can we expect to win matches?" she said. "Perhaps we could not acclimatise ourselves in the cold and wet conditions in England. We also missed the injured Rumeli Dhar. Her experience would have played a crucial role," she said.

Interestingly, Rumeli Dhar was recovering from an injury but was called for the camp. Having regained fitness over the course of 10 days, she was selected and even her visa was stamped. But, just before departure, Dhar was informed that she had been dropped because of poor fitness.

Heading: Organisational nightmare at lifting meet - Indian Express
Content:
Steven Dias and Mahindra United finally reached an agreement over the midfielder's contract on Thursday.

Dias said he had decided to stick with the Mumbai club after they agreed to a salary hike that the player had been demanding having being offered a bigger deal by Kolkata's East Bengal club.

"I have been given a hike and have signed a two-year contract. I am happy and will join the team from Monday. They have also promised to release me next year if a club matches the transfer fee Mahindra ask for," Dias told The Indian Express.

Meanwhile, team mate NP Pradeep, also in the centre of the transfer drama, is yet to speak to the club as he is currently in his hometown in Kerala. "I am hopeful things will fall into place after we speak," Pradeep said.

Heading: Bhullar showers birdies on rainy day - Indian Express
Content:
The first day of the Junior National Weightlifting meet at the Noida Club was an organisational nightmare.

A small hall and a makeshift dais meant that the lifters had to be extra careful dropping the barbells back after their attempted lifts, with referees and officials seated rather too close to the dais. The announcer was at his hoarse best, fumbling with names and even shouting at an official manning the electronic scoreboard.

To add to the confusion, there was no sign of Sports Authority of India anti-doping officials for the first two sessions. The officials were apparently delayed because the vehicle to pick them up from the Jawahar Lal Nehru Stadium did not arrive on time. Even after they arrived, the officials could not find a proper sample-collection room.

Sample bungle

In any case, the samples of participants in the first two sessions could not be collected, rather callous for a sport that has been under the dope cloud in the country. But the officials had a ready answer: "We will collect their urine samples when they make it to the India camp (for the Pune Youth Commonwealth Games)."

With not much time left to pick the squad for the Youth Commonwealth Games, the organisers have declared this meet to be the basis for selection. But some lifters feel this would give a distinct advantage to "outsiders," that is, those who are not regular trainees and hence outside the WADA net.

Heading: Four years later, Daniel comes calling - Indian Express
Content:
Not for nothing is Gaganjeet Bhullar considered one of the most exciting young pros on the domestic circuit. On a rain-marred day, the big-hitting golfer was in his element as he set the par-72 Golden Greens ablaze with a blistering nine-under 63 — his best round as a professional.

Conditions were hardly ideal, windy with an intermittent drizzle, but it wasn't an issue for Bhullar, who showered the course with eagles and birdies — two and six, respectively — to break the course record en route to grabbing sole lead at the halfway mark of the AIS Open.

Bhullar, who shot two-under 70 on Wednesday, now totals 11-under 133, a lead of one stroke over Rahul Ganapathy, who carded his second successive 67.

A tenth-tee starter, Bhullar made four consecutive pars before sinking birdies on the 14th and 16th. The 20-year-old then made his first and only bogey on the 17th, followed by an eagle on the par-five 18th, where he landed his second shot seven feet away.

After the turn, there was no looking back. He began with a birdie on the first and sank another eagle on the second. Three more birdies followed on the fourth, seventh and ninth.

"I am really thrilled with my effort today," he said. "It was a mixture of good hitting and putting. I think I was also a little lucky with my putting today as everything was falling in," Bhullar said.

Ganapathy, who played in the same three-ball as Bhullar on Thursday, took his total to 10-under 134. The Mysore lad started with a birdie on the 10th and then knocked down another birdie on the 13th to make the turn at two-under. He then hit a purple patch with three consecutive birdies on the first, second and third. Ganapathy bogeyed the eighth and picked up a birdie on the ninth to finish with five under for the day.

The cut was applied at six-over 150. Fifty-six players made it to the next two rounds.

3 Feroze Ali 136 (68, 68)

6 Ashok Kumar 139 (68, 71)
