Federer's victory reminds us of Pete Sampras too. Clearly, he is the first tennis great since Sampras to match him in calibre and heroism. Federer has proved once again that he is, still, the invincible ace of this generation.

— Siddharth Patel

Baroda

Right step

• This refers to 'Judges and justice'. The chief justice of India, K.G. Balakrishnan, has taken the right decision in asking the prime minister to impeach the Calcutta High Court judge, Soumitra Sen. Prompt action is required to ensure the delivery of justice to all.

— Deepak Chikramane

Mumbai

Heading: No promises, no guarantees - Indian Express
Content:
The NSG waiver given to India has triggered a variety of comments in the Urdu press. In a banner headline on November 7, Delhi-based Hamara Samaj described it as a "historic success". The paper has however, highlighted the reactions of the Left and the BJP as well. Milap, published from Delhi, in an editorial (Sept 5), describes the issues arising out of The Washington Post's revelations about interactions between the US administration and Congress as "of an internal nature relevant to the US, but it may have a direct result on India's government and its future." . The paper says that it shows that the Indian government was in the know of what was revealed by The Washington Post. Delhi's Jadeed Khabar says that the NGS waiver has been given to India not because it is a responsible nuclear nation but because the US wants such a waiver to be given. Because of the assurance given for unilateral moratorium about nuclear tests, India will no longer be able to maintain its position of high pride. Referring to the letter, Jamaat-e-Islami's bi-weekly organ, Daawat (Sept 7), writes: "Ultimately, the truth behind the Indo-US Nuclear Deal has come out. The Bush administration will not be much worried, because it has prepared its defence. Indian government's credibility has been questioned and its propaganda has been proved to be false."

Zardari's Pakistan

Recent developments in Pakistan culminating in the election of Asif Ali Zardari as the country's new president have been viewed with all kinds of doubt and apprehension about the entire region. Almost unanimously, these papers have questioned Zardari's credibility as a balanced and sincere leader and human being. Hindustan Express, in a September 8 editorial writes, "If Zardari is truly mentally imbalanced (sanki) whose temperament is such that he might do anything in a fit of anger, the apprehension is not without basis that the fingers of this imbalanced person are on nuclear weapons ...Pakistan's neighbours, particularly India, would have to be very cautious with regard to that country". Rashtriya Sahara, in an editorial entitled, 'Promises of Asif Zardari' (Sept 8) has talked about Zardari's statement that the presidency in Pakistan would be subordinate to the Parliament. It says, "The problem is that in view of Zardari's political postures so far, this statement of his can not be relied upon." The paper has also expressed disgust at the president's former reputation as 'Mr. 10 Per Cent' and the many charges of corruption and criminal acts against him. Noted writer and journalist, Hasan Kamal, in his column in Rashtriya Sahara (Sept 6) has raised the question, "Is Pervez Musharraf's return possible?", in view of the present state of confusion and political confrontation in Pakistan. Taking a leaf out of Indira Gandhi's story of return to power after the debacle following the Emergency in India, he does not overrule such a possibility.

Floods: the great leveller?

Amid the shock and sorrow for flood victims in Bihar and elsewhere, there is some resentment about those who seek to politicise the catastrophe. Hyderabad-based Munsif (Sept. 2) has drawn attention to despicable elements exploiting the flood to loot and harass the flood victims. It hopes that now that the army has taken control of relief work, "the loot of gold and silver from the deserted houses and the rotting bodies would be stopped." Hindustan Express (Sept 5), taking an altogether different line in a page 1 report from Purnea writes, "The so called efforts at different levels to put an end to the unpleasant differences between the rich and the poor have proved unsuccessful so far. But they have been eliminated in a very painful manner by the high tides of river Kosi's flood. "The flood has washed away the differences in a society badly afflicted by discriminations of caste and creed and the rich and the poor have been brought down to the same level. They are helping each other in relief camps, rising above all kinds of differences and discriminations", it writes.

The Big Bang

Rashtriya Sahara on September 11 has provided copious details of the experiment conducted by CERN in a six column lead with colour pictures. Hindustan Express has also mocked the dark speculation surrounding the event as as qayamat pasand (those wanting to see Doomsday.)

Heading: The who, when, why and how - Indian Express
Content:
The US government's takeover of mortgage giants Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac constitutes a huge bailout of these institutions' creditors, whose losses have ballooned as house prices continue to plummet. With the government now fully guaranteeing Fannie's and Freddie's debts, American taxpayers will have to pay for everything not covered by their creditors' inadequate capital.

Why is this bailout happening in the world's most avowedly capitalist country? Don't venerable capitalist principles imply that anyone who believed in the real estate bubble and who invested in Fannie and Freddie must accept their losses? Is it fair that innocent taxpayers must now pay for their mistakes? The answers to such questions would be obvious if the moral issues in the current financial crisis were clear-cut. But they are not. Most importantly, it is not clear that the bailout will actually impose any net costs on US taxpayers, since it may prevent further systemic effects that bring down the financial sector and, with it, the world economy. Just because systemic effects are difficult to quantify does not mean that they are not real.

The bonds issued by Fannie and Freddie were widely thought to carry an implicit US government guarantee. Even though there was no official guarantee, the US government's failure to come to the rescue could destroy confidence in government debt, and, by association, other financial paper as well. The issues go far beyond the US economy. The global economy has been d

riven in recent years by remarkable speculative asset booms and busts, which bring into the equation questions of confidence and trust, as well as fairness. Similar housing booms in many other countries are now ending, and they may face the pain — and the moral dilemmas — that the US economy is now experiencing.

Moreover, housing markets are not the only issue. So are stock markets. The Shanghai Composite in China rose by a factor of five in real terms from 2005 to 2007, and then lost two-thirds of its real value. The Sensex in India rose by a factor of five in real terms over 2003 to 2007, and has since lost a third of its value. Similar stock market booms and busts have occurred in many other countries. While they lasted, the booms that preceded these busts caused these economies to overheat. Now that the booms have been reversed, a decline in confidence could engulf the world economy, throwing it into recession. To prevent that, some selective bailouts will likely be needed, not to support the market but to deal with injustices.

There is no accurate science of confidence, no way of knowing how people will react to a failure to help when markets collapse. People's reactions to these events depend on their emotions and their sense of justice. The booms and busts have caused great redistributions of wealth. People who bought into the stock market or housing market did either well or poorly, depending on their timing. People will judge the fairness of these outcomes in terms of what they were told, and what kinds of implicit promises they inferred.

What were people in all these countries told about the markets in which they invested? Was it all really truthful? Unfortunately, there is no way to find out. Policymakers can provide only general responses, not deal with all cases individually. We do know that recent economic growth in many countries has been spectacular. But were investments in their markets oversold?

To be sure, while there may have been much "cheap talk" — general advice with disclaimers —most of the losers in this game are not starving. But we cannot blithely conclude that all the losses should be allowed to stand in full force. The gnawing problem is one of "good faith." Economies prosper only on the perception that "good faith" exists. The current situation, in which speculative booms have driven the world economy — and, having collapsed, are now driving it into recession — suggests that there may have been a lot of bad faith by people promoting certain investments.

Consider investors in Fannie and Freddie bonds. While the US government never officially promised to bail them out, it did create a special agency, which was to assess their strength in an annual report. But this agency never even acknowledged that there was a housing bubble. Government leaders gave no warnings. So can we say that investors must suffer the consequences of any losses?

The world is discovering capitalism and its power to transform economies. But capitalism relies on good faith. A perception of unfair treatment can be deadly to economic growth, because it means that people will lose trust in businesses, and hence be less willing to offer to them their precious capital and labour. Is that outcome morally superior to a bailout?

The writer is professor of economics at Yale University .Project Syndicate

Heading: Gujarat farmers grapple with shortage of power, water - Indian Express
Content:
The issue of conduct and accountability of judges is again making headlines. Under our current system, all subordinate judges are governed by and accountable to the respective high courts. For the higher judiciary, the only disciplinary action allowed against a judge is that of impeachment.

This paper carried an op-ed describing how judges can be removed from office, and the proposed bill that modifies this process. Four significant changes are being proposed in the Judges (Inquiry) Bill, 2006. First, any person may complain against a Supreme Court or high court judge; currently, 100 Lok Sabha MPs or 50 Rajya Sabha MPs are required to initiate the process. Second, the bill proposes a National Judicial Council (NJC) consisting of Supreme Court and high court Judges to conduct an inquiry . Third, it provides for minor measures such as issuing advisories and warnings, withholding work, asking the judge to resign, and censuring privately or publicly. Fourth, it allows the judge to appeal to the Supreme Court against the finding of the NJC and even against the final order of removal.

There are four conceptual issues that need to be addressed by Parliament. First, who judges the judges? Opinion on this is divided. The Supreme Court has held several times that judicial accountability should be enforced by the judiciary itself. It has also ruled that the president has to heed the advice of the serving judiciary while appointing judges. The law commission in its 195th report stated that the judiciary must be held accountable, but that the oversight should be with a committee consisting solely of the serving judiciary. It argued that this is the norm on the independence of the judiciary. However, the standing committee while examining this bill stated that the composition of the proposed NJC "is not in consonance with the principle of accountability." It stated that either the NJC should be expanded to include non-judicial members representing the legislature and the executive or alternatively, an empowered committee, with members from the judiciary, executive, legislature and the bar, should be set up to screen complaints before they are investigated by the NJC. International practice also varies: Canada, US and Germany have only judges in the investigating bodies whereas England, Wales and South Africa include lay persons.

Second, can a judge impeached by Parliament appeal against his removal? In 1992, the Supreme Court held that the question of judicial review would arise only after the impeachment motion was passed by Parliament. The law commission relied on this judgment and determined that the remedy of judicial review cannot be ousted because it is part of the "basic structure of the Constitution and cannot be removed even by constitutional amendment". However, the standing committee has recommended against including any provision for appeal after a removal order has been passed by the president following an impeachment motion in the Parliament. The committee said that constitutionally mandated due process is inherent in the process for removal, and any appeal would amount to an action against the constitutional authority of the president.

Third, should any lay person be allowed to file a complaint? The standing committee has observed that "an individual is being equated with 100 MPs of Lok Sabha and 50 MPs of Rajya Sabha for making a complaint against a judge". It recommended that an impartial empowered committee, comprising of members from the legislature, executive, judiciary and the Bar should be created to screen complaints, and recommend which ones need to be investigated by the NJC.

Fourth, are the "minor measures" constitutional? The Constitution is silent on this. The law commission stated that the NJC should be enabled to impose minor measures against the judge if he was found guilty and the offence did not warrant removal. It stated that the US and Canada have established minor measures to discipline judges despite having no such clause in their constitutions. The US Supreme Court has upheld the constitutionality of such measures reasoning that it was permissible for the judiciary to regulate itself and set its own house in order. The standing committee felt that the bill did not need a constitutional amendment but nevertheless it stated that "the issue of constitutional validity of this bill be thoroughly examined once again before proceeding further with the bill because many witnesses including jurists were of the opinion that this Bill will not withstand constitutional validity in its present form".

The writer works with PRS Legislative Research at the Centre for Policy Research, New Delhi

Heading: Terai gives Punjab farmers a lesson in banana cultivation - Indian Express
Content:
With less than normal rainfall, the farms in Gujarat are grappling with shortage of both power and water for irrigation. While the state Government has already decided to reduce power supply to the industries to facilitate irrigation, the farmer bodies maintain that agricultural production will suffer heavy losses because of water shortage.

"If we don't get any more rains, the farm produce will be reduced to half of our normal production," said Jivan Patel, co-ordinator, Bharatiya Kisan Sangh (BKS). "However, if it rains from now on, maybe we can get to about 80 per cent of our regular yield," he added.

Meanwhile, the state Government has already announced extra power supply to the farmers for irrigation to save the crops. "We understand that the industries will have to suffer some reduction in production for a short period, but unless the farmers are given power now, they will lose the crop of the entire year," said a highly-placed official from Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Limited (GUVNL). "Since last two days, we have been providing about 55 million units to the farmers for irrigation as against the demands of 60million units," he added.

However, power is not the only issue that worries the farmers and the Government. "The farmers have to be sensitised to make judicious use of water," said the official adding that GUVNL is also meeting the farmers and trying to generate awareness about alternative modes of irrigation.

"There is no water in the rocky farmlands of north Gujarat and the water level of the wells, too, have gone down in the Saurashtra region," Patel says.

"At BKS, we are holding regular meetings at the block levels to train the farmers about various modes of economic irrigation," he says.

"Like in cotton, we are asking them to water every alternate row, which will reduce the need for water. While the Government has announced additional power supply to the fields, we are still not getting uninterrupted power for eight hours, which is very important now," said Praful Sanjaliya, president, BKS.

"With a situation like this, the standing crop of groundnut, cotton and paddy will suffer heavy losses, which now seems almost inevitable," he added.

Meanwhile, aggrieved with the power cut, the industry sector in the state has pointed out that it is losing about Rs 1,200 crore worth production per day. "We are expecting the situation to get better in a week's time when we start getting additional 450 MW power from two plants at Gandhinagar and Paguthan at Bharuch, which are under maintenance now," said the official.

Heading: Himachal apple growers cash in on Amarnath land controversy - Indian Express
Content:
For a state that consumes nearly Rs 500 crore worth of bananas every year - one of the highest in the country - it is no mean achievement that it is now growing its own bananas and that too king-size. What started as a small attempt in some of the districts of the state such as Ludhiana and Mohali in 2006, after farmers and scientists from Ludhiana-based Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) went to Terai area of Uttaranchal to get tips on banana cultivation, is now spreading across the central and southern parts of the state.

While Punjab claims its fruit is sweeter and better, for farmers such as Chamkaur Singh of Tohra village its sweetness has more to do with the good returns it is fetching. With just two acres of his land under banana cultivation, he has been able to earn Rs 1.25 lakh per acre. The fruit's inclusion in the National Horticulture Mission recently is likely to further sweeten the proposition for Punjab farmers, as up to 50 per cent subsidy will now be offered for its plants and drip irrigation. So out of Rs 16 that the plant costs, the farmers will have to bear just Rs 8 as the cost per plant, explains Dr P S Rangi, consultant with the Punjab Farmers Commission, which is piloting the project.

There are, however, certain points of concern. The first crop carries a risk of failure though the commission says the next three crops are practically risk-free. Also, bananas are sensitive to frost and excessive cold — the reason why most of northern Punjab has been found to be unsuitable for its cultivation. "In the northern parts of Punjab, temperatures dip as low as minus four degrees. This can destroy the crop, which is why districts such as Amritsar, Gurdaspur, Hoshiarpur, Nawan Shehar are off the list and the farmers of central Punjab such as Patiala, Moga, Ludhiana, Ropar, Mohali and the cotton belt such as Bathinda and Sangrur are being encouraged to grow the fruit. Besides the strategy is to cut the fruit by November before the winter strikes, as bananas are also in huge demand then due to the festive season," adds Rangi.

As bananas flourish in Punjab, a more scientific way to store and ripen them is also being developed. This is urgently required, as the state gets the fruit from the southern and western states as raw, and ripens it with banned products such as calcium carbide.

While private agencies developing farm-to-fork post-harvest facilities with a few already having set up their packaging houses for scientific storage of perishables for their retail operations in the state, as many as 10 markets of the state will also be modernised under various schemes of the Punjab State Marketing Board.

To start with, the first such fruit and veggie market will come up in Ludhiana with the technical assistance of Voltas group of Tatas. "The modern markets will have ripening chambers where fruits such as mangoes, bananas and papayas will be ripened through ethylene gas and not banned products, as is the practice at present. These markets will also offer the facility of storage of fruits," says Dr B S Ghuman of PAU 's Post Harvest Technology Centre, which has done the feasibility study for the modern market coming up in Ludhiana.

Heading: UP’s farming sector cries for reforms - Indian Express
Content:
The Amarnath land row which prevented the Kashmir apple crop from reaching the wholesale market, proved to be a blessing in disguise for Himachal's orchards. Despite less than optimum production this year, Himachali apples have been a big draw for the buyers.

However, with the Kashmir agitation dying down, for the last one week prices have crashed by atleast Rs 200 per box as apple trucks from Kashmir have already reached major markets, including Chandigarh, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Nagpur and Kolkata. Yet, the Himachal growers are a contented lot at the end of the peak season.

Over 1.30 crore apple boxes from Himachal Pradesh have already been marketed and it will take another 10 to 15 days till the apple growers start counting their cash. Every day about 550 trucks are leaving Shimla in addition to an almost equal number from Kullu, Sirmaur, Mandi and Chamba taken together. State government estimates expect the total production to be between 1.12 crore and 1.15 crore boxes, atleast 28 lakh boxes less than 2006 — a bumper season. Last year, Himachal Pradesh produced 1.21 crore apple boxes.

Nonetheless, the market price remains higher than 2007, when the price had crashed to Rs 600 to Rs 700 per box during the corresponding month. The Royal Delicious apple variety from Himachal is selling at Rs 800 per box and the best ones can still fetch Rs 900 per box. The Red Richer, a recently imported American variety, is fetching Rs 725 per box, nearly Rs 50 to Rs 75 more than last year.

Himachal apple growers are an obviously satisfied lot. "The direct buying by the corporate sector and wholesale traders helped in stabilisation of the markets.That's what the apple growers require for long-term returns," says Lekh Raj Chauhan, president, Himachal Fruits and Vegetable Growers body.

But it hasn't all been smooth sailing. Excessive rains this year coupled with a series of landslides have been a serious impediment in marketing their produce. Rohit Thakur, a former Congress MLA, holds the government responsible for not keeping the link roads open. "First, there was a shortage of trucks and then blockades. Suddenly, when the roads opened, the market got flooded with apple and the prices crashed," he says.

Heavy rains also had other side-affects. This was the first time when apple scab —a disease caused by trapping of excessive water, which had taken a heavy toll on the apple crop in the early 80s — reappeared in some of the apple-growing areas. Fortunately, the Horticulture Department and the growers took precautionary steps to save the crop from being wiped out completely.

The growers also bore the brunt of higher input costs, with fungicide prices being 60 to 70 per cent higher and the the apple cartons and trays costing Rs 20 to 25 more than earlier seasons.

Meanwhile, Horticulture Minister Narinder Bragta said, "Setting up fruit-processing units and cold storage facilities will be the government's priority. The growers should get sale-points at the orchard gates," said Bragta.

Heading: Almond Cracks record - Indian Express
Content:
In the very first year of the 11th Five Year Plan, the agriculture sector in Uttar Pradesh has suffered a setback with the state failing to achieve the target growth rate of 5.1 per cent. The growth rate in the period has been 2.8 per cent.

The growth rate of agriculture sector during the 10th Five Year Plan was only 2 per cent.

Despite the grim scenario further aggravated by the growing population and increasing vagaries of weather affecting both the rabi and kharif crops, the political establishment of the state seems to be in no hurry to implement reforms in the sector.

The Agriculture Infrastructure and Investment Policy, announced by Chief Minister Mayawati on August 3, 2007, had fuelled the hope of the revival of the agriculture sector in UP. Following opposition by the traders to the entry of the retail sector in the state, particularly of the Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Fresh, Mayawati rolled back the policy within 18 days and Reliance asked to down its shutters on August 21.

The policy cleared the decks for the retail industry to invest in the sector. The government then projected that an amendment to the UP State Agriculture produce marketing Board Act, on the lines of the model APMC Act circulated by the Centre, would attract investment to the tune of Rs 40,000 crore in the agriculture sector by 2011. The new policy, besides eliminating middlemen in agriculture trade, was projected to give boost to 'big' retail players in the state. The Act provided for the setting up of mandis by retail stores, besides allowing them to directly purchase the agriculture produce from the farmers.

In the absence of retail stores for the agriculture produce, the traders continue to rake in huge profits at the cost of farmers. The potato farmers had to sell their produce at the rate of Rs 100-120 quintal in April last while the retail price of potato remains at Rs 1,000 per quintal.

The wheat farmers also suffered during the rabi season in March-April 2008, as the government refused to issue licence to private companies to make direct purchase from the farmers. The farmers were forced to sell wheat at Rs 950-975 per quintal to the 'Arathia' appointed by the state Government. The Arathias had the best of both the worlds, as they exploited the farmers and also bagged a commission of Rs 65 crore at the rate of 2.5 per cent from the government for the total wheat purchase from the farmers.

Decades of neglect of the agriculture and allied sector in UP has resulted in the stagnation of the sector. UP achieved the highest growth rate of 9.7 per cent during the Sixth Five Year Plan (1981-85) period. During the Ninth Five Year Plan (1997-2002), the growth rate dipped to lowest-ever to 0.8 per cent.

During the first five FYPs, from 1951-1979, the plan outlay for the agriculture sector in UP was double digit, ranging between 24.69 percent to 13.69 per cent of the total plan outlay. In subsequent five year plans, from 1981 to 2007 till the end of the 10th FYP, the outlay for this sector fell to single digit, between five to seven per cent. During the current 11th Five Year Plan, the outlay is expected to marginally cross 10 per cent.

For over 25 years, successive governments ignored the crucial sector of UP's economy despite the fact that as much as 79 per cent of the state's population is dependenton this sector, which contributes 30 per cent to the state's GDP. UP contributes 19 per cent to the total national food production.

The agriculture universities of UP had played a stellar role in ushering in the green revolution in the state in the 60s with for developing new varieties of wheat, paddy and crops of oilseeds and pulses.

The three agriculture universities in UP are no longer known for any research and development and the state Government has frozen their grants. The priority accorded to research in agriculture can be gauged from the fact for over three decades, the total expenditure on R and D in agriculture is only 0.08 per cent of the total agriculture GDP of the state. The same in Himachal Pradesh is as high as 1.37 per cent.

Said Dr R S Rathore, deputy director general of the UP Council of Agriculture Research, "No short-terms measures will work in UP for reviving the agriculture sector. Be it the opening of agriculture to retail sector or a hike in outlay for research and development, a holistic long-term policy for the agriculture and allied sector should be worked out by all the private and government agencies involved in the sector."

Heading: Plan to dispose of, auction the last remaining vestiges of Partition in city - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: Change regulation zone rules for Navi Mumbai airport: state - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when the simmering dispute over Jinnah House in Malabar Hill still awaits the court's verdict, the state government has decided to dispose of six properties that are the remaining vestiges of Partition in Mumbai.

The property once belonged to the Currimbhoy Ebrahim family, leading mill-owners of Mumbai in the pre-Independence days. In the 1950s it was declared as evacuee property and passed over to the Custodian of Evacuee Property. Several years and court petitions down the line it was transferred to its current landlord, the state government.

"For almost three decades now, the state government has been maintaining these properties. The Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority was asked to attend to the repairs of these structures," said an official from the state revenue department. He added that following the repeal of the Displaced Persons Act in 2005, the state government has now mooted a proposal to auction the properties on 'as is where is basis'. The proposal will soon be placed before the cabinet.

"We are examining various options like auctioning or redeveloping the buildings," said revenue secretary Ramesh Kumar. The six structures include Colaba Chambers next to the Colaba Post office, Currimbhoy Manor at Warden road, Mohamedbhoy Mansion at Kemps Corner, Mehboob building at Musafirkhana road, Mahim mansion and Dossa building at Dongri.

Each of these buildings houses tenants who have been living here for 50 to 100 years and pay a minimal rent to the government. Some have been staying here since the pre-Independence days while others have been allotted the flats by the government after they were vacated by its former tenants.

For instance, the heritage structure of Colaba Chambers houses one Sindhi family. A few flats have been given to the Army and Navy, several of which are vacant and sealed. "This building is over a century old. Both mine and my husband's grandfathers are few of the original tenants here," said Irene Adeshir, one of the tenants. The view from her old sprawling apartment is today marred by a massive steel and glass high-rise a few metres away, ominously mirroring a fate that awaits her own building.

At Mohamedbhoy Mansion, another heritage structure located below the flyover at Kemps Corner, booklovers pour in and out of the Crossword bookstore in the ground floor of the building. Three floors above, Gyan Dayal, who runs a recruitment business out of his 50-year-old 4,000 sq ft flat said, "We tenants had long petitioned the government that whenever they take some decision, we be given the first preference to buy over the property. We hope they take that into account."

His former landlord's namesake building at Warden road is a quaint art deco structure. Eighty-three-year-old Thrity Taleyarkhan, who lives in the flat that was once the residence of Currimbhoy Ebrahim family, still remembers the day when she moved into the apartment. "It was in the year 1950-51. We were staying in a nearby building with my in-laws and were on the lookout for a house as we needed more space after my son was born. That was when a friend told us that the Currimbhoy Ebrahim family had migrated to Pakistan just a month ago leaving behind this huge empty flat as well as the flat next door," she recollects.

Her husband and former diplomat Homi Taleyarkhan, who has held positions such as that of governor of Sikkim and public health minister of Maharashtra, soon got permission from the government to stay in the house as a tenant. "I hope that this building is left untouched and not redeveloped. At least not during my lifetime," said Thrity, who is the sole resident of the four-bedroom apartment that, as she remembers, once resonated with noises emanating from the extravagant parties thrown by its former owner.

Heading: Air Traffic Controllers’ Guild has doubts on new navigation system - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to get the ambitious Greenfield international airport at Navi Mumbai on track, the state government has sought modifications in the coastal regulation zone (CRZ) rules to enable the airport's construction.

At a meeting here on Friday, which was attended by Vijai Sharma, secretary, union ministry of environment and forests and chief secretary Johny Joseph, senior officials present said they had asked for a modification in the CRZ so the construction on the airport could begin in April 2009.

Though Greenfield airports are permitted in the proposed Coastal Management Zone (CMZ) with such airports being allowed in CMZ I, II, and III areas, officials said they were unsure about when the regulations would come through due to the ongoing debate over it.

"We have asked for the same amendment in the CRZ (to allow Greenfield airports in CRZ I, II and III areas). There is no point in waiting for the CMZ as it is taking time due to the objections received," an official added.

Senior officials from the City and Industrial Development Corporation (CIDCO), which is executing the project, said they had asked for an amendment in the CRZ or the adoption (finalisation) of the notification of the proposed CMZ, depending on whatever came fast to expedite work on the project.

Of the 2,100 hectare of land required for the airport, around 115 hectare falls in the eco- sensitive CRZ I (i) zone, and the rest in the CRZ- I (ii) zone and CIDCO officials said there were instances where airstrips were approved in these areas.

Officials added that according to their original targets, the airport, which is initially expected to carter to 10 million passengers annually, was to be completed in October 2012 if work was awarded in April 2009. "If we are not able to do it (according to schedule), then there will be a delay of as many months," the CIDCO official said, adding that the airport needed 3.5 years to complete.

Though the state has received an approval from the union cabinet for the airport, no CRZ clearance has been received.

Mumbai is expected to see around nine crore air travelers annually by 2030, and the existing international and domestic terminals at Sahar and Santacruz are expected to cater to just around 4 crore travelers annually. The Navi Mumbai airport, with two parallel runways, and an estimated cost of over Rs 9,970 crore is expected to augment the capacity.

Senior officials present at the meeting said they also made a presentation and brought out various issues regarding the implementation of the CRZ, particularly with regard to the scarcity of land in Mumbai. Less land could be used for development due to issues like the CRZ, they added, which lead to a reduction in the land availability in the commercial capital, which in turn caused a rise in the realty prices, and a decrease in the housing stock, causing proliferation of slums.

Heading: Our metropolis less livable than ever, says BMC’s annual stock-taking exercise - Indian Express
Content:
With the Performance Based Navigation System (PBNS) having failed to ease out air traffic congestion at the Mumbai airport after its implementation and owing to severe infrastructure problems, it now appears that the Air Traffic Controller's Guild, in a feedback on the introduction of the new system at Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport (CSIA) had already expressed their discontent to the Airport Authority of India (AAI).

In a letter to the Chairman, AAI, K. Ramalingam (dated 7 th August 2008) — exactly three weeks prior to its implementation — the ATC Guild had outlined at least 14 drawbacks against the new system ranging from flaws in the training method given to Air Traffic Controllers (ATCOs) to insufficient number of available controllers to meet the number of sectors that had been proposed in the procedures.

"There were some issues raised about the quality of training that was being given to the controllers following which an agreement was reached that if ATCOs were uncomfortable with the new system, they can revert back to the old system until they become comfortable with the new procedures," said D.K Behera, General Secretary, Air Traffic Controller's Guild.

In its letter, the guild had pointed out issues such as non-availability of Arrival Manager (AMAN) software for traffic flow management. This would, in turn, mean that the sequence of arrival would have to be decided manually increasing holding time for arriving aircraft. In addition to this, according to an airport official who requested anonymity, Arrival Managers, a new post that has been created to cater to the new system, are also in short supply as they need to be radar certified and it's a well known fact that ATC is short-staffed when it comes to Air Traffic Controllers (ATCOs).

"The Guild is apprehensive that the management under pressure of the airlines and the airport operators will not pay heed to these sane suggestions and go ahead with implementation of these radically new procedures, thereby compromising safety and careers of ATCOs," the letter stated. Terming the apprehensions as not baseless, the guild has taken the example of introduction of the simultaneous runway operations at New Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGI). "This apprehension is not baseless, as can be seen from the earlier disastrous forced introduction of simultaneous runway operations at Delhi wherein Controllers were victimised by taking away their rating whereas the fault was with the faulty training and faulty SOPs," the letter stated.

However, M G Jhungare, General Manager, ATC Mumbai, brushed away the matter saying that he had no knowledge of the letter. "The procedure has been established and whatever issues that might have been there would have been resolved. As of now PBNS is running smoothly," he said. S S R Rao, Regional Executive Director, AAI, refused to comment.

"Considering the nature of training and other associated problems, ATCOs at IGI Airport and Mumbai Airport are not very confident of adapting to the changes. We need to see how other countries have implemented the PBN/ RNAV SIDS/ STARS and what type of difficulties did they face," the letter concluded.

Heading: Two held for stealing gold jewellery from processing unit in Sewri - Indian Express
Content:
Environment Status Report released: Vehicle numbers up 6%, water contamination and pollution worse; open space crisis deepening

The loss of charm of the coastal city that was once the stuff of dreams, the destination for all starry-eyed youngsters and the rich and famous alike, is now officially quantified: High levels of air, water and noise pollution, worsening traffic congestion, few open spaces functioning as green lungs, quality of life in Mumbai has never been worse, according to the annual Environment Status Report of the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC).

Consider this: 12.47 per cent of water samples are found to be contaminated in the city, noise levels have worsened as compared to previous years and the level of Suspended Particulate Matter, Respirable Suspended Particulates and oxides of nitrogen in the city all exceed levels prescribed as safe by the Central Pollution Control Board. Alarmingly, the vehicle population has jumped by 6.39 per cent since last year, adding immensely to road congestion.

"Mumbai is beseiged by multiple problems. Inadequate sewage treatment facilities, rapid disappearances of open spaces, ever increasing number of automobiles and consequent air pollution¿are a few manifestations of the inadequate attention and priority attached to the environmental management in metro," the just-released report says candidly.

Experts admit that the environmental situation in the city is grave. "At certain pockets like Malad, Kandivili and Sion junctions, there has been an increase in air pollution. One of the main reasons for this is high continuity of vehicles moving at a slower pace," says Dr Rakesh Kumar of the National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI). The report points out that of the six air monitoring stations, four have recorded heavy pollution levels — Maravali (Chembur), Andheri, Bhandup and Khar. Like every year, levels of SPM have exceeded prescribed safe standards at all sites except Borivali. "This is due to extensive public and private construction and related activies," the report says.

The report also notes that traffic density at peak hours is so high that vehicles move at 5 km to 8 km per hour. Traffic experts says the increase in road congestion is already showing on the health of people. "There are increasing incidents of road rage and problems people face while travelling by road. The only solution is augmentation of public transport through initiatives like the Bus Rapid Transit System," says transportation expert Sudhir Badami.

The report has asked for quick-fix solutions like environmental planning, fixing air and water pollution and development of open spaces.

Curiously, civic officials insist the situation is not alarming. "There are a large number of people who still choose to make Mumbai their home even after retirement," said Additional Municipal Commissioner R A Rajeev. "If the levels of pollution: air, water and noise are bad here then it is worse in other cities."

Although the civic body has undertaken several infrastructure projects that officials claim will improve quality of life in the financial capital in coming years, these will be completed only in the next four to five years. "The projects are in gestation period as of now, but when completed the city will be much better," Rajeev added.

Heading: To make room for more passengers, BEST to remove one row of seats in buses - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai Police Crime Branch on Friday arrested two youths involved in a theft of gold jewellery worth an estimated Rs 12 lakh from a jewellery processing unit in Sewri last month. According to the police, one of those arrested used to work at the unit and managed to smuggle out the stolen ornaments in a tiffin container.

The arrested accused have been identified as Sukhdev Singh Bairogya (18) and Sunil Das (22). While Bairogya hails from Hooghly district in West Bengal, Das hails from Midnapore district in that state.

According to the police, a theft case was registered at RAK Marg police on August 20 by Dilkhush Jain, the owner of Suvarn Shilp gold unit located in Rajeev Industrial Estate in Sewri. Jain in his complaint said a worker named Pradeep Mandal had stolen 1,040 gm of gold jewellery worth Rs 12 lakh.

"The unit has 70 to 80 workers who are divided into groups of three to four and given gold jewellery for processing. On August 19, a group of four was given 1,040 gram of gold to work on. At 11 pm that day, two workers left leaving behind Gopal Das and Pradeep Manal, who continued working till 3.30 am the following day. After the work was completed the duo went to sleep in the unit itself. At 7.30 am, Das woke up to go to the bathroom and saw Mandal sleeping. He returned from the bathroom and went to sleep. When he woke up again at 8:30 am, he found Mandal was missing along with the gold," said Joint Commissioner of Police, Crime, Rakesh Maria.

"Crime Branch Unit 4 started conducting parallel investigations in the matter and arrested the two accused involved today. During investigations it was learnt that Pradeep Mandal was a bogus name, and that the addresses provided by the worker were also false. It was Bairogya who worked at the unit for six months using the alias, before making away with the jewellery. Sunil Das had hatched the plan with him, and it was his job to sell the stolen property," said Maria.

According to the police, Sunil Das worked at an imitation jewellery factory in Laljipada, Kandivli (West), and got Bairogya a job there the day after the theft. Bairogya is wanted by the Gujarat Police for stealing 40 gram of gold from a unit in 2007.

"There was heavy security outside the Sewri unit and guards check the workers before they leave. Bairogya hid the gold in a tiffin container, covering it with rice he had deliberately not eaten. When the guards on duty checked him, he told them that he did not feel like eating that day," said Maria.

Heading: HC allows 7-yr-old to pursue studies after father withdraws petition against school - Indian Express
Content:
Next time when you get onto a BEST bus and find an entire row of seats removed, don't be surprised. It's an endeavor to increase the capacity of buses.

This move came into effect after Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Sanjay Barve made a presentation proposing modifications in seating arrangements in the Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST) undertaking's buses and the suburban trains at a brainstorming session organised by Unified Mumbai Metropolitan Transport Authority (UMMTA) in August. During the presentation, Barve said, "With the proposed modifications, the carrying capacity of BEST buses and suburban trains will be doubled." According to senior official at Mantralaya, in the UMMTA meeting, it was decided that the BEST and railways should consider the proposed modifications on a pilot basis.

Meanwhile, the BEST has geared up to modify the seating arrangements in the buses. According to the proposal, the buses will be having only a row of seats while rest of the seats would make way for standees. "A bus has been already prepared for this pilot project. But, when this bus would be rolled out on the roads is not decided yet as we're awaiting a go ahead from the Regional Transport Office (RTO)," said Uttam Khobragade, general manager, BEST.

"A single-decker BEST bus has a seating capacity ranging from 49 to 51, while it can accommodate as many as 20-21 standees. During peak hours, the number of standees will be high," said Khobragade.

According to a senior official in the transport planning department of the undertaking, over 25 seats have been removed in the bus prepared the pilot project. "It would definitely increase the carrying capacity of the buses as there would be more space to accommodate standees," an official said on condition of anonymity.

The official also said that if the pilot project was a success, the undertaking could possibly earn more for the cash-strapped transport body. While Barve said if the passengers responded positively to the step taken by the undertaking, idea of increasing the carrying capacity could be taken to the next level.

Heading: Five arrested for robbing gold merchant - Indian Express
Content:
A seven-year-old boy will be able to pursue his studies in the the Bright Start school at Gowalia Tank in the current academic year, after the management of the school agreed before the Bombay High Court that it would allow the boy to complete his academic year, if his father withdrew all the petitions filed against the school management.

Mehta, a school trustee, informed a division bench of justice P B Majmudar and justice Amjad Sayed on Thursday that the school management would allow the boy to complete his academic year in standard two on a condition that his father withdrew all petitions made against the school management. He also said that the boy would have to find another school in the next academic year. Considering the request made by Mehta, the court amicably settled the case.

Earlier, the court had directed the Bright Start Fellowship School, Gowalia Tank, and the boy's parents to end their ongoing legal battle for the sake of the child's future. The bench had then observed, "This child will remain illiterate for whole life in this battle between you (the school management and the parents)." The court had also sought help from Advocate General Ravi Kadam on actual rules. Following this, the school was asked to admit students.

According to the petition, the parents alleged that the school had refused to admit their son in standard 1. The petition also alleged that since their son was a student of the kindergarten section of the school, he was eligible for the admission in standard 1.

The parents also alleged that as he enquired about the heavy fees collected by the school and justification regarding the same, their son was singled out and harassed by the teachers.

However, the school management said that the child was refused admission due to the misconduct of the parents, who allegedly assaulted the school staff and a teacher.

In June 2007, the High Court ordered the school to admit the child, but the school authorities ignored the order. In November, 2007, the HC again directed the school to implement the order. Then, the school authorities moved the Supreme Court challenging the HC order by filing a special leave petition (SLP). "On January 3, the apex court observed that there was no need to interfere in the HC order and dismissed the school's SLP. Following this, the school had admit the child to standard 1. But, the parents were again informed on February 5 that the child would not be allowed to pursue his studies in the school," the petitioners told the court.

"We moved the court again against the school authorities after the school had refused to allow the child to continue his studies in standard II. The High Court order had mentioned that the child be admitted to standard I and the SC had passed its order citing the HC order," the petitioners said.

Heading: Minor scuffle leads to murder - Indian Express
Content:
The Thane police on Thursday arrested a gang of five for allegedly robbing a gold merchant of his valuables on September 2. The complainant, Girish Dhananjay Baikerikar, was cornered and robbed while he was on his way to deliver ornaments to a client. He then registered a complaint with the Kalwa police station following which the accused were arrested by the Thane police Crime Branch, Unit 1. The police recovered gold worth Rs 10 lakh from the arrested accused.

After Baikerikar approached the police, a police team visited the spot where he was robbed. Subsequently a source tipped the police that one Kiran Aanwekar and his gang committed the robbery. The police then traced the gang's whereabouts and arrested five men identified as Aanwekar, Farukh alias Raj Hafiz Khan, Mohsin Mokim Khan, Ranjit alias Bunty Nair, Vipul Vilas Pradhan and also recovered 432 gm of gold from them.

Joint Commissioner of Police, Crime Branch, Prashant Borde said that the gang also confessed to robbing another gold merchant Prakash Revankar in July. In connection to this case, the police arrested Suresh Khandagale, Atul More alias Mowgli and Mahesh Shinde, all three hailing from Airoli. Gold weighing 149 gm and 680 milligram were recovered from them.

According to the police, Aanwekar, a native from Karnataka has four brothers, two of whom are involved in the gold business. "Investigation has revealed that Aanwekar instituted two groups for carrying out both the robberies. While five of the arrested accused robbed Baikerikar near Mhape MIDC, three others robbed Revankar near Kalwa Railway Colony," said Borde.

Heading: Tie-up for bank polls could redefine local politics - Indian Express
Content:
An argument over the shirking of duties regarding mandal work turned ugly in Tardeo when Jerry Fernandez, a 37-year-old man working as a driver was killed by Deepak Chavan, a 22-year-old unemployed youth staying in the same locality in the early hours of Thursday morning at the Om Mitra Mandal Ganpati mandal in Tardeo.

Senior Police Inspector Vilas Joshi from the Tardeo police station said, "According to Deepak, both the accused and the deceased stayed in the same locality and had been part of the organizing team of the area's Ganpati mandal since the past many years. As Chavan was one of the youngest organizers, he was generally given leg work assignments regarding mandal work. However, for the past many days, Jerry had been displeased with Chavan as the latter had been shirking work."

According to the police on late Wednesday night, the two had been sitting in the mandal to keep an eye on the idol when they got engaged in an argument with Jerry scolding Chavan for not doing his work properly. The argument soon escalated and they started inflicting blows on each other. An enraged Chavan picked up a piece of bamboo lying nearby and struck Jerry on his head severely. As a bleeding Jerry was writhing on the ground, Chavan picked up a large rock lying in the rubble of a construction site and smashed it on his head. Chavan then fled from the spot. A few other members of the mandal who were alerted by the sounds of the fight discovered Jerry and took him to Nair hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries later in the morning.

A case of murder was registered against Chavan and after due inquiries he was arrested from a relative's place in Dombivali on Friday morning. A police official from Tardeo police station who had been in the arresting team said on condition of anonymity, "When we arrested Chavan, he was absolutely remorseless about his act. When we interrogated him, he confessed that he had a case against him at the Samta Nagar police station though we are not aware of the details of that case yet."

Jerry is survived by his wife and 7-year-old son who were unavailable for comment as they had gone to attend some funeral ceremonies. A member of the mandal who had known both the accused and the deceased said, "Usually, there is a group of 6-7 people who remain near the idol for safe-guarding during nights. But that night, only Jerry and Chavan were there ."

Heading: Tight security, traffic curbs  for Ananth Chaturdashi - Indian Express
Content:
New equation in Vasai-Vihar after Vivek Pandit, Hitendra Thakur join hands for Coop Bank elections

The recent alliance between social worker-turned-politician Vivek Pandit and Vasai-Virar's Hitendra Thakur, forged on the eve of the Bassein Catholic Co-operative Bank's elections on Wednesday, is likely to have an impact on local politics as well.

Pandit has managed to broker a new alliance between Congress-affiliated Sahakar panel and Samvichari panel, which is affiliated to Thakur's Vasai Vikas Mandal, along with a handful of independents that had its impact on the bank's election for the post of chairman and vice-chairman.

With the help of the support of Thakur's Samvichari panel, Domnika Dabre was on Wednesday elected as the chairman of the bank — the first woman to do so in the bank's history. The bank has deposits over 1000 crore and is a popular bank in the Christian dominated Vasai belt.

The results of the bank's elections would not have been so significant had it not been for the emergence of a new political equation.

The development gains more significance as Pandit and his Shramjivi Sanghatna was considered as the last bastion of socio-political resistance against the Thakur gang in the Vasai-Virar belt. Moreover, the bank was the only frontier that had not been infiltrated by the Thakur gang in the Vasai-Virar belt.

Speaking to Newsline, Pandit said: "I had unsuccessfully tried for alliance of Congress and Janata Dal for the election of the chairman and vice-chairman. I told local leader Gilbert Mendonca and Hitendra Thakur to put aside their political differences and support the cause of the bank. They responded to my appeal and extended unconditional support."

Pandit clarified that he was still against anti-social and criminal elements. "I believe in supporting those people who do good work. I appreciate Thakur for his unconditional support," he said, and added that he has not come across any criminal activities of the Thakur gang in recent times. `

Heading: Krishna goes free, Rajkumar gets bail as CBI draws a blank: So who killed Arushi, Hemraj? - Indian Express
Content:
The Joint Commissioner of Police, (Traffic), Sanjay Barve, while addressing a press conference at the traffic police headquarters on Friday, outlined the traffic and security arrangements made for an exceptionally huge turnout for Anant Chaturdashi.

"We are expecting atleast 1,500 large idols and 2,500 domestic idols in Girgaum Chowpatty alone and since it is a Sunday there will be a heavy flow of regular traffic as well," said Barve. The traffic police have set aside certain roads as one way and will even block some other roads to prevent traffic congestion. Roads leading to visarjan points will be open only for passage of idols. In order to facilitate coordination, 5 control rooms and 37 watchtowers will be set up. The police will be aided by NGOs and other volunteers.

Keeping in mind the security arrangements, the police have installed 81 CCTV cameras along the important Visarjan routes with 4 of them dedicated to Laalbaghcha Rajas route. "No cars without idols will be allowed to enter the beaches. Firecrackers will also be prohibited. We appeal to the people not to bring big bags to ensure that checking does not take time," said Barve. In order to facilitate a smooth flow of traffic, the police have directed the cars to exit from the left and trucks from the right after visarjan. "We have requested drivers not to leave their vehicles as it will be difficult for us to move them later. We have also requested all the people with small domestic idols to try and finish immersions by 6 pm to avoid unnecessary congestion," he added. Some roads that should be avoided during the day are the Jagganath Shankar Sheth Road, Tilak Bridge, LBS Marg Mulund as these are closed for regular vehicular traffic.

Pandita Ramabai Road will be one way up till Nanachowk from its junction with NS Patkar Marg. Bellasis Bridge will be one way towards Mumbai Central Junction. Southbound traffic at PD'Mello Road will have to use the northbound carriage from Kaklidge Chowk to Wadi Bunder. Dr BA Road will be one way from Supari Baug to Kings Circle and Annie Besant Road will be closed from Worli Naka to Haji Ali. In the suburbs, Juhu Road will be one way till Juhu Tara Road which in turn will be one way till Centaur. There will be parking restrictions on Jagannath Shankar Sheth Marg, Grant Road Bridge, Walkeshwar Road, Netaji Subhas Marg, Pandita Ramabai Marg, Marishi Karve Road, SV Road and Juhu Tara Road.

Heading: Day after he hit and fled, BMW driver caught, out on bail - Indian Express
Content:
The special CBI court on Friday granted bail to the remaining two accused in the Noida double murder case: Krishna, a compounder at the Talwar couple's dental clinic, and Rajkumar, help at family friends Duranis' household.

The bail comes after the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) failed to provide evidence against any accused in the May 15 murder of teenager Arushi and Talwars' domestic help Hemraj. The third accused, Vijay Mandal, a help in the Talwar neighbourhood, was granted bail on September 4.

While the court of Special Magistrate (CBI) Sapna Mishra Tripathi granted Krishna bail, Rajkumar's bail petition was accepted by Sessions Judge Rama Jain even before his 90-day gets over. Rajkumar was arrested on June 27. Both were asked to furnish two sureties of Rs 25,000 each, and a personal bond of similar amount.

Though CBI again tried to convince the court by calling it a sensitive case but lack of evidence went against the agency. Opposing Rajkumar's bail, senior CBI counsel R K Saini told the court, "The accused is a resident of Nepal and once he escapes to Nepal, nabbing him will become tough once CBI is able to get the evidence. Rajkumar can also destroy evidence. We have scientific evidence against him in which he has confessed to his involvement in the murder."

But Rajkumar's counsel Naresh Yadav told the court that CBI has not furnished evidence against the accused: "If Rajkumar wanted to escape to Nepal, he would have done so long ago."

With today's bails, all accused in the double murder case are now out. Arushi's father Dr Rajesh Talwar was the first accused; he was arrested by Noida police on May 23. He was released on bail on July 11 following a clean chit from CBI.

CBI officials said they would keep an eye on Rajkumar and Krishna's activities now that they are free.

Family reunion
GHAZIABAD: 8 pm, Wednesday. Krishna, co-accused in the Arushi-Hemraj murder case, comes out of Dasna Jail after 90 days in detention. Heading straight towards his niece Sunita and brother-in-law Bhim Singh Thapa, the erstwhile compounder at Dr Nupur and Rajesh Talwar's clinic claims: "I am innocent. I was trapped in the case by the CBI."

Sunita reiterates the family's faith in the judiciary, something, she stresses, has not dimmed even once since Krishna's arrest on June 13. "He (Krishna) is innocent," she says. "and we are saying this from Day One. We missed him terribly; it's a joyous reunion tonight."

But Rajkumar, another accused in the case, may have to wait till Monday to get out of jail, for his family is still striving to arrange for the surety amount of Rs 75,000, defence counsel Naresh Yadav says.

The Durani couple, Rajkumar's employers before his arrest, refused to help him. "The CBI has not given a clean chit to Rajkumar yet," Anita Durani, Talwars' friend, says. "We will not take him back (as yet)." The Duranis had claimed Rajkumar was innocent when he was picked up by the CBI on June 27.

Heading: Dengue: 21 more, total past 200 - Indian Express
Content:
Management student Utsav Bhasin, who crashed his father's BMW car into a motorcycle in the early hours of Thursday, was picked up from the bus terminus at Kashmere Gate, the police have said.

He was at the inter-state bus terminus (ISBT), trying to catch a ride to Chandigarh at 7 am on Friday, officers said. He was presented in a city court later which granted him bail on a bond of Rs 20,000.

Investigations by the South Delhi police have found Bhasin was driving his father's BMW-525i at a speed of over 100 kilometres when he hit the motorcycle near the Moolchand flyover, critically injuring its two riders Mrigank Srivastava and Anuj Chauhan. Both are admitted in AIIMS. Srivastava, who was riding the bike, is recovering but Chauhan's condition is very critical.

Deputy Commissioner (South) H G S Dhaliwal said Bhasin has been booked under Section 279 for rash and negligent driving. "Shortly after the arrest, we medically examined him to check if he was drunk the night before," Dhaliwal added. Officers said Bhasin has a driving licence that expires in 2019.

Bhasin has maintained before the police that he did not drink that night. He said he used the car whenever his father went abroad — this time to China. He was with his girlfriend when the accident took place, officers said, though they had earlier suspected his companion was sister Sakshi.

Bhasin had left home on Wednesday evening at 7 pm for a drive around the city. He told officers he had dropped in at 24/7 — a provisional store at Greater Kailash II — to buy hotdogs. This shop is open at all times.

A senior officer said: "During interrogation, Bhasin said the vehicle's speed was under control and that the motorcycle suddenly sprung up before him from nowhere. He could not stop in time and ended up hitting it. Judging from where the mobike was found, it is clear the two-wheeler had got entangled in the car's wheels and was dragged some distance."

Bhasin has also admitted he panicked after the accident and that his first instinct was to escape. But the safety airbags in the car had exploded from the impact of the crash, blocking his vision. Bhasin could only drive a little distance before he hit a pole, before the car clambered on top of the pavement.

Auto-driver Vijay Kumar witnessed the incident. He saw Bhasin and his friend break open a window and get out of the car. They then flagged down an auto and left the spot. Officers said Bhasin dropped his friend home before he reached his West Punjabi Bagh residence.

The BMW (HR 26 AK/0020) was registered with Golden Rolls Ltd in Sonepat, a company owned by the boy's industrialist father R K Bhasin.

Bhasin is an alumni of Delhi Public School and was studying at the Institute for Integrated Learning in Management (IILM), Ghaziabad. He was pursuing a degree in Business Administration.

Heading: Gurgaon pubs tap into Euro culture, to make their own beer now - Indian Express
Content:
With 21 more cases of dengue viral fever reported on Friday, the total number of cases reported so far this season crossed the 200 mark. And with their inspection staff on mass strike, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) is grappling with the problem of containing mosquito breeding.

"Twenty-one more patients tested positive for the virus today; it takes the number of afflicted persons to 209 this season," MCD's health committee chairman V K Monga said. While five fresh cases were reported from Rohini, three each were found in Shahadra, Civil Lines and South Delhi. The remaining cases were detected from Narela, Najafgarh and West Delhi.

This comes at a time when 2,500 mosquito-breeding checking employees are on strike. The workers, employed with MCD on contract basis, are demanding regularisation of their jobs. "It is still not an epidemic situation as cases are expected to peak during this time of the year," Monga said.

Heading: Dog skin for tiger’s, fake market thriving in Capital - Indian Express
Content:
THE WEEKEND STORY: Brewing high-brew to suit your taste

Forget the can, and certainly the bottle. You can now take a swig from the barrel.

Come October, and a new trend in tippling will be established in Gurgaon for those who are connoisseurs of beer, and yet indulgent of the belly.

Known as micro brewpubs, two of its kind will open shop at the Ambience Mall and in Galaxy Hotel, just off the Gurgaon Expressway. In concept, these pubs will brew the beer on the spot, adjusting the quality of the brew — in flavour, bitterness and viscosity — according to the needs of the customer. The focus will be on the ale's style rather than on its mass appeal.

Germany, which has a tradition of such brewpubs or brauhaus, is lending technology to Delhi-based Rockman Breweries. Two German companies, Lowenbrau Buttenheim and Kaspar Schulz, will collaborate with Rockman. The other Indian company to dabble in this independently will be the Galaxy Hotel. The main attraction of these micro brewpubs, proprietors said, will be to serve fresh and non-pasteurised beer, unlike the bottled ones that contain preservatives.

Rockman's managing director C S Agarwal said, "The ingredients behind the beer will include hops, malt, yeast and water, and customers will be able to watch their ale brew."

Haryana is the first state in the country to have opened its doors to brewpubs, courtesy its new excise policy that allows microbreweries for an additional Rs 2.5 lakh as annual license fee, said the state's deputy excise and taxation commissioner Ashok Sharma. He said, "Several hotels, bars and pubs are interested in serving freshly-brewed beer. Microbreweries and beer gardens will be a hit in Gurgaon."

Other states also wish to cash in and those like Punjab, Maharashtra and Goa might soon change their respective excise and taxation policies to accommodate this trend. In Europe, microbreweries have existed for hundreds of years and are classified as those which produce less, cater to a small area, to the informed beer drinker, and often have pubs attached to the breweries.

Adding to European technology here, will be home-made Indian imagination. Rockman introduces a copper device, something familiar to a vending machine, filled with warm water. The beer will be made to flow out of this if one prefers it at a particular temperature. The ale can also be served directly from the barrel.

If it is beer and football in Europe, it is beer and cricket at the Galaxy Hotel's pub — sofas that look like the crescent of the keeper's gloves, umpire-hat ice buckets et al, said senior executive H N Nautyal.

Heading: Cheer for Lear - Indian Express
Content:
A 'tiger' skin, which eventually turned out to be fake, has only served to blow the lid off the illegal trade in animal skin and bones taking place in the Capital.

Acting on a tip-off, the Crime Branch of Delhi Police found animal skin and bones being peddled as tiger skin, in Nehru Place on Thursday.

Officials brought in from the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau found that the painted skin was actually of a dog. No arrests have been made.

"Investigations showed the canines and jaw were a dog's," says WCCB Deputy Director Ramesh Pandey.

"The skin was being sold as real tiger skin. The claws and the teeth were also being sold as those of a tiger's. This shows that Delhi is a hub of wildlife crime and many buyers and middlemen operate in the city. All illegal wildlife products from Punjab, Haryana, Himachal and Uttarakhand find their way to Delhi," he said.

On August 1, the bureau had seized a leopard skin in Delhi.

Though peddlers who sell fake wildlife parts cater to an illegal market, there are no provisions under the Wildlife Protection Act to arrest them, as the Act only covers 'wildlife'.

Under the 1972 Act, it is illegal and punishable to trade in tiger parts.

"Since the skin turned out to be fake, we have not registered a case. This is not even cheating, but an attempt to cheat and there is no case," says DCP (Crime Branch) Neeraj Thakur.

The high demand for wild animal parts has pushed an industry bent on creating fakes, say officials.

"There are people who specialise in creating tiger skin that looks genuine, with stripes or spots and amulets with teeth or claws of a common animal. Only a person with specialised knowledge would know the difference between a fake and an original," Pandey says.

Earlier this year, two fake tiger skins were found in Wayanad in Karnataka and later in Chhattisgarh.

These skins usually find their way to China and Tibet, where they are used for ornamental purposes, while other parts are used in traditional eastern medicine.

Heading: Double Trouble - Indian Express
Content:
He may have bowed down to MNS chief Raj Thackeray's diktats on free speech, however, actor Amitabh Bachchan remains unflustered by the storm The Last Lear has created. "There is no harm if one renders an apology. It does not make one small," clarified the baritoned Bachchan, at the premiere of the movie held in Delhi's Select CityWalk. (The premiere in Mumbai was cancelled.) The film released yesterday. Dressed formally in a black suit, Bachchan came accompanied by director Rituparno Ghosh and co-stars Arjun Rampal, Divya Dutta and Shefali Shah. Ghosh's debut English venture, The Last Lear tells the story of a 65-year-old (Harry) played by Bachchan, a veteran Shakespearean actor who detests cinema, and considers it an apology for art.

Arjun Rampal plays a director (Sidharth) who tries to convince Bachchan to act in his film.

The Last Lear is an interaction between Rampal's character and Bachchan's. "This talented repertoire of actors have given birth to my vision through their talent," said Ghosh.

Critics are raving about Bachchan's performance in the movie and appreciation has been coming from as far off as the London Film Festival.

It's been a big break for Rampal, who shares a lot of screen space with Bachchan, and finally seems to be coming into his own, as an actor. "It is a relief that finally I'm getting noticed for my acting abilities rather than my looks," he grinned. A love for Shakespeare, Bachchan says, runs in his family. "Many years ago my mother directed Macbeth and the play was inaugurated by the first PM of India, Pandit Nehru in Delhi," said Bachchan. The tradition continues.

Heading: Hue & Call - Indian Express
Content:
Season six of MTV Roadies promises many more twists, and twice as much of Raghu Ram as well

If you found one Raghu Ram a bit hard to take on MTV's Roadies, there's some bad news in store. On the sixth season of the dramatic adventure reality show Raghu's identical twin Rajeev Laxman will join him to create even more hell for the contestants. "Every year we take the show to another level. This time we have upped the stakes even further," smiles Raghu, the irreverent boss of the Roadies, and Associate VP, MTV shows. With the number of roadies increased to 20 and the prize money doubled to Rs 10 lakhs, contestants are in for hell Down Under with difficult tasks on the deadly terrains of Austalia and biting observations and sheer wrath from the Raghu-Rajeev duo.

Rajeev— who has been part of the casting process of the Roadies for the last four years— agreed to even turn bald for the show on Raghu's insistence. Hard to tell the two apart, Rajeev will now be introduced to the viewers for the first time. "Roadies is not just about the money. It's a badge that makes people discover a side to them that they didn't even know of," adds Rajeev, who appears to be almost as aggressive as his twin. "Actually I'm more violent and Raghu is more aggressive," smiles Rajeev wickedly. "But we use these characteristics only to push the buttons of the contestants to get their reaction."

But what really prompted them to bring the twist of the twins? "Over the past years people have started observing my behavioral pattern. So essentially, now with both of us appearing on the show, the contestants will not know who they are dealing with," adds Raghu with a smile.

While it's the curses and abuses by Raghu that have made contestants quake with fear and seethe in anger in the past, some of the past roadies have overcome it all and even found alternative careers in the course of it. While Rannvijay, Bani J and Ayushmann all became VJs on the channel, others like Ashutosh Kaushik went on to participate in Big Boss and Shambhavi Sharma has been roped in for a Suniel Shetty movie.

However, MTV Roadies— the only Indian format to be licensed abroad by the ARY Pakistan— will journey through every place from Great Barrier Reef to the Great Outback this year. "It's a scientific fact that there are more ways of dying of natural causes in Australia than anywhere else in the world," quips Ashish Patil, GM, MTV India. While their parameters to zero in on the tasks include dangerous topography, Patil agrees imbibing the local culture is as important. While there might be the Roadies Cheat Code DVD available in the market to crack the auditions, Raghu still warns, "Fakes not allowed. I don't like people who plan. You need to be real and we'll take it from there."

If you thought it was Raghu walking in to twist things at Splitsvilla, MTV's reality show about love, here's a trivia —it was Rajeev. Expect the unexpected.

Delhi auditions from October 3- 5 at NCUI Auditorium

Heading: Booze News - Indian Express
Content:
Inspired by a film, an art show presents the various shades of sociopolitical turmoil

It was in 2003 that art critic Ina Puri first watched Uttara, Buddhadev Dasgupta's reel version of author Samaresh Bose's tale of violence and lawlessness in an ostensibly peaceful setting. She remembers being spellbound through the movie set in Purulia district in Bengal and realising back then that every frame in the screenplay was a work of art.
