Five years later the film has stayed with her, and now as her tribute to the classic narrative, she has got five artists — Manu Parekh, Valsan Kolleri, Jagannath Panda, Riyas Komu and Golak Khandual — to transform it from the 70mm screen to their artwork. The result is on display in an exhibition titled Urgent Conversations currently on at Art Alive Gallery. "The show has been on my mind for two years now. It is an outcome of the discussions I had with the artists. The focus is on the need for an urgent conversation required to discuss several sociopolitical issues," says Puri.

So CDs of the film were sent to each artist and Puri arranged for some of them to interact with the filmmaker. "This helped them to discuss the subject and understand his perspective better," smiles the curator as she points out how each artist has interpreted the film in his own manner and made it an integral part of his artwork.

While Komu has made use of some scenes from one movie in his installation titled The Other Village, Panda has zeroed in on violence-plagued society in The Urban Hooligan series that includes watercolour on paper and a video.

Dasgupta's film is being screened in one corner of the gallery and a wall close-by has Manu Parekh's canvases depicting associated concerns through hard-hitting imagery painted in bright shades. Artist Golak Khandual may not be directly inspired by Uttara but his work is closely associated with another Dasgupta film Bagh Bahadur. His photographs of the Bagh dancers from Orissa, dressed in opulent costumes, calls attention to the need to support the neglected art and the urgency to conserve tigers and forests. "The exhibition will only initiate the discussion, which hopefully will continue beyond it," notes Khandual.

The exhibition is on till September 20

Heading: Sparkling Smile - Indian Express
Content:
Jack Daniel's 158th birthday bash at Delhi's Forbidden City, Indo Chine, rocked to the groovy sounds of Metallica's new album, Death Magnetic, amid muted lights and exotic cocktails. Amrit Kiran Singh, VP, Brown & Foreman, played perfect host with wife Farah to guests mostly from the fashion fraternity and the diplomatic community. In typical JD style, the cake was cut by five of the prettiest girls of the evening.

Models Joey Mathews, Sonalika Sahay, Vasuki Sunkavalli, Diva and Aanchal Uberoi got the party going on the dance floor to heavy metal beats. Part of a month long programme, which has turned into a cult event across the world, the India leg includes JD parties in Delhi, Mumbai and Bangalore.

Heading: Attack of the young guns - Indian Express
Content:
If flaunting a crystal ring on your finger is too passé, now you have the option of flashing it on your teeth. Weird though it sounds, jewellery for your teeth is the newest fad in the fashion circuit these days.

"We use pure Austrian Swarovski crystals for teeth jewellery. It is a very simple and safe procedure that takes 10 minutes and the crystal can stay for a month on an average. However, if you consume less acidic food, it could last for eight months," said Madhuruchi Lamba, president, ConfiSmile at the launch of The ConfiSmile Oral Hygiene kiosk at Select CityWalk Mall recently.

The teeth jewellery procedure costs Rs 2,000 and you can choose between white and pink crystals according to your taste. Greeshum Panesar, a 19- year-old college student, was flaunting a chic pink crystal on one of her incisors. "The crystal makes me look and feel cool. And, of course, it makes you want to smile more often," she laughed.

Besides the teeth jewellery procedure, the kiosk will also offer quick and painless cosmetic oral hygiene solutions like teeth whitening and breath management. "The kiosk will fill the need for an easily accessible platform," says Lamba adding that for longer dental treatments, The ConfiSmile Dental Spa will open in November at Lajpat Nagar Market. So much for that dreaded visit to the dentist.

Heading: A quick dash to the Taj and some football lessons for Swiss schoolboys - Indian Express
Content:
20-year-old Bhullar opens up five-shot three-round lead, Sandhu, 19, turns in day's best card

Big hitters lend a primitive charm to this otherwise sophisticated game, their bludgeon-like drivers threatening to launch balls into orbit. However, it hasn't just been raw power that has made Gaganjeet Bhullar's tee shots a treat to watch in the AIS Open golf tournament, but also his immaculate swing. For example, his tee shot on the par-three third landed just inches from the pin to send the spectators, although not many, into rapturous applause.

But not everyone was enjoying the spectacle — definitely not his competitors, who've seen him making a mockery of the competition over the last two days. Having taken sole lead on Thursday with a record-breaking nine-under 63, Bhullar all but slammed the door shut on the rest of the field with a blistering six-under 66 at the Golden Greens golf course on Friday.

Gunning for his first win as a professional, the 20-year-old from Kapurthala reeled off half-a-dozen birdies in a blemish-free third round to take his aggregate to 17-under 199 and open up a yawning five-shot lead. Rahul Ganapathy, who shot a two-under to total 12-under 204, was in second place with Ashok Kumar (68) and Feroze Ali Mollah (71) joint third at nine-under 207.

Bhullar picked up from where he had left on Thursday, holing in two birdies in the first three holes. And after the turn, it seemed he decided to trade only in birdies. Under a scorching afternoon sun, he sank in four in a row — from the 12th to 15th — and had near-misses on some of the other holes.

"The credit goes to my pre-shot routine," Bhullar said later. "I'm consistently hitting in regulation because of it. And my putting has also been great this week." However, he knows the job is not done yet. "I now need to keep my focus and stick to my routine. The key tomorrow will be to keep the ball in play."

Ganapathy, in the same group as Bhullar, was having trouble on the greens — with the leader slowly drifting further away, his putts repeatedly kept falling short. "I was reading the line well but the ball was stopping on the edge of the hole," he rued. "Bhullar played exceedingly well. He was hitting great and his putting was phenomenal. But anything could happen tomorrow. Golf is a funny game."

Who knows that better than Ajeetesh Sandhu. On a day when the young guns boomed, the 19-year-old from Chandigarh returned the best card — an eight-under 64. The funny part is that it came a day a nightmarish 80. "I drove really well today and made all the fairways. That set up a number of birdie opportunities. This was my best round as a pro and I'm now looking forward to a good finish," said Sandhu, who is playing only his sixth tournament as a professional.

Heading: Aqeel ends Prajnesh’s dream run in a hurry - Indian Express
Content:
In the 48-year long history of the Subroto Cup, teams from Israel, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Nepal have brought in the foreign element that is associated with big competitions. The 49th edition, though, apart from introducing a new preliminary format, has an unprecedented European participation — Kuesnacht FC, a Swiss club.

The idea behind inviting a European team was just exposure for the Indian teams as the visitors were here for two exhibition matches.

Benjamin Brown, Jake Knoepfel, Allain Stamm, Lorenz Gassitann are all school students, living in and around Zurich, and playing at their club.

The common reaction after their 3-0 victory over The Air Force School on Wednesday was: "We practice regularly and they (the Indian team) practice only for tournaments".

On Friday, though, the organisers decided to throw an all-star team against Kuesnacht FC, picking the best boys from Jharkhand, Sikkim and West Bengal's U-14 squads. While the 5-0 result favouring the Subroto XI reflected the overnight efforts to turn the tables, it opened up Markus Weber, the Swiss coach's eyes.

"Our opponents were too good today. Especially with their runs through the flanks. I think my boys were a bit tired too," Weber said.

Suddenly, all technical problems related to tackling and dodging that Weber was working on at clinics with the Indian boys seemed to have disappeared.

Benjamin, the skipper, and Allain, a striker, explained the defeat saying it was 'just a bad day at the office'. The quick trip to Agra on Thursday looked to have taken their energy away, and the sappy weather adding to the worries.

Fond memories
LEAVING out the one-win-one-loss record, though, the Swiss team's one-week tour of India will have a lot of fonder memories.

The word 'excitement' found numerous repetitions in coach Weber's description of the mood in the camp, irrespective of the results. If getting rid of their school bags for seven days was the reason during their journey, landing in India opened up a whole new world. If the weather was a bit 'heavy' on the boys, the Capital's temples and religious places made them get over it.

They braved a tour to Agra on Thursday and watching the Taj Mahal rising out of their books was perhaps the most exciting moment. For their little knowledge of English, Benjamin, Allain, Diogo Anlikar, Lorenz couldn't describe it better than calling it 'beautiful and white', but Weber expatiated on the 'excitement'.

"The kids have done a lot of reading on Taj Mahal, before going to Agra. And inside, it was crazy. There were so many things to see," Weber said. And the tour? "It was fun, but don't focus on the lessons. They will get over it, or understand it only after they get back home," Weber added.

Heading: Zaheer comes calling at Delhi net session - Indian Express
Content:
An open court, a chance to smash, and Aqeel Khan waiting resignedly for Prajnesh Gunneswaran to make it deuce as the player from Pakistan served for the first set — the Chennai youngster appeared to have worked out the point perfectly. Instead, he drilled the ball straight into the net.

That moment, perhaps, amplified many times over in Prajnesh's mind as he looked skywards in shock, summing up his morning at the DLTA courts on Friday. His semi-final of the $15,000 ITF Futures tournament ended in a tame 6-3, 6-2 defeat to Khan, and was most unlike his earlier dominant performances of the week.

Prajnesh was not in the best physical shape on Friday, and even though cramps had started affecting his opponent too towards the end of the match, the 19-year-old was in no condition to take advantage of Khan's restricted movement.

Last year's runner-up at the national championships would have wished for a better start to the match — wayward shots on his backhand caused him to concede his serve in only the second game.

In the second set, Prajnesh was broken in the first and third games as Khan set up a final meeting with top seed Peter Gojowcyk. The German defeated Chinese Taipei's Hsin-han Lee of Chinese Taipei 6-2, 6-1.

The doubles title was won by Ashutosh Singh and Sunil Kumar Sipaeya, who beat Divij Sharan and Vishnu Vardhan 6-2, 6-2.

Heading: Focus on technology, improved road safety before 2010 Games - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi team had a surprise guest at their nets on Friday evening: Zaheer Khan, the India paceman who they have to encounter in two weeks' time, dropped in to train with them in the build-up for the most high-profile domestic event in the last three decades. "Bus Irani (Cup) ki tayyari kar rahe hai," he says with a big smile.

Zaheer, who was in Delhi on a personal visit, didn't bowl at the nets but completed his prescribed fitness regime before stretching out on the sidelines and chatting with Delhi players.

"By the way, it's very hot in Baroda during this time." His good friend and former new ball partner Ashish Nehra was quick to intervene, "Are you telling us or scaring us," he joked even as players debated the strange weather patterns during this part of the year.

Ishant at full burst
His current partner in the Indian team, Ishant Sharma, made an appearance at the nets today as well and bowled two short spells at full burst as Zaheer watched him closely. "Zaq bhai, I will see you at the Irani match," he said, looking completely fit and declaring his intention of playing the September 15 match against the visiting Pakistan team.

The Sui Northern Gas Pipeline Limited team, Pakistan's Qaid-e-Azam champions this year, will arrive in the Capital on Saturday evening. Delhi, meanwhile, have decided to take a day off from practice and both teams will have a final net session on Sunday morning. Virat Kohli, who returned from India A duty, will join the team on Sunday.

Coach Vijay Dahiya is hoping to field their full-strength side though there are still doubts over Virender Sehwag, who skipped practice today and is still rehabilitating from an ankle injury. Gautam Gambhir is on a holiday after a hectic international season.

Heading: Buying a home? Check if previous owner has cleared all tax arrears - Indian Express
Content:
With an eye on the upcoming Commonwealth Games, the Delhi Traffic Police is planning to introduce advanced systems in communication and computers for traffic management in the Capital. The system, called the Intelligent Transport System or ITS, aims at cutting commuting time.

"The Commonwealth Games are likely to require a special emphasis on the regulation of additional flow of traffic, especially in routes of athletes or roads leading to games venues," said S N Shrivastava, Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic) at the ongoing Safety Convention 2008, organised by Institute of Engineers.

More than 200 safety experts and engineers are taking part in the two-day convention. According to Shrivastava, the ITS will help in reducing traffic jams, through the use of loop detectors, traffic cameras, changeable message signs, transit location systems, electronic traffic traveller information displays and traffic operation systems. He said unlike the present system, where the operation of traffic lights is automatic for a fixed time period, or manual during peak hours, electronic sensors at major crossings will regulate signals according to traffic congestion. The ITS will help in reducing accidents and delays.

Signal timings of over 100 traffic junctions are to be adjusted in accordance with traffic volume to ease congestion. Six disaster management vehicles are to be set aside for meeting road accidents.

Critical questions were also raised about the incomplete implementation of the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) system in Delhi. Prof P K Sikdar, former director, Central Road Research Institute, said while BRT had been working successfully in various countries, the lack of its popularity in Delhi could be due to a partial implementation of the system.

Heading: Chandela quits BJP, after flak from party - Indian Express
Content:
You have bought your dream home with the sale deed clearly reading "the property is free from all kinds of encumbrances and burdens". But you need to hold back and ask your civic body first if all the property taxes till the date of the agreement have been paid by the previous owner. The burden to pay would pass on to you if he had shirked payment. Reason: the property tax on land or the building, and the liability to pay would travel with transfer.

As the civic body was not a party to the sale deed between the two sides, it cannot be made to suffer the financial loss owing to the transaction, according to legal logic.

A city court has sounded a note of caution for all such prospective property buyers, who miss out on making necessary inquiries regarding the tax arrears while striking deals.

Clearing the air on the contentious issue as to whether the new owner could be made accountable to pay taxes which had accrued to the previous title-holder, Additional District Judge (ADJ) Kamini Lau has said property taxes had to be recovered from the new owner as the his title with respect to the land or building would also transfer the burden upon him.

"Since property tax constitutes the first charge upon the land or building and because property is fastened with this liability, the liability travels with it. The transferee is liable to pay property tax due not only for the period subsequent to transfer in his favour but even to the period anterior to the transfer," observed the court, reading from a Supreme Court judgement.

ADJ Lau said the primary liability to pay the taxes was upon the lessor, who has or is entitled to let off a building but if he had failed to do so, it can very well be recovered from the occupier. The occupier then would have to take legal recourse to get reimbursed the amount from the previous owner.

Way out? Ask the previous owner to send a notice to the civic body asking it to record your name as the new owner so that your liability starts from the date of the execution of the deed. Unless the authority is intimated about the transfer, all the notices served to the previous owner would be deemed to be served upon you and the accountability with respect of taxes would mount.

The observations came as the court decided an appeal by the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) against a lower court's order.

The lower court had directed the MCD to mutate a property bought by Sukhbir Singh Behl in Bulwara Road without asking him to pay the house tax ensuing before July 1990, when he had purchased the house.

MCD claimed in the appeal that the law was clear in this regard that the tax was on the property and not on any individual and since Behl had the title, he had to clear the arrears before the property could be mutated in his name. The civic body further said it was never officially informed about the transaction so that it could change its records.

ADJ Lau found substance in MCD's contentions and said Behl, a lawyer, would have to pay the arrears of Rs 20,473 in accordance with the provisions of Delhi Municipal Corporation Act for mutation of property in his name.

Heading: At AIIMS, BMW victim in coma, family, friends - Indian Express
Content:
In a blow to the BJP on the last day of the monsoon session in the Delhi Assembly, party MLA Dayanand Chandela submitted his resignation to Speaker Chaudhary Prem Singh. Stung by criticism from party colleagues after his speech in the Assembly appreciating the Congress government for regularising unauthorised colonies on Wednesday, Chandela decided to call it quits on Friday.

"I do not believe you need to criticise every move of the party in power. I think the Congress move to distribute provisional regularisation certificates to unauthorised colonies is for the welfare of the people and should not be panned," Chandela said, speaking to the media. Chandela, had contested the last elections on a BJP ticket from Khayala.

Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit, however, was tight-lipped. "I just know he has resigned. It is too early to comment on whether he is joining us or not. But he is welcome," Dikshit said.

Chandela's dramatic move has triggered speculations. BJP insiders claim Chandela would not have managed a ticket this time due to his bitter relations with senior Delhi BJP leaders.

The boundaries of his constituency have altered drastically after the delimitation notification. His Vishnu Garden constituency now includes a large portion of Tilak Nagar and Rajouri Garden with a strong Punjabi population. He would be clashing with Leader of the Opposition Jagdish Mukhi.

The Congress might be no cakewalk either. Chandela will face competition from Congress MLA Ramesh Lamba gunning for the same constituency.

Chandela has a turbulent history in the BJP. In 2004, he was expelled from the party after he openly criticised the party chief for not giving a ticket for the municipal corporation elections to his son Meghraj. Meghraj is now a Jharkhand Mukti Morcha councillor from Vishnu Garden in West Delhi.

The Chandelas take family politics to a different level altogether. With wife Dhanwati, Chandela has appeared in The Guinness Book of World Records in 1997 as the only married couple to have contested and won from two different wards in the same municipal elections. His daughter-in-law is also an MCD councillor.

Meanwhile, in the season of change, Shoaib Iqbal, the deputy speaker of Delhi Assembly who had contested the last election from JD(S) is now joining Lok Janshakti Party.

The LJP announced its first list before the Delhi Assembly Elections. The first list consists of 30 candidates, including 10 Muslims and two women.

Heading: Property dealer murdered in Rohini Sec 17 - Indian Express
Content:
At 12.30 pm, family members of Anuj Chauhan, hit by a BMW on Thursday night and admitted in a critical state at AIIMS, were told by a reporter that the youngster was "dead". Some 50 or so journalist friends of Chauhan, some here from Kanpur and Lucknow among other places, immediately went into a huddle, consoling each other.

But within minutes, doctors at the AIIMS Trauma Centre said Chauhan's situation was critical but he was still "alive". Chauhan's friends and family took a deep breath, hoping for the best all afresh.

"On our part," a doctor said, "we can only say he is alive. His situation has not improved."

In coma, Chauhan's cervical cord is "totally damaged", the doctor said.

"His nervous system is close to dead; he will probably collapse anytime due to other injuries he has sustained," another doctor, who did not want to be named, told Newsline.

The doctor said Chauhan's right ankle has been "brutally damaged", and he has sustained other grave injuries in the body, including a few fractures.

Mrigank Srivastava, a senior editor at a television channel till recently, was accompanying Chauhan last night when they were heading home after catching a late-night film show at PVR-Saket. He also sustained serious injuries but is now said to be out of danger.

Srivastava underwent operation at AIIMS at 8 pm today.

Family members of the two victims, meanwhile, have not initiated any legal action till now.

They alleged that Utsav Bhasin, who was steering the BMW car that hit the duo's motorcycle near Moolchand flyover in South Delhi, was "drunk".

A police official told Newsline that could have ascertained whether Bhasin was under the influence of alcohol when the accident occurred if "he had he been caught within 24 hours".

DCP (South) H G S Dhaliwal had told the media on Thursday that the BMW driver was in an inebriated state a1t the time. Bhasin was held at ISBT, Kashmere Gate, on Friday morning.

Chauhan's brother Kshitij said, "We do not know if the culprit will be punished — our priority and concern right now is Anuj should live on. He should not collapse, as the doctors fear could happen."

Heading: Missing student found dead in Noida park - Indian Express
Content:
Had objected to alleged killer's affair with friend's daughter

A 48-year-old man was shot following a dispute over an affair in Rohini Sector 17 in Northwest Delhi on Friday. Police said the deceased was allegedly having an affair with a 50-year-old divorcee, Renu Saini, and the accused was in a relationship with her daughter.

The accused, 30-year-old Robin, killed Munna Singh, a property dealer, after he objected to the relationship between Renu's daughter and Robin. Robin, police said, is a history sheeter.

"The incident took place in front of Renu's house in Pocket-A of Sector 17. Robin came on a motorcycle and pumped two bullets into Munna Singh at 8.15 am. Renu's son, Chintan, witnessed the murder and told police that he saw Robin roaming in the area on his motorcycle," a police officer said.

The victim was rushed to Baba Sahib Ambedkar Hospital for treatment, where he succumbed to injuries in the afternoon.

A case of murder has been registered against Robin who is absconding.

According to neighbours, Munna Singh was approaching a parked Maruti car owned by Saini.

"I heard gunshots. When I came out of my residence, I saw Munna bleeding profusely and trying to enter Renu's house. I raised alarm and called the Police Control Room. Along with a few other neighbours, I rushed him to hospital," said Neelam Kapoor, president of the Sector 17 Residents' Welfare Association.

Local residents said Singh had been visiting Renu Saini regularly for the last two-and-a-half years.

"Renu had divorced her husband, a lawyer, five years ago and was living with her two sons and a daughter. As far as I know, Munna and Renu were not happy about the relationship between Bhawna and Robin. Bhawna had eloped with Robin two or three times," said a neighbour, on condition of anonymity.

Police officers said Renu, her daughter Bhawna and son Chintan, have been detained for questioning.

The body of the deceased has been sent for postmortem.

"We have registered a murder case against Robin. We are trying to establish a motive for the murder," said DCP Northwest, N S Bundela.

Heading: JNU library to now get printer for Braille - Indian Express
Content:
When Abhishekh Kumar went missing on September 8 in front of ICICI Bank, where he went with his grandfather to withdraw money, no one in his family could even remotely imagine he would be found dead in the play area of a colony park of Sector 26, Noida.

The suicide note the police allegedly found on the 19-year-old-boy, blamed nobody for the extreme step that he took on Friday morning.

"We were sleeping when the police called us up around 6 am today to say that Abhishekh had committed suicide by hanging from the slide in the park," said Kishore Kumar, the deceased's uncle.

A former student of Amity International, Saket, the deceased had failed his class XII chemistry examinations, but when he filed for revaluation, his results were cleared.

"His result was not updated on the CBSE website. He had to go to the board's office the day he went missing. His suicide is a mystery. He was quiet and obedient," said his uncle whom he was living with for last two years in a rented apartment in Sector 26.

]A spokesperson for Amity International School said Kumar had taken provisional admission in a private engineering college in Jaipur.

Morning walkers found the body in the park, hanging by a plastic cable from the ladder of a slide around 5.30 am on Friday.

A complaint of the missing boy was registered by his maternal uncle on September 9 in police station of Sector 20.

Family members had no clue of his whereabouts for the last four days.

Father Shivdutta Kumar Sinha, a government employee, has been informed. His father had stayed on in Patna while his mother rushed to Noida on hearing that he was missing.

"There were no visible injury marks on his body which has been sent for autopsy and further investigation would be based on the report," said Ashok Tripathi, SP, City Noida.

Heading: Court to cops: Tell parents to keep guns off kids - Indian Express
Content:
After a 200-seat computer laboratory in February, the main library at Jawaharlal Nehru University is set for another technological upgrade. It is set to procure an advanced printer for the visually challenged — the printer has the technological prowess to translate English books and print them in Braille. Each line of Braille in the translated mode will be followed by its English translation.

The university's librarian, Krishan Gopal, claimed it would be the first such printer in India.

"We have placed the order to an agency in Dehradun, which will procure it from Switzerland," Gopal said. "This is one of our biggest efforts to improve facilities for the visually challenged students."

He said the printer would come in about a month's time, and would cost approximately Rs 4 lakh.

The university at present has a separate section for the visually challenged students called Helen Keller Unit, named after the world's first deafblind graduate. The centre has 20 computers equipped with special hardware and software, such as Kurzweil and JAWS among others. The two are screen-reading software that allow users to hear text read, as it appears on computer screen.

Besides the new printer, the library also plans to translate books into e-journals. For this digitisation process, Gopal said, the library would take help of the biggest names in the publishing industry — the likes of Oxford and Wiley.

Gopal said the library is also in the process of making some 11.5 lakh newspapers clippings into digital format; they will be available in the library's Newspaper Clipping Unit and the work is expected to be completed within a year.

Heading: ‘Verification of only 81% of draft electoral rolls possible’ - Indian Express
Content:
Incidents involving use of licensed weapons of a family member, at times by juveniles, have seen an increase in the past few months. Considering one such case as an example, a city court has asked the top brass of Delhi Police to develop awareness programmes for the safe custody of licensed weapons.

The April 16 order says, "It is directed to send the order to the Commissioner of Police, Additional Commissioner of Police (Licensing) and all district DCPs seeking their feedback and support to develop an awareness programme by way of public campaign and workshops for licence holders of weapons and firearms for the safe custody of weapons and also for curbing instances of crude display and use of weapons in public that in any case violate the terms and conditions subject to which these licences are granted."

The step was taken on the basis of an incident, which took place in April in Ashok Vihar area of northwest district. In the case, a juvenile had used his father's weapon in a shooting incident, injuring one person. Later, Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) took up the case.

The court had also ordered that both the juvenile and his parents, who were co-accused, should attend a counselling session at the Juvenile Justice Board once a month for a year. The order said, "The father of the juvenile, who was co-accused, should be made to understand his responsibilities towards society to maintain pro-social behaviour." A case in this matter was registered at the Ashok Vihar police station.

When contacted, the Deputy Commissioner of Police (northwest district), N S Bundela said, "We are making license holders aware of the safe use of weapons and also give offering them counselling whenever they visit the police station for registration of arms."

PAST INCIDENTS
August 28: Five persons had suffered injuries after a teenaged son of a police head constable had allegedly opened fire at his neighbours from his father's licensed revolver. The incident took place on August 28 and the accused, Avaneesh, had taken out his father's gun from a box in their home.

May 30: A 17-year-old girl allegedly shot herself in Mayur Vihar area using her father's revolver after her lover, Hitesh, refused to marry her. Families of the girl, Rashmi Maurya, and her lover Hitesh had met to sort out the matter. However, when her lover rejected her, the girl took out her father's revolver from the Skoda car and shot herself.

February 21: A 22-year-old man, Sandeep, shot himself in the New Ashok Nagar area in the chest with his father's revolver. He was in an inebriated condition when the incident occurred and had an argument with his father before taking the step.

Heading: MCD engineers on strike after arrest of 13 engineers - Indian Express
Content:
With the Delhi Assembly elections just a couple of months away, the Delhi government on Friday admitted the electoral office would be able to verify and finalise only 81 per cent of the draft electoral rolls made public.

Responding to complaints reported by BJP MLA's Jagdish Mukhi and Puran Chand Yogi about discrepancies in the photos of voters, Mangat Ram Singhal, Minister of Election, admitted there have been discrepancies reported in the draft photo rolls put up for verification by the electoral office and that all measures are being taken to clear the discrepancies and complaints regarding the electoral rolls.

Heading: Moview reviews - Indian Express
Content:
A day after 13 engineers were arrested by the anti-corruption branch of the Delhi government, engineers under the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) went on indefinite strike crying foul. Nearly 1175 engineers went on strike with work at the civic agency coming to a standstill.

AP Khan, general secretary, engineers' association alleged, "We pawns caught between clashes of the government and the BJP-led MCD. The arrests were unfair as the cases were pending for the last eight to ten years. We were under the impression that they had been settled. It is surprising that they have suddenly been reopened without any notice."

Heading: Stephen’s steps back for step ahead - Indian Express
Content:
THE LAST LEAR
CAST: Amitabh Bachchan, Preity Zinta, Arjun Rampal, Shefali Shah, Divya Dutta
DIRECTOR: Rituparno Ghosh
Can you imagine anyone else in Hindi cinema's A-list doing Shakespeare, seriously, on celluloid? Amitabh Bachchan's lineage and leanings have always pointed to an actor who, like his character in The Last Lear, would count having brought to life the Bard's greatest creations, as a professional peak.

Rituparno Ghosh could have given Bachchan the role of a lifetime in The Last Lear. But what we get is Bachchan declaiming Shakespeare, buoyed by a soundtrack which toplines thunder, lightning and rain, and spotlit by a bright beam. The actor that he plays in the film, Harish aka Harry, wouldn't have needed the props. He would have done it all himself, not letting anything, not the least Bachchan's starry persona, come between him and his part.

Ghosh's latest, in English with a smattering of Bangla, is a film within a film. Sixty-five-year old Harry, an eccentric, vodka-swilling theatre actor, is inveigled into doing his first film by smart young director Sidharth (Arjun). A terrible accident takes place on a hilly outdoor location, making everyone complicit. Including the film's deeply conflicted lead actress (Preity), leading her to the bedside of the comatose Harry, who is being looked after by two resentful women, a much younger partner (Shefali), and an on-the-verge-of-quitting-nurse (Divya).

The director's skill in creating Kolkata lives, with the street outside Harry's charming old apartment a strong participant, is evident in the initial interactions that take place between Sidharth and Harry. The former entices and cajoles, and the older man, who starts out reluctant, and dismissive, gives in  perhaps to bury the ghosts of the past, perhaps to clear the cobwebs in his future  and starts seeing the new medium as one with infinite possibilities.

If Ghosh had stuck to this mood, the film would have been a classic, contemplative study of a long-time actor doing an actor. But The Last Lear never becomes the sum of its nicest parts  Preity in a meaty role after a long gap, Bachchan in pure actorly moments. In which he is all art, not just craft.

1920
CAST: Rajneesh Duggal, Adah Sharma, Raj Zutshi
DIRECTOR: Vikram Bhatt
It is 1920. Why? Because, first, it lets Vikram Bhatt dress his brand new heroine in flowing dresses, place her in a horse-drawn carriage, and plonk her in the middle of a Victorian mansion with several splendid rooms, curving staircases, a grand piano, and a murderous bhoot.

It also lets him bring in a segment of the then recent past: the ghaghra-clad daughter of an 1857 revolutionary snares, with her pretty wiles, a gaddaar. He is strung up and, voila, we have a vengeful ghost!

Sixty years later, the lady in the flowing dresses, Lisa (Adah) and her devoted architect husband Arjun (Rajneesh) fetch up in a quiet hill station. His brief is to break down the mansion, and build a hotel. Her intention is to stall him. Something in the huge house is reaching out to her, and telling her to stop.

The first half builds up slowly. Too slowly, despite the creaking doors, flickering lamps, and one bloody killing. The second half is better, because here the aatma comes into its own. Or, rather, enters the body of  the lady in flowing dresses, who henceforth is to be seen only in a white nightgown. She also acquires a chalky white face, discoloured teeth, gruff voice, and inhuman strength.

Debutant Adah may not have been much when she is all prettied up under her parasol. But as a possessed creature, she is very effective: full marks to the make-up artists. Co-debutant Rajneesh chants the 'Hanuman chalisa' with volume enough to send the evil spirit away to the deep. 

1920 is not just about possession; it's also got punarjanam, good priests, and bad doctors. And lavish production values.

Post-Raaz, Vikram Bhatt comes into his own, again. 1920 has a very scary ghost; the only thing scarier is Rakhi Sawant in a bad item number. If only Bhatt hadn't wasted so much time on non-essentials, this one could have been the first really spooky movie of the year.

RU BA RU
CAST: Randeep Hooda, Shahana Goswami
DIRECTOR: Arjun Bali
Bangkok-based adman Nikhil (Randeep) behaves boorishly with loving live-in girlfriend Tara (Shahana). He forgets everything: dates, special moments, even the fact that the play she has been working towards for the past two years is slated to be held that evening. All through the performance, for which he arrives late, he's thinking of dinner with his clients, not with her. It ends badly. She gets into a taxi angrily, and goes off. And then something happens, which changes everything.

We can't reveal anything more. What we can tell you is that this is another of those could-have-been films. Everything is overstated, nothing is left to the imagination. Randeep as repentant lover boy does what he can, but the real victim of Ru Ba Ru is Shahana, who sparkled in her last outing, Rock On!! She is made to address Randeep as "Baybee", and underline all emotions.

shubhra.gupta@gmail.com

MAMMA MIA!
CAST: Meryl Streep, Pierce Brosnan, Colin Firth, Stellan Skarsgard, Amanda Seyfried
DIRECTOR: Phillida Lloyd
In 2007 there was Across the Universe, which used Beatles songs to convey the heartbreak, confusion and ambition of the tumultuous '60s. Nothing as grand about Mamma Mia!, though: it just lays all its love on you, and there you go again. My, my how can we resist this?

It's the story of a bride-to-be trying to find her father on the eve of her wedding, set against the backdrop of an idyllic Greek island, and using hit songs by ABBA. The film uses a screenplay that has already proved successful in a musical by the same name. And from the high points to the low, Mamma Mia! doesn't strike a wrong note.

The hotel that Streep's Donna runs may be out of a Hallmark romantic card, her daughter just rightly tanned, her future son-in-law a veritable Adonis, and the story unabashedly contrived, but everything is forgotten and forgiven as the music rolls and washes over you. The best example perhaps is Dancing Queen, which has the whole island tapping. And isn't it nice that the lead actors are all of the age that ABBA group members would be now? Music has no age, and here is a perfect example.

There have been complaints about girls in the film having just too much fun but, hey, it's two days in a lifetime of raising a kid alone! And on the eve of a wedding! Give them a break.

Leading from the front in this joyride is Streep, as the former wild pop star who is now owner of a rundown hotel, and afraid of what her daughter will think if she finds out that her mother doesn't know her real father. Brosnan as Sam, Firth as Harry and Skarsgard as Bill  who could all be the prospective fathers  are also charming as three men chastised in middle-age.

However, the person who really charms your heart is Julie Walters as Streep's friend Rosie, another former wild musician turned dotty writer. She knows her mind, and speaks it too. Not for nothing does she get the song Take a chance on me. In the end, that's what Mamma Mia! is about.

RIGHTEOUS KILL
CAST: Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Carla Gugino, John Leguizamo
DIRECTOR: Jon Avnet
"Most people respect the badge. Everybody respects the gun."

Obviously Righteous Kill prides itself on that tagline, seeing the way it has been playing over and over in promotions and features twice at least in the film. But there is another thing truer: most people respect De Niro and Pacino, but everybody respects a good story. And sorry to say, despite all the wait for these two titans together, Righteous Kill has nothing new to offer. It even casts them as, guess what, police officers not averse to crossing the line.

For most part the film just drags, hiding behind vague explanations when the going gets tough and dragging on the climax far after almost everyone in the audience has guessed it.

As for the tagline, it was Jack Nicholson who said it best in The Departed: "You can become a cop or a criminal. But when you're facing a loaded gun, what's the difference?"

JOURNEY TO THE CENTER OF THE EARTH
CAST: Brendan Fraser, Josh Hutcherson, Anita Briem
DIRECTOR: Eric Brevig
A successor to Indiana Jones and National Treasure, Journey to the Center of the Earth is the start of what promises to be another new adventure film franchise. Atlantis, the filmmakers leave no doubt, will be the next plot. And that's not to say the film doesn't at least feature all of the landmarks which have come to be associated with such a film: a dour professor, an inquisitive child, a pretty co-adventurer, an undefined source of income, crazy special effects, crazier storyline, big animals, bigger threats, one truly astonishing train ride, some truly harmless volcanoes and three remarkably unharmed individuals. And then there is Fraser; what can you say, he has survived three Mummies hasn't he?

Don't go expecting anything extraordinary, take along a seven-year-old, and his screams of delight will make the trip worthwhile.

shalini.langer@expressindia.com

Heading: Campaign to promote rapid transit system as a brand - Indian Express
Content:
Selects former OSD Thampu as principal after operating for over a year without helmsman

Without a principal for more than a year, St Stephen's College on Friday selected its former Officer on Special Duty Valson Thampu as the new principal.

Thampu was forced to quit on March 15 this year following controversy over his "fake" PhD degree. Late Friday afternoon, the college's supreme council picked Thampu from among 12 candidates, interviewed since 10 am.

Controversy began stalking Thampu earlier this year when he sent showcause notices to two History teachers and began calling himself "principal". Since Delhi University rules make it mandatory for a college principal to have a PhD degree, Thampu also declared he had a doctorate in Theology from Allahabad Agricultural University.

The twin moves led to an agitation by the Delhi University Teachers' Association: dubbing his degree "fake", the teachers' body sought his resignation. In March, in reply to an RTI application made to University Grants Commission (UGC) by The Indian Express, UGC said there were doubts about the veracity of the doctorate conferred on Thampu. He resigned as Stephen's OSD on March 15 after the UGC reply became public; M S Frank was declared the new pro-tem administrator.

However, UGC later clarified that Thampu's PhD was valid.

On August 22, the High Court ruled that Stephen's was a "minority institution", with a free hand to select a qualified candidate as principal.

Today, after Thampu was selected for the post, a senior UGC official refused to comment, calling it the "university's issue".

Thampu himself was not available for comments but there were mixed reaction from within the faculty. Calling it a "fantastic" news, Nandita Narain, head of Mathematics department, said: "I can't believe it since there has been so much controversy and propaganda against him. This is the best decision the supreme council could have taken."

But another department head (name withheld on request) said Thampu's appointment would deepen the divide between teachers for and against him. But Narain said Thampu would "heal the divide" in the college: "When he was OSD last year, he was not given a chance. But as a permanent head, divisions will be healed."

Aditya Narayan Mishra, the DUTA president who in February had sought Thampu's resignation, said, "It is unfortunate that a person whose PhD is in question has become the principal of a premier institution."

Besides nine outstation candidates, the supreme council today interviewed present Stephen's pro-tem administrator M S Frank and Professor of English at Jesus and Mary College Shobhana Bhattacharya for the post. The interviews were conducted at the Church Lane residence of Bishop Sunil Kumar Singh.

Dateline Thampu
March 2007: Valson Thampu becomes Officer on Special Duty (OSD), St Stephen's College

April-December 2007: Controversy grips his policies like quota for Dalit students and disbanding Indian Mathematical Association

January 2008: Thampu sends showcause notice to two History teachers for allegedly promoting 'anti-OSD' feelings in class. Triggers resentment among DU teachers' Association

February 2008: Questions about Thampu's PhD degree becomes a stumbling block from him becoming principal - DU rules make doctorate mandatory. Thampu maintains he has PhD in Theology from Allahabad Agricultural University

March 15, 2008: Thampu resigns; M S Frank becomes college's pro-tem administrator

Heading: Crematorium was used for disposal of spray cans - Indian Express
Content:
In a move to breathe new life into the much-criticised pilot Bus Rapid Transit System (BRTS), the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) has now sought to attract more commuters, by undertaking to promote and market it under the tag of 'BRT Branding'. The promotional campaign will be carried out through multimedia platforms including television, radio, newspapers and outdoor advertising hoardings.

However, the initiative will not be confined solely to the promotion of BRTS, as the civic administration has also proposed to use the multimedia platform for social messaging like advising people to follow traffic rules, to conserve water, to pay the property tax regularly, and others, as well as public outreach programmes to introduce PMC projects to people.

The proposal, which municipal commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi has tabled before the civic standing committee, says: "In order to make the BRT project a success, as also to streamline the chaotic traffic in and around the city and to urge people to make use of the public transport system, the issues need to be communicated to the people. Only through such measures can the project become a success."

The civic administration has sought the standing committee's approval to hand over the promotion task to two agencies at a cost of Rs 2.66 crore. Out of the total cost, the Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal Limited's (PMPML) share would be Rs 33.20 lakh, while the rest of the expenses are proposed to be shouldered by PMC through its annual budget under the CYG head.

In a similar but separate proposal, the civic administration has also proposed to campaign for the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG), which is exactly a month away. The PMC plans to jointly campaign for this with the CYG office. As per the proposal, the campaign exercise will cost Rs 14.50 crore. The PMC has tabled this proposal in response to a request made by the Additional Director General of CYG to PMC requesting the latter to jointly promote the CYG.

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has opposed this proposal saying the PMC should not participate in the advertisement campaign as it is not part of its job. BJP corporator Vikas Mathkari said, "PMC campaigning the CYG would be a wrong move. It would be a waste of public money. The PMC has contributed a lot for the infrastructure development in view of this event. The duties of the PMC are well-defined and it should not act beyond that. There are much more serious problems before the PMC like water shortage, which it should strive to meet first."

Heading: Root of urban migration: Not enough water to drink - Indian Express
Content:
THE DAY AFTER: Probe finds cause of fire that killed two at biomedical waste plant

Kailash crematorium near Shivaji Nagar RTO was doubling up as an unauthorised centre for disposal of outdated aerosol cans, leading to a fire on Thursday that has till now claimed the lives of two youths and injured five others, say Pune police. Coming barely a fortnight after the disaster that struck Bhosari-based Sai Industries killing 10 women workers, the authorities are waking up to the disquieting reality that many such mishaps may be waiting to happen in Pune.

A day after the fire at Pune Municipal Corporation's (PMC) biomedical waste disposal plant on Kailash crematorium premises, PMC Commissioner Pravinsinh Pardeshi said that the corporation has ordered additional commissioner Machhindranath Devniker to conduct an inquiry. The commissioner has also sanctioned Rs 1 lakh each to the families of the dead and Rs 75,000 to the injured.

PMC health officer Dr Pramod Dhaygude said that empty deodorant cans do not come under biomedical waste and was unsure how these cans landed at the incinerator. "The contract given by the PMC to Sun Enviro Management Private Limited (formerly Image India Limited) was to collect, transport and dispose only biomedical waste," he said.

Vikas Mathkari, leader of the opposition, asked why aerosol cans that do not fall under biomedical waste were being disposed of using the incinerator. He also said the unit seemed to have been given out on a sub-contract and cited past incidents where the company misused the plant.

"Earlier, it was found that medicines past expiry dates, which were brought to the disposal system, had been sold in the open market. On another occasion, the company was found disposing of animal carcasses using the incinerator," Mathkari said.

Congress legislator Balasaheb Shivarkar has alleged the accident took place due to the negligence of the civic administration and the concerned contractor.

Earlier, the police booked four persons including Sunil Jugalkishor Singhanai, company head of Sun Environ Management Private Ltd, for unauthorised disposal of outdated deodorant cans at the plant. While Singhania is absconding police have arrested assistant general manager Piyush Kantilal Solanki (38) and site supervisor Hemant Namdev Jagjal (38). Police are searching for Dharmendra Dube, assistant manager of Avon Beauty Products, Navi Mumbai.

"There was an agreement between Singhania's company and PMC only for disposal of bio-medical waste. But a huge quantity of outdated aluminum and plastic bottles of deodorant body spray of Avon Company at the bio-medical waste disposal plant was being disposed of here without the consent of PMC," investigation officer, senior police inspector Ranjeet Dhure, said.

"The deodorant bottles carried a caution that the solution inside might explode when exposed to over 50°C. But the company authorities took no precautions and asked the workers to break the spray bottles in the open space near the incinerator," Ghure said.

On Thursday, 20-year-old Shabbir Ganibhai Sheikh (20) of Wanavdigaon was charred to death while Manohar Chatsingh Sotte (24), resident of Azadnagar Wanavdi, died in hospital on Friday morning.

Heading: Fail to produce info under RTI, get a rap in service book - Indian Express
Content:
It is the scarcity of drinking water resources that is causing people to migrate from rural parts of the state, especially the drought-prone regions, said Richard Mahapatra of Wateraid India on the sidelines of the first consultation meeting for preparation of the Citizens' Report on Domestic Water and Sanitation.

"It is not so much the lack of water for irrigation. If people lose crops, they can still depend on public wage schemes like NREGS, but if they do not have drinking water, they cannot get a water bottle," said Mahapatra.

Water Aid has been collaborating with over 220 citizens' groups across the country and over 10 groups attended the first meeting today, where groups pointed to the existing network and lacunae in promoting equitable water accessibility. The Citizens' Report, which is expected by December 2009, will highlight domestic water, sanitation and hygiene related issues from the citizens' point of view.

The drinking water situation has been acute in the past five years, with the government's response continuing to be poor. "People do not get even a minimum of 3 litres of water a day. The government's response of providing tankers has not been effective and hand pumps continue to deplete ground water resources, as adequate recharging is not being done," Mahapatra noted.

Over the last few decades groundwater levels have depleted with the movement from wells to handpumps and borewells. "The ground water level is also polluted because of the presence of fluoride and chlorine in several districts of the state. The bacterial contamination of water in rural areas is between 19 and 59 per cent, according to statistics

from the Groundwater Survey and Development Agency (GSDA)," said Seema Kulkarni, SOPPECOM, in a presentation at the workshop.

The gap between coverage and access to water, too, has been increasing. "Since Independence, the records show that we have covered 10 lakh villages in this country of 6 lakh villages. Every year new villages are covered under some scheme... but they slip back five years down the line. It is the case of taking one step ahead and two steps behind," lamented Mahapatra.

Heading: Course to career: Film institute tracks down last three batches - Indian Express
Content:
From now on, Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) officers who fail to furnish accurate, complete and timely information under the Right to Information (RTI) Act will get a remark in their respective service books. Following directions from the State Information Commissioner, PMC Commissioner Pravinsinh Pardeshi on September 8 issued an office order stating that the details of the penalty, too, would be mentioned in the service book of the defaulting officer, said RTI co-ordination officer in the PMC Nandkishor Jagtap.

RTI activist Vihar Durve had recently filed an application seeking details of PMC officers who had failed to follow the RTI mandate of replying to RTI applications with complete and timely details. "It has been revealed that around seven such defaulting officers have been promoted after due penalty was paid. Some of these officers have even been penalised more than thrice for not following the RTI rules," Durve said.

He added that J B Pawar, who was a junior engineer between 2002 and 2006, was penalised 34 times during this period. Despite that, he was promoted to the post of assistant engineer.

Similarly, Madhav Latkar was the development engineer when penalized and has now been promoted to development engineer (road department). Madan Adhari has been promoted to development engineer from deputy engineer while Aniruddha Pawaskar has been promoted to the post of deputy city engineer from development engineer after being penalised, he said.

However, Durve claimed that Information Commissioner Vijay Kuwalekar had directed that the reason for the penalty, as well as the amount, must be mentioned in the concerned officer's confidential report. "A service book merely keeps a record of the officer's attendance, medical details, provident fund etc.

A confidential report, however, keeps a record of the behaviour of the officer towards his/ her colleagues and work performance. Ideally, details of the penalty should go into the confidential report," Durve said. He has also written a letter to the State Information Commissioner requesting him to direct PMC officers to make an entry in both the service book and confidential report.

Heading: IAC to set up manufacturing unit in Chakan - Indian Express
Content:
With placements being quite the buzzword among educational and training institutes in the country, the Film and Television Institute of India too, it seems, has decided to get its act together on that front.

In a first-of-its-kind exercise, the institute carried out a survey to find out the placement positions of the last three batches of students that passed out. The survey that began last month has put together the current work positions and earnings of students who passed out of various courses since 2004.

While the information is still being formated, at the outset the picture seems to be positive for FTII, with most of the students having found work within the industry, said Pankaj Rag director FTII who commissioned the survey. "No such survey had been done by FTII till now and I thought something like this was needed. The findings are very satisfactory. For instance we found that the average income amongst the students who passed out in cinematography in 2004 is about Rs 6 lakh per annum, while for the editing batch of the same year it's between 3.6 to 4 lakh. Graduates of the art direction batch of 2005-7 are earning between Rs 40,000 to a lakh per month. From the script writing course seven of the 12 students who passed out this year have already sold their scripts to producers," said Rag elaborating on the details of the survey. He added though that the current media boom in the country had much to do with good placements.

Another reason for carrying out the exercise said Rag was to do a reality check on the courses being offered at the institute. "We wanted to see if there are any loopholes and lacunae in our teaching methods and if so try and plug them," he added. The survey, said the director, was a mammoth exercise that involved taking out the names and contacts of all the past students of the last three years and getting faculty members to contact them to find out their current work status. "But fortunately we managed to contact almost all of them, except perhaps for a handful," he added.

In the acting batch too the results were fairly good. "Anurag Sinha of the 2004-6 batch has already done Black and White with Subhash Ghai, KP Nishan featured in Cycle Kick and Swati Sen in Breaking News. Then there is Noel Masasehe who's acted in Sudhir Mishra's Tera Kya Hog Johnny while Aurushikha Dey is working with Nagesh Kukunoor. Even in the present batch there is a student who has already bagged a Bengali film role," he said even as he admitted that of all the courses it's the acting batch that perhaps takes the longest time to get placed, while cinematographers and editors find immediate work. "Finally all actors do get work, only it may not be the kind they are looking for. That takes time and struggle," he said.

The results of the survey will soon be put up on the FTII website.

Heading: ‘Changed DP should be made public’ - Indian Express
Content:
The US-based International Automotive Components Group (IAC) here on Friday, announced the setting up of its new manufacturing and engineering plant in Chakan, Pune spread across 12.5 acres.

Addressing a press conference, Jim Kamsickas, president and CEO of IAC Group North America and Asia said the new facility would help the company better to cater to the domestic market. " IAC was awarded new contracts to supply interior and exterior components to Mahindra and Mahindra (M&M) utility vehicle, Mahindra Navistar Automotive Ltd.-medium and heavy truck programme and a Volkswagen Polo small car. All of which will be supported at this new location,'' he said.

The new IAC facility with a 25 million investment will manufacture vehicle interior components and systems, including instrument panels, cockpits and door assemblies. Kamsickas said with the growth expected in the automotive market in the coming decade the Pune centre would support the global growth needs. For the M&M SUV the IAC will be supplying instrument panel, door trim panel and floor console and for the Volkswagen it will supply glove box assembly.

Speaking about the future plans of the company in the country Gajanan V Gandhe, vice-president, Asia operations said the company would be targeting all the major automotive players in the region.

He said the strategy of the company in the country would be to concentrate in the vector where there is a lack of quality components. IAC has engineering, sales location in Japan as well as in China. The company has manufacturing unit in 17 countries.

Heading: World junior TT tourney: Tough morning session for Indian girls - Indian Express
Content:
Expressing concern over the changes made in the Development Plan (DP) of the Baner-Balewadi, two of the 23 merged villages of the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC), the civic standing committee chairman Shyam Deshpande and environment activist Vandana Chavan have alleged that the state government has directly lifted the reservations without intimating anybody. They have also demanded that the map of the changed DP be made public.

The draft DP for the 23 merged villages has been divided into 10 units and first unit of Baner and Balewadi villages was approved by the government at a meeting attended, among others, by Minister of State for Urban Affairs Rajesh Tope, Additional Chief Secretary Ramanand Tiwari, Mayor Rajlaxmi Bhosale, Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi and City Engineer Prashant Waghmare, in January.

However, regarding the changes made by the state, Deshpande said, "The state government has made changes in the DP of the Baner-Balewadi and issued a notification to this effect on August13. Despite this, the state government has not yet made available the map of this changed plan for the people to register their suggestions and objections. It is improper on government's part to lift the reservations earmarked for gardens or as playgrounds."

Chavan said, "The state government has completely altered the DP the reservations meant for gardens, garbage processing units, hot-mix plants has been removed. The path of the road has been lifted from one place and put in the land reserved for Biodiversity Parks (BDP). The reservations meant for increasing the green cover, are being turned into residential places. All this is objectionable, especially when the PMC general body had sent the DP." Deshpande and Chavan are soon going to tender a memorandum demanding the speedy availability of the altered DP maps.

Heading: Zilla Parishad U-16  football tournament: JN Petit beats Loyola - Indian Express
Content:
The Romanian paddlers avenged Thursday's defeat to India 'C' by defeating India 'B' contingent - 3 games to 2 in the Junior's quarter final of the Bajaj Group Indian Junior Open 2008 ITTF World Junior Circuit Table Tennis tournament being organised at the Balewadi Sports Complex.

India was off to a good start with Pooja Bhude defeating Romanian counterpart Szocs Bernadette- 3 games to 1. Although Bhude lost the opening game 8-11, she came back strongly to win the next three 11-8, 11-8, and 11-6. In the second singles event Sanhya Sehgal (India) was crushed by Camelia Postoaca (Romania) - 0-3. Postoaca had complete control of the proceedings right from the start and comprehensively defeated her opponent 11-1, 11-7 and 11-6. In the double's event Romanians made a clean sweep. The pairing of Postoaca and Bernadette proved to be too strong for opponents Bhude and Sehgal. They won with a score of 11-7, 11-7 and 11-7. They were now leading 2-1 at this stage. Bhude displayed her skill and superiority in the single's event when she won her reverse singles match against Postoaca. S

he breezed past her opponent 11-7, 11-5 and 11-6. By doing so she levelled the score 2 -2. Now it was left to Sanhya Sehgal to achieve victory for the Indian team, but she failed to do so. Szocs Bernadette blanked out her opponent, 3 games to 0. Sehgal offered some resistance in the first two games but lost both 10-12. She gave up the fight in the last game with a score 5-11.

In the second Junior quarterfinal between India 'C' and Singapore, the host team lost the game 3-1. Singapore's Sim Kai Xin Zena gave her team a good start when she beat India's Preeti Mokashi 11-9, 13-11, 6-11 and 11-7. The visitors looked in complete control when Kwa Hui Qi defeated Prajakta Tipale 11-7, 11-8, 9-11 and 11-6. However, the Indian paddlers showed some character in the doubles event when the pairing of Tipale and Mokashi beat their opponents Kwa Hui Qi and Sim Kai Xin Zena 3-11, 12-10, 6-11, 11-3 and 11-6. But the Singaporeans got back on track and wrapped the match up when Kwa Hui Qi beat Tipale 11-9, 15-13 and 11-6 in the first match of the reverse singles.

Heading: Food path - Indian Express
Content:
JN Petit beat Loyola by 1-0 to win under-16 inter-school football tournament organised by the Zilla Parishad held at the SSPMS grounds on Friday.

JN Petit had a confident start and passed the ball around well. They took a couple of attempts on goal and won a free kick in a good position but could not manage to score. Loyola then had a good spell of possession and were launching attacks on opposition goal. However, they could not get past the strong Petit defence which was orchestrated well by their captain Riyan Yadgiri. Ten minutes ahead of halftime, Yadgiri had an excellent opportunity to give his team the lead through a free kick. But he failed to convert the opportunity as the keeper saved his shot well. In the very next move, at the other end, Loyola nearly took the lead when their player's shot went an inch over the target. Both defences remained strong and the half ended goalless.

Loyola started the second half well winning a corner in the opening few minutes. The corner itself nearly resulted in a goal as the ball curled inches wide of the post. Loyola had the upper hand as they had yet another chance to take the lead in the very next move. Parth Kalyani turned his defender well before slashing the ball just wide off the goal. Petit then responded well to the passionate cries of coach Nandu Angirwal and started playing a much calmer game. They strung a few good passes together and played some good flowing football. Then in the 45 th minute Petit drew first blood through Riyan Yadgiri. Yadgiri expertly guided the ball into the net after receiving a good cross from the corner position. With 5 minutes to go, Loyola put the opposition goal under constant threat, but could not find the equalizing goal. Soon after, the referee blew his final whistle and the match ended 1-0.

Heading: LAST BITE  with Kim Sharma - Indian Express
Content:
With countless food items on display by the roadside, Ganesh festival is a real treat for food lovers

Other than the fact that millions of devotees from diverse cultural backgrounds contribute towards the 10-day Ganesh festival in some way or the other, there is another factor that makes Ganesh festival truly diverse. And that is food. With the increasing volume of devotees flocking in to see the decorations of Ganesh Mandals, what also goes high is the number of food joints on the city streets.

Laxmi road, Kumthekar road and Sawargate resemble the look of a food street during Ganesh festival. Dagdu Gaikwad is a resident of Mulshi, who comes down all the way to Pune from his village to sell bhuttas. According to Gaikwad, "We have our own farm and business in Mulshi and we come down to Pune only during these four days. The demand for corn during the festival is so high that we bring an entire truck filled with bhuttas and there hasn't been a single year when the truck has not gone back empty."

Santosh Dosa center is the name of a haath gadi that is normally located on Paud road near Ideal colony. But during Ganesh festival, the location changes to Laxmi road. The owner Santosh Pawar makes the complicated equation easy by saying, "The number of dosas that I normally sell during a week is equal to the number that I sell during one night in Ganesh festival. The number might reach up to 100 to 200 dosas during one night of the festival." What also attracts food lovers to Pawar's haath gadi are the South Indian items like set dosa, butter dosa, uttappa, cut dosa and so on. Pawar eliminates the probability of customers going away due to hygienic reasons by providing paper plates and tissue papers. "By doing this, I get a satisfaction that I am providing quality service to my customers," smiles Pawar.

And how can wadapav, the most common roadside snack be an exception when the demand for roadside food is so high? Pandurang Gurav who owns a wadapav shop near Swargate adds, "These four days make me feel happy about the location of my shop. I mean demand for wadapav is never ending but during these four days the requirement goes so high that I have to take help of some of my friends to meet the demand."

While walking on the streets one can see temporary hotels set on the roads with food lovers enjoying roadside delicacies like pav bhaji, kachchi dabeli, sandwiches, egg bhurji, chanachur, guddi ke baal and so on. Devdatta Bhingarkar is one such food lover, for whom deciding between pav bhaji, wadapav, dosa, tawa pulao and countless other food items is the most challenging task. "I am an active participant in the final day processions and after the processions when we are tired, gathering at one of the food stalls and tasting maximum possible food items is our favourite activity. Recently there have been new introductions like Chinese stalls and tawa pulao as well. However, the fun there is not about the food items but about the euphoric night it is," he smiles.

Heading: MEAL TICKET - Indian Express
Content:
Rendang curry
(Pronounced as rend-ang)
This Red hot curry is to die for. Originally from Indonesia, Rendang is very popular in Malaysia and Singapore too. In fact, it is a popular food during Malay festivals.

Traditionally Rendang is made by simmering chunks of mutton, chicken or beef in coconut milk and spices for a long time till the liquid is gone.

In the Malay version, the curry is thin in consistency and very flavourful. The meat absorbs the spices and each bite is heavenly. Spices used in the gravy include garlic, ginger, chillies, ground coriander, tamarind paste and ground turmeric.

Chicken Rendang is best eaten with steamed rice just in the same way we eat our curries. It can also be eaten with roti canai which is the Malay version of our lachcha paratha. Sample these at Trident, Nariman Point.

Heading: Gear up your fitness - Indian Express
Content:
Final year LLB student, Aniket Dilip Sanghvi from the city is flying to Beijing this October to participate in the World Mind Sports Games in bridge, as a part of a six-member team representing India

He is 23 and feels the game of bridge is like life, always dragging one to be on the edge. Seven years of experience of simultaneously playing and exchanging the roles of a declarer, opening leader and dummy in the game, makes him conclude that life is nothing but a game of cards. It might sound cliché, but here we have someone who is speaking out of experience. Sanghvi, who is going to represent India in World Mind Sports Games in bridge along with five others, believes bridge is a game sharing similar traits as life. "Just like life gives us unlimited scope of making mistakes and one wrong move destroys it all, same is with bridge. The best part is that it's plotted, planned and is strategy-based but at the same time it's unpredictable and at times instinctive too," elaborates Sanghvi who has participated in over 50 state level championships for the game.

Bridge, essentially known as an intellectual's game in the card world, that heavily depends on co-ordination between players and calculated moves, which are instrumental steps towards victory. "The game demands alertness all the time. You cannot afford to lose your attention for even a second. It's a mind sport like chess, where luck can never work, what works is your alertness and presence of mind. The combination of these two is a must to make you win," says Sanghvi, who has also won junior national level championship for the game four times in a row.

Though his passion now, Sanghvi took to the game as sheer time pass because he did not have anything to do when he waited in the long queues to play snooker. "After my standard X exam I got interested in snooker and it was a time when snooker was the in thing. There used to be long queues and that is when I took up bridge," reminisces Sanghvi. "You can play the game for 10-hour at a stretch. If I add the hours for which I have played the game till now I think the number will go in million or even more than that," smiles he.

All set for the competition, he is thrilled about representing India internationally. "I am excited, thrilled and above all positive about winning it." Playing for the under 28 section Sanghvi considers his experience of seven years in the game his major trump card. "No one starts playing this game at such an early age as mine. Since I have an experience of so many years as I am playing it since my 11th grade, I think this is what will give me an edge over others," avers he.

On his way to become a doyen in a world where aces, spades, kings and queens are arsenals, Sanghvi sure is set to achieve a real big feat at an age when people still strive to search their grounds.

Heading: SMALL TALK - Indian Express
Content:
After Rampal in Rock On, watch her nag Hooda in Ru Ba Ru

A walk from the Raghuvanshi Mills compound to Phoenix Mills with newbie actor Shahana Goswami seems longer than usual. Every second glance from a passers-by speaks volumes of her popularity and her newly-acquired celebrity status. Post Rock On, this versatile actress is on a runaway to success. "With the success of Rock On, my life has taken a U-turn. Today, wherever I go my character Deby goes with me," she smiles, pleased with the adulation.

Dressed in blue denims, a white top and beads around her neck, she is your typical collegian with oodles of ardour and zest. And for this 22-year-old, her success story has only begun.

After doing minuscule roles in Yun Hota To Kya Hota and Honeymoon Travels Pvt Ltd she is now seen in her recent big release Ru Ba Ru with Randeep Hooda. "This one is a romantic story, about a live-in couple's relationship and the ups and downs they go through. I nag quite a bit in this movie too," she says, afraid of the fact that after two 'nagging wife' roles she might be stereotyped as one.

A Delhiite by birth, Mumbai has been her home for the last four years. "I have lived here through my graduation years and I have been a part of Jaimini Pathak's theatre group, Working Title, which initially helped me get into films," she says, looking around for some shade to escape the city's humid weather. But she has never been trained in acting. "It is in my genes," she proudly states, giving instances of her parents' involvement in theatre and dance.

For Goswami, Ru Ba Ru happened while she was still in college completing her graduation. She gave her first shot for Ru Ba Ru in Bangkok, much before she was signed on for Rock On. But ironically enough the latter has turned out to be her first big release. "It is all good. What I fear is with the success of Rock On, expectations are sky high. Everyone around me expects me to give a brilliant performance in this one as well," she says, as we pass by a magazine stall with posters of Rock On.

Success has kept her grounded. This, we can see in the little things that make her happy. As we walk around Phoenix Mills, she stumbles upon a host of white and mauve periwinkle flowers along the periphery of the compound which she admires, something that is typical of her character in her forthcoming movie as well. However, she refuses to look at any of the restaurants around. "I am on a strict diet; I can only have juice right now. This profession makes you do all sorts of things. But I make sure I binge once a week at least," she says, while climbing the stairs that lead to The Bowling Company.
