After a nine-year trial, on Friday, the Ahmedabad City Civil and Sessions Court acquitted six persons including a former principal judge accused in a case of abetting suicide and demanding dowry.

The court pronounced the verdict in the case where the former judge, his wife, two sons and two daughters are the accused. Additional Sessions Judge of Fastrack Court R R Bhatt pronounced the accused 'not guilty'.

On September 9, 1999, Jyotika Shelat, wife of Shahsikumar Shelat had succumbed to burns sustained in the kitchen. Subsequently, a case of abetting suicide and cruelty to a woman by her husband and his relatives under the provisions of the Dowry Protection Act were registered against Shashikumar, a bank employee and his family members including his father Indu Shelat.

The accused were acquitted on the basis of the dying declaration of Jyotika. According to advocate H N Dhruv, who appeared for the accused, it was her dying declaration made before a doctor, executive magistrate and the police that came to the rescue of the accused. All the three had termed it as 'accidental'.

Heading: With tribal uplift in mind, govt to convert 199 forest villages to revenue villages - Indian Express
Content:
Focus on reorientation to minimise accidents due to human error

In a first of its kind initiative, the Regional Transport Office (RTO), Ahmedabad together with Ahmedabad Motor Transport Association will start a series of training programmes for the city truck drivers on September 26.

A B Gor, the Chief Regional Transport Officer of Ahmedabad, on Friday said that the training will be free of cost for around 60 drivers of the Transport Nagar's Truck Drivers Association, Narol.

"The modules will consist of focus and classroom training. Medical camps and free eye checkup camps will also be organised for the drivers," Gor said.

He added: "Similar training programmes and medical camps will now take place every month."

Citing the need of such programmes, Gor said that as per reports, about 77 per cent of accidents occur due to human error. "So, we need to train the drivers. Detailed briefing on driving during night, effects of drunken driving, or driving while talking on the phone, will also be given in the training. If any driver is found colour blind, then the cost of his treatment will be borne by the Ahmedabad Motor Transport Association," he said.

Jitu Sanghvi, President of Ahmedabad Motor Transport Association told Newsline, "Most of the truck drivers are educated. With this training programme, they will feel more confident and will be able to read sigh boards."

He said further, "After a few successful programmes here, we plan to train other associations of the state."

The schedules have been made only after getting the responses on their preferable timings. The first training program will be headed under the guidance of a former RTO officer. Some NGOs have also come forward for the same.

Around 4-5 trained and experienced people have also agreed to lend support and impart the training without charging anything.

Heading: Bridge to be named after Sam Manekshaw - Indian Express
Content:
The move will enable state to adopt development measures in these villages

To accelerate the development process in the tribal areas, the state government plans to convert around 199 forest villages to revenue villages, as part of a major endeavour by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India.

Dr Chandrakant Upadhyaya, Director of Tribal Research and Training Institute,

Gujarat Vidhyapith, said: "These forest villages were set up in remote and inaccessible forest areas during the British era to provide regular manpower in forestry operations."

He added: "Even after Independence, the land in these villages was recorded as forestland as per the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980. As a consequence, the tribals living in these forest villages had no claim over the village land. They were also denied the benefits of various welfare schemes, as the jurisdiction of the block and the revenue administration does not cover the forest villages. To say the least, the condition of tribals living in forest villages remains precarious."

He further said that now, with the de-notification of the requisite forestland by the Ministry of Environment and Forests, Government of India, these 199 forest villages will be converted into revenue villages.

Dr Chandrakant said, "The conversion comes with a lot of benefits. Firstly, the state will be able to take up comprehensive measures to improve the infrastructure viz. healthcare, education, drinking water, sanitation, electricity, irrigation, markets and livelihood."

He added: "Secondly, in revenue villages, the villagers are conferred heritable but inalienable rights over the land, which itself has manifold benefits. The villagers can use this land as a guarantee for seeking bank loans to set up any vocational occupation and also in matters dealing with law as they are often denied bail on account of no guarantee."

Data of Ministry of Tribal Affairs point out that there are around 2,474 forest villages in the country having about 2.5 lakh tribal families that are spread over 12 states.

Madhya Pradesh has the highest number with 893 forest villages, while Uttar Pradesh has just 13 villages.

Out of these, about 500 have been converted in to revenue villages till now. Proposals from other states are coming in for the same, said Dr Upadhyaya.

Even the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act 2006, recognises the conversion as one of the forest rights, he said.

Citing the reason why none of the forest villages of the state have been converted to revenue villages till now, T L Patel, Joint Director of Tribal Development Department, Gujarat Government, said: "This conversion means that there is a loss of forest land. So, in order to compensate for this, equal measure of wasteland must be transferred to the forest department to be converted into forest. This is the main issue that needs to be resolved."

He added: "The Government of India has, in principle, approved the conversion of 111 forest villages in to revenue villages in Gujarat and the Forest Department has sent the proposal regarding this to the district collectors concerned.

As soon as the collectors demarcate the wasteland for compensation and send their replies, the process of conversion will start."

Heading: JSM to spearhead rally against terror, anti-terror law - Indian Express
Content:
Inadequate rainfall this season has resulted in less supply of water to Kutch from the Malia waterworks on the Narmada canal. The district, as a result, is facing an acute water crisis.

"For the last one week, we are getting less water from the Narmada canal. We need a minimum of 8 MLD (million litres a day), but our present supply is only around 4 MLD, which is again irregular. The higher authorities told us that there is lesser flow of water from the Narmada canal to the Malia sumps," Ramesh Solanki, head of water supply department of Bhuj municipality told Newsline on Friday.

The situation in the twin port towns of Gandhidham and Adipur is no different. "We receive water from three sources. Adipur, which is mainly a residential area in the Kandla complex, gets its supply from the Narmada pipeline as well as from tube-wells. In case of Gandhidham, Narmada and Tapar dams are the sources. Here again, the nodal authority is the state water supply board. The reason given for this is power shortage. However, it is the fall in the water level in the Narmada that is the actual reason. Surendranagar farmers illegally draw water from the canal despite police patrolling all along the canal," said Gul Bellani, senior councillor and former executive committee chairman. Certain areas of the townships receive water after five days, added Bellani.

Sources in the water supply department privately admitted that the farmers of Surendranagar district are heavily drawing water from the Narmada canal between Dhanki in Surendranagar and Malia in Rajkot district. They said that the theft is difficult to detect, as the SSNNL has permitted farmers to pump water from the canal to water their crops recently.

So much water has been pumped this time that three huge pumps at Khirai near Malia have been shut down, they said. The district is now dependent upon the Narmada pipeline for the required 140 MLD, but this can only happen if there is adequate water.

When contacted, B K Sighada, member secretary of the state water supply board said he has already talked to N M Patel, the chief engineer regarding this. Patel later assured that the shortage would ease in a day or two with supply from Dhanki waterworks. He said one more pump has been pressed into service to augment the supply.

Meanwhile, Ashok Yadav, Superintendent of Police, Surendranagar, said patrolling was intensified a month ago when a complaint about pilferage was received from the water supply authorities. A company of the Homeguards (border wing) was deployed initially, but it was later sent to Ambaji. Now, policemen are patrolling the area and there has been no fresh complaint of theft, he added.

Heading: GMDC share prices dip after MD, chairman give AGM a miss - Indian Express
Content:
Jan Sangharsh Manch (JSM) and other NGOs will take out a rally on Saturday afternoon to protest against terrorism and the government's demand for GUJCOC (Gujarat Control of Organised Crime).

Named as Insaaf Rally (rally for justice), it will begin from Roopalee Cinema, pass through Electricity House and Lal Darwaza and finally terminate at Sardar Baug in a public meeting.

According to JSM secretary Amrish Patel, the aim of the rally is to condemn terrorism, ensure safety and justice for the people and establish communal peace. He said the claim of the state government that the fight against terror cannot be successful without laws like GUJCOC is baseless.

The government, said Patel, is trying to hide its failure and negligence by trying to convert GUJCOC into a political issue. More stringent laws like POTA could not prevent incidents like Akshardham, but it was used against the minorities in the state selectively. Many of them are still languishing in jails. But none of those who indulged in violence during the post-Godhra riots were booked under POTA and all of them procured bails from the court, he added.

Heading: Kim River may soon become state’s sorrow - Indian Express
Content:
A day after the stormy general board meeting, which was given a miss by the managing director and the chairman, share prices of the Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation Limited (GMDC) went down by Rs 15. Shares were listed at Rs 169.25.

On Thursday, the 45th annual general meeting of the state-owned Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation Ltd (GMDC) had turned stormy over the issue of the state government's policy for setting aside 30 per cent of the profit before tax deduction for social development.

The state government has a 74 per cent stake in the corporation while the rest is public money.

On the one hand, while the key board members including Managing Director Vijayalakshmi Joshi and Chairman Gauri Kumar gave the AGM a miss, the shareholders on the other hand, disrupted the proceedings of the meeting, which has now been rescheduled for September 24.

GMDC is also the first public sector enterprise (PSE) among the six others in the state to hold the AGM after the announcement of the state government's policy for setting aside a percentage of profit for social development.

Though resolutions were made with respect to receiving, considering and adopting the profit and loss account of the corporation for the year ending on March 31, 2008, it was the absence of the managing director and the chairman of the corporation that annoyed the shareholders, who had come from distant places.

It was the government appointed joint secretary, who responded to the queries of the shareholders in absence of the MD and the chairman.

The GMDC officials said not attending the AGM was a 'last minute decision' of both the chairman and the MD.

Heading: VMC discusses Vishwamitri project - Indian Express
Content:
Heavy rains, presence of tectonic zones in its path may force the river to change course, warns geologist

The changed course of the Kosi in Bihar has left many homeless. In the years to come, a similar catastrophe may soon affect Gujarat too, claimed a geologist at the Maharaja Sayajirao University. One of the major and independent drainage basins, Kim, may possibly be dangerously changing its course.

The 140 km Kim may change its route due to heavy rains. Its presence in the high tectonic zones between Narmada and Tapi rift systems may also be the reason for its change of course.

"Kim River also shows the pattern of 'Oxbow lake phenomenon'. It is a crescent-shaped lake formed when a meander of the river or a stream is cut off — near Pansim area in south Gujarat," said MSU geologist S I Vaid, who has mentioned it in a research done by his student Naresh Mulchandani titled 'Late Cenozoic Geomorphic Evolution of the Kim River basin, Western India'.

In due course, the Kim could change its sinuous path and start flowing straight due to the high river currents, created either due to heavy rains in the upstream or due to manmade activities, sources said.

"A large amount of data about structural and seismic complexity has been collected by geologists in the area where Kim is located. The river has made a 15-metre incision in Deshad area of Valiya taluka of Bharuch district," said Vaid.

"The zone between Narmada to Bharuch is sensitive because the Indian tectonic plate of south Gujarat is moving towards the north, while the Eurasian plate which starts from Vadodara district is steady. Therefore, a lot of compression is created in the landforms in these areas, which is indirectly affecting the course of Kim which emerges from a hilly terrain," he added.

Surat district collector Dilip Rawal agreed that Kim is vulnerable to floods. "We do face problems due to Kim every year. As far as meandering is concerned, we have not received any information from the Water Resource department. If there is any change in the pattern, we would certainly like to check it," Rawal said.

Heading: Scent of crime: Sandalwood smugglers have nexus with dealers, claim cops - Indian Express
Content:
Former and present officials of the Vadodara Municipal Corporation discussed issues related to the development of Vishwamitri River project at a meeting organised here in Friday.

According to a statement issued by the VMC, mayor Balkrishna Shukla said different suggestions were made during the meeting for faster implementation of the project.

Former mayor Bharti Vyas suggested it was necessary to see to it that the level of Vishwamitri remained 35 feet. The level of Dhadhar should also be checked, she said. Earlier, a project was initiated to ensure that water from Bhukhi river did not enter Vishwamitri. The Express Highway is also responsible for the heavy flow of rainwater.

Opposition leader Chirag Zaveri suggested that necessary steps should be taken to increase the water capacity of the river. Suggestions were also made regarding the expansion of bridge over Vishwamitri at Kalaghoda and faster implementation of Crocodile Park and separate space for swimming.

Heading: Capt off to London, says not running away - Indian Express
Content:
Forest officials, district police claim breakthrough with two more arrests

District forest officials and Sankheda police claim to have cracked the sandalwood thefts case with the arrest of two more persons from Nadiad taluka of Kheda district. Probe into the case has exposed a well-knit nexus of sandalwood mafia and dealers.

Sankheda police inspector M Gujjar told Newsline that sandalwood stolen from Sankheda, Nadiad, Vadodara and other areas in central Gujarat was taken to three villages in Nadiad. "We have arrested sandalwood dealers Bharat Patel (35) and Sathi Miya Chawda (54) from near Mangroli village after questioning the nine accused who were arrested in the sandalwood theft case in Sankheda earlier," said Gujjar.

Divisional Forest Officer, Yogendra Verma probing the case said the stolen sandalwood is used for making beads, soaps and incenses, which are sold near Swaminarayan Temple in Nadiad. "The two arrested from Kheda were supplying sandalwood to various beads, soap and incense makers in the area, who in turn sell it to shopkeepers catering to the needs of devotees," said Verma.

The three villages in Nadiad taluka where sandalwood trade takes place in a major way are Mangroli, Najigadh and Rakkuma, police said. Patel and Chawda have their own sandalwood plantations in the villages. Since felling of sandalwood requires permission from the forest officials, they occasionally cut the trees with the permission showing that they were engaged in a fair practice, they added.

"Stolen sandalwood from places such as Bodeli, Sankheda, Vadodara and others would be stored at Patel and Chawda's houses," said Gujjar. Last week, 20 kg of sandalwood was seized from the store of Patel and Chawda in Mangroli village.

Kingpin of sandalwood trade in central Gujarat, Kanu Wagde and his brother Suresh Wagde are still absconding, Gujjar said. "However, questioning of the nine members of Wagde's team arrested recently from Sankheda and the two dealers arrested in Nadiad, hold clues about their possible hideouts, he added. Meanwhile, the sandalwood mafia's links with Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh still need to be probed.

Heading: Harpreet Kaur murder case: Taxi driver turns hostile - Indian Express
Content:
Claims has prior engagements in London, including medical check-up

Former chief minister Capt Amarinder Singh left for London yesterday, reportedly for medical treatment. In a statement, he claimed that he was visiting his doctors for a thorough check-up, as he had not been keeping well for some time now.

He claimed that he was not "running away" after his indictment and ouster as MLA, but "would return soon to fight a decisive battle in Punjab". The former CM also stated that he was to attend to some other pre-determined engagements in London, which included meeting with his publishers regarding his forthcoming book on the history of Punjab in the mid-nineteenth century, besides a social function.

However, his departure has given rise to intense speculation, especially as no calls were taken by him and his MP wife, Preneet Kaur. The former CM's detractors could not resist a dig at him, with Patiala's Mayor Ajitpal Singh Kohli saying, "He was never to be found by Patiala's residents ever since he got elected."

However on Friday, Preneet Kaur, accompanied by Congress leader Hardial Kamboj, met some Lok Bhalai supporters at their residence, who joined the Congress under the leadership of Balwinder Kaur Cheema.

Capt Amarinder Singh was unseated as MLA of Patiala on Wednesday after he was indicted by the Punjab Vidhan Sabha's House Committee on charges of corruption. The former CM has already moved court against the Committee report.

'Get back plundered money'
CHANDIGARH: Shiromani Akali Dal leaders on Friday emphatically demanded that the Punjab government should enact a legislation to recover people's money "plundered through corrupt means by Capt Amarinder Singh and his coterie" through promulgation or ordinance. In a joint statement, the SAD leaders said Capt Amarinder Singh and his coterie should be booked and the ill-gotten money so recovered from them should be deposited in the government treasury. They dared Capt Amarinder Singh to contest and refute the basic facts about his involvement in the Rs 2,460-crore scams of Amritsar and Ludhiana, instead of issuing what they described as "hollow statements wrapped in legalistic jargon". The statement was signed by Member Parliament Dr Rattan Singh Ajnala, Guljar Singh Ranike, Manjinder Singh Kang, Malkit Singh Jadiala, Dr Dalbir Singh, Amarpal Singh Anjnala, Manjit Singh Mianwind, Harmeet Singh Sandhu, Virsa Singh Valtoha, Gurbachan Singh Babehali, Balavir Singh Bath and Lakhvir Singh Lodhinagal. They also expressed surprise that the "self-styled general" had virtually "fled" the country instead of facing the investigation against his "corrupt" malpractices.

Come clean: Sukhbir
CHANDIGARH: Shiromani Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal has asked Capt Amarinder Singh to come clean on the facts revealed in the House Committee report. Badal said it was sad to see the Captain "fleeing" the country within hours of any crises he faces. He asked Amarinder to come clean on whether or not the records of the Amritsar Improvement Trust were tampered with to change the agenda and carry out the land sell-out. "If it was tampered with, then who did it, at whose instance and who was the principal beneficiary?" he asked. Expressing surprise on the plea that 'corruption committed during the tenure of the previous legislature could not be probed by the present House', Badal said, "Does murder or rape or an act of corruption cease to be that merely because there has been a change of government or a new assembly is in place?" Sukhbir said, adding that the Congress nominated its members to the Committee and they took active part in the proceedings of the committee during the investigation.

Heading: State to have another Sainik School: Manpreet - Indian Express
Content:
A key witness in the high-profile murder case of Harpreet Kaur, daughter of former SGPC chief Bibi Jagir Kaur, was today declared hostile by the Central Bureau of Investigation. Akali leader Bibi Jagir Kaur is the prime accused in the case. With this, the total number of witnesses declared hostile in the case by the CBI, the investigating agency in the case, has touched 15.

Devi Lal, a taxi driver in Rai, near Sonepat in Haryana, today stated before the court of Sessions Judge Inderjeet Singh that he had never stated before the CBI that he was hired by Kanwaljit Singh and Harpreet Kaur to go from Rai to Phagwara on April 9, 2002.

He stated before the court that he was made to sign some blank papers under pressure and refused to recognise photographs of Harpreet Kaur and Kanwaljit's sister.

The CBI had stated in the chargesheet that Devi Lal was hired by Kanwaljit to travel from Sports School in Rai, Haryana, to Phagwara in Punjab on the said date. Kanwaljit travelled in the taxi along with Harpreet and Kanwaljit's sister. Though recognising his signature and handwriting on some documents presented by the CBI in the case, the taxi driver stated in the court that he never gave any statements to the CBI and his signatures were obtained forcibly by the CBI on blank documents.

The taxi driver did agree before the court that he had purchased a taxi bearing number DDI-1L-1932 and used to drive it in and around Rohtak since the car was not transferred in his name and he did not have any papers for it.

When asked by CBI counsel R.K. Handa that he had visited a palatial house in Phagwara, the taxi driver refused ever having gone to Phagwara. He was told about the fare of Rs 2,300 charged by him for travelling from Rai to Phagwara, which including fuel charges of Rs 700.

When asked about his signatures at the back of Harpreet and Kanwaljit's photographs, Devi Lal said he was never shown any photograph and did not recognise both Harpreet and Kanwaljit. "My signatures were taken on a blank white paper and the back of the photograph," he told the court.

The CBI later declared him as a hostile witness in the case. The defence was represented by counsels S.S. Kler and Maninder Pal Singh, while prime accused Bibi Jagir Kaur was also present in the court.

Heading: Officer with ‘tainted past’ given prime posting - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab Government will set up a Sainik School in the state on the lines of the one in Kapurthala, with an aim to motivate the youth to join the defence forces.

This was stated by Punjab Finance and Planning Minister Manpreet Badal, who was here to preside over a state-level function organised at the historic Saragarhi Gurdwara .

The function was organised in the memory of the 22 soldiers of 36 Sikh Regiment, who had sacrificed their lives during an attack of thousands of Pathans on September 12, 1897.

Janmeja Singh Sekhon, Irrigation Minister; Hari Singh Zira, former minister; Kamal Sharma, general secretary BJP; B.S. Sudan, Commissioner, Ferozepur and Faridkot divisions; Brigadier Inderjit Singh, Director, Sainik Welfare; Megh Raj, DC; Dinesh Pratap, SSP; senior Army, civil and police

officials and a large number of ex-servicemen attended the function.

Manpreet said Punjabis have always remained in the forefront while sacrificing their lives for the country. He said that the battle of Saragarhi was one of the most stirring episodes of rare valour, not only in the history of the Sikh Regiment and the Indian Army, but the world over.

Badal distributed financial assistance among war widows, ex-servicemen and their families. He also stated that Punjab has seen a major jump in the collection of VAT and other taxes. As against a collection of Rs 5,100 crore the previous year, Rs 7,500 crore was expected to be generated during the current fiscal year, which showed a 43 per cent increase in collection, he said.

Meanwhile, a Saragarhi Cycle Expedition a was organized by the Golden Arrow Division of the Army to mark the day. Lt Gen R.S. Sujlana, Colonel of the Sikh Regiment, along with local dignitaries, received the cycle expedition at the Saragarhi Gurdwara. The expedition was organised by 4th Battalion of The Sikh Regiment to commemorate the 111th anniversary of the Battle of Saragarhi. It had been flagged off from Mamoon Cantonment by Maj Gen RH Vardhan, General Officer Commanding, Gurj Division, on September 10.

The team, led by Lt Nirmalendu, included a JCO and eight jawans. During the expedition, the team paid homage at the Golden Temple and the Saragarhi Gurdwara. The expedition, while traversing border districts, interacted with villagers and educated them about misuse of drugs.

Heading: The Fazilka that once sailed the seas - Indian Express
Content:
With corruption cases pending against him, Grewal appointed Conservator of Forests

The Punjab government has posted H.S. Grewal, an officer with a "tainted past record", as Conservator of Forest, Patiala. The Vigilance Bureau has registered cases against Grewal at Patiala itself, pertaining to cheating, forgery, and also under the Prevention of Corruption Act.

As per the orders issued on Tuesday, Grewal has been posted as Conservator of Forests, South Sector, Patiala, replacing Jarnail Singh. He has earlier served as Divisional Forest Officer, Patiala, from July 1997 to January 2001.

A meeting of the members of the Indian Forest Services (IFS) and Punjab Forest Services (PFS) associations, held in August 2004, had unanimously resolved that "in public interest, these officers (Grewal and two others) should not be posted on territorial or other responsible positions, where they have access or control over finances". This was also stated in the letter signed by more than 41 Punjab cadre IFS and PFS officers.

A senior officer of the Forest Department revealed that with the new posting, Grewal will head divisions of Fatehgarh Sahib and Mansa, Sangrur and Patiala.

The Principal Chief Conservator of Forests, Punjab, had written to the Financial Commissioner and Secretary, Department of Forests, in 2004 that Grewal, while working as Conservator, Shiwalik Circle, was placed under suspension on account of "prima facie involvement in a serious case of illicit felling of over 90,000 trees in Nurpur Bedi Range of Ropar Forest Division".

The letter gives reference of four cases registered against Grewal on various charges by the Vigilance Bureau at Chandigarh and Patiala. "Disciplinary action is therefore recommended against him,"

concludes the letter dated October 25, 2004, a copy of which is with The Indian Express.

When contacted, SSP, Vigilance, Patiala, Shiv Kumar confirmed that there were cases registered against Grewal. "I cannot stop his posting in Patiala, as it is the decision of the government. But I have two inquiries pending against him in Patiala," he added.

When questioned in this regard, Forest Minister Punjab Tikshan Sud said that he has so far received no complaint against Grewal from any quarter.

"As far as inquiries and FIRs are concerned, I would say that mere registration of an FIR does not mean that an officer is guilty and cannot be posted," he told The Indian Express. "However, if someone has some complaints against Grewal, he should come and tell me, and I will get the matter probed," Sud stated.

Heading: Encroachment in the name of God - Indian Express
Content:
Fazilka, the namesake of a small town in Punjab, was once a steamship that dumped Indian labourers at Fiji

Not many, including the inhabitants of this sleepy little town tucked away in a corner of Punjab, will know that there was once a steamship that not only dumped Indian labourers at Fiji, the country they starting ruling half a century later, but the ship even carried the name of their town - Fazilka.

The story behind the name is a mystery, though. Henk Jungerius, a Holland-based ship enthusiast and historian, says the ship was named after a town in Sirsa district of northern India.

Adds Navdeep Asija, a researcher based in Chandigarh, "More information about how the name came about is not available, but the town of Fazilka did have a special place in the Britishers' heart. This is because Fazilka was as far as they could go inside Punjab, before the death of Maharaja Ranjit Singh."

In British India Steam Navigation Company Ltd, the practice of naming ships on places in India was common enought. Joseph Conrad, in his book, 'Lord Jim', refers to 'The Patna' and 'The Rawalpindi'.

'The Fazilka' is listed in the book, 'BI The British India Steam Navigation Company Ltd' by W A Laxon and F W Perry. It is stated to be a 4,152-ton single-cylinder steamship, built by William Doxford and Sons in 1890. Fazilka made six trips to Fiji, carrying a total of 4,972 passengers.

There's more. Fazilka SS (Steam Ship) has some terrific and terrifying tales associated with it. It was first used to carry troops from India to South Africa, during the Boer war. During a return trip from South Africa, a shaft of the ship broke between Mauritius and Colombo on February 6, 1900. After some excruciating days of hard labour, the Fazilka was able to make her way to Colombo at a reduced speed of 9 knots on March 3, a total of 48 days after the breakdown, with all hope of rescuing the ship long lost.John Macdonald, the third Engineer, received a gold watch and the sum of £30 for steering the ship safely - something that his grandson Ian Macdonald still proudly boasts of possessing.

After repairs, the Fazilka found itself ferrying soldiers to China for the Boxer Rebellion. It ran aground on the east coast of the Great Nicobar Island while sailing from Penang to Calcutta on October 31, 1919. No deaths were reported, though some peg the number of casualties at six.

"There were some odd tales about some of the crew involved in skullduggery and gold bullion too," writes J B Hollingworth in his article 'Sail, steam and seaplanes' . Hollingworth's grandfather Vivian Lockyer Wiles was in command of the ship at the time of its wreckage, and was rescued. Records of it being in Australian waters are found in the state records of New South Wales of the 1890s. "Even the Lutine Bell was rung when it was wrecked," claims Ian Macdonald.

Whether this is true or not needs confirmation, but The Fazilka's place in Indian history will forever be derived from Fazilka, a town more than the proverbial thousand miles away from shore.

Heading: City man on mission to conquer new heights - Indian Express
Content:
307 unauthorised religious structures stand on 650 acres of land in Chandigarh

Fifty-seven temples, 27 gurdwaras, 10 churches and seven mosques — that's the number of religious places for which provisions had been made in the UT. The statistics maintained by the Administration, however, say there are 408 places of worship in the city. Needless to say, 307 of them are unauthorised structures.

With religious sentiments attached to the issue, neither the Administration, nor the Municipal Corporation has been able to remove these structures, which have been earning money in the name of God.

Sources in the Administration said a report prepared in 2006 indicated that around 665 acres of prime land had been thus encroached upon in the city with a total area of 114 square kilometres. According to the statistics, there are 240 unauthorised temples, 56 gurdwaras, six churches and five mosques in the city.

In December 2005, the UT Administration had recommended relocation of all unauthorised religious structures. Subsequently, a sub-group on "encroachment and unauthorised religious structures" was formed. It was proposed that the managements of such religious organisations be offered alternate land at concessional rates near the sites, where labour colonies were proposed to be shifted under a rehabilitation scheme.

In its report to the Administration, the sub-group recommended that residents' welfare associations should be associated with the mechanism to check unauthorised encroachment on government land. It said officials should be taken to task for dereliction in duty and a task force be constituted. The Administration, however, failed to implement the recommendations and get the unauthorised structures removed or shifted.

While the issue had been discussed several times during the Administrator's Advisory Council meetings, the authorities have not been able to nail the offenders and formulate a policy to demolish such structures or provide alternate land.

Talking to Newsline, the official spokesperson of the UT Administration said: "The Administration is aware of these structures. Corrective steps are taken from time to time."

Heading: Top B-school to open campus in Mohali - Indian Express
Content:
At first glance he looks like any other 30-year-old executive working in the corporate world. Dressed in his stripes, lugging along a laptop bag, he walks in with a stride that is both straight and quick. But, Harinder Sidhu, an operations manager with Tech Mahindra, is also one of the country's few non-military mountaineers.

And the man is on a mission.

"I am aiming to summit the highest peaks of all seven continents. I want to hoist the Tricolour on all these points," tells Sidhu, who has over the last many years trained to be a professional mountaineer. He has scaled more than a dozen peaks in the country, some as high as 17,000 feet. "I did my certification course from the Directorate of Mountaineering and Allied Sports. I have also trained in Alpine Skiing from GMVN, Auli," Sidhu lists his credentials. Besides, he is a regular with rafting expeditions on the mighty Ganges, Alakananda and Zanskar.

This seven-summit expedition, regarded as a challenge, will be his toughest till date. "The first attempt will be Mt Kilimanjaro, the highest mountain in Africa, followed by Mt Aconcagua in South America, the highest in the Western Hemisphere and outside Asia. After these, I will try and scale the highest peaks of Asia, Australia, Europe, North America and Antarctica." He plans to kick-off the first leg of the Summit on September 21. On December 5, he is booked for the Mt Aconcagua attempt. His last summit will be Mt Everest, which he hopes to climb by May 2009. Sidhu is leaving no stone unturned as far as training sessions are concerned.

"I have planned out a rigorous schedule for myself," says Sidhu who trudges up Morni Hills on a 35-km bicycle ride every alternate day, followed by an 8.5-km run along the Sukhna every morning and climbing 1,000 stairs. "I spend two hours on weekdays at the rock climbing wall at the MCM DAV College. On weekends, I head to Kasauli and beyond for a 7-km trek," he adds.

Son of an Army officer, Sidhu took to mountaineering with an aim in mind. "Adventure sports is a way of life with me. It's an amazing feeling to be one with nature. I was into rafting, trekking and gliding, but I realised if you have to ace it all, you have to be a mountaineer. That's when I worked towards it professionally," he explains. He has created a website —www.goadventuresports.com — solely for the purpose of helping fellow enthusiasts discover remote places as well as clinching good deals while undertaking any adventure activity.

"Mountaineering costs serious money. So far I have funded myself with family support," says Sidhu who has meticulously planned his Seven-Summit project. "The total cost to attempt all the peaks, except Mt Everest, is close to Rs 20 lakh. A summit to Mt Everest alone costs Rs 20 lakh." Sidhu is currently scouting around for sponsorship. Apart from digging into his own pockets, he has got a generous contribution of Rs 2 lakh from Tech Mahindra. "Mountaineering as a sport is limited to the armed forces at present. If I am able to accomplish this feat, it will help promote the sport for the masses," Sidhu hopes. Here's wishing him all the luck.

Heading: Kharar MC polls: Allegations fly thick and fast as campaigning ends - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian School of Business (ISB) plans to open a campus in Mohali, said its Dean M Rammohan Rao on Friday.

Ranked as one of the top 20 Global Business Schools by the Financial Times Annual MBA 2008, the ISB management will sign an agreement with the Punjab government shortly and its Mohali campus will come up by 2011-12.

Though the formal modalities are yet to be chalked out, ruling Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Badal has welcomed the ISB's plan to set up base in Punjab and has offered requisite land for Mohali campus of ISB in the upcoming Knowledge City in Sector 81, Mohali.

Under its expansion plans, the ISB also plans to increase the total number of seats from 440 this year to 560 next year at its campus in Hyderabad.

The business school's expansion plans were made keeping in view the fact that India produces nearly 2.5 million graduates every year. The alarm is already being raised in the country and the Tatas, a leading Indian business group, have outsourced their software work to Mexico.

Meanwhile, the Knowledge Commission has identified that the country will need another 1,500 universities to cope with the demand.

"We not only need more graduates, but we need quality graduates," said a Commission official.

It was also felt that India needed better infrastructure to grow at 7-8 per cent over the next 20 years. Whether it be roads, educational institutions or other infrastructure, they all need capital investment, which not only Punjab or Mohali but the entire country needs in large quantity.

Commenting on the ISB's achievement of becoming the first ISB to be listed and ranked as one of the top 20 global business schools, its chairman Rajat Gupta said the school has the potential to climb up the ladder from the current 20.

Stressing on the need to upgrade the quality of education, Gupta stressed on the "inclusive system of education" to achieve upgradation. The ISB Chairman, however, did not make any direct reference to the reservation policy of the institute.

Heading: Punjabi University to set up environment cell - Indian Express
Content:
With about 24 hours to go for the civic polls to elect 15 members to the Kharar Municipal Council (MC), the election campaign ended on Friday after reaching a feverish pitch.

After addressing a series of election rallies and corner meetings, Punjab Cooperation Minister Capt Kanwaljit Singh walked down the narrow lanes of the town to muster support for the ruling SAD-BJP combine nominees. "Mere umeedwara nu jeetao (elect my candidates)," were the only words which the senior Akali stalwart uttered with folded hands to the local electorates.

Capt Kanwaljit's son Jasjit Singh Bunny, SAD MLA from Morinda Ujjagar Singh Badali and Independent MLA from Chamkaur Sahib Charanjit Singh also joined the minister duringthe campaigning.

Punjab Tourism Minister Hira Singh Gabria, incharge of the SAD affairs in Mohali district, spent a lot of time wooing voters.

For the BJP, its Mohali district president Khushwant Rai Geega, Member of Parliament from Hoshiarpur Avinash Rai Khanna and former Punjab Health Minister Dr Baldev Raj Chawla were among those who canvassed for the SAD-BJP combine that is contesting all 15 seats on the "Rising Sun" election symbol.

To counter the ruling combine's bid to wrest control over the civic body, the Kharar MLA was the lone Congress leader, who came to the rescue of its candidates contesting under the election symbol of the "Hand".

While the SAD-BJP combine leaders are playing the development card to seek votes, the Congress is confined to accusing the present regime of "total failure" during its rule and alleging that they are preparing to "rig" the polls.

The ruling alliance had also brought in SAD president Sukhbir Badal to boost the electioneering. "If you elect us, we will usher a new era of development and prosperity by showering plenty of funds and schemes for Kharar but in case you opt for the Congress, you will again have to suffer without even the basic amenities," Sukhbir said while addressing the Kharar electorates at an impressive election rally at the Dussehra Ground.

Kharar MLA Balbir Sidhu, meanwhile, trained his guns at Capt Kanwaljit for playing all tactics to make his son the "leader". "As was evident from large scale irregularities in the voters' lists, free and fair elections have become a farce," rued Sidhu while apprehending that the minister "could go to any extent to snatch power".

Heading: Abandoned at birth, 3-month-old gets a home - Indian Express
Content:
Punjabi University has decided to set up a cell to provide free consultancy service to make people aware about the environment and render help in fighting the threats of global warming and other forms of pollution.

This was stated by Jaspal Singh, Vice-Chancellor of Punjabi University while inaugurating a seminar on 'Global Warming', organised by the Social Work department, in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Public Administration, here today.

Global warming, he said, was leading to widespread agriculture failure, water shortages, droughts, increased disease level, sea-level rise and reduced forest cover.

He highlighted the need of minimising the usage of fossil fuel, electricity consumption by using energy efficient appliances, minimising vehicular pollution by using public transport system and using 'clean' technologies like wind energy, solar energy, bio diesel and hydro power to reduce global warming.

He also released a book on violence, published by the university on the occasion.

M S Saini, Dean, Academic Affairs, claimed that climate change will impact geopolitics and the wellbeing of nations as well.

He asserted that natural disasters due to global warming, see no boundaries. "Global warming is the reason for all nations to unite, cutting across their monetary and territorial interests, to save the earth," he said.

Manjit Singh, Dean College Development Council, also spoke on the occasion.

Heading: School heads accountable for mid-day meals: UT - Indian Express
Content:
A three-month-old abandoned baby girl got a home on Friday. An issueless couple from Patiala adopted the child from an orphanage in Padiala village near Kharar, where she was being brought up ever since she was found abandoned.

On the evening of June 18, an unknown person had left the newborn infant in a cradle placed outside the Universal Disabled Caretaker Social Welfare Society, which had been taking care of her since then. The society members had christened her as Navkiran.

Society's spokesperson Rajinder Kaur said that Daljit Singh and his wife from Patiala approached them with a wish to adopt any abandoned baby.

After verifying their antecedents and completing all legal formalities, the society handed over the child to the couple.

This is the second such case in a week. A couple of days ago, a couple from Kharar had adopted a 10-month-old abandoned baby girl from the same orphanage.

Society president Shamsher Singh said that in its endeavour against female foeticide, the Society has placed a cradle outside its centre on the Kharar-Ropar stretch of National Highway-21 where anybody can leave a child without giving a reason. The society will bring up the child until he or she gets a permanent home, he added.

Heading: A year on, underpasses hit a roadblock - Indian Express
Content:
In order to ensure healthy and hygienic mid-day meals for the students, the UT Administration has directed all heads of schools to check the quality of the food served withing the school premises.

The Administration has also asked for a complete involvement of all persons engaged in the mid-day meal scheme, so that all of them will be accountable for the good or bad food served to the schoolchildren.

It has been decided that the heads of the schools will have to report for duty at the base kitchens from 5 am onwards as per the duty roster. As per the roster, the school heads have also been given the time, place and date for their duties.

On receiving the meals, it will be the responsibility of the head of the school to inform the authorities about any problem or shortcomings found in the meals. Any complaints filed later would be considered as a dereliction of duty.

The Administration has also decided that the school will give daily feedback to Anita Sharma, Subject Expert (Home Science) who will further consolidate the weekly report and submit it to the District Education Officer (DEO).

The Administration officials maintained that the government is committed to and concerned about providing the best quality food prepared in hygienic conditions to the students through the mid-day meals.

"For making the system more transparent, the Administration has come up with the mid-day meal feedback forms, which are to be duly filled by the students from every school. Feedback by students was put in place to counter-check the reports submitted by the staff. Adequate measures have been taken by deploying supervisors, looking after the quality of food received, and maids to ensure that the utensils are properly cleaned," said a senior UT Administration official.

Heading: mc councillors condemn walkout by BJP, INLD members - Indian Express
Content:
It has been over a year since the Chandigarh Administration came up with a plan of constructing underpasses on Madhya Marg, Dakshin Marg and Udhyog Path to deal with severe traffic congestion.

Apart from sending a three member team for a study tour to Brussels and handing over the project from its engineering wing to the Chandigarh Housing Board (CHB), the Administration has made little headway in the project.

It was announced by the Administration in May last year that each underpass would take about seven to nine months to complete. The officials now are, however, unable to confirm a scheduled time for the commencement of the project as floating and re-floating of tenders and feasibility studies pre-occupy the babus.

The only study done so far is the digital topographic survey of the Madhya Marg, Dakshin Marg and Udhyog Path, where eight underpasses — three each at Madhya Marg, Dhakshin Marg and two at Udyog Path — are expected to come up.

The CHB had invited an Expression of Interest (EoI) in February this year, for which, only two agencies had applied. Consequently, the EoI was floated again on July 9 and this time, the CHB claims to have received six applications which have been forwarded to the concerned engineers for scrutiny.

The CHB also invited tenders in June for engaging an agency for traffic survey at various junctions on the Madhya Marg. In response, two applications were received.

When asked about the progress in the project, a senior official of the CHB said, "The geotechnical study of the route chalked out for these underpasses is in process. This study is done to map out the feasibility of the underpasses."

The Administration, initially, planned to construct underpasses at four places at Madhya Marg with each underpass being 400 metres long and 7.5 metres wide. The number was increased from four to eight. The estimated cost for construction of each underpass including civil, electrical, drainage, landscaping works and shifting of utilities and services was Rs 8 crore a year ago.

The UT Engineering department also carried out a study regarding traffic movement at the Press Chowk, which revealed that 35,420 vehicles pass the chowk during peak hours. Of these, 14,100 Passenger Car Unit (PCUs) included traffic from Panchkula to PGI and vice versa.

With the construction of the underpass, these 14,100 PCUs would use the same, thereby reducing traffic at the intersection to 12,950 PCUs — a reduction by 52 per cent.

The Administration anticipated these underpasses to be economical compared to the flyovers with almost half the cost, fuel saving to the tune of Rs 3.08 crore per annum.

With the changing demography and rising inflation, these figures changed manifold over the last year.

The relevant question, however, that remains unanswered is — when will construction actually start?

Heading: Movie reviews - Indian Express
Content:
The three nominated councillors of the Panchkula Municipal Council today condemned the walk out by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Indian National Lok Dal (INLD) members during a recent meeting of the council, which was attended by their relatives and supporters. They said this while addressing a press conference in Sector 10 today.

"It was highhandedness on the part of the BJP and INLD to walk out of the MC meeting that was held at the Indradhanush auditorium. It was after the prior approval of the council president, Ravinder Rawal, that we had called our relatives and supporters," said JS Sangari, one of the three nominated councillors of the council.

To further add to the problems, he said, the BJP was questioning their appointment.

Talking to Newsline, BJP councillor and senior leader, VK Sood said: "In one of the meetings held a few months ago, a family member of one of our BJP councillor sat for the MC meeting and was asked to leave. So, it would be nothing short of double standards if the family members and relatives of the nominated councillors were allowed to attend the council meeting."

He added: "Furthermore, it was nowhere mentioned in the agenda that the outsiders would be attending the meeting. It is for this reason that we staged a walk out."

Heading: Fighting AIDS: Forum meets to voice concerns, battle discrimination - Indian Express
Content:
THE LAST LEAR
CAST: Amitabh Bachchan, Preity Zinta, Arjun Rampal, Shefali Shah, Divya Dutta
DIRECTOR: Rituparno Ghosh
Can you imagine anyone else in Hindi cinema's A-list doing Shakespeare, seriously, on celluloid? Amitabh Bachchan's lineage and leanings have always pointed to an actor who, like his character in The Last Lear, would count having brought to life the Bard's greatest creations, as a professional peak.
Rituparno Ghosh could have given Bachchan the role of a lifetime in The Last Lear. But what we get is Bachchan declaiming Shakespeare, buoyed by a soundtrack which toplines thunder, lightning and rain, and spotlit by a bright beam. The actor that he plays in the film, Harish aka Harry, wouldn't have needed the props. He would have done it all himself, not letting anything, not the least Bachchan's starry persona, come between him and his part.
Ghosh's latest, in English with a smattering of Bangla, is a film within a film. Sixty-five-year old Harry, an eccentric, vodka-swilling theatre actor, is inveigled into doing his first film by smart young director Sidharth (Arjun). A terrible accident takes place on a hilly outdoor location, making everyone complicit. Including the film's deeply conflicted lead actress (Preity), leading her to the bedside of the comatose Harry, who is being looked after by two resentful women, a much younger partner (Shefali), and an on-the-verge-of-quitting-nurse (Divya).
The director's skill in creating Kolkata lives, with the street outside Harry's charming old apartment a strong participant, is evident in the initial interactions that take place between Sidharth and Harry. The former entices and cajoles, and the older man, who starts out reluctant, and dismissive, gives in — perhaps to bury the ghosts of the past, perhaps to clear the cobwebs in his future — and starts seeing the new medium as one with infinite possibilities.
If Ghosh had stuck to this mood, the film would have been a classic, contemplative study of a long-time actor doing an actor. But The Last Lear never becomes the sum of its nicest parts — Preity in a meaty role after a long gap, Bachchan in pure actorly moments. In which he is all art, not just craft.

 

1920
CAST: Rajneesh Duggal, Adah Sharma, Raj Zutshi
DIRECTOR: Vikram Bhatt
It is 1920. Why? Because, first, it lets Vikram Bhatt dress his brand new heroine in flowing dresses, place her in a horse-drawn carriage, and plonk her in the middle of a Victorian mansion with several splendid rooms, curving staircases, a grand piano, and a murderous bhoot.
It also lets him bring in a segment of the then recent past: the ghaghra-clad daughter of an 1857 revolutionary snares, with her pretty wiles, a gaddaar. He is strung up and, voila, we have a vengeful ghost!
Sixty years later, the lady in the flowing dresses, Lisa (Adah) and her devoted architect husband Arjun (Rajneesh) fetch up in a quiet hill station. His brief is to break down the mansion, and build a hotel. Her intention is to stall him. Something in the huge house is reaching out to her, and telling her to stop.
The first half builds up slowly. Too slowly, despite the creaking doors, flickering lamps, and one bloody killing. The second half is better, because here the aatma comes into its own. Or, rather, enters the body of  the lady in flowing dresses, who henceforth is to be seen only in a white nightgown. She also acquires a chalky white face, discoloured teeth, gruff voice, and inhuman strength.
Debutant Adah may not have been much when she is all prettied up under her parasol. But as a possessed creature, she is very effective: full marks to the make-up artists. Co-debutant Rajneesh chants the 'Hanuman chalisa' with volume enough to send the evil spirit away to the deep. 
1920 is not just about possession; it's also got punarjanam, good priests, and bad doctors. And lavish production values.
Post-Raaz, Vikram Bhatt comes into his own, again. 1920 has a very scary ghost; the only thing scarier is Rakhi Sawant in a bad item number. If only Bhatt hadn't wasted so much time on non-essentials, this one could have been the first really spooky movie of the year.

RU BA RU
CAST: Randeep Hooda, Shahana Goswami
DIRECTOR: Arjun Bali
 BANGKOK-BASED adman Nikhil (Randeep) behaves boorishly with loving live-in girlfriend Tara (Shahana). He forgets everything: dates, special moments, even the fact that the play she has been working towards for the past two years is slated to be held that evening. All through the performance, for which he arrives late, he's thinking of dinner with his clients, not with her. It ends badly. She gets into a taxi angrily, and goes off. And then something happens, which changes everything.
We can't reveal anything more. What we can tell you is that this is another of those could-have-been films. Everything is overstated, nothing is left to the imagination. Randeep as repentant lover boy does what he can, but the real victim of Ru Ba Ru is Shahana, who sparkled in her last outing, Rock On!!. She is made to address Randeep as  "Baybee", and underline all emotions.

SHUBHRA GUPTA
shubhra.gupta@gmail.com

MAMMA MIA!
CAST: Meryl Streep, Pierce Brosnan, Colin Firth, Stellan Skarsgard, Amanda Seyfried
DIRECTOR: Phillida Lloyd
IN 2007 there was Across the Universe, which used Beatles songs to convey the heartbreak, confusion and ambition of the tumultuous '60s. Nothing as grand about Mamma Mia!, though: it just lays all its love on you, and there you go again. My, my how can we resist this?
It's the story of a bride-to-be trying to find her father on the eve of her wedding, set against the backdrop of an idyllic Greek island, and using hit songs by ABBA. The film uses a screenplay that has already proved successful in a musical by the same name. And from the high points to the low, Mamma Mia! doesn't strike a wrong note.
The hotel that Streep's Donna runs may be out of a Hallmark romantic card, her daughter just rightly tanned, her future son-in-law a veritable Adonis, and the story unabashedly contrived, but everything is forgotten and forgiven as the music rolls and washes over you. The best example perhaps is Dancing Queen, which has the whole island tapping. And isn't it nice that the lead actors are all of the age that ABBA group members would be now? Music has no age, and here is a perfect example.
There have been complaints about girls in the film having just too much fun but, hey, it's two days in a lifetime of raising a kid alone! And on the eve of a wedding! Give them a break.
Leading from the front in this joyride is Streep, as the former wild pop star who is now owner of a rundown hotel, and afraid of what her daughter will think if she finds out that her mother doesn't know her real father. Brosnan as Sam, Firth as Harry and Skarsgard as Bill — who could all be the prospective fathers — are also charming as three men chastised in middle-age.
However, the person who really charms your heart is Julie Walters as Streep's friend Rosie, another former wild musician turned dotty writer. She knows her mind, and speaks it too. Not for nothing does she get the song Take a chance on me. In the end, that's what Mamma Mia! is about.

RIGHTEOUS KILL
CAST: Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Carla Gugino, John Leguizamo
DIRECTOR: Jon Avnet
"Most people respect the badge. Everybody respects the gun."
Obviously Righteous Kill prides itself on that tagline, seeing the way it has been playing over and over in promotions and features twice at least in the film. But there is another thing truer: most people respect De Niro and Pacino, but everybody respects a good story. And sorry to say, despite all the wait for these two titans together, Righteous Kill has nothing new to offer. It even casts them as, guess what, police officers not averse to crossing the line.
For most part the film just drags, hiding behind vague explanations when the going gets tough and dragging on the climax far after almost everyone in the audience has guessed it.
As for the tagline, it was Jack Nicholson who said it best in The Departed: "You can become a cop or a criminal. But when you're facing a loaded gun, what's the difference?"

SHALINI LANGER
shalini.langer@expressindia.com

Heading: Led by Mayor, MC team checks parking lots - Indian Express
Content:
As part of the general body proceedings of the Indian Network of Positive People, over a 100 HIV positive persons gathered to form strategies on strengthening the network of positive people in the northern states on Friday.

The Network, along with the Chandigarh Network People Living with the HIV/AIDS, organised the Annual General Meeting 2008 which was attended by the representatives from different states.

To apprise the government of their demands and challenges, the Network is planning to organise a rally in Chandigarh from Sector 17 Plaza to Chandigarh Museum and Art Gallery in Sector 10.

Expressing the problems faced during the ART treatment, the free drug distribution at the listed centres and to the discrimination at the hands of the society, the Network urged for more facilities for those living with HIV.

The members also discussed ways to improve the quality of life of those affected with the virus and to make them self-sufficient in their decision-making process. It also urged for setting up more centres in Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh.

A regional conference on the role of Police in Prevention of the HIV/AIDS among the police personnel was organised at the CRPF Headquarters (north zone) in Hallomajra today.

A S Sidhu, DIGP, CRPF Chandigarh range, briefed in his inaugural address about the steps taken by the CRPF towards prevention of spreading of the HIV and the challenges ahead in combating the disease.

Dr Vanita Gupta, Project Director of the State AIDS Control Society of UT, gave an overview on the extent of the problem in Chandigarh and the representatives of Punjab and Haryana presented the facts about HIV and AIDS patients in their respective states.

Heading: Councillors engage in war of words at MC - Indian Express
Content:
Several challans were issued and various anomalies were found when a team from the Municipal Corporation, led by Mayor Pardeep Chhabra, conducted checks at various parking lots in the city on Friday.

The parking lots which were checked included— Sector 35-C, Sector 34 Zone-I and Zone II, Piccadily cinema, Sector 34 and Sector 35-B, parking lot outside the Medical Officer of Health- Sector 17, Bank Square, CMC, Gurdev Studio parking, Sahib Singh and Sons parking, Empire store, Jagat and Anand theatre and Shanti Kunj-Sector 16.

During the checking in Sector 34, the team found a parking attendant not wearing his uniform and no parking attendant was seen deployed inside the parking area at a distance of 50-metres. While one attendant in Sector 34 Zone-II was not wearing his uniform, 12 haphazardly parked vehicles were also found.

While in Sector 22-B, 11 vehicles were parked haphazardly in the parking area, 22 vehicles were similarly found in Gurdev Studio, Sector 17.

The parking contractors were warned to implement the terms and conditions to avoid strict action against them. They have also been asked to install CCTV cameras at the entry and exit gates of each paid parking area for recording the registration numbers of vehicles.

The mayor said that public convenience would not be compromised with. "We are streamlining the paid parking lots. Various measures have been taken for the same. We would see that these are strictly implemented," added the Mayor.

Heading: PGI employees found drinking on premises, suspended - Indian Express
Content:
Huge drama was witnessed at the Municipal Corporation office on Friday when a nominated councillor and former councillor entered into an argument that was resolved only after police intervention.

The incident took place in the evening when the car of P C Sanghi, former councillor and chairman of Federation of Sector Welfare Association Chandigarh (FOSWAC) hit the car of Siddharth Sanwaria, son of nominated councillor Dr A P Sanwaria.

Dr Sanwaria alleged that Sanghi deliberately banged his car into his son's car.

"My son had demanded that Sanghi submit the accounts of how he had spent the money of the residents' welfare association, Sector 21. Since he did not submit these, my son filed a case against him," said Dr Sanwaria.

He added, "My son is fighting the case of a sweeper who was abused by Sanghi. It was to settle personal scores that Sanghi banged his car. After this incident, Sanghi went to the Mayor's room and sat there for a long time."

Sanghi, however, refuted the allegations. "I had a meeting with the Mayor in the evening. My car accidentally touched Siddharth's. After that, Dr Sanwaria and his two sons came to the Mayor's office and abused me. They have old grudges against me which they tried to settle," said Sanghi.

The issue was resolved after the two were taken to the police station where a compromise was reached.

Heading: Admn forms panel to preserve heritage sites - Indian Express
Content:
Four technicians of the Engineering wing of the PGI were suspended on Friday after they were allegedly caught consuming liquor during duty hours in the hospital premises.

The incident took place around 1 pm when Madan Lal, Ram Singh, H B Sood and Anil Kumar, all employed with the Engineering department, were caught at the central workshop building by the security staff.

The matter was then reported to the police. Confirming the move, the PGI spokesperson said, "After the four employees were caught red-handed, we handed over the matter to the police. We have suspended them after the medical test confirmed that they were in an inebriated condition."

Heading: Roads panel sanctions paver blocks along judges’ houses in Sector 24 - Indian Express
Content:
The Chandigarh Administration has constituted a state-level committee for protection and maintenance of the centrally protected archeological heritage and for close coordination with the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).

The committee comprises Secretary (Culture) as Chairman, UT Chief Architect, Chief Engineer, Director (Tourism) and Director (Museum) as its members. Principal (Chandigarh College of Architecture) Prof Rajnish Wattas and Prof Kiran Joshi will be the experts in the committee.

The committee will look into various issues including preventing encroachments in and around the monuments with the help of the state and district administration and change the land in the name of ASI on priority basis by issuing directions to the concerned departments.

The committee has also been asked to obtain necessary permission from the ASI for any development work within the prohibited and regulated areas of centrally protected monuments and keep away from any conflicting situation.

The centrally protected monuments, Religious Endowment Boards/ Wakf/ Devasthanams, under the control of the state government, will not be included without the consent of the ASI.

Before preparing any master plan in the city, the committee will also consider preserving its heritage and the unprotected monuments.

Heading: Strong determination sustains weak muscles, as three siblings fight muscular dystrophy - Indian Express
Content:
The Roads Committee of Municipal Corporation has approved the work to be taken in different parts of the city.

A meeting was held today under the chairmanship of Ravinder Pal Singh, which was attended by other members of the committee.

It was decided that paver blocks will be provided on road berms and alongside judges' houses in Sector 24 at the cost of Rs 15.22 lakh.

The Phirni road in village Kajheri in Sector 52 will be widened, paver blocks will be bought for Sector 33 and a mini rose garden will be set up in Sector 24, it was decided.

Besides a green belt in Sector 35, it was also decided to recarpet the parking lot near the Shastri Market in Sector 22.

In Sector 18 and 44, paver blocks will be laid and parking space in market in Sector 44 will be widened at a cost of Rs 10.72 lakh, it was decided in the meeting.

Nehru Park in Sector 22 will be renovated and upgraded at Rs 7.19 lakh and a park in Milk Colony, Dhanas, will be lined with paver blocks at Rs 17.98 lakh.

A stone platform will also be built as a kitchen in Community Centre in Sector 42 and a platform for day market will also be built at the Charan Singh Colony in Mauli Jagran.

The committee also decided to develop a green belt in Sector 9 at the cost of Rs 15.65 lakh.

Heading: No violence, a peaceful end to student polls - Indian Express
Content:
When three of the six siblings gradually discover in their growing years that their muscles are constantly weakening and life on the wheelchair appears inevitable, it takes more than just acceptance to believe that a life long battle with Muscular Dystrophy (MD) has started.

The Goels from Solan—two brothers and one sister — are courage personified as they not only fight the incurable ailment but also assist others shun the shackles of the degenerative disease.

"Yes, it was difficult not only for us but also for our parents to accept that we suffer from an incurable disorder. But the first step is to accept the living ailment and then make the best use of life," says Vipul Goel, the eldest of the three siblings and the General Secretary of the Indian Association of Muscular Dystrophy (IAMD).

His younger sister Sanjana Goel is currently the president of the association while his younger brother Atul Goel handles other affairs. They are in the city to attend the 18th National Camp of the IAMD being organised by the Chandigarh chapter at Indira Holiday Home.

It was in 1992, Vipul recalls, that the three decided to form the association and hold camps so that patients suffering from the disorder can come forward and share their experiences.

The network has today grown manifolds with nearly 100 registrations. "We also provide wheelchairs, including motorised wheel chairs to the patients. We are glad there are lot of generous donors helping us in our cause," says Goel.

The family has not stalled their individual growth while fighting the ailment. Preaching self-reliance and independence to those suffering from MD, the Goels are carrying on with their own professions to earn a livelihood. While Vipul has been handling his gas agency, Sanjana is a trained dress designer and Atul runs a hardware business.

Talking of the challenges faced by MD patients, Vipul says: "The attitude of the people needs to change and the discrimination between the abled and the differently-abled has to end. Disabled-friendly buildings should be constructed so that accessibility is not restricted for us."

Heading: Victorious parties switch to celebration mode - Indian Express
Content:
Days of frenzy, raising slogans and hectic canvassing finally came to an end with the announcement of the students' poll results today. With no violence reported this year, elections were, by and large a peaceful affair.

The Lyngdoh Committee guidelines, which seemed to have dented the election spirit, however, failed to affect the voter turnout. Colleges recorded an attendance of 60 per cent voters — a fair amount considering the lacklustre response of students towards elections this year. DAV College, Sector 10, lived up to its reputation of having the maximum voters this year too, with 64 per cent of students casting their vote.

DAV College saw a close fight between the two presidential candidates, with Karamvir Singh of the SOPU-INSO alliance winning by a narrow margin of 45 votes, defeating Simranjit Singh of PUSU. Candidates for the other posts, meanwhile, had been elected on Wednesday. Daljeet Singh, a SOPU member, said: "We were sure of our victory this year. The election results have made it clear that students have lost faith in PUSU and that is why, they elected a different party."

In Government College, Sector 11 and S D College, the PUSU-INSO and SDCU-SDHU alliance respectively, had a clean sweep. Expressing happiness over the victory, Amarinder Singh from PUSU said: "We are happy that the students have elected us. Since they have shown confidence in us, we will make efforts to live up to their expectations."

At Khalsa College, meanwhile, there was no change of guard, as students chose the SOI-KCSU alliance. Jarnail Singh of SOI was elected as the president of the college's student council. "The party has worked a lot for the students, especially on improving infrastructure. As we want them to continue with the good work, we voted for them," said Sameer Saluja, a student at Khalsa College. At Khalsa College for Women, the independent candidates had a close fight with their counterparts. While vice-president Shruti Kalta was elected unanimously, Amanpreet Kaur was elected president by 125 votes.

Heading: This year’s polls see new political equations emerge - Indian Express
Content:
Nervousness gave way to relief as anxious faces broke into broad smiles as the results of the elections started pouring in. Once the final results were announced, the joy of victory washed away the exertion of the past week as the winning parties got into the celebration mode. Fireworks, dhols, car rallies and more mirrored the euphoria of the victorious.

Students at various colleges including the Government College, Sector 11, and DAV College could be seen dancing away to celebrate their triumph. "Our hard work has finally paid off. For more than ten days now, we have been on our toes, interacting with students and working on various strategies. Since our party has won, we will not rest now but celebrate the occasion," Rahul Kadyan of Government College said.

At DAV College, the celebrations were no less than that of a wedding as the winning party had roped in a band along with a dhol and trumpet to celebrate. "This occasion is no less than a festival for us. Our efforts have been awarded and we will celebrate it in grand style. This is just the beginning. We plan to hold week-long celebrations," said Raman Randhawa of DAV College.

The din of happiness increased with fireworks and music lighting up the atmosphere. All the colleges in the city wore a festive look as the jubilant students made merry all through the evening. If on one hand, cheering students of the Khalsa College took out a car rally to celebrate, others at the DAV College rushed to the nearest sweet shop and distributed sweetmeats among their supporters. "We cannot overlook the voters who have made this possible. We are grateful to them and they deserve to be an equal part of the celebration," remarked a joyous Angad Singh from SOPU.

Among all the noisy celebration, there were some who chose to retire for the day and savour the victory. Simranjeet Kaur of Khalsa College was one of them. "I am happy that we have won but I plan to celebrate it in a different way. I would like to go back home and sleep as the hectic activities of the week have taken a toll on me."

Heading: ‘Improve infrastructure to promote cinematic tourism’ - Indian Express
Content:
From fresh faces to new equations, the students' council elections at the Panjab University this year were different. According to observers, this is indicative of the high political stakes, involved in the upcoming Lok Sabha elections, for which every party will need to work on augmenting its strength.

This year's election was a rare occasion when there was a direct involvement of both the Congress and the Akalis.

The Third Front alternative, provided by the Akali Dal-backed SOI and the Lok Dal-backed INSO, was clearly rejected by the students.

The results have shown that the students preferred to go along with the time-tested traditional parties, instead of experimenting with anything new.

Irrespective of the outcome, the keenness exhibited by political parties, particularly the Congress and the BJP (though covertly), shows they will now have enough reasons to make the most of the 'advantage' they gained in the run-up to the university polls.

Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) president Sukhbir Badal had openly come in support of the SOI during various functions organised by the party. In fact, he was one of the few leaders to have organised a rally on the campus.

Another first this year was the Congress coming out in open support of the National Students' Union of India (NSUI). The Chandigarh Congress Territorial Committee held a meeting prior to the elections, asking councillors to help the student leaders.

The win of SOPU-ABVP alliance after more than a decade sent a wave of happiness in the BJP camp. Leaders, including former MP Satya Pal Jain, have termed it as a reflection of the changing political situation across the country.

SOPU and PUSU are both known to have the backing of different factions of the Congress. Though the support has never been open during campaigning, it is visible at different functions when members of the student organisations come out in full force to welcome the leaders from mainstream parties.

Heading: No more shady deals, state gets tough with realty brokers - Indian Express
Content:
Himachal Pradesh has attracted the Mumbai film industry in the past decade, offering picturesque locations in Shimla, Kufri and Manali, to name a few. But when it comes to shooting in the untouched interior locales, there is no infrastructure to support such shoots.

Film producer and director, Harry Baweja, said the producers have to look for foreign locations over domestic locations as they are more economical. Giving an opportunity to the northern states to promote themselves as prospective destinations for cinematic tourism, the Institute of Tourism and Future Management Trends (ITFT), Chandigarh, is holding a conference on the World Tourism Day on September 27. Baweja, who is the co-Chairman of Centre for Media and Entertainment Studies (CMES) of ITFT said the states would pitch for creating better infrastructure in best of locations.

Himachal, Jammu and Kashmir, Uttarkhand, Haryana, Punjab and Rajasthan have been invited to participate. "Shooting at off beat locations like South Korea and Singapore has resulted in boasting the tourism in these countries. Similarly, films can help promoting states like Himachal," he said. North India Acting Talent Hunt competition of ITFT was also announced today and auditions would be held in Himachal Pradesh University campus on September 20, said Executive Director of ITFT Dr Gulshan Sharma.

Heading: Committee formed to look into guest teachers’ demands - Indian Express
Content:
Bill passed in recent Assembly session stipulates licence for property dealers; brokers to be made party to disputes

Property dealers in Haryana are in for a greater role in land deals, but it will come with increased accountability and transparency from their side. The welcome change from the 'shady' deals undertaken earlier by the brokers has been brought about by the Haryana Regulation of Property Dealers and Consultants Bill, 2008, that was passed by the Assembly in its recent session.

The state government is also hopeful that it would help curb benami land deals. After the enactment of the bill, no property dealer or his representative or employee would be allowed to function without obtaining a licence from the collector concerned, the fee for which would be decided later.

As per the bill, the broker would be responsible for the veracity of facts provided in the deal besides the identities of the seller and purchaser. This implies that in case of a dispute, the broker would also be a party and the dispute shall be decided by the collector of the region. Earlier, property dealers were almost completely immune to any litigation in case of disputes.

"All the property deals would now be monitored closely by the district authorities and the new legislation would ensure that the broker verifies the property involved in the deal and ensures that it is free from any legal issues," said a senior official.

The increasing number of complaints regarding fraudulent land deals, especially in the National Capital Region (NCR) where the rich and higher-ups used to buy benami land to avoid income tax is a big reason behind government's move. Use of black money was also reported several times in such deals. A senior official said that licencing of property dealers would ensure that only genuine brokers enter the trade and the legislation would help cut down on unscrupulous land deals.

Heading: Hooda’s China trip cancelled - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda today announced the setting-up of a committee under the chairmanship of Education Minister Mange Ram Gupta to look into the demands of the guest teachers.
