Hooda also assured withdrawal of the cases registered against the guest teachers and said that no guest teacher would now be arrested in connection with the incident at Rohtak on September 7, in which a teacher was killed. The guest teachers, whose services had been terminated, would be adjusted on vacant seats with first priority given to their own districts, he said.

A sum of Rs 50,000 for Hans Raj, who was critically injured at the rally in Rohtak, was also announced by the Chief Minister.

The guest teachers, led by the president of the Haryana Guest Teachers Association, Arun Malik, called on Hooda at his residence to "regret" the agitation on September 7 at Rohtak. They said that the present Government had taken a significant step in the year 2005 when it appointed the guest teachers and gave an opportunity to the youth of Haryana.

Vice-president, Haryana Guest Teachers Association, Ranbir Suhag; principal general secretary of the association, Rajinder Shastri and head of the women's wing of the association, Baljinder Kaur were also present on the occasion.

Heading: Taking Stock - Indian Express
Content:
Haryana Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda's proposed four-day trip to China later this month has been cancelled. The CM was to leave for China on September 26 to participate in the second meeting of the New Champions' World Economic Forum. Top government officials were to accompany Hooda on the trip.

The meeting is being held in Taijin, China on September 27 and 28, where Hooda intended to promote Haryana as an investment destination. It is expected to bring together 1500 business leaders from across the world.

No official explanation for the cancellation of the Chief Minister's trip has been given, but according to sources, it has much to do with the recent Indo-US nuclear deal, where China had first opposed India's quest for clearance from the NSG before giving its nod.

In the past, Hooda has led many trips to South East Asian nations, Europe and the US for inviting foreign direct investments to Haryana. The proposed trip to China could have resulted in flow of more investments for Haryana.

Heading: Old and infirm, jailed Phool Devi spends more time in UP hospitals - Indian Express
Content:
Director Shona Urvashi mints sense out of sensex

At the risk of causing a severe bout of indigestion to the opposite sex, we'd like to quote, and agree with fillmaker Shona Urvashi when she states 'women are smart'. "Take an ordinary housewife, the way she runs a house on a strict budget and manages to save and invest. Women know how to do business and they can be savvy with the sensex," Shona, who turned 'bullish' with her latest film, Saas, Bahu Aur Sensex, takes 'stock' of the situation and shares that it's no rocket science. "It became more clear when I got down to research women as investors and came across amazing examples, most of them housewives...in fact, there was one in Chandigarh I talked to, one Anu Rai, who tracks the market on a regular basis," for Shona, the idea of getting a nation's favourite characters, saas and bahu, and hitting a high on the sensex with these unlikely players was simply irresistible. "C'mon, what can be more typical? The obsession with them is finally justified," she chuckles, the film being her second after Masumeh (they are sisters) and Zulfi Syed's Chupke Se.

In a country where women are still treated as second class citizens, Shona's tried to tweak the laws of physics in her favour and give the audience, especially the women, something to feel great about. For starters, she has the adorable Farooque Sheikh as the women-hating stockbroker and Kirron as the vivacious on-the-move housewife. "I'm trying to capture a silent revolution where women are more than just bhenjis and bhabhijis," she feels that a lot of under confidence among women is due to negative perceptions men enforce on them. "We should take pride in whatever we do, after all women make up half of the planet," she shrugs off the 'niche subject' adage and exclaims - "move over men, we need our space!" Had she not had her baby girl, Shona, who comes from a family that's given us masterpieces like Hero Hiralal, Chashmebaddoor, Jalwa and Khatta Meetha, would've directed Jaane Tu Ya Jaane Na. But that was then, now is the time for raging bulls and bear hugs, which reminds us of the spat with Tanushree Dutta. "Bollywood has this thing of blowing up the teeniest of issues. It was something real small and people do it just to attract attention and be different," she reasons.

She's a trained Bharatnatyam dancer, a sharp photographer, great writer (in days when Maharashtra Herald had only men reporters), and fine actor. "All in one, it's being a director," Shona's sticking to her choice of profession, and yes, making everyone see green with her investments. "Of course, I'm hooked," she chirps. Lookout for her next: "a romantic commercial blockbuster script." Till then, lets 'stock' and 'share'.

Heading: LMC garbage dumps adorn city - Indian Express
Content:
Jail record says Phool Devi is 82 years old. Her lawyer puts her age at 94. According to her grandson, she is actually 108. Whatever her age is, Phool Devi can't walk or even sit, her eyesight is poor and she is hard of hearing, and she has cancer of the gall bladder.

Phool Devi was sent to jail in 2003 for a murder she and her son committed in 1976. When she is not in the Nari Bandi Niketan of the Lucknow Model Jail, the old woman is found in hospitals.

If not cancer, it is for her breathing problem, or some other illness that she has to be taken to one hospital or the other almost every alternate day. Last week, she was first taken to the Balrampur Hospital and later to the Chhatrapati Shahuji Maharaj Medical University (CSMMU).

On Thursday, Phool Devi was discharged and sent to jail again.

"She needs a surgery for her stomach ailment. But her age doesn't allow it. Doctors keep her under observation when her condition deteriorates and discharge her when she is a little better," said a jail employee.

What the jail authorities call "stomach ailment" is cancer of the gall bladder, according to Dr Rama Kant, head of the surgical department at the CSMMU.

Given her condition, the jail staff is always on tenterhooks. And for her grandson Bhola Nath Pandey, it means making frequent trips to Lucknow.

"Four days ago, I got information that my grandmother had been hospitalised. We rushed to Lucknow from Mirzapur. It has become routine for us to rush to Lucknow to be with her. We requested the jail administration to release her on parole so that we could take care of her at home, but they did not agree," said Bhola Nath.

Phool Devi's relatives are preparing to file another petition. The process involves taking opinion of the police and the district administration and tabling a report before the Jail Committee. The committee's report is forwarded to the state government for a final decision.

Prisoners are released from jail on four grounds — mercy petition, premature release, by nomination, or in case of infirmity. Bhola Nath, a farmer, doesn't even know they can apply for her release on the ground of infirmity.

In fact, a petition for release on this ground has a better chance because, as Senior Superintendent (Jail) VK Jain said, the other grounds for release from jail require a prisoner to have spent over 14 years behind the bars.

"When an inmate of such ripe age is admitted in the hospital, we inform their family members," said Jain. Though they had the facility of in-house doctors, patients are referred to hospitals when they show no sign of recovery, he said. The last inmate to be released on grounds of infirmity was Prabhu Baga, a murder convict. He was released from the Varanasi Central Jail on May 14, 2008.

Inspector General (Prison) Sulkhan Singh said: "We have prepared a list of elderly inmates and will try to take up their case on priority basis."

Phool Devi's crime
The Mirzapur police had registered a case against Phool Devi and her son Kashi Nath Pandey, who is now serving term in the Varanasi Central Jail, on November 20, 1976, on the complaint of their neighbour, Santram Pandey. The two had been accused of killing Pandey's two minor sons owing to enmity. The sessions court awarded life imprisonment to Phool Devi and her son on March 31, 1979.

The duo challenged the conviction in the Allahabad High Court, but it upheld the conviction on April 13, 2003. Since then, the mother and son have been in jail. The family says their appeal in the Supreme Court is pending.

Heading: Ahead of LS polls, communal tension heats up - Indian Express
Content:
The Lucknow Municipal Corporation (LMC) has been recently dragged to court for dumping garbage at Smriti Upvan — a green area. But the civic body continues with similar activities at a few other places in the city.

The agency's largest unauthorised dumping ground is near Avantibai Lodhi crossing on Hardoi Road. On an average, a truck arrives every five minutes on any given day. The illegal dumping ground is close to a site earmarked for the construction of Manyawar Shree Kanshiramji Uttar Pradesh Institute of Technology.

According to LMC workers at the site, they have been dumping garbage here for over a year now. The land, owned by the nearby villages, is full of garbage.

The whole area smells foul. Bulldozers are constantly at work, spreading and compacting the waste.

For the people of nearby villages — Mansud Nagar, Barwankhurd, Hayat Nagar, Peer Nagar and Barikalan — life is miserable. "There is a stench and insects all over. But what can we do?" said Santosh Kumar, a resident of Mansud Nagar.

Sandeep, a food stall owner at Aavanti Bai Lodhi crossing, said: "It has ruined my business. Earlier, my stall used to be abuzz with students, as there is an engineering college nearby. But they don't come here anymore."

Vikas, another food stall owner, said: "When we opposed the dumping of garbage in the beginning, LMC officials threatened us that they will dump garbage right in front of our shops."

The agency had stopped dumping garbage at Smriti Upwan after a public interest litigation was filed in the High Court last week. According to LMC authorities, by dumping garbage there, it was levelling a low area. This is a standard excuse offered every time LMC is caught dumping garbage illegally. They also claimed that the "low-lying area" in Smriti Upvan is, in fact, a water body.

An employee at Smriti Upvan said: "The number of visitors and morning walkers began to decline when the LMC had started dumping garbage here. About 10 days ago, when reports of garbage dumping appeared in the media, LMC began to cover the garbage with soil.

Earlier, the civic body had attracted flak from the High Court for dumping garbage on the bank of river Gomti near Gandhi Sethu. The court had not only directed it to stop the practice, but had also asked the National Environment Engineering Research Institute to recommend steps to check the damage caused. The agency was told the implement the measures at the earliest.

The Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board's (UPPCB) Chief Environmental Officer, Swami Nath Ram, said: "Garbage dumping is unscientific, as it affects the environment. In the past, the board had served notice to the municipalty for dumping garbage near Gandi Setu and asked it to identify sites for garbage disposal."

Additional Municipal Commissioner A C Sinha admitted that the agency was dumping garbage at several sites near Hardoi Road and Mohan Road. "There is no other place. Dumping at Hardoi Road and Mohan Road is a temporary arrangement. Under the JNNURM scheme, the Lucknow Development Authority has identified two sites for dumping grounds. Soon, the sites will be developed waste disposal." he added.

LDA pulled up for changing Smriti Upvan's old design
The Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court pulled up the LDA on Thursday for changing the old design of Smriti Upvan at Bangla Bazaar and levelling a water body by dumping garbage there. The High Court also directed LDA to submit all details about Smriti Upvan on September 29. The Bench issued the directions while hearing a PIL filed by two retired Army officers. LDA Vice-Chairman Mukesh Kumar Meshram said a few changes were being made in the structure of Smriti Upvan.

Other dumping sites


* BASANT KUNJ, HARDOI ROAD: A scheme of the Lucknow Development Authority, where garbage is being dumped on around 100 plots of Sector O. "For over five months now, LMC has been dumping garbage on these plots and nearby areas," a LDA employee at adjacent Jogger's Park said. An LMC official, however, claimed the waste was being dumped to level the ground.
* DUBAGGA, RING ROAD: Some shanties stood here until the LMC razed them some time ago, terming them illegal. After clearing the "encroachment", LMC started dumping garbage on the land, said Mohammad Sahrif, a butcher.

Heading: State has a feather in its cap: The highest number of child labourers - Indian Express
Content:
The recent incidents of communal violence in eastern UP are threatening to accelerate the communal polarisation in the state ahead of the next parliamentary elections.

In a law and order review meeting held in August, Chief Minister Mayawati had cautioned the police about the attempts made to create communal discord in the state. Yet, the administration had failed to respond to the situation in several districts.

The first incident occurred in Azamgarh on September 7, when the cavalcade of BJP parliamentarian Yogi Aditya Nath, was attacked. One person was killed as the police had to open fire to quell the riotous mob. Several stray incidents occurred next day during the bandh called by the Vishwa Hindu Parishad. Incidents of stone pelting and clashes occurred in Gonda, Bahriach, and Jaunpur and Sultanpur districts.

While the Congress and Samajwadi Party accused the ruling BSP of being soft on the Hindutuva forces, BJP blame the rest of pursuing appeasement policy with an eye on Muslim votes.

"After the arrest of SIMI member Abu Bashar, his village overnight turned into pilgrimage for the secular parties like Congress and the SP and Imam Bukhari," said Raghavendra Pratap, of Yogi Aditya Nath-led Hindu Vahini. "SP parliamentarian Abu Azami and Bukhari delivered provocative speeches threatening to create 1947 like situation in the country. But no action was taken against these leaders," he said.

Congress leader Akhilesh Singh, on the other hand, said: "Since elections are round the corner, both BSP and the BJP are returning to their original agenda of creating polarisation in the society." SP leader Rajendra Chowdhary said: "Communal clash in Azamgarh was not possible without the tacit support of the administration."

The administration talked tough on tackling any such future incidents. "There was communal tension only in Azamgarh. The SP and the DIG were suspended as they had failed to respond despite being alerted by the state government," said Brijlal ADG (Law and Order).

The BJP, meanwhile, submitted a memorandum on Friday to Governor T V Rajeswar. The party alleged that the Congress, SP and BSP had issued provocative statements during their visit to the village of SIMI member Abu Bashar.

Heading: Khurja state’s most polluted town, Lucknow comes second - Indian Express
Content:
Uttar Pradesh now has earned another dubious distinction: 19.27 lakh child labourers, the highest in the country.

The state, which was behind Andhra Pradesh with 14.10 lakh child labourers in 1991, has witnessed a 26 per cent increase in the last seven years. Interestingly, Andhra Pradesh, which had 16.61 lakh child labourers in 1991, has managed to bring down the number to 13.63 lakh in the same period.

The bad news comes even as the state government continues spending Rs 2.65 crore every year on the rehabilitation and welfare of child labourers. The rehabilitation notwithstanding, the state has over 15,000 child labourers who are still out of school. This number keeps on increasing, with a large number of children still remaining unchecked and untraced.

"Ironically, children who work indoors are not factored in. That figure will include the children of the craftsmen and those who do petty jobs. And in this case, it is not the parents but the employers who should be caught and penalised," said Shanta Sinha, Magsaysay award winner and chairperson of National Commission for the Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR).

Sinha and her NCPCR colleague Sandhya Bajaj, who are in the state capital to participate in the regional consultation on Abolition of Child Labour and Right to Education — jointly organised by UP government, UNICEF and NCPCR — felt the state government needs to identify the problems related to child rights and child labour.

"We want to ensure child rights even for those children who work in the agricultural sector. Ironically, they may not be covered under the purview of the Child Labour Act, yet they need to be identified as child labourers too," Sinha said.

Echoing the words of Sinha, Bajaj said: "The state of child rights in UP is bad and this can be ascertained from the fact that we get the maximum number of complaints regarding child labour and child rights violations from the state."

"We cannot disclose the exact figure, but children in UP need to be heard even more," Bajaj added.

Incidentally, the state government runs the National Child Labour programme in 42 districts, which has 79,674 students. Yet, child labour remains a major problem and duplicate enrollment adds to it.

Shamshad Khan of Creda, an organisation working on the issue of child labour in the carpet belt of Bhadohi, said: "Often, there is a duplication in school enrollment figures between the education department and the labour department, both who are targeting children who are out of school. And then, the Inter State Migrant labourers Act is non-existent in UP, which is why we cannot take care of children who come with their parents as labourers from other states."

According to Sinha, setting up of a state child rights commission would help children, including child labourers in the state, voice for their rights. "We have seen that children are very responsive and vocal when you ask about their problems. And with a state child rights commission, we can delegate a lot of our work to it," Sinha said.

Officials from labour department, education department, women and child development department, and UNICEF were present during the consultation.

Heading: Govt vehicles flaunt banned pressure horns - Indian Express
Content:
Situated 100 km from Delhi, Khurja has emerged as the most polluted place in Uttar Pradesh, having the highest level of suspended particulate matter (SPM) in the air, according to the data compiled by the Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board (UPPCB).

When it comes to rating towns on the pollution parameter, Khujra is followed by Lucknow and Kanpur.

The high level of SPM and respiratory supended particulate matter (RSPM), may not only lead to respiratory and lung diseases, but also cause asthma, bronchitis and cancer.

"We began monitoring Khurja last year. The reason behind the increasing pollution level in the area is the presence of pottery factories, which lack the use of modern technology. They still use low chimneys and old-designed furnaces," said a senior UPPCB official. "In the past, UPPCB had notified the Central Pollution Control Board about the increasing pollution level in various parts of the state and suggested preparation of an action plan to tackle the situation," he added.

The permissible level of SPM in residential and commercial areas is 140 micrograms per cubic metre. When it comes to RSPM, it's 60 micrograms per cubic metre.

For industrial areas, the permissible limits are 360 micrograms per cubic metre and 120 micrograms per cubic metre respectively.

In 2007, Khurja's ambient air quality was the worst with an yearly average of 430.29 micrograms per cubic metre SPM in residential areas, followed by Kanpur and Lucknow at 421.7 micrograms per cubic metre and 390.9 micrograms per cubic metre respectively.

The yearly average of RSPM level in residential areas of Khurja was also highest at 221.88 micrograms per cubic meter. Next was Kanpur at 188.7 micrograms per cubic meter and Lucknow at 186.6 micrograms per cubic meter.

In industrial areas, the SPM level was recorded highest at 500.07 micrograms per cubic metre in Khurja, followed by Kanpur at 464.05 micrograms per cubic metre and Ferozabad at 463 micrograms per cubic metre. The RSPM level in the industrial area of Kanpur was highest at 244.95 micrograms per cubic metre followed by Ghaziabad at 232.15 micrograms per cubic metre and Khurja at 223.25 micrograms per cubic metre.

Heading: Flood lesson: disaster management authority to come up in districts - Indian Express
Content:
When it comes to senior government officers, there is only one rule: rules can be given a go-by if it is convenient. These days, that rule is applying to the use of banned pressure horns in their own government vehicles.

The pressure horns, considered illegal under the Motor Vehicles Act, are freely available in the state capital. But the worst of it is that the cars of senior government officers — including those whose job is to prevent the use of these horns — flaunt them.

These horns produce a harsh, shrill and a alarming noise. Section 119(2) of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules reads: "No motor vehicle shall be fitted with any multitoned horn giving a succession of different notes."

Still, the horns are to be had at the Lalbagh market for a paltry Rs 1,350 — even if they are not on conspicuous display.

"There is a market for pressure horns. Why else would we sell them?" said one of the shopkeepers. Another said he sells at least two a day.

The traders agree that the biggest users are government vehicles and owners of big cars "who know they can easily get away with it".

Asked about the regular use of pressure horns, ASP (Traffic) Rajendra Kumar said: "We penalise vehicles which use pressure horns under Section 190 (2) of the Motor Vehicle Act. They have to pay a penalty of Rs 1,500."

But he was also quick to pass the buck. "It is the Civil Lines which is responsible for the control of the sale of these horns," he added.

It is probably another matter that Circle Office (Traffic) Sukhbir Singh — who is supposed to keep a check on its use — too, flaunts one of these horns.

Singh has his own defense. "Yes, there is a hooter and a pressure horn in my vehicle. But I do not use either of them. These were attached even before I got the car. I have already disconnected the wires," he said.

In fact, every officer whose vehicle has a pressure horn, has some explanation or the other. Some even vehemently deny its presence. Among them is Superintendent of Police (Traffic) Rajender Singh, who said, "My vehicle does not have a pressure horn but only a hooter. I travel with the chief minister's escort, so I am permitted to keep it."

Heading: Students clash with police in Lucknow - Indian Express
Content:
In the wake of the state's worst-ever floods in a decade, the state government has decided to form a District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) in each district.

According to the plan, this body will work in close coordination with the State Disaster Management Authority and will play an integral role in tackling different types of disasters at the district level.

Speaking about the government's latest initiative, Principal Secretary (Revenue) Balvinder Kumar said DDMAs are being formed keeping in mind that almost all the districts in the state face disasters of one kind or the other.

"While flood is one of the biggest problems, affecting over two dozen districts, other problems include drought, terrorism, Naxal activities and crop failure, which also need proper handling," Kumar said.

"Hence, with a district authority having a specific plan in hand, it would become easier for us to be prepared to face any disasters," he added.

The DDMAs, which will function on the lines of the State Disaster Management Authority, will have the district magistrate as its chairperson.

The district's senior superintendent of police, chief development officer and chief medical officer will be the principal members of the authority. Representatives of two NGOs working on the issue of disaster and nominated by the district magistrate will also find their place in the authority.

The government plans to allocate Rs 2.5 crore to each DDMA as annual budget, which can be hiked in case of disaster.

"We will have the funds divided into two sections — the mitigation fund and the response fund. The mitigation fund will be for constructions and awareness programmes regarding the district-specific disasters. And the response fund will help us manage things like rescue operations, rehabilitation programmes etc in case disaster strikes," Kumar said.

He added that the budget amount, especially in the response fund, can increase in times of disasters.

The districts will be asked to make a disaster management plan keeping in mind the major problems hitting them. Some districts, which suffer from two or more problems, will have a comprehensive disaster management plan.

The Department of Revenue has finalised the plans related to the formation of these bodies. It expects the final nod sometime next week.

Heading: CSMMU docs out to support arrested private practitioners - Indian Express
Content:
Protesting against the arrest of a student leader, students of Lucknow Christian PG College blocked roads and pelted stones on policemen, leaving two of them injured on Friday. Police later arrested seven more students and lodged FIRs against 149 others — including two teachers of the college — for rioting.

On Thursday, S W Prasad, a teacher of the college had lodged a complaint with Wazirganj police alleging that Fahrul Hassan, a student leader, was threatening to kill him as he had expressed his inability to allot him a room in a college hostel.

This led to the arrest of Hassan on Friday morning and that triggered the protests. The road blockades led to traffic chaos near the college and Balrampur Hospital.

When police reached the spot, students pelted them with stones in which two policemen, including Sub Inspector JP Singh, were injured.

To disperse the mob police resorted to mild lathicharge. The two teachers — CA Macfarland and TR Hamlin — against whom police have filed an FIR, has been accused of inciting the violence.

Both teachers, however, denied the charges. "When students were blocking road, I was in the Principal's office. If police asks me, I will give them all the details," Hamlin said. Macfarland said: "I was not involved at all. I am also not aware that my name has been included in the FIR."

Heading: Eight IPS officers transferred - Indian Express
Content:
Following the arrest of two doctors on charges of negligence and fraud, the faculty members of the Chhatrapati Shahuji Maharaj Medical University and doctors of Provincial Medical Services came out in their support on Friday. 

The private practitioners threatened to close down their respective ICUs "if the government does not stop harassing the doctors."

"Right from police to other government officials — all come to us for their treatment. Now they allege that we are thieves. Doctors are unnecessarily being harassed and we will not let this happen any more," said Dr A M Khan, member of the Nursing Home Association.

Two doctors — Mirza Waqar Begh and Satish Kumar Bose — were arrested on Wednesday in connection with the death of a two and half-month-old child on April 17.

Heading: Metro in pipeline for Lucknow, Kanpur - Indian Express
Content: The state government transferred eight senior IPS officers, including Gorakhpur SSP Piyush Mordiya, on Friday. Mordiya swapped places with R K Srivastava, SP of CB-CID (Headquarters) at Lucknow while Sanjay Kakkar, another SP posted with the CB-CID Lucknow, was transferred to Regional Intelligence office in the state capital in the same capacity. IG (Establishment) Ram Deo was transferred to the Telecom wing of the UP Police in the same capacity. The secretary to the Chief Minister, Vijay Singh, has been given the additional charge after Deo vacated his post. DIG Basti Range K K Tripathi has been asked to join Gorakhpur Range while DIG Abhay Kumar Prasad, who was transferred earlier to Aligarh Range from Gorakhpur, has been asked to replace Tripathi.

Heading: Buddhadeb govt offers 70 Nano acres but Mamata wants 300 - Indian Express
Content: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) will soon begin a preliminary survey for the construction of Metro rail project in Lucknow and Kanpur. The state housing department will soon make a request to the DMRC to prepare the detailed project report (DPR) for both cities. A DMRC team met Chief Secretary Atul Gupta on Friday and discussed the feasibility of the project. The team indicated that it will need at least six months time to prepare the DPR. The team expressed confidence that the work on the metro project can commence within the next 12 to 18 months.

Heading: Don’t make Tata ‘secret’ deal public: HC - Indian Express
Content:
DEADLOCK: Trinamool rejects first offer, insists on land in project area

Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee rejected the first land-for-land offer by West Bengal Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee this evening effectively taking the Nano deadlock back to where it was before both sides agreed to talk.

In an 80-minute meeting, the CM told Mamata that the government was prepared to return 70 acres, mostly from within the project premises — but not affecting the mother plant or the vendor park — to rehabilitate unwilling farmers. This includes 47 acres that was returned to the West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation and 20 acres of waterbodies. He also offered financial assistance to farmers to help them buy land adjacent to the project area.

But Mamata refused, saying she wanted 400 acres back, of which 300 acres should be from within the project area. "It's a gentleman's agreement that we signed in the presence of a Constitutional authority — the Governor. We won't agree to anything less than 300 acres from within the Tata Motors factory," she said.

As per the agreement, the government had committed to "the maximum" land that can be returned from within the project area. Officials said that worked out to 70 acres since anything more would disturb the project. With suspension of work by the Tatas entering its third week, officials indicated that should the deadlock continue, Tata Motors is ready to shift machinery and equipment outside the state.

For the record, though, Mamata kept the door open. Saying she would apprise the Governor on today's meeting, Mamata said: "We have kept our word about suspension of agitation. If necessary, we will again meet and discuss the matter...We suspended the agitation, Tatas can start work. Why are they still not doing anything?"

Heading: ‘China to invest only after Singur resolution’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Calcutta High Court directed the state government on Friday not to make public the "secret" part of the March 9, 2007, agreement between Tata Motors and the West Bengal government for the next two weeks.

In a petition, Samaraditya Pal, counsel for Tata Motors, said the government and the West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC) — having already made public a portion of the agreement — may now disclose the "secret" part.

The disclosure that has been made already is a violation of the Right to Information (RTI) Act 2005, he contended. The agreement, being signed between the government-owned WBIDC and the Tata Motors, cannot be disclosed to a third party according to the provisions of the Act.

The WBIDC had disclosed the portion of the agreement on their website on September 5, after a direction by the Chief Information Commissioner. Sudip Bandyopadyay, Congress legislator and chairman of the Standing Committee on business and commerce, had also urged the government to make the agreement public. Following that, Commerce and Industries Minister Nirupam Sen had read out a portion of the agreement on August 27 in the Standing Committee meeting and the WBIDC had published the three-page agreement in its website.

Heading: Last Lear is special, says Big B - Indian Express
Content:
With the Singur impasse putting a question mark on the investment climate in West Bengal, Chinese Consul-General in Kolkata, Mao Siwei, on Friday said his country's businessmen will look forward to invest in the state only after the deadlock over Tata's car factory project is resolved.

Speaking to the media on the sidelines of a seminar "Doing Business with China", organised by Engineering Export Promotion Council (EEPC), Siwei said: "Hopefully there will be a good business environment after the resolution of the deadlock."

Chinese companies are in the process of entering into joint ventures with West Bengal and will be interested in setting up manufacturing units in steel, power and tyres, he said.

These investments are, however, in the initial stages and the exact figures are not available, the counsul-general added.

The Export India Promotion Council (EPCC), meanwhile, said its 20th Indian

Export Engineering Exhibition (INDEE) will be held in Shanghai from November 4 to 8. According to the members of EPCC, China imported $11.13 billion worth machinery tools in 2006 and this figure increased by 11.58 per cent the next year with India managing a meagre share of 0.1 percent of the market.

"Potential products that we can export to China are metalwork, CNC machine tools, industrial automation, environment protection equipment, and information and communication technology," said M C Shah, chairman, publication, exhibition and delegation committee of EPCC.

Heading: Anti-CPM nest in Buddha’s own backyard - Indian Express
Content:
His father wrote in Madhushala — "Jo beet gayi so baat gayi". There doesn't seem to be a follower more ardent than son Amitabh Bachchan, who has let bygones be bygones, and refused to be drawn into a discussion on the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena's agitation against his family.

Claiming he has forgiven and forgotten, the Shehenshah of Bollywood is now concentrating on his latest release The Last Lear.

In a promotional event in Kolkata on Friday, Bachchan said: "It is a closed chapter now. I don't see any point discussing it further. All has been forgotten. We are friends."

"Overwhelmed" by the city's response to his latest film, the superstar said: "Kolkata has always been nice to me, but this event was special. This is the first time that I have worked with Rituda (Rituparno Ghosh) and this film is very important," he said.

The Last Lear team, including Bachchan, Rituparno Ghosh, Arjun Rampal, Jishu Sengupta and Divya Dutta, went around the city attending various functions. The film is based on Utpal Dutt's play Aajker Shahjahan.

"I wanted to work with Rituda for a long time and we worked on various ideas. This script seemed to be the most potent, which is why we went ahead with it," said Bachchan. The Utpal Dutt connection was another incentive, he added. "I shared a wonderful relationship with Utpalda. We have worked together in many films. In fact, my first film, Saat Hindustani, was with him."

Meeta Mondol, the eight-year-old child whose heart disease treatment is borne by Bachchan, also made an impromptu appearance during the function.

"I was watching television one day when I saw the smiling face of this child and heard her story. I decided I must do something about it," he said.

Heading: Scientists return home after Geneva trip - Indian Express
Content:
In the Writers' Buildings, Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's backyard, government employees have adapted the "Nandigram model" to press for their demands.

For the last two weeks, cutting across political borders, employees have joined hands to throw the state secretariat into total chaos. The Mahakaran Sangram Committee — a cluster of ten organisations — has been created as an anti-CPM forum with the backing of Naxals, the SUCI, Trinamool Congress and the Congress. It has dealt a massive blow to the government, forcing the chief secretary to issue a circular and asking the police and CID to initiate inquires.

To begin with, the organisation has been telling the workers that compared to the Central government, state government employees are grossly underpaid.

The message has hit home: at least three breakaway groups of the CPM-backed coordination committee and a section of RSP are supporting the Mahakaran Sangram Committee.

The most influential of the organisations is the West Bengal Government Employees' Union (Naba Parjaya), a breakaway group of the coordination committee.

Its general secretary, Samir Ranjan Mazumder, who has repeatedly travelled to Nandigram, said: "It would not be wrong to say this is not based on the Nandigram model, but actually this is a concerted movement against the Left Front government. We have different ideologies, but we have decided to fight against an autocratic government led by Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee."

On Thursday, the chief secretary issued an order that employees are only allowed to hold small informal meeting during the lunch hour. They cannot disturb other employees or hold demonstrations in the office.

"Such activities amount to acts of indiscipline," the order said.

But on Friday too, the members of the organisation paraded through the Writers Building, shouting slogans even after 2.30 pm. "We don't care about these orders. If we let go of our rights now, we will be snubbed forever," said Shyamal Mitra, one of its leaders. The development has put the coordination committee in a spot. Manoj Guha, its joint secretary, said: "We are aware that some people from our organisation have left to join the movement. Do you want us to begin fisticuffs? We have asked our people to inquire into it."

Heading: 160 Bangla infiltrators detained - Indian Express
Content:
Hard work, analogue chips, quark-gluon plasma, a new country and a whole new experience — the two scientists of Variable Energy Cyclotron Centre (VECC) who have just returned from Geneva after taking part in the CERN project, are now busy sharing tales of everything with their fellow mates in Kolkata.

Dr Zubayer Ahammed and Mriganko Mondol, who were present in Geneva when the proton beams of the historic CERN project were fired, returned to the Salt Lake centre on Thursday morning.

Ahammed, who is charge of the software and calibration along with the overall operation of the Photon Multiplicity Detector (PMD), worked at the CERN project in Geneva for more than a month.

"I not only missed home food but I also missed the first day of Ramzan that I usually spend with my family," said Ahammed.

Back home in Kaikhali, his wife Nazia Alam and twin daughters Marhia and Aisha could not, however, gauge the importance of the CERN project and used to wait longingly for a phone call from Ahammed, who did his schooling from KD Vidyalaya in a remote village called Chhabghati in Murshidabad. "Since childhood I used to prefix 'Dr' to my name. Even though there wasn't enough scope for higher studies in my village, I had a dream to pursue higher education," said Ahammed.

"It was the best experience of my life to be at CERN when the experiment started. Hundreds of experimentalists and theoreticians across the world had been waiting for this day," he says, a glint visible in his eyes.

While Ahammed had his wife and children eagerly waiting for his return, somewhere in Kishorepur near Arambagh, Mriganko Mondol's parents were also awaiting their son's return.

Mondol, who had gone to Geneva for the CERN experiment, is a doctoral student at VECC and is working on a thesis on quark-gluon plasma.

While the project in whole might have been an enriching experience for the duo, they both confessed that when it came to satiating their hunger, they had a harrowing time. It took them two whole days to find an Indian market from where they could buy cooking ingredients.

"I did not know how to cook. But since we used to have European food for breakfast and lunch, I decided to learn to cook Indian food and finally ended up learning new recipes," said Mondol.

"When I came back, I visited my village. My father, a teacher of Sanskrit in the village school, always believed in me. The other villagers are proud of me, but it is quite difficult for them to understand what I actually do," he said.

Heading: Three days on, Jadavpur still in grip of enteric menace - Indian Express
Content:
The Border Security Force (BSF) rounded up 160 Bangladeshi nationals from three different locations in North 24 Parganas on Friday after the foreigners had trespassed into the Indian territory in boats.

In total, three boats were intercepted between 7 and 8 in the morning.

This is one of the largest interceptions in recent years when such a large group of Bangladeshi civilians were apprehended in a single drive. The BSF was tipped-off about the arrival of boats carrying Bangladeshi nationals in the South Bengal Frontier.

Later, the BSF invited both Indian and Bangladeshi scribes to interact with the apprehended foreigners. A large contingent of media personnel was taken to the Hasnabad area for the purpose.

The issue will be taken up in the next DIG-level talks between the border forces of the two nations, BSF officials said. "The BSF will lodge a protest note on the issue," said Vikash Chandra, additional DIG (G).

The Bangladeshi nationals had crossed over into the Indian territory in broad daylight taking advantage of the frequent ferry services in the area. In the first case, the boat carrying the Bangladeshi nationals had crossed the Icchamati river and ventured three kilometres into the Indian territory when its journey was cut short by a BSF patrol boat. The location was the Mangalchandi area near the Indo-Bangla border. One hundred seven people were on board of which 70 were men, 20 women and 17 children. Preliminary interrogation revealed that the passengers had begun their journey from Satkhira in Bangladesh.

In the second incident, the BSF intercepted another boat ferrying 42 Bangladeshi nationals without valid documents on the Raimangal river near Yogeshganj. As many as 18 children, 13 women and 11 men were on board. The boatman was an Indian.

In the third and the final interception, 11 infiltrators were apprehended when they were making way to the ferry ghat on a rickshaw van after crossing the Icchamati river that forms a riverine boundary between the two nations.

BSF officials said it was difficult to monitor each and every boat ferrying in the area. "They keep sneaking through this riverine route in small numbers.," said a senior BSF official.

Heading: ‘Polybag ban may end in crisis for plastic industry’ - Indian Express
Content:
The enteric outbreak in Rabindra Pally and Purba Phulbagan in ward number 101 in Jadavpur area is not under control even after three days. The number of people affected, as estimated on Friday, has reached nearly 270.

"30 people have registered their names in the health camp today. Ten of them have been admitted in several hospitals of the city including MR Bangur, Beleghata ID Hospital and Bagha Jatin Hospital. Around 270 people have been affected till date," said an official at the health camp set up in the area.

The enteric outbreak has been caused by water contamination following a breach in the water supply line, and whether the water is safe for consumption or not, is yet to be determined. The KMC has collected samples of the water from the area to conduct tests and is awaiting the report.

The health department of the KMC, meanwhile, has declared the water "safe" even before getting the report. "We have taken prompt action to control the contamination and now the water in the area is safe," said Debdwaipayan Chattopadhyay, Chief Medical Health Officer, KMC

The health officials at the camp, however, have reasons to believe otherwise. "We are collecting water samples from several places and have sent them to the laboratory. But we are yet to get the report that the water is safe for use. The contamination has spread over a large area so it will take time to control it," said a camp official.

Heading: KMC lacks infrastructure to fight vector-borne diseases - Indian Express
Content:
The ban imposed on plastic bags in the city by the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) is costing the plastic industry dear. The manufacturers of plastic goods claim that lack of awareness among common people has led to this ban, and this, in turn, is pushing the entire plastic industry towards a crisis and making it suffer huge losses.

"Many municipalities, including the KMC, have restricted the use of plastics. So shop owners have started using paper bags. It is a misconception that all kinds of plastic bags are harmful. We expect the state government to come forward and increase the awareness among people about use of plastic materials," said Arup Chakraborty, general manager, Haldia Petrochemicals Ltd.

According to Ajit Bagade, regional manager, Reliance Industries Ltd, paper bags consume 40 to 70 per cent more energy than plastic bags when they are manufactured. "Moreover, paper bags generate 80 per cent more waste than plastic bags since the scope for recycling paper bags is very less," added Bagade.

Environmentalists, however, are up in arms against the use of plastic bags in the city. "The plastic manufacturing industries may have some commercial interests in saying that plastic is not harmful for the environment. Plastic is non-biodegradable, so it has already spoilt the drainage and sewerage system by choking it," said Subhas Dutta, environmentalist.

"Since the KMC does not have a waste segregation system, plastic mixes with the soil. This way it also harms the soil," added Dutta.

Heading: HC directs govt to submit action plan for hawkers - Indian Express
Content:
Even after having spent around Rs 1.5 crore in taking preventive measures to control vector-borne diseases, the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) still lacks the adequate infrastructure to do so.

"Some advanced proposals to fight vector-borne diseases, including one to set up an entomology unit, are gathering dust since the health department is unwilling to change the existing system," said a senior civic official on condition of anonymity.

The KMC, moreover, seems to be the only municipality among other metropolitan cities like Delhi, Mumbai and Bangalore, which is still carrying on with the practice of fogging — something that has become obsolete in other cities.

Environmentalists and entomologists often criticise the practice of fogging. Even the health department of the KMC agrees that fogging can cause severe health hazards because of its high carbon monoxide content. Moreover, fogging has become ineffective in destroying mosquitoes.

"Since the eco-behavioural pattern of mosquitoes has changed with time, fogging seems to be resistant to mosquitoes. Earlier the concept was based on the principle that mosquitoes remain in the room after sucking blood from an infected person and thus fogging was effective. But, now it has been found that after sucking blood the insects move out. So fogging cannot be effective now, " said Debashis Biswas, vector control officer, KMC.

Sahidul Islam, joint commissioner of the KMC, however, said fogging has to be used 'under pressure'. Islam said: "We are forced to practise fogging since it is more popular than other methods. There is a lack of awareness in common people about the negative effects of fogging. We are often asked by several councillors to use fogging in some areas. We also understand that fogging should be banned but we have to use it under pressure".

Heading: CU looks into ragging allegation, but only after Gandhi intervenes - Indian Express
Content:
A division bench of Chief Justice S S Nijjar and Justice Maharaj Sinha has directed the state government to place the action plan on hawkers of the city after the Puja vacation. The bench was not happy with the traffic movement owing to hawkers who have encroached into the city footpaths .

Balai Roy, state advocate-general, informed the bench that the state government has already submitted the proposal on hawkers to the Central government. The Central government, meanwhile, has formulated a national policy on hawkers and it would be implemented accordingly to legal provisions, Roy said.

Roy also explained that the state government is thinking of earmarking some zones for hawkers in different city locations. For example, a fast food zone for office-goers will be earmarked in BBD Bag, and the hawkers will be allowed to hawk during a particular time.

During the hearing, the division bench expressed unhappiness at the traffic situation in the city, and said the free flow of traffic is being regularly disrupted because of hawkers.

Taxis and other public vehicles are parked in no-parking zones and the police officers never take any steps against it, the bench observed.

Environmentalist Subhas Dutta alleged that shop owners in Burrabazar dump articles on footpath, which create obstructions. But Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) does not take steps to remove it.

The division bench has asked the KMC for a report.

Heading: Kolkata Port registers 13% growth in container handling - Indian Express
Content:
It took a letter from Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi to make the authorities of the Calcutta University sit up and look into the ragging allegations made by a first-year student of Nutrition Honours of Calcutta Women's College.

On Friday, the registrar of Calcutta University, Basab Chaudhuri, met the student and her father, Smriti Kumar Giri, almost two months after she had complained that her seniors at the V L Mita Student Hall had ragged her.

The college, which had earlier dismissed the complaint saying that it was not a serious issue as the girl was merely teased, received a letter from her father on August 12. Giri, a resident of Contai in East Midnapore, had also sent a copy of the letter to the Governor in which he had stated that her daughter was forced to sing, dance and imitate her local dialect. She was also fined for skipping meals and was made to sit for hours together by putting a finger in her nose, Giri wrote in the letter. According to Raj Bhavan sources, on August 21, the Governor wrote a letter to the Vice-Chancellor of the university asking him to look into the matter and take appropriate steps.

After meeting the student and her father, the registrar of the university said: "I had a discussion with the father of the girl. Since the last few days the girl is attending classes at her college. It also appears to me that the parent has also been convinced in this regard." The university still states that it is not a case of ragging.

Giri, meanwhile, said that he was successful in persuading his daughter to go back to the college and resume her studies. "Today, the university offered to arrange accommodation for my daughter in the same hostel. The officials asked me whether I wanted the students involved to be punished," he said. The girl had joined the hostel as a guest boarder for one month on July 14, but had to leave the hostel on August 10.

Heading: HC appoints officer to look into park encroachment - Indian Express
Content:
The Kolkata Port Trust (KoPT) has achieved an all time high figure of 41,379 Twenty Equivalent Units (TEUs) in container handling in August, 2008.

According to KoPT officials, in the period between April to August, this year, the port handled 1,91,589 TEUs against 1,66,205 TEUs during the same period last year.

A K Chanda, Chairman of the KoPT said that in comparison with the container traffic of 36,634 TEUs in August 2007, the port has registered a growth of 13 per cent for August 2008.

With the introduction of sophisticated handling equipment like mobile harbours cranes, rubber tyred gantry cranes and reach stackers port productivity has improved considerably, the chairman added.

The commodities that have contributed to the growth of container traffic include electronic goods, chemicals, spare parts of machinery, metal scraps in the import leg and jute and jute products, tea, ferrochrome, industrial raw materials, tin plate, cotton in the export leg.

Heading: On a fortnight trip, life in metro enthralls Ladakh girls - Indian Express
Content:
A Division Bench of Chief Justice S S Nijjar and Justice Maharaj Sinha on Friday appointed a special officer to inspect the park at BD block in Salt Lake and earmark the area that Bidhannagar Municipality had allegedly encroached into while shifting the market there.

During the hearing on August 8, a Bench headed by Chief Justice Nijjar had asked the municipality to ensure that the market does not occupy over 40 per cent area. Locals, however, moved a plea stating that the municipality had encroached into 60 per cent of the space. The counsel of the municipality admitted that over 50 per cent of park's area is occupied.The bench appointed advocate Partha Sarathi Dev Burman to look into the situation and file a report within one week.

Heading: Mohun Bagan rule - Indian Express
Content:
In the middle of her two-week long tour of Kolkata, 21-year-old Tsatan Dolma, a resident of Ladakh, is already bedazzled by the city. She thanks God for getting an opportunity to marvel those wonders of science which till now she had been watching in the tube.

Dolma is part of the 30-member team — 27 students and three teachers — that has come down to the city from the remote areas of Ladakh.

The visit, which is a part of Indian Army's Sadbhavana project, aims to integrate these women living in remote part of the country into the mainstream.

The visit has also given them an opportunity to get a first hand account of a life in metro and the varieties of cultures and languages that are integral to the India's diversity.

"It is a whole new experience for me, something that is very different from our everyday life," said Dolma. She and her friends learn making different crafts at Women Empowerment Centre in Nimu in Ladakh run by the army. Dolma who loved her trip to Science City plans to return again in near future.

The team visited places like Eden Gardens, Fort William, Victoria Memorial, Dakhineshwar, Belur Math and National Museum among other places. The tour got underway at Karu, 40 kms from Leh, on September 1 and will conclude on September 17. While the elders admired the science projects at Birla Planetarium and Science City, the young souls had a rollicking time at Nicco Park.

"I loved the city. Three of us came with our students and we were taken to various places and had a memorable experience," said Yangchan Dolma, the teacher at the empowerment centre.The empowerment centre in Ladakh teaches the girls computers, knitting, carpet weaving and shawl making, apart from other socially relevant occupations. "We roamed around the city and saw things and places that till now we had only seen on television," said Karshi Aang (25).

Besides seeping in the Bengali culture and heritage, some like teenagers Sonam Yangzin and Padma Yangdol left a memoir of their culture as they performed traditional dance of Zankar clad in colourful Kos traditional dress.

"The armed forces have been doing a stupendous work under Sadhbavna project for the benefit of the people of Ladakh region. The aim of this tour is to provide an insight into the cultural heritage of the city and expose them to the metro life beyond the Himalayan range," said Group Captain RK Das.

Heading: Shame! - Indian Express
Content:
The green-and-maroon clinch Premier Division title after a draw against their arch-rivals at YBK

Ahead of this tie, Mohun Bagan lost a battle in the IFA against the combined force of East Bengal and Mohammedan Sporting. Today, they won the Calcutta Football League (CFL) Premier Division title.

A team with the likes of Baichung Bhutia, Jose Barreto in their ranks and wily Karim Bencherifa on the bench, are too professional to be distracted by any off-the-field incidents. Against their arch-rivals at Yuba Bharati Krirangan (YBK), they proved that they were too tough a nut to crack despite the fact that injuries and suspension forced them to field a second-string XI.

Peter Odafe, Habibur Rahaman Mondal, Dipak Mondal have been nursing injuries and were ruled out of this match. Isfaq Ahmed was out suspended. Bhutia made a very brief appearance. Still, Bagan finished as the better side in a 1-1 draw. The result, however, was enough to give them back-to-back CFL titles.

A win definitely would have been an icing on the cake and it looked like that they were on course till an Edmilson Maques blinder — a 25-yard free-kick — in the 83rd minute restored parity. Earlier, Bagan took the lead in the 25th minute through a Jose Barreto penalty.

The draw took the green-and-maroon to 31 points from 14 matches, insurmountable by any other team in the CFL. Md Sporting, who were Bagan's nearest rival, can reach 30 for maximum if they win their last match against Chirag United tomorrow.

The Bagan fans, who already had a celebration after the match against George Telegraph, wanted seven in a row against East Bengal at YBK. They were a tad disappointed. Some of them unnecessarily got involved in a scuffle with the East Bengal crowd after the match.

Temper flew on the ground as well with seven players receiving yellow. East Begal's Rahim Nabi had to leave the field as S James Singh's tackle landed on his jaw. James escaped marching orders. Referee Mrinanshu Bhattacharya erred on occasions.

Bagan took the lead as East Bengal centreback Nirmal Chhetri made hash of a simple clearance. He had all the time in the world but deposited the ball to Barreto. The latter sent a through pass to Shylo Malaswamtlunga who cut inside the 18-yard box and was tripped by Chhetri. Berreto didn't miss from the sport. Strangely, East Bengal went into a shell after conceding the goal.

For first 15 minutes, they had the better of the exchanges with Asim Biswas playing well upfront. But with no proper midfield functioning, their attacks gradually became too predictable. They tried to make inroads with high crosses from the flanks. Bagan central defenders, tall and lanky Anand Vasan and NS Manju were only too comfortable against that style of play.

East Bengal's first and only chance came in the 28th minute when an unmarked Nabi couldn't convert an Alvito D'Cunha free-kick from close range. The header went wide.

Bagan, on the other hand, had better goal-scoring opportunities. Barreto should have doubled the lead in the 62nd minute.

Eight years ago, Bagan and East Bengal had met in the last match of the National League with the former having already won the title. The then East Bengal coach Subhas Bhowmick was able to motivate his players who played for pride and won 3-1. This East Bengal side seemed to have little stomach for fight.

Heading: Baichung, Karim hail youth brigade - Indian Express
Content:
Things are getting more risky and hazardous by day when Mohun Bagan are involved in a football match. Blame it on a section of Bagan fans who are pushing their limit too far, both in victory and defeat.

Today after the derby, they allegedly roughed up two East Bengal players, Edmilson Marques and Mehtab Hossain. The players were returning on a bike from the Yuba Bharati Krirangan. They were booed and taunted by some Bagan supporters who were on a matador. There was an altercation and reportedly a fight on the EM Bypass near Ruby Hospital. Supporters, who outnumbered the East Bengal duo, allegedly manhandled the latter. Dipankar Roy, who was also there, rescued his team-mates.

"We will hear from the players about the whole incident tomorrow morning and will decide our future course of action," East Bengal official Debabrata Sarkar told The Indian Express.

Earlier, Chirag United coach Subrata Bhattacharya was at the receiving end as irate fans turned the heat on him after their CFL match a few weeks ago.

Then, after the match against George Telegraph last Tuesday, Bagan fans gate-crashed into the club ground to celebrate, putting the players in a real spot of bother.

Meanwhile, East Bengal have set sights on India team assistant coach Stanley Rozario as Manoranjan Bhattacharya's replacement. The latter has all but taken a final decision to quit the job. Sarkar, however, said that they would consider an alternative only after Bhattacharya put in his papers.

Heading: Saturday reviews - Indian Express
Content:
For any Indian youngster, who worth his salt as a footballer, words of encouragement from iconic Baichung Bhutia is like a dream come true. The Lalawmpuias, the Masihs must consider themselves lucky as they have the opportunity to share the dressing room with their hero.

Today, after Mohun Bagan won the CFL Premier Division title, Bhutia lavished praise on the juniors saying they deserved all the accolades.

"I couldn't take part in the CFL because of my India engagements and then due to injury. But that didn't matter. I'm very happy to see a bunch of juniors who played quality football and handled the pressure very well. They have guided us to this title," Bhutia said.

"Lalawmpuia, Rakesh Masih, Mohonraj, S James Singh — all are very talented. I'm confident that they would prove their mettle in the I-League as well." Mohun

Bagan coach Karim Bencherifa concurs. He also thanked the club officials after winning his maiden title in Kolkata.

"The key factor to this title is the team spirit. Throughout this grueling tournament we had an excellent team spirit that did the trick," he said after the match.

The Bagan coach chose Mohammedan Sporting, George Telegraph and Chirag United as their "toughest opponents". According to him, the late goal that ensured a draw against Md Sporting in the second-leg was the turning point.

As far as Bagan's chances in the I-League is concerned, Bencherifa said: "I must say that this league by no means was an easier tournament. Now that the boys have gone through the rigours of the CFL and have succeeded, they should play better in the I-League."

East Bengal coach Manoranjan Bhattacharya, on the other hand, seemed to have made up his mind to quit. "I have already expressed my unwillingness to the club. I will take the final decision by Sunday," he said.

Heading: ‘New state industrial policy by June 2009’ - Indian Express
Content:
A Measure for Treasure
Film: The Last Lear
Director: Rituparno Ghosh
Cast: Amitabh Bachchan, Priety Zinta, Arjun Rampal, Shefali Shah, Divya Dutta, Jisshu Sengupta
Rating: ******
Running at: Inox (Forum, City Centre)
Where have I been? Where am I? Fair daylight? I am mightily abused. I should e'en die with pity, to see another thus. I know not what to say. King Lear.

As his rich, stentorian voice envelops you, you can't help but wonder—wasn't this role just waiting to happen to him? Evidently, Amitabh Bachchan was meant to recite Shakespeare, as much as other Shakespearean greats like Sir Lawrence Olivier or Richard Burton. As he erupts on the screen after a good 20 minutes into the film, you realise that like Harry, the character he plays in the film, Bachchan too is driven by hunger. A hunger which drives him to sink his teeth deep into the skin of the character and draw blood. The analogy may seem a bit too grisly, but there is no other way to describe his performance. It's almost carnal.

Ironically, that is the film's undoing. So overwhelming is Bachchan's powerhouse performance, that everything else, including the nuances of the women members of the cast, seem to be lost under its formidable shadow.

The film is a complex interplay of present moments and flashbacks, which proceeds in a languorous pace like quirky old storyteller prone to bouts of reverie. If you are the kind to get swept away by the sheer brilliance of Shakespeare's verse recitation, and be allured with the quirks of an old, creative man, The Last Lear can be an enjoyable, inspirational journey. But if you are expecting a taut narrative (Shubho Mahurat) or layered performances (Bariwali), you are most likely to be disappointed.

Harry (Bachchan) is a renowned Shakespearean theater actor who is coaxed out of a self-imposed hibernation by a young filmmaker Siddharth, (Rampal), to act in his new film about a disfigured clown. As they begin shooting the film, their ideologies clash, but Harry slowly starts believing in Siddharth's vision and seeks creative refuge in coaching the emotionally disturbed, model-turned-actress, Shabnam ( a restrained Priety Zinta), the finer tricks of the trade. Eventually, his dedication to his craft, proves to be his undoing.

The bracing interplay between Bachchan's old lion and Rampal's savvy young prodigy is pure cinema. Also engaging are the conversations between Shabnam and Vandana (Shefali Shah), Harry's live-in girlfriend. Shah as Vandana, is a revelation. Initially, she spews spite at Shabnam, who comes down to visit her ailing mentor. But as she slowly warms up to the person she so hated, she reveals a vulnerable, sad woman who has lost everything she loved.

The Last Lear is not the fastest-paced film in the world, nor the most stirring. It is, however, the most complete portrait of what it means to be an actor that I've seen in a long time. Which is why Rituparno Ghosh should take a bow. Sometimes it's more important to focus on what they're trying to say, than how it is said. Looking at it that way, this film is an astonishing success.

Here We Go Again!
Film: Mama Mia!
Director: Phyllida Lloyd
Cast: Meryl Streep, Pierce Brosnan, Colin Firth, Stellan Skarsgard and Amanda Seyfried
Rating: *******
Running at: Inox, New Empire
So I was born a generation too late to have listened to ABBA on the radio, and my mother probably can sing their songs better than me, but frankly that did not stop me from singing aloud every time an ABBA song was played on screen. You will tap your feet, sing loudly and cry because that is what musicals are supposed to do to you. And Mama Mia! does that very well. It's mindless, quirky, heartwarming and for hours you will be completely entertained by Meryl Streep and her gang.

The on-screen adaptation of the hit West End musical of the same name has Streep playing Donna, a single mom living on a Greek island, whose 20-year old daughter Sheridan (Amanda Seyfried) is about to get married. Determined to find out who her father is, she sends out letters inviting the three men her mother had been with some 20 summers ago. The three, Sam (Pierce Brosnan), Harry (Colin Firth) and Bill (Stellan Skarsgard) have no clue of her existence and Sheridan has only a day to find out the identity of her father. Right from the first scene that starts of with Sheridan posting letters to her potential dads by singing 'I have a dream' till the last credit where she sings 'Thank you for the music', it's a trip down all those years ago, when lyrics were simple and spoke about dreams and hopes.

And set in a Greek island, the film might not have much of a story line, but then do musicals really need that? Not when they have some of the most popular hits making up for the plot. When Donna is sad and her friends try to cheer her up they do not use words, they use lyrics — they sing Chiquitita. When Donna decides to entertain guests at her daughter's 'hen party' (as opposed to the bachelors' party) she sings Super Trouper, in the tight shiny suit totally popularised by the original troupe.

But if these are still not reason enough to buy a ticket, then watch it only for Meryl Streep. She sings, dances, cries with abandon and makes a fool of herself while throatily belting out the songs — all done in pair of ill-fitting dungarees and old sneakers. If you think she's one of the finest actors in her generation, you cannot miss out on her dance moves, she and her on-screen friends (played by Julie Walters and Christine Baranski) can certainly teach a thing or two about shaking their booties to the young. They move and how! Frankly you do not even notice the men, it's women power all the way in this film.

Watch the film and you will want to go to the music store and pick up ABBA's greatest hits once again. But watch it quickly, judging by the empty halls, this one's not here for long unfortunately.

PS: For those die-hard ABBA fans a special cameo by Benny Anderson and Bjorn Ulvaeus might be your only chance to see them on-screen after so many years.

Spooksvilla
Film: 1920
Director: Vikram Bhatt
Cast: Rajneesh Duggal, Adah Sharma, Anjorie Alagh, Raj Zutshi
Rating: ****
Running at: Inox (Forum, City Centre)
If a cloyingly sweet girl noisily feasting on a dead cat, is not exactly your recipe for thrills, then 1920 might not be the movie for you. Because the movie treads along the border of usual Bollywood scare fare, tottering between the eerie and the snatches of the outright macabre. Very predictably it goes overboard with the howls and groans of the evil spirit. Something that might be mildly unsettling.

But what Vikram Bhatt's film achieves amid the crowd of Bollywood cliches, is pace. So before 1920 dwindles into a celebration of the Hanuman chalisa or an Ekta Kapoor-goes-spooky revenge drama, Bhatt winds up his film leaving you just a little short of breath.

Arjun Singh Rathod (Rajneesh Duggal) goes against his family to marry Lisa (Adah Sharma). To escape the hatred, the once devout Hindu, leaves home for Mumbai and also denounces God and religion. Soon, Arjun's architecture firm sends him to a small hill station where a very old house has to be broken down to make way for a hotel. A house, that unknown to Arjun, has a history of getting back at anyone who has tried to pull it down.

It is imperative that ghosts from Bollyland live in sprawling beautiful houses and have a predilection for hill stations. Seems like director Vikram Bhatt shares their fascination because the setting, except for the difference of a century, is almost identical to Raaz. There are the usual close-ups of lost-very scared faces in deserted half-lit halls, wooden staircases, and a pining heroine whose eyes go yellow with evil effect every now and then. There's also the selfless parish priest and an inquisitive servant, like the legion of Bollywood spook flicks, but Bhatt's taut narrative prevents them to becoming too obvious till the very end of the film.

Adah Sharma has a lot to do with the watch-ability of the film. When she is not making you go all mushy with her sugary sweetness perfectly complemented with a neat set of typically Brit skirt ensembles, she brings evil alive on screen. For a change her eyes speak more than all the red paint on her face and she has more expressions that the -don't-you-dare-come-closer look that most Bollywood ghosts are stuck with. Rajneesh Duggal is tolerable but sure has to work on scenes, which demand angst off his face.

Heading: Two held for taxi driver’s murder - Indian Express
Content:
The state's industrial policy will be declared by June 2009, said S S Channy, Principal Secretary of the Commerce and Industry Department in Ludhiana on Friday. He added that suggestions of various industrialists will be accommodated while framing the policy.

Channy was in the city to attend a seminar on water conservation, jointly organised by the Commerce and Industry Department, Punjab Pollution Control Board (PPCB) and Punjab State Council for Science and Technology, at the Punjab Trade Centre.

He said small industries operating from residential colonies will be shifted to a new location. Sources said the new policy will allow funds to industrialists to maintain the focal points.

Channy added that the policy would stress the zero-liquid discharge norm wherein industrialists have to recycle effluents within the unit rather than flushing it out into the sewers.

"Ludhiana has contributed immensely in polluting the Buddha Nallah, which was clean a few years ago. Now, the industry should join hands to bring the waterbody to its pristine look once again," he added.

Joginder Kumar, president of the Ludhiana Electroplaters' Association, also spoke on the occasion. Inderjit Singh Pardhan, president of the Small Scale Industry Board, Satish Dhanda, vice-chairman of Medium Scale Industry, T R Mishra, Ajit Singh Kular and Malwinder Singh from the PPCB were also present at the seminar.

Heading: Dengue cases rise to 14 in city - Indian Express
Content:
Two persons were arrested by the Ludhiana police today for their alleged involvement in the murder of taxi driver Kamaljit Singh, alias Sonu, on September 5.

Kamaljit Singh was allegedly shot dead by Suraj Ahluwalia, president of Shiv Sena (Bal Thackerey) students' wing, at Neelkanth taxi stand in Upkar Nagar.

The arrested have been identified as Gurprem Singh, Ahluwalia's gunman, and Happy, a worker at the taxi stand.

Station House Officer of Division Number 8 police station, Ravinder Singh, said the accused surrendered late on Thursday evening.

"They were produced at a local court today and have been remanded in police custody till September 15," he added.

The deceased's family and a few local councillors, meanwhile, met Senior Superintendent of Police R K Jaiswal and Superintendent of Police (Detective) Gurpreet Singh Toor.

They demanded the arrest of the others accused in the case, including prime accused Suraj Ahluwalia. The senior police officers assured them of immediate action.

"We have formed special teams, comprising Crime Investigation Agency and Division Number 8 police personnel, to trace the absconding men," said SP Toor.

Heading: Heroin by courier: DRI questions detainees - Indian Express
Content:
The number of dengue cases in the city went up to 14 today, with the Health Department confirming another case.

District Health Officer Dr S S Dhir said there are nearly 70 suspected cases of the disease.

Various city hospitals have admitted about 11 fresh patients, the preliminary reports and clinical tests of whom, have suggested dengue fever.

Four suspected cases, two of whom belong to Ludhiana, were admitted in Dayanand Medical College and Hospital today.

So far, Dayanand Medical College and Hospital has admitted 105 patients suspected of dengue. Of them, 50 are from Ludhiana while the rest hail from other districts of Punjab.

SPS Apollo Hospital has also admitted five suspected cases, three of whom are residents of the district. Shri Rama Charitable Hospital in Dholewal has also registered two more cases of the suspected disease.

The Health Department, meanwhile, started an awareness campaign in the city to inform the residents about guarding against mosquito bites.

A team of the department, led by District Health Officer Dr S S Dhir, conducted checks at various houses today and helped clean up about 200 coolers while asking residents to regularly change the water in coolers.

Heading: 30-bed unit soon for burn victims at civil hospital - Indian Express
Content:
Four persons, detained by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) for their suspected involvement in drug smuggling, were questioned about Thursday's heroin seizure. No one, however, has been arrested yet.

Sources said the accused were workers of an Amritsar-based firm which published religious books.

Raids were also conducted in Amritsar and Ludhiana to trace the suppliers of the drug.

Directorate of Revenue Intelligence Joint Director, Dheeraj Rastogi, said the smugglers will be arrested soon.

On Thursday, 48 packets of heroin (hidden in Canada-bound courier packets containing religious material including VCDs, DVDs and religious books) were seized by the DRI from a van near the Jalandhar bypass.

Each packet contained 100 grams of the drug. The value of the seized heroin (4.8 kg) is estimated to be over Rs 6 crore in the international market.

Heading: Residential Bridge Course in offing for special children - Indian Express
Content:
The unit will be set up with a grant of Rs 1 crore under the National Rural Health Mission

Now, burn victims will not have to suffer for want of better infrastructure at the Ludhiana Civil Hospital.

The hospital will soon be equipped with a 30-bed burns unit housed in a separate building, said Deputy Medical Commissioner Dr Y P Mehta.

The unit will be set up with a grant of Rs 1 crore under the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM).

"A burns unit with increased capacity and better infrastructure was always required at the civil hospital, given the kind of fire accidents the city has faced in the past," said Mehta.

The decision assumes significance as Ludhiana is an industrial hub and faces frequent fire accidents.

Also, several areas of the city are prone to fire outbreaks owing to congested markets and illegal firecracker manufacturing units.

"The new burns unit will be a boon for poor patients as they cannot afford the expensive treatment at private hospitals," said a resident.

Heading: ‘Soil health angle should be factored in while introducing new crops in state’ - Indian Express
Content:
After drawing flak for the proposal for Non-Residential Bridge Course for special children of rural areas, now the State Education Department is going to start Residential Bridge Course (RBC) for them. Under this, the school drop-out special children, including mentally retarded suffering from multiple-disability, hearing impairment etc will be taught free of in this one-year course.

Anil Sharma, District Coordinator of Inclusive Education for Disabled Project of Sarv Shiksha Abhiyan, said, "We will educate 150 special children free-of-cost. Under this project, we will have a proportionate time-table for the mentally retarded children through which they will be taught daily learning activities (DLA)." The hearing impaired will be taught through sign language. We have 19 special teachers in all the educational blocks of Ludhiana district. They will help us in teaching these children in RBC, while the other staff will be deputed for assisting them.

For this course, school drop-outs from the age of 6 to 14 years will be admitted. The grant of Rs 10,000 per child per annum will be released for running this course by SSA. "We will start this course in a rented accommodation in an area where such children will be more," said Anil.

Anil said, "From tomorrow, the assessment camps for special children are being held at different places. Under this, we will come across children with physical disability. And with the consent of parents, we will enroll these children for this course. And as soon as we get the grant, we will start this course."

It needs to be mentioned here that about two years ago, a project was prepared by Sarv Shiksha Abhiyan to open a non-residential school in Lehra village of Ludhiana district. But it was not approved by the Central government as it was a non-residential school project and the government was to approved residential school. So after a span of two years now, this project has been prepared and grant is being awaited.

Heading: PAU Kisan Club,  planning team discuss issues - Indian Express
Content:
The Ludhiana chapter of Indian Society of Soil Science organised a lecture on "Relationship between potassium nutrition and plant protection" by Dr M. Assaraf of the International Potash Institute (IPI), Horgen, Switzerland.
