The 16-member GSEDS headed by the CM and having seven ministers and as many secretaries on it will also meet shortly to expedite the process of availing funds from the government companies — both listed and unlisted.

Heading: Blanket ban on doctors’ private practice - Indian Express
Content:
Country's politics needs more young blood, says former prez

One out of 60 students at the IIM-A replied in the affirmative when Dr APJ Abdul Kalam, the former President of India, asked them if they would like to join politics. Kalam was present on the IIM-A campus to deliver a lecture to the students of 'Globalising Resurgent India Through Innovative Transformation' (GRIT) course that has been introduced by Prof Anil Gupta of the institute in tune with Kalam's Vision-2020.

Around 70 students of second year post graduate programme, post graduate programme for executives, post graduate programme-agri-business management and the fellowship programme have been selected for the course, which will have 20 lectures, of which, nearly half would be delivered by Kalam himself.

The Saturday lecture was an interactive session with the students where they discussed their project topics. Kalam's energetic talk enthused the students. He tried motivating the students to have an optimistic view of India and narrated incidents of his life to explain his point. It was his wit that lifted the spirits of students, many of whom were nervous about his lecture.

The students were given 10 project topics, which were actually the ten pillars of the 2020 strategy visualised by Kalam — transparent governance, policies, synthesis of agriculture, industry and service sectors, education without reservation, healthcare facilities and a nation free of terrorism. The students will also be given the opportunity to interact with the parliamentary committees and the ministers on specific policies.

Kalam also gave a presentation on each of the pillars and discussed issues at length.

"It being a project-based course, Kalam has encouraged a good interaction with us through e-mails. When he is working so hard to groom us, we also want to support him to achieve his vision of 2020," says Saurabh Basantani, second year postgraduate programme student.

When asked about terrorism, Kalam said that in order to counter terrorism, one needs to make people their partners. He further added that the governments in India should create a unified intelligence agency, make the laws stringent and justice quicker. As a mandatory practice, every citizen should have a National Citizen Identification Card.

Kalam also appreciated the Indo-US nuclear deal, saying that the availability of uranium was a major concern for the nation. He appealed to all the uranium-rich states to open their doors for the country. Besides, he pointed out that scientists were developing thorium reactors for the future, but till then, India needs uranium, which will be facilitated by this treaty.

Kalam encouraged the youth of the nation to understand the importance of young blood in politics. According to him, the youngsters can generate good opinion and add their valuable contribution in shaping national policies. He also said that education in our country should focus on employment and not on academic records. Opportunities of employment have to be generated to encourage Indian students to study in India.

"I was teaching in Anna University in 2002 when I got a call from Delhi (for Presidentship). But I am ready to teach again as I love teaching," said Kalam candidly.

Kalam will visit IIM-A again on October 25 and November 26-27 of this year to continue his lecture series on GRIT.

Heading: GU yet to provide enrolment forms to its colleges - Indian Express
Content:
Non-Practising Allowance made mandatory for all medicos irrespective of seniority

The ongoing unrest among the government doctors in the state has finally come to an end, with the government putting a blanket ban on private practice and announcing mandatory Non Practising Allowance (NPA) for all doctors irrespective of length of service, in a resolution passed on Friday.

The 8,000-odd government doctors said the move was in greater public interest, especially for the people living in rural areas and smaller towns.

The decision proves to be a major setback to the state government, which was keen to oblige senior doctors, having more than 15 years of service, by giving them an option between NPA and private practice. It is also a blow to doctors who have been doing their government jobs unwillingly and pursuing private practice secretly by distributing visiting cards of their private clinics to the patients who come to government hospitals.

However, a large number of government doctors, especially in remote areas, are in a helpless situation, as they will neither get NPA nor do they have any private practice.

The government had cancelled the NPA in November 2006 and allowed all doctors to practice privately. As a result, a series of petitions were filed, which led to a stay order by the High Court in December, 2006. Later, the Heath Department passed a resolution, declaring that only doctors with over 15 years of service are eligible for NPA. The petitioners again challenged the decision and thus the High Court ordered the cancellation of the resolution. Since then, the petitioners had been demanding a government resolution for the continuation of NPA.

Indian Medical Association's Gujarat Branch has welcomed the latest move. Its honorary general secretary, Dr Bipin Patel, said that this will ensure better medical services and induce doctors to stay on in government service.

He said this will also reduce the degree of distraction among doctors, who would be able to pay undivided attention to patients being fully aware of the fact that they do not have a consulting room to go to and treat patients.

Dr Shailendra Vora, president of ESIC Class II Doctors Association, said: "The old policy of allowing doctors to practice privately was full of flaws and was the principal reason behind the long queues outside operation theatres of government hospitals."

Heading: Schemes for tribal welfare bearing fruit, but it could have been better - Indian Express
Content:
Around two lakh first-year undergrads yet to become bonafide students of the university

The first year under- graduate (UG) students who took admission in the colleges affiliated to the Gujarat University (GU) for the academic year 2008-2009, are yet to become bonafide students of the university. Thanks to GU's laidback attitude, none of the colleges have received enrolment forms from students till now.

Around two lakh first year UG students have taken admission in GU this year. Every year, the last date of acceptance for enrolment forms is July 31. If a student is unable to submit the form by July 31, he or she can submit it by August 10 with a fine of Rs 20, by August 21 with a fine of Rs 2,000 and latest by September 7 with a fine of Rs 5,000.

The principal of one of the most reputed Arts colleges in the city said on condition of anonymity: "I have sent clerks of my college to the GU office several times to enquire about the enrolment forms. But every time varsity authorities tell them to contact Vice Chancellor (V-C) Parimal Trivedi with the enquiry. A clerk cannot possibly go and meet the V-C to ask about the enrolment forms."

Asked about the issue, GU Registrar Minesh Shah told Newsline: "We have already informed all the colleges about the delay in the printing of enrolment forms. They will get the forms by Monday."

The colleges, however, say that they were not informed about the delay in the enrolment forms. The principal of a Commerce college said: "Every time a student or any college gets late in submitting the form, GU charges a fine. None of the first year UG students can be called legal students till the submission of the enrolment forms. There will be a definite delay in the registration, as well as the annual examination process of GU."

Heading: Kin of youth killed in police firing get compensation after three years - Indian Express
Content:
TRTI's impact assessment says subsidies insufficient, land ownership records not updated

The Tribal Research and Training Institute (TRTI) at Gujarat Vidyapith in Ahmedabad has submitted a detailed impact assessment report to the Tribal Development Department, Gujarat government, after analysing the performance of the 'Development of Forest Settlements' (DFS) scheme being implemented in all the 199 forest villages in Gujarat.

As per the scheme, the Union Ministry of Tribal Affairs issues grants as Special Central Assistance (SCA) under the Tribal Sub Plan to respective state governments. These grants are further transferred to the Forest Development Agencies (FDA) for the implementation of various welfare schemes in the forest villages.

The scheme was approved by the Union Ministry of Environment and Forests in January 2005, under section 2 of the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980, allowing diversion of forest lands for providing the basic and essential development facilities to the tribal/forest villages.

The report prepared by three researchers of TRTI, Arun Patel, Chandrakant Patel and Ravindra Pancholi, has looked at the implications, benefits and loopholes in the scheme. According to their report, since 2005, FDAs in Gujarat have received around Rs 28 crore as SCA to be used in 72 development schemes in both community development and individual welfare programmes.

While explaining the welfare programmes, Pancholi said: "At the community level, wells, check dams and metal roads have been built. Fencing of villages is also underway at some places. As far as individual welfare programmes are concerned, housing, bank loans and Sarv Rog Nidan Camp to improve health care in forest villages have been undertaken. The seeds, fertilisers and equipments to increase the agricultural produce have also been supplied."

Patel said: "In some areas, the Forest Department has allowed the tribals to use minor forest produce such as Timroo, Gond and Bili Patra for commercial purposes. We also found that in some villages, pipelines have been laid to supply water for irrigation purposes."

Apart from the plus points, the report has highlighted some loopholes in the scheme too. The biggest problem, according to TRTI, is of insufficient subsidies. Pancholi said: "While the subsidy for a cow is Rs 7,000, it is Rs 8,000 for a buffalo. However, the market price of these animals is around Rs 15,000. This shows that the whole subsidy scheme is irrelevant."

Another major loophole in the scheme is that there has been no 'versaii' in these villages. This essentially means that the ownership of land in forest villages has not been transferred across generations. Patel explained: "For example, if the old land record enlists only 100 residents of a village, the grant for welfare schemes come for only 100 people, despite the fact that the population of the village may have reached 1,000. This makes the grants extremely insufficient for the villagers."

Heading: NRI conman runs out of luck, arrested from city - Indian Express
Content:
The Gujarat High Court, on Friday, ordered a compensation of Rs 50,000 to be paid to the relatives of Saiyed Irfan who died in police firing during the Ganapati procession in Wadi Mohalla of Vadodara in September 2005.

A Division Bench comprising Chief Justice K S Radhakrishnan and Justice Mohit S Shah asked the state government to pay the compensation within a period of one month.

Earlier, a single-judge court had rejected the plea for compensation on the ground that the 21-year-old youth shot dead by the police was an accused.

However, this time, the two-judge bench considered the compensation claim on the ground that police had no evidence to prove that the youth was an accused.

Saiyed, according to his family members, had gone to procure medicines for his ailing 75-year-old grandfather when clashes broke out between members of the two communities during the passage of the Ganapati procession. Saiyed was shot in the head when the police resorted to firing to disperse the riotous mobs. He had died on the spot.

His father had expired a few months before the incident.

Heading: Miscreants strike at Gaekwad’s Laxmi Vilas palace - Indian Express
Content:
Niranjan Patel, accused of duping 154 people in US, nabbed following a Red Corner notice

A man, accused of cheating at least 154 people in the United States, was arrested by the Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) on Friday evening after the Interpol issued a 'Red Corner' notice against him. The accused, Niranjan Patel, will be extradited and tried in a US court, police said.

According to DCB police inspector, R B Dawda, there are about 37 cases pending against Patel. He is accused of cheating nearly 154 US citizens by promising them jobs in other countries and taking money for VISA procedure.

Senior police officials said that Patel was nabbed from Ashapura society in Akota area of the city and is now in judicial custody.

"Extradition is a long drawn procedure and might take some time," said Joint Commissioner of Police, Praveen Sinha.

Vadodara police commissioner Rakesh Asthana said that no officials from US Federal Bureau of Investigation had come to arrest Patel.

"We acted on the letters sent to the DIG-CID (Crime) by Interpol, which in turn directed the DCP Vadodara to arrest the accused," said Dawda.

Patel, who was arrested from his residence, has been staying in Vadodara for about six months now, according to the police. The Interpol will extradite Patel to try him in the US courts for his pending cases.

Heading: Leptospirosis cases on the rise, three more dead - Indian Express
Content:
Ganesh pandal was raided too, say cops; no formal complaint from the royal family

Robbers took away valuable articles from the famous Laxmi Vilas Palace, built by Maharaja Sayajirao Gaekwad III, on Saturday. The Raopura police said that no formal complaint regarding the theft has been lodged till now. The royal family has not confirmed the theft so far.

According to police officials, the thieves also broke into the Ganesh Chaturthi pandal inside the palace premises.

Following the incident, security guards of the palace barred devotees from entering the pandal. A minor scuffle also broke out between the security guards of the palace and the visitors who wanted to see the pandal.

Additional police security was called in to prevent outsiders from entering the pandal. Police said that the area was sealed off because some articles were stolen from the pandal as well.

Heading: All India NCC Trekking Camp 2008 begins in Dangs - Indian Express
Content:
Doctors at the New Civil Hospital (NCH) announced three more deaths of farm labourers undergoing treatment for Leptospirosis on Friday evening. A total of 83 people have already fallen victim to this deadly disease in the current rainy season.

The dead have been identified as Champa Patel (45), a resident of Ranpada village in Dharampur taluka; Raju Rathod (39), a resident of Varad village in Bardoli taluka; and Parvati Vasawa (55), a resident of Wadi village in Mangrol taluka.

On Friday, eleven more such patients were admitted to the NCH. They were referred from Bardoli and Navsari Community Health Care Centres.

The disease is mostly seen among farm labourers of south Gujarat who regularly work in the fields. Every year, more and more villages in the region suffer from the menace created by the Leptospira bacteria.

The first case of Leptospirosis was recorded in Valsad district in 1994. The disease later spread to the neighbouring districts of Navsari and Surat. The mortality rate in Navsari is comparatively higher than Surat and Valsad.

Sources at the Department of Preventive and Social Medicine, NCH said that in the last 14 years, a total of 750 labourers have died because of Leptospirosis.

The Health Department officials have been trying to bring down the mortality rate apart from spreading awareness about precautions.

It has been found that people affected by Leptospirosis are mostly farm labourers and care-takers of cattle.

Dr. Naresh Godara, Assistant Professor at the Preventive and Social Medicine, NCH said, "We are trying our level best to control the disease for which we have distributed free tablets to farm labourers in different villages. We have also asked them to consume the medicines every weekend. We have also opened two new centres at the Community Health Care Centre at Bardoli taluka in Surat and at the Civil Hospital in Navsari. We have also instructed them to wear gloves and shoes while working in the fields. Children should not be taken to the fields."

Heading: Man killed in Tilakwada for making overtures at live-in partner's daughter - Indian Express
Content:
The All India NCC trekking camp 2008 got under way at Saputara in Dangs district on Saturday.

The NCC Baroda group commander Colonel Rahul Bali flagged off the 20-day camp on Saturday.

The cadets aged between 14 and 18 from different states like Punjab, Haryana, Gujarat, Delhi, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh arrived at Dandkaryawan village near Vaghai in Dangs on Friday.

More than 1,000 cadets are participating in the camp.

Bali said that the cadets will have to trek 131 kilometers starting from Dungarda village in Ahwa taluka to Sakpatar village near Saputara.

"During the camp, the participants will also meet local tribal people and learn about their lifestyles. The

District Administration officials are giving us full support to carry out trekking activities," he said.

Heading: Bihar floods: City docs rush to provide medical aid - Indian Express
Content:
A 32-year-old man, Haresh Tadvi, was brutally murdered by one Usha Tadvi and her children in the wee hours of Saturday. Haresh, a resident of Vyadar village of Tilakwada taluka of Narmada district, had a live-in relationship with Usha for the past eight years.

Tilakwada police officials said that the incident occurred when the deceased reportedly tried to physically exploit Usha's daughter, Heena, 14, in her absence. Later, on Saturday afternoon, Usha, Heena and her son Dixit (16) surrendered before the police and admitted to the crime.

Police Sub Inspector M D Dhawale of Tilakwada police station said, "The incident occurred when Haresh tried to misbehave with Usha's daughter. Haresh and Usha's two-year-old son, Dhruv, also woke up on hearing the commotion. The situation soon turned ugly with Heena and Dixit assaulting Haresh with a baton. He later succumbed to the injuries on his neck, head and stomach."

While Haresh was a labourer, Usha had been married to one Dinesh Mansukh, whom she had left many years ago.

Heading: Exaggerated - Indian Express
Content:
Over 15 ambulances, medicines and other amenities have been sent with the team

Taking into account the requirement of medical expertise for the victims of Kosi flood, the Gujarat government has sent a team of three doctors from Vadodara to attend to the flood affected areas of Bihar. Also, over 15 ambulances, medicines and other amenities have been sent with them.

The team of doctors include Dr Bhagwati Itare, Chief District Health Officer (CDHO), Vadodara, Dr Jeevraj Damor, assistant associate professor of Preventive and Social Medicine at Baroda Medical College and Dr Gulal Katravat, quality assurance, medical officer of district panchayat, Vadodara. The team that was sent on Wednesday will be deputed in Bihar for 15 days till further notice. "We are fully ready with a team of hundred doctors and all other medical amenities. We are dispatching the medical aid as per the Bihar Government's requirement," said Gujarat Health Commissioner Amarjit Singh.

Heading: Dull dudes - Indian Express
Content:
Randeep Hooda and Shahana Goswami are a live-in couple in Ru Ba Ru

Movie name:Ru Ba Ru
Cast:Randeep Hooda, Shahana Goswami
Directed by:Arjun Bali
Showing at:Gold Adlabs, City Pride( Kothrud), City Pride (Satara Road), Mangala

Bangkok-based adman Nikhil (Randeep Hooda) behaves boorishly with loving live-in girl-friend Tara (Shahana Goswami). He forgets everything: Dates, special moments, even the fact that that evening is the play she has been working towards for the past two years. All through the performance, for which he arrives late, he's thinking of dinner with his clients, not with her. It ends badly. She gets into a taxi angrily, and goes off. And then something happens, which changes everything.

We can't reveal anything more. What we can tell you is that this is another of those could-have-been films. Everything is overstated; nothing is left to the imagination. Randeep as repentant lover boy does what he can, but the real victim of Ru Ba Ru is Shahana, who sparkled in her last outing, Rock On!!. She is made to address Randeep as Baybee and underline all emotions.

Heading: After joint military exercise, IAF team returns from US - Indian Express
Content:
Movie name:Righteous Kill
Cast:Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Carla Gugino, John Leguizamo
Directed by:Jon Avnet
Showing at:Gold Adlabs

Most people respect the badge. Everybody respects the gun. Obviously Righteous Kill prides itself on that tagline, seeing the way it has been playing over and over in promotions and features twice at least in the film.

However, there is another thing truer: most people respect Robert De Niro and Al Pacino, but everybody respects a good story. And sorry to say, despite all the promise of and wait for these two movie titans together, Jon Avnet's Righteous Kill has nothing new to offer. It even casts them as — guess what — police officers not averse to crossing the line.

For the most part the film just drags, hiding behind vague explanations when the going gets tough and dragging on the climax far after almost everyone in the audience has guessed it.

As for the tagline, it was Jack Nicholson - and moral dubiousness is his middle name — who said it best in The Departed: "You can become a cop or a criminal. But when you're facing a loaded gun, what's the difference?"

Heading: 'Start construction soon or face consequence' - Indian Express
Content:
The multi-lateral joint exercise of the Indian Air Force in the United States along with the air forces of United States, Korea and France recently came to an end with the Indian contingent receiving praise from the United States Air Force for their meticulous performance.

In a first of its kind event, non-NATO pact nations had been invited to participate in the prestigious Red Flag exercise. The Indian contingent comprised of eight SU-30 MKI aircraft of the Lightening Squadron. It was supported by two IL-78 flight refuelling aircraft and one IL-76 Transport aircraft. The entire contingent was 250 members strong, which included 90 officers, 36 pilots, and other technicians. Over 100 tons of equipment was carted along with the planes to the United States.

Wing Commander George Thomas who was commanding the Lightening Squadron said, "We flew a trans-atlantic flight across, Doha, Turkey, France and then landed at Idaho in the United States. Over the course of sixty days we had over 800 hours of flying. At Red Flag we flew 200 hours in which we flew six sorties in ten flying days, with each sortie variying from 60 minutes to 90 minutes."

Also present on the occasion on Saturday was Air Marshal K.D.Singh, the Air Officer, Commanding-in-Chief of the South Western Air Command.

He said, "this is a first of its kind joint venture between the four nations, the United States and India have participated in an exercise (Indra Dhanush) but that was only a bilateral exercise. The exercise has provided the Indian pilots a hand on hand experience of training in actual simulated test conditions. The exercise has given us a 100 percent efficiency rate." On their way back the pilots also had an exercise with the air force of the UAE at Al-Dafra, making this a first of its kind between the two nations. They landed at the Lohegaon air base on September 13.

Heading: Green development plan: Dharia cries foul - Indian Express
Content:
Guardian minister Ajit Pawar has warned industrialists, who hoard up land, to start construction within a specific time frame or face consequence of their land being taken back. Addressing a meeting of industrialists, at the Mahratta Chamber of Commerce, Industries and Agriculture (MCCIA) on Friday, he was giving a hearing to the industrialists on the shortage of land in the district.

"Strict action should be taken against those who hoard up land for industrial purpose and do not use it for industrial purpose for a long period. A time frame needs to be worked out," said Pawar at the meeting.

With the industrialists mentioning that there was hardly any land remaining in Pune and Mumbai for expansion, Pawar was candid enough to say that new industrialists should look at Supa in Ahmednagar and Khandala in Satara districts. "There was no land remaining in the industrial zones of Kurkumb, Indapur and Baramati in the district," he added.

Pawar said that Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal Ltd (PMPML) should have more buses. The meeting also took up the issues of shifting the garbage depot from Hadapsar and completion of the road from BG Shirke factory to Hadapsar. He however, assured the industrialists that all care would be taken to give the necessary benefits to them.

Heading: Purke visits CYG office - Indian Express
Content:
Reacting to the state government altering green development plan (DP) of Baner-Balewadi, environmentalist and former union minister Mohan Dharia has alleged that there are irregularities worth crores of rupees in turning the reserved land into residential areas in the DP. He urged the chief minister of Maharashtra Vilasrao Deshmukh and Pune guardian minister Ajit Pawar, to look into the matter.

Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) standing committee chairman Shyam Deshpande, environment activist Vandana Chavan along with other activists have opposed state government's stand to lift all the reservations in the DP, without providing any convincing reason. As part of their opposition, all activists and representatives of various non-government organisations (NGO) have come under one roof - 'Green Pune Movement' - and have decided to file a public interest litigation (PIL) in this regard.

Dharia was chairing a meeting of activists on Saturday to oppose the changes in the DP proposed by the state government. He strongly cracked his whip on the state government for not furnishing the maps of the altered DP and for using vague language in the notification. "For instance, some parts of the notification reads as 'survey number 12, 13, 14, 15 etc', where it is left for the reader to understand which other survey numbers are included," he said.

Heading: Indian paddlers do well against Pakistan - Indian Express
Content: State Minister for School Education, Sports and Culture Vasant Purke on Saturday paid a visit to the office of the Commonwealth Youth Games Pune 2008 at ICC Trade Tower on Senapati Bapat Road, after a visit to the Shiv Chhatrapati Sports Complex in Balewadi. The minister reviewed the work for the games as well as all other sporting and non-sporting venues. MP Suresh Kalmadi welcomed Purke and detailed him on the work.

Heading: Glitz and glamour at the Pune Race course - Indian Express
Content:
Soumyajit Ghosh and Meghna Kataria win comfortably, Arnab Adhikari comes back from two games down

Indians from the Cadet Category, Arnab Adhikari and Meghna Kakaria, did well to beat their Pakistani opponents in the Singles tournament of the Bajaj Group Indian Junior Open 2008 ITTF World Junior Circuit Table Tennis tournament held at the Balewadi Sports Complex on Saturday.

Arnab Adhikari showed some real grit when he came back from two games down to win the match 3-2 against Pakistan's Virk Salman . Salman won the first game 11-8 without much difficulty. The second game was fought hard till the end but was edged by Salman again 13-11. Adhikari then pulled up his socks and played with some real determination. He took the next three games 11-3, 11-8 and 11-8 and deservedly won the match.

In a less intense match, India's Meghna Kakaria blanked out Pakistani opponent Ayesha Khan 3-0. Kakaria hardly broke into a sweat before routing her opponent 11-7, 11-6 and 11-6.

Doubles champion Soumyajit Ghosh met some resistance before defeating his Nepalese counterpart S Pravin 3-1. The Indian won the first game with ease dropping only 3 points in the process.

Pravin came back strongly and held his nerve to win the second game 15-13. Soumyajit was not too affected by this as he won the next two games 11-2 and 11-8.

In the Junior category, the Indian boys had a rough day as both Yashwant Aacharya and Noel Pinto lost their matches 3-0 each. Aacharya was comprehensively beaten by the world no 65, Morimoto Kohei of Japan. Kohei was in total control of the match and won it 11-9, 11-8 and 11-1. In the other match, Noel Pinto of India lost to the world no 70 Felipe Olivares of Chile. Pinto was completely outclassed by the Chilean and in the end lost the match 4-11, 7-11 and 2-11.

Heading: Spirited - Indian Express
Content: The Poonawalla million, one of the more popular races in the city circuit, is to to be held this Sunday, The race has been instituted by the RWITC in honour of  Soli A. Poonawalla. The poonawalla Group has guaranteed a whopping stakes of rupees one point five million which includes rupees eight Lakhs added from the RWITC fund. The Poonawalla Group has further contributed Rs. 2,50,000/- towards lavish prizes which will be given away to the winners of the Free Contest of Skill. The onwer of the winning hourse is likely to walk away with a purse of around rupees one millions. Several schools, hospitals and roads are named after him. His grandson  Prakash Kedari was the first Vice President of Pune Cantt. Board and Chairman of Pimpri Chinchwad New Town Development  authority and a Royal follower of the Congress party.
