Heading: Only 15 inspectors for 400 hazardous units - Indian Express
Content:
Movie name:1920Cast:Rajneesh Duggal, Adah Sharma, Raj ZutshiDirected by:Vikram BhattShowing at:Gold Adlabs, City Pride( Kothrud), City Pride (Satara Road), Mangala

It is 1920. Why? Because, first, it lets Vikram Bhatt dress his brand new heroine in flowing dresses, place her in a horse-drawn carriage, and plonk her in the middle of a Victorian mansion with several splendid rooms, curving staircases, a grand piano, and a murderous ghost.

It also lets him bring in a segment of the then recent past: The ghaghra-clad daughter of an 1857 revolutionary snares, with her pretty wiles, a gaddaar. He is strung up, and voila, we have a vengeful ghost.

Sixty years later, the lady in the flowing dresses, Lisa (Adah Sharma) and her devoted architect husband Arjun (Rajneesh Duggal) fetch up in a quiet hill station. His brief is to break down the mansion, and build a hotel. Her intention is to stall him. Something in the huge house is reaching out to her, and telling her to stop.

The first half builds up slowly. Too slowly, despite the creaking doors, flickering lamps, and one bloody killing. The second half is better, because here the spirit comes into its own. Or rather, enters the body of the lady in the flowing dresses, who henceforth is to be seen only in a white nightgown. She also acquires a chalky white face, discoloured teeth, gruff voice, and inhuman strength.

Debutant Adah may not have been much when she is all prettied up under her parasol. But as a possessed creature, she is very effective: full marks to the make-up artists. Co- debutant Rajneesh chants the Hanuman Chalisa with volume enough to send the evil spirit away to the deep. 1920 is not just about possession. It's also got reincarnation, good priests, and bad doctors. And lavish production values.

Post-Raaz, Vikram Bhatt comes into his own, again. 1920 has a very scary ghost ; the only thing scarier is Rakhi Sawant in a bad item number. If only Bhatt hadn't wasted so much time on non-essentials, this one could have been the first really spooky movie of the year.

Heading: Coming soon: Wheelchair rugby meet; PRC to play host - Indian Express
Content:
Collector seeks increase; with no fresh recruitment by Industrial Safety and Health Department since 1989, disasters waiting to happen

Fifteen inspectors to cover 400-odd hazardous units in the district and no fresh recruitments for almost two decades has taken its toll with the Bhosari industrial unit claiming 10 lives on August 27. Now district collector Chandrakant Dalvi has sent a recommendation to the state government recommending an increase in the number of inspectors under the Industrial Safety and Health Department (ISHD).

He has further recommended that the inspectors from the department need to present a detailed report regarding these 400 units in two months time. With the department not having any recruitment since 1989, Dalvi said the department will go in for a survey and present their requirements considering the number of hazardous units in the district. The recent industrial fire at the Bhosari unit has been an eye-opener with the department expressing the shortage of staff to assess these units, he said.

Pune district houses over 5,000 industrial units, of which 400 come under the hazardous category that deal in explosives, chemicals and highly inflammable materials.

"There has been hardly any detailed report on these units and I have recommended these inspectors to go in for a detailed report on these units, on the production and the staff and the safety awareness," he said. These units are spread right across the district, with a heavy concentration in the Pimpri-Chinchwad area. The Bhosari unit that killed 10 women had followed almost no safety measures, Dalvi pointed out.

Also, it was high time the state government had a relook at the three-yearly renewal of license format and instead went in for a yearly one, he said. "There is a need for a thorough inspection of these units as they come under the hazardous category. They should compulsorily be made to renew their licenses every year," he said.

Regarding the 400 units, he said that only some of the units had trained staff and most of them had only beginners who are not briefed on the desired safety measures. "These were not being looked into, with the department unable to keep a check on these units because of the shortage of staff. This needs to change and the onus is on the units to give training to their staff on safety measures, said Dalvi.

Heading: Delhi blasts effect: City on high alert for visarjan, 7000 security personnel on duty - Indian Express
Content:
In a few weeks from now, the residents of Paraplegic Rehabilitation Centre, Pune may soon get involved in a whole new ball game, literally. On Saturday, Jonathan Sigworth, a 21-year-old quadriplegic from the United States who is also a part of his country's wheelchair rugby team, made a proposal to the paraplegics and quadriplegics at PRC to put together a wheelchair rugby team that could participate internationally.

The immediate target is the World Wheelchair Sports Meet scheduled in India in 2009. Sigworth, who was paralysed from below his arms after a tragic accident while he was in Mussoorie in 2005, is of the belief that the sport will also work wonders in making the paraplegics more confident and independent. This, he says is the real motive behind the project.

After his accident Jonathan had been treated in Delhi for five weeks after which he flew back to his home in Connecticut in the US. But those five weeks were enough for him to grasp the lack of motivation and facilities faced by those with spinal cord injuries in India. Aided by his mother Vicky, Jonathan was back in India last December as part of the Empowering Spinal Cord Injured Persons (ESCIP) project where he introduced wheelchair rugby at Delhi's Indian Spinal Injuries Centre.

On Friday night, the duo arrived in Pune at the PRC where they hope to set up the country's first wheelchair rugby team. "Pune is most suited for the formation of the team. Though we introduced the sport in Delhi last Christmas and tried to put together a team, we found it's not very easy, for the simple reason that the patients do not stay there. This makes it difficult to get them together for regular practice. Here in Pune the patients stay on the PRC premises and that's a big advantage," said Vicky Sigworth.

The mother-so1n duo will put together six modified wheelchairs in the city over the weekend out of which they will leave behind four for the players as they tour other places like Bangalore to reach out to more wheelchair sportspersons.

"The World Wheelchair and Amputee Sports Federation (WWASF) that organises different wheelchair sports across the world is planning to hold the 2009 World Wheelchair Meet in India in 2009. They are very keen to have an Indian wheelchair rugby team ready for these games and have asked us to talk to the In1dian Paralympics Committee in this regard," said Vicky. This would also make India the first developing nation to participate in an international wheelchair rugby competition.

"While a new rugby wheelchair costs about $ 500, the old ones can be modified by putting an extension and covering the spokes with metal. We are trying to locate someone in Pune who can do that for us," said Jonathan, who will start practice sessions with the PRC residents from Monday.

According to the rules of the game only quadriplegics are allowed in the team. With PRC having 20-25 quadriplegics, Maj Mahesh Bisht, in charge of administration, is hopeful that the sport will receive a positive response.

According to Lt Col S P Jyoti, Director PRC, talks on introducing the sport at PRC has been on since March this year.

The training and initial introduction to the sport will be conducted jointly by Jonathan and Amit Saroha, former hockey player, who has also come to Pune from Sonepat with the Sigworths.

"I want to teach the people here all that I picked up. The ultimate aim of course is the creation of a team that can compete internationally," said Saroha, who was rendered a quadriplegic after a road accident last September and is today the best wheelchair rugby player in the country.

Along with setting up the teams, Vicky and Jonathan are also shooting a film on wheelchair rugby in India and the problems faced by paraplegics and quadriplegics. The film will be later shown in hospitals around the country in a bid to encourage other patients with spinal injuries and give them hope for the future.

"I think it's a great idea and we will certainly participate in the training," said Amarjeet Singh, a quadriplegic at the PRC. Another quadriplegic S. Radhakrishnan added that they had seen the sport on a CD two years ago and have been keen since then to take it up.

Wheelchair rugby
Invented by Canadian quadriplegics wheelchair rugby is a full contact sport played on the basketball court. Also known as murderball it is played in over 25 countries today.

Heading: ‘High-tech’ transfers to nullify corruption in Octroi posts - Indian Express
Content:
The serial bomb blasts in Delhi just a day before the Ganapati immersion procession has put the Pune police on a high alert.

Over 7,000 police and security agency personnel have been deployed on bandobast duty. Security cameras have been installed at strategic points. There would be special watch on railway stations, bus depots, airport, markets and religious places. "We appeal the Ganesh Mandals and citizens of Pune to avoid bursting crackers on the day of immersion. People should stay alert about strangers," said Joint Commissioner of Police Rajendra Sonawane.

Sonawane said that in the wake of serial blasts at Delhi, a nakabandi operation was launched in the city on Saturday night.

"We also appeal the Ganesh Mandals to follow the prescribed noise levels while playing the loud speakers and music system during the immersion procession. Loud speakers would not be allowed after 12 pm. Speakers kept on after the deadline would be seized," he added.

The police have set up 14 watchtowers along the route of the procession and each tower will be manned by three police men, equipped with binoculars and guns. The police have also made arrangements to capture the procession on camera. Mayor Rajlaxmi Bhosale will flag off the immersion procession on Sunday morning by offering a puja to the first Manacha, Kasba Ganpati.

The Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) has installed a reception pandal at Alka Talkies chowk, where all the Ganesh mandals participating in the Ganesh procession, will be given a warm welcome by the civic authorities.

Citizens have been asked to contact the police control room at - 100 or 26126296 in case of emergency.

Heading: Mom and dads - Indian Express
Content:
The search by the octroi department of the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) to prevent malpractices in the Octori posts has ended on a high-tech note.

Now, the department is guided by a software system, which automatically generates a transfer list of employees in the octroi posts every month.

Named 'Employees Transfer Software', the software automatically generates a transfer list of octroi staff every month. The system has been designed such a way that no employee returns to one particular post within the duration of six months.

Chief of the PMC octroi department Kundalik Karkar said the system was very effective. "We installed the software six months back and the system is very effective. After the installation of the software, the transfers of the employees working at the octroi posts of the PMC have become easier," Karkar said.

"Before this automatic system, we used to follow the manual process of transfers, which used to take about three months. The other obvious benefit is that it prevents anybody from indulging in any kind of malpractice or corruption," he said.

There are 40 octroi posts located on the outskirts of the city.

The strength of the employees at a particular octroi post that include supervisor, senior clerk, junior clerk and help is determined by the workload. Now, the total strength of octroi staff is 350.

"Since the Phugewadi octroi post witnesses churning out of more business than others, there are about 25 persons each working in three different shifts, while the smaller posts might just have three employees in each shift," Karkar added,

Earlier, the department had installed a biometric sensor at the office in order to keep a check on the attendance of its employees "With this, we can track the exact arrival and departure time of the employees.

This system does not allow anybody to furnish wrong time," said Karkar. The system has been in place since December last year.

Heading: Rock bottom - Indian Express
Content:
Movie name:Mamma Mia!
Cast:Meryl Streep, Pierce Brosnan, Colin Firth, Stellan Skarsgard, Amanda Seyfried
Directed by:Phillida Lloyd
Showing at:Gold Adlabs

In 2007 there was Across the Universe which used Beatles songs to convey the heartbreak, confusion and ambition of the tumultuous 60s. Nothing as grand about Mamma Mia! It just lays all its love on you, and there you go again. My, my how can we resist this?

It's the story of a bride-to-be trying to find her father on the eve of her wedding, set against the backdrop of an idyllic Greek island, and using hit songs by ABBA. The film uses a screenplay that has already proved successful in a musical by the same name. And from the high points to the low, Mamma Mia! Doesn't strike a wrong note.

The hotel that Meryl Streep's Donna runs may be out of a Hallmark romantic card, her daughter just rightly tanned, her future son-in-law a veritable Adonis, and the story unabashedly contrived, but everything is forgotten and forgiven as the music rolls and washes over you. The best example perhaps is Dancing Queen, which has the whole island tapping.

And isn't it nice that the lead actors are all of the age that ABBA group members would be now? Music has no age, and here is a perfect example.

There have been complaints about the girls in the film having just too much fun, but hey it's two days in a lifetime of raising a kid alone! And on the eve of a wedding! Give them a break.

Leading from the front in this joyride is Streep, as the former wild pop star who is now the owner of a rundown hotel, and who is afraid of what her daughter will think if she finds out that her mother doesn't know her real father. Pierce Brosnan as Sam, Colin Firth as Harry and Stellan Skarsgard as Bill - who could all be the prospective fathers - are also charming as three men chastised in middle-age.

However, the person who really charms your heart is Julie Walters as Streep's friend Rosie, another former wild musician turned dotty writer. She knows her mind, and speaks it too. Not for nothing does she get the song Take a chance on me. In the end, that's what Phillipa Lloyd's Mamma Mia! is about.

Heading: Patients at receiving end as R G Kar Hospital reels under powercut - Indian Express
Content:
A Still from the film Journey to the Center of the Earth

Movie name:Journey to the Center of the Earth
Cast:Brendan Fraser, Josh Hutcherson, Anita Briem
Directed by: Eric Brevig
Showing at:Gold Adlabs

A Successor to Indiana Jones and National Treasure, Journey to the Center of the Earth is the start of what promises to be another new adventure film franchise. Atlantis, the filmmakers leave no doubt, will be the next plot.

And that's not to say Journey doesn't at least feature all of the landmarks which have come to be associated with such a film - starting with a dour professor, an inquisitive child, a pretty co-adventurer, an undefined source of income, crazy special effects, crazier storyline, big animals, bigger threats, one truly astonishing train ride, some truly harmless volcanoes and three remarkably unharmed individuals. And then there is Brendan Fraser - what can you say, he has survived three Mummies hasn't he?

Don't go expecting anything extraordinary, take along a seven-year-old, and his screams of delight will make the trip worthwhile.

Heading: BSF hands over 150 Bangla infiltrators to police - Indian Express
Content:
Following yet another powercut at the R G Kar Medical College and Hospital, patients of the emergency department of the state-run hospital had a harrowing time on Saturday morning.

There was no electricity for nearly an hour. In the last few weeks, the hospital has witnessed frequent loadshedding that has left patients and their relatives at the receiving end.

Tarapada Das, who was in the emergency department with his daughter and ailing wife, was affected by the powercut. "We are here for the last two days and have been suffering because of the powercuts," said Das, a resident of Barasat. While some patients complained that the heat was unbearable, others were afraid that functions of operation theatres might be affected.

Although there are generators to supply power to some blocks in the hospital, sources say these are never put into service. Hospital authorities claim that operation theatres and intensive care units have generators but the Public Works Department officials do not make these operational. The hospital authorities admit that it is not possible to provide power backup to each section of the emergency units. The R G Kar College Principal, Utpal Dutta said, "We cannot connect every department with a generator because we do not have sufficient capacity. We are planning to bring more generators."

A doctor said, "While generator facility is not available for the all the emergency units, even existing generators are not being used. It makes things worse."

According to hospital employees, powercuts have become a regular affair and this makes their work difficult, as patients and their relatives get annoyed by it.

"We face loadshedding almost everyday. This affects the functioning of the hospital. Yesterday one of our elevators got stuck midway because there was not enough power backup in the hospital," said an employee.

Heading: 25 fresh cases of enteric in Jadavpur - Indian Express
Content:
The Border Security Force has handed over more than 150 people, who entered into the Indian territory from Bangladesh on Friday, to the Hingalgunj police in North 24 Parganas on Saturday. They were produced before the magistrate's court at Basirhat and were sent to 14-day judicial custody.

Police investigations reveal that an infiltration racket is thriving in the area, owing to a nexus between touts in Bangladesh and West Bengal. The racket is flourishing in Hasnabad and Hingalgunj in North 24 Parganas and Satkhira district in Bangladesh.

After the BSF intercepted nearly 150 infiltrators on Friday morning —- one of the highest number in recent years —- several touts operating in the area have come under the scanner. Aswini Mondal from Sankarkathi in Bangladesh and Sukumar Jotdar and Surdarshan Mondal from Kalitala in Hingalgunj are considered to be the prime suspects.

Sources say these touts charge Rs 600 from a person to cross the border and another Rs 1,500 to be taken to Kolkata. They also take away their cash and promise to return once they reach the city. It is rarely returned though.

The infiltrators mostly work as labourers in brick-kilns and at construction sites. Most of the infiltrators detained by the BSF on Friday were in the age group of 20 to 40 years.

Since they are ready to work at lower wages than their Indian counterparts, the touts easily find jobs for these Bangladeshi nationals.

BSF sources say that the touts make huge money from these labourers. "They regularly take a batch of nearly 20 infiltrators to Kolkata and charge Rs 1,500 from each person. They also take commission from those, who employ these labourers," said a BSF official.

Additional DIG (general) South Bengal Frontier BSF, Vikash Chandra said, "Tomorrow we will file a protest note with the Bangladesh authorities. Once we get their response, a meeting will be held at the DIG level."

The BSF, however, has not been able to arrest any tout. "We raided their houses but they had fled away by then. We are keeping a close watch on them and they will be arrested soon," said Chandra.

Heading: After mapping the world, woman ‘tests’ motherhood in City of Joy - Indian Express
Content:
On the fourth day of the enteric outbreak in Jadavpur, a health camp set up in the area by the Kolkata Municipal Corporation recorded 25 cases of severe gastroenteritis.

Nearly 300 people have been reported to be affected by the disease in the area so far.

A health official working at the camp said, "Nearly 50 people came to the camp today but only 25 of them were detected with enteric ailments. Nine of these have been admitted to the Baghajatin State General Hospital and Beleghata ID hospital."

The KMC, however, sees no reason to worry. Local councillor Chandana Ghosh Dastidar said, "The situation is under control. The number of affected people is gradually decreasing. Four health teams, consisting of two health workers, are visiting houses in the area to spread awareness."

Director General (water supply department) of KMC, Bibhas Maity said, "The water sample collected yesterday has been found to be safe. Though today also we have collected water samples, people can start using KMC supplied water." The civic body will send water tankers till the health camp is positioned in the area, he added.

Heading: Toppers’ answers now online - Indian Express
Content:
She travelled from London to Rome but what she could not get there, she found it in Kolkata. Joshna Das (45), a resident of Milan in Italy, gave birth to a test tube baby on Thursday at one of the private fertility clinics in the city. This is perhaps the first test tube case from Europe being treated in Kolkata.

"We have had some test tube cases from the USA and other parts. But this is the first time that a woman from Europe has come down to us for treatment. Medical tourism in Kolkata is expanding and we are being recognised in the international market," said Dr Sudarshan Ghosh Dostidar, who heads a private fertility centre in the city.

Originally from Bangladesh, Das is at present a citizen of Milan. Married for 20 years, Das had earlier conceived twice. Each time, however, she met with a miscarriage. At the age of 41, when Das stopped having her menstrual cycle, she went for treatment to various cities across Europe. But every time she was disappointed.

Finally, a year ago she came to Kolkata and sought treatment from Dr Dostidar, one of the team members involved in the delivery of the second test tube baby in India. After receiving an egg donor and going through the entire treatment, Das delivered a test tube baby girl a couple of days back.

"I visited many places abroad. But nowhere could I get the satisfaction of becoming a mother and the process ended up being expensive and time consuming until I came to Kolkata," said Das.

Heading: Dream come true - Indian Express
Content:
With the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) posting the answersheets of the 2008 Board examination toppers on its website, both the teachers and the students have found the best way to answer a question to get the maximum marks.

The CBSE has posted the high scoring answerscripts in streams of science, social science and mathematics of Class X students and of biology, chemistry, physics, mathematics, accountancy and business studies of Class XII.

While the Board has not mentioned the names of students with the answersheets, answers of the language papers are not posted online.

Teachers said the online display of answers would help students to score better in examinations. Principal of Birla High School for Boys, Mukta Nain said: "It will give a student an idea of the model answers."

Principal of Mahadevi Birla Girls School, Malini Bhagat said, "It is a very innovative mechanism. I have told my students and teachers to follow the answersheets of the toppers."

On why the board has not posted the answers of the language subjects, teachers feel that these subjects are highly subjective. "Since there can be different ways to attempt a question of a language paper, the board has decided not to disclose answersheets of these subjects," said a teacher.

Teachers also termed the CBSE the most progressive examination Board that has been gaining an edge over the other Boards. Within a few years, the number of schools affiliated to CBSE in Kolkata has increased to 30, principals of several schools pointed out.

Heading: A challenging job - Indian Express
Content:
Shamik Chakrabarty in conversation with Gautam Dasgupta, a former BCCI joint-secretary, who has given shape to many a poor child's dream to make it big in the cricketing world

Chandranath Chatterjee, a budding cricketer barely in his 20s, died after a heart attack while playing cricket. The untimely death of Chandranath led a few Shyambazar Club officials to set up the Chandranath Chatterjee Memorial Cricket Coaching Centre (CCMCCC) at Girish Avenue in north Kolkata in 1993.

That perhaps opened the floodgates to a host of underprivileged sports aspirants who loved to dream big.

Poverty is a killer. It kills hope. It forbids dreaming. But there are always exceptions to the rules.

At Chandranath Chatterjee Memorial Cricket Coaching Centre you can enjoy the difference. Poverty doesn't get a snub here. Rather, it gets support. For those who love cricket but don't have the means to dream big, this centre has the solution.

The man who has made this cricket coaching centre an exception is a former BCCI joint-secretary — Gautam Dasgupta.

The general impression about Dasgupta is that he is a man who loves to control the show from behind the scenes in the Cricket Association of Bengal (CAB). That's half the story. There's a different side as well. This dark, wisecracking cricket administrator genuinely cares for the grassroots. Social service is his joie de vivre.

P Lakshman's case is perhaps the biggest example. A boy from Kidderpore with South Indian roots who makes a living by selling idli, is now seriously contemplating pursuing a cricketing career. Without Dasgupta's help this wouldn't have been possible.

The CCMCCC trainees and their parents used to contribute to most of Lakshman's daily sales. Life changed suddenly. One day the camp was short of bowlers and coach Swapan Sarkar was a bit worried. Suddenly a ball came to Lakshman. The sheer irreverence and exuberance of youth prompted him to bowl it back to the fielders with a full run-up.

The coach spotted talent in that run-up and action. Later in the evening he told Dasgupta about the entire episode. The latter ensured that the talent didn't go in vain.

Lakshman was admitted to the coaching centre free of cost, was provided with kits and also some pocket money that could make up for the loss he would incur during practice hours.

Today the 18-year-old is playing in the CAB first division league and is also among the Bengal Under-19 probables.

"After Chatterjee's death, we the committee members of Shyambazar Club decided to do something in his memory. The consensus was to set up a cricket centre after his name that would open its heart and hearth to the underprivileged. It was easier said than done because at that time we barely had the funds. But we were committed to the cause that saw us through," Dasgupta said.

Lakshman, on the other hand, pays his gratitude to his "Gautam Sir" and other members of the centre.

"Without their help my aspirations would have been nipped in the bud. Cricket is still not a poor man's game. For a hawker like me, it's almost impossible to pursue a cricketing career without any financial assistance," he says in broken Hindi.

He is not alone. There are more of his type in that coaching clinic. The centre is happy to help them. The centre ensures they are treated on a par with those who belong to the privileged class.

A walk through Girish Avenue in north Kolkata and you will bump into this cricket coaching centre. Spend some hours and you will get to know how fetters can be broken, how barriers can be transcended.

Heading: Against all odds - Indian Express
Content:
Generating employment for locals of a particular area is his forte. Madhuparna Das finds out that Dr Santanu Banerjee, an ENT specialist, has also done his bit for the deaf as well

After a hectic schedule in office most of us hardly think of doing anything else apart from looking after our family. But Dr Santanu Banerjee is a class apart. He is one who loves helping out poor villagers find some employment opportunities even at the cost of his busy schedule.

Dr Banerjee, an ENT specialist by profession, heads a non-profitable organisation, Science Association of Bengal. The association comprises of around 20 members who are either doctors or scientists. It works tirelessly to find a way out for generating employment for the poor and the deprived by teaching several scientific procedures to the uneducated people in the state.

"We try to understand the need of the people of a particular village and study what kind of vocational training can generate employment in the area. Accordingly, we provide the locals with free vocational training," said Dr Banerjee.

Dr Banerjee and his team have visited far-flung villages in several backward districts of Bankura and Purulia. They have been trying to educate the poor villagers about the use of solar energy, scientific ways of food processing and more than a few ways of fruit cultivation.

"We have started a training course in Purulia and Bankura where the villagers are trained to cultivate coloured and ornamental fishes since they are in great demand. The training has been a success. At least 250-300 families in each village have benefited from this," said Dr Banerjee.

Not only in rural areas, even in urban areas and in the city too Dr Banerjee tries his best to generate employment among the local youths.

"I always try to find out the needs of a particular area and consequently generate some work for the unemployed youths there. I found out that vocational training in automobile technology can generate some job opportunities for the locals. So I started a training course in automobile repairing in Jadavpur," said Dr Banerjee.

For funding these training programmes, Dr Banerjee sometimes gets some funds sanctioned by the Central or the state government. The rest is borne by the members of the association.

Not merely content at that, Dr Banerjee is a prolific writer who has authored several dramas on social issues. One of his dramas, "Hasir Phansi", sponsored by the recreation club of the Legislative Assembly and staged at Rabindra Sadan, depicts the needs of the deaf.

"Often we find that people are sympathetic to the blind but they crack jokes at the expense of the deaf. Perhaps people cannot understand that the blind and the deaf are equally challenged people and both need sympathy, love, care and affection. Keeping this in mind, I wrote the drama to communicate the problems of the deaf to the world," said Dr Banerjee.

The dramas and books he wrote are purely for social interest and not for any commercial benefit. "Bed no. 0" is one of his famous plays which was staged at the Academy of Fine Arts recently.

Heading: Tata in reverse gear, silently begins moving out of Singur - Indian Express
Content:
Life may not have been kind to Tulsi Jyoti, but that hasn't diminished her love for music or her desire to help others. Sabyasachi Bandopadhyay meets the feisty woman

Just behind the VIP block of Writers' Buildings, at a far corner of the verandah, she has her small food stall where she sells goodies for the babus of the state secretariat. Sometimes her customers can hear her crooning a popular song while at other times she is seen using the table in front of her as a tabla.

Meet Tulsi Jyoti, a resident of Chetla, whose world came crashing down about 15 years ago when her husband, Bimal Chandra Jyoti, lost his job and later his sanity following the closure of the Metal Box factory at Taratala. Tulsi, who has two children, had no other option but to set up a stall at Writers' Buildings to eke out a living.

"I used to teach music to quite a few students while my husband worked at the factory. Those were happy times for me because I had a brother who used to compose songs and sing them. There was a kind of festive mood in our house almost all the time. Then came the bolt from the blue and everything changed,'' the woman, in her mid-40s, reminisces.

Tulsi first learnt music from her brother Somu Dutta and later from her cousin Pratap Kumar Mandal who in turn learnt music from such stalwarts as Sudhirlal Chakraborty and Shyamal Mitra.

"I learnt music for 14 years and later started teaching it. But after my husband lost his sanity, I had to do something to eke out a living. I heard about Writers' Buildings and people said setting up a shop there was equal to discovering a gold mine. But I found out that it was all a myth. Now for the whole day I remain busy at Writers' and I find very little time for my musical pursuits,'' the feisty woman said.

But she always helps others who have talent and have a strong desire to excel in life. One such person was Raghunath Dolui, who is an expert in mimicry and an employee at the finance department at Writers' Buildings.

"Owing to his lack of training in music, particularly the ragas and raginis, Dolui could not establish himself as a complete artiste in mimicry. I told him that he would have to learn music and I trained him whenever I found time. Now he has learnt the ragas and raginis and is a much better artiste,'' Tulsi said.

And Raghunath acknowledges the help he got from didi.

"Without her help, I could not better my performance. And not only music, I have seen she is an embodiment of courage and swagger. Whenever somebody is in distress she stands by him/her,'' Raghunath added.

Tulsi also helps the youngsters of her locality learn music. "Sometimes young children who are learning music come to me for help and if I have time I help them when they are stuck. I never charge a penny for that,'' she says with a smile.

Heading: All is not well at Singur yet: Left Front backs Buddha’s compensation package - Indian Express
Content:
In a silent midnight operation in the middle of this week, authorities at Tata Motors are said to have shifted several key equipment and machinery from the Singur plant. As the Singur talks collapsed on Friday, the move is seen as a first step towards the company's Plan B: launching Nano, the Rs one-lakh car, from its plant in Pantnagar in Uttarakhand or in Pune.

Senior police officials, officials and workers associated with the Nano plant and villagers in Singur confirmed to the Sunday Express that Tata Motors had arranged to have several of its key equipment—including automobile moulds and casts—shifted out from the 'press shop' of the factory at Singur.

When asked about the midnight operation, Debasish Roy, chief of communications for Tata Motors, said: "I cannot comment on this matter. Work at the Singur plant remains suspended. We had announced that Nano would roll out in the October-December quarter. We will stay as close to this plan as possible."

But an officer at the Singur plant said, "The equipment was packed off and transported at night on September 10 and 11. The moulds are specific to Nano and are not available at any other plant. So these had to be taken to our other facilities. The rest of the shops are untouched." According to a source, two consignments—one in 12 trailers and the other in 8—left on two consecutive nights.

Police officials on duty at Singur also confirmed that some machinery and equipment had been moved out. An inspector general of state police, who didn't want to be named, confirmed the midnight operation.

Plant officials and engineers said the moulds had to be shifted immediately since it takes some time to get them going after the installation. But they said the shifting hadn't been done at the cost of the Singur plant. If a turnaround in the Singur situation does happen—though that looks increasingly bleak—the plant here will be ready to manufacture the one-lakh car and can be "operationalised within a short period of time for limited production".

Company officials said some men were already being relocated. Sapoorji Pallonji, the firm engaged by the Tatas for site construction, has already withdrawn its workforce of 260 personnel, including 60 engineers, and have transferred them to other sites.

"We have got clear indications that work (in Singur) is not going to resume anytime soon. So we are planning to transfer some of our engineers," said an executive of Sapoorji Paloonji. He said they have already transferred 60 engineers from the Tata plant to TISCO in Jemshedpur, Tata Cancer Research Institute site in Rajarhat and other construction sites.

The Singur deadlock is back to where it all began when on Friday, Trinamool leader Mamata Banerjee refused to accept the government's offer to return 70 acres of land from within the plant site to rehabilitate unwilling farmers.

On Saturday, at an emergency meeting, Left Front partners backed Buddhadeb Bhattachajree and resolved that agitators should either accept the government's offer or "leave it". Front partners unanimously decided to launch a "political offensive" against Mamata Banerjee with a public meeting at Singur on Monday.

The chief minister may also address the rally. Mamata Banerjee will respond with a rally at Singur on Tuesday, where, she said, she would explain to farmers how the government had gone back on its words.

Heading: Game of one-upmanship: Mamata to take out rally in Singur too - Indian Express
Content:
On Friday, Mamata had rejected the CM's revised compensation package

The Singur imapsse showed no signs of resolution on Saturday after the Left Front approved Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee's decision of not giving more than 70 acres from within the Nano factory site to farmers.

The move came a day after Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee had rejected Bhattacharjee's proposal of a revised compensation package.

In an urgent meeting, the Front decided to organise a huge rally at Singur on Monday in support of the Nano factory. The rally will be held at the Mallikpur cold storage ground, nearly 2 kms from the Nano site. Even though talks between Bhattacharjee and Banerjee on Singur land return issue are not officially over, the Front gave a nod to Bhattacharjee to go ahead with his compensation package.

The Front's stamp for Bhattacharjee's initiative is being seen as a clear move by the ruling coalition to counter the Trinamool chief's demand of returning 400 acres of land to the farmers from the Singur car factory project site.

The state government will also make public the new compensation package in Sunday's newspapers to attract the unwilling farmers, who are in Mamata Banerjee's camp.

On Saturday, CPM activists held a rally at Joymollah area of Singur to highlight the features of the package. It is not clear whether Bhattacharjee will address the rally or not. "All the major Front leaders will be in Singur on Monday to address the farmers," CPM state secretary and Front chairman Biman Bose told mediapersons at the party's Alimuddin Street office.

"Our slogan is Singur chalo," Bose said. He also blamed Becharam Manna, the Trinamool Congress leader of Singur, for not arranging the alternative land for unwilling farmers.

"Why should the government move forward to arrange the land for these farmers? Why the Trinamool Congress panchayat samities at Singur are not taking the responsibility," he said.

Manna, a member of Singur panchayat samity, however, said, "Today we were asked to attend the meeting at the West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation. We are not going to attend any meeting now. We feel the issue of the land return will not be discussed any more."

Heading: Child dies of medical ‘negligence’ - Indian Express
Content:
Within hours after Left Front announced to hold a pro-industrialisation rally at Singur on Monday, Trinamool Congress supremo Mamata Banerjee also decided to hold her party's rally the next day.

While the Front's rally will be held at the Mullickpara cold storage ground in Singur, the Trinamool will organise its rally in front of the gates of the Tata Motors' car factory.

"They (the Left Front ) are not adhering to the gentleman's agreement and have given a call for a rally. The Front rally gives Trinamool the right to hold rallies. We have decided to hold a protest rally the very next day to press forward our demand for return of the land," said Banerjee.

She added that further protest programmes of the Trinamool would be announced once the Governor, now on a visit to New Delhi, returns to Kolkata on September 19.

Blaming the Left Front government for the failure of the talks to resolve the Singur crisis, she said: "They do not seem interested in implementing the agreement drafted between us and the state government in presence of the Governor."

The Trinamool leader alleged that the committee set up to finalise the modalities to return the land had stopped functioning after three days.

"When our representatives enquired about it, the MD of West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation said the state government had directed them not to proceed further," said Banerjee.

Heading: Over 20,000 cases resolved at Lok Adalat - Indian Express
Content:
A private diagnostic centre in north Kolkata was accused of medical negligence after a seven-month-old child died on Saturday.

A complaint has been filed at the Phoolbagan police station against the diagnostic centre and the doctor concerned.

A police officer said that Shibam Shau, a resident of Dattabad area in Muchipara, was undergoing treatment at the B C Roy Children's Hospital. Sources said the child was being treated for thalasaemia.

On Saturday, he was referred to a local diagnostic centre for an ultrasonography and a blood test. At the centre, Shau was administered a sedative before the tests. His parents were told to take the child and return after sometime for the tests so that the sedative could start its action.

The child's mother, Sunita Shau said, "We brought the child to our home but after sometime, his condition deteriorated and he died."

The centre, however, claimed that it was normal to administer a sedative to a patient and the child could not have died due to the injection. They claimed that the child had a tumor in the stomach, which caused his death.

Heading: Open heart surgery performed on 5-yr-old - Indian Express
Content:
Compensation to the tune of Rs 20 crore was awarded to litigants

More than 20,000 cases were settled today with the mutual agreement and understanding of both parties at the state-level Lok Adalat held here in the city.

Compensation to the tune of Rs 20 crore was also awarded to the litigants.

Justice Mehtab Singh Gill, a Punjab and Haryana High Court judge and Executive Chairman of the State Legal Services Authority, presided over the Lok Adalat proceedings.

Justice Gill stressed upon the need for further strengthening of the concept of Lok Adalats.

"Lok Adalats not only provide speedy justice to the litigants, but also help in reducing the number of pending cases in the courts," he said.

He appealed to the people to bring their cases in the special Lok Adalats for immediate and final settlement.

G K Rai, District and Sessions Judge and Chairman District Legal Services said that earlier Ludhiana district had conducted 292 Lok Adalats in which a record number of 64,728 cases were settled and an amount of Rs 103 crore had been disbursed to the litigants.

He also said that presiding officers of the Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Labour Officers and Conciliation Officers participated in the Lok Adalat and a number of social workers and advocates were also involved as members of the Benches.

A total number of 31 Benches were set up in today's Lok Adalat.

Among others who were present on this occasion included G S Bakhshi Member Secretary, A K Mehta, P S Dhanoa, M S Virdi, A S Grewal, Kishore Kumar, Manjinder Singh, G S Saran, R L Ahuja (both Additional District and Sessions Judge), Rajinder Aggarwal Aditional CJM, Lachhman Singh CJM, Civil Judge K K Bansal, DBA President P S Ghuman, J K Kapila, Rajnish Gupta, Ramesh Lakhanpal, Nitin Kapila, Rajan Kumar (both advocates), Ruby Farnadies and Pappu Avinash Singh (social workers).

Heading: Festival of Holy Cross celebrated in city church - Indian Express
Content:
The Cardiac Surgery department of SPS Apollo Hospital has successfully performed a open heart surgical closure of a large VSD with severe pulmonary artery hypertension (continuous high blood pressure), on a five year old child, weighing just 10 kg.

The pulmonary arteries are the blood vessels that carry deoxygenated blood from the heart to the small arteries in the lungs.

The Cardiac Surgical team headed by Dr KC Mukherjee, Senior Consultant and Coordinator was supported by Dr Anupam Srivastava, Dr Ankit Mathur, Dr Preet Kamal, Dr Maninder, Dr Ranjeet and Cardiologists Dr RP Singh, Dr JS Grewal and Dr Chetan Sharma and paediatrecian Dr TS Gambhir.

Jessica, a 5-year-old girl and a resident of Hansa, was underweight and practically showed no signs of growth.

She was diagnosed to have a hole in the heart (VSD) which was bigger than the aorta (main artery of the body).

Because of this hole, most of the blood was being diverted to the pulmonary artery(PA) and then to the lungs. This high flow of blood in the pulmonary artery since birth had raised the pressure in the PA as high as aorta (normally it is one-fourth of aorta).

Increase in PA pressures and low body weight of the patient made it a very high risk surgery.

A team at the SPS Apollo Hospital successfully operated this patient in two-and-half hours and the patient regained consciousness in 6 hours and started walking in 48 hours.

The patient was discharged on the sixth post-operative day in normal condition with a normal heart. Dr K C Mukherjee stated that such kinds of operations require excellent skill, good team, good infrastructure and multispeciality support.

Heading: Poor solid waste handling stinks all the way - Indian Express
Content:
The Holy Cross Church at Sarabha Nagar in the city celebrated its annual day with much gusto and fervour.

The day also marked the festival of the Holy Cross, which is celebrated in the Catholic Church every year on September 14.

Dr Anil Jose Thomas Couto, the Bishop of the Diocese of Jalandhar was the chief guest on the ocassion.

He was accorded a warm welcome by the Parish Priest Father Joseph K, Father Antony Khokhar, the council members of the church and all those who had gathered for the festival.

The Bishop was also welcomed by the Sarabha Nagar Market Committee.

As the Bishop reached the Holy Cross Church, people sang hymns to greet him. Father Mathew N V, Father Daniel Gill, Father John E, Fr Mathew K, Fr James and Fr Jospeh T J were all present on the occasion.

A number of nuns from in and around the city as well as scores of people from across the district joined in the prayer service.

Prior to the festival, a three-day family renewal prayer session was organised in the church.

Hundreds of people participated in this preparatory prayer session.

Among those who organised this festival were Sacred Heart Convent School nuns, Babu Samuel, Robert, Mukhtiar, George Kutty and Albert Dua along with the members of the Parish Council.

Heading: Heroin in couriers: two arrested - Indian Express
Content:
The municipal corporation has only 68 vehicles for transporting 900 metric tonnes of garbage churned everyday

In the ever-expanding industrial hub of the state, there is little mechanism in place for garbage arising out of human activity - let alone the processing of the garbage that could as per an estimate generate power up to 7 MW or can be used for creating 300 tonnes of fuel pellets, if handled properly.

The city churns out as much as 900 metric tonnes of garbage every day. It comes as no surprise that the municipal corporation has not lived up to the rules stated under the Municipal Corporation Solid Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2000, notified by the Ministry of Environment.

While most of the city areas do not even have garbage containers for collection of domestic waste, leaving the garbage collection in private hands, the transportation of garbage is also done in the most unhealthy way as open trucks carry filth to landfill sites while spilling it on the roads all along the way. This is against the rule that clearly states that the garbage has to be carried in covered vehicles and garbage should not be visible to the public.

There are nearly 68 vehicles used by MC for garbage transportation, and many of them are in a bad shape, and not to mention, without cover.

As for collection of garbage from houses, in areas where garbage is picked up in door-to-door collection, the workers have been charging heavily. However, Section 44 (C) of the Punjab Municipal Corporation Act, 1976, states it as an obligation of the MC to scavenge, remove and dispose filth, rubbish, and other obnoxious or polluted matter.

According to the MC figures, there are 269 overall sites in the city including nine open dumping sites 260 containerised sites. Around 50 per cent of them are condemned containers that have never been replaced. Therefore, at most of these collection points where bins are placed, garbage is mostly scattered all around the bins.

Notably, there are hardly any containers or 'bins' in most areas of the city, be they posh localities like Sarabha Nagar or the congested and old areas of the city. MC too admits that the 'City Development Plan' that 'Solid Waste arising out of human activity is one of the major environmental problems causing extensive pollution and threat to human health'.

A city resident, on the condition of anonymity, makes scathing remarks for the LMC saying that it should adopt some stern measures to deal with this problem before it becomes a potential health hazard and MC offices are forced to be used as dumping sites. Notably, MC has also failed to meet all the deadlines to set up processing and disposal facility.

The two landfill sites - at Jainpur village on Hambran Road and at Jamalpur, opposite new jail on the Tajpur Road - are also posing potential health hazards to the nearby residents. There are no walls on the peripheries, as per the rules, and the garbage is also not segregated into bio-degradable and non-degradable.

LMC Commissioner GS Ghuman who has recently taken charge says that two things that are high on his agenda are condition of the roads and garbage disposal. "I have received some 30 calls on a single day about this problem and that speaks volumes about the urgency to tackle it.

I have found that there are not sufficient containers for garbage collection in the city so first thing I have done is that I have invited tenders for buying 125 new bins," he says.

He maintains that for a better and economical solution to the problem, the MC is mulling to give it on BOT (Build-Operate-Transfer) basis to a private contractor. "We are soon going to hold a meeting with an organisation which has offered to undertake this job," he says.

The figures
* Domestic waste and open waste accounts for 56.31 per cent of the total MSW.
* Commercial waste from hotels, restaurants, shops, and other establishments, accounts for 23.95 per cent of MSW.
* Industrial waste accounts for 19.74 per cent of MSW.

Heading: Students’ polls in colleges can be considered: minister - Indian Express
Content:
The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has arrested two persons in connection with the seizure of heroin in the courier parcels a couple of days ago. The arrested persons have been sent to the custody of the DRI for three days for further questioning.

The arrested persons include Roopjit Singh, director of an Amritsar-based publishing house which publishes religious books and one Gurpal Singh, director of a local music company.

Sources said that on Friday, the DRI sleuths had questioned some persons after the seizure of heroin in the courier parcels. On Wednesday night, the DRI had seized 48 packets of heroin from some courier packets which were being sent to Canada through a courier company. Each packet contained 100 gm heroin and a total of 4.8 kg of heroin was seized. The DRI had intercepted a van of the courier company on late Wednesday night following secret information. The packets of heroin had been concealed in the couriers containing religious material such as books, VCDs and DVDs.

Rs 2.6 lakh burgled
A domestic help decamped with cash and goods worth over Rs 2 lakh from the Vikas Nagar house of the Sidhwan Bet police station SHO Sandeep Kumar Wadhera. The Sarabha Nagar police have registered a case.

The theft was reported on Thursday and the Sarabha Nagar police registered the case on Friday.

According to the police, Wadhera had hired Krishan Bahadur, a resident of Nepal, a few days ago.

Sources said the day when the theft took place, Krishan Bahadur and a maid were at the house. Sources said that Krishan Bahadur broke opened the almirahas and stole Rs 2 lakh and other items.

The Sarabha Nagar SHO Devinder Kumar told Newsline that the police had started investigating the matter after registering a theft case against the domestic servant. He said that efforts were on to search the accused.

SHO Devinder Kumar further said, "SHO Wadhera had taken the photo of the accused and had also taken his original address in Nepal. So it will help trace the accused."

Heading: From Mahima to ‘ma’ - Indian Express
Content:
State Education minister Upinderjit Kaur said if student bodies from colleges approach her with their demand to hold elections in the colleges across the state, she would consider the matter positively.

She said this while replying to a question on the student elections in the colleges of the state at Ramgarhia Girls College.

The minister was in the city today to preside over a state-level cultural festival 'Mela Dhiyan Da'.

Speaking at the function, the minister also remarked about the demand to accord central status to Panjab University, Chandigarh, and said the state government would rather ask the Centre to give more funds to PU, than asking for a central status in order to get funds from the Centre.

"Why is it that Centre can give funds only when it has a central status, and not otherwise.

The people of the state deserve to get their due for the services and, therefore, there should not be any discrimination when it comes to giving funds to the university," she said.

About the compulsory use of Punjabi in the government departments and as a compulsory subject in the schools, she said, "The language will gets its due now and we are happy that the Bill was passed by the House unanimously."

When asked about certain objections raised about its feasibility, she added that the language will be studied by students up to Class X in all schools across the state. "All the schools in the state will teach Punjabi as a compulsory subject, along with Hindi and English."

Replying to a question, she said that it would be an addition in the personality of even those students whose parents are working in the central government or are the wards of defence personnel. "The children at the tender age have more capacity to learn new things, so Punjabi will be a benefit for them," she remarked.

The minister also said the government will constitute an award titled 'Punjab Shikhya Ratan' for excellence in education. She also reiterated the government's steps to convert Mohali into a knowledge city and also have two central universities in the state apart from an IIT.

About recruitment of the vacant posts in the colleges, she said that the vacant post of 265 lectures and 12 posts of principals will be finalised soon.

Also present on the occasion was Sukhbir Singh Badal's wife Harsimrat Kaur Badal.

Heading: ‘There is a dire need to pass the HIV/AIDS Bill’ - Indian Express
Content:
Bollywood actor Mahima Chaudhry, who has been missing from the silver screen for a while now, proudly sums up her 'absence' by narrating her journey from Mahima to 'ma' (mother).

"Motherhood has not only changed my life, it has made me a complete woman. I feel blessed to have a daughter and she is the most wonderful thing to have happened to me," says the actor, who had won the best debut (female) in the Filmfare Awards in 1998.

Mahima's bundle of joy Ariyana is now more than a year old.

"Motherhood and fatherhood is something everyone should experience in their lives. It is simply unmatchable. She (Ariyana) has been bliss for me," she beams, while speaking on the sidelines of a function organised by a liquor company at Hotel Park Plaza last evening.

"I thought my life would slow down after having a child, but it has rather raced up," she said while speaking to the audience in a jam-packed hall at the hotel. Having starred in over 30 movies, Mahima started her career in 1997 after she was reportedly shortlised from amongst 3000 participants in the audition for the role of Ganga in Subhash Ghai's Pardes.

Declaring her love for the state and its people, she remarked, "Punjab is full of pretty girls and good-looking men. It has always been a pleasure to come to this part of the country where there is beauty all around."

Commenting about item numbers and skimpy dresses becoming a fad, she said, "It varies from person to person and I don't believe by doing all this, one can become more successful." Apparently, Mahima seemed impressed with new releases that have been based on nice themes. "I really loved Mumbai Meri Jaan and there have been some nice releases in the recent past," she said.

When asked about acting in a Punjabi movie, she replied that she would not mind acting in Punjabi flicks. "Punjab is going global and Punjabi music is now sold internationally," she said. About her upcoming acting projects, she said that she was finalising a few scripts.

Motherhood has not only changed my life, it has made me a complete woman. I feel blessed to have a daughter and she is the most wonderful thing to have happened to me. Motherhood and fatherhood is something everyone should experience in their lives. It is simply unmatchable.

Heading: Kalyan, Katiyar against any alliance with RLD for Lok Sabha elections - Indian Express
Content:
"The government is not taking up the law on HIV/AIDS on priority basis. It was first submitted to NACO in 2006. The bill has remained stalled with the Ministry of Law and Justice since November 2007.

The bill aims to protect people living with HIV/AIDS (PLHA) from facing discrimination in both public and private sectors. There is a dire need to table and pass the long pending HIV/AIDS Bill as quickly as possible," said Raman Chawla, an advocacy officer of the Lawyers Collective HIV/AIDS Unit.

Chawla along with other members of his NGO held a meeting on Saturday with the Punjab Network of Positive People (PNPP), which is working actively for and with HIV+ people of the state.

He said that the bill was drafted by the Lawyers Collective HIV/AIDS Unit in consultation with stakeholders including PLHA groups, vulnerable communities, doctors, lawyers and civil society organisations working in the field of HIV/AIDS.

Jagjit Singh Mann, founder chairman of PNPP said, "Discrimination against HIV+ people is common in various sectors including education, health care and employment. This discrimination in turn prevents people, especially those communities at a high risk of contracting HIV, from accessing healthcare services due to the fear of stigmatisation."

He added, "We have no law in our country to prevent HIV-related discrimination. The Bill is central to that effort and should be tabled and passed soon by the Parliament."

The Lawyers Collective HIV/AIDS Unit is visiting the state for the first time.

"We will make the community aware about the need of this Bill by holding rallies, seminars and workshops," said a member of the NGO.

Heading: UP receives JE vaccine unfit for use - Indian Express
Content:
Finally, the senior leaders of Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Kalyan Singh and Vinay Katiyar, who stayed away from the party's national executive meet in Bangalore, expressed their opinion on having any pact with the Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) in western UP during the next Lok Sabha elections.

Sitting in New Delhi, former chief minister Kalyan Singh refuted reports about his ill health, which had been cited as the reason behind his absence from various party conclaves. "I am healthy both mentally and physically. I consciously opted to stay away from these programmes," he told The Sunday Express over the phone although he refused to elaborate any further.

Singh was, however, candid about his truck with RLD leader Ajit Singh. Terming any move to ally with the RLD as suicidal, Kalyan Singh said: "I strongly oppose any tie-up with Ajit Singh, as he is not trustworthy."

"Four times in the past, we won more than a dozen seats in western UP without any alliance, but after we joined hands with him we were left with only one seat," he said and listed the names of the Lok Sabha seats in western UP, which were once won by the BJP without any help from the RLD. "Mathura, Agra, Ferozabad, Etah, Jalesar, Hathras, Aligarh, Bulandshaher, Ghaziabad, Meerut, Baghpat, Kairana, Saharanpur, Moradabad, Amroha, Bareilly, Amla, Pilibhit and Badaun seats in western UP were won by the BJP without any help," he added.

Kalyan Singh is not the only one in the BJP who opposes any alliance with the RLD, even firebrand leader Vinay Katiyar also disapproves of any such move. "It is BJP that gave some base to Ajit Singh and in return, our own support base has been weakened," Katiyar said who too remained conspicuous by his absence in the national executive meeting.

Speaking to The Sunday Express over phone, Katiyar explained: "The party contested the 1997 Vidhan Sabha elections under the leadership of Kalyan Singh and won eight seats from western UP. During the 1998 Lok Sabha polls, Ajit Singh could not save his own seat and was defeated by BJP leader Sompal Shastri. In the following Lok Sabha elections, Ajit Singh was the lone candidate from RLD to retain his seat. At that time too, Kalyan Singh was the CM."

"But in the 2002 Assembly elections, the party under the leadership of Rajnath Singh, forged an alliance with Ajit Singh and gave 30 to 32 seats to him. We even scrapped the tickets of our sitting MLAs and the result was that RLD numbers grew from eight to sixteen," Katiyar said.

Both the BJP leaders maintained, "The need of the hour is to motivate party workers and lift their morale." Ajit Singh, meanwhile, is exploring different prospects after BSP leader Mayawati refused to meet his demands. "So far, no decision has been taken on the alliance," said one of his close aides.

Heading: Lucknow women find it difficult to complain against workplace abuse - Indian Express
Content:
The stock of nearly 4.5 lakh vaccines for Japanese Encephalitis (JE), which was found unfit for use after arrival in the city on Friday, had already suffered a loss of potency before being dispatched from the Government Medical Store Depot (GMSD) at Karnal.

Experts from an international NGO Path, who visited GMSD on Saturday, found that Vaccine Vial Monitor on a large number of vials stored there had undergone change of colour, indicating Stage II exposure due to heat and loss of efficacy. Path is providing technical support to the government in implementing the JE programme.

Dr Jagdish Chandra, Chief Medical Officer in-charge of GMSD, said: "When we inspected the stock today, some of the vial monitors had reached Stage II. It should not be much of a problem as vials with exposure of Stage II can be used for vaccination."

Chandra said, " The vaccine stock sent to UP was already at stage II. But if proper temperature was maintained during transportation, then it would not have been damaged further."

Dr Pritu Dhalaria, JE Programme Manager for Path in India, said: "The Stage II exposed vaccine can be used for vaccination, as its efficacy is only slightly reduced, but such damage at the initial place of storage is a cause of concern. For it means that even a little exposure to heat during transportation can completely damage the vaccine."

When the stock had arrived in Lucknow last evening, officials found that many samples showed Stage III and IV exposure. The officials immediately informed the Union Health Ministry and demanded replacements. A Union Health Ministry team is expected to arrive here on Monday to examine the stock.

UP officials insist that nothing was wrong at their end. M L Khatloiya, Director General (family welfare) of the state government, said, "We checked the supply as soon as it reached us and informed the senior ministry officials in the ministry that a large number of samples had reached Stages III and IV." Sources, however, said the vaccine stock remained at the Lucknow airport for over five hours and this could have damaged it.

Union Health Ministry officials refused to discuss the matter, stating they would comment only after assessing the situation. The JE vaccine is imported from China National Biotec Group. It is initially stored at GMSD, Karnal and from there it is supplied to 24 districts in 10 states for the vaccination programme. The states include UP, Bihar, Haryana, Kerala, Assam and Karnataka.

Following the reports of damaged stock landing in Lucknow and the finding of Stage II exposure vaccine in Karnal storage facility, inspection of stocks in other states has also begun.

Heading: Bulandshahr jailor, deputy escape murder bid - Indian Express
Content:
Two decades have passed since the groundbreaking judgment in the Vishakha vs Government of India case in which the Supreme Court had ordered all the offices to set up committee against sexual harassment. But working women in Uttar Pradesh are not aware of any such committees and are clueless about their need.

A survey conducted by All India Democratic Women's Association (AIDWA) in Lucknow has come out with some shocking results.

* In 18 offices, including state government and central government offices, 144 women were asked whether they know about the Vishakha case guidelines given by the Supreme Court or whether they were aware of any sexual harassment committee in their offices. Nearly 80 per cent of them were not aware whether such a committee exists in their offices.

* Only 7 out of the 18 offices surveyed had separate bathrooms for women and men employees.

* Most of the women said that if they ever complained about sexual remarks or overtures, they were humiliated and hence, preferred to keep quiet.

Ironically, the conditions are worse in offices of railways, banking and telecom sectors. On Friday, women working in these three sectors in the state came together to attend a meeting organised by AIDWA and North Eastern Railway Women Workers Welfare Association.

Refusing to be named, a railway employee from Lucknow said: "Despite having a large number of women in the office, such lewd acts are not punished. In fact, women find it difficult even to even lodge any formal complaints."

The women employees of railways decided that they would form small committees and groups to counter the problem in their respective offices.

It was also decided that instead of having a centralised system for complaints, each office in different zones should be forming such committees.

Former MP and national president of AIDWA, Subhashini Ali said that government is not serious about providing safe working zones for its women employees.

Heading: Maya dissolves college affiliation committee - Indian Express
Content:
The jailor and deputy jailor of Bulandshahr district jail escaped a near-fatal attack when two motorcycle-borne youths opened indiscriminate fire on them. The incident took place at the main gates of the residential quarters in the jail premises on Saturday morning.

SSP Bulandshahr Raj Kumar, said: "Though the jail officials have not spoken about any dispute with undertrials, the attack appeared to have been orchestrated from inside the jail." A police team has been asked to investigate the matter. IG (Prisons) Sulkhan Singh too echoed same reasons.

According to the police, jailor Shiv Singh Bhadauria and deputy jailor M R Yadav were standing at the main gates of the campus — located right opposite the jail — when the incident took place. The youth sitting pillion on the bike opened indiscriminate fire at the jail officials. The bullets missed the target. By the time, the armed constables rushed to the spot, the assailants had vanished from the place, police said.

Additional SP (City) J K Shahi said: "A few of the dreaded gangsters have been sent to jail recently and the jail staff was dealing with them strictly. It appeared as if some of the jail inmates have orchestrated the shootout."

Heading: Panchkula resident crushed to death by truck - Indian Express
Content: Chief Minister Mayawati dissolved the one-member empowered committee that was set up on September 2 for giving affiliation and NOCs to colleges and private universities. The committee was headed by UP Pollution Control Board chairman Anil Kumar Mishra, a close relative of national general secretary of ruling BSP Satish Chandra Mishra.

Heading: Chandigarh on the road to development - Indian Express
Content: A 29-year-old man died after a truck rammed into his Pulsar motorcycle near plot number 1 in Industrial Area around 11.15 pm on Friday. The deceased was identified as Rakesh Kumar, an HDFC employee and a resident of Sector 20, Panchkula. He is survived by his wife and a one-year-old son. Kumar sustained serious head injuries as he was crushed under the rear tyres of the truck and dragged for quite a distance. He was rushed to Government Medical College and Hospital, Sector 32, where he was declared 'dead on arrival'. The truck driver is absconding. A case under Sections 279 and 304 A (death due to negligence) of the IPC has been registered by the Industrial Area police against the unidentified driver.
