Heading: Students protest outside warden’s office, demand removal - Indian Express
Content:
The V-C and I have had several arguments as our way of working differs significantly. He chooses to overlook certain issues but I prefer to follow all rules and regulations. I was very hurt by the way Professor Sobti spoke to me
Professor Shashi Sharma
Head of the Law department, PU

Trouble seems to be brewing at the Panjab University after the just concluded students' elections.

Head of the Law department, Professor Shashi Sharma, tendered in his resignation following a heated argument with Vice-Chancellor Professor R C Sobti on the issue of campaigning by a Students' Organisation of Panjab University (SOPU) member. The V-C, however, did not accept Sharma's resignation.

Last week, Sharma complained to Dean Students Welfare, Professor Naval Kishore, against Brinder Dhillon, a SOPU member who went ahead with campaigning in classrooms against the code of conduct.

In response, SOPU members later raised slogans outside the V-C's office and Sobti summoned Professor Sharma to clarify the issue.

Sources said Sharma explained to the V-C that Dhillon was an outsider and had no business in the varsity while Professor Sobti tried to pacify him saying sometimes rules need to be overlooked.

The very next day, Professor Sharma submitted his resignation.

Talking to Newsline, Professor Sharma said: "The V-C and I have had several arguments as our way of working differs significantly. He chooses to overlook certain issues but I prefer to follow all rules and regulations. I was very hurt by the way Professor Sobti spoke to me."

Vice-Chancellor Professor R C Sobti preferred to maintain silence on the issue. "I would prefer not to comment," he said.

Heading: Immigration agent booked for working without licence - Indian Express
Content:
The residents said the warden had not allowed them to call a DJ to celebrate the victory of SOPU-ABVP in the students' elections on Friday

Residents of Sarojini Hall today gathered outside the office of hostel warden Meena Vinayak and raised slogans demanding her ouster. They alleged she was "excessively stern and troubled them".

The issue was resolved with the intervention of Vice-Chancellor Professor R C Sobti. Even Dean of Social Welfare Department Professor Naval Kishore wast present at the spot.

Both of them gave a patient hearing to the complaints against the warden. They later decided to remove Vinayak for the time being. The additional charge of the hostel was given to another warden.

The girls said that the warden had not allowed them to call a DJ to celebrate the win of SOPU-ABVP alliance in the students' elections.

Talking to Newsline, Brinder Dhillon, a SOPU member, said: "We had taken up the issue a number of times. The girls had been complaining against the warden some time and demanded that proper action be taken against her."

The girls had sat on a strike and had refused to move till the warden was not removed from the post.

Heading: Senior citizens to share their precious experiences with school students - Indian Express
Content:
The agent has been booked under Section 24 of Immigration Act, 1983

The Kharar police on Saturday booked an immigration agent for allegedly working without licence. The case under Section 24 of the Immigration Act, 1983, was registered on a complaint of K P Tiwari, immigration official of High Commission of India in Kuala Lumpur, said the police.

Tiwari complained that the proprietor of A Broadways Overseas Consultants in Nasib Complex, opposite bus stand in Kharar, Balwant Dhaliwal was allegedly working without a valid license and sending people abroad on the pretext of getting them employed at Chin Chai Enterprises in Malaysia.

In his complaint to Chandigarh SSP, which was later forwarded to Mohali SSP, Tiwari alleged that one such person-Rajinder Singh Sahota-went to Malaysia but failed to report at the Embassy office there despite being called. During scrutiny of records, it was found that Sahota was allegedly sent by Dhaliwal.

Kharar City SHO Manjit Singh was assigned to probe the case, added sources.

Heading: Reserve 10-15% seats for poor: CM - Indian Express
Content:
With an aim to engage senior citizens in social activities and help the coming generations derive benefit of their rich experience, the UT Administration has decided to give them free access to city schools as honourable guests.

The schools will make arrangements for transportation of the senior citizens from old age homes or those living in the vicinity of these schools.

One NSS volunteer, scout or guide will attend each senior citizen throughout their visit to the school. Students have been asked to undertake a survey in their neighborhood to identify old people and know their educational status. They will formulate a data, which will help in comprehending the requirements of senior citizens.

Heading: Policeman found guilty of attempt to rape, dismissed - Indian Express
Content:
Medical education minister hints at raising retirement age of doctors to 65

Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal called upon the private medical and dental colleges in the state to reserve 10-15 per cent seats for the economically weaker sections but bright students on the pattern of the recent decision taken by the managements of the private engineering and technical institutions in the state.

Badal and Punjab Medical Education Minister Tikshan Sood were in Mohali to attend a national workshop on Inter-Relationship of State Dental Councils and the Dental Council of India.

In his inaugural address, Badal said it was our foremost duty to provide equal opportunities of education thereby bridging the gap between the rich and poor.

He asked Sood to device ways and means to implement the proposal with detailed deliberations with the management of the private medical and dental colleges to enable the poor and capable students to avail of this opportunity.

Badal also urged the Dental Council of India (DCI) to start short-term courses in dentistry and oral hygiene in collaboration with the Punjab Dental Council (PDC) so that Punjabi youth can be gainfully employed.

He added that Punjab was the first state in the country to take a lead in launching the continuing dental education programme.

He said medical education was an ongoing process and such workshops and conferences offer an ideal platform to dentists and researchers to brush up their knowledge.

Speaking on the occasion, Sood hinted at raising the retirement age for doctors from present 60 to 65 and also reemploying those recently retiring at 60 in Punjab.

He also emphasised the need to have a separate directorate of dental health services to ensure smooth functioning of the dental wing of the Health department.

He said the workshop was aimed at improving the standards of dentistry on par with the dental education being provided internationally.

Heading: Labourers beaten, electrocuted by contractor for ‘stealing’ money - Indian Express
Content:
A sub-inspector with the Chandigarh Police was dismissed on Saturday after he was found guilty of attempt ing to rape a woman at her house in Maloya Colony in 2007.

The police have arrested Satpal Sharma on charges of attempting rape and trespassing under Sections 376, 511 and 452 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).

The victim had lodged a complaint with the senior superintendent of police, following which the complaint was marked to DSP (South) KIP Singh.

The case was registered after residents of the colony assembled at the Maloya police post and raised slogans against the police.

Just after the incident, Satpal was placed under suspension and a departmental inquiry was initiated against him.

The victim in her complaint on July 23, 2007, had stated that her husband had lost his mobile phone and they went to the police to report the matter.

The following day, around 8.30 am, the SI had reached their house. She stated that her husband was away and she was taking a bath. The SI allegedly pushed open the door and tried to molest her. She struggled to free herself and managed to kick him off. Thereafter, the accused warned her with dire consequences and left. She also alleged that the SI threatened to implicate her husband in a case and get him "suspended from his government job".

Heading: Dental council is a recommendatory body: Kohli - Indian Express
Content:
All the accused have been arrested and remanded in judicial custody

Five local residents were allegedly thrashed and given electric shocks by a contractor and his associates around 10 pm on Friday after the latter accused them of stealing Rs 50,000.

The five labourers — Monu, Arun, Sanjay, Manju, and security guard Harish Mishra — were beaten up by contractor Mohammad Kurban, near Pepsi turn where the four labourers and the security guard work for the construction of an under-bridge in Darwa.

When Monu and Manju expressed ignorance on being asked about the money, they were allegedly beaten and given electric shocks by the contractor and his associates.

After thrashing the two, the contractor then called Sanjay and Arun and thrashed them with iron rods.

When the security guard came to rescue the injured, he was also given electric shocks and beaten.

Monu and his friends received serious injuries and have been admitted in GMCH-32, Chandigarh. All the accused have been arrested and remanded to judicial custody.

A case under Sections 323,506,342 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) has been registered against Mohammad Kurban, Zahid, Rehman, Izhar, Saved, Irshad, Usuf, Fazal, Gulzar, Quarsh, Qaqli and Imran, at the police station, Industrial Area, Chandigarh.

Heading: UT Admn allows an inch, Punjab cops usurp a mile - Indian Express
Content:
Dr Anil Kohli, President, Dental Council of India, said the council had written to the government a number of times, complaining about the mushrooming of dental institutes across the country.

Kohli said granting affiliation is the fourth and the final step, where the chances of rejection are very less. After the state government, it is the university that gives provisional affiliation to the college, followed by the Centre and only then does the council come into action.

He said: "The Council is just a recommendatory body and most of the work depends upon the government."

Talking about the institute, Dr Kohli said it lacks both infrastructure and faculty.

He added that with the consent of Vice-Chancellor Professor R C Sobti, a laboratory for conducting stem cell research would be set up in the institute.

He added: "We wish to set up the laboratory for research, since desidous (baby teeth) are quite helpful in carrying out research. A big set up will be added to further work on stem cells."

Professor R C Sobti (left) along with Dr Anil Kohli at the inauguration of academic session of Dr HSJ Institute of Medical Sciences and Hospital in PU on Saturday. Sumit Malhotra

Heading: 69 contestants, 15 wards, Kharar all set for MC polls - Indian Express
Content:
82nd Battalion of Punjab Police has encroached upon 20 acres of land in Capitol Complex

The Capitol Complex is under siege-by our very own Punjab Police. The 82nd Battalion of the Punjab Police has blatantly encroached upon around 20 acres of prime land in the city, while the Chandigarh Administration looks the other way.

In 2002, the Chandigarh Administration gave permission to the police to pitch tents in a 6.5-acre area behind the Punjab Civil Secretariat. Later, the regulations were relaxed to allow the construction of pre-fabricated structures.

But an extremely different scenario prevails today with the policemen cordoning off approximately 20 acres and constructing cemented structures at the site. A swanky mess, canteens, barracks and even a guesthouse pass off as pre-fabricated structures. The mango grove and guava orchards between the Chandigarh Club and Punjab Civil Secretariat have also been encroached upon.

A barbed wire mesh, which starts from the boundary of Chandigarh Club and finishes at the road to Kansal village, cordons off the area with sentry posts at all entry points.

When Newsline tried clicking photographs of the 'restricted area', a Punjab Armed Police guard opposed the action adding no one could enter the area owing to 'security reasons'.

It seems the area is a popular hangout for senior Punjab police officers and bureaucrats. "Relatives and guests of bureaucrats and officers normally stay at the Gazetted Officers' (GO) mess. Even officers, from outstation posts, prefer staying at the mess when they visit Chandigarh," said an official.

The UT Administration officials seem to have recently woken up to the goof-up. UT Deputy Commissioner R K Rao said: "We received information about such violations and are verifying the facts. The place in question is indeed a sacrosanct part of the city's Capitol Project."

Sources said UT Chief Engineer S K Jaitley has been ordered to conduct an immediate survey to identify the encroachment and submit a report to UT Home-cum-Finance Secretary Sanjay Kumar at the earliest.

Right under the Commandant's nose
The office of the Commandant of the Punjab Armed Police, Surinder Pal Singh, is located in the same complex. But he confesses ignorance. "I joined duty here just a few months ago and am unaware of the developments. But I'm sure that prior permission of the Chandigarh Administration must have been taken if a certain area has been cordoned off," he said.

Heading: Blood transfusion: Experts stress extensive research for better results - Indian Express
Content:
With Kharar all set to elect its new municipal council on Sunday, the top brass of the ruling Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD)-Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) combine is taking a personal interest in these elections.

The top leaders of the SAD, including president Sukhbir Badal, have been closely following the election related activities.

In the fray are 69 candidates from 15 wards. The total electorate strength is 29,873, including 15,474 males and 14,399 females. With only the Congress contesting openly on its party symbol "Hand", the SAD-BJP combine nominees are using "Rising Sun" symbol from all wards. While both the SAD-BJP alliance and the Congress maintain that the results of these elections would not reflect on their popularity in the township, the elections strategies of both speak otherwise.

The final rehearsal by the election staff was, meanwhile, held at Government Polytechnic Institute in Khoonimajra village on Saturday. It was followed by the distribution of election material and dispatch of polling parties to their respective destinations.

For the Kharar residents, this is the first time they will be using the electronic voting machines (EVMs) to elect their municipal councillors.

Security Check
Kharar SDM Rajeev Kumar Gupta, who is the Returning Officer, claimed to have made full proof arrangements to ensure free, fair and peaceful polling and counting.

A total of 150 employees of different government departments will man the 30 polling booths with each booth having a Presiding Officer, an Assistant Presiding Officer and 3 polling officers. Reserve group of polling officials has also been kept for alternate arrangements in case of emergency.

A team headed by an NGO and comprising head constable and 3 constables, will be on security duty at each polling station. Nine special checkpoints have been set up on the entry and exit points while 5 special patrolling parties will cover 6 booths each during the polling and counting process.

Mohali SP (Detective) will be overall incharge of security arrangements while the Kharar DSP will assist him.

While all 7 general category wards having been identified as sensitive, the 8 wards reserved for different categories are in normal category, said Kharar DSP Rajbalwinder Singh Mrar while speaking to Newsline.

On poll eve: township dons a festive look
It was a festive scene with over a hundred men gathered outside the election office of a candidate from Ward 1 in the township, on poll eve for the Municipal Council elections.

A langar was in progress as some of those who had taken liquor were having food, while others were waiting for their share to arrive.

"They have already exhausted ten cases of whisky and more are expected to arrive soon," said a mechanic Ramesh while attending a langar orgainsed there.

A vendor who had parked his rehri opposite the office was jubilant with his sales showing a phenomenal increase. Asked about the strict enforced rules, Raju quipped: "Kya kar lenge, kafi maal to pehle hi aa gaya hai (What can they do now? Enough stock as already arrived.)"

Candidates, who till last evening were seen engaging senior leaders for campaining, today rushed from door-to-door canvassing till midnight.

Heated discussions were a common phenomenon at almost all public places as processions by supporters of candidates marked the poll eve.

Prestige of three stalwarts at stake
Apart from political and social prestige, a lot is at stake for three stalwarts who are backing the 69 candidates in the fray for the 15 wards of the Kharar Municipal

Council.

Punjab Cooperation Minister and ruling SAD general secretary Capt Kanwaljit Singh, Kharar Congress MLA Balbir Sidhu and Independent MLA from Chamkaur Sahib Charanjit Singh have worked overtime to muster support for their respective candidates.

While Capt Kanwaljit and Charanjit have joined hands to field the SAD-BJP combine candidates from all wards on the "Rising Sun" symbol, Sidhu has gone ahead alone to field all his candidates on the Congress party's election symbol "Hand".

While no former MC president or other senior political leader is in the poll fray, most of the first timers were relying on the support of their political mentors.

Heading: Sector 15:Cars, cars everywhere, but not a place to park - Indian Express
Content:
A two-day national workshop on blood transfusion, organised by the department of transfusion medicine, started at the PGI on Saturday. Director PGI Professor K K Talwar inaugurated the workshop. Dr Talwar stressed on the need for increasing research activities in the field of Transfusion Medicine and creating and retaining manpower in the field.

Nearly 250 delegates and eminent personalities from various states — Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Uttranchal, Jammu and Kashmir and Delhi — participated in the workshop.

The organising chairperson Professor Neelam Marwaha said, "Though there are economic and technical challenges in Nucleic Acid Testing (NAT) for our country, the overall reduction in 'window period' by early detection of the above agents will make blood safer for the patients."

Dr R N Makroo spoke on the need of consent by the patient prior to transfusion of blood or components in the present scenario of litigation.

Dr R R Sharma discussed the timely role of transfusion services in providing the right dose of appropriate components in life-threatening bleeding situations either due to trauma, obstetric haemorrhage or during various surgeries.

Heading: Declare Ravinder Singh proclaimed offender: CBI to court - Indian Express
Content:
As the city jostles with the problem of inadequate parking space all over, residents of Sector 15 are also sailing in the same boat. The chaos created by haphazardly parked vehicles is haunting the residents.

Whether it is the market or the residential areas, instances of haphazardly parked vehicles persist everywhere. The problem intensifies when a mandi is set up every Wednesday. Several vehicles parked on either side of the road leaves little space for cars to navigate. J S Singh, a resident of the area says, "While each house has three to four cars, there is not enough space for parking even a single car. This causes chaos and the problem becomes more acute early in the morning or late at night when most of the people are returning home."

Another resident Isha said: "The authorities need to take some action soon. We had heard about a proposal to start community parking in the various sectors. It needs to be implemented at the earliest otherwise the situation could worsen."

Sonam, a resident of the area, says, "The sector has well-maintained parks which we appreciate. Cleanliness is also maintained. However, the streetlights on the inner roads do not function properly. During rains, the residents suffer as waterlogging takes place at several places. The problem needs to be addressed."

Councillor says
While the issue has been debated a number of times in the MC, no concrete solution has come up yet. Area councillor Anu Chatrath, however, said that there are various development plans for the sector. "The site of the mandi is likely to be shifted to the extension of the floral garden. The carpeting of the roads will also be done."

She adds, "The residents of the area have a community programme where they ensure the cleanliness of the back lanes. The programme will continue in the coming days."

Heading: Condom theft: Vending machines damaged, AIDS control panel seeks police help to handle situation - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) today moved an application in the court demanding permission to declare Ravinder Singh, an accused in the judge bribery case, as proclaimed offender.

The application was moved today in the court of Special CBI Judge Jagdeep Jain. Notices were issued to Ravinder Singh on the application filed by the CBI. The CBI has sought permission to declare Ravinder Singh a proclaimed offender since it has failed to arrest him till date. Ravinder Singh is wanted by the CBI as he is alleged to be the kingpin of the Judge-bribery case.

The CBI has also demanded that the property belonging to Ravinder Singh shall be attached by the court under Sections 82 and 83 of the CrPC. On the other hand, the four accused-former Additional Advocate General Sanjeev Bansal, Prakash Ram, Rajiv Gupta and Nirmal Singh-have been remanded in judicial custody till September 27.

The four were produced in the court in relation with the case. The defence counsel for Ravinder Singh has been directed to file a reply on his behalf by September 18.

The anticipatory bail application moved by Ravinder Singh will come up for hearing on September 16 in the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

Heading: Out of jail, Grant wants shelter home property back - Indian Express
Content:
The State Aids Control Society (SACS), Chandigarh has a tough task at hand as acts of vandalism have left a few of the condom vending machines in the city damaged.

Dr Vanita Gupta, SACS Chandigarh Director, while attending a seminar on the "Role of Police in prevention of HIV/AIDS" at the CRPF Headquarters, Hallomajra, expressed concern on the increasing acts of stealing and vandalism and has sought help from the police.

"Under the condom promotion campaign, we have installed condom vending machines at different locations of the city, so that people have easy access to these. But at some of the prominent locations, people have damaged and broken these machines and stolen the condoms. We require the assistance of the police to check these acts of vandalism," said Dr Gupta while highlighting the extent of the disease penetration in Chandigarh.

As many as 22 triple column condom vending machines have been installed in Chandigarh. They have been installed at key locations for easy availability. The officials have described the response to these vending machines as "good".

HIV/AIDS patients organise rally
A rally by the HIV / AIDS patients under the aegis of the Indian Network of Positive People (INPP) and Chandigarh Network of People Living with the HIV/AIDS (PLHA) was organised on Saturday. Nearly 100 HIV-infected people walked from the Sector 17 Plaza to Sector 10 Government Museum and Art Gallery, urging the authorities to address their problems. The representatives from different states had gathered since Friday for the annual general body meeting of the INPP. Their aim was to strengthen the network base in the northern states of Punjab, Haryana, Himachal and Jammu and Kashmir.

Heading: Fresh focus on Ganpati immersion security after Delhi serial blasts - Indian Express
Content:
Leased Colaba property was taken over by a man using forged documents

British national Duncan Grant, who was acquitted in July by the Bombay High Court after being jailed for sexually exploiting children in shelter homes run by him, is seeking the return of his 'Anchorage Shelter Trust' in Colaba from a man alleged to have taken over the property using forged documents when he was in jail.

The Anchorage Shelter Trust house at 301, Colabawala Building, Shahid Bhagat Singh road, was leased by Grant and his Indian partner V Sangliraj in 1995 and it was used by Grant to house street children. The property was vacated and remained locked after he, along with fellow Briton Alan Waters and their Indian colleague William D'Souza, were convicted by a city court. But the tenancy apparently remained with Grant.

However, earlier this year, a man identified as Vivekananda Uphaday allegedly broke open the doors and occupied the place. In April, the landlord of the building, Gulbanno Ahmedali Porbunderwala, from whom Grant had leased the property, lodged a complaint at Colaba Police Station against Uphaday, accusing him of cheating and criminal trespass.

Senior Police Inspector of Colaba Police Station, Deepak P Vishwasrao, said, "Acting on the complaint, police found that Uphaday had forged the signature of Grant on the registration documents and transferred the property to his name. He had also changed the electricity bill and household gas card in his name with the forged documents. So we arrested him under IPC Section 420 for cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property and Section 441 for criminal trespass. Presently the accused is out on bail."

Investigating Officer N Kakade said that since the property is under dispute, a report under Section 145 of the Criminal Procedure Code informing the court about the property details and the ownership was also filed. Uphaday could not be reached for comment but police said that he had told them that Grant had given him the property as he had helped him with his legal problems during the paedophilia trial.

On Thursday, Grant approached the metropolitan court seeking papers connected to Uphaday's case and a copy of the report filed by the police. Magistrate N Shrimangale asked Grant to prove his locus standi in the case as he was neither the complainant nor the accused.

Grant's lawyer Shekhar Bhandary told Newsline that, "Grant is the original tenant, he has the agreement papers and electricity bills in his name. Our aim is to vacate the property as the Colaba police has sealed it. We will move an application before the Colaba police station on Monday informing them that we are the original tenants and accordingly move an intervening application before the magistrate court, for getting our property back."

In March 2006, after a 15-month trial, the City Civil and Sessions Court had convicted Grant, Waters and D'Souza for sexually exploiting children and ordered the British nationals to pay a fine of 20,000 pounds each. While the Britons were sentenced to six years rigorous imprisonment, D'Souza was sentenced to three years. However, the Bombay High Court acquitted them on July 23 saying there was not enough evidence against them. They were released from Nagpur jail, where they were lodged, about a week later.

Heading: Sena take on Prasad remark: Poor hold over Hindi, let police speak Marathi - Indian Express
Content:
Vigil stepped up, 20,000 cops to guard city streets; NSG units, bomb squads will be on duty

With the serial bomb blasts in Delhi coming on the eve of Ganpati visarjan, perhaps the financial capital's biggest annual event, the challenge of providing security to Sunday's immersions came under fresh focus today as Maharashtra Police sounded an alert minutes after the bombings in the national capital.

Vigil was stepped up across Mumbai and traffic slowed down as vehicles were checked on arterial roads. Particular attention was being given to areas near the immersion sites. "We will be conducting many security checks tomorrow across the city and we request citizens to be patient and bear with us and co-operate when such checks take place," Mumbai Police Commissioner Hassan Gafoor told Newsline.

Officials said that a total of 20,000 policemen and women would be guarding the streets of Mumbai on Sunday along with 1,600 traffic policemen besides units from the National Security Guard (NSG) and bomb detection and disposal teams.

Gafoor said that Mumbai Police has been regularly sensitising Ganpati mandal committees on security arrangements and a detailed security plan had been made for the city for the immersion day this year. "The field officers have been briefed on the screening and the checks to be conducted at various sensitive places. We will also have our anti-sabotage teams across the city and their priority also includes checking vehicles in which idols will be taken for immersion," he said.

"The traffic wing has also been asked to ensure that vehicles are not parked at sensitive places or at crowded junctions. The other teams already on the streets and in sensitive areas are men from the state CID and Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad and Home Guards."

Mumbai Police have erected five control rooms and 37 watch towers across the city to control traffic on Sunday. They have also installed 81 CCTV cameras along important visarjan routes, four of them on the Lalbaugcha Raja route alone. Main roads leading to the immersion sites of Girgaum Chowpatty, Dadar Chowpatty, Juhu Beach and Versova will remain closed for traffic.

Cars without Ganesh idols will not be allowed to enter beaches and firecrackers will not be allowed.

Heading: Four months on, Grover murder still haunts Susairaj’s building - Indian Express
Content:
The Shiv Sena has once again latched on to a controversy triggered by the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena of breakaway leader Raj Thackeray. Days after Raj slammed Mumbai Joint Commissioner of Police (Law and Order) K L Prasad for saying that Mumbai was not anyone's father's property, the Shiv Sena mouthpiece Saamna today called the top officer's comments "outrageous" and mocked at his command over Hindi.

Prasad had made the remark while briefing the media on the recent agitation by the MNS against the Bachchans, following Jaya Bachchan's supposedly "anti-marathi" comments at a Bollywood event. In his scathing response, Raj had challenged Prasad to take off his uniform and come on to the streets of Mumbai to find out to whom the city belonged.

On Saturday, a Saamna editorial said that no police officer in Mumbai had made such a statement in the past. It speculated that the officer's Hindi could be poor, resulting in the use of wrong words and demanded the government to instruct all police officers to address press conferences only in Marathi. "These people spend their whole life in Maharashtra and refuse to learn or speak Marathi. This is unacceptable," the editorial said. The editorial also came down strongly on talk of separating Mumbai from Maharashtra and asserted that only Maharashtrians had rights over the city and the Shiv Sena would continue to fight for this.

Saamna said, "Those who want to know about the fatherhood of Mumbai should visit the Hutatma Smarak in Fort area bearing testimony to the supreme sacrifice made by 105 Maharashtrians during the Samyukta Maharashtra agitation that kept the umbilical cord of Mumbai with the state intact."

Citing the historical role of Shivaji, the editorial said that those who tried to hurt and insult Maharashtra in the past had bitten dust. It also quoted former Maharashtra Chief Minister V P Naik as saying, "Maharashtrians do not get angry even if you do not favour him. But you are sure to antagonise them and make them your enemy if you hurt their self-respect." Naik was the longest serving Congress Chief Minister of Maharashtra, lasting 13 years, it pointed out.

Prasad did not react to Raj Thackeray's comments and was not available on Saturday to respond to the editorial either. (with PTI inputs)

Heading: Rlys to restore heritage steam engines, one will chug on Neral-Matheran track - Indian Express
Content:
Two tenants have vacated, others taking measures to keep controversies at bay and step up security

It is nearly four months since small-time Kannada actor Mariah Susairaj was arrested in connection with the murder of television executive Neeraj Grover and with the gruesome incident gradually disappearing from the front pages, the apartment building where it took place was expected to have moved on as well.

But the story at Dheeraj Solitaire in Malad is quite the contrary. While two tenants have vacated the new building after the incident apparently due to its "image" since the gruesome murder, other residents are adopting desperate measures to keep controversies at bay and step up security while landlords have become extremely cautious in choosing new tenants, residents and realty agents told Newsline.

Grover, a creative head at Synergy Adlabs, was allegedly stabbed to death by Susairaj's friend and naval officer Emile Jerome Mathew in her flat on May 8. The duo is then believed to have cut his body into several pieces and disposed it in the jungles of Manor in Thane. Susairaj, 27, and Jerome are both in judicial custody since their arrest on May 21.

"After the incident, flat owners are sceptical to lease their flats to young single people, especially those who aspire to be a part of the glamour world," said Rajesh Yadav, a real estate agent who has brokered a couple of deals in the building. "Paperwork is now considered a necessity rather than a formality as tenants are handed the keys to the flat only after they provide detailed documents proving their identity."

"Our business has obviously suffered as now owners prefer to keep their flats locked than lease it out fearing new tenants. They are willing to forego the money they would earn as rent rather than risk keeping tenants who could rake up controversies," he added.

Craig Fernandes, a resident of the building who also dabbles in real estate, says he tried to lease his flat as a service apartment to expatriates posted in the city but was unsuccessful as the reputation of the building discouraged potential tenants.

"Clients feel that the Susairaj case also reflects on the building's security, and moreover, companies are unwilling to let employees stay in a building where a murder is being investigated," said Fernandes.

Residents said that the floor on which Susairaj lived in apartment number 201 has been largely deserted since the incident. "Flats 201 and 202 are owned by the same person, and after the police sealed 201, the tenants of 202 also moved out. The tenants of two other flats on the floor also vacated it within a fortnight of the incident. However, two of the flats will be occupied soon," said Bimal Kumar, the building's supervisor. Susairaj's landlord is said to live abroad and could not be reached for comment.

Besides elaborately questioning new tenants, apartment owners have also formed an association which takes decisions about the safety of residents. "As the building is just over a year old, we are yet to form and register a co-operative society. However, after the incident we have formed an ad-hoc committee to address the residents' grievances," said Fernandes.

"After the Susairaj case, residents have unanimously demanded more security personnel from the builder and stressed that the credentials of the housekeeping staff be thoroughly checked. One of the two entrances to the building has been cordoned off and the sole entrance has several security guards to ensure better security," he added.

Heading: BMC makes arrangements in  hospitals for Ganesh visarjan - Indian Express
Content:
Central Railway (CR) has decided to bring back the glory of steam engines, which served the railways several years ago. In the wake of the CR's decision, work has already started at the Parel workshop. Work on a narrow gauge engine, which was one of the four engines purchased from Germany, to be run between Neral and Matheran, is on in full swing at the workshop. The engine made its maiden trip more than 100 years ago.

An official from CR said, "It will take time to complete the work. Tubes have been taken out to replace with new tubules. Apart from this, many components and parts are being taken out from the engine at Matheran station to place them on this engine." H V Kulkarni, Assistant works manager, is supervising the work at the workshop. JN Lal Divisional Railway Manager, Mumbai Division, Central Railway informed, "This steam engine has its historical value, so it is being repaired for ceremonial purpose. It will be run on mini railway ( Neral- Matheran ) occasionally." According to railway records, these narrow gauge steam engines (7-38,7-39,7-40, 7-41) were bought from a German firm, Orenstein and Koppel. Between 1907 and 1982, steam engines used to run on the Neral- Matheran mini rail. However, in 1983, these were phased out. From 1987 to 1992, by order of the General manager, Central railway, 7-38 engine was put under the statue of Lady of Progress at the main gate of Chatrapatti Shivaji Terminus. After that, it was sent to the Parel workshop. Steam engine was sent to National museum of Railway, Delhi. Engine 7- 41 is placed as a showpiece at Matheran station. BL Patil, Chief works Manager, said, "It is very difficult to forecast the time of its completion as it is more than 100 years old so its components are also very old and hence unavailable. But work is on in full swing. A team of 12-13 staff is working day and night on it. As old staff members who knew about steam engines have retired, staff which has knowledge about steam engines has been called from Bhusaval. We are working as per the directives of Indian railways which is more interested in preserving the heritage of the railways."

In fact an interesting story about engine 7-38 finds a mention in the book 'Unforgettable on Matheran Hills'. The books says that Abdul Hussain Peerbhoy visited Germany to negotiate prices for buying engines from Orenstein and Koppel. Peerbhoy travelled on 7-38, when it made its maiden trip. He travelled with the driver and two attendants to prove both the safety of the railway and the capability of the engine. Despite being warned on grounds of personal safety, Hussain still boarded the engine. He said that the lives of the driver and the two attendants were as precious as his own. All along the track from Neral to Matheran workers remained apprehensive and ready for any unforeseen eventuality. The engine however, slowly and steadily chugged its ways to Matheran. As the news of Abdul Hussain's safe arrival was conveyed to his father, Sir Adamji Peerbhoy, he broke down into tears of joy. Ali Akbar Peerbhoy, great grandson of Adamji Peerbhoy is happy with the decision of CR. He says, " It will a be great pleasure for me and my family members to see steam engine- purchased by our fore-fathers- running on tracks of Neral and Matheran." While three of the other engines have become showpieces, 7-40 which was sold to England and is still operational, It pulls passenger cars along the four mile, Leighton-Buzzard railway in Britain.

Heading: MNS activists released on bail - Indian Express
Content:
Doctors at 3 major civic hospitals are gearing up to deal with patients with multiple injuries

The three major civic run hospitals are gearing up for the Ganesh visarjan on Sunday with doctors expecting patients with multiple injuries. With instances of enthusiasts, first timers and even non-swimmers venturing out into the sea to immerse their idols without realizing the risk involved, hospitals have made arrangements to tend to the injured. Apart from separate beds designated for people coming with injuries, X-ray departments in these hospitals including the X-ray department in KEM hospital which is otherwise shut on Sundays, will function till late in the night.

A total of 65 ambulances from hospitals and few other trust run ambulances will be stationed at the visarjan spots including the big sites like Girgaum, Juhu, Varsova and Marve beaches. "There will be one doctor and one nurse in each ambulance," said Dr Jairaj Thanekar, executive health officer, BMC.

"We have stationed two ambulances at Girgaum chowpatty to tend to those seriously injured. For those who need first aid treatment, medical booths have been set up at different immersion spots," said Dr Sanjay Oak, dean Nair hospital. A total of 65 medical booths with medication, IV fluids and medicines have also been set up.

Doctors from the orthopedic and general surgical section have been told to be on standby at R N Cooper hospital, B Y L Nair hospital, and KEM hospital. A minimum of five beds has been kept reserved in each hospital to treat casualties during visarjan. Apart from ambulances, BMC has also arranged for fire extinguishers, motorboats, lifeguards and volunteers to ensure a smooth visarjan process.

Heading: At Gaffar, Express staffers hear the blast - Indian Express
Content: Six MNS activists who were arrested on September 11 from Borivali (West) by the MHB Colony Police for their participation in the anti-Jaya Bachchan demonstration in Dahisar on September 10 have been released on bail. One of them, Deepak Aarey (33), is a Shakha Pramukh and the others have been identified as Santosh Vare (25), Lalchand Maurya (26), Sandeep Kamble (28), Vinod Kadam (26) and Sahdev Joshi (45).

Heading: Ragpickers help deter blasts six, seven at India Gate, Regal Cinema - Indian Express
Content:
Engrossed in bargaining for footwear at Gaffar Market in Karol Bagh, we suddenly heard this loud noise.

It took us a few minutes to register what exactly was happening around us.

Pushing our way through the crowd to reach the spot, we saw two mutilated bodies being taken in a cart.

With police struggling to cordon off the area, the crowd surged with the arrival of ambulances, fire brigades and mediapersons.

Next, we headed for Jassa Ram Hospital, where most injured victims were taken. Soon, officials there put up a list of those admitted in the hospital. The irony? The list was in

English, a language most victims' relatives could not comprehend. The absence of a translator just made it a few notches worse.

As we made our way out of the hospital, there was Basanti, about 50 and grandmother of two-year-old Kishan, the first to be declared dead at Jassa Ram Hospital. The evening's images imprinted on our mind, and Basanti's cries still echoing in our ears, we made our way from Ghaffar Market.

Heading: West side story - Indian Express
Content:
It was a couple of street urchins who saved the Capital from two more blasts that would have occurred at India Gate and Regal Cinema. While the police made courtesy patrols at the high-alert zone at India Gate, they remained oblivious to the bomb ticking away in a dustbin.

Ten-year-old Ravi, a regular ragpicker at the busy tourist spot, fished it out with trembling hands. Knowing full well that for once he had found something of value, Ravi called for his uncle Vinod Krishna, a sweeper, to inspect the device and then called for help.

"I could see it was a bomb — it had wires dangling from it. I was the first to see it," said Ravi, who accompanies his uncle every day from Nizamuddin. "Uncle told me to take it to a deserted side of the park. Then he called the constables who were patrolling the area and the bomb was defused," he added, hardly able to believe he actually saved so many lives. The bustling area was evacuated within minutes of the detection of the bomb.

Live bombs were also found in a dustbin at Regal Cinema and at Central Park in Connaught Place. Another ragpicker found the bomb at the cinema hall, wrapped in a black polybag, and informed beat constable Suresh. Suresh, who tried removing the wires, luckily managed to defuse the bomb without expert help.

Sub-inspector Rajesh Kumar Maurya, who was patrolling India Gate, said, "The bomb detected here looked exactly like the ones that were found in Surat. We found it at around 7.30 pm and began evacuating the people from the spot, which was cordoned off for further inspection. Had the bomb exploded here, it would have been a shame for the police."

"The first unexploded bomb was recovered near India Gate, while the one at Regal Cinema was found soon after," said Ajay Kashyap, Joint Commissioner of Police.

Sniffer dogs and policemen with metal detectors were deployed to scan the sites. National Security Guard experts on explosives were also rushed to vulnerable spots. The ragpickers who saved the day were taken aside by the police for further questioning.

Heading: Feast for the senses - Indian Express
Content:
A slew of fashion shows across the world see Indian designers headed west

With the New York Fashion Week getting over on Friday and the London Fashion Week starting this week, the fashion season has kicked off across the globe with a bang. Big events like the Paris Fashion Week are scheduled for the end of the month. If that's keeping the likes of Anamika Khanna, Manish Arora and Rajesh Pratap Singh busy, there's more happening over the next couple of weeks to keep everyone on their toes. Here's a lowdown on who is headed where in the world from the Indian contingent:

Ravi Bajaj
In his career spanning well over a decade, designer Ravi Bajaj has always kept well away from the Indian fashion weeks. However, it seems Bajaj is more than game to put up a show abroad. The Delhi designer will be showcasing eight collections comprising 65 ensembles at a show at Los Angeles' swanky Hilton Hotel today. With a bunch of American models and a guest list of about 250, Bajaj is all set to give his NRI clients a taste of home-grown fashion with his latest coup: a poncho sari. "For many NRIs, the sari is something immensely attractive though they cannot wear it properly. I have taken that into account for this collection," he says. Post the show in LA, Bajaj will then head to Dubai and Jakarta over the next six weeks for further shows and exhibitions.

Renu Tandon
Come October and Delhi designer Renu Tandon will head to Dubai for her maiden appearance at the Dubai Fashion Week scheduled between October 5-9. Tandon has been invited by Dubai-based fashion boutique, Mumbai Se, to showcase her label Mynah. The designer known for her high-bling quotient is quite popular with the NRIs and had recently been invited to Singapore for an exhibition by the local Sindhi Association. In Dubai, though, her show on October 7 would be sponsored by the company Red Sea Housing Services.

Rina Dhaka
Her beach collection with its abbreviated bikini tops and patchwork thongs had created a furore at a desi fashion week appearance a couple of years back, but Delhi designer Rina Dhaka has mellowed down since. This season, Dhaka is headed for London Fashion Week to take part in the exhibition there. The exhibition, LFW's official showcase of talents from across the world has over 210 designers participating.

Samant Chauhan
A young designer, Chauhan has already carved a niche for himself in the industry. After an outing at the London Fashion Week last season he will now be seen at the Ethical Fashion Show in Paris, promoting fair trade practices and eco-friendly materials. Then there's the Tranoi Fair in Paris before he turns homeward for the India Fashion Week. His new collection will see his take on indigenous fabric.

Heading: Blast after blast - Indian Express
Content:
For several new restaurants in the city, the food plate looks like an artist's canvas

A simple smoked duck salad at the European diner Manre attempts the unusual. It is served as a beautifully sculpted portion, the paper-thin sheets of smoked duck neatly stacked over a bed of pok choi with a light drizzle of peanut sauce dressing and a sliver of caramelised orange delicately perched on top. Restaurants, till recently, garnished their spaghetti with piles of parsley, laid down meats over herb-flecked risotto and everything arrived with a drizzle of pesto. Today, chefs cast a beady eye over the finer points of food presentation and the aesthetics of the plate now involve drafting the right colour scheme and delicately sculpting a dish before it reaches your table.

"A dish must appeal to the eyes first. The right presentation can whet your appetite even before you taste the food," says chef Anil Mohan of The Oak Tree in Gurgaon. "Earlier, dishes were decorated with loads of grilled tomatoes that would come back to the kitchen uneaten. We now use a lot of tomato coulis and reductions like balsamic vinegar to add a new texture and flavour." Consider a watermelon salsa served with grilled vegetables, lamb chops served with grilled peach or pan-seared mangoes complimenting a fish fillet. These colourful fruits are integrated into main courses to add a new texture to the dish and perk up the flavour and colour.

Indian dishes, too, are getting a makeover. The tikki chaat or a masala sea bass at Varq, a contemporary Indian diner at Taj Mahal hotel, looks like a grand French treat. Similarly, at Varun Tuli's Chinese specialty diner The Yum Yum Tree, a regular steamed fish and tofu dish is transformed into a visual treat. "We stack the fish and tofu in layers and blanket it with black bean sauce. It adds a character to the dish and the flavours are intact," saysTuli. "We have to ensure that the garnishing is edible and often use the ingredients of the dish to bring out the visual appeal. The restaurant also uses aioli, a sauce made with garlic and olive oil, as a regular garnish in some of its dishes.

"A perfectly assembled dish is its own best advertisement. We experiment with a lot of imported vegetables to add a new character to the dish," says Vinay Kumar, executive chef at Qashqai that serves soups in bowls that resemble upturned hats.

Kula Naidu of Kayalan, which home delivers Malaysian food in fancy packaging agrees with Kumar, "Presentation is as important as the flavour of the dish." Even a simple Malaysian chilli chicken will arrive at your doorstep wrapped in banana sheets and packed in wooden boxes.

At The China Kitchen at Hyatt, the blue tableware is just a prelude to the exquisitely decorated food it will hold. "Food is more that a biological necessity. It is an art form that is meant to be savored. Most chefs are trained in turning the platters into things of beauty," says chef Marcus Mathyssek of Hyatt. Clearly, some works of art are good enough to eat.

Heading: Hospitals struggle with skeletal staff - Indian Express
Content:
Almost daring the terror men, Inner Circle goes on with business; Outer Circle shuts down, panics

In terror times, A world of two CPs

An invisible divide was at work in Connaught Place an hour after the two blasts in the area on Saturday evening. While the Outer Circle, near the site of the blast at Gopaldas Building, was dark with all shops downing shutters, with panic and a shade of lawlessness writ large, Inner Circle sported the look Delhiites associated with CP: some reassuring lights with many shops and eateries choosing to stay open.

The freshly renovated L-block stood like a beacon in the dark: couples and shoppers still moved around, with many lining up in front of restaurants and showrooms that decided to stay open. Shaken, but confidence not broken.

Model Town resident Gaurav Vashisht, with three-year-old son Chaitanya in tow, took the Metro from Vishwavidyalaya and reached CP around 8 pm. Once there, he was reassured: "I wasn't here when the blast occurred. But this is not so different from the Connaught Place I know.

"I am not scared; I will continue to stay here and even visit some shops."

The first reaction at TGIF, a popular restaurant in Inner Circle, was to down shutters after the blast that shook Central Park. Then, the management thought again. "Our customers said they felt safer inside the restaurant, that they didn't want to go outside," manager Subodh Mathur said. "Also, people wanted to have their meals. If some one wants to have a meal, they are welcome."

And even as the police reached the spot, students and couples continued their stroll — now almost a resolute vigil.

In contrast, chaos and panic seemed to rule Outer Circle. With shops shutting close almost immediately, the area was dark in no time flat. People, in groups, shouted for autorickshaws that refused to stop. With police barricading Barakhamba Road and all cellphone networks shut down due to congestion, it looked like a mad scramble as worried shoppers tried to leave the area at the earliest.

On Inner Circle, autorickshaw driver Ramanuddin said he would go "anywhere customers want to go". Gaurav Yadav, another auto driver waiting nearby, echoed the sentiments.

In the end, it's those who are alive who matter, said May Lindgren, 62, visiting India and staying at a hotel in CP. "We were in a beauty parlour in Inner Circle when we heard the blasts. I heard one close by, and the other a little further away," said Lindgren, accompanied by friend Annette Alvin, 42. "Hearing the sound I told my friends it was a blast, and they were still laughing at me. I have stayed in Afghanistan and I knew it wasn't such a big blast since no windows broke.

"In the end we have to count our blessings — we are not panicking and running away because it's important to be normal."

Post-conversation, the two went back to what they were doing: chatting with a vendor selling cheap dark glasses. In the end, it was the indomitable CP spirit that survived.

Heading: Anuj Chauhan dies, friends block road protesting police inaction - Indian Express
Content:
At 11.07 pm, a good three hours after the blasts, the only neurosurgeon in Delhi's biggest government hospital, Dr PN Pandey, of Lok Nayak was at home. Worse, he did not know how many patients had been taken to Lok Nayak hospital or the kind of care they needed. The serial blasts brought to the fore the lack of preparedness of the Capital's hospitals once again. For victims and families, lack of information from hospitals, shortage of blood, skeletal staff and absence of trauma specialists — especially neurosurgeons — made the blasts even more deadly.

Most emergency medical care provided in Delhi's government hospital on Saturday night was by interns, resident doctors and general surgeons.

As far as the availability of drugs is concerned, at LHMC 50 students donated blood to meet the demand, while Indian Red Cross Society has offered 150 units of blood to hospitals that may face shortage.

Hospitals in the Capital had to cope with rushing ambulances, tense doctors and wailing family members.

At the AIIMS Trauma Centre, attendants in green gowns and gloves waited outside with stretchers to accommodate patients.

Entries were barricaded at AIIMS, to avoid any untoward incident that could jeopardise the safety of the institute.

The inmates themselves were, however, safe with minor injuries, informed hospital attendants.

While the Emergency ward of the hospital had two male victims, the trauma centre had three.

Family members and relatives complained that they could not find their relatives. Some were not even allowed inside to check on their near and dear ones.

Relatives of Rajni Gupta, 42, who died of the blasts, and was brought to Ganga Ram Hospital said hospital authorities stopped them from entering.

"We have been asked to stay out. Only Rajni's husband is inside," said the brother of the victim.

Heading: Uphaar Tragedy: HC judge to hear appeals of Ansals - Indian Express
Content:
For family and friends of 25-year-old Anuj Aditya Chauhan, Saturday morning brought news they had been dreading to hear at the AIIMS Trauma Centre. Anuj in a coma, in the ICU for the last two days, breathed his last.

Anger spilled on to the streets as Anuj's friends protested police inaction.

Mrigank Srivastav (29), who was also injured in the accident, is still in hospital. One of Anuj's closest friends, Mrigank inquires about him whenever he regains consciousness. He has not been informed of his death as his condition is critical. "He won't be able to take it. He is in great pain since yesterday. Whenever he opens his eyes, he asks for Anuj," said Rahul Gupta, a close family friend.

Anuj died around 4.30 am. While family members had been waiting at the hospital, around 50 of his friends, most of them journalists, reached the hospital. Kshitij, Anuj's elder brother, fainted on hearing the news.

Not satisfied with police action against BMW driver Utsav Bhasin (19), Anuj's friends and relatives blocked traffic on the road near Trauma Centre. They shouted slogans against Delhi police for late action and did not allow anyone to move.

"Had the accused been arrested within 24 hours, it could have been proved that he was drunk and was driving fast despite knowing he could kill someone. Police deliberately arrested him later," said Rahul. Anuj's friends moved from road only after police and senior members of the Chauhan family intervened. "We all are here because Anuj was a very good human being and a very intelligent person," said another friend Yatharth Patel.

Anuj was pursuing an animation course from Maya Institute of Advanced Cinematics at South Extension. He had journalism background and always participated in interactive political debates. He had also recently joined Salsa classes. "He had varied interests and wanted to prove himself in journalism," said Yatharth. Anuj was also working on some documentaries. The post mortem was conducted around 11.30 am and the body was handed over to the family. The family took the body to their Ghaziabad house from where they went to Garhmukteshwar for cremation in the evening. His inconsolable father said, "I don't know what will we do without him."

Anuj was in coma since Thursday when he was taken to hospital in the early hours after he and Mrigank were hit by a BMW car in Lajpat Nagar.

Heading: Six-year-old found dead in school water tank in Uttam Nagar - Indian Express
Content:
Following the Supreme Court decision to assign an "appropriate" court to hear the Uphaar Fire Tragedy case, the Delhi High Court Chief Justice A P Shah has moved the appeal hearings in the matter to Justice S Ravinder Bhat.

Justice Bhat, a judge with the High Court, will hear the appeals of Gopal and Sushil Ansal, along with those of their ex-staffers and co-accused, on a day-to-day basis from Monday (September 15).

The trial court had on November, 20, 2007 convicted the Ansal brothers along with three others under Section 304-A IPC (causing death due to rash and negligent act) and had sentenced them to two years' imprisonment.

Seven others, including Ajit Chowdhary and Nirmal Chopra, managers of the theatre, were convicted under Section 304 IPC (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) and sentenced to seven years' imprisonment.

Others convicted under section 304 IPC were - Radha Krishan Sharma, Manmohan Unniyal (cinema's gatekeeper), Brij Mohan Satija, A K Gera and Bir Singh (all DVB officials). The High Court, on January 4, had granted bail to the Ansal brothers and two other accused.

Justice H R Malhotra of the Delhi High Court had been hearing the appeals since February, 2008.

Heading: Women rush at JNU makes hostels dearer - Indian Express
Content:
A six-and-a-half year old boy was found dead in the water tank of his school under mysterious circumstances in Uttam Nagar area of west district on Saturday afternoon. The victim, Vibhuti Nath Sharma, had been missing since Friday and his parents had lodged a complaint with the police on Friday evening.

According to the police, acting on the basis of the missing complaint, they asked the school authorities to search the school premises. "As he went missing from school, we had asked the school administration to thoroughly search the school. On Saturday afternoon his decomposed body was found in the water tank near the toilet," a senior police officer said.

Vibhuti was a student of class II at Central School, Hastsal Vohar and lived at flat number 16, pocket 7, DDA Janta flats in Naseerpur, Dwarka. Vibhuti's father, who works as an assistant with the DRDO, had approached the police with the missing complaint at about 6 pm on Friday. Meanwhile, the police are further investigating the case from every possible angle.

"We are not able fathom as to how and why the boy went up to the tank. We are questioning the school authorities in connection with the incident too," a senior police officer said.

Heading: Protection officer seeks security on the job - Indian Express
Content:
A Policy of affirmative action for admitting more women students has resulted in an "unusual" increase in the number of women at the Jawaharlal Nehru University. Women students, however, are taking the news with a pinch of salt as the increased numbers have led to a space crunch in the hostels.

As a result, many are forced to share rooms.

"This is the first time that five rebate points have been given to all girl students, resulting in an increase in the number of girl students this year," deputy registrar (admissions) D Tekchandani said.

University figures how 1,174 students out of a total 1,545 applicants for hostel accommodation have so far been allotted hostels. The break-up shows 83 per cent of male students have got accommodation, compared to 67 per cent of women students who have been successful.

JNU has three hostels for women, four for men, four "mixed hostels" and a hostel for married scholars.

But the shortage for rooms for women has meant the university authorities are resorting to alternative provisions. These include accommodating women students at a temporary dormitory in Chandrabhaga Hostel and allowing new students to share rooms with those already allotted hostel rooms.

But even such emergency steps are not adequate to solve the problem, students said. Ning, an MPhil student, said: "I was allotted hostel. But since there were no rooms available, I was put on the waiting list." For now, she has to do with sharing a room with an acquaintance as the third roommate.

Dean of Students' Welfare V K Jain said a new hostel, Koyna, would be ready by this December, or latest by next January. The hostel is slated to accommodate 544 students.

Heading: Cowboy hats all the rage, at least for this street vendor - Indian Express
Content:
A recent incident of violence against a protection officer, who was assisting a victim of domestic violence, has opened a floodgate of grievances by other women officers. They now want protection before they go out to perform their duties as per court orders.

Protection officers are appointed by the Social Welfare department for assisting the courts in dealing with complaints of domestic violence. They are required to help victims in proceeding with the case, while simultaneously aiding the courts by filing the necessary reports relating to the matter at hand.

During a recent hearing before Metropolitan Magistrate Sanatan Prasad at the Rohini courts, Kiran, an official from the Northwest district, expressed her apprehensions when asked as to why she had not complied with a previous order. She had earlier been directed by the court to ascertain the means of income of one Vinay, husband of complainant Meenakshi, who had allegedly faced physical violence at the hands of the former.

Kiran told the magistrate that it was difficult for her to go ahead with the court's direction in the wake of several incidents of violence against protection officers, one of which was also reported in the media.

She said it was unsafe for her to go to the house of the accused as per the order, unless government authorities made arrangements for her safety. The officer referred to a recent incident, in which Protection Officer Parmesh Tokas was assaulted by five women, when she went to a house in Kishangarh to serve court summons.

After giving her a patient hearing, the magistrate told the officer that it was "not logical" to decide against complying with the court's orders on the grounds that she would not act until the government takes action. The court, however, also told Kiran it could understand her apprehensions very well and was competent to redress her immediate fears.

"The officers are entitled to physical protection while serving the summons and executing other processes," the magistrate said, asking Kiran to seek the help of the police whenever required.

Prasad then issued directions to the SHO, Mangolpuri, seeking the provision of necessary assistance and protection to the officer on her request.

Another protection officer, on condition of anonymity, told Newsline that she had requested a magistrate to appoint some other protection officer after she was threatened with dire consequence when she tried to help a complainant collect her clothes and articles from the house of her husband.

When her plea was turned down, she also sought protection before executing the court's process. "We have frequently been writing to the department regarding the problem but we have received no response till date," she said.

Heading: After error in marksheet, DU Maths student takes RTI route - Indian Express
Content:
If you have always fancied the 'Wild West' look and just needed the right accessories, look no further than your nearest traffic intersection

Drive past the ITO traffic intersection, going towards the Laxmi Nagar crossing, and you will be able to buy yourself a swanky felt cowboy hat. Pitched at Rs 300, with decent bargaining skills, you can get them for a tidy sum of Rs 150 or less. The hats are available in light beige, shades of brown, black and white.

The simplicity of the hats is their unique selling point. The only pattern is stars woven on either side, with shoelaces acting as a strap to hold the hat in place.

Twenty-year-old Satish may be oblivious to the name of the hats he sells at the intersection but the Rs 1,500 he earns from daily sales are rewarding enough. "Many people drive up to me and enquire about the hats. I sell more than a dozen daily. Someone asked me to get these hats due to the scorching heat and I started selling them at the traffic light. In no time, I was making a profit," he says.

Satish was selling colourful children's books at the same intersection earlier. His brothers also assist him in selling the hats at the intersection.

He buys 20 to 25 hats from wholesalers in Sadar Bazaar at Rs 125 each. He says he makes a bigger profit selling the hats, as compared to children's books. "I am able to have a decent meal every day now," he says.

What will he do once the winter sets in? "These big hats are a fashion statement. And no matter what the season, people can always wear them," he says, vowing not to sell children's books any more.

Heading: Security in hospitals tightened - Indian Express
Content:
The marksheet for the annual examination was anything but normal for Niju K Ram, a post-graduation student of Mathematics at Delhi University's Zakir Hussain College. Issued last month, the marksheet allotted him, and all his classmates, scores in 'Differential Geometry', instead of 'Calculus' that they had studied the whole year.

The problem: Differential Geometry was a subject removed from the MA-Mathematics syllabus three years ago.

After complaints to the mathematics department failed to generate any result, Ram filed an RTI with the university on Tuesday. "We studied Calculus the whole year but the subjects were changed for the entire class in the annual marksheet," he said.

Though Ram's classmates confirmed the mistake, none of them were willing to come on record.

Ram, however, wants an answer for the goof-up: "I had to ask the university how they could have made a mistake in the marksheets, and why they have not corrected it yet."

Ram, who graduated from Delhi University, said authorities at the mathematics department asked him to take his complaint to the Dean of Examination's office. But Ram said he does not want to knock "on different doors": "It is the university's mistake, so they should be offering to correct it. I should not have to pay for their negligence."

M L Singla, the Dean of Examination at DU, said: "Computers cannot (always) ensure mistake-free marksheets. We cannot always be right on the computer."

He said the university would investigate the issue if an old subject had mistakenly been entered in this year's marksheet.

Heading: Blueline crushes two - Indian Express
Content:
After last month's blast at Ahmedabad's civil hospital that claimed 36 lives, the administration is taking no chances. Minutes after the serial blasts in the city, the administration sent orders to beef up security within and outside all hospitals.

"We have deployed security personnel around all hospitals and are checking all activity here, while the Delhi Police is monitoring all activity outside," said a security officer.

Police said all vehicles around the hospital were being checked. "While we are manning the entry to the hospital, security personnel have been asked to be on their toes round the clock. People are being checked and bags and suitcases searched," said a Delhi

Police officer.

"All vehicle movements around the hospital are being scrutinised and we are not letting anyone without a staff identity card enter the hospital beyond a certain point. Temporary barricades have been put up for the purpose," he added.

Heading: Air India staff, travel agent get 2-yr RI - Indian Express
Content: A speeding Blueline bus again took a killer turn as it crushed two people in Peera Garhi while trying to overtake another DTC bus on Friday night. The Blueline on route number 929, from Mubarakpur to Old Delhi, was speeding while the two men — Rajan Kumar (17) and Chandan Pande (22) — were standing near the bus door when the incident took place around 10:30 pm. The duo got crushed between the Blueline and the DTC bus. While the two victims died on the spot, the driver has fled with the Blueline.

Heading: 15 fresh dengue cases, takes total to 224 - Indian Express
Content: A suspended Air India traffic supervisor and a travel agent have been sentenced to two years' rigorous imprisonment by a Delhi court for duping the airlines of over Rs 35 lakh by forging and refunding tickets in a two-decade-old case. pecial CBI judge V K Maheshwari also imposed a fine of Rs 50,000 each on the suspended Air India employee Arun Kumar Maurya and agent S K Khosla after holding them guilty under Section 420 of the IPC and under various provisions of the Prevention of the Corruption Act.

Heading: On Saturday evening, all of Delhi turns a victim - Indian Express
Content:
Fifteen fresh cases of dengue were reported in the national capital on Saturday, taking the number of infected people to 224 this season.

As the number of cases head northwards, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) is faced with another problem: dealing with staff engaged in checking mosquito breeding who have gone off work demanding regularisation of jobs.

With September and October normally considered as peak months for the spread of dengue, the number of cases is expected to rise, civic officials said. However, they said there is no reason to panic as the outbreak is well within control and the disease will not break into epidemic proportions.

"While negotiations are on with the employees on strike, a new batch of breeding checkers will be brought into the field by Monday," MCD's public health committee chairman V K Monga said.

The onslaught of dengue has been more intense this year compared to last couple of years, a phenomenon attributed to the early arrival of monsoon and the high levels of humidity.

Heading: ‘Suddenly, there was a sound, thought it was an earthquake - Indian Express
Content:
At 6.34 pm, Zahid was the first injured victim of the serial blasts to be brought to RML Hospital. What followed was a deluge of victims from the blast spots at Gaffar Market and Central Park in CP, all seeking immediate medial attention.

Some of them writhed in pain while others, still conscious, were left in a daze.

The injury count went up to 76 by 8.30 pm. At 9.20 pm, neither hospital authorities nor the police had a list prepared to provide details to friends and family members waiting for information.

Newsline spoke to some victims inside, and some outside, also 'victims' seeking information.

PRADEEP RAJ had spoken to his 23-year-old nephew Harshit Vyas at 6.25 pm on phone when the latter was at Pizza Hut, near CP. Raj got the news of blast in 10 minutes, but by then the networks were jammed. "I was told that injured have been taken to RML, and I rushed in. But no one in the hospital could tell me whether Harshit was even admitted here."

Till 9.30 pm, there was no information. "I understand it is a difficult situation but we are neither allowed inside the wards nor do the staff provide any information."

THE evening seemed perfect for Vikas to catch up with the latest with friend Rahul, his classmate from JNU's Korean language department. A thud, and suddenly he saw Rahul writhing in pain ¿ "his back was hit by something". He soon realised it was a blast, and all he could see thereafter was Rahul being taken to the hospital.

Vikas also rushed to RML but despite a long wait and repeated attempts there was no news about his friend till 9.30 pm.

SATURDAY was supposed to be his day off, meant to be spent in front of the television. By evening, Mahender Prasad's weekly off had turned into a nightmare. Two of his brothers were missing and one was dead in the Karol Bagh blast.

The family earns a living by selling TV remote covers to shoppers in Karol Bagh.

Mahender's brother Ganga Prasad, 38, is one of the victims. "We work in shifts and my cousins were working while I was home," Mahender said. "Suddenly I heard an explosion. But I could not fathom what had happened — I realised the magnitude only after I came out."

Out there lay his brother, bleeding. "A PCR van took him to Lady Hardinge Medical College Hospital. But he died before reaching the hospital."

Mahender is now looking for his other brothers: Raju and Ramlal.

MOOLCHAND, 40, could never have thought the auto just ahead of him was carrying a bomb. Minutes later, admitted at Jassa Ram Hospital's general ward, Moolchand said, "I was in the auto next to the one carrying the bomb. I heard the explosion suddenly and my auto flew some 20 meters from the spot."

BHIKESH, also admitted in Jassa Ram Hospital, "only

remembers" the sound. "And then everyone started shouting." Employed with a marketing company, Bhikesh often visits Gaffar market.

 

NAND Kishore, who came back to the spot with a bandage on his head two hours after the blast, said: "The police should have arrived at the spot earlier. Initially, it was all down to the locals. There were scores of people around me seconds after the blast occurred."

A birthday gone horribly awry
IT was her birthday, and Saturday looked perfect for a family outing for Leena. By evening, she would much rather forget the day. Her younger brother Akhilesh, 19, was one of the injured victims of the blast at Central Park, Connaught Place. An engineering student, Akhilesh was near exit gate-1 of Palika Bazar, just leaving for India Gate to join his family for the birthday celebrations, when the blast occurred.
He suffered burn injuries and was admitted in RML Hospital. For Leena, though, it was an agonising wait for over three hours before she got any information. "I was not even sure whether Akhilesh was alive... Later a hospital employee took me to the emergency ward — there I saw Akhilesh." Leena had earlier lost a close friend in the Sarojini Nagar blasts in 2005.
— Ayesha Arvind

Heading: Relatives throng hospitals to meet victims - Indian Express
Content:
BARAKHAMBA ROAD
"IT was exactly 6.25 pm."
Jaspal Singh, an executive with Reliance Industries, was sitting on the 15th floor of Gopal Das Building when he heard the blast. He was with a friend and thought, at first, "it must be a high-intensity earthquake".
He looked — all hell had broken loose by then: "There was blood all over. And smoke."
The bomb was hidden in a garbage can outside the Metro station.
"I was across the road and suddenly there was this deafening sound, and then utter chaos," said Kishore Yadav, a parking attendant in the lane next to Oxford Bookstore adjoining Barakhamba Road Metro station. "There was an auto near the garbage can and I remember a lady sitting inside. There was lot of blood everywhere."
Yadav saw "at least five people injured — they were taken to RML and Lok Nayak hospitals".
Eyewitness accounts suggest at least two persons, a priest and a woman, were killed.
As police vans started arriving, most shopkeepers began downing shutters. "We have just heard there has been another blast near Central Park, besides the ones at GK-I and Karol Bagh," said Sudhir Prasad, who sells juice next to the Metro station.

 

Central park
At 6.42 pm, Arun Kumar Gupta, who works in Palika Bazaar, was standing in front of the park when the explosion occurred. "There was blood all over — I saw a woman's stomach ripped apart; I and a few friends shifted her to the police van," Gupta said.
V K Jain, officer on duty in CATS who shifted the injured to hospitals, said many were serious: "My van took 16 people from CP."

Greater kailash
It was a typical weekend in the GK-I M-Block market. And the crowd was just beginning to pull in. Manoj Jain was inside his jewellery shop in front of M-29 when he heard the blast at 6.43 pm.
"I came out and saw people running all over the place," he said. "There was a lot of smoke coming out of the park. A couple of cars were damaged and glass from three different shops lay shattered on the ground. "Just then someone shouted on the public announcement speakers to assemble in the park. We all did."
That was when the second blast took place. Gireesh Kumar, employee at the Lewis showroom, said: "We downed shutters and stayed in after the first blast. Within minutes, we heard another — we opened the shutters and saw smoke from a dustbin some 100 meters ahead, in M-29."
After the mayhem, Kumar saw his Splendor motorbike, parked outside the showroom. It was damaged beyond repair.

 

Gaffar market, karol bagh
Saturday shopping turned into panic with the blast on Bidenpura lane no.42, behind the market building. Vidyaratan Jindal, in the market to meet a friend, said: "I had just stepped into my friend's shop when the blast occurred. We ran out, and found smoke all around. It was all over in five minutes."
Kuldeep Singh, a sevak at the nearby Sant Sujan Singh Gurudwara, was on his way back home at the time: "People started screaming; everyone was pulling others away from the spot. I picked up two small children; they were badly injured. I hope they survived.
"I saw five bodies myself."

Heading: Court martial dismisses major general for sexual misconduct - Indian Express
Content:
Frenzied relatives thronged several of the city hospitals where victims of the serial blasts in the capital lay admitted even as police said the toll stood at 20 so far.

The maximum activity was seen at RML hospital in central Delhi which received most of the casualties and the injured.

The Saturday evening blasts at the Central Park in Connaught Place killed soon-to-be married Kamini, who along with her fiance Rawat Kashyap, had come to the city.
